entry.summary: This paper shows that forward-KL distillation can retain only 0.01 percent of the teacher's vocabulary support with no observed MMLU-Pro degradation, dramatically cutting the cost of computing and storing teacher targets. The study distills Qwen3 4B to 1.7B with confirmations on larger pairs and under answer-only supervision.

entry.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Jiali Cheng, Oleg Rokhlenko, Joo-Kyung Kim, Hadi Amiri, Xingzhi Guo

entry.summary: Introduces DecArena, a benchmark for decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication where agents see only local state and interact with neighbors, featuring scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Experiments probe how agents discover non-local resources and collaborate without a global orchestrator, motivated by privacy and scalability concerns of personal AI agents.

entry.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning

author.name: Haofeng Wang, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang, Tiange Zhang, Boren Zheng, Xuanyi Liu, Siyu Tao, Danni Yu, Gan Lin, Haocheng Tang, Tianzizhe Guo, Mingyuan Su, Boyuan Chen, Zhongyuan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PhysCapBench, a benchmark measuring whether video captions preserve the physical interactions, transitions, and state evolution that define real-world processes, spanning internet videos and embodied demonstrations. It provides a yardstick for assessing annotation quality and captioning strategies for physical AI training supervision.

entry.title: A New Framework for Quantum Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Alireza Tavakoli, Mohsen Heidari

entry.summary: The authors propose a fully quantum reinforcement learning framework in which agent, environment, rewards, and return accumulation are all quantum, motivated by the limitations of classical interfaces where measurement collapses state and discards entanglement. This is a step toward QRL formulations suited to genuinely quantum environments such as quantum system control.

entry.title: Look Here, Then Decide: Small Decision Models in a Harness Find Memory-Safety Vulnerabilities at Scale on Commodity GPUs

author.name: Tim De Wachter, Kyryl Volkov, Myrto Eleftheria Gkogkou, Mathieu Huysman

entry.summary: This work shows that a 4B-parameter open-weight decision model, Intern-Decision-4B, can support large-scale memory-safety vulnerability discovery in C/C++ open-source projects when embedded in a harness with deterministic incomplete-fix miners and shape localizers. The small model alone is weak, but ranks candidate functions to prioritize queues, with no frontier model involved, running on commodity GPUs.

entry.title: Probe What-If Worlds Before You Ship: Persona Simulation for Real-World Decision Making

author.name: Julie Zhu, Jianheng Hou, Zhixu Silvia Tao, Shi Bo, Yilan Fan, Yixuan He, Zhiyuan Hu, Shirley Huang, Fangyu Liu, Yijun Wang, Zibu Wei, Haimingyue Xu, Zhen Xu, Zichen Yuan, Jierui Zuo, Jintao Huang, Yifan Wang, Qianfeng Wen, Jiahan Li, Zhejian Peng, Bowen Yang, Shushu Liang, Yuexing Hao, Xiaomin Li

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework and infrastructure for translating real industry product questions into controlled experiments with simulated LLM persona users, supporting concurrent runs across cohort-stimulus-environment combinations with auditable logging and aggregation. It aims to replace or augment parts of user research and A/B-style testing.

entry.title: Outcome-Mass Alignment: Controlling Length-Dependent Trajectory Influence in Multi-Turn LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dawei Zhang, Yubin Huangfu, Jessica Fan, Boyu Wei, Likang Wu, Hongke Zhao, Ming He, Zhu Teng

entry.summary: Identifies two accounting pathologies in stepwise group-relative RL for multi-turn LLM agents: outcome-statistics multiplicity, where one episode outcome is counted multiple times across expanded rows, and objective-mass imbalance, where token-level reduction gives long trajectories disproportionate weight. The proposed Outcome-Mass Alignment method makes both accounting choices explicit and corrects the biases.

entry.title: Back to the Question: Tracing Visual Distraction Through Text Tokens

author.name: Marie Amale Huynh, Regev Cohen, Serena Yeung-Levy, Sivan Doveh

entry.summary: This mechanistic study shows that distractor images reduce vision-language model accuracy even when models correctly identify the relevant image, indicating image selection alone is insufficient. Combining attention analysis with targeted knockouts in Qwen2.5-VL and IDEA models, the authors trace distraction through text tokens, localizing where visual interference enters reasoning. The findings inform how to build distraction-robust multimodal systems.

entry.title: A General Concept-based Decomposition for Vision-Language Embeddings

author.name: Simone Alberto Peirone, Ortal Senouf, Francesca Pistilli, Giuseppe Averta, Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: GRACE learns concept-based structure directly at the vision-language feature-space level, producing semantic and general concept decompositions that capture a model's global semantic structure rather than only local, instance-level attributions. Prior decomposition methods optimize per-instance and miss compositional generalization across inputs, tasks, and domains. The work aims to make VLM representations align with how humans would naturally describe visual inputs.

entry.title: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Wenchuan Zhang, Chengyang Zhang, Fengling Li, Ting Yin, Chen Shu, Jie Chen, Shuwan Zhang, Xiaoyan Wu, Zhang Zhang, Yuhao Yi, Jiancheng Lv, Hong Bu

entry.summary: CaseScope benchmarks multimodal LLMs on case-level pathology diagnosis from multiple curated fields of one lesion, mimicking how pathologists integrate low-power architecture with high-power cytology across views. It includes a teaching-hospital cohort harmonized against a WHO-based ontology with pathologist re-review, addressing the limits of single-image or whole-slide-only benchmarks. The benchmark probes a more realistic diagnostic workflow for MLLMs.

entry.title: Fog-FWL: A Large-Scale Full-Waveform LiDAR Dataset for Recovering Fog-Hidden Objects

author.name: Kazuma Ikeda, Kotaro Oishi, Ryosei Hara, Ryo Yoshida, Takahiro Kado, Ibuki Fujioka, Taro Beppu, Mariko Isogawa, Kentaro Yoshioka

entry.summary: Fog-FWL provides a foundation for recovering fog-hidden objects from full-waveform LiDAR, which retains weak returns discarded by conventional peak detection. It pairs a real-world benchmark of 7,527 foggy FWL frames across 8 scenes with a large-scale synthetic training set, enabling research previously blocked by data unavailability.

entry.title: BrickFlow: Connectivity-Guided Brick Reconstruction

author.name: Peter Kulits, Cordelia Schmid

entry.summary: Addresses inferring the pose of each LEGO part from an image of an assembled object, a combinatorial problem with discrete physical constraints. The approach trains a set-conditioned SE(3) flow model on procedurally generated assemblies, finetunes it with image conditioning using 1% of the data, and adds analytic connectivity-field guidance to enforce connected assemblies.

entry.title: CrowdMAPS: Crowdsourcing Multiple Actions per State for Real-World Imitation Learning

author.name: Yilong Song, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Karthik Desingh, Chen Zhu-Tian

entry.summary: CrowdMAPS is a web-based crowdsourcing paradigm that lets remote annotators specify multiple alternative valid actions for states visited by a real robot through a 3D interface, expanding datasets along the width dimension (actions per state) rather than only collecting more trajectories. This addresses the high cost of physical demonstrations in robot imitation learning. The idea of cheaply densifying action supervision is promising for scaling real-robot datasets.

entry.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Zhenghan Zhu, Yutong Han, Jiayin Zou, Gao Kejun, Chang Liu, Shaoxuan Xie, Chi Zhang, Shi Haoyang, Zongxuan Lai, Sen Cui, Guocai Yao, Miao Liu

entry.summary: HEIR is a dataset resource pairing human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, preserving successive episodes in which requests are fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. With human-authored annotations, it supports research on intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion in human-robot interaction. It targets the underexplored combination of egocentric intent cues and long-horizon robot assistance.

entry.title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents

author.name: Jiani Zhang, Manav Garg, Eugenie Lai, Cheng Zhen, Eva Sharma, Yang Pan, Yaming Lin, Alon Halevy

entry.summary: SynthCorp is a platform that generates customizable synthetic corporate data estates and evaluation benchmarks for LLM data agents by simulating how business events modify databases, documents, and catalogs over time. It interleaves routine and disruption events and pairs estates with tasks and executable gold programs to counter benchmark saturation.

entry.title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Jie Ren, Jonathan Rosenfeld, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: The paper improves parallel test-time scaling by using internal confidence signals early, pruning low-quality reasoning paths before they are fully expanded. It offers a new analysis showing confidence matters most near the decision boundary and that even small confidence gaps amplify under multi-sample aggregation, yielding better performance per unit of compute.

entry.title: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark

author.name: Shunming Liu, Jianyi Peng, Cheng Li, Lu Hou, Pei Huang, Yajing Sun, Huaxiao Liu

entry.summary: Introduces MVDriveBench, a video QA benchmark for multimodal LLMs in autonomous driving featuring synchronized surround-view inputs, spatio-temporal understanding, and reasoning-chain-oriented evaluation across 12 task categories spanning low-level perception to high-level driving decisions. It targets the gap where existing MLLMs focus on front-view information.

entry.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents

author.name: Quanjiang Guo, Sijie Wang, Qianyang Zhu, Ben Zhang, Jinchuan Zhang, Ke Yan, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: MemCredit reframes agent memory selection around decision utility rather than semantic relevance, estimating the conditional marginal contribution of individual memories via controlled counterfactual interventions and distilling those credits into a lightweight utility estimator. The goal is to identify which stored memories actually improve an agent's actions during long-horizon web tasks.

entry.title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents

author.name: You Wu, Guhong Zhang, Hongwei Li, Xinyue Hong, Yuan Jia

entry.summary: AstroMemBench is a benchmark for evaluating memory systems of embodied agents for long-term spacecraft autonomy, covering 16 memory subchallenges via 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration. A deterministic environment scores task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use, and ablations across nine conditions demonstrate the benchmark's discriminative power.

entry.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Haochen Liu, Qianhao Zhu, Zixuan Wang, Dingming Li, Tongbo Chen, Peng Qiu, Yingqi Qu, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: This work separates the roles a decision model can play in long-horizon agents — actor (choosing actions), judge (evaluating trajectories), and teacher (scoring actions for RL) — and empirically compares LLMs in each role on ALFWorld and WebShop. Notably, models that act poorly can still judge or teach well, since judges seeing full trajectories credit subgoal steps that actors skip.

entry.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?

author.name: Ethan Lin, Akanksha Sarkar, Ziang Liu, Kristin Branson, Jennifer J. Sun

entry.summary: AgentSSL frames semi-supervised learning as a program search problem for MLE agents operating under limited labeled data and weak feedback. The study finds that agents can synthesize code combining and adapting established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines under matched compute, filling a gap since MLE agents had been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised regimes.

entry.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy

author.name: Bokai Pan, Ruijie Yang, Mingyue Cheng, Jiahao Wang, Xiaoyu Tao

entry.summary: Introduces CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting spanning 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets with external variables, events, and historical cases. It provides a modular harness with 49 forecasting-native tools and a state-adaptive evaluation loop that scores agents beyond one-shot numerical accuracy.

entry.title: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation

author.name: Zhenqi He, Dunyuan Xu, Yang Bo, Kien T. Pham, Yanghao Wang, Shuhan Li, Xintong Guo, Yuyang He, Fang Liu, Huankang Guan, Jingyan Chen, Rui Liu, Long Chen

entry.summary: MemInStream is a benchmark for evaluating memory in streaming video understanding, arguing that QA accuracy alone conflates forgetting with visual understanding failures or reliance on linguistic priors and recent frames. It introduces an evidence-controlled validation protocol to isolate genuine memory capabilities as video history grows.

entry.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models

author.name: Alejandro Ca\~nada, Chema Garabito

entry.summary: Iris-Z applies the bitter-lesson argument to visual intelligence: rather than task-specific monocular geometry architectures, it uses a single general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together, with one backbone denoising and reasoning jointly. The paper claims this unified approach scales past specialist geometry models.

entry.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents

author.name: Cheng-Yu Hsieh, Ting-Yao Hu, Sanjoy Chowdhury, Oncel Tuzel, Raviteja Vemulapalli

entry.summary: JudgeMix addresses the training-inference distribution mismatch in SFT for LLM agents by using a judge model to guide mixed rollouts between the expert and target model, replacing blind intervention heuristics and indiscriminate uniform step-wise supervision. The judge selectively determines when and how expert assistance is applied, grounding training data in the target model's native state distribution.

entry.title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation

author.name: Carolina Fortuna, Blaz Bertalanic

entry.summary: Tests the averaging argument behind multi-agent LLM systems using Fermi estimation, decomposing 2.51M answers from 15 open-weight models (3B-72B) into item-shared and residual error components. It finds that errors are correlated at the item level across teammates, so ensemble error does not shrink as 1/sqrt(N), limiting the value of naive model aggregation.

entry.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination

author.name: Wei Feng, Meiling Chen, Boxiao Chen, Lu Liu, Bin Zi, Libin Ye, Xingyu Lu, Lei Xu, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: This systems paper presents coordinated optimizations to reduce batch makespan for LLM agent workloads that alternate between inference and environment interaction, as in benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. It introduces a workload-based resource model for GPU-memory allocation between KV cache and recurrent state, trajectory-aware routing and scheduling for cache reuse, and decoupled sample admission under constrained environment capacity.

entry.title: Introducing Feedback Delays to Non-Delayed Adversarial MDPs: Optimal $\sqrt S$ and $\sqrt K$ Dependencies in Tabular and Linear AMDPs

author.name: Aarush Kulkarni, Khang Nguyen, William Chang, Yan Dai

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves open regret gaps in adversarial MDPs with bandit feedback: it achieves the optimal sqrt(S) dependence in tabular AMDPs, closing a long-standing gap to the lower bound, and improves linear AMDP regret from K^(3/4) toward optimal sqrt(K) dependencies. The core technical challenge is estimating the Q-function of a changing policy from correlated historical data.

entry.title: Stealthy, High-Impact False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Grid Using Physics-Constrained GAN

author.name: Md. Mainul Islam, Hasan Kurban, Abdulrahman Takiddin, Muhammad Ismail, Rachad Atat, Erchin Serpedin

entry.summary: Proposes PCGAN, a detector-agnostic physics-constrained GAN that learns power-flow sensitivities from deployed sensor measurements to craft stealthy false data injection attacks on smart grid state estimation. It implements PCGAN and seven existing attacks on the IEEE 300-bus system, jointly optimizing stealth and impact while relaxing assumptions about attacker knowledge.

entry.title: TabOmics: A Small, Open Tabular Foundation Model for Wide Omics Data

author.name: Andrea L\'opez-Garc\'ia, Luis Bote-Curiel, Francisco Javier Gimeno-Blanes, Jos\'e Luis Rojo-\'Alvarez, Sergio Mu\~noz-Romero

entry.summary: Introduces TabOmics, a 7.3M-parameter open tabular foundation model pretrained only on synthetic tables, designed for high-dimensional, low-sample omics data. It processes all features jointly in one forward pass to produce predictions, attention-based feature importances, and sample embeddings, evaluated on 46 classification tasks across three benchmarks.

entry.title: Constructing and Validating Memorisation Audits for EHR Foundation Models

author.name: Inigo Stibbe, Joshua Placidi, Padmanabhan Ramnarayan, A. Aldo Faisal

entry.summary: Builds and validates memorization audits for GPT-2-style models trained on MIMIC-IV electronic health records, testing token reconstruction, sensitive-attribute disclosure, and random patient-level canaries across checkpoints. Findings show small training-vs-held-out differences and limited excess sensitive disclosure, suggesting memorization is harder to detect than in web-text settings due to clinical predictability.

entry.title: From Link Prediction to Linear Community Detection: A Finite-Sample Guarantee for Graph Pretraining

author.name: Ying Chen, Zhangyang Wang, Yixuan He

entry.summary: The paper provides the first quantitative finite-sample theory explaining why link-prediction pretraining yields embeddings useful for node classification, proving a conditional reduction from LP excess risk to community-classification error in the stochastic block model. The bound decomposes into optimization, generalization, and decoder terms for any bounded GNN encoder with a symmetric bilinear decoder.

entry.title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration

author.name: Kaixuan Ji, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: The paper closes the gap between known bounds for smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction against adaptive adversaries, constructing an adversary whose outcome mean tracks the forecaster's cumulative residual to force Omega(sqrt(T)) error. This matches the previously known upper bound, resolving the minimax rate.

entry.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

author.name: Tomohiro Sawada, Kartik Goyal

entry.summary: The paper identifies that LoRA adapters, especially high-rank ones, use far less effective rank than their configured rank, contributing to poor performance versus full fine-tuning in heterogeneous and continual learning. It proposes training mechanisms that maximize adapter effective rank to improve the learning-forgetting trade-off.

entry.title: An Eyring-Kramers Formula for Singular Wells

author.name: Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu

entry.summary: The paper extends the classical Eyring-Kramers transition-rate formula to low-temperature Langevin diffusion between singular, non-isolated wells of a real-analytic potential, motivated by the dynamical persistence of learned behaviors in AI safety. It introduces an inclusion-minimal gate construction and proves that gate uniqueness is equivalent to all minimizing paths passing through the unique saddle.

entry.title: ShadowBench: Exposing Lexical Anchoring and the Illusion of Forgetting in Large Language Models

author.name: Sujan Maharjan, Lu Liu

entry.summary: ShadowBench introduces a shortcut-resistant benchmark for latent entity association, demonstrating that LLM knowledge is lexically anchored: models retain extensive factual information but struggle to retrieve it when explicit name tokens are removed. The evaluation reveals a pervasive Shadow Gap across scales, including frontier models such as GPT-5.4 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 (both long-established releases), quantifying retrieval failure without surface lexical cues.

entry.title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation

author.name: Jinze Tao, Yuxiao Han, Kangkang Dong, Yancong Wei, Xiaojun Zhu, Bokui Chen, Houde Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes H2E, a method that distills successful LLM-planner agent sessions into a vision-language-action (VLA) model so the VLA can navigate alone at test time without the costly planner in the loop. It converts agent motions into VLA actions under original task instructions, masking losses on goal-divergent steps and labeling states near the goal, addressing the mismatch between agent sessions and clean demonstrations.

entry.title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help

author.name: Yihan Xia, Wenxin Xu, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a four-layer framework connecting verifiable AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels, and hardware platforms, and reviews the zero-knowledge-proof literature for neural network verification. It includes original measurements across six systems to clarify how hardware acceleration affects end-to-end proving costs for large transformer models.

entry.title: ToolTurns: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Milad Gholami, Brendan King, Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: ToolTurns is a benchmark of 2,620 multi-turn tool-use dialogues spanning 1,827 tools and 11,004 API endpoints, where each conversation starts underspecified and includes context-dependent follow-ups testing clarification and context retention. An open-source user simulator with a checker-fixer pipeline accompanies the benchmark, and the best of nine evaluated agents completes only a fraction of full conversations despite solving 69.6 percent of individual requests.

entry.title: Can We Make an LLM Dumber, or Is It Just Playing Dumb? An Empirical Study of Believable Performance Throttling

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, QingHao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: Studies the inverse problem of benchmark scores: can a model be driven to a target capability score with failures that resemble a naturally weaker model? Introduces CapLadder, an IRT-calibrated 1,985-item suite, and finds a weak-teacher LoRA dial achieves precise calibration while prompting, temperature, and weight noise cannot.

entry.title: EvenVLM: A Text and Multimodal Dataset for the Even Language with Vision-Language Fine-Tuning

author.name: Daniil Makovetskii, Ivan Bondarenko

entry.summary: Introduces the first text and multimodal (VQA) dataset for Even, an endangered Tungusic language with roughly 6,800 speakers, built from 50,521 dictionary/phrasebook entries expanded into 107,543 synthetic training examples. The authors also propose a tokenizer expansion algorithm tailored to Even's agglutinative morphology, cutting average tokens per word by 27%, and fine-tune with LoRA.

entry.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate

author.name: Minhae Oh, Jeonghye Kim, Jinwoo Koo, Yeongoon Kim, Jimin Seo, Minsik Seol, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: Diagnoses why remasking fails in diffusion language models: hidden states contain error signals not exposed by token confidence, and remasking an isolated error with fixed context reproduces it. The proposed DiVR verifier predicts whether a partial sequence will reach a correct answer and decides when and what to regenerate, improving LLaDA-8B-Base average accuracy on five reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: HeadIO: Body-Frame Heading Decomposition for Neural Inertial Odometry on Head-Mounted Devices

author.name: Taeyoung Yeon, Yiquan Li, Chenfeng Gao, Vasco Xu, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: HeadIO improves neural inertial odometry for VR headsets, AR glasses, and earbuds by decomposing heading in the body frame, addressing the yaw-equivariance limitations of gravity-aligned world-frame methods. It uses a bidirectional Mamba backbone and achieves equivariance properties at roughly one-third the FLOPs of the prior EqNIO pipeline. The result enables camera-free head tracking on resource-constrained wearable devices.

entry.title: From Concepts to Interactions: Dynamic Graph Semantic Recomposition for Safe Visual Generation

author.name: Qinghui Gong, Jinshan Lai, Xunlei Chen, Hua Meng, Zhengchun Zhou

entry.summary: DGSR addresses safety alignment in flow-matching text-to-image and text-to-video generation by modeling how a concept's safety depends on semantic context, using dynamic graph semantic recomposition instead of static concept erasure. This prevents over-suppression of safe scenes containing potentially sensitive terms, such as a knife in a cooking context versus a violent one. The approach balances suppressing unsafe content with preserving legitimate generation quality.

entry.title: ThermalSplat: Generalizable Pose-Free Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Thermal 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Prasanna S, Gopi Raju Matta, Divya Madhuri Vemunuri, Kaushik Mitra

entry.summary: ThermalSplat tackles 3D reconstruction from thermal infrared images, where low texture and view-dependent emissivity break standard pose estimation and Gaussian splatting pipelines. The method is generalizable, pose-free, and works under sparse views without aligned RGB-thermal data, targeting search-and-rescue and navigation applications. It removes key practical bottlenecks (dense capture, per-scene optimization, RGB-thermal alignment) from thermal 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Where to Generate Touch: Do Image Latents Preserve Material Recognition?

author.name: Wanghao Ye, Aarosh Das, Sihan Chen, Yiting Wang, Bowei Tian, Guoheng Sun, Shwai He, Zheyu Shen, Ziyao Wang, Yexiao He, Zhaoyi Liu, Meng Liu, Yuning Zhang, Meng Feng, Ziyi Wang, Yilong Dai, Yifei Dong, Siyuan Peng, Zhenle Duan, Joshua Liu, Lang Xiong, Daeun Jung, Aditya Sarkar, Parastoo Pilevar, Xiaochuan Gong, Yancheng Zhu, Yingying Fan, Qiong Wang, Ang Li

entry.summary: This large-collaboration paper tests whether tactile generators can reuse pretrained image-model latent spaces by checking if a material classifier trained on real GelSight presses survives encode-decode reconstruction. Discrete 16x tokenizers lose 6.5-9.7 accuracy points while Stable Diffusion VAE reconstructions lose only 0.3, and retraining on reconstructions without new labels narrows the discrete gap. The findings guide latent-space choice for touch generation in robot learning.

entry.title: Reconstruct What You Can: Distractor-free 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Joel Julin, Liuyue Xie, Ananya Bal, Mose Sakashita, Koichiro Niinuma, Laszlo A. Jeni

entry.summary: ReCan-GS is a 4D Gaussian Splatting framework that separates coherent scene content from transient distractors (occluders, shadows, volumetric effects) in casual video using a Jacobian-based deformation-sensitivity score derived from the learned deformation field. The score guides partitioning into dynamic Core Gaussians and per-view Distractor Gaussians or post-hoc pruning, avoiding ghosting from joint modeling.

entry.title: Sprint3D: Accelerating End-to-End 3D Asset Generation through Pipeline Optimization

author.name: Sho Kuno, Ruihan Yu, Yonghao Yu, Guixu Lin, Lian Fu, Muyao Niu, Yu-Ju Tsai, Zheng-Hui Huang, Yi-Chuan Huang, Siqi Yang, Fengbo Lan, Erwin Wu, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: Sprint3D accelerates image-to-3D asset generation by profiling the public Pixal3D pipeline and finding that mesh post-processing, mostly CPU-based UV unwrapping, consumes 85 percent of wall-clock time versus 14 percent for the rectified flows. The authors rebuild post-processing on the GPU, remove it from the critical path, and cut network sampling time, offering a broadly reusable lesson that pipeline bottlenecks often lie outside the generative networks.

entry.title: HiVE-VQA: Hierarchical Interaction via Volumetric Embedding for Video Quality Assessment

author.name: Robbie Hamilton, Fan Zhang, David Bull

entry.summary: Proposes HiVE-VQA, the first no-reference video quality assessment framework built on a frozen JEPA-based video encoder (V-JEPA 2.1), extracting token grids from multiple depths and fusing them with a compact 3D convolutional head. It avoids complex multi-branch pipelines or heavy fine-tuning while achieving strong VQA performance.

entry.title: I See What You Want: Decoding Hierarchical Operator Intent from Visual Teleoperation History

author.name: Xiangyi Jia, Kaixian Qu, Shengzhi Wang, Chenyu Yang, Robert Katzschmann, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Formulates hierarchical intent prediction for teleoperation, jointly inferring ongoing atomic actions and broader missions from short visual history, and introduces VI AMO, a dataset of 6,600 episodes from eleven robot sources with over 13,000 action and 9,700 mission annotations. Findings show large proprietary models struggle on held-out settings, motivating specialized approaches.

entry.title: Galop: Billion-Scale Genetic Programming on a Single GPU

author.name: Xavier Hill Roy, Stephen Kelly

entry.summary: Presents Galop, a hybrid CPU-GPU linear genetic programming system that assigns one individual per CUDA warp to align GP evaluation with GPU execution, outperforming the recent EvoGP system in 27 of 28 comparisons with speedups up to 13.6x on data-rich symbolic regression. It enables billion-scale GP on a single GPU.

entry.title: From a Single RGB Image to Robot Execution: Metric Scene Alignment and Contact-Guided Retargeting

author.name: Zhenxuan Ding, Yu Huang, Xinmiao Wang, Chenghao Sun, Ziyang Dong, Wenhao Cui

entry.summary: This work presents a unified pipeline that takes a single RGB image, reconstructs metric scene geometry, generates scene-conditioned humanoid interaction motion, and retargets it to a robot with contact-guided corrections to prevent support errors. It eliminates the need for prebuilt 3D scene assets when transferring humanoid interaction skills to new environments. The contribution addresses a practical bottleneck in scaling humanoid imitation to unstructured real scenes.

entry.title: Does Your World Model Know Actions Have Consequences?

author.name: Ayush Gaggar, Jared Berry, Todd D. Murphey

entry.summary: This paper argues that existing world model metrics (reconstruction quality, task success) fail to measure whether models correctly predict consequences of counterfactual actions, and proposes sensitivity-analysis-based auditing of forced responses to action perturbations. The framing matters because world models deployed on hardware must reliably simulate alternative actions without physical trials. It contributes an evaluation methodology rather than a new model, filling a genuine gap in embodied world model assessment.

entry.title: ActionCodec2: A Streaming Action Tokenizer

author.name: Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Shiduo Zhang, Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Jinqiu Wang, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: ActionCodec2 is a non-neural streaming action tokenizer for autoregressive VLA models that releases actions incrementally rather than requiring full chunk decoding, while bounding trajectory reconstruction error within a tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state so errors are corrected rather than accumulated, and the minimal primitive set is derived via geometric covering results (exact for translation, tight-bounded for rotation), with Set-BPE for compression. This could meaningfully reduce latency and improve precision in action-token-based robot policies.

entry.title: Remember What Changes the Odds: Critic-Gated Event Memory for Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Xuanzhuo Liu, Chuankang Li, Maoqing Yao, Guanghui Ren

entry.summary: The paper introduces decision aliasing in long-horizon manipulation, where identical observations require different actions depending on execution history. CGEM is a critic-gated event memory that stores only events which substantially change the critic's predicted probability of task success, providing an outcome-grounded criterion for what to remember. This is a principled alternative to perceptual or semantic event-selection heuristics.

entry.title: ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience

author.name: CaP Team, Changxu Wei, Yunpeng Qing, Guozheng Ma, Bowen Liu, Zexin He, Yilun Kong, Haoming Gu, Jingyuan Liu, Tianyu Zhu, Jianfei Wang, Junqiang Kou, Huinan Mo, Hao Lv, Pengbin Li, Yuesong Wang, Bo Li, Huan Zhou, Shunyu Liu, Chunxiao Liu, Bixuan Jin, Shaopeng Yin, Fei Wang, Zhi Hou, Jiaxing Huang, Changqing Zou, Dacheng Tao, Xiaogang Wang

entry.summary: ACE-CaP-0 investigates building reliable code-as-policies for agentic robot control while limiting physical experimentation cost, using human guidance as a source of action priors and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing generated code. Executable programs let reasoning invested during development be reused across runs, reducing repeated frontier-model calls during execution. It extends the Code-as-Policies paradigm toward experience-driven, sample-efficient robot skill acquisition.

entry.title: A Sensitivity Framework for Assessing External Validity

author.name: Ariel Boyarsky, Naoki Egami, Hongseok Namkoong

entry.summary: The authors develop a partial-identification framework for assessing whether causal findings generalize beyond experimental sites, accommodating affine families of parameter restrictions such as the effect hierarchy principle via an optimization-driven approach. This addresses the common setting where the number of sites is smaller than the number of moderating site-level variables.

entry.title: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Abhinav Gupta, Ben Slivinski, Yashica Patodia, Michael Saldivar

entry.summary: This evaluation examines LLM-judge proof-step verification pipelines on open-weight models across GPQA, AIME-2025, and MATH-500, finding large precision gains on hard tasks but big coverage losses. Notably, a simple token-matched self-consistency selector nearly matches the verifier, and a diagnostic reveals many verifications end in invalid certificates.

entry.title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity

author.name: Eduardo de Avila-Armenta, Ra\'ul Alejandro Aquino-Ibarra, Jorge Octavio Nicol\'as-D\'iaz, Umberto Leon-Dominguez

entry.summary: The authors built nine negotiation architectures spanning rule-based, search, optimization, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning families and ran them simultaneously on both sides of a Gale-Shapley matching market (e.g., freight brokering) under balanced and two scarcity conditions rotated across 36 pairs. This goes beyond prior one-on-one duels to capture how strategies behave against several live rivals under shifting supply-demand conditions.

entry.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds

author.name: Pengcheng Zhou, Xuanyu Liu, Yanchen Yin, Tianjie Ju, Bobo Li, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: GeoWorld is a controllable platform simulating continuously evolving geographic environments grounded in real-world structure, and LiveGeo is a benchmark requiring agents to actively acquire information, verify whether evidence for prior decisions remains valid, and revise plans as the world changes. Results reveal shortcomings of agents that plan over fixed states.

entry.title: Mach2: Scientific Discovery Platform with Deterministic Execution Constraints

author.name: Vansh Sharma, Venkat Raman

entry.summary: Mach2 couples LLM agent orchestration with deterministic, lint-like checks of tool requests, source changes, acceptance tests, and artifact contracts so that natural-language operating rules are enforced rather than merely prompted. It combines test-driven development, AST-based analysis, and evolutionary search for verification and optimization in scientific workflows.

entry.title: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage

author.name: Jue Xu, Yue Wang, Qi Zhao

entry.summary: Presents QSim-Arena, a framework where AI agents in a closed loop of verification and benchmarking translate published quantum simulation techniques into executable components, reproduce results, and benchmark across Hamiltonian families to continuously map where quantum simulation advantage holds against classical methods.

entry.title: When Does Learned Constraint Selection Pay in Security-Constrained Optimisation? A Boundary Map from SCOPF to Unit Commitment

author.name: Milad Kazemi, Behzad Kazemtabrizi

entry.summary: Analyzes when learning-to-optimize constraint selection for security-constrained optimal power flow beats a learning-free fixed umbrella set of all training-observed binding constraints. It introduces the price of a spare criterion—showing the umbrella is exactly optimal wherever feasible—and maps the boundary where learned selection pays, testing every PGLib-OPF network up to 10,000 buses.

entry.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs

author.name: Sachin Acharya, Niyoj Oli, Shishir Adhikari, Aminu Lawal, Yash Raj Shrestha, Prashnna K Gyawali, Binod Bhattarai

entry.summary: Proposes MAGIC, which detects hallucination in medical large multimodal models by quantifying modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads with the Gini coefficient, framing hallucination as disproportionate attention distribution during answer generation. The method demonstrates statistically grounded detection of clinically unverifiable outputs in high-stakes medical settings.

entry.title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models

author.name: Y. Zhu, K. Marlor, V. Lavelle, T. S. Brettin, M. Sacco, C. Siniscalchi, H. W. Raeder, M. R. Weil, R. L. Stevens

entry.summary: This dataset paper releases drug screening data from patient-derived organoids (PDOs) across four studies, including multi-omics profiles, to improve evaluation and training of anti-cancer drug response prediction models. PDOs better recapitulate patient tumors than the immortalized cell lines most DRP models currently rely on, helping bridge the gap toward precision oncology.

entry.title: Agentic Computational Algebra

author.name: Ryan A. Anderson, Matthew Trager, Ben Bowman, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: The paper proposes computational algebra as a benchmark environment for evaluating AI agents, since problems there have independently verifiable answers and controllable structure and difficulty, and the key challenge is time rather than correctness. It evaluates how effectively agents discover and exploit special structure within and across tasks to reduce computational costs, using benchmark families of systems.

entry.title: Label-Efficient Document-Grounded Factuality Detection via Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning

author.name: Chao Chen, Shanshan Lin, Dongsheng Hong, Sibo Ju, Wenjie Yang, Sihong Xie, Xiangwen Liao

entry.summary: Proposes CPIL, a two-stage Siamese framework that converts a small labeled set into relational supervision for document-grounded factuality detection by constructing positive pairs from label-preserving paraphrases and negative pairs from perturbed instances. This yields compact factuality detectors without the large labeled or synthetic corpora usually required.

entry.title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting

author.name: George Cazenavette, Angelina Quan, Giannis Daras, Antonio Torralba, Vincent Sitzmann

entry.summary: The paper proposes a new dataset distillation method that learns synthetic samples approximating the per-class data distribution directly, rather than optimizing against a classifier. Distilled data are drifted in the latent space of a feature extractor toward real data and away from each other, without a classification objective, yielding synthetic samples that cover the real distribution well.

entry.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware

author.name: William Fleshman

entry.summary: STEALTH addresses a fragility in provably secure linguistic steganography: bit-exact schemes fail almost entirely when the receiver's floating-point precision, quantization, or GPU architecture differs from the sender's, or even when scoring text in parallel versus sequentially. The paper presents a steganography scheme built for this setting, robust to such hardware-level differences.

entry.title: Designing Institutions for Autonomous AI

author.name: Petter T\"ornberg

entry.summary: A perspective paper arguing that institutional design for populations of autonomous AI agents deserves to be a distinct research focus, since collective capability and alignment depend on the institutions governing agent interactions. Drawing on institutional political economy, social epistemology, and organizational theory, it proposes seven principles for AI institutions supporting cooperation, reliable collective judgment, and accountability to human purposes.

entry.title: PhysICL: In-Context Learning of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes from Procedural Priors

author.name: Fabien Casenave

entry.summary: PhysICL demonstrates that a single model pretrained on procedurally generated tasks can perform in-context learning of physical field prediction on unstructured meshes, predicting fields with quantiles from a few labeled simulations without weight updates. The same checkpoint handles variable context examples, scalar inputs, output fields, and arbitrary mesh connectivity.

entry.title: Detection Is Not Early Warning: Evaluating Token-Level Alarms on Language Model Failures

author.name: Marco De Negri (ETH Zurich), Luca Sartori (ETH Zurich), Lorenzo Baggi (ETH Zurich), Moritz Reihs (ETH Zurich), Eduard Frank \v{D}urech (ETH AI Center), Mennatallah El-Assady (ETH Zurich), Valentina Pyatkin (ETH Zurich, ETH AI Center), Anna Hedstr\"om (ETH AI Center, Solaris Research)

entry.summary: The paper introduces PREWARN, an evaluation protocol that scores LLM failure monitors on whether they warn before a failure's annotated token-level onset, rather than only on response-level AUROC. Applied as a case study to repetitive degeneration in three open language models, it shows that detection and early warning are distinct capabilities.

entry.title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for Fairness under Data Imbalance: Theory and Adaptive Allocation

author.name: Zhengchi Ma, Kaifeng Zhang, Anru R. Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies two mechanisms, prevalence imbalance and group-size imbalance, through which training-distribution shifts induce Equal Opportunity disparities, and studies exact full-balance synthetic data augmentation that equalizes all group-label cells. It establishes conditions under which full balancing strictly improves Equal Opportunity, with an adaptive allocation scheme and prediction-error comparisons.

entry.title: What Makes a VLA Reactive? A Study of Execution Strategies for Dynamic Manipulation

author.name: Zhuoyue Li, Zhendong Han, Pankhuri Vanjani, Wenting Li, Rudolf Lioutikov

entry.summary: This systematic study examines how prediction and execution horizons, synchronous versus asynchronous inference, action-delivery strategies, and policy adaptations affect the reactivity of pretrained vision-language-action models on dynamic manipulation tasks. Using a VLA on simulation and real-robot benchmarks, it finds that roughly one-second prediction horizons are best and that trajectory-continuity methods outperform alternatives.

entry.title: Learning Mixtures of Exponential Family

author.name: Mansi Sood, Devavrat Shah

entry.summary: The paper studies learning mixtures of two bounded-support exponential-family distributions with shared interaction parameters and component-specific linear parameters, with structured label sequences. It proposes a convex-loss estimator avoiding the log-partition function and establishes finite-sample identification and error bounds for the interaction matrix.

entry.title: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on a Single GPU

author.name: Fuyi Chen

entry.summary: BlinkMimic builds on SuperMimic and InstantTrack to dramatically speed up humanoid whole-body motion tracking policy training by backpropagating through a learned world model with parallel simulation and Muon updates. On a simulated Unitree G1, it trains one policy covering all 40 LAFAN1 clips in 3.4 minutes on a single RTX 4090, a large efficiency gain over hours-long training.

entry.title: Janus-MOPD: Tracing the Student Learning Dynamics in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zongji Yu, Ming Zhang, Dongcheng Zhang, Jiawei Zhou, Haotian Pang, Yiliu Sun, Xiang Wang, Youbang Sun, Chaochao Lu, Chen Gong

entry.summary: Studies how student learning dynamics unfold in multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD), where multiple domain-specific teacher models are distilled into one reasoning model. The paper identifies why students fail to acquire multi-domain capabilities simultaneously under domain heterogeneity and analyzes the dynamics of degradation.

entry.title: From Pixels to Prompts: Physics-Guided Language Enhancement for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Mei Qiu

entry.summary: The paper identifies stable physical image characteristics that discriminate natural from AI-generated images across 15 handcrafted descriptors and over 20 generative models, then injects them into a vision-language representation without external textual prompts at inference. By grounding detection in physics-based cues rather than generator-specific artifacts, it targets better generalization to unseen generators. This addresses a core weakness of current AIGC detectors.

entry.title: Semantic Consistency of Vision Tokens: A Vision-Centric Perspective on Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Nikola {\DJ}uki\'c, Tim Lebailly, Tinne Tuytelaars

entry.summary: The paper analyzes token-level semantic consistency in language-aligned encoders used by MLLMs, distinguishing semantically consistent and inconsistent tokens, and asks whether self-supervised encoders with higher-quality patch representations could benefit MLLMs on vision-centric dense tasks. This provides an analytical lens on why MLLMs underperform on dense vision tasks despite strong language alignment. The findings inform vision encoder design for multimodal models.

entry.title: Raysemble: Metric 3D Bone Reconstruction from a Single X-ray

author.name: Xiaoyang Li, Xinghao Yan, Yuan Chai

entry.summary: Raysemble reconstructs eight lumbar and pelvic bones from a single X-ray by separating bone shape from placement: 3D queries sample regional and global features at their projections, a shared decoder predicts normalized shapes, and predicted depth plus camera geometry resample shapes onto a millimeter grid. Evaluated on 43 CT scans from 23 held-out patients, it leads 15 methods with 65.24 percent Dice without rigid CT alignment.

entry.title: Genie Sim Benchmark: Real-to-Sim Fidelity and Evaluation

author.name: Di Yang, Da Huang, Yang Lv, Fan Yang, Yi Lu, Zheyuan Xing, Linting Guo, Jiaen Shen, Wenjun Sun, Maoqing Yao, Qian Wang

entry.summary: The authors quantify real-to-simulation fidelity of the Genie Sim benchmark across 22 paired robot-task sets, showing fine-tuned pi0.5 policies achieve a 0.9686 score correlation between simulation and reality, alongside system-identification studies of torque agreement, contact transfer, and teleoperation command shaping. Rigorous real-to-sim fidelity measurement is foundational for trusting sim-trained policies. As an industry effort with production-scale robotics context, it provides valuable calibration data for the field.

entry.title: APG-Planner: Learning Vision-Based High-Speed Trajectory Planning via Analytic Policy Gradient

author.name: Jinwoo Lee, Geunsik Bae, Changseung Kim, Jiwoo Kim, Woojae Shin, Hyondong Oh

entry.summary: This paper proposes APG-Planner, a vision-based high-speed trajectory planner trained with analytic policy gradients (APG) rather than noisy sample-based estimates typical of model-free deep RL. By leveraging differentiable dynamics within the planning pipeline, the framework learns reactive, collision-free trajectory generation from onboard visual observations. The method matters because it targets a known weakness of deep RL for robotics control — gradient estimation inefficiency — in a safety-critical, high-speed navigation setting.

entry.title: Maximizing LLM Utility While Managing LLM Fallibility

author.name: Ekta U. Samani, Christopher G. Atkeson

entry.summary: This review frames how autonomous systems should maximize the utility of LLM-provided plans, predictions, and judgments while managing their errors, by adapting reliance on the LLM as performance evidence accumulates. It argues that classical methods for handling imperfect components — noisy sensors, faulty software — transfer to LLM-based systems, and surveys ways to modulate reliance depending on the LLM's role. It connects established reliability engineering to the new wave of LLM-in-the-loop autonomy.

entry.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy

author.name: Haoyang Zhang, Qumeng Sun, Xiao Zhang, Xiang Liu, Zhidong Fan, Junjie Wang

entry.summary: EvoX is a Rust-based multi-model agent runtime that treats the harness as an Operational Policy complementing the model's Semantic Policy, combining model-facing guidance with deterministic runtime control via Action Realization, Execution Continuity, and Outcome Grounding. It also introduces Contrast, an auditable evaluation framework that avoids suppressing harness-native behaviors.

entry.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents

author.name: Subodh Lonkar

entry.summary: The paper introduces Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework governing whether autonomous agents should persistently adopt self-generated modifications to prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires improvement on a prespecified primary objective, and uses reference-relative non-inferiority tests to protect declared capabilities. It directly targets the safety problem that local gains can hide baseline degradation.

entry.title: SPARC: Accurate Photonic Matrix Multiplication via Representative Vectors

author.name: Yasuhiro Fujiwara, Tatsuhiro Nakamori, Hideyuki Kawashima

entry.summary: This work addresses accuracy limits of photonic neural network accelerators caused by low-bit quantization and analog noise. SPARC exploits similarity among activation vectors by computing a representative vector's inner product digitally at high precision and offloading only residual inner products to the photonic hardware, improving inference accuracy while retaining energy benefits.

entry.title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills

author.name: Qijia Zhuang, Yanyi Gou, Wenbin Ma, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: Skill Adapter enables LLM agents to personalize general-purpose skills and route among them online during long-horizon tasks. It distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback into Adapters linked to shared skills, and selects currently applicable skills from an expanding pool while preparing candidates for subsequent steps.

entry.title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation

author.name: Saleh Ashkboos, Dhruv Desai, Lavinia Ghita

entry.summary: An extensive ablation study fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with LoRA on financial data, comparing response-only training, single-adapter training with teacher reasoning traces, and dual-adapter composite training. The work addresses the key tension of improving task performance without degrading general capabilities.

entry.title: MechFoundry: An agentic loop that poses and performs engineering analyses and optimization of real-world objects

author.name: Xue-Ling Luo, Marco Conte, Peter Yichen Chen, Nikolaos Bouklas

entry.summary: MechFoundry is an agentic loop with bespoke software that automates structural analysis of real-world objects from a lexical description — generating geometry, posing loading cases, assigning materials, and judging results — addressing the lack of easily verifiable checks in engineering analysis that makes automation hard compared to software engineering.

entry.title: Graph Label Alignment: A Diagnostic Atlas for Graph Classification

author.name: Neelam Akula, Varun Shiralkar, Murat Kantarcioglu, Baris Coskunuzer

entry.summary: Introduces graph label alignment, a lightweight diagnostic measuring how accessible class labels are from restricted marginal views of graph benchmarks without training a graph encoder, via structural and feature label alignment probes. The data-centric analysis helps explain why some graph classification benchmarks are trivially solved while others remain hard.

entry.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning

author.name: Jaeseong Lee, Jinwoo Kim, Jinho Jeong, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: Argues that text-aware image super-resolution requires reasoning, since severely degraded text often cannot be recovered from local visual evidence alone. The paper contributes ReasonText, a benchmark separating reasoning-required from locally recoverable text, and GTTCA, a recognition-based metric for text restoration quality, reframing TAISR as a reasoning task.

entry.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models

author.name: Lichen Li, Ziping Dong, Sicheng Feng, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: SO-Arena is a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of fast, non-chain-of-thought System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. It emphasizes evidence-grounded evaluation with manually verified reference labels and fine-grained capability assessment rather than aggregate scores.

entry.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety

author.name: Junru Zhu

entry.summary: SwarmSafe-Delta is a paired executable protocol that isolates whether an upstream message caused a tool-using LLM agent team to violate policy, by freezing upstream computation and varying real, hidden, and placebo delivery under preassigned budgets. Across four models, real delivery at N=4 produces 21.4% risky-world violations versus 5.0% with placebo, while also improving benign task success, showing a utility-safety tradeoff.

entry.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression

author.name: Sikui Zhang, Haowei Liu, Ziyun Gan, Chunfeng Yuan, Guangze Gao, Nian Liu, Boyu Cai, Bo Li, Xiaolei Lv, Jun Gao, Bing Li, Weiming Hu

entry.summary: Proposes CoMem, a query-guided selective context compression framework that learns memory representations conditioned on both document and query, using Contrastive Compressor Learning to retain task-relevant evidence that varies from localized spans to information dispersed across documents. This improves soft context compression for long-input LLM inference under tight memory budgets.

entry.title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences

author.name: Gaurav Parmar, Zhengqi Li, Richard Zhang, Jun-Yan Zhu, Srinivasa Narasimhan, Eli Shechtman, Yotam Nitzan

entry.summary: vid2vid-long is a correspondence-based video-to-video translation method that maintains long-range temporal consistency in real-time interactive generation. It computes patch-level correspondences in the input video to retrieve previously generated outputs in matching regions, conditioning the model on them rather than relying solely on a fixed causal context window.

entry.title: Probabilistic State Space Enumeration in Neural Network Computation

author.name: Victor O. K. Li, Yang Han, Jacqueline C. K. Lam

entry.summary: Recasts Transformer MLP computation exactly as an expectation over a combinatorial binary-inclusion state space over channel groups, with input-dependent distributions and importance-corrected masked outputs, approximating the expectation by evaluating only the most probable configurations. This offers a structured route to efficient sparse-ish inference with exact dense equivalence.

entry.title: A hybrid machine learning-analog framework for downscaling unprecedented climate extremes

author.name: Nina Effenberger, Florian E. Roemer, Maybritt Schillinger, Maxim Samarin, Erich Fischer, Reto Knutti

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid framework combining ML generative downscaling with analog-based methods to downscale coarse-resolution ensemble-boosted climate simulations of unprecedented heat extremes, validated for Paris heatwaves. It bridges high-resolution realism with large ensemble sampling of rare tails, addressing a key computational bottleneck in climate risk assessment.

entry.title: Fewer Expert Transfers Without Changing Routing: Expert Eviction for MoE Offloading

author.name: Pierre-Luc Bacon, Diego Calanzone, Jean-Maxime Larouche

entry.summary: The paper measures CPU-to-GPU expert copying for MoE offloading directly and finds that fixed-expert-set policies trained to reduce routing switches still raise next-token loss, while a simple change to the eviction policy - evicting the expert whose next use is latest - reduces transfers without altering any routing decision. This offers a loss-free improvement over LRU caching for MoE serving.

entry.title: Hiding a Gap Does Not Close It: The Price of Removing the Mean Group Contrast from Learned Models of Learning Dynamics

author.name: Sosth\`ene Bidojesussi Hounzinhin, Ahmed Ratnani, Abdeladim El Akri

entry.summary: The authors quantify the accuracy cost of removing group signals from predictive models used in adaptive tutoring, deriving a closed-form minimum extra error for removing the mean group contrast and an audit procedure to estimate this cost before deploying a fairness correction. A controlled study shows the fairness remedy can carry a large accuracy price even when the state appears predictive.

entry.title: What Does an RF Fingerprint Identify? A Cross-Corpus Evaluation of Hardware-Family-Associated and Unit-Level Signal

author.name: Hyojung Han

entry.summary: The paper asks whether RF fingerprinting classifiers actually identify individual devices or merely hardware families, comparing real hardware groupings with size-matched random groupings using calibrated variational lower bounds under device-level cross-fitting. On WiSig, generation grouping exceeded all 999 random groupings (permutation p=0.001) though no grouping attained a positive certified bound, with a preregistered LoRa replication.

entry.title: Computational Explanations of Semantic Universals

author.name: Shane Steinert-Threlkeld, Jakub Szymanik

entry.summary: A Cambridge Element presenting a framework for computational explanations of semantic universals across languages, using principles like ease of learning and efficient communication to explain cross-linguistic patterns in quantifiers, color terms, modals, and indefinites.

entry.title: RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Yue Zhou, Jiawei Liu, Jue Chen, Ziyang Gong, Haojia Wei, Jingxiang Li, Xue Jiang, Zhihang Zhong, Pai Peng, Xue Yang, Yansheng Li, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: RSLiveBench-UAV is a continually evolving vision-language benchmark for aerial spatial intelligence built on recurring real UAV image acquisition, with a protocol that admits post-release imagery and delays answer disclosure to limit contamination. An entity-centered workflow uses geometry-assisted association to link repeated observations of physical vehicles and reuse human verification. It addresses benchmark staleness for aerial scene understanding.

entry.title: Beyond the Explicit: Benchmarking and Detecting Implicit Harm in Short Videos

author.name: Chenyang Li, Qifan Yu, Saihui Hou, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: The paper introduces DeepHarm-7K, a 7,110-video dataset with a fine-grained taxonomy for implicitly harmful short-video content, such as videos that subtly promote misleading values via narrative framing or cross-modal cues. It also proposes detection methods for this harder implicit-harm setting, complementing prior work focused on explicit violence or hate speech. The benchmark fills a real gap in content moderation research.

entry.title: Image Deblending with Diffusion Models

author.name: Dan Botchan, Ohad Fried, Yacov Hel-Or

entry.summary: The paper formulates image deblending, decomposing a composite into two plausible source images, as a joint inverse problem solved with diffusion posterior sampling, showing a single diffusion prior can disentangle two full images simultaneously. A training-free approach inspired by human perceptual disambiguation is proposed. This extends diffusion inverse-problem solvers from single-output to joint multi-output reconstruction.

entry.title: Gravity and Flight: Learning to Navigate Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Scenes

author.name: Yuheng Zong, Minghua Wang, Xin Zhao, Xiaobin Liu, Yongjian Dong, Chanho Eom

entry.summary: G&F is a framework for scene-specialized VLM reasoning in remote sensing with limited supervision, combining Evidence-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning for faithful observation and reasoning with Relational Transfer Policy Optimization, which independently samples responses on scene-matched image pairs with fine-grained visual differences under rubric-based rewards.

entry.title: Spatial Foundry: A Multimodal Dataset for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Ethan Lin, Yang Song

entry.summary: Introduces Spatial Foundry, a dataset of 5,280 furnished residential 3D scene configurations with aligned floor plans, RGB (perspective and panoramic), metric depth, point clouds, meshes, 3D bounding boxes, and camera trajectories paired with video. Shared scene coordinates link observations across views and time, and editable source scenes enable controlled variation.

entry.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight

author.name: Donglin Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yantong Zhong, Wenhao Zheng, Zihan Ding, Yue Liao, Hongsheng Li, Ke Xu, Si Liu

entry.summary: Formulates Flying-on-a-Word, a task requiring UAVs to convert concise language instructions, egocentric observation, and state dynamics into continuous flight actions, and introduces UAV-Flow with 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories plus simulated data for policy learning and closed-loop evaluation. It fills a gap in short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers versus long-horizon planning.

entry.title: ILA: A Transferable Interface-Level Adapter for Compliant Humanoid Motion Tracking

author.name: ZhuoChang Cai, Zihao Yan, Jinxuan Zhu, Yanjie Li, Hao Xiong

entry.summary: ILA is an adapter module that makes pretrained humanoid motion trackers compliant, letting robots respond to physical guidance and interact safely in constrained environments without dedicated interaction sensors, by inferring corrections from the robot's observation history. It plugs directly into different pretrained trackers, preserving their capabilities. Compliant, sensor-free interaction is important for safe teleoperation and physical human-robot contact.

entry.title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments

author.name: Yuxuan Feng, Fujing Xie, S\"oren Schwertfeger, Hermann Blum

entry.summary: PreNav targets object navigation in semi-static indoor environments by keeping persistent maps of walls and large furniture for path planning while using a target-furniture co-occurrence prior, generated with a diffusion model, to decide where to search, avoiding repeated expensive vision-language model calls. This bridges prior-map systems (which expire as objects move) and online methods (which are compute-heavy). The design is well-matched to realistic household and office semantics.

entry.title: STVLA: Spatial-aware and Temporal-memory forVision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhuo Han, Yeqiang Wang, Xinran Wang, Hongwei Han, Yi Xiong, Zunian Wan, Jianbo Mao, Huan Peng, Yongcheng Liu, Wei Shan, Maoqing Yao

entry.summary: STVLA augments vision-language-action policies by integrating features from a pretrained visual geometry foundation model into a temporal memory alongside visual representations, letting the policy recall past scene structure during action decisions. An informed history-selection mechanism filters which memories to use, addressing occlusion and viewpoint sensitivity of appearance-based memory. It targets manipulation tasks needing both spatial understanding and task history.

entry.title: AI Security Issues Are Social Engineering Issues

author.name: hiblick

entry.summary: An EFF-veteran author argues that AI-era security problems are fundamentally social engineering problems and that capability-based security is part of the fix, framing the current wave of AI-discovered vulnerabilities (day 42 of Black October / Vulnpocalypse) as validation of Peter Eckersley's predictions about near-superintelligent AI exploiting ecosystem-wide flaws.

entry.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI

author.name: Xiulin Yang, Sirisha Gudavalli, Jennifer Hu

entry.summary: Using the cooperative card game The Mind, where time itself is the only communication channel, this study compares 150 humans against computer-use agents and other AI operationalizations of time for fine-grained social coordination. It asks whether AI systems can exploit implicit temporal cues like pause duration to coordinate without explicit communication.

entry.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving

author.name: Binghang Lu, Lang Cao, Changhong Mou, Yige Sun, Cindy Xiangrui Kong, Zheyuan Deng, Tian Yuan, Bing Hu, Runyu Zhang, Na Lu, Guang Lin

entry.summary: RSI-PDEbench is a benchmark of 1,001 cases across 42 equation templates for evaluating LLM agents on identifying and solving PDEs from sampled data, covering equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and solver configuration. It includes noise-free, noisy, and hard out-of-distribution evaluation settings to test robustness and self-improvement.

entry.title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs

author.name: Tek Raj Awasthi (Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg), Babita Awasthi

entry.summary: metalSPARSE provides the first 2:4 semi-structured sparse GEMV kernels and a fused decoder for Apple Silicon GPUs written in Metal, streaming weights in compressed form and expanding in registers since Apple GPUs lack sparse-matrix hardware. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 2:4 sparsity in decoder layers, decoding achieves 3.6x speedup over HuggingFace PyTorch-MPS on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 1.52x over a denser baseline.

entry.title: From Nodes to Pixels: Topological and Structural Two-View Graph Imaging

author.name: Md Joshem Uddin, Soham Changani, Sai Karthik Navuluru, Cuneyt Gurcan Akcora, Baris Coskunuzer

entry.summary: Introduces G2Image, a framework converting graphs into two fixed-budget image-like views: TopoGrid, a topological multipersistence surface grid, and GraphGrid, a higher-bandwidth structural view aggregating edge densities over intrinsically scored node groups. Both views are permutation-invariant, giving graph learning a reusable input interface analogous to patches in vision or tokens in language.

entry.title: CoLaX: Context-Aware Local Explanations for Time Series Classification

author.name: Kexuan Zhang, Paolo Frazzetto, Xiaobei Zou, Gustau Camps-Valls, Yang Tang

entry.summary: Proposes CoLaX, a context-aware post-hoc explanation framework for time series classifiers that conditions shapelet-driven Shapley attributions on a learned representation of the full sequence. Global context produces sample-specific prototype weights and a temporally resolved reweighting of local activation maps, so the same motif can receive different attributions under different regimes.

entry.title: AutoOntic: Automatic Ontology Induction from Text for Knowledge Graph Construction

author.name: Alla Chepurova, Aydar Bulatov, Mikhail Burtsev, Yuri Kuratov

entry.summary: Presents AutoOntic, a pipeline that automatically constructs ontologies from text for graph-based RAG by canonicalizing open-vocabulary entity types and relations, inducing a type hierarchy via corpus-derived relation-argument profiles with LLM-adjudicated parent/child checks, and mining domain/range constraints. This addresses the flat, schema-free graphs produced by typical LLM extraction pipelines.

entry.title: Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Federated Bayesian Optimization through Neural Network Surrogates

author.name: Alexander Gr\"afe, Max van Gemmeren, Paul Brunzema, Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: GLOBAFED is a federated Bayesian optimization framework that transfers knowledge across different but related objectives without exposing raw data, using a probabilistic neural network surrogate with a shared feature extractor. It relaxes restrictive assumptions like near-identical objectives or shared GP hyperparameters that limit existing FedBO methods in heterogeneous real-world settings.

entry.title: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match

author.name: Jung Ho Choi, Mario Milone

entry.summary: The paper develops a two-tower neural network measure of worker-firm match quality, embedding workers and firms into a common space where match quality is cosine similarity, with the functional form grounded in skill-weights theory and estimated via a separation hazard. It is trained on over a billion person-periods covering 101 million workers.

entry.title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram

author.name: Raymundo Arr\'oyave

entry.summary: Presents a framework for making CALPHAD thermodynamic assessments for materials design fully reproducible, encoding the expert judgments that normally go unrecorded when building phase-diagram databases. Aimed at self-driving laboratories, it turns collected data, machine-learned interatomic potentials, and experimental refinement into a regenerable, updatable assessment pipeline.

entry.title: Mask-Pattern Position Augmentation: Training-Free Long-Context Extrapolation for Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Gaurav Sarkar (International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad), Syed Affan Daimi (International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad)

entry.summary: Proposes MPPA, a training-free RoPE position extrapolation method for diffusion LLMs that adds per-position, per-step offsets derived from the evolving mask pattern of partially decoded sequences, unlike static NTK scaling transplanted from autoregressive models. This restores rotary phase resolution for long-context generation in dLLMs.

entry.title: PRELUDE: Separating Common Components from Target-Specific Dependencies for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Dongqing Song, Jianyu Xu, Haobin Ding, Xinyi Guo, Jiahao Du, Ruiqi He, Ruiqi Liu, Yuntong Xie, Chao He

entry.summary: Shows via intervention experiments that cross-variable modules in multivariate forecasting models read nearly identical content for all targets, so apparent cross-variable gains come largely from a common shared component, a phenomenon it terms spurious dependency. PRELUDE then separates common components from target-specific dependencies to improve forecasting.

entry.title: FADO: Learning Causal Explanations with Prior-Fitted Networks

author.name: Seth Flaxman, Jess Carr, Annabel Jakob, Marek Masiak, Dino Sejdinovic

entry.summary: Proposes FADO, an amortized inference method using prior-fitted networks trained across synthetic causal tasks to estimate feature intervention effects (difference of do-intervention expectations) directly from observational tabular data, moving beyond SHAP-style predictive attribution toward causal explanations.

entry.title: Orbit: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on IT Operations Reasoning

author.name: Sathwik Narkedimilli, Rakshit Verma, Rahul Soni, Ankit Kushwaha, Balaji Ganesan, Kaustabha Ray, Sunil Saumya, Pratibha Moogi

entry.summary: ORBIT is a benchmark of IT operations questions in multiple-choice, open-ended, and troubleshooting formats, each with reference answers and recorded sources, built with an audit process that removed template-defective items. Evaluation of five LLMs shows strong multiple-choice performance but poor troubleshooting ability, and models judged their own answers overly favorably.

entry.title: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Contextual Anomaly Detection and Explanation in Tabular Data

author.name: Zhong Li, Qi Huang, Yuhang Wang, Yang Cao, Thomas B\"ack, Niki van Stein, Matthijs van Leeuwen, Lincen Yang

entry.summary: Flow-CAD applies flow matching to contextual anomaly detection in tabular data, learning a single global, amortized conditional generative model of behavior given context rather than shallow conditional models or per-context localized estimators. The generative framing also supports explanations of detected anomalies.

entry.title: Overcoming Spurious Correlations in Conditional Diffusion Models via Doubly Robust Target Correction

author.name: Eiichi Sakurai, Kenji Yamanishi

entry.summary: DR-Diff is a fine-tuning framework that corrects spurious correlations memorized by pre-trained conditional diffusion models using a doubly robust, covariate-shift-adjusted target risk. It derives a functional-gradient pseudo-target capturing the residual between the base model's noise predictions and ground-truth noise under the target distribution, avoiding costly retraining.

entry.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs

author.name: Peter Sharpe

entry.summary: ISLA is an invariant slice-attention transformer for neural PDE surrogates that enforces coordinate invariance, noting that state-of-the-art aerodynamics surrogates lack such invariances: rotating a car PDE raises surface-pressure error from 4% to over 100% and re-meshing raises it to about 30%. The model is coordinate-free and measure-weighted for boundary-driven PDEs.

entry.title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate

author.name: Tosca Lechner, Vinayak Pathak, Sivan Sabato, Ruth Urner

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes AI safety via debate as a training protocol rather than just a game, studying what functions can be learned when a weak human judge evaluates debates between two competing models. It extends prior complexity-theoretic results toward learnability questions for alignment.

entry.title: The norm, not the labels: training and evaluating finite-element surrogates for stress analysis in the energy norm

author.name: Ruifeng Cao, Xidan Song

entry.summary: The authors argue that neural surrogates for finite-element stress analysis should be trained and evaluated in the energy norm rather than displacement loss, showing that for linear elastostatics minimizing the discrete potential energy is exactly supervised regression in this norm. They demonstrate the approach on perforated plates and solids with cavities where stress concentration matters for engineering decisions.

entry.title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion

author.name: Shengbo Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops an asymptotically exact characterization of the transient error in synchronous Q-learning on finite discounted MDPs, separating last-iterate error into components that the leading Gaussian limit misses because CLT normalization removes initial nonlinear displacement. This bridges the gap between worst-case finite-sample bounds and instance-specific error mechanisms.

entry.title: REWEAVE: Online Learning for Workload-Adaptive HNSW Indexes

author.name: Minghao Li, Nick Koudas, Raghav Mittal

entry.summary: REWEAVE is an online index-maintenance method for HNSW vector databases that learns edge utility from query feedback and periodically rewires the bottom-layer graph within degree caps, supporting sparse exact-neighbor feedback and zero-overhead serving when adaptation is disabled. It proves value-estimation and graph-stabilization guarantees and improves held-out recall by up to 23.3 percentage points under stationary query skew.

entry.title: Distribution-First Framework for Learning Risk-Sensitive Individualized Treatment Rules

author.name: Zhen Fang, Guanting Chen, Yufeng Liu

entry.summary: The authors propose a distribution-first framework for risk-sensitive individualized treatment rules that first estimates treatment-specific conditional outcome distributions and then evaluates any criterion (quantiles, CVaR, cumulative prospect theory) by plug-in. This unifies previously criterion-specific pipelines and enables comparison across multiple risk criteria within one framework.

entry.title: Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time

author.name: Felix Zhou

entry.summary: This paper gives a polynomial-time algorithm for estimating linear regressors under self-selection bias with correlated noise, improving on prior work with exponential dependence on the number of regressors. As a corollary it yields the first polynomial-time algorithm for a related max-affine regression variant.

entry.title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation

author.name: Minh-Anh Nguyen
