entry.summary: Investigates how much depth is needed for LLM-based decision making, finding decision information concentrated in intermediate layers and the final layers removable without loss. Proposes a method (named via a placeholder in the text) that jointly trains a full model with adaptive depth computation to share computation across different layers.

entry.title: Fast Slice-Wise Deep Learning Motion Correction for Spinal Cord Functional MRI

author.name: Thomas Dagonneau, Sandrine B\'edard, Nontharat Tucksinapinunchai, Uten Yarach, Lo\"ic Le Folgoc, Pietro Gori, Julien Cohen-Adad

entry.summary: Proposes lightweight convolutional networks that regress in-plane translation per axial slice to correct motion in spinal cord fMRI, trained without motion labels in two stages for large and residual motion. On 3T and 7T datasets it outperforms the Spinal Cord Toolbox on every metric (tSNR +10-25%, DVARS -20-38%) while running orders of magnitude faster.

entry.title: In-orbit demonstration of object-based change detection applied to the maritime domain

author.name: Cristopher Castro Traba, Tom Hendrix, Amaury Perrocheau, Francesco Pasanisi, Finian Rogers, Aubrey Dunne, David Rijlaarsdam, Roberto Del Prete, Nicolas Long\'ep\'e, Gabriele Meoni

entry.summary: The paper reports a successful in-orbit validation of an onboard AI change-detection pipeline for low-latency maritime monitoring on the CogniSAT-6 satellite. It uses a three-phase sequence of dual-acquisition scheduling, real-time onboard vessel segmentation, and multi-temporal matching combining the Hungarian algorithm with RANSAC filters, validated across 11 diverse maritime scenarios. This demonstrates practical edge-AI deployment in space for Earth observation.

entry.title: Fear of Memorizing Objects: End-to-End Zero-Shot Model-Based Object Detection

author.name: Leon Greiner, Wout Boerdijk, Junwen Huang, Benjamin Busam, Rudolph Triebel, Maximilian Durner

entry.summary: FOMO is an end-to-end trainable transformer for zero-shot model-based object detection that injects multi-view CAD template information early via bidirectional attention among latent tokens, templates, and query features. This replaces loosely coupled proposal-and-match pipelines that suffer fragmented proposals in clutter and degraded matching under occlusion. The architecture design improves robustness for detecting novel objects given their 3D models.

entry.title: GOOSELoc: A Multimodal Benchmark for Ground-to-Aerial Localization in Unstructured Off-Road Terrain

author.name: Fabian Deuser, Peter Mortimer, Robin-Nico Kampa, Anna B\"o{\ss}end\"orfer, Mirko M\"ahlisch, Martin Werner, Norbert Oswald

entry.summary: GOOSELoc is a multimodal benchmark for ground-to-aerial cross-view localization in unstructured off-road environments (forests, fields, rural tracks), comprising 9,356 four-season scenes around Munich pairing aerial orthophotos with surround-view RGB and 3D LiDAR. It fills a gap left by urban-dominated benchmarks like VIGOR and cross-view KITTI, relevant when GNSS is unreliable.

entry.title: TokenStream: Multi-Subject Personalized Video Generation with Token-wise LoRA and Guided Attention

author.name: Hung Nguyen, Quang Qui-Vinh Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen

entry.summary: TokenStream composes independently learned subject identities in text-to-video generation without reference-video training or joint optimization per combination. Token-wise LoRA restricts low-rank updates to cross-attention value projections of subject-associated tokens, while a T2V-guided stream copies queries and keys from the frozen base model early in denoising to preserve layout and motion priors.

entry.title: SpotDiff: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Zero-Shot Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Anit Upadhyaya, Ata Akbari Asanjan, Chaitanya Jalluri, Subash Yeggina, Jeremy Kravitz

entry.summary: SpotDiff is a training-free framework for zero-shot change detection in remote sensing that composes vision foundation models: DINOv3 for semantic features, AnyUp for pixel-resolution reconstruction, and SAM 3 for text-guided region proposals. It addresses poor fine-grained localization of prior zero-shot methods without requiring aligned pixel-level annotations.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators

author.name: Jiayun Wang, Ram Daftari, Weijie Gan, Valentin Duruisseaux, Ruibo Wang, Armeet Singh Jatyani, Boris Bonev, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: Introduces KIR-NO, a resolution-agnostic neural operator for full 3D MRI reconstruction that can be trained at low memory-feasible resolution yet deployed at higher resolution, avoiding slice-by-slice 2D reconstruction that ignores through-plane structure. The coarse-to-fine strategy addresses GPU memory limits of full-volume training.

entry.title: Terrain-Aware Thompson Sampling for Multi-Drone Search and Rescue

author.name: Riana Gagnon Souleiman, Giovanni Beltrame

entry.summary: The authors propose a decentralized multi-drone search and rescue algorithm that uses Thompson Sampling over a per-cell Gaussian posterior informed by established lost-person behavior models (displacement ring, elevation, watershed, dispersion angle, track offset) derived from historical SAR data. Drones balance exploration of uncertain terrain-informed regions with exploitation of high-probability areas. This grounds multi-robot Bayesian search in real SAR practice, potentially improving outcomes for missing-person missions.

entry.title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models

author.name: Chenhao Qiu, Shuyi Chen, Songen Gu, Shufeng Nan, Tianyu Wang, Siyu Lin, Yifan Li, Bingwen Zhu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Bind-WAM tackles when a World Action Model should actually generate an imagined visual future, since doing so at every replanning step is costly and often unnecessary. It uses language-object binding uncertainty to trigger joint future-state and action generation only when the current observation cannot support stable task-relevant actions, with an offline pipeline labeling reference mismatch, invisibility, and identity issues. This is a meaningful efficiency contribution to the rapidly growing world-model-for-robotics literature.

entry.title: VOKE: Visual Object Kinematics Estimator for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

author.name: Shengjia Zhu, Wenqiang Xu, Lin Shao

entry.summary: VOKE is a kinematics-aware perception framework that augments existing pose estimators to recover full object kinematic state — pose, linear and angular velocity, and acceleration — for dexterous in-hand manipulation. A pluggable kinematics module attaches to off-the-shelf estimators, and a downstream application study demonstrates the value of explicit dynamics estimates. It moves beyond static perception outputs that force controllers to infer motion implicitly.

entry.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets

author.name: Gerhard Trippen (University of Toronto)

entry.summary: This paper reframes handwritten chess scoresheet digitization from pure handwriting recognition to full game reconstruction. Zugwise borrows computer-chess machinery such as quiescence search and static exchange evaluation to build an absurdity detector that catches legal-but-wrong move misreads that silently corrupt all downstream positions.

entry.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts

author.name: Songshi Liang, Ting-En Lin, Zixuan Huang, Yuchuan Wu, Yongbin Li, Zihe Wang, Rui Yan

entry.summary: MuEdit diagnoses why sequential multi-task knowledge editing collapses in LLMs, tracing it to inter-domain null-space misalignment where heterogeneous tasks shrink the common null space. It introduces a Conflict Index and mitigates interference via conflict-aware task ordering and dynamic low-rank approximation to expand admissible update directions.

entry.title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model

author.name: Shunming Liu, Pei Huang, Yajing Sun, Huaxiao Liu

entry.summary: This paper applies discrete diffusion generation to vision-language models for autonomous driving, proposing a multi-stage optimization pipeline spanning post-training and inference that works with standard VLM architectures without auxiliary action experts or MoE components. It addresses domain gaps when transferring diffusion-based generation from general settings to driving, optimizing planning representation during supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: Turning Multi-Agent Communication into Token-Level Credit with On Policy Self Distillation

author.name: Zixu Wang, Yu Zhao, Xing Zheng, Bingbing Xu, Tian Xueyun, JiaTang Luo, Weiqiang Wang, Bowen Song, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: OPSD4MAS converts future communication in LLM multi-agent systems into fine-grained token-level credit via On-Policy Self Distillation, replacing coarse scalar rewards. An external model extracts facts and filters trajectories coarsely, then leave-one-out filtering assesses target-token influence against agent-wise outcome advantages, combined with GRPO through an annealed joint objective. This addresses the credit assignment problem that plagues multi-agent RL for LLMs.

entry.title: SignRot: LLM Quantization with Massive Outlier-Aware Sign-Adjusted Rotation

author.name: Jaehun Gim, Jaewoo Kim, Gyuwan Kim, Seo Yeon Park

entry.summary: This paper introduces SignRot, a quantization method for large language models that addresses performance degradation caused by massive outlier activations. It identifies how randomized Hadamard rotation approaches can create fragmented activation distributions with empty bins when a massive outlier dominates, and how the placement of outliers in the down-projection input limits training-based rotation methods. SignRot uses sign-adjusted rotation to handle these massive outliers and improve low-bit quantization quality.

entry.title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation

author.name: Ethan Mollick, Lilach Mollick, Ben Przystanski, LJ Ciccarelli, Natalie Bach, Laura Zarrow

entry.summary: Primer is an open-source, LLM-agnostic multi-agent system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations by encoding instructor knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students while generative AI produces responsive practice variations. The system centers the educator's instructional intent rather than replacing it, addressing the high cost of building quality simulations.

entry.title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution

author.name: Peng Yin, Zhiwei Chen, Tianyi Liu, Chen Li, Kai Li, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: The paper identifies an executability-acceptability gap in LLM agents for OpenFOAM CFD workflows — successfully executed simulations often fail numerical or QoI criteria — and introduces ExtFoamBench as a more demanding benchmark beyond tutorial-level cases. EasyFoam decouples domain expertise from bespoke agent architectures via skill libraries with evidence-driven evolution for reuse across agent implementations.

entry.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer

author.name: Mingjie Cao, Gewei Zhang, Deqing Wang, Lizhao You, Fei-Yun Wu, Liqun Fu

entry.summary: Introduces LLM4UACP, a framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step prediction of underwater acoustic channel states, addressing error accumulation from recursive rollout and the scarcity of sea-trial data. It preserves multipath structure across time- and transform domains to deliver more accurate long-horizon forecasts for acoustic communications.

entry.title: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age

author.name: Caroline Chin, Shagun Kala, Nadav Kunievsky, Teng Liu, Alex Martin Richmond, Carl Shan

entry.summary: An empirical economics study of how generative AI reshapes freelance labor, comparing ChatGPT usage patterns with client demands on the Upwork marketplace. The key finding is substitution at the task level: activities common in ChatGPT lose Upwork market share, while less-AI-exposed activities gain it, and AI-related jobs are being rebundled into larger-budget, longer, more diverse multi-task projects. It matters because it provides early, data-driven evidence of how AI changes labor market structure rather than just eliminating tasks.

entry.title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals

author.name: Jaerock Kwon, Elahe Delavari, Donghyun Kim, Haewoon Nam

entry.summary: Identifies a posterior-prior gap in an RSSM world model with active-inference planning in CARLA: an obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states but decays to 0.71 over 15 imagined steps, showing the transition model progressively loses task-relevant information during rollouts. The identical probe isolates the transition model as the cause of the decay.

entry.title: Reframing Video Inverse Tone Mapping as Blind Posterior Inference via Latent Luminance Supervision

author.name: Hanwool Sul, Chang-Hoon Jeong, Kisung Shin, Bomseok Park, Donghoon Cha, Hansl von Kwon, DoHyung Ku, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: Recasts SDR-to-HDR video inverse tone mapping as a blind posterior inference problem with latent luminance supervision, addressing the systematic brightness bias in clipped regions found in all public generative-prior methods tested. The motivation is especially strong for generated video, which has no HDR master and must be finished alongside HDR live-action material.

entry.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation

author.name: Quang Qui-Vinh Nguyen, Hung Nguyen, Rang Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen

entry.summary: Shows that strong reported results in personalized image segmentation are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when scenes contain multiple visually similar same-category objects, prior point-prompt methods collapse. The authors propose a training-free framework that surfaces and disambiguates the correct instance, targeting realistic applications like AR, robotics, and content editing.

entry.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition

author.name: Yue Liu, Zhongying Ru, Shimin Di, Jipeng Zhang, Ruiyuan Zhang, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: This paper introduces QDRAG, an attributable retrieval-augmented generation framework that decomposes input questions into atomic subquestions to identify implicit entities before answering. It uses a reranker to prune distractor contexts, aiming to fix over-citation, entity identification failures, and poor generalization in multi-hop and multimodal settings.

entry.title: RUMI: A Robotiq-Matched Universal Manipulation Interface for Robot Learning with Augmented Reality and Haptic Feedback

author.name: Kevin Avdiu, Seongjin Bien, Yannik Blei, Philine Meister, Johannes Hechtl, Philipp Schmitt, Kai Wurm, Georg von Wichert, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: RUMI is a handheld data-collection interface matched to the Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, with exchangeable fingertip sensors that preserve the gripper geometry while letting operators feel interaction forces and provide natural input before contact. It integrates tracking into a VR headset for real-time augmented reality, addressing the scarcity of force-aware manipulation datasets for robot learning.

entry.title: Guided Generation of Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Language Models

author.name: Mohanned Ahmed

entry.summary: Investigates whether small open language models on a laptop can generate Coccinelle semantic patches for Linux kernel API changes by learning from reviewed conversion examples. The pipeline decomposes examples into change-variant trees, generates rules with execution feedback, and uses a compile critic to repair or reject non-building rules.

entry.title: ReliaGuard: Reconstruction-Aware Watermarking for Source Attribution and Blind Edit Localization

author.name: Hailong Wang, Wuzheng Tan, Zixin Zhang, Xujun Fang, Fengjuan Gong

entry.summary: Proposes ReliaGuard, a watermarking framework for generative image editing that optimizes keyed feature responses in both the protected image and its VAE reconstruction, enabling source attribution and blind edit localization. A reader with only the received image and secret key combines watermark responses with local context via residual evidence refinement.

entry.title: DesignTaste: Benchmarking AI-Generator Visual Design Against Award-Wining Works

author.name: Zhou Chen, JiaXiang Li, DanYing Pan, Ye Li, TianRui Yang, EnBao Zhang, YaNan Xiao, LiXin Sun, Anqi Liu, Dong Zhao, JianYuan Li, YuanYuan Ding, Kai Kong, Xinwen Xu, HuiTang Du, Min Zhou, Zhiqiang Li

entry.summary: DesignTaste is a benchmark that evaluates text-to-image models on open-ended visual design quality rather than mere text-image alignment, comparing generated outputs against award-winning design works across 403 briefs derived from Beste Plakate 2025 and ADC 2026 competitions. Six leading commercial text-to-image models are tested with a single model judge scoring on five dimensions, and only ArtArk beats the human award-winning mean on each dataset. This provides a new yardstick for aesthetic design capability, a dimension most existing image benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach

author.name: Shengtao Wu, Zichao Dong, Weixuan Qiao, Xiaolu Liu, Xin Zhan, Junbo Chen, Jianke Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents a counterintuitive finding that off-the-shelf general VLMs already adapt well to diverse driving tasks, with metric depth being the main missing link, addressable via onboard sensors and depth foundation models. It introduces the Triplet Incremental Training Framework, a non-intrusive paradigm that instills 3D geometric awareness into a general VLM backbone while preserving its open-world capabilities, driven by automatically curated data.

entry.title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data

author.name: Bagzhan Karl, Alizhan Karl

entry.summary: Kezek converts a mono recording of two people into per-speaker tracks with original length and timing, keeping overlaps and short backchannels on the correct speaker's track. It uses a two-stage design: a two-voice activity model guided by a phase-insensitive speaker fingerprint decides who speaks when, then a conditioned time-domain separator realizes the decision, with outputs summing to the input.

entry.title: ElasticDino: Dense Semantic Features Using Elastic Deformations

author.name: Ulysse Mizrahi, Sean Zaretzky, Dov Danon, Amit H. Bermano

entry.summary: ElasticDino is a lightweight adapter for vision transformers that produces high-resolution, pixel-aligned feature maps for dense prediction tasks like segmentation and depth estimation. It exploits the consistency of self-attention spatial artifacts across channels and resolves them via spatial deformations, avoiding quadratic attention costs at full resolution.

entry.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution

author.name: Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, Felix Zhou

entry.summary: The paper studies leave-one-out context attribution: how removing each token changes a language model's output, which naively requires n model evaluations. Under a stability assumption, the authors give an algorithm estimating all LOO values with O(sqrt(log(1/eps))/eps) evaluations, prove a matching lower bound in an oracle model, and empirically verify the stability assumption.

entry.title: SPIRE: Task-agnostic embodied continual learning through autonomous situation inference and causal motor-primitive reuse

author.name: Yiyang Jia, Mingyang Lyu, Gongce Cao, Feifei Zhao, Yinqian Sun, Yi Zeng

entry.summary: SPIRE is a recurrent-spiking control system that autonomously infers latent contexts from action-outcome evidence and learns context-specific motor actors online without task labels. Mature actors are protected and reused with residual adaptation, demonstrating retention and skill reuse across coordinate, joint, and hidden-force control tasks.

entry.title: When Does Causality Help in Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection?

author.name: Long Zhang, Wei Huang, Aishui Rao, Jian Hu, Binxiang Wu, Jie Li, Chen Gong, Linxi Feng

entry.summary: Provides a controlled analysis of when causality-aware scoring helps in multivariate time-series anomaly detection, varying causal-graph quality, anomaly type, and evaluation protocol while holding a causality-guided autoencoder fixed. Results show gains decay with graph corruption, depend on structural break severity, and that point-adjusted F1 can mask differences that range-aware VUS reveals.

entry.title: Regret Bounds for Quantum Linear Bandits

author.name: Maoli Liu, Zhuohua Li, John C. S. Lui

entry.summary: Resolves an open question in quantum linear bandits by proving a minimax lower bound of Omega(d^1.5 log T), matching existing upper bounds, via a construction of hard instances with gap proportional to squared distance from the optimal action. This shows the d^1.5 dependence is unavoidable, closing the gap between known lower and upper bounds.

entry.title: Overcoming the Resolution Limit: Significance-Aware Regularization for Intersectional Fairness

author.name: Antonio Ferrara, Andr\'e Panisson, Francesco Cozzi, Alan Perotti, Francesco Bonchi

entry.summary: Identifies fairness overfitting in intersectional fairness: fine-grained subgroup estimates become unstable at small sample sizes, and certainty-blind in-processing methods penalize sampling noise. It introduces a significant-excess metric family that measures only disparity exceeding sampling variation at a given confidence level, and builds a regularization scheme around it.

entry.title: Continual Event Recognition for Autonomous Optical Network Monitoring

author.name: Khouloud Abdelli

entry.summary: This paper proposes a continual learning framework for recognizing disturbances in polarization-based optical network monitoring, combining prototype representations, open-set recognition, and few-shot registration of new event classes. Validation on a 2600-km ROADM optical testbed shows 99.82% closed-set accuracy and successful adaptation to novel disturbances without full retraining.

entry.title: Manifold Attracting Flow Matching: Physics-Constrained Sampling via Continuous Geometric Dynamics

author.name: Guanyu Chen, Jinchen Wang, Shengze Xu, Xingyu Ren, Tieyong Zeng, Antonios Armaou, Dong Ni

entry.summary: MAFM enforces equality constraints in scientific data generation by continuously evolving a persistent anchor through an ODE that drives samples toward the constraint manifold, rather than repeatedly correcting endpoints discretely. The geometric correction preserves model-guided tangent motion while contracting constraint violations.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Regret for Oracle-Efficient Adversarial Contextual Bandits

author.name: Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi

entry.summary: The paper gives an oracle-efficient algorithm for adversarial contextual bandits with expected regret O(sqrt(KT log(2N)) log(2KT)), improving the T^(2/3) horizon dependence of prior oracle-efficient bounds to the optimal rate up to log factors. The algorithm perturbs policy scores using Poisson-sampled auxiliary contexts with context-specific Laplace noise.

entry.title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design

author.name: Lucy Liu, Leon M. Kamp, Katia Bertoldi, L. Mahadevan

entry.summary: Using an origami design problem with four discrete hinge types optimized via bilevel autodiff, the paper explains why continuous relaxation followed by rounding selects unfavorable design basins. From a strong group (Liu, Kamp, Bertoldi, Mahadevan), it provides interpretable analysis of gradient-based discrete design failure modes.

entry.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation

author.name: Zeynep Y{\i}ld{\i}z, Satchit Chatterji, Ercan Atam, Erman Acar

entry.summary: This paper extends neurosymbolic reinforcement learning to continuous action spaces for portfolio allocation, building on the Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) framework. It estimates the probability that a policy's executed action complies with institutional investment mandates (constraints on asset allocation conditioned on market regimes) using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling. This matters because deep RL for finance typically ignores rule compliance, limiting real-world deployment under formal investment policy statements.

entry.title: Arbor: When Labels Are Not Coarsened at Random

author.name: Faisal Mohammad, Mohamed Younis

entry.summary: Arbor addresses dataset merging across taxonomy levels where coarse labels are not assigned at random, showing that standard superclass-probability objectives fail for classes that never receive fine labels. The method models the coarsening process with virtual novel classes and a logistic gate, improving classification when some classes are only coarsely labelled.

entry.title: Smart Model Routing for Order-of-Magnitude LLM Cost Reduction

author.name: Hesham Elbakoury, Deep Shah, Ankur Sharma

entry.summary: This paper formalizes cost-quality optimization for LLM routing, deriving optimal threshold-policy structure, a calibration-versus-discrimination distinction, cascade breakeven conditions, and sensitivity analysis over price ratios and traffic skew. It situates the framework against prevailing routing architectures to assign each query to the cheapest adequate model rather than the most capable one.

entry.title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation

author.name: Liman Wang, Hanyang Zhong, Sun Zhaole, Wenting Cao, Babar Jamil, Andy Tyrrell, Shan Luo, Jihong Zhu

entry.summary: DexRemo presents a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, plus a nine-scenario real-robot suite for removal manipulation (adhesive detachment, cleaning, occluded retrieval). Fingertip forces are expressed in a shared wrist-centered frame to ease multi-finger force fusion under partially observable contact states.

entry.title: GC-MoE on SM120: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with Warp-Level FP8xFP4 Block-Scaled MMA on Consumer Blackwell

author.name: Yong Li, Haoyu Wang, Kan Liu, Tao Lan

entry.summary: This systems paper rebuilds a fused Mixture-of-Experts decoding kernel (GC-MoE) for consumer Blackwell SM120 GPUs over PCIe, where block-scaled tensor cores are only accessible via warp-level mma instructions. It uses a swap-AB warp-level FP8/FP4 block-scaled MMA with FP4 weights and FP8 activations, plus SM120-specific optimizations, to overlap token dispatch, grouped GEMM, and combine phases.

entry.title: Joint Null-Space Projection for Data-Free Model Merging

author.name: Tian Xia

entry.summary: The paper recasts data-free model merging as a subspace interference problem, removing from each task vector the components that lie in the union of other tasks' top singular subspaces. The resulting Joint Null-Space Projection method avoids the entrywise heuristics of averaging, magnitude pruning, and sign election.

entry.title: FIBER: Bayesian Fusion of Fast-DetectGPT and IRT-Informed Detector Evidence for LLM-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Yan Li, Guangsheng Bao, Zhipeng Chen, Guandong Zhang, Yanbin Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes FIBER, a zero-shot LLM-text detection method that fuses continuous Fast-DetectGPT scores with auxiliary detector outputs using Bayesian evidence recalibration. Item response theory (IRT) models historical detector-correctness patterns to produce class-conditional output likelihoods, aiming to improve robustness under domain and generator shifts.

entry.title: Low Language Transfer Speech-to-Text

author.name: Husein Zolkepli

entry.summary: Evaluates cross-lingual transfer of 28 open multilingual ASR models to 50 low-resource languages in 11 writing systems, fine-tuning 24 of them with at most 1,000 clips per language. Fine-tuning lowers macro CER substantially (16.6 to 53.1 points, to 9.5 at best), and the study quantifies transfer for languages with no listed support.

entry.title: Neural Compression for Scientific Particle Data: Perspectives on How Learning Can Help

author.name: Tian Qiu, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro, Sheng Di, Haewon Jeong

entry.summary: This position/analysis paper examines whether neural point cloud compression methods, which excel on computer vision benchmarks, transfer to large-scale scientific particle simulations in cosmology, molecular dynamics, and plasma physics. The authors identify a key structural difference in fractal dimension (CV point clouds are locally planar, scientific particles are not) that undermines the octree data structures underlying most PCC methods, and show neural codecs offer only marginal bitrate reductions over the traditional G-PCC baseline. The work charts where learning-based compression could genuinely help scientific data.

entry.title: PCLSegNet: Anatomy-Aware Deep Learning Framework for MRI-based Pancreatic Cyst Segmentation and Size Assessment

author.name: Hanyi Zhang, Tongyu Wang, Manuel Debic, Markus Wennmann, Johannes Haubold, Tamara Schikowski, Wilfried Reichardt, Fabian Bamberg, Christopher L. Schlett, Steffen Ringhof, Thoralf Niendorf, Tobias Pischon, Michael Leitzmann, Carsten Oliver Schmidt, Mark Oliver Wielp\"utz, Thomas Kroencke, Josua A. Decker, Stefan N. Willich, Thomas Keil, Rafael Mikolajczyk, Miriam Klau{\ss}, Hans-Ulrich Kauczor, Philipp Mayer, Bettina K. Budai

entry.summary: The authors present a two-stage anatomy-aware framework for segmenting pancreatic cystic lesions on abdominal MRI, first localizing the pancreas with an existing model and then applying PCLSegNet, which incorporates anatomical priors. Since MRI offers better soft-tissue contrast than the CT used in most prior AI work, this supports earlier detection and follow-up of cysts with malignant potential. The work addresses a clinically important but under-served modality-task combination.

entry.title: AcrossPlace: Do Vision--Language Models Recognize Places Beyond Their Source Views? A Comprehensive Benchmark

author.name: Zhenyu Li, Tianyi Shang, Shuhan Dong, Ruotong Xu, Qingyu Zhu

entry.summary: This paper introduces AcrossPlace, a provenance-aware benchmark for bidirectional language-vision place recognition, built on GSV-Cities with 56,726 places across 23 cities, over 156,000 filtered descriptions, and 113,404 target images. Its key innovation is separating observation transfer, gallery competition, and linguistic evidence in retrieval evaluation by retaining source-image provenance and testing on disjoint target observations. This provides a cleaner measure of whether vision-language models can genuinely recognize places across views rather than exploiting dataset artifacts.

entry.title: Sub-actions in Action: Text-Guided Hand-Role Alignment for Sub-Action Recognition

author.name: Sadegh Rahmaniboldaji, Filip Rybansky, Quoc Vuong, Frank Guerin, Andrew Gilbert

entry.summary: BiScopeNet augments video-LLMs to recognize left- and right-hand roles and manipulated objects within ongoing egocentric actions, via a gated text-guided attention module (FocusAlign) and a masked object-weighted loss (MetaLoss) that do not modify the underlying vision encoders or language models. It defines sub-action detection as a new task for fine-grained egocentric action understanding.

entry.title: Selective Generative Restoration for Video Deraining via Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion

author.name: Yi'ang Chen, Han Li, Laibin Chang, Hui Liu, Kui Jiang, Junjun Jiang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a selective generative restoration paradigm for video deraining that adaptively activates diffusion-based generative priors depending on the spatial heterogeneity of rain degradation. Reliable regions receive faithful deterministic reconstruction while severely occluded regions get stronger prior-driven generation, avoiding both over-smoothed outputs and unnecessary hallucinations. The work matters because it reframes video restoration as a hybrid deterministic-generative problem rather than choosing one paradigm globally.

entry.title: Model Distribution-Aware Multimodal Dataset Distillation

author.name: Jiajun Shen, Yonglin Wu, Ruonan Yu, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: MDA-DD improves multimodal dataset distillation by supervising with a dynamic staggered queue of models at different training stages, preventing synthetic data from over-specializing to encountered model representations. It adds asymmetric dual projection for visual-linguistic alignment and an uncentered second-order moment objective preserving mean-related cross-modal information.

entry.title: HIFC-IQA: Train-Free Cross-Domain Image Quality Assessment via Dual-Process Cognition

author.name: Yu Li, Zhengran Shen, Puchao Zhou, Yukang Ding, Yachun Mi, Boyuan Yang, Xi Zhai, Shaohui Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces HIFC, a training-free framework for no-reference image quality assessment that handles the domain shift between synthetic distortions and real-world degradations. It uses asymmetric perceptual decomposition to separate semantic content from distortion-sensitive features and draws inspiration from dual-process human cognition, avoiding the retraining overhead and pseudo-label error propagation of unsupervised domain adaptation approaches.

entry.title: TuMAP: A Dual-View, Morphotype-Aware Pathomics Pipeline for Quantifying Renal Tubular Remodeling

author.name: Ruijie Wu, Yuechen Yang, Yanfan Zhu, Yu Wang, Shilin Zhao, Ming-Tsun Tsai, Szu-Yuan Li, Shuo-Ming Ou, Tz-Heng Chen, Haichun Yang, Yuankai Huo

entry.summary: Introduces TuMAP, a pathology pipeline combining dual-view foundation-model representations with morphotype annotation to quantify renal tubular remodeling in kidney biopsies. It identifies eight image-based tubular morphotypes across 456,158 tubules and shows morphotype proportions differ across six diagnostic groups, enabling patient-level statistical inference.

entry.title: Neural Render Proxies for Interactive and Differentiable Lighting

author.name: Sergio Sancho, Alexander Rath, Marco Manzi, Pascal Chang, Amit H. Bermano, Derek Nowrouzezahrai, Markus Gross, Marios Papas

entry.summary: Introduces a neural render proxy for CG production pipelines that decouples path sampling from emission computation, collecting light transport data from a single light-agnostic render pass to enable differentiable relighting of static scenes at interactive rates. This dramatically reduces lighting iteration times from minutes-to-hours per frame.

entry.title: DeNA-SGN: Deterministic Neighborhood Aggregation for Verified Spiking Graph Inference

author.name: Sanjay Das, Xi Zhang, Emily Herron, Prasanna Date

entry.summary: This paper introduces DeNA-SGN, a spiking graph network that uses fixed OR and tie-inclusive Majority neighborhood aggregation of binary node features combined with a learned signed-weight threshold classifier, compiled into the SuperNeuroMAT neuromorphic simulator. Across seven datasets and 41 mapped classifiers, native spiking simulation exactly matches the exported ANN in every class decision and output-spike pattern, with 83.93% accuracy on a new Amazon Photo benchmark. The work matters because verified equivalence between spiking and conventional inference is a key step toward trustworthy neuromorphic graph learning.

entry.title: SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots

author.name: Yoo Jin Lee, Melanie Torres Crespo, Zhongxiao Deng, Andrew Tejada-Vega, Rebecca Kramer-Bottiglio, Wenzhong Yan, Yimin Luo

entry.summary: This paper introduces SunLightBots, a class of subgram-scale, untethered soft robots that achieve autonomous locomotion powered solely by continuous sunlight at roughly 1 Sun intensity. The work addresses the core mismatch between low-power environmental energy harvesting and the high mechanical output power needed for rapid, cyclic actuation, without conventional onboard power or control hardware. It matters because it demonstrates a pathway to energy-autonomous embodied systems at scales where batteries and electronics are impractical.

entry.title: Recover, Don't Just Continue: Learning from Feedback for Physical Failure Understanding and Correction

author.name: Miao Pan, Kaixiang Yao, Xiaohe Zhou, Xu Wang, Qinfeng Li, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: Embodied-Corrector targets capabilities that current multimodal LLM-based embodied agents lack: causal failure localization, capability-constrained adaptation, and experience-driven revision of decisions. The authors build failure-recovery training data by injecting perturbations at subtask boundaries of successful trajectories, teaching models to understand why execution deviates and how to revise plans. This addresses a real gap between planning from instructions and reliable physical execution.

entry.title: MotionSkill: From Bipedal Motion Video to Control across Embodiments

author.name: Philip Niu, Xiaofeng Han, Sylvie Pan, Yang Wang

entry.summary: MotionSkill extracts a timed locomotion reference from a single monocular video of bipedal motion and adapts it to ten different simulated bipedal embodiments via alignment, retargeting with target segment lengths, and inverse kinematics under joint constraints. Each embodiment then trains a residual policy on the mapped reference in MuJoCo. The approach enables cross-embodiment motion reuse from casually captured video.

entry.title: XBot-Omni: An Omni-Modal Model for Embodied Understanding and Interaction

author.name: Kerui Gu, Xing Fu, Shuoyang Sun, Cheng Peng, Jingru Duan, Huayu Gu, Zhenyu Chen, Jiaxin Huang, Cheng Wen, Rui Zhen, Kairui Chen, Zhihui Peng, Shaoli Huang

entry.summary: XBot-Omni is a Thinker-Talker-Actor architecture that extends omni-modal models to robotic modalities, processing text, images, audio, and video and realizing responses through speech, coordinated body motion, and facial expressions. It introduces a dedicated Actor component for generating embodied nonverbal behaviors alongside verbal communication. This targets socially capable embodied agents that communicate intentions multimodally.

entry.title: BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qiren Wang, Mingyu Guo, Zixuan Wang, Weisong Shi

entry.summary: BEVCast is a two-stage bird's-eye-view representation for camera-based end-to-end autonomous driving that allocates high resolution only to cells predicted to lie on the vehicle's future path, keeping the rest of the scene at coarse resolution under a fixed compute budget. The approach removes the need for HD maps or navigation commands while improving efficiency relative to uniformly fine BEV grids.

entry.title: Post-Glasswing cybersecurity projects

author.name: osmarks

entry.summary: The post assesses the aftermath of AI-driven vulnerability discovery efforts like Glasswing, arguing that while open-weights models now match scary hacking capabilities predicted months ago, systemic compromise has not materialized due to exploitation friction. It contends that patch-via-report pipelines are unsustainable and lossy, citing findings such as 948 local privilege escalation exploits found by OpenAI in Linux.

entry.title: Delaying Internal Deployments Until After X Days of Safety Testing

author.name: annawang

entry.summary: The author proposes a concrete policy mechanism: no model checkpoint may be used internally beyond safety testing until a fixed number of calendar days have elapsed since its hash was filed with an auditor. The post walks through implementation details, adjustable axes (wait duration, what is blocked, when the clock starts), and potential failure modes, building on an AI Futures Project idea about internal deployment lags.

entry.title: Open Challenges and Opportunities in Human-Agent Systems

author.name: Reuth Mirsky, Sarath Sreedharan, Nitay Alon, Stefan Sarkadi, Munindar P. Singh, Liz Sonenberg, Peter Stone, Silvia Tulli, Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou, Shlomo Zilberstein

entry.summary: A position-style survey organizing open challenges in human-agent interaction, drawing on foundations from the AAMAS community and covering partnerships, teams, and larger groups with differing roles, authority, and objectives. It structures computational approaches around understanding others, coordinating capabilities, and sustaining socio-technical relationships.

entry.title: Advancing Weighted Partial MaxSAT Solving via Differentiable GPU Guidance

author.name: Mingju Liu, Curie Kim, Steve Dai, Cunxi Yu

entry.summary: This paper presents a GPU-CPU hybrid framework for Weighted Partial MaxSAT that complements state-of-the-art CPU solvers with differentiable GPU optimization of instance-specific decision parameters. It introduces a hierarchical differentiable loss prioritizing hard clause satisfaction before optimizing weighted soft objectives, requiring no training data or pretrained model.

entry.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models

author.name: Ritvik Rastogi

entry.summary: The paper re-implements five readout designs for typed-decision models — models that read text with a language model and score typed options (yes/no checks, labelled choices, graded scores) via small readout heads — and trains them under controlled conditions to identify which design choices actually matter. Motivated by a wave of such models including TypeSafe's Jev, Nimble, and the Decision 1.0-3.0 family, whose heterogeneous recipes confound comparisons.

entry.title: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench

author.name: Sungbin Im

entry.summary: Running 2,160 tau2-bench episodes in airline and retail domains with every database write recorded, the paper scores each episode four ways: native gold-state scoring, an LLM judge, the judge given the policy document, and a minimal boundary evaluator checking expected versus observed writes. The study quantifies whether benchmark-style evaluation and deployed LLM-judge evaluation, often treated as interchangeable, actually agree.

entry.title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction

author.name: Yaxin Zhang, Xingyu Wu, Yuchen Yan, Yuqin Dai, Hong Zhao, Lixing Shen, Zhan Chen, Jian Shao, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Presents SimRec, an RL framework that trains the full interaction policy of a tool-integrated LLM recommendation agent rather than isolated components like query rewriting. It uses a task-anchored user simulator providing per-recommendation feedback (via an external LLM or self-play) and a task-aligned reward optimizing the whole search-ask-recommend loop.

entry.title: AskALCF: A Self-Improving Agentic System for Intelligent HPC User Support

author.name: Jingyan Jiang, Akhilesh Bondapalli, Krishna Rauniyar, Murat Keceli, Yasaman Ghadar, Haritha Siddabathuni Som, Venkatram Vishwanath, Michael E. Papka, Rong Ge, Huihuo Zheng

entry.summary: AskALCF is an agentic log-analysis and improvement pipeline deployed for HPC user support at ALCF. It evaluates production interactions at fine granularity, attributes failures to missing knowledge, retrieval, prompting, model behavior, or tool execution, and routes each failure to an actionable repair, addressing the static nature of prior QA systems after deployment.

entry.title: Knowledge Transfer for Conditional Flow Matching: Frozen Estimation and Adaptation

author.name: Yian Huang, Jian Huang

entry.summary: Develops a transfer learning framework for conditional flow matching supporting distinct source and target distributions and dimensions, with a frozen-representation variant and an adaptive variant under a functional anchoring penalty. It provides Wasserstein risk bounds accounting for source estimation, target fitting, representation mismatch, and integration error.

entry.title: The Illusion of Diversity: Aligning LLM Exploration via Effective Entropy

author.name: Xiaoliang Fu, Jiaye Lin, Yangyi Fang, Cong Qin, Binbin Zheng, Chaowen Hu, Zekai Shao

entry.summary: Argues that standard entropy-based exploration signals in RLVR are validity-blind, rewarding chaotic degeneration rather than useful exploration, creating an illusion of diversity. It proposes Effective Entropy, a validity-aware entropy measured only within valid solution space, to align exploration diversity with reasoning correctness.

entry.title: Characterizing Predictive Multiplicity in Ranking and Its Fairness Implications

author.name: Ainhize Barrainkua, Mikel Malag\'on

entry.summary: This paper extends predictive multiplicity - the phenomenon of competing models with equal performance but conflicting outputs - to score-based ranking problems, introducing formal definitions and theoretical guarantees. It also examines the relationship between multiplicity and algorithmic fairness in high-stakes settings like welfare resource allocation.

entry.title: Helgason-Fourier Random Features for Scalable Hyperbolic Latent Variables

author.name: Koshi Watanabe, Daichi Mochihashi, Hideitsu Hino, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: The paper introduces Random Helgason-Fourier Features (RHFF), an explicit finite-dimensional feature map for kernels on hyperbolic space with a characterized spectral density and a uniform approximation error bound, enabling scalable hyperbolic kernels including the Matern family. Building on RHFF, the authors develop RHFF-LVM, a hyperbolic latent variable model requiring no quadrature, variational bounds, or auxiliary variables.

entry.title: Can a search hold its own bar? In-loop deflation and its exploits in autonomous strategy discovery

author.name: Eray Gen\c{c}ay

entry.summary: The paper analyzes what happens when backtest-overfitting corrections like the deflated Sharpe ratio are moved inside autonomous LLM-driven search loops, indexing the acceptance threshold to the search's own trial count and dispersion. It shows analytically that naive in-loop bars admit a variance-dilution exploit where mediocre near-duplicate candidates lower the bar.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Certificates for Portfolio Optimization Under Uncertainty: A Gated Reinforcement-Learning Approach

author.name: Mohammad Zarei, Amirhossein MohammadpourAzari, Moslem Habibi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a gated conformal semantic risk control framework that separates return-seeking portfolio allocation from text-conditioned downside-risk verification, using an instruction-tuned language model to convert disclosures into schema-validated semantic risk states. The goal is a calibrated, replayable pre-trade audit trail that satisfies emerging regulatory expectations for automated portfolio systems.

entry.title: What Do Tokenizer Comparisons Measure? Disentangling Granularity, Root Assignment, and Word-Level Readout across Amharic and Hausa

author.name: Abdul Rehman Antall, Baidya Nath Saha

entry.summary: The paper disentangles why morphology-aware tokenizers outperform BPE in morphologically rich languages, separating segmentation granularity and sub-token readout effects from the effect of grouping words by roots, using a lossless root-and-pattern tokenizer with controlled comparisons. It studies Amharic, whose Ge'ez abugida hides consonantal roots, with Latin-script Hausa as an orthographic contrast.

entry.title: Parsed, Plausible, Wrong: Output Format Controls Silent Errors in Small-Model Semantic Parsing

author.name: Umar Ahmed, Maxim Dunaev, Mohammad Nour Al Awad, Sergey Ivanov, Ivan Khodnenko

entry.summary: This study fine-tunes two sub-billion parameter models on six lossless encodings of the same parse target to test whether output format controls silent parse errors. Across 300 runs with pre-registered statistical corrections, shortening the target never helps, but encoding targets in ordinary words is most accurate, showing format choice materially affects reliability.

entry.title: The Neighbour's Label: Opposite Subgroup Effects of Same-Dialogue Exposure in Next-Act Evaluation

author.name: Ali Amini, Masoumeh Chapariniya, Rytis Maskeliunas, Robertas Dama\v{s}evi\v{c}ius

entry.summary: Demonstrates that overlapping windows and similarity retrieval in next-act dialogue evaluation can leak the labelled predecessor of a test target, causing opposite effects in two subgroups: copying the predecessor's act helps continuation cases and hurts transition cases, which aggregate averages hide. Controlled experiments on SGD, STAR, and AMI confirm the mechanism and its removal by purging adjacent rows.

entry.title: Validation of a Facial-Video Digital Hydration Biomarker Score for Tracking Hydration State Transitions in a Real-World Fasting Model

author.name: Yudara Kularathne, D. M. J. Prathapa, Thanveer Ahamed, Janindu Athukorala, Thisara Perera

entry.summary: This study validates a facial-video-derived digital biomarker for tracking hydration transitions using Ramadan fasting as a natural model of fluid abstinence. Across 104 participants and 208 videos, the score rose from a mean of 36.6 in the fasting state to 70.6 after rehydration, with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 2.03) and 102 of 104 participants showing the expected direction. It provides initial real-world evidence for camera-based physiological monitoring.

entry.title: ChartGalaxy++: A Richly Annotated Dataset for Chart Understanding and Generation

author.name: Duan Li, Zheng Wang, Jiangning Zhu, Yuhui Yuan, Shixia Liu

entry.summary: ChartGalaxy++ provides 217,195 infographic charts annotated with scene-graph representations whose nodes capture visual elements and semantic groups and whose edges encode hierarchical and spatial relationships. This richer annotation supports tasks beyond element-level detection, such as understanding infographic organization and generating well-structured designs. It significantly extends the usefulness of chart data for document intelligence.

entry.title: SPEM: Scan-Prior Entropy Modeling for LiDAR Point Cloud Compression

author.name: Bojun Liu, Yangzhi Ma, Jie Li, Dong Liu, Li Li

entry.summary: SPEM exploits LiDAR scanning regularities inside the entropy model for point cloud geometry compression without transforming coordinates into spherical or beam-aligned systems, arguing acquisition priors should guide probability modeling rather than dictate the coding representation. This preserves exact recovery of original Cartesian geometry while improving compression.

entry.title: RADIANT: Redundancy-Aware Information Allocation for Universal Multi-Modal Fusion

author.name: Shenghai Wu, Yue Lin

entry.summary: RADIANT reframes multimodal fusion around information allocation, distinguishing redundant cross-modal overlap to suppress, modality-unique evidence to preserve, and task-conditioned synergy to compose, using stable matrix-exponential projections to reduce interference. It is presented as a task-general fusion framework rather than a task-specific architecture.

entry.title: K2V: Generative Keyframing For Physically Plausible Video Generation

author.name: Felix O'Mahony, Daniel Olmeda Reino, Roberto Cipolla, Ayush Tewari

entry.summary: Proposes redistributing physical reasoning in video generation onto a language-model-backed keyframe module that explicitly reasons in language about key moments, then conditions a video diffusion model on those keyframes. This reduces physical errors compared to forcing all physical reasoning inside the diffusion process.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Modular Obstacle and Spatial-Aware Framework for Manipulation In Cluttered Scenes

author.name: Richard Shi, Mohammad Mahdavian, Mehrdad Momeni Zadeh, Mohammed Elmahgiubi, Amir Rasouli

entry.summary: Proposes MOSAIC, a modular framework augmenting pretrained vision-language-action policies with auxiliary semantic grounding tasks that predict role-specific masks for target objects, destinations, and surrounding obstacles, adding explicit spatial and obstacle awareness. It targets safer manipulation in cluttered scenes where 2D-only VLAs make small spatial errors that cause collisions.

entry.title: NSDL: Neuro-Symbolic Division of Labor for Multi-Robot Task Planning

author.name: Xincheng Tan, Ke Wang, Yining Di, Minfeng Zhu

entry.summary: NSDL splits multi-robot task planning between a small vision-language model, which makes scene-grounded judgments such as goal status and robot-task assignment, and a deterministic solver, which expands the resulting plan sketch into executable joint plans with prerequisites, handoffs, and timing. This neuro-symbolic division exploits the strengths of each component. It offers a scalable alternative to end-to-end LLM planning for heterogeneous robot teams.

entry.title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling

author.name: Christa Cuchiero, Francesca Primavera, Sara Svaluto-Ferro

entry.summary: The authors develop score-based generative models for time series and finite-dimensional data built on a new class of jump-diffusions whose characteristics are linear combinations of their own signature components. They show the expected signature is computable via linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, reducing score learning to solving ODEs plus deterministic optimization.

entry.title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception

author.name: Guy Azran, Sarah Keren

entry.summary: The paper proposes a middle ground between brittle single-best-guess state estimation and intractable full belief distributions over symbolic states. It constructs a theta-confidence Minimal Belief Set from the pretrained perception model's own output probabilities, enabling task-aware decisions that remain feasible under perception uncertainty.

entry.title: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Chengwei Liu, Yutao Hu, Tao Zhang, Junsheng Wu, Hongping Gan, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This study tests whether problem-statement reformulation helps LLMs, defining three legal rewrite types: decomposition, typed reformulation, and concept reduction. Across eight math, logic, and code benchmarks with eight models, the oracle best-rewrite gains are large but effectiveness depends heavily on problem type, highlighting selection difficulty.

entry.title: A physics-constrained deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes

author.name: Hanmin Li, Tao Wang, Shuangliang Liu, Zhe Zhang, Maodeng Li

entry.summary: Proposes PCM-PPO, a physics-constrained maskable proximal policy optimization method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes, using a Titan-specific discrete-time MDP and incorporating system dynamics and geometric models to enforce physical feasibility under deep space uncertainty.

entry.title: Marginal-Preserving Coupled Diffusion Composition for Long-Horizon Planning

author.name: Hengrui Zhang, Qiyu Wang, Yuhu Cheng, Brooks Paige, Xuesong Wang

entry.summary: This work tackles incoherence when stitching independently denoised trajectory chunks in compositional diffusion planners, proposing graph-structured dependence among chunk-wise initial noises as a lightweight coordination mechanism. Unlike prior inference-time search or guidance approaches, the method preserves marginals while enforcing global consistency for long-horizon goal-conditioned planning.

entry.title: Causals: An Open Knowledge Graph for Research on Causal Reasoning

author.name: Miaozhe Lin, Qiongzheng Lin, Zhongwei Liang, Zijun Liu

entry.summary: Causals is a large open knowledge graph for causal reasoning research, built from news reports with 369,184 nodes and over 1.27 million edges linking events, organizations, commodities, and financial instruments. It preserves distinct semantics for structural relationships, observations, and attributed causal claims, with links to source records. The paper characterizes its connectivity and multi-hop retrieval properties.

entry.title: How Should Planning Agents ReSHAPE Their Search Space?

author.name: Yilin Zhang, Xinran Zhao, Tong Chen, Ziming Yuan, Tongshuang Wu

entry.summary: The ReSHAPE task formalizes how planning agents should revise a user's initial specification, judging a revision by whether its search space matches the plans the user would accept and whether a planner can find one there. Using ReSHAPE Planter, which builds instances from planning benchmarks with a human-validated simulated user, the authors analyze 5,800 agent-revised specifications in travel and shopping. They find that a single correct trade-off can substantially change planner outcomes, showing request revision matters for planning agents.

entry.title: Large Language Models as Digital Twins: a Distribution-Aware Questionnaire-Based Evaluation

author.name: Francesco Di Cursi, Chiara Boldrini, Andrea Passarella, Marco Conti

entry.summary: The paper tests whether LLMs can act as personal digital twins by completing the BFI-2-60 Big Five personality questionnaire as specific individuals based on their social-media posts. Evaluating GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, and Mistral on the MyPersonality dataset, the authors compare predictions against baselines without user text to determine whether predictions reflect actual writing-based trait information.

entry.title: The Impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on Code Review Process

author.name: Antonio Collante, Samuel Abedu, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Ahmad Abdellatif, Ebube Alor, Emad Shihab

entry.summary: An empirical study of 25,473 pull requests from 9,254 GitHub projects, identifying GPT-assisted PRs via a semi-automated heuristic combining keyword detection, regex filtering, and manual verification. The study measures effects on PR resolution time, phase-specific review performance, and developer assistance patterns.

entry.title: MITRA-Swarm: Injecting Explicit Linguistic Structure into Foundation Models for Classical Machine Translation

author.name: Kayshav Bhardwaj, Pragun Seth, Kush Bhardwaj, Vijay Nagasamy, Kurt Keutzer

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent translation architecture for Classical Sanskrit that decomposes the problem into specialized agents for Sandhi splitting, translation, and discourse-aware ellipsis restoration, with separated routing and quality judges. The approach addresses morphophonemic fusion, dense compounding, and zero-anaphora that monolithic single-call models handle poorly.

entry.title: What Entropy-Based View Selection Cannot See: An Audit of Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sivasuthan Sukumar, Uthayasanker Thayasivam

entry.summary: Audits test-time adaptation methods for CLIP-style vision-language models that select among augmented test views using prediction entropy or embedding typicality, showing the shared reliance on the model's own per-view responses limits what these scoring functions can detect. The paper identifies blind spots in the dominant confidence-based view selection paradigm.

entry.title: LLM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning with Human-in-the-Loop Calibration for Real-Time Optimal Power Flow

author.name: Jiayang Tu, Bozhen Jiang, Bojun Du, Yunxiao Ling, Ershun Du, Qin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-enhanced deep RL framework for real-time optimal power flow that augments physics-based rewards with sparse language-based evaluative feedback during offline training, allowing semantic operational and safety requirements to shape policy learning. A selective human-in-the-loop calibration mechanism improves reliability under time-varying conditions.

entry.title: Moving Beyond the DRW Model: Learning Quasar Variability with Generative Models

author.name: Nadav Bojan Sellam, Kevin Park, Alex Bronstein, Zolt\'an Haiman

entry.summary: Investigates biases arising when the widely used damped random walk model serves as an incorrect null hypothesis for quasar variability analyses (periodicity searches, TDEs, changing-look quasars, reverberation mapping). The authors learn quasar variability with generative models to provide more faithful null distributions and quantify the impact on significance estimates.

entry.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose

author.name: Ivan Poddiakov, Ivan Kruzhilov, Galina Zubkova, Svetlana Erofeeva, Andrey Savchenko, Pavel Blinov

entry.summary: Introduces Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive benchmark for time-series classification in electronic-nose breath-based disease screening, built on the largest public clinical eNose dataset (1,234 patients). The work emphasizes realistic conditions, notably sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode that prior small private-dataset studies ignore.

entry.title: Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?

author.name: Theo Keane, Anthony Onwuli, Richard Tomsett, Robert M. Forrest, Jonathan J. Bean

entry.summary: This study examines data scaling behavior for machine-learned interatomic potentials (M3GNet, MACE, PET) trained on subsets of a 1.16-million-structure MatPES-MP-ALOE pool, from 10,000 to 640,000 structures. It compares uniform sampling, chemistry- and structure-informed stratification, iterative DIRECT, and furthest-point sampling using pretrained MLIP embeddings to test whether scaling laws transfer across heterogeneous, expensive-to-generate materials datasets.

entry.title: Latent Imagination for Parameterized Action Spaces

author.name: Atahan Cilan, \.Ihsan Mert Muhac{\i}ro\u{g}lu, \"Umit Can Bekar

entry.summary: HyLI is a model-based agent for parameterized-action MDPs that learns a hybrid policy entirely in the latent imagination of a world model and acts with a single forward pass, combining sample efficiency with fast action selection. It adds counterfactual mode evaluation so every discrete action receives a learning signal, and success-window replay to retain rare successes.

entry.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces

author.name: Mahmut S. Gokmen, Mitchell A. Klusty, Evan W. Damron, Caroline N. Leach, Samuel E. Armstrong, V. K. Cody Bumgardner

entry.summary: DuoJEPA trains one self-supervised encoder per modality with the LeJEPA objective and adds a single transformer layer that translates each embedding into the other encoder's space, without ever aligning the two own spaces directly. It studies whether cross-modal retrieval and classification can be achieved without forcing encoders into a shared space.

entry.title: Show Your Work in Swahili: Reinforcement Learning for Native-Language Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Jessica Lundin, Katherine Rosenfeld, David Adelani, Geoffrey Mosoti Nyakiongora, Halfan Ngowo, Sloan Coffin, Ralph Abboud, Guillaume Chabot-Couture

entry.summary: Fikiria is a two-stage SFT+GRPO recipe for Swahili math reasoning, rewarding a format gate times a weighted sum of answer accuracy and ChrF++ similarity of the Swahili reasoning to an in-language reference chain of thought. Trained on a 2.3k-problem translated GSM8K dataset, Fikiria-AfriqueQwen-14B reaches 79.2% on AfriMGSM Swahili, outperforming GPT-4o under strict scoring.

entry.title: Rectified Looped Transformer

author.name: Musheng Li, Jiawei Zhang, Ziyuan Liu, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: Proposes RLT, which redesigns feedback between loops of a shared transformer block by interpolating between the current state and its prediction, inspired by flow-based modeling, to prevent hidden-state scale growth and perturbation amplification in deep recurrences. The paper provides theoretical analysis showing smoother state trajectories and improved parameter efficiency for language modeling.

entry.title: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated LVLM for Chest Radiograph Report Generation

author.name: Chayan Mondal, Duc-Son Pham, Tele Tan, Ashu Gupta, Vincent T. Y. Tiong, Shreya Ghosh, Tom Gedeon

entry.summary: Presents TransXplainRRG, an LVLM for chest X-ray report generation that combines a Swin Transformer encoder, a text encoder incorporating patient medical history, and an expert-guided inside-out approach extracting abnormal findings for report refinement. The system emphasizes explainability and workflow integration and is evaluated with radiologists to support clinical adoption.

entry.title: MuSeToM: Multi-Sensory Evaluation of Belief Revision with Textual Cues Across Six Senses

author.name: Chunkit Chan, Kawai Chung, Sze Heng Douglas Kwok, Yuxuan Liu, Yauwai Yim, Tianshi Zheng, Haochen Shi, Qing Zong, Wong Kai Chung, Pak Hin Lau, Calvin Yang, Yifan Gao, Xiaoman Pan, Ginny Wong, Simon See, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: MuSeToM is a human-validated benchmark of 2,415 instances adapted from BigToM and OpenToM that evaluates epistemic belief revision in theory-of-mind reasoning: whether LLMs can decide when perceptual evidence is sufficient to justify another person's belief revision, with textual cues spanning six sensory categories. It addresses a gap beyond static belief attribution and false-belief tasks.

entry.title: Look It Up: Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Codebook Search

author.name: Jaros{\l}aw Janas, Pawe{\l} Morawiecki, Josef Pieprzyk

entry.summary: The paper proposes a codebook-based multi-bit watermarking scheme for LLM text, mapping an n-bit payload to a longer u-bit codeword embedded via token-level logit biasing, and recovering payloads by nearest-codeword matching under Hamming or Levenshtein distance. It achieves near-perfect recovery of 16-24 bit payloads on 200-token generations and strong performance on 127-token generations.

entry.title: Adversarial Risk in the Generative AI Era Necessitates Dropping the Small Epsilon Ball

author.name: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil G. Marchant, Paul Montague, Jiani Xie, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: This position paper argues that the field's fixation on minimal l_p-norm epsilon-ball perturbations is a metrological trap that distorts perceived risk and misdirects defenses, especially in the generative AI era. It contends that this paradigm fails to reduce harm and may actively facilitate attacks by incentivizing adversaries to exploit non-overlapping adversarial pathways.

entry.title: Machine Learning Moment Closure for the Boltzmann Transport Equation: Enforcing Hyperbolicity

author.name: Bongseok Kim, Jiahao Zhang, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Develops the first data-driven closure for multidimensional Hermite moment systems of the Boltzmann transport equation with guaranteed hyperbolicity in every direction. Learned closures previously lacked structural constraints, risking complex characteristic speeds and unstable simulations.

entry.title: AROMA: Adaptive Representation-Oriented Multimodal Actuation for Vision-Language Model Control

author.name: Zhaoning Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a frozen-VLM control framework that decides where, how, and when to intervene in internal representations, demonstrating in Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct that four causally validated cross-attention dimensions explain most cardinality sensitivity despite low activation energy. Magnitude-normalized subspace actuation converts this into improved exact-count control.

entry.title: Schedule-Calibrated Commitment Order in Blockwise Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Gaurav Sarkar (International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad), Umang Pandey (Advanced Micro Devices), Pratik Prabhanjan Brahma (Advanced Micro Devices), Zicheng Liu (Advanced Micro Devices), Emad Barsoum (Advanced Micro Devices)

entry.summary: Analyzes whether token commitment in masked diffusion LLMs is intrinsically left-to-right or an artifact of block schedules, using a Spearman-rank identity to decompose global position-commitment correlation into schedule and within-block components. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct show block size strongly shifts apparent commitment order once calibrated against uniform-random references.

entry.title: The Noise Floor of a Quantization Comparison: Engine, restart, batch and kernel drift, measured against 8-bit and 4-bit effects in two decision models

author.name: Aleks Blagojevich, Trevor Sunderland

entry.summary: The paper disentangles non-quantization sources of output drift (serving engine, restarts, batching, kernel selection) from actual 8-bit and 4-bit quantization effects, measuring these on 2,400 real decisions from two Cloudflare decision models on NVIDIA GB10 hardware. It finds infrastructure noise can move 0-0.92% of decisions, providing a careful methodology for attributing quantization impacts.

entry.title: A Recipe for Physical Action Model Training

author.name: Shaojiang Wang, Geer Yang

entry.summary: The paper connects decisions about model capacity, demonstration budgets, data composition, representation, optimization, and deployment for robot action models through a common conditional-distribution target, using nested learning oracles for exact risk accounting. It includes numerical checks exposing capacity-data coupling and cases where deployment KL worsens while NLL improves, plus an analysis of 206 public PushT trajectories.

entry.title: Asymmetric Multimodal Learning with Decomposed JEPAs

author.name: Yusuf Shihata

entry.summary: This paper proves an Alignment Redundancy Bound showing that cross-modal alignment as a sole objective is fundamentally lossy when modalities are informationally asymmetric, discarding modality-unique and synergistic information. It proposes decomposed JEPAs that preserve non-redundant structure, with visual question answering as a motivating example.

entry.title: Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences

author.name: Torben Berndt, Lingyi Yang, Federico Nardi, Yi Heng Lim, AJ Shears, Benjamin Walker

entry.summary: The paper introduces ci-proto, a family of time series foundation models built on Mamba-3 whose linear state recurrences enable chunk-wise parallel-in-time training and linear-cost inference. It alternates recurrent temporal processing with cross-variate attention for multivariate probabilistic forecasting.

entry.title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs

author.name: Arnab Sanyal, Gourav Datta, Sandeep P. Chinchali

entry.summary: LazyWeights compresses existing integer-quantized LLM weight formats with entropy coding and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged while DRAM moves only coded bytes. Coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B, and SmolLM-1.7B are 5.7-31.4% smaller than the best llama.cpp format, supported by a bit-exact 0.21 mm2 ASIC.

entry.title: Beyond Foreign-Key Connectivity: Semantic Relationship Representation for Relational Deep Learning

author.name: Noy Cohen-Shapira

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that foreign-key constraints in relational deep learning carry semantic information beyond mere structural connectivity, and introduces a framework separating schema-defined relationship semantics, association entities, and explicit relationship-level attributes. It aims to enable relationship-aware representations for graph-based learning over relational databases.

entry.title: Taxonomizing Synthetic Data for Law

author.name: Ignacio Cofone, Katherine J. Strandburg, Nicholas Tilmes

entry.summary: The authors extend a prior taxonomy of synthetic data to legal and policy analysis, arguing that background knowledge and ground-truth assumptions used to create synthetic data matter as much as its connection to collected data. The paper addresses privacy, competition, and data-quality implications of treating synthetic data as categorically different from real data.

entry.title: Analysis choices decide whether untrained networks beat trained ones at V1: a multiverse analysis of model-brain RSA

author.name: Nils Leutenegger

entry.summary: This multiverse analysis revisits claims that untrained convolutional networks rival trained ones as models of visual cortex, showing that under a pre-specified ridge readout the untrained advantage disappears, and that across 36 analysis combinations the sign of the V1 contrast flips depending on methodological choices. It is a cautionary reproducibility study for model-brain representational similarity analyses.

entry.title: HybridCT: ML Accelerated Tomography for Climate Relevant 3D Cloud Observations

author.name: Linda Forster, Nicholas J. LaHaye, Marcin J. Kurowski, Anna Jungbluth, Bernhard Mayer, Anthony B. Davis

entry.summary: HybridCT combines an ML emulator mapping multi-angle radiances to cloud optical thickness with a classical SART inversion to retrieve 3D cloud extinction from passive observations. Trained on synthetic cloud fields from radiative transfer simulations, it targets the long-standing lack of detailed 3D measurements of low-level clouds, a major source of climate prediction uncertainty.

entry.title: LLMs and the Homogenization of Teaching

author.name: Mei Tan, Hyunji Nam, Hari Subramonyam, Dorottya Demszky

entry.summary: The paper measures diversity in LLM-generated educational content, comparing frontier and open-weight models to human-authored distributions on math item generation and essay feedback using lexical, semantic, and domain-grounded measures. It evaluates prompting methods and post-training against the concern that homogeneous outputs narrow student thinking.

entry.title: Hy ASR 3.0 Technical Report

author.name: Aoxiong Yin, Auden Li, Chao Huang, Chuanyang Hu, Eitan Wang, Ethan Zou, Fangming Feng, Guangyu Chen, Guinan Li, He Wang, Jiahong Li, Meng Yu, Mingyu Cui, Peng Wang, Rongjie Li, Steve Yves, Teddy Sun, Tian Zheng, Wei Liu, Yang Zhou, Yixuan Zhang, Zhennan Lin, Zhihang Xu, Zhuohao Li, Ziqiang Zhang, Anji Zhang, Bang Wang, Caisheng Ouyang, Chengqi Zhu, Chong Li, Conglian Xie, Dongdong Wang, Edward Wang, Evelynn Liu, Ferman Yang, Feng Lu, Gang Zhang, Jathon Zhang, Jaxl Liu, Jiachen Luo, Jian Li, Jingxi Gui, Kysun Wang, Liang Dong, Longsha Zhou, Na Hu, Qi Chen, Rilin Chen, Rui Yuan, Shanshan Sang, Siyu Yan, Steven Hong, Taihui Wang, Weiwei Li, Xiangyu Zhang, Xiaotong Yang, Xue Hu, Xue Jiang, Yameng Li, Yifu Sun, Yuhuan Zhou, Zhiang Chen, Zhibin Wang

entry.summary: Hy ASR 3.0 is an LLM-based automatic speech recognition system supporting Mandarin, English, and 13 Chinese dialect groups, reporting the lowest aggregate error rates among evaluated systems on public Mandarin, English, and Cantonese benchmarks. It also supports contextual conditioning via hotword lists and question-answer style context beyond audio-only transcription.

entry.title: Towards Better Legal Reasoning LLMs: Signal Balancing and Reward Scheduling

author.name: Yinghao Hu, Qian Xiao, Yuting Huang, Kaisong Song, Yiquan Wu, Ang Li, Junjie Cao, Jun Lin, Kun Kuang, Fei Wu

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage training framework for legal-domain reasoning: JurisCoT-SFT with a length-normalized dual objective to balance reasoning-trace and answer signals, followed by reward scheduling to address GRPO limitations like reward hacking and plateaus. Targets high-quality, reliable legal reasoning traces.

entry.title: Can Agents Relive Past Experiences? Diagnosing Event-Affect Decoupling in Affective-Episodic Retrospection

author.name: Tingna Xie, Ming Wang, Shi Feng, Yongkang Liu

entry.summary: Formulates Affective-Episodic Retrospection (AER) as a task to evaluate whether memory-augmented agents recall past events, their associated affects, and their correspondence, defining Event-Affect Decoupling as a failure mode. Proposes EM-TRACE, a stage-wise framework decomposing AER into retrieval, affect, and correspondence components.

entry.title: Saidzoda-Kazakh-EmbeddingGemma-300M: How Far One Epoch of Generated Questions Takes a Small Kazakh Embedder

author.name: Tohir Saidzoda, Madina Abdusalomzoda, Abubakr Abdullozoda, Amin Jalilov, Faroiz Bobokhon, Aibek Shokanuly

entry.summary: Fine-tunes the small open EmbeddingGemma-300M embedder for one epoch on 208,511 generated Kazakh question-passage pairs (with model verification and English/Russian replay), lifting Kazakh Belebele recall@1 from 60.8 to 78.0 percent and outperforming 161 of 194 MTEB-published models, including OpenAI text-embedding-3-large.

entry.title: Morphological Simplification in Alzheimer's Disease: Computational Analysis and Identification From Connected Speech

author.name: Mohamed Zakaria Kurdi

entry.summary: Computes 55 automatic morphological features (seven families of them new) from Cookie Theft picture descriptions in the ADReSS corpus to identify Alzheimer's disease from connected speech, using group comparisons, SHAP, ablations, classifiers, and BERT baselines. The study finds morphological signals carry diagnostic information beyond transcript length and vocabulary.

entry.title: Vision-Grounded Semantic Learning and Alignment for Scalable Multilingual Text-Based Person Retrieval

author.name: Xinyu Zhou, Fan Li, Shasha Chen, Min Cao, Ahtamjan Ahmat, Qiaoming Zhu, Mang Ye

entry.summary: Tackles multilingual text-based person retrieval with MultiPedes, the first large-scale multilingual pedestrian-centric pretraining dataset, plus a model with separate multilingual text encoding and cross-modal alignment that avoids English-pivot bias. The approach targets scalable retrieval across languages rather than English-only settings.

entry.title: Bridging Update Coordination and Flatness in Federated Learning

author.name: Chongwei He, Shichen Huang, Jiayun Li, Deyuan Lin, Wangze Jiang, Shengjia Li, Xu Wang, Xiaofan Li, Zhi-Ri Tang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified federated learning framework connecting update coordination (reducing interference among heterogeneous client updates) with flatness optimization (improving generalization via reduced parameter-perturbation sensitivity). Clients accumulate descent signals and flatness corrections along the same local trajectory while the server coordinates, enabling flexible combinations beyond algorithm-specific joint designs. This bridges two previously separate FL research threads.

entry.title: IncR-3DSGG: Incremental Posed RGB Image Based 3D Scene Graph Generation via Privileged Depth Supervision

author.name: Mrunmai Phatak, Daniel Kienzle, Roman K\"uble, J\"org H\"ahner, Rainer Lienhart

entry.summary: IncR-3DSGG generates 3D scene graphs incrementally from posed RGB images alone, removing the need for depth sensors at inference, which broadens deployment to robots without depth hardware. It uses privileged depth supervision during training and a Parametric Relation Predictor to learn relations without test-time point clouds. This is a practical efficiency and deployability contribution for embodied agents.

entry.title: Real Pairs Are Not Enough: Physically Anchored Supervision for Volumetric CT Super-Resolution

author.name: Haoran Liu, Zipei Yan, Mingzhe Liu, Jizhou Li, Guibin Zan
