entry.summary: The paper analyzes why super-resolution models trained on synthetic or naively mixed real LR-HR pairs oversmooth fine structures in volumetric CT, and proposes a Physically-anchored Implicit Network with Real-Pair Dual-Anchor learning. The HR anchor teaches fine structure via pair-conditioned spectral replay while the LR anchor constrains predictions, decoupling the two supervision roles. This improves fidelity of CT reconstruction for clinical use.

entry.title: Disentangled Embedding Optimization for Diffusion-Based Dataset Distillation

author.name: Hongcheng Li, Yucan Zhou, Yibin Wang, Xiaoyan Gu, Bo Li, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: This paper improves diffusion-based dataset distillation by addressing entanglement near cluster boundaries, which makes cluster prototypes overly similar and degrades generated distilled samples. It proposes disentangled embedding optimization to increase inter-cluster separation in the diffusion latent space, enabling more effective compact synthetic training sets.

entry.title: Hand in Silhouette: Synthetic-to-Real Multi-View Hand Reconstruction via Binary Masks

author.name: Leiyao Cui, Lecheng Ruan, Zihang Zhao

entry.summary: SilHand is a calibrated multi-view hand reconstruction framework operating on binary hand masks rather than RGB, substantially narrowing the synthetic-to-real appearance gap and enabling training on cheap synthetic data with accurate supervision. It projects metric 3D hypotheses into each view as masks for supervision and matching.

entry.title: ReFineR: Single image to dense point cloud registration at pixel level with point splatting

author.name: Ugo Insalaco, Jean-Emmanuel Deschaud, Pierre Dellenbach

entry.summary: ReFineR performs fine-grained image-to-point-cloud registration from a single image and a roughly estimated camera pose, using point splatting to correct residual reprojection errors of several pixels that arise from desynchronization, vibration, and reconstruction inaccuracies on robotic platforms. This addresses decimeter-level geometric discrepancies that degrade cross-modal supervision and texture mapping.

entry.title: One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Yimeng He, Yibin Xie, Yi Zheng, Yifan Gao, Lixia Wang, Yin-Chen Hsu, Yufeng Wang, Meng Lu, Debiao Li, Xiuzhen Huang

entry.summary: Proposes LoopMR, which reuses a single sufficiently large transformer block across all cascades in unrolled MRI reconstruction networks, motivated by looped transformers that match or exceed distinct-weight counterparts. This avoids parameter growth with cascade count while matching or beating state-of-the-art models like PromptMR+.

entry.title: Evolved Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Seizure Detection: Calcium Dynamics and Delay Mechanics

author.name: Tuba Aksoy

entry.summary: Using the EONS neuroevolution framework, this paper evolves spiking neural network topologies, weights, thresholds, and delays for EEG seizure detection, testing whether activity-dependent calcium currents in integrate-and-fire neurons improve performance. Per-neuron evolved calcium dynamics raised record-level MCC from 0.592 to 0.726 on 10 held-out CHB-MIT patients and cut false-alarm rate from 0.17 to 0.10, with statistically significant gains. The result demonstrates that biologically inspired calcium mechanisms can meaningfully improve evolved neuromorphic medical classifiers.

entry.title: DroneDiffusion: Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Path Planner for UAV Navigation

author.name: Ivan Valuev, Iana Zhura, Valerii Serpiva, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: DroneDiffusion generates local 3D UAV trajectories with a diffusion model conditioned on a vision-language perceptual reliability map marking degraded-sensing regions (lens flare, overexposure, reflective surfaces), the RGB image, goal, and initial velocity, with training-free CHOMP guidance for obstacle avoidance. Trained in simulation, it deploys zero-shot on real platforms. Explicitly modeling perception failure zones in trajectory planning is a distinctive angle on robust UAV navigation.

entry.title: Low-Cost Mobile Bimanual Manipulation for Long-Horizon Toilet Cleaning

author.name: Sven Schreiber, Bernard Burdiek, Lasse Huber-Saffer, Yung-Hui Li, Donglin Chen, Shang-Ching Liu, Jianwei Zhang

entry.summary: This work builds a low-cost, reproducible mobile bimanual platform from two LeRobot SO-101 arms on a TurtleBot 4 with a LeRobot-ROS 2 stack, and uses long-horizon toilet cleaning as a stress-test task. The authors collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate pi_0, pi_0.5, SmolVLA, and GR00T under identical embodiment conditions, with SARM progress signals and MEM observation-history variants; pi_0 performs best at 60% strict / 70% relaxed success. It provides a valuable open benchmark for comparing VLAs on accessible hardware.

entry.title: COMBS: Concealed Object Multi-modal Bayesian Search

author.name: Taylor Bergeron, Kevin Leahy

entry.summary: COMBS addresses finding concealed objects by unifying partially observable MDP formalisms with multi-modal priors from ontologies, semantic networks, LLMs, and VLMs. It introduces a concealment-adaptive mixed-observability Bayes-adaptive MDP where uncertainty spans both object locations and which nodes can conceal them, a hierarchical transition system for planning, and a COMBS-score fusing human, LLM, and VLM knowledge. This is a novel formal framework connecting LLM/VLM common sense with principled Bayesian search.

entry.title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation

author.name: Shuai Yang, Fangyi Xu, Yishu Shen, Kecheng Zheng, Yinghao Xu

entry.summary: HALO is a teleoperation/data-collection system for whole-body mobile manipulation that aligns operator perception and action with the robot while preserving physical feedback and natural locomotion. Operators perform kinesthetic teaching on end-effectors and drive a low-resistance platform separate from the deployed mobile base, enabling bimanual mobile manipulation demonstrations. This targets the difficult demonstration-collection bottleneck for coordinated locomotion plus manipulation.

entry.title: Sampling the Funnel: A Comprehensive Survey of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for Hierarchical Bayesian Inference

author.name: Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana, Aitor Almeida

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of the HMC algorithm family organized around Generalized HMC, using the pathological funnel geometry of hierarchical models as a motivating case study. It unifies many Hamiltonian and Langevin samplers as special cases of trajectory length, momentum refreshment, and Metropolis correction choices, and maps remaining methodological directions.

entry.title: Conformal prediction for censored life history data

author.name: Lu Mao

entry.summary: The paper develops a conformal prediction method for individual predictions of multistate trajectory summaries (e.g., time alive out of hospital) under right censoring, introducing a coverage-determining time and inverse-probability-of-censoring weighting to calibrate prediction regions. It supports both scalar and vector summaries over fixed clinical horizons.

entry.title: Provably Optimal HBT Legalization in Seconds: Certified Optima Reveal Where the Headroom Really Lies

author.name: Kadhir Parani, Manjunath Bezawada, Divya M, Kesana Jathin, Kolli Sarath, Sm Zobaed

entry.summary: The paper builds an open benchmark for hybrid bonding terminal legalization in 3D ICs and introduces GEO-Exact, an exact solver with independent dual certificates proving optimality in seconds. Certified optima reveal that prior RL legalizer claims of 19-22 percent displacement reduction overstate the true remaining headroom.

entry.title: Recursive State-Augmented Language Models: Persistent Latent-State Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models

author.name: Omer Haq

entry.summary: Introduces Recursive SALM, a framework where a persistent latent state evolves with each observation and generates adaptations of a frozen pretrained LM via a read-transition-write architecture separating encoding, latent dynamics, and predictor adaptation. Experiments with frozen GPT-2 small on a four-turn hypothesis-inference task show latent-gated LoRA matching a full-context LoRA baseline while excluding earlier context from the decoder.

entry.title: Your Hypergradient is Skewed: Antithetic Neumann Estimation for Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Jason Bohne, Pawel Polak, Gary Kazantsev, David Rosenberg

entry.summary: This paper identifies skewness as a previously overlooked third source of error in truncated Neumann series hypergradient estimation for bilevel optimization, showing third-moment error grows with truncation depth and conditioning. It proposes antithetic Neumann estimation to correct the skew and improves applications like hyperparameter tuning and data reweighting.

entry.title: Provenance-tracked, experimentally validated neural operator surrogates of three-dimensional laser melting with keyholes and free-form paths

author.name: Alix Benoit (Light-Matter Dynamics Group, Laboratory for Multifunctional Materials, Interfaces, Empa), Elia Iseli (Light-Matter Dynamics Group, Laboratory for Multifunctional Materials, Interfaces, Empa)

entry.summary: The paper trains FNO, RIGNO, and GAOT neural operators to predict temperature, melt-pool, and free-surface fields in 3D laser melting, covering keyhole regimes and free-form multi-beam scan paths, with FLOW-3D WELD data validated against measurements. An AiiDA framework tracks provenance of every simulation, model, and evaluation.

entry.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research

author.name: Jie Wang, Tong Zhu, JiaHao Kuang, Zhe Xu, Yunkai Chai, Dehong Zheng, Yu Cheng, Tao Ji, ZhouHan Lin, Qi Zhang, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: ArchSpace is a public platform for recording, reviewing, and referencing LLM architecture proposals, addressing the gap that industrial innovations from teams behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi are rarely documented while academic evaluations lack consistent baselines. Each recorded proposal includes experimental context to enable replication and comparison.

entry.title: Calibrate, Don't Retrain: Decomposing the Value of Annotator Disagreement in Cyberbullying Severity

author.name: Arslan Bisharat, Katelyn Skees, Manuel Sandoval Madrigal, Mujtaba Nazari, Ayaan Khan, Deborah L. Hall, Mohammed Abuhamad, Yasin N. Silva

entry.summary: Shows that collapsing five annotators' severity judgments into a majority vote discards substantial information in cyberbullying datasets, where full agreement occurs on only 4.1% of comments, and proposes predicting the full distribution of annotator judgments instead of a single label via calibration rather than retraining.

entry.title: FoveaDet: Software-Hardware Co-Design of Foveated CNN-Transformer for Object Detection

author.name: Deepak Mewada, Apporva Saraf, Ashwin Lele

entry.summary: FoveaDet applies biological foveation to real-time edge detection: the model predicts fixation points from saliency and aggressively prunes ViT patches to discard background, with optimized interpolation and patch-selection algorithms to avoid sequential slowdowns. This reduces floating-point operations by about 65 percent while maintaining detection quality, targeting power-constrained edge platforms. The work spans algorithms and implementation co-design.

entry.title: What Limits Thermal Infrared Drone Detection? A Cross-Dataset Benchmark Analysis

author.name: Tamara R. Lenhard, Jan Kels, Tobias Koch

entry.summary: This benchmark study systematically characterizes variability in public thermal infrared drone detection datasets, establishing an artifact taxonomy covering optical and sensor effects, tone mapping, enhancement, and annotation practices. It analyzes how these undocumented inconsistencies affect detector performance and cross-domain generalization.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement

author.name: Zhuangzhuang Ma, Rukuan Chai, Qianqian Ma, Yanghua Wang, Branko Bijeljic, Martin J. Blunt

entry.summary: Introduces a transformer-based 4D segmentation framework combining spatial and temporal information to segment time-resolved micro-CT images of pore-space evolution, improving on thresholding and per-image 3D networks whose temporally inconsistent errors could be mistaken for physical change. Applications include carbon storage, hydrogen storage, and groundwater transport.

entry.title: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering

author.name: Noah J. Bagazinski, Cyril Picard, Faez Ahmed

entry.summary: GenPFN is a training-free candidate generator for engineering design that uses a pretrained tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network to interpolate between labeled desired designs and refine candidates via gated classifier gradients. Evaluated on fourteen problems up to 44 parameters, it targets settings where costly simulations limit data availability.

entry.title: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction

author.name: Eno Agolli

entry.summary: This single-author theoretical paper applies the epistemology concept of akrasia to AI agents that judge their own reasoning defective and must decide whether to abandon conclusions. It shows that obeying self-assessments can actually worsen an agent's ability to distinguish sound from defective reasoning, formalizing limits of self-correction.

entry.title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution

author.name: Haojun Tang, Wenda Zhao, Xiang Zhou, Qiwei Lin, Lida Huang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: SkillEarth introduces a self-evolving skill extraction method for remote sensing agents that externalizes tool-call knowledge from demonstrated trajectories into reusable, retrievable skills without expert intervention or parameter updates. This addresses the limitation that existing RS agents require retraining or expert updates whenever new tools or tasks emerge.

entry.title: One Fuzzer, Many Reasoners: Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzing with Reliability-Calibrated and Context-Gated Guidance

author.name: Jinghao Wen, Xianglong Yu, Shaohuang Wang, Xun Jiao

entry.summary: NSAI-Fuzz is a unified semantics-aware fuzzing framework for testing heterogeneous neuro-symbolic AI systems, which are fragile because small semantics-preserving mutations can trigger discontinuous reasoning failures. It separates task-specific valid mutation from architecture-neutral guided search and characterizes candidates with five availability-aware risk signals including boundary pressure, grounding uncertainty, and representation drift. This fills a real gap in systematic testing of NSAI systems.

entry.title: From More to Better: Causal Inference and Digital Experimentation in the Age of AI

author.name: Winston Chou, M{\aa}rten Schultzberg, Lo-Hua Yuan, Wenjing Zheng, Avi Feller, David Holtz, Widad Machmouchi, Sven Schmit, Gagan Bhat, Simon Ejdemyr, Veronica Hannan, Amy Hartwig, Mahnaz Islam, Nathan Kallus, Jeremy Karp, Kyle Kretschman, Hannah Li, James McQueen, Evan Miller, Nicolas Stier, Sean Taylor

entry.summary: Drawing on a roundtable of academic researchers and industry practitioners, this paper argues that AI expands analytical capacity and thereby shifts the data scientist's leverage toward assessing credibility, importance, and generalizability of findings. It examines three themes: preserving the learning value of experimentation beyond individual tests, combining experimental, observational, and synthetic evidence, and ensuring evidence quality. The author list includes prominent figures in experimentation at major tech companies.

entry.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse

author.name: Saehun Chun, Wonje Choi, Jinwoo Jang, Taeyoon Kwack, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: HeMeR addresses embodied agents that combine declarative, procedural, and working memory modules by enabling selective key-value cache reuse for unchanged memory contents across consecutive decisions. Existing memory modules process each updated context as a new input, forcing full KV recomputation even when most content is unchanged. Structured KV reconciliation avoids this waste, improving efficiency for memory-rich embodied agents.

entry.title: Studies on Sign Language Retrieval in Low-Resource Dictionary Settings

author.name: Ushnish Sarkar, Vineet Kumar Rakesh, Bhaswar Chattopadhyay, Tapas Samanta

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether a pose encoder trained with metric learning on American Sign Language transfers zero-shot to six other sign languages with only dictionary-scale data (one or a few clips per sign). With a single enrolled clip, the frozen encoder retrieves the correct sign first in 36.4-80.7 percent of queries, substantially beating the best learning-free baseline.

entry.title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling

author.name: Changzeng Fu, Songyang Wang, Chang Gao, Xinyi Zhang, Peilin Li, Mo Meng, Jiarui Wu, Mingze Li, Hongwei Ding, Shiqi Zhao, Yong Li, Lang He

entry.summary: InertiaMPDD is a multimodal depression screening method that models emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, using a world-model-inspired latent predictor of healthy next-state patterns. It derives reference-deviation, residual decay, and Jacobian spectral descriptors as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision support from speech, visual behavior, and language.

entry.title: CAFIN: CUDA-accelerated Adaptive Fisher Information Matrix Network Optimization via GPU-Native Kernel Fusion

author.name: Maryam Arshad, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: CAFIN accelerates the AdaFisher second-order optimizer by fusing its sequential CUDA kernel launches (FIM preconditioner construction, EMA updates, gradient preconditioning, momentum accumulation) into GPU-native kernels, improving execution efficiency without changing the optimization formulation.

entry.title: Where Should the Code Go? Locating Foundation-Model Errors in Bitemporal Inventory Simulation

author.name: Durga Sandeep Saluru, Lanchen Song, Aditya Kumaran

entry.summary: Uses an exactly solvable lost-sales inventory environment with 36,672 rescored requests to determine where code augmentation helps or hurts foundation-model agents that maintain state under bitemporal (event-time vs report-time) uncertainty. Weak models fail in separable ways, and the study isolates which remedy removes which error class across twelve configurations of closed and open-weight models.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks

author.name: Amin Farajzadeh, Melike Erol-Kantarci

entry.summary: This paper proposes RACE, a framework that adapts wireless reliability requirements (SINR targets) for edge inference in 6G networks based on predicted action-failure probability and task criticality, replacing fixed SINR provisioning that wastes resources on low-risk tasks and underprovisions high-risk ones. An LLM operating on a slow timescale proposes task requirements, combined with deadline-derived constraints. It matters because it addresses a concrete systems problem at the intersection of physical AI, wireless networking, and inference deployment.

entry.title: A Time-Frequency-Condition Multimodal Fusion Foundation Model for Universal Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis under Multi-Element Heterogeneous Scenarios

author.name: Xinyu Zou, Jian Ma, Liang Ma, Chen Lu, Tao Peng, Yingjie Li

entry.summary: Proposes TFC-MMFD, a multimodal fusion foundation model for rotating-machinery fault diagnosis that fuses statistical indicators, time-frequency images, vibration sequences, and textual machine/condition descriptions. It targets universal diagnosis across heterogeneous machines and operating conditions, preserving machine-specific characteristics that domain-invariant transfer tends to discard.

entry.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory for Verified Science

author.name: Hans-Martin Will

entry.summary: Develops the type-theoretic foundations of Eigenkind, a proof-relevant type system for verified scientific knowledge stores that must compare independent derivations of the same claim, incompatible with judgmental proof irrelevance in Coq/Agda/Lean 4. The paper also shows that combining proof irrelevance with subsingleton elimination breaks strong normalization and non-transitive algorithmic conversion.

entry.title: Are We Ready for Snow-tonomous Driving? Challenges Toward Robust Automated Driving in Extreme Weather

author.name: Eren Erdal Aksoy, Abu Mohammed Raisuddin, Thien-Thu Ngo, Eren Aydemir, Osman Tahir Ek\c{s}i, Paula Litkey, Petri Manninen, Heikki Hyyti, Jyri Maanp\"a\"a, Tarmo Kivioja, Tuomas Herranen, V\"ais\"anen Sofie, Niemi Kalle, Isabelle Morvan, Pierre Duthon, Ian Marsh, Martin Sanfridson, Henrik Toss, Thanh Bui, Yuri Poledna, Maikol Funk Drechsler, Mikko Tarkiainen, Matti Kutila, Topi Miekkala, Stefan Parzefall, Valentina Donzella, Pak Hung Chan, Sogol Kharrazi, Mario Ceccarelli

entry.summary: Reports insights from the EU Horizon Europe ROADVIEW project on autonomous driving in snow, rain, and fog, conditions where current perception and control systems degrade severely. The paper characterizes failure modes, discusses sensor modalities under harsh weather, and outlines weather-aware perception and control approaches with industry and research partners.

entry.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories

author.name: Xiao Ma, Yijun Chen, Zhiquan Hu, Jicheng Zhao, Yuming Li, Chuang Dai

entry.summary: Proposes CARE-Drive, which improves vision-language-action end-to-end driving models by decomposing trajectory refinement into physically specialized, coupled corrections for position and heading, applied in alternating fashion. This targets limitations of prior unified refinement, residual denoising, and token-correction approaches that ignore distinct physical quantities.

entry.title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation

author.name: Zenghui Yang, Xinan Wang, Danyang Li, Zhe Xu, Zheng Yang, Jingao Xu, Qiang Ma

entry.summary: EMS-Nav is a biologically inspired navigation framework for industrial inspection robots that must reach destinations spanning scales from whole regions down to individual objects. It organizes perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions to enable online, on-device operation without heavy storage or compute, suiting environments with incomplete wireless coverage.

entry.title: Terms of Care: Designing for Participation in Data Governance by Disability Communities

author.name: Madiha Zahrah Choksi, Reeda Shimaz Huda, Rita Faia Marques, Anja Thieme, Cecily Morrison

entry.summary: Working with three disability advocacy organizations, this HCI study explores how disability communities can participate in dataset governance through context-sensitive modular licensing. Findings highlight the role of organizational memory of situated harms, formal and informal authority structures, communication practices, and trust in governing community-specific AI datasets.

entry.title: Spec-Driven PBT: Deriving Semantic Invariants from Code Specifications for Agentic Property-based Testing

author.name: Aditya Shukla, Kartik Gupta, Ali Alavi, Pashootan Vaezipoor

entry.summary: This paper proposes deriving property-based testing invariants from natural-language specifications (e.g., product requirements) rather than from the implementation alone, for agentic coding workflows. The goal is to catch characteristic failure patterns of AI-generated code by checking specifications against generated inputs.

entry.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup

author.name: Duc-Cuong Dang, Roman Kalkreuth, Andre Opris

entry.summary: This paper provides the first rigorous runtime analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming (CGP), proving that the (1+1) CGP with common mutation operators evolves an equivalent program on the Max problem with an expected exponential speedup over Tree-based GP, whose runtime was previously shown superlinear in the optimal program length.

entry.title: Trained on What Screen Readers Cannot Read: Accessibility Debt in the GUI Corpora Behind Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Obada Kraishan, Kulsawasd Jitkajornwanich

entry.summary: The paper measures content-description coverage in two Android GUI corpora used for computer-use agents, finding only 17.74% of elements needing descriptions in Rico (2017) carry one versus 57.27% in AndroidControl (2024), a 39.5-point gap robust across coding rules and app resampling. Because agents train on the same accessibility trees screen readers consume, they inherit accessibility debt.

entry.title: SMIC: Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning across Transformer Layers for Natural Language Inference

author.name: Xin Zhang, Victor S. Sheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces SMIC, a conditioning mechanism that builds a single input-dependent multiscale reference reused across Transformer layers, with each layer applying its own multiscale transformation before the attention update. The authors instantiate it in a token-context Transformer (TCT-SMIC) and report the highest ten-seed mean accuracy across all three ANLI rounds against decoder and MLP baselines, supported by ablations. It matters because it offers a targeted architectural improvement for robustness against localized lexical perturbations in NLI.

entry.title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates

author.name: Yingqi Hu, Nan Deng, Changxiao Shao, Xiaozhou He

entry.summary: Introduces SUMNO, a multigrid neural operator for fluid flow surrogates that goes beyond multi-resolution topology by aligning network components with geometric multigrid principles. It targets more accurate prediction of complex flows where no existing U-shaped architecture dominates.

entry.title: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication

author.name: Oleg Zendel, Kun Ran, Chenglong Ma, Nguyen Khoi Vo, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Describes the RMIT-ADM+S team's TREC 2026 RAG track system using seven research-agent runs on the ClimbMix corpus with both proprietary OpenAI and open-weight models. Ablations identified writer selection and adjacent-chunk expansion as key quality factors; six of seven runs exceeded the track median and the best run tied the track maximum (0.892) for Batch-1 vital coverage.

entry.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Gabriel Manalu, Minh Son Hoang, Hyeontaek Hwang, Jaesung Lee, Hyojin Choi, Tran Tuan Phong, Seon Kwon Kim, Saad Wazir, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: DashBench is a benchmark of 1,709 curated driving videos spanning collision-related and other safety-critical corner cases, testing 25 Video LLMs on understanding rare events that existing benchmarks miss, which focus on routine traffic. It aims to provide interpretable scene description and decision-making evaluation for autonomous driving.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Verification in Dafny

author.name: Wieger Wesselink, Kees Huizing, Huub van de Wetering

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic ten-step workflow for LLM-assisted formal verification of scientific algorithms using the Dafny verification system, integrating algorithm formalization, contract development, empirical validation, and the iterative process of building specifications, invariants, and proofs while diagnosing solver failures.

entry.title: AURA 2.0: From User-Driven Responses to Model-Initiated Conversations in Streaming Video

author.name: Shuhan Li, Huankang Guan, Xintong Guo, Yang Bo, Yuyang He, Dunyuan Xu, Jingyan Chen, Fang Liu, Tsz Kin Wan, Jinpeng Chen, Zhenqi He, Yuxuan Hu, Wenbo Li, Han Gao, Qijun Li, Long Chen, Hongsheng Li, Rui Liu

entry.summary: AURA 2.0 is a streaming video LLM that can proactively initiate conversation at appropriate moments in a live video stream without a user query, alongside stream-aware tool calling and interactive visual grounding. This shifts the interaction paradigm from purely reactive assistants to model-initiated conversation.

entry.title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon

author.name: Haozhe Wang, Lina Chen, Fanqi Wan, Qi Han, Yinmin Zhang, Zheng Ge, Daxin Jiang, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Metal Sandbox provides infrastructure for training and evaluating LLM agents that generate Apple Metal GPU kernels, combining restricted per-instance file access, native command execution, and command-level scheduling across interconnected Macs. Parallel commands run concurrently while serial ones share execution slots, with migration of waiting commands to available nodes, reducing GPU idle time during rollouts.

entry.title: Beyond Row-Level Prediction: Evaluating and Learning Composition for Reusable Table Representations

author.name: Ali Younes, Saeed Ghoorchian, Maximilian Schambach, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Johannes H\"ohne

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark evaluating table-level embeddings against four desiderata including consistency under partial views, discriminability across label granularities, robustness, and efficiency. It evaluates twelve methods on synthetic and real corpora, arguing that row-level prediction is an inadequate proxy for table embedding quality.

entry.title: PhysXAI: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Physical Hallucinations in Weather Foundation Models

author.name: Anjan Mahapatra, Nikhil Raj

entry.summary: Defines physical hallucinations, weather forecast states violating conservation laws or balance relations, and proposes PhysXAI, a learnable diagnostic framework that detects, localizes, and attributes such inconsistencies while decoupling forecast error from physical plausibility. It uses a joint condition on numerical and physical residuals with a multi-branch encoder.

entry.title: Winter wheat improves soil carbon sequestration with reduced gains in warmer climates

author.name: Georgios Giannarakis, Vasileios Sitokonstantinou, Dimitrios Bormpoudakis, Ilias Tsoumas, Nikiforos Samarinas, Gustau Camps-Valls, Charalampos Kontoes

entry.summary: Applies causal machine learning to a five-year nationwide Lithuanian dataset to estimate how winter wheat-based crop rotations affect field-level soil organic carbon. Results show winter wheat generally improves SOC sequestration but with climate-dependent effect heterogeneity, with smaller gains in warmer regions.

entry.title: Learning Rate Transfer and Feature Learning Across Depth for Constrained Spectral Optimizers: Complete Scion

author.name: Eline Pot, Laurent Lefebvre, Mathieu Segond, Antonio Silveti-Falls

entry.summary: This paper extends the CompleteP framework's 1/L residual scaling rule for depth-wise learning rate transfer from Adam-family optimizers to constrained optimization methods, specifically Frank-Wolfe and projected non-Euclidean normalized steepest descent, where updates are governed by linear minimization oracles. The authors derive scaling rules confirming that the same 1/L residual scaling applies, though the proofs require different arguments. This widens the practical toolkit for calibrating hyperparameters on shallow networks and transferring them to deeper architectures.

entry.title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement

author.name: Mohammad Malekpouri, Somayeh Lotfi

entry.summary: Critically examines whether conformal selection can genuinely certify CRISPR guide-design decisions, showing the arithmetic constraint that calibration cohorts must far exceed available validated data (e.g., 20,000 needed vs 10 available), leaving the certified set empty in over 96 percent of practical cases. Also flags benchmark leakage and free-baseline issues.

entry.title: Beyond Reweighting: Certified Improvements from New Transitions in Discrete MCMC

author.name: Yishan Xi, Tinglan Wang

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops a framework for transition-support design in discrete Markov chain Monte Carlo, deriving necessary and sufficient dual conditions under which adding new transitions strictly reduces asymptotic variance. It provides computable primal-dual certificates and constructs examples where a single added edge yields polynomial-factor improvements in integrated autocorrelation time.

entry.title: Does Deep Knowledge Tracing Learn Semantic Relations Between Knowledge Components?

author.name: Kia Karbasi, Mahdi Saiedi, Kevin Hong, Gregory Pottie

entry.summary: The paper asks whether relation graphs learned by Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) are semantic, testing DKT-derived KC relations against text-derived semantic embeddings across nine representation pipelines. Across datasets and embedding models, the structures align only weakly, suggesting DKT's cross-KC effects are not meaningfully semantic.

entry.title: Capacity-Constrained Delayed Feedback for Online Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Bowen Wang, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The paper develops CA-OCRC, extending online conformal risk control to settings where feedback is delayed and limited tracking capacity causes some feedback to be lost. It jointly optimizes the allocation of tracking capacity and prediction-set construction via a randomized tracking policy while preserving long-term risk guarantees.

entry.title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data

author.name: Fateme Golivand Darvishvand, Saurabh Mathur, Nikhilesh Prabhakar, Michael A. Skinner, Ameet Soni, Neel Shah, Ethan L Sanford, Lakshmi Raman, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: FQI-SC is an offline RL framework for pediatric ECMO management that improves cautiously on clinician behavior by optimizing only over empirically supported state-action pairs and defaulting to the clinician baseline in low-data regions. It is evaluated on 78 pediatric trajectories totaling over 6,000 hours of clinical data using FQE and expert review.

entry.title: Linking Rapid Learning to Compositional Structure in Neural Networks: Evidence from Additive Analogies in Meta-Learned Parameter Spaces

author.name: Abigail L. Tenenbaum, R. Thomas McCoy

entry.summary: The paper investigates why meta-learned networks learn new functions rapidly, finding additive, word-embedding-like structure among learned parameters analogous to classic king-man+woman vector arithmetic. This links compositional parameter-space structure to fast adaptation.

entry.title: Learning Nonlinear Transient Dynamics in Fluid Flow Networks with the Neural Basis Method

author.name: Aijaz Nazir, Yuhe Wang, S. K. Rasel, Min Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops a neural basis method based on a representation-then-projection principle for fluid flow networks, avoiding the ill-conditioning and weak error guarantees of penalty-loss physics-informed approaches on hyperbolic systems. It enables rapid many-query evaluation across pipeline and biological flow network parameters.

entry.title: Supervision-Aware Evaluation of MedGemma for Reference-Assisted Radiotherapy Contour Ranking

author.name: Jaden Moon, Caiwen Jiang, Songlin Zhao, Wei Liu

entry.summary: This study evaluates frozen MedGemma 1.5 for ranking radiotherapy contours in a supervision-aware design across HaN-Seg and SegRap2023 data, showing that supervised readouts of internal prompt states substantially outperform readouts of yes/no output probabilities. The work carefully separates gains attributable to supervision from those of the underlying VLM representation.

entry.title: Taming Neural Fields with a Frequency-Lipschitz Curriculum for Sparse-View CT Reconstruction

author.name: Songtao Hu, Jingrui Wu, Hong Ding, Fanhao Zhu, Yunhao Liu, Suyang Xi

entry.summary: FLIC introduces a capacity-controlled implicit neural representation framework for sparse-view CT reconstruction that jointly schedules frequency content and Lipschitz constraints, making when high-frequency capacity is exposed explicit and controllable. This prevents fitting streak artifacts and hallucinated structures in the under-determined inverse problem.

entry.title: ATune: Unsupervised Photo Retouching Through Image-Editor Controls

author.name: Divyanshu Goyal, Gabriel Ruiz, Amir Meisami

entry.summary: ATune learns photo retouching without expert-annotated pairs by artificially degrading millions of unretouched stock photographs, then training a model to predict target values for 13 measurable attributes like brightness, contrast, and sharpness. The declarative, editor-control-based edit representation makes the model's outputs interpretable and compatible with standard photo editors.

entry.title: Machine Learning for Scalable Multi-AP Coordination in IEEE 802.11bn Networks

author.name: Maksymilian Wojnar, Szymon Szott

entry.summary: The authors develop a stack of ML methods for multi-access-point coordination in the IEEE 802.11bn Wi-Fi standard, progressing from lightweight hierarchical multi-armed bandits to a generative pipeline combining graph neural networks and flow matching. Evaluated in simulation and on a hardware testbed, the methods improve throughput over legacy access and scale coordination to dozens of APs.

entry.title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks

author.name: Ashvin Gupta, Brendan Delaney, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: The paper proposes tEHR, an approach that represents electronic health record events as natural language descriptions and applies continued pretraining plus LoRA fine-tuning on a causal language model used as a longitudinal patient encoder. It evaluates this against standard structured EHR pipelines across multiple prediction tasks.

entry.title: Is Jev a Good Multilingual Judge?

author.name: Wei Liu, Yi Fan, Xiyan Fu

entry.summary: The paper evaluates the Jev model as a multilingual LLM judge against generative judges on four benchmarks covering up to 47 language varieties and three evaluation formats. Jev is competitive at roughly 1/31 to 1/61 of the cost of GPT-6.1, an existing flagship model, but lags on knowledge-intensive answer verification and is weaker on low-resource languages.

entry.title: ChJGBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chinese Legal Judgment Generation with Diagnostic Evaluation

author.name: Yinghao Hu, Linggang Kong, Qian Xiao, Yuting Huang, Yunlong Zhang, Yujie Zhang, Yiquan Wu, Fei Duan, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Kun Kuang, Fei Wu

entry.summary: Introduces ChJGBench, a benchmark for generating reasoning and dispositive sections of Chinese judgments across civil, criminal, and administrative cases, built from 3,462 real judgments with a case-type-aware diagnostic framework of 13 metric types. It addresses the gap left by benchmarks focusing on isolated legal tasks.

entry.title: We Are What We Remember: Mental-State-Driven Memory for Long-Term Character Dialogue

author.name: Zhicheng Jia, Shuchen Wu, Zhuoshi Tong, Haisen Liao, Sicheng Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes MindMem, a mental-state-driven memory framework for long-term character dialogue inspired by cognitive psychology's Self-Memory System, which consolidates shared experiences into source-linked mental states of characters, users, and their relationship. A mental-state reasoner contextualizes these states to anticipate user needs and proactively retrieve relationally pivotal experiences rather than relying on passive similarity.

entry.title: Beyond Word Error Rate: A Failure Taxonomy of Streaming Dictation ASR

author.name: Harras Mansoor, Muhammad Wisal, Hassan Bhatti, Masood Shakir

entry.summary: Argues that word error rate on cleaned transcripts misrepresents dictation quality and introduces a four-level error taxonomy (recognition, output formatting, language handling, audio dropped before processing) for streaming dictation across eleven ASR systems and 106 scripted English dictations plus multilingual sets. The taxonomy captures errors users actually have to fix.

entry.title: Disentangling Spurious Correlations: How IRM Handles Diverse Shortcuts in Text Classification

author.name: Paul Grunenwald, Beno\^it Crabb\'e, Guillaume Wisniewski, Pirmin Lemberger

entry.summary: Evaluates Invariant Risk Minimization under three shortcut-generating mechanisms (label-generated features, confounding, selection bias) in text classification using a causality-driven framework. IRM successfully rejects shortcuts across causal and anti-causal structures, even with limited environmental variation.

entry.title: FreeDeshadow: Shadow Removal for User-Specified Objects With Multimodal Prompts

author.name: Zhiliang Wu, Jihao Gu, Kun Li, Hanyu Xuan, Hehe Fan, Meng Wang, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: Introduces object-aware controllable shadow removal, where a user specifies a target object via a prompt and only that object's cast shadow is removed while other content is preserved, addressing object-shadow asymmetry with a unified controllable framework using multimodal prompts.

entry.title: Lines Are Ideas: Visual Creativity Assessment in Hyperbolic Space

author.name: Baoliang Chen, Zihao Lin, Hao Liu, Xiangjie Sui

entry.summary: The authors recast drawing-based creativity assessment as structured semantic deviation between paired sketches, decomposing it into novelty (geodesic distance in hyperbolic space) and appropriateness, aligned with psychological theory. This hyperbolic formulation avoids costly expert annotation and captures creativity's structure better than single regression targets. It offers a scalable automated alternative for evaluating human creative ability.

entry.title: Toward Cross-Rubric Surgical Skill Assessment via Joint Embedding Prediction

author.name: Jiajun Cheng, Haidar M. Abdul-Muhsin, Juha Choi, Shan Lin

entry.summary: This paper proposes Predictive Rubric Alignment (PRA), a joint embedding prediction method for AI-assisted surgical skill assessment that scores surgical videos using natural-language descriptions of skill levels. Instead of predicting probabilities over fixed rubric levels, PRA predicts a rater-weighted combination of skill-level description embeddings, enabling transfer across semantically equivalent but differently worded assessment rubrics. It matters because automated surgical feedback could reduce the labor-intensive expert review needed for surgical training.

entry.title: WaveletLoRA: Frequency-Aware Content-Style Decomposition for Personalized Image Generation

author.name: Peiyao Wang, Jiahui Sun, Weining Wang, Jing Liu

entry.summary: WaveletLoRA performs content-style decomposition from a single image using wavelet-domain supervision: a multi-level discrete wavelet transform splits the reference into subbands, and dedicated LoRA branches handle low-frequency content and high-frequency style. This explicitly exploits frequency characteristics that spatial-domain methods ignore, enabling flexible recomposition in personalized generation. The approach adds parameter-efficient, interpretable control to diffusion personalization.

entry.title: FlowIR: Depth-driven Rectified Flow for Resolving Thermal Ambiguity in Infrared Super-Resolution

author.name: Xingyue Zhu, Qinyun Mei, Zhexi Min, Yang Zou, Xingyuan Li, Zhiying Jiang, Jinyuan Liu

entry.summary: FlowIR resolves ambiguity in infrared super-resolution by injecting pseudo-3D depth cues into a rectified flow framework, using depth-guided 3D convolutions to disentangle overlapping heat sources and cluster-wise inter-attention to prevent cross-source feature contamination. A thermal-geometry consistency loss enforces physically plausible restoration, avoiding hallucinated structures from ambiguous 2D evidence.

entry.title: RICapBench: A Fine-Grained Visual Understanding Benchmark Dataset for Vision-Language Models in Remote Sensing

author.name: Xue Wang, Yubin Xu, Kun Tan

entry.summary: RICapBench is a dataset and benchmark unifying instance localization and captioning for remote sensing imagery, testing end-to-end fine-grained understanding without target-specific textual cues across challenges of object scale variation, geospatial relations, and limited visual detail. It aims to expose ungrounded descriptions from current VLMs.

entry.title: Context-Predictive Low-Rank Adaptation for Face Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Aminu Yusuf, Shakeel Muhammad Ibrahim, Sulaimon Oyeniyi Adebayo, Muhammad Sohail Ibrahim, Muhammad Shahid Jabbar, Shujaat Khan

entry.summary: CP-JEPA adapts a pretrained CLIP image encoder for face presentation attack detection by combining low-rank tuning with a joint-embedding predictive objective in which a student predicts teacher features at masked spatial locations. Additional masked and unmasked classification losses keep the representation tied to anti-spoofing decisions under partial observation.

entry.title: EG360: Efficient and Generalizable $360^\circ$ Depth Estimation via Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation and Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion

author.name: Laiyan Ding, Chongxi Meng, Rui Huang

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces EG360, a lightweight panorama depth estimation model that aims to combine the zero-shot generalization of large pretrained models with the real-time efficiency needed for embedded platforms. It proposes an Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation (APPD) strategy guided by scene geometry, plus spherical cross-level feature fusion, to close the gap between heavyweight generalist models and efficient single-domain models.

entry.title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes

author.name: Robert Fonod, Nikolas Geroliminis

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode in drone video stabilization where moving objects supply mutually consistent correspondences that corrupt homography estimation, a phenomenon called consensus capture that inlier statistics cannot flag. The paper provides a two-part benchmark with static and dynamic protocols scoring ten registration pipelines on 4K urban aerial frames.

entry.title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion

author.name: Dimitrios Chatziparaschis, Georgios Georgakis, Adnan I. Ansar, Shehryar Khattak, Konstantinos Karydis

entry.summary: Presents EM-ViT, a monocular depth model that adapts affine-invariant relative depth from a foundation model prior to metric scale using online observations from robot ego-motion. It targets safe robotic operation in novel, unstructured environments while replacing expensive LiDAR or stereo hardware.

entry.title: A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule

author.name: Wei-Chang Yeh

entry.summary: This theoretical work models the simplified swarm optimization update rule as a finite Markov chain, deriving an explicit stationary distribution, an exact convergence rate of c_w^t, and geometric hitting-time bounds for the elitist chain. It also proves exponential lower bounds on expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum and polynomial generation counts on OneMax and LeadingOnes under specified parameter regimes. The paper provides rigorous foundations for a widely used but under-analyzed swarm algorithm.

entry.title: Can I join you? Extended Social Force Based Model with Predictive Control and Barrier Functions for Humanoid Group Repositioning Amidst Obstacles

author.name: Chuxuan Zhang, Niloofar Jahanshahi, Yasaman Etesam, Mo Chen, Angelica Lim

entry.summary: The paper extends social force models with model predictive control and control barrier functions so humanoid robots can socially appropriately reposition group formations when agents join, leave, or pass through, even amidst obstacles. Prior social-force work largely ignored obstacle handling and safety in humanoid group reconfiguration. This addresses a real gap for service robots operating in shared public spaces, combining safety guarantees with social conventions.

entry.title: Helping Hand: A Continuum Robotic Grasper for Traction in Single-Channel Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection

author.name: Bendavid Maimon, Thompson Wong, Aedan Mangan, Sukjun Kim, Michael C. Yip, Tania K. Morimoto

entry.summary: Helping Hand is a two-segment continuum robotic grasper that fits through a single 3.7 mm endoscopic working channel and enables tissue traction alongside an electrosurgical knife via a slotted base design, addressing a key barrier to adoption of endoscopic submucosal dissection. The paper evaluates workspace and traction forces from the device. This is a clinically motivated surgical robotics contribution that could broaden adoption of a minimally invasive procedure.

entry.title: PERA: Plug-in Experts for Robotic Actions in Continual Whole-Body Control

author.name: Shangchao Hu, Yadan Sun, Xibo Yu, Wei Huang

entry.summary: PERA enables humanoid robots to acquire new whole-body skills without forgetting by freezing a pretrained mixture-of-experts policy and training small added task experts with routing scores, using task rewards or teacher-action supervision. Each new task module adds roughly 1.03% of the base actor's parameters, and on a Unitree G1 simulation setup the method completes ten new tasks while disabling the expert restores prior behavior. It is a clean continual-learning solution for humanoid control.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Parallel Policy Learning for Collapse-Reactive Retreat via Hybrid Terrain Modeling

author.name: Yuki Kadokawa, Ritsuki Matsunaga, Yuqi Yang, Edgar Anarossi, Takamitsu Matsubara

entry.summary: The paper tackles massively parallel RL for robots that must retreat when terrain collapses, where a shared collapsing terrain induces indirect interference between parallel agents. Rather than duplicating expensive rigid-body terrain, the authors replace full collapse modeling with learned collapse-induced contact responses, enabling memory-efficient parallel sampling. This is a clever domain-specific simplification for training safety-critical locomotion policies.

entry.title: Non-normal Limits and Joint Calibration of Cross-fitted Heterogeneity Tests

author.name: Even He, Zaizai Yan

entry.summary: The paper shows that the standard normal-calibrated test for treatment-effect heterogeneity based on cross-fitted rankings is invalid because dependence among folds changes the shape of the null distribution, not just its variance. The authors characterize the actual limits (bimodal or skewed) and propose jointly calibrated alternatives.

entry.title: Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher

author.name: Felipe de Jes\'us F\'elix-Arredondo, Nezih Nieto-Guti\'errez, Carlos Astengo-Noguez, Alejandro Ucan-Puc

entry.summary: The paper observes that a discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network with a fixed linear memory and three weights mapping one-to-one to PID gains, and shows that training it on a one-step physical cost with no demonstrations reduces to a strongly convex least-squares problem whose unique optimum recovers one-step optimal PID gains.

entry.title: AI #194: Spy Versus Guy

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI news roundup covering three lead stories: the release of Claude Fable 5.2, the Jensen Huang affair story, and the METR report on AI R&D acceleration, plus a note that GPT-6 Astra underperforms on safety research tasks. It aggregates commentary across utility, security, media generation, policy, and industry news.

entry.title: How to evaluate AI R&D acceleration without transparency

author.name: Edimah

entry.summary: A LessWrong newcomer to AI safety reflects on METR's November 5 assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, which estimated a highly uncertain 1.9x acceleration rate. The post argues that because Anthropic redacted most of the informative evidence before public release, the report's credibility rests on trust in METR, and proposes publicly detailing evaluation methodology and assessor reasoning as a credibility-enhancing alternative.

entry.title: Prior-as-Skill: Remember Outside and Read Inside with On-Policy Self-Distillation for Self-Evolving VLM Agents

author.name: Yan Lin, Jingyu Sun, Yifei Qian, Zhengtao Yao, Yuxia Wang, Daizong Liu, Chun Pong Lau, Zhongliang Guo, Stephen McGough

entry.summary: PriorSplit addresses fragility in self-evolving vision-language agents whose learned skills are stored as keyframes with step notes: when frames go missing or steps are reordered at deployment, internalized models guess or let stored order override observations. It keeps the task order as an external prior and fills in missing frames via on-policy self-distillation, improving robustness.

entry.title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests

author.name: Vahid Haratian, Atakan Akar, Eray T\"uz\"un

entry.summary: ADAPT uses an autonomous coding agent to generate change-focused regression tests for pull requests, aiming to guard the behavior a PR introduces rather than optimizing whole-unit code coverage. The agent analyzes the PR diff and produces targeted tests, addressing the common failure of developers submitting PRs without behavior-specific tests.

entry.title: Closing the Loop: Co-Evolving EM for Irregular Time Series Generation in Lifted Representations

author.name: Idan Arbiv, Gal Fadlon, Omri Azencot

entry.summary: The paper shows that the standard one-shot imputation pipeline for generating regular time series from irregular data is structurally flawed, since imputations go stale as the generator evolves. It introduces a co-evolving Monte Carlo EM framework where E-steps sample missing values from the current generator's posterior and M-steps retrain the generator, preserving unconditional generation quality.

entry.title: AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields

author.name: Zhenyu Zou, Junjue Liao, Hao Yang, Luowei Yin, Chenyu Wang, Yufeng Wei, Zhichao Peng, Chun Chen, Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Kangxin Liu, Haoran Guan, Rubing Han, Yipei Chen, Peiting You, Yuwei Fan

entry.summary: Systematically compares five surrogate architectures (Coordinate MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, FNO, Transolver) for predicting plasma fields in capacitively coupled plasma simulations, measuring how many reference simulations are needed to reach 1-2 percent relative error. FNO achieves the lowest or joint-lowest data requirement in seven of eight comparisons.

entry.title: Sparse PCA with Overlapping Supports: NP-Hardness and an FPTAS

author.name: Alberto Del Pia, Dekun Zhou

entry.summary: This work studies sparse PCA with multiple components having arbitrary support overlaps and individual sparsity constants, proving the general problem NP-hard and giving the first FPTAS for fixed-rank covariance matrices. It closes a gap between previously solved disjoint-support and common-support cases.

entry.title: Characterizing the Edge of Stability in Variational Training Without Priors

author.name: Juraj Marusic, Jonathan Wenger, Beau Coker, John P. Cunningham

entry.summary: The paper extends edge-of-stability analysis to variational deep learning trained without explicit priors, relying instead on optimizer implicit regularization, and characterizes how key optimization hyperparameters behave in this regime. This addresses the practical challenge of prior elicitation in variational methods for uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Credal Wrapper for Uncertainty Modelling in Sparse Geological Data

author.name: David Jeevankumar, Maryam Sultana, Alexander D. Rast, Fabio Cuzzolin

entry.summary: For mineral exploration models trained on sparse samples, the paper contributes a simulation protocol making epistemic uncertainty directly computable and gradeable, disentangling reducible error from estimator spread with an oracle reference. It proposes a credal (imprecise probability) wrapper for uncertainty modelling in prospectivity mapping.

entry.title: Federated Class Incremental Learning: A Pseudo Feature Based Approach Without Exemplars

author.name: Min Kyoon Yoo, Yu Rang Park

entry.summary: FCLPF mitigates catastrophic forgetting in federated class-incremental learning by generating pseudo features from prototypes instead of storing past data or using GANs, reducing communication costs. On CIFAR-100 it achieves 51.87% average accuracy and 9.62% forgetting, outperforming baselines at 47.72% accuracy.

entry.title: CoLFA: Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yufei Luo, Yuchen Ling, Chunrong Fang

entry.summary: CoLFA is a method for failure attribution in multi-agent LLM systems that exploits records of how agent executions connect and pass content to organize attribution inputs, tracing the decisive error step and responsible agent at lower token cost. It tackles interleaved steps and cluttered content that make naive attribution expensive.

entry.title: RECALL: Real-Time Recalibration of Multi-Camera Rigs via Learned OEM-Anchored Residuals

author.name: Mario Alberto Tapia de la Cruz, Charalambos Poullis

entry.summary: Presents a feed-forward method that recalibrates a movable multi-camera rig in a single pass, predicting per-camera intrinsics and extrinsics as a shared global rig rotation plus small per-camera drift, anchored on the nominal OEM calibration and a brief observation of a known object, avoiding costly bundle adjustment.

entry.title: From Classification to Generation: Vision-Language Models for Roman Imperial Coin Description

author.name: Pedro Lourenco, Ognjen Arandjelovi\'c

entry.summary: Reformulates Roman Imperial coin cataloguing as image-to-text generation rather than classification over predefined labels, adapting an open-weight vision-language model to transcribe obverse and reverse legends and describe imagery, with training data built from approximately 30,000 structured auction records.

entry.title: Test-Time Selective Adaptation for Cross-Modal UAV Object Tracking with Token Shift

author.name: Yun Xiao, Hailong Ye, Zhicheng Zhao, Lei Liu, Amir Hussain

entry.summary: TSAT addresses cross-modal UAV object tracking by deriving spatial and temporal adaptation signals from unlabeled test sequences for online optimization, handling modality-switching appearance gaps and abrupt target-position shifts. A controllable token shift auxiliary task imposes explicit spatial correspondence between predefined token trajectories during test time. The method complements offline representation learning with localization-oriented online adaptation.

entry.title: CGOcc: Learning Cross-Gaussian Dependencies for 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Zirui Huang, Jiongle He, Yunfan Zeng, Yuanzhi Lu, Guangye Li, Boyan Tang, Weite SU, Pedro V. Sander, Amy Hui Zhang

entry.summary: CGOcc improves Gaussian-based 3D semantic occupancy prediction by explicitly modeling cross-Gaussian dependencies, since overlapping primitives give ambiguous class predictions that spatially weighted mixtures handle poorly. It refines Gaussian states with appearance and geometric observations and encodes dependencies in a diagonal-plus-low-rank representation integrated into voxel classification. This is a multi-camera supervised framework for autonomous-driving-style perception.

entry.title: MuViRL: Multimodal View-Invariant Visual Speech Representation Learning via Calibrated View Aggregation

author.name: Fei Su, Kai Qiu, Juan Liu

entry.summary: MuViRL is a self-supervised framework for visual speech representation learning that combines synchronized 3D Gaussian view synthesis with multimodal self-supervision and calibrated view aggregation, learning representations consistent across camera views despite varying visibility of articulation cues. It targets audio-visual speech understanding under view variation.

entry.title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning

author.name: Yike Qiao, Xiaodong He, An Zhuo, Zhiyong Sun, Weimin Bao, Zhongkui Li

entry.summary: DIVAL addresses the mismatch between a nonholonomic robot's initial heading and a nominal vector field by locally reshaping the field via a diffeomorphic deformation of the workspace, so the robot can follow the field immediately without transient collisions. The approach removes the two-stage design-then-track structure of conventional vector-field planners. This is a theoretically clean improvement to reactive motion planning for nonholonomic platforms.

entry.title: Input-output characterization of robotic grasping: Connecting design parameters to grasp behavior through the admittance

author.name: Julien Vanderheyden, Guillaume Drion, Pierre Sacr\'e, Fulvio Forni

entry.summary: The authors propose characterizing grasps dynamically via their admittance — a transfer matrix relating load perturbations to object displacement around equilibrium — rather than with static grasp metrics. Applied to a planar two-finger gripper under PD control, the analysis recovers stiffness and stability at zero frequency and captures natural frequencies and peak gain under time-varying loads. It shows grasps with identical position and contacts can behave very differently dynamically.

entry.title: Gradient Flows over Convex Bodies for Learning Optimal Regularizers

author.name: Nilava Metya, Oscar Leong, Yong Sheng Soh

entry.summary: The paper lays foundations for learning optimal convex regularizers for ill-posed inverse problems from prior data, defining optimality as minimizing expected gauge evaluation and developing gradient-flow dynamics over the space of convex bodies to describe the evolution of regularizer iterates.

entry.title: One Model, Two Precisions: Does Disagreement Between Quantized Copies Tell You When a Small Model Is Wrong?

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Allan Kevin T

entry.summary: This study tests whether disagreement between two precisions of the same model weights (an 8-bit answering copy and a lower-precision reader) serves as a per-question error signal for abstention and escalation, at the cost of one extra forward pass. The authors simulate round-to-nearest quantization on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B and score 8,398 multiple-choice questions from ARC, MMLU, and HellaSwag using AUROC, risk-coverage curves, and ECE. This is a training-free uncertainty estimation method for local models.

entry.title: TopoST: Topology-Conditioned Node Specialization for Urban Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models

author.name: Kaiyun Wei, Yue Xu, Wenying Duan, Zichen Xu, Shuai Ma, Xiaoxi He

entry.summary: Proposes TopoST for urban spatio-temporal foundation models, combining shared learning over local subgraphs with node specialization generated by a shared topology-to-parameter mapping. Using identity-independent topological representations, the approach makes specialization itself transferable across the 20+ urban datasets analyzed.

entry.title: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous

author.name: Xin Li

entry.summary: This paper critiques the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, showing that under the hard-whitening population objective, same-state positive pairs make the induced world kernel the identity, so every centered whitened state function is a global minimizer and the uniqueness claim is vacuous in the idealized same-state limit. Only one of the original paper's four quantitative results survives: a gap-free lower bound.

entry.title: PISim: A Unified Photonic Inference Simulator for Hardware-Aware Cross-Layer Design-Space Exploration

author.name: Andreas Falkenberg

entry.summary: Presents PISim, a unified simulator coupling pretrained neural network execution with physics-based models of six photonic accelerator architecture families, six electro-optic modulator technologies, and four optical source organizations, enabling cross-layer EDA design-space exploration before fabrication. It captures how electro-optical interfaces and physical non-idealities bound precision, throughput, and application accuracy.

entry.title: SAME: Semantic Watermark Embedding for Open-Source Large Pretrained Models

author.name: Xinyao Song, Jialiang Shen, Hui Kang, Huajie Chen, Ruiqi Liu, Jiyang Zheng, Huaxi Huang, Zhenliang Lu, Chris Russell, Runqi Lin

entry.summary: SAME introduces a watermarking scheme for open-source large pretrained models based on a semantically meaningful private vocabulary, enabling flexible composition of adaptive triggers that transfer across downstream tasks. It improves durability under benign fine-tuning compared with task-specific trigger-response watermark designs for IP protection.

entry.title: Imitating the Imperfect: Offline-to-Online Robust Imitation Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrators

author.name: Cheng Pan, Nan Lu, Kai Arulkumaran, Josie Hughes

entry.summary: The paper proposes LEOS-IL, a framework for imitation learning from heterogeneous demonstrators with unknown and varying expertise, jointly learning a latent expertise model and optimality scoring of demonstrations. It targets the realistic offline-to-online setting where mixed-quality data is the norm rather than near-optimal expert demonstrations.

entry.title: Improved last-iterate bounds for SGD with and without replacement

author.name: Yimin Zhong, Jiaxin Zhou

entry.summary: The paper improves last-iterate convergence bounds for SGD on convex beta-smooth losses in the interpolation regime from O((log T)^3/T) to O((log T)^3/(T log log T)), using a horizon-dependent multiscale gradient estimate. The bounds apply to both with-replacement and single-pass without-replacement sampling.

entry.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction

author.name: Minh Nghia Nguyen, Beate Paulus, Akhil S. Nair

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, from random sampling to various active learning approaches, across different model classes and representations. The goal is to maximize predictive performance while minimizing labeled examples, addressing over- and under-representation of chemical space in arbitrarily curated datasets.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust BEST-RQ For Speech Representation Learning

author.name: Muhammad Khan, Xiaodong Cui, Brian Kingsbury, George Saon

entry.summary: The paper proposes a distributionally robust extension of BEST-RQ self-supervised speech pretraining that formulates training as a group DRO problem over codebook-defined groups, adaptively reweighting groups instead of optimizing average loss. The goal is representations that are robust to the choice of quantization targets.

entry.title: Dynamic Block-Online Streaming ASR for Low-Resource Agglutinative Code-Switching Speech with Morphology-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Kazi Rafat, Afifa Imran, Md. Ismail Hossain, Md. Romzan Ali, Fuad Rahman, Sifat Momen, Shafin Rahman, Nabeel Mohammed

entry.summary: Presents the first comprehensive study of streaming ASR for intra-sentential Bangla-English code-switching, identifying a mismatch between strict causal streaming and long-range morphological dependencies. Introduces a Dynamic Block-Online framework with VAD-aligned inference and Script-Anchored Loanword Injection to address data scarcity.

entry.title: Similar but Not Redundant: Embedding-Gated Refinement for High-Granularity Topic Models

author.name: Daniel Denley, Robert L. Nicol, Mike J. Chantler

entry.summary: Argues that over-clustering in high-granularity topic modeling conflates genuine redundancy with semantically similar but distinct topics, and proposes EGIM, a hybrid that iteratively uses LLM-generated context with embedding-based gating to decide which topic merges are warranted. Existing embedding thresholding and LLM-guided merging alone are shown to be insufficient.

entry.title: From Seeing to Remembering: Brain-Informed Agentic Text-to-Video Generation for Enhancing Memorability

author.name: Shengqi Dang, Yi He, Jiaying Lei, Feilin Han, Nan Cao

entry.summary: MemCrafter is a brain-informed agentic framework that enhances text-to-video memorability through iterative prompt refinement guided by a cortical region-based neuro-memorability signal predicting video memorability from estimated neural responses. The signal serves both as an optimization objective and interpretive feedback within an agentic generation loop. It targets applications in advertising, education, and storytelling.

entry.title: Elastra: A Simulation Framework for Elastic Bodies

author.name: Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Xingyu Ren, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Elastra is a simulation framework for robot interaction with deformable elastic surfaces like mattresses and trampolines, using vertically moving elements with elastic connections and damping, validated against an independent implementation and real mattress load curves, and used to train Unitree robot control policies. Deformable-contact simulation is a known pain point for legged robots and physical human-robot environments. It enables training and evaluation where conventional rigid-body simulators fail.

entry.title: BiPOP: Partial-Order Planning for Long-Horizon Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Kun Chu, Xufeng Zhao, Jan-Gerrit Habekost, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: BiPOP is a framework that combines LLMs with temporal logic-style partial-order planning to coordinate two robot arms over long-horizon bimanual tasks. It decomposes behavior into reusable unimanual skills plus a small set of synchronous bimanual skills, treating spatio-temporal coordination as the main bottleneck rather than skill acquisition itself. This matters because bimanual coordination under coupled spatial and temporal constraints remains a core unsolved problem for general-purpose manipulation.

entry.title: BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: BWM Team

entry.summary: BWM-Forge is a code-driven framework for controllable robot video generation: given robot assets and a task description, a coding agent constructs editable Blender scene programs specifying objects, robot motion, and cameras, whose proxy videos provide structural and motion references for a video generation model that adds visual detail, coordinated by a multi-agent harness. This gives explicit control over scene geometry, motion, and viewpoints that end-to-end video generation lacks, supporting targeted edits and reuse for robotics data generation.

entry.title: Between Niti and Nyaya: A Society-Centered Framework for AI Governance

author.name: Snehalkumar `Neil' S. Gaikwad, Punya Aragula, Shiva Kruthi Palpanoori, Pratik Patekar

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Society-Centered AI Governance Framework that evaluates AI policy instruments across jurisdictions by whether an individual can receive notice that AI influenced an outcome, challenge the decision, and see it corrected. It reads instruments together by date and binding status and separates agency duties from individual rights. The framework offers shared vocabulary for assessing governance while policy is still forming.

entry.title: DIAGNO: Diagonal Spherical Neural Operators for Heterogeneous Earth Dynamics Modeling

author.name: Herui Li, Bin Lu, Haonan Qi, Lei Zhou, Luoyi Fu, Xinbing Wang, Meng Jin

entry.summary: DIAGNO proposes Diagonal Spherical Neural Operators that drop the rotation-equivariance assumption used in existing Spherical Neural Operators for Earth systems forecasting, treating the Earth as heterogeneous rather than homogeneous. By relaxing this assumption, the operator captures richer spectral dynamics while retaining spherical geometry benefits. This targets a real modeling gap in geophysics-oriented machine learning.

entry.title: Time and Space: A Dual-Axis, Evidence-Grounded Context Substrate for Personal Agents

author.name: Haitao Cheng, Jerry Hu, Longdong Mao, Dong Huang, Dongming Li, Lijuan Zhang, Mengting Zhang

entry.summary: The authors argue that the binding constraint for personal agents is not model capacity but context representation: agents fail to know which entity a phrase denotes, when a fact held, or which source record licenses a claim. They formalize spatio-temporal context (STC) on two axes, temporal (event time, validity intervals, ingestion time) and spatial (a relational entity space with semantic distance), with every relation anchored to immutable source records and every answer closed over those records. Six invariants define the substrate.

entry.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification

author.name: Maryam Ostadsharif Memar, Behzad Nazari

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-branch architecture combining an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification from scalp EEG. The graph branch groups 61 electrodes into anatomically informed regions, providing interpretable representations of brain regions emphasized by the model, evaluated with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner dataset.

entry.title: Acoustic Respiratory Phase Detection on Mobile Devices

author.name: Julian Szymanski, Tomasz Sankowski, Piotr Sulewski, Iwo Czartowski, Javier Medina Quero

entry.summary: The paper presents a non-invasive framework for respiratory phase detection from acoustic signals recorded on commodity smartphones, using a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture combining local spectral features with long-range temporal modeling. Evaluated with leave-one-subject-out on the Foundation Dataset and an independent test set of over 1300 breathing cycles, the 3-class formulation achieves around 72.8 percent accuracy.

entry.title: Gaussian processes for real-time urban traffic estimation using a fleet of drones

author.name: Batuhan Avci, Marko Susnjar, Marko Maljkovic, Nikolas Geroliminis

entry.summary: A spatio-temporal Gaussian process framework reconstructing network-wide urban traffic states from partial aerial observations by drone fleets, using a graph Matern kernel embedding road-network topology into spatial covariance and an exponential temporal kernel, with historical loop-detector data used for calibration. It targets real-time monitoring beyond what static sensors can cover.

entry.title: Evaluating AI Musical Creativity: Towards a Quantitative Multi-Dimensional Framework Based on Value, Novelty, and Surprise

author.name: Hindy Rossignol, Giorgio Franceschelli, Mirco Musolesi

entry.summary: Proposes a quantitative framework for evaluating AI-generated musical creativity, operationalizing Margaret Boden's value, novelty, and surprise dimensions into domain-specific metrics. The work aims to bring more objectivity to an underexplored evaluation area as generative music models grow more sophisticated.

entry.title: Outcome Over Learning? Evidence from Student Use of AI Code Assistants for Unit Test Writing

author.name: Daniel Hinbest, Jeremy S. Bradbury, Michael A. Miljanovic

entry.summary: A user study of students with unrestricted access to AI code assistants for unit test writing found most students adopted one-shot interaction, requesting complete solutions directly rather than iterating or critically evaluating AI output. This shifts focus from learning the skill to completing the task, with implications for computing education design.

entry.title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production Planning via Multi-Modal Transformer Sales Forecasting

author.name: Ge Fan, Kai Wang, Chaoyun Zhang, Yingjie Li, Yuze Liu, Junyang Chen

entry.summary: Presents SkinAdvisor, a decision framework for planning production of cosmetic in-game skins, powered by SkinCast, a deployed multi-modal Transformer forecasting 180-day daily sales trajectories for unreleased skins. SkinCast fuses a pretrained Informer time-series encoder, a player-hero-skin graph embedder, and attribute and release-context Transformers.

entry.title: "I don't know what I don't know": Exploring the Benefits and Challenges of AI in Interdisciplinary Research

author.name: Indu Panigrahi, Tal August

entry.summary: A survey (N=62) and interview study (N=23) of interdisciplinary researchers examining how AI affects workflows spanning unfamiliar disciplines. Participants saw AI as both a remedy for and an amplifier of unknown unknowns—enabling broad awareness of new fields while also creating an illusion of understanding.

entry.title: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Using V-JEPA Features

author.name: Anwar Shamim, Jeffrin Sam

entry.summary: Studies supervised RGB-only multi-view 3D reconstruction built on video-pretrained V-JEPA features, combining camera estimation, scene aggregation, epipolar transport, and residual pointmaps. Experiments on CO3D show spatial-camera regression cuts trajectory error 29.3% versus global-camera regression, yet both underperform simpler baselines like identity poses in some metrics.

entry.title: Dual Representation Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling

author.name: Yunyi Zhao, Wei Zhang, Cheng Xiang, Vadakkepat Prahlad, Zuming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes DredRL, a reinforcement learning scheduler for flexible job-shop scheduling that builds dual representations of operations and machines via self- and cross-attention and uses a diffusion model as the policy network to generate scheduling decisions. The aim is to maintain performance as problem scale and processing-time uncertainty grow.

entry.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories

author.name: Daniel Ogenrwot, Jorge Gonzalo Delgado Cervantes, Woojoong Kim, John Businge

entry.summary: Presents GHAgentCI, a dataset of 15K+ GitHub Actions workflow histories from 6K+ mined repositories, comprising 159K+ revisions and 205K+ agent-evidence records linked to workflow triggers and execution constraints. An open-source extractor, cai-miner, detects coding-agent integrations with high manually validated precision, enabling study of how agents are actually deployed in CI.

entry.title: Contour-Assisted Evolutionary Computation: Estimating Peaks From the Contour Lines of Evaluated Solutions

author.name: Jun Zhang, Tong Qian, Hua Ding, Zhi-Hui Zhan, Wei-Jie Yu, Jian-Yu Li

entry.summary: This paper treats evaluated solutions in evolutionary algorithms as spot heights of a topographic survey, drawing contour maps to decompose the search region into peaks using contour trees with persistence and interpolated hill climbing. A memory of explored peaks, extrapolated via an area law, directs the search toward new regions.

entry.title: What Roles Do System Prompts Really Assign? Validating and Steering Occupational Role Vectors in LLMs

author.name: Jose L. Sampedro Mazon, Ilmi Yoon, Nadim Saad
