entry.summary: The paper introduces a framework for extracting and injecting occupational role vectors, activation-level directions capturing how a person in a given role would respond, validated on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The vectors are shown to be reproducible across runs and temperatures, separable even for similar roles, and usable for steering.

entry.title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions

author.name: Yinghao Zhang, Yalin Liu, Hong-Ning Dai, Yan Zhang, Qubeijian Wang, Bishenghui Tao, Yaohan Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes an agent-aided drone scheduling system for time-critical wilderness victim search, where an LLM-based agent at the ground control station reasons about where to search and a classical optimizer determines how to dispatch drones under energy constraints across successive search cycles. It handles moving victims, uncertain detection, and mixed structured/unstructured mission information. Simulation results show improved search performance.

entry.title: DPA: Decentralized Primal Averaging with Quasi-Global Momentum for Highly Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Diyako Ghaderyan, Stefan Werner

entry.summary: DPA is a decentralized training algorithm combining primal averaging with a local quasi-global momentum buffer to handle heterogeneous data across agents, maintaining three coupled sequences for optimization, gradient evaluation, and output averaging, and constructing a network-aware momentum direction without transmitting auxiliary tracking variables. It targets sparse communication graphs and on-device learning.

entry.title: SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection

author.name: Alex Jiang, Didier Schwab, Chuyuan Li

entry.summary: SPADE is a framework for detecting AI-generated text that uses the prompt's influence as a discriminative signal, rather than relying solely on generated text or its probability distributions. By characterizing the prompt's influence, it transfers better across datasets in open-world scenarios.

entry.title: StructRL: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning with Replay Graphs

author.name: Ivo Nowak

entry.summary: StructRL converts RL experience into an explicit replay graph and applies dynamic programming over observed transitions to form a graph policy transferred to model-free learners as action preferences (DQN) or target directions along shortest paths (SAC). It substantially improves sparse-reward results, e.g., raising DQN DoorKey success from 0.10 to 0.90, outperforming plain DQN given triple the budget.

entry.title: UniPipe: Unified Inference Serving and Fine-Tuning for Deadline-Constrained DNN Surrogate Workflows

author.name: Jaiaid Mobin, Avinash Maurya, M. Mustafa Rafique, Bogdan Nicolae

entry.summary: UniPipe unifies inference serving and concurrent fine-tuning of DNN surrogates on a single GPU for scientific workflows with hard latency deadlines, such as ptychographic imaging at X-ray light sources. It addresses GPU contention between serving and tuning contexts that inflates latency variance and causes deadline misses.

entry.title: Epigraph Form Reinforcement Learning-based Safe Trajectory Tracking Control for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Xiaoke Yang, Jin Chen, Yafei Wang, Qi Zhang, Ming Li, Haiwen Wu, Chengliang Yin, Yong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a constrained RL framework for safe trajectory tracking in connected autonomous vehicles using epigraph form to avoid the unstable policy-gradient scaling issues of Lagrangian methods. The approach aims to combine accurate trajectory tracking with collision avoidance in highly dynamic environments.

entry.title: DGPExplainer: Generating Prototype Sequence Explanations for Dynamic Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Jinlong Hu, Shixu Fan, Chongzhang Li

entry.summary: Introduces DGPExplainer, a post-hoc, prototype-based explanation method for dynamic graph neural networks that produces case-based, human-understandable model-level explanations. It addresses the gap that static GNN explanation techniques do not transfer well to temporal graphs with spatiotemporal dependencies.

entry.title: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries

author.name: Ruizhi Deng, Guohao Shen, Tangrui Xiong

entry.summary: The paper characterizes parameter-space symmetries of ReLU and Leaky ReLU networks across fully connected, convolutional, and residual architectures, proving that any quasianalytic parameter map preserving the network function is a composition of positive channel scaling and channel permutation. By quotienting out these symmetries, the authors derive uniform covering-number upper bounds where positive scaling reduces the complexity exponent from the total parameter count S to S-H. The result shows that nominal parameter counts can overstate the functional complexity of neural networks.

entry.title: MORA: Correcting Time Series Forecasts with Coarse Future Signals

author.name: Hu Li, Kenan Li, Haonan Xu, longlong, Shuqin Gao, Yucheng Zhang, Feng Dai

entry.summary: Observes that diverse time-series forecasters leave residual energy concentrated in few low-frequency components and that historical inputs still predict forecast-mean errors. It proposes MORA, a model-agnostic residual adapter that refines frozen forecasters' outputs via structural extrapolation and learned estimation of segment-wise means, without extra inputs.

entry.title: Learning a calibrated decision head from logged bandit feedback

author.name: Ye Yuan

entry.summary: Studies adapting LLM-based decision heads (LoRA on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B-Base) from logged bandit feedback, showing that naive Brier/log-score REINFORCE rewards cause collapse since wrong actions earn at least gold's reward, sometimes cratering accuracy. It proposes scoring probability as a pathwise-gradient loss to avoid the collapse and obtain calibrated probabilities.

entry.title: SpaceMCP: Vision Language Model Spatial Reasoning via Model Context Protocol

author.name: Ameen Izhac, Nobuko Yoshida, Ronald Clark

entry.summary: SpaceMCP augments vision-language models with an MCP-style interface of structured function calls that query a real-time scene graph built from feed-forward 3D reconstruction and open-vocabulary segmentation. This lets VLMs access metric spatial information such as distances and object positioning, addressing their weak spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Few-Shot Cross-Subject Neural--Image Retrieval via Stimulus-Anchored Latent Bias Calibration

author.name: Xizhang Yao, Li Zhang, Gan Huang, Zhen Liang

entry.summary: SA-LBC addresses confounding between subject-specific neural representation shifts and stimulus composition effects in cross-subject neural-image retrieval, estimating first-order bias shifts against same-stimulus source anchors with shrinkage based on source-derived uncertainty. The paper derives exact finite-population MSE expressions for its estimators.

entry.title: Class-Competence Aggregation: Output-Layer Routing for Federated Multiclass DDoS Detection under Class-Concentrated Non-IID Data

author.name: Tapu Datta, Hafiz Imtiaz

entry.summary: The paper identifies a specific failure mode of federated averaging when an entire attack class resides on one client: the output-layer neuron for that class receives an active anti-signal and collapses, driving the concentrated LDAP class to 0% F1 on CIC-DDoS2019. It proposes Class-Competence Aggregation, which aggregates output-layer weights per class using client-local competence signals.

entry.title: Bellman Contraction under MMD: A Unified Framework

author.name: Baptiste Debes, Tinne Tuytelaars

entry.summary: The paper builds a mathematical framework for contraction of the distributional Bellman operator under Maximum Mean Discrepancy, reducing it to conditional positive definiteness of a Bellman difference kernel and connecting radial-kernel cases to Bernstein functions via Schoenberg's theorem. It unifies known kernel results, identifies 11 new contracting kernels, and proposes a chaining construction.

entry.title: Null-Corrected Conditional Coverage in Materials Property Prediction: A Five-Dataset Replication

author.name: Irene Boruah

entry.summary: The paper shows worst-bin conditional coverage statistics in materials property prediction are downward-biased in finite samples and replicates a prior conditional coverage study across five regression datasets, seven interval methods, and 50 splits with a null correction. It separates marginal miscalibration from genuinely uneven conditional coverage.

entry.title: Probe Before You Preach: Conformal Ambiguity Sets and Neuro-Symbolic Counterfactual Probing for Diagnosing Algebraic Misconceptions in Middle School Mathematics

author.name: Caihong Xu, Xiangyu Yu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes how distinct misconception rules can produce identical wrong answers in algebra, deriving conditional Bayes error bounds and proposing Mondrian Adaptive Conformal Misconception Sets plus symbolic-verified counterfactual micro-probing to design diagnostic questions. It provides coverage guarantees at the curriculum-group level rather than per-student.

entry.title: Nested Ensemble Learning with Topological Data Analysis for Graph Classification and Regression

author.name: Innocent Abaa, Umar Islambekov

entry.summary: The paper proposes a nested ensemble framework using Topological Data Analysis for graph classification and regression, computing persistence diagrams from lower-star filtrations under three centrality filter functions and integrating them via a three-level stacked architecture. Base models per filter are combined by meta-learners to overcome reliance on any single topological summary.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Multi-View Clustering via View-Aware Quantization

author.name: Khadija Ardif, Meryeme Ayache, Nidal Nasser, Ouiame Marnissi

entry.summary: This work targets high communication overhead in federated multi-view clustering by dynamically allocating quantization bits across views according to iteratively updated view-importance scores. The approach preserves privacy while reducing transmitted representation size and adapting to unequal view contributions.

entry.title: Bet Imaginatively, not Historically in Independent-Data Sequential Testing

author.name: Nathaniel Xu, Feng Liu, Danica J. Sutherland

entry.summary: The paper proposes FLOE (follow the leave-one-out e-power), a simple betting strategy for sequential testing in stochastic, independent-data settings, where conventional adversarial betting strategies are suboptimal. The method exploits knowledge of the data distribution to improve evidence accumulation in testing-by-betting frameworks.

entry.title: Generative AI models for exploring diffusion dynamics from multi-frame particle tracking

author.name: Jianan Wei, Qiang Zhang, Hao Sun, Yi Yang, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: DiffTR-Flow3D is a diffusion-based model that estimates 3D flow motion from spatiotemporal particle recordings, addressing temporally under-sampled sequences with large inter-frame displacements. It conditions the diffusion process on global and local particle dynamics and leverages historical trajectories to improve flow estimation in fluid mechanics measurements.

entry.title: Rethinking Actions: Continuity-Aware Priors for World-Model Planning

author.name: Shaobo Yang, Zichen Ai, Ziyang Ma, Qian Yang, Bin Fang

entry.summary: The paper shows expert demonstration actions exhibit temporal structure and proposes LG-DKGP, a locality-gated deep-kernel Gaussian-process prior that predicts continuations of executed action histories for visual world-model planning. A learned exploration scale initializes search around a corrected mean, with a frozen world model evaluating goal progress.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning based on Dempster-Shafer theory

author.name: Marie Kempkes, Jakob Spiegelberg, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Vedran Dunjko

entry.summary: The authors introduce an uncertainty-aware quantum classification framework based on Dempster-Shafer theory, which assigns uncertainty weights to sets of labels rather than individual labels. They devise a training strategy enabling parameterized quantum circuits to learn such assignments directly from data, with efficient state preparation enabling downstream uncertainty-aware decision procedures.

entry.title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics

author.name: Zaid Abulawi (Department of Nuclear Engineering, Texas A&M University), William Oliveira (Department of Energy, Nuclear Engineering Division, Politecnico di Milano), Akzhol Almukhametov (Department of Nuclear Engineering, Texas A&M University), Jun Fang (Nuclear Science and Engineering Division, Argonne National Laboratory), Ling Zou (Nuclear Science and Engineering Division, Argonne National Laboratory), Rui Hu (Nuclear Science and Engineering Division, Argonne National Laboratory), Stefano Lorenzi (Department of Energy, Nuclear Engineering Division, Politecnico di Milano), Yang Liu (Department of Nuclear Engineering, Texas A&M University)

entry.summary: Researchers develop a physics-informed neural network closure that predicts turbulent kinetic energy and timescale for the SAM thermal-hydraulics code, applied to the Molten Salt Fast Reactor. The learned closure preserves invariance and keeps the momentum equations well conditioned without solving turbulence transport equations.

entry.title: When Local Definitions Are Missing: Stable Errors in Language Models

author.name: Zengqing Wu, Chuan Xiao

entry.summary: Investigates LLM errors when locally defined words are read without their in-context definitions, using multiple-choice questions drawn from synthetic vocabulary, contracts, Reddit glossaries, and decentralized exchange docs. Tests whether models' repeated answers and stated confidence can reveal their own errors without an answer key.

entry.title: Human-Likeness and Conversational Preference Diverge for Synthesized Agent Speech in Customer-Service Calls

author.name: Jeffrey M. Girard, Antony D'Avirro, Jason Z. Zheng, Jacqueline R. Vertino, Benjamin Peloquin

entry.summary: Compares human-likeness and conversational preference judgments in paired-choice listening tests on improvised customer-service turns across six commercial TTS systems and actor recordings. It finds the two judgments diverge: some systems rank higher on human-likeness, others on preference, and listeners chose systems over actors in only 19 percent of human-likeness trials.

entry.title: Optimal Single-History Tokenization Disambiguation for Provably Secure Linguistic Steganography

author.name: Feng Jiang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical treatment of provably secure linguistic steganography, proving that any single-history receiver with exact extraction must operate over a prefix-free candidate set and consequently forfeits the stop entropy of prefix tokens, then characterizes optimal disambiguation under this constraint.

entry.title: Saying No by Asking Yes: Affirmative Decomposition and Evidence Reflection for Frozen CLIP

author.name: Aashish Pokhrel, Tejas Anvekar, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar

entry.summary: The paper tackles negation blindness in frozen vision-language models with Negation-Aware Evidence Scoring, which reformulates negated descriptions like 'a kitchen with no toaster' into affirmative queries combined by caption structure. A lightweight decomposer, NegSplit, extracts negated spans and affirmative context, applying presence-based corrections for denials. This exploits the asymmetry that models match affirmative descriptions far better than negations.

entry.title: SCR-Mamba: Skeleton-conditioned Mamba with cross-scale incremental refinement for efficient 3D human pose estimation

author.name: Jie Wang, Xuejing Gu, Congzhe Zhang, Zibo Zhao

entry.summary: SCR-Mamba improves Mamba-based video 3D pose estimation by conditioning selective state updates on skeletal structure (bone connections and left-right symmetry) and applying cross-scale incremental refinement to balance efficiency with per-frame detail. This addresses the lack of skeletal priors in standard Mamba temporal modeling and the compute-accuracy tradeoff from stacking blocks. The result is an efficient long-sequence pose estimator.

entry.title: RipBench: A Unified Benchmark for Multi-Level Rip Current Detection, Classification and Segmentation

author.name: Andrei Dumitriu, Aakash Ralhan, Florin Miron, Florin Tatui, Radu Tudor Ionescu, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: RipBench is a unified benchmark for rip current analysis covering classification, axis-aligned and oriented object detection, and instance, semantic, and panoptic segmentation on a common dataset. Rip currents are the leading cause of coastal drownings but are hard to detect due to their amorphous structure and environmental variability, and prior research has been fragmented across incompatible datasets and metrics. The benchmark enables controlled, apples-to-apples comparison of models for this safety-critical application.

category.term: AI for Safety and Social Good

entry.title: AIFR: Adaptive Identity Feature Recovery for Diffusion-Based Makeup and Anime Portraits

author.name: Linyan Dai, Xinwei Zhang, Yaxin Xiao, Mengyu Sun, Xinwei Liu, Renyang Liu, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: AIFR corrects identity features within a frozen face-recognition model to recover original embeddings for diffusion-generated makeup and anime portraits, avoiding costly gallery re-encoding or lossy input restoration. Because appearance changes vary in strength and affect facial regions differently, the framework applies adaptive region- and strength-aware corrections. This matters for identity-based content screening as stylized portraits proliferate online.

entry.title: Pothole Risk Assessment with Geometrically Grounded Vision Language Models

author.name: Abdalmalek Aburaddaha, Zaid A. El Shair, Ali Al-Bustami, Samir A. Rawashdeh

entry.summary: This paper presents a five-stage pipeline for assessing pothole severity from dashcam images, combining perspective transformation, zero-shot SAM segmentation, geometric feature extraction, and Gemini 2.5 Pro severity classification with composite risk scoring and natural-language warnings. It evaluates on 3,092 potholes across 1,119 dashcam scenes, showing that geometric grounding improves over ungrounded VLM assessments.

entry.title: Description-Guided CLIP Adaptation with Local Evidence Calibration for Few-Shot Plant Disease Recognition

author.name: Zhenkun Ye, Qian Zhou, Hua Zou

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage, description-guided adaptation of CLIP for few-shot plant disease recognition, using symptom and comparative descriptions plus fine-grained local visual cues rather than coarse class semantics and global image representations. It also guards against over-specialization that would erode the generalization from large-scale pretraining. The work is relevant to intelligent agriculture, where labeled data is scarce and diagnostic symptoms are localized and subtle.

entry.title: PiLLVD: A Real-World Low-Light Video Dataset for Dynamic Scenes Captured with Off-the-Shelf Cameras

author.name: Yaser Abu Awwad, Paul L. Rosin, Oktay Karaku\c{s}

entry.summary: PiLLVD is a paired low-light/normal-light video dataset captured with a Raspberry Pi-based multi-camera rig using off-the-shelf cameras, addressing the scarcity of real-world paired video data for low-light video enhancement. The hardware design tackles alignment, motion blur, and exposure mismatch problems that make paired dynamic-scene capture difficult.

entry.title: SALT: State-Aligned Low-Rank Transfer for Single-Temporal Cross-Dataset Structural Localization in Remote Sensing

author.name: Aggelos Psiris, Georgios Angelidis, Giorgos Sfikas, Maria Vakalopoulou, Thomas Lagkas, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos

entry.summary: SALT is a state-aligned low-rank transfer framework for single-temporal change detection in remote sensing, aligning feature adaptation parameterization with the states used for prediction to prevent over-specialization of pretrained features and improve cross-dataset generalization. It transfers structural evidence such as building regions from labeled source data to unseen target imagery without bi-temporal pairs.

entry.title: ProtoVis-Nav: Prototypical Visual Imagination for Visual-Spatial Aligned UAV Navigation

author.name: Guangyuan Sui, Yunzhong Hou, Chi Harold Liu

entry.summary: Proposes ProtoVis-Nav, a vision-language navigation framework for UAVs that predicts feature prototypes whose linear combination estimates the visual appearance of the target region for the intended next movement, aligning language, spatial prediction, and imagined visuals before waypoint prediction. This reduces navigation errors and collisions from imprecise 3D motion prediction.

entry.title: MiniPose: Miniature-Based Real Data Collection for 6D Pose Estimation of Large Industrial Pipe Segments

author.name: Hyunjun Kim, Youngjin Seo, Sungwon Seo, Jiyou Shin, Kunwoo Kim, Chanyong Park, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: MiniPose is a pipeline that fabricates scaled-down replicas of large industrial objects (pipes, structural components) so real RGB-D training data with diverse poses can be collected without physically moving heavy objects, addressing both acquisition burden and the sim-to-real gap of synthetic data. This enables 6-DOF pose estimation in shipyards and petrochemical plants where pose diversity is otherwise impractical. A pragmatic data-collection contribution for an underexplored industrial perception niche.

entry.title: FloCOS: Predicting Compact Forward Occupancy Sets of Surrounding Vehicles via Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Chuansheng Dong, Yinxiao Zhan, Zongdian Li, Peng Hou, Jin Wang, Jiayu Fan

entry.summary: FloCOS is a conditional flow-matching framework that predicts compact yet well-covered forward occupancy sets for surrounding vehicles, avoiding both dangerous under-approximation and overly conservative prediction that breaks planners. It represents the occupancy set as a time-varying union of half-space convex polygons parameterized by temporal basis coefficients learned via flow matching. This improves the safety-planning tradeoff in autonomous driving prediction.

entry.title: GraSLA: A Lightweight Spatial-Language-Action Model with Grasp Hypotheses as Geometric Priors

author.name: Jibao Yuan, Zixiang Zhao, Wensong Xu, Siqi Lu, Shaofei Chen

entry.summary: GraSLA is a lightweight language-conditioned manipulation policy that injects 6-DoF grasp detection hypotheses as geometric priors, combining the behavioral diversity of grasp hypotheses with the adaptability of continuous-action imitation policies. This addresses the restricted behavioral diversity that plagues continuous-action policies trained on limited demonstrations, while improving responsiveness relative to open-loop grasp execution. It is a sensible architecture-level improvement for language-conditioned grasping.

entry.title: What World Model Does Active Object Search Need? A Study under Imperfect Detection

author.name: Kyeongryeol Go

entry.summary: The paper introduces BAMOS (Bayesian Active Miss-aware Object Search) to study which belief representations a world model needs for reliable object search when the detector produces false positives and false negatives. Comprehensive ablations in Isaac Sim and HSSD houses examine the roles of target belief, occupancy belief, and detector error models in deciding where to look and when to stop. Its finding that target belief and its update mechanism are central offers useful guidance for active perception system design.

entry.title: A Coupled Control Barrier Function Approach to Deadlock-Free Multi-Robot Conflict Resolution

author.name: Gary Rostomyan, Ketan Savla, Petros A. Ioannou

entry.summary: The paper presents a QP-based feedback controller for multi-robot conflict resolution with input constraints, using coupled Control Barrier Functions for safety and a yielding matrix to encode how robots influence one another, guaranteeing deadlock-free operation by design. The authors establish sufficient conditions for the controller to be locally Lipschitz and prove finite uniform bounds on the optimal CBF sign-indefinite slack. This is a rigorous theoretical contribution to safe multi-robot coordination.

entry.title: Robot Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance from Randomly Positioned External Cameras

author.name: Raul Steinmetz, Jair Augusto Bottega, Ayanori Yorozu, Akihisa Ohya

entry.summary: The authors show that standard PPO fails to learn indoor navigation end-to-end from fixed exocentric cameras due to a perspective mismatch between external observations and egocentric actions. They propose VINE, which trains a supervised obstacle-map estimation network to produce viewpoint-invariant intermediate representations before navigation. This addresses a practical deployment setting where infrastructure-mounted cameras replace onboard sensing.

entry.title: Collaborative Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems Through Iterative Clustering

author.name: David R. Martin, Brooks A. Butler, Scott Nivison, Magnus Egerstedt, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque, Pramod Khargonekar

entry.summary: The paper presents an iterative clustering algorithm for allocating heterogeneous robot teams to tasks where collaborations produce emergent capabilities beyond individual robots. By iteratively forming clusters of robots and tasks and optimizing assignments within each cluster, it decomposes a computationally intractable global allocation problem into tractable subproblems. The approach handles synergy effects that make classic assignment formulations inadequate.

entry.title: A Class of Bayesian Conjugate Distributions on $SE_n(3)$ for Motion Estimation

author.name: Shijie Wang, Haichao Gui, Rui Zhong

entry.summary: The paper introduces a class of Bayesian conjugate distributions on the extended special Euclidean group SE_n(3), constructed by restricting matrix Gaussian distributions to avoid singular local coordinates. This yields exact closed-form Bayesian inference for motion estimation, with two natural mean estimators and supporting estimation machinery.

entry.title: Sharp Gaussian approximation for Polyak--Ruppert averaged linear stochastic approximation

author.name: Bogdan Butyrin, Eric Moulines, Alexey Naumov, Sergey Samsonov

entry.summary: The authors prove sharp bounds on how quickly the normalized Polyak-Ruppert averaged iterate of linear stochastic approximation approaches its Gaussian limit, showing an n^(gamma-1) upper bound with a matching lower bound for step sizes k^-gamma, and an O(n^-1/2) bound for the recursive multiplier bootstrap.

entry.title: A Latent Semiparametric Mixture Model for Robust Heterogeneity Learning in High Dimensions

author.name: Lyuou Zhang, Boxiang Wang, Lulu Wang, Wen Zhou, Hui Zou

entry.summary: The authors propose a latent semiparametric mixture model in which observed data follow a Gaussian mixture after latent coordinate-wise monotone transformations, combining the theoretical guarantees of model-based clustering with robustness to non-Gaussianity. A sparse optimal clustering rule is assumed in the latent space.

entry.title: AI acceleration?

author.name: Eugene Earnshaw

entry.summary: The author builds a simple quantitative model grounded in the METR acceleration report and historical data (frontier training compute growing about 5x per year, efficiency about 3x, capability about 15 points per year) to argue that many models used in acceleration discussions predict faster AI progress than the empirically anchored parameters support.

entry.title: Chips for Humanity: Compute for AI safety research

author.name: heyanuja

entry.summary: The author announces a new initiative, Chips for Humanity, to pre-secure compute and inference tokens for third-party AI safety researchers before crunchtime, on the theory that compute will be a scarce bottleneck when the most important safety research (increasingly done by AI) happens around short-timelines scenarios. The post launches a survey of compute needs.

entry.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers developed a training technique for climate emulators that boosts performance and adaptability while requiring only a fraction of the usual data, using carefully selected synthetic training data. An emulator trained this way accurately predicts outcomes of unseen scenarios, cutting production time for fast tools that let scientists test thousands of climate scenarios in seconds.

entry.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning

author.name: So-Bin Jung, David Yoon Suk, Sang-Wook Kim

entry.summary: Studies how node structural properties relate to hyperbolic embedding radii in hypergraphs, finding bridge nodes behave differently than in ordinary graphs and that conventional bridge scores fail to capture groupwise connectivity. Proposes HyBridge, a self-supervised hyperbolic hypergraph representation learning method guided by these findings.

entry.title: Protocol-Aware Auditing of Domain-Blind Feature Attribution in Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Emmanuelli El-Mahmoud, Abanisenioluwa Kolawole Orojo, Pablo Rivas, Erika Leal

entry.summary: The paper formalizes domain blindness - attribution methods querying model behavior outside the operational domain in network intrusion detection - and proves a valid-query invariance guarantee for protocol-aware query control. It instantiates the principle in LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and DeepLIFT, revealing hidden attribution instability that standard evaluation misses.

entry.title: Enhancing Resolution and Reliability with Attention Mechanisms in Nuclear Accident Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Wonung Jeong, Sangam Khanal, Jeongik Lee, Sangseung Lee, Joongoo Jeon

entry.summary: The ABC-Transformer is a decoder-only surrogate combining causal self-attention and temporal attention pooling to emulate MAAP severe-accident codes at 5-minute resolution over 72-hour transients, trained on 11,000 simulations of a loss-of-cooling scenario for the OPR1000 reactor. It enables faster dynamic probabilistic safety assessment.

entry.title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control

author.name: Maarten De Baecke, Flavia Sofia Acerbo, Andrea Giusti, Wilm Decr\'e

entry.summary: The paper imitates a long-horizon nonconvex time-optimal MPC controller with hard terminal constraints using neural networks for real-time deployment, introducing self-informed sampling (SIFS) to query the expert only where the policy deviates from it. The integrated architecture addresses data scarcity from expensive expert solves and real-time deployment challenges together.

entry.title: STeP-C: Real-Time Neural Compression for Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing at Scale

author.name: Tingfeng Li, Ming-Fang Huang, Shaobo Han, Yue Tian

entry.summary: STeP-C is a neural compression framework for distributed acoustic sensing data that decouples spatial encoding, temporal prediction, and entropy coding to run on a live streaming acquisition system. The paper claims the first end-to-end demonstration of neural compression on continuously streaming DAS data at scale, where raw rates exceed hundreds of megabytes per second.

entry.title: Do the Details Help the Whole? One-Way Transfer from Person Actions to Group Intent in VLMs on JRDB-Social

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Zhixi Cai, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, QingHao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: Tests the assumption that jointly training on person actions and group intent benefits both tasks in vision-language models, running eight training arms with three seeds on Qwen3.5 4B and core arms on Qwen3.5 9B and Qwen3-VL 4B on JRDB-Social. Results show at best one-way transfer, with intent macro-F1 gains of about one point and no benefit to action prediction.

entry.title: CT-SGAL-LIO: Causal Continuous Time Refinement of Discrete LiDAR Inertial Odometry

author.name: Nam Tran, Thu Tran, Toan Nguyen, William J Beksi, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: CT-SGAL-LIO adds a continuous-time refinement module that smooths the posterior pose stream of a discrete SGal(3)-based LiDAR-inertial odometry estimator without modifying the estimator itself. It addresses short-horizon pose oscillation between propagation and correction steps while avoiding the delayed updates of full continuous-time optimization. The result improves robustness during rapid rotations and accelerations.

entry.title: Posterior contraction rates for banded approximations of Gaussian processes

author.name: Omar Kassi, Bernhard Stankewitz, Botond Szabo

entry.summary: The paper analyzes banded (spatial-proximity-based) sparsification of Gaussian process covariance matrices as an approximate posterior method for large datasets, providing posterior contraction rates that quantify the statistical accuracy of the approximation against its computational savings over the O(n^3) exact GP.

entry.title: Edge-Native Multimodal RAG: Hardware-Aware Quantization and Architectural Optimization for Consumer GPUs

author.name: Zahraa Selim, Menna Hamed, Wesam Ahmed, Sohyla Said, Sara Basheer, Rami Zewail

entry.summary: This is an engineering study of deploying multimodal RAG on consumer Turing-architecture GPUs, quantifying tradeoffs between GPTQ and NF4 quantization on throughput, VRAM, and long-context stability. The system-level analysis shows GPTQ achieves higher throughput but exhibits context instability beyond 2048 tokens on this hardware.

entry.title: FPSRG: Heterogeneous User Simulation First-Person Post-Training and Multidimensional Semantic Response Grids

author.name: Ruimin Pei, Haibo Liu, Fang Zhang, Xunhua Guo

entry.summary: FPSRG is a method for building heterogeneous LLM user simulators with profile construction: shared first-person post-training teaches a model to answer as a participant, then self-report and behavioral targets refine dimension-specific control vectors. With the model frozen, joint scores for vector-coefficient combinations are measured, inadmissible configurations filtered, and results stored in a searchable per-token catalog. This enables controllable, retrievable simulated users across many dimensions.

entry.title: Estimating Image Creativity

author.name: Nisan Chhetri, Christopher G. Healey, Sina Baghbanijam

entry.summary: Proposes a framework to predict human-rated creativity of images by first predicting the strengths of psychological creativity dimensions—novelty, surprise, and arousal—and then combining them into an overall creativity estimate. The work aims to operationalize subjective aesthetic judgment using grounded psychological constructs.

entry.title: GingivitisSeg: A Public Dataset and Comparative Benchmark for Gingivitis Segmentation in Intraoral Images

author.name: Zeynep Ozdemir, Zehra Hasgul, Irem Ulku, Omer Ozgur Tanriover, Fatma Karacaoglu, Murat Akkaya

entry.summary: Introduces GingivitisSeg, a public dataset of 961 intraoral photographs with pixel-level annotations of gingival inflammation, plus standardized train/validation/test splits. The paper benchmarks seven segmentation model-backbone configurations and runs controlled ablations on loss functions and auxiliary supervision, providing the first systematic reference point for computer-assisted periodontal assessment.

entry.title: Learning-Based Interpolation of Detector Gaps in Photon-Counting X-ray Imaging

author.name: Johannes B. Thalhammer, Patrick Ilg, Tina Dorosti, Sebastian Peterhansl, Theresa Hiu, Daniel Frey, Zijin Huang, Florian Schaff, Daniela Pfeiffer, Franz Pfeiffer

entry.summary: The authors adapt WGAN-GP and conditional Pix2Pix generative models to fill physical detector gaps in tiled photon-counting X-ray imaging, with masking that only modifies gap pixels and loss terms preserving mean intensity and intensity distributions. Preserving intensity statistics is critical because small shifts cause ring artifacts in downstream tomographic reconstruction.

entry.title: HeriKGQA: Grounded Knowledge-Graph Question Answering over Cultural Heritage Sensor Data

author.name: Lingxiao Kong, Vasileios Arampatzakis, Vasileios Sevetlidis, George Pavlidis, Zeyd Boukhers

entry.summary: HeriKGQA constrains LLMs to question interpretation and answer phrasing while leaving computation to SPARQL over a knowledge graph aligned with W3C SOSA/SSN and CIDOC-CRM ontologies, with a grounding layer for temporal, spatial, and anomaly facts. This prevents the silent miscomputation that occurs when LLMs answer directly over raw sensor records.

entry.title: Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN

author.name: Xijun Wang, Zhaoyang Liu, Xiang Chen, Howard H. Yang, Chenyuan Feng

entry.summary: The Context Graph is a heterogeneous directed graph organizing policies, measurements, decisions, and alerts into a queryable explanation layer for AI-RAN (AI-native radio access networks), where multiple autonomous agents share radio resources. Its Decision-Event node acts as a causal junction, capturing triggering context, to address the gap that existing explainability tools handle only single-model attribution or linear event logs.

entry.title: Scalable Conversational Assessment: Chat-Based Exams with a Two-Agent LLM Pipeline

author.name: Geoffrey Challen, Craig Zilles

entry.summary: The authors present scalable conversational assessment, an LLM system that administers interactive text-based oral-style exams to students, using a two-agent architecture where an interviewer asks questions and a hidden evaluator tracks goals without leaking answers. This brings the benefits of oral exams, such as reasoning probes and follow-ups, to a scalable format.

entry.title: A Transferable Pretrained 3D Model for Impedance Inversion with Sparse-Well Prior Conditioning

author.name: Gen Li, Zhaoyun Zong, Diqiong Jiang, Man Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a transferable 3D seismic impedance inversion framework that separates offline learning from deployment: a masked autoencoder learns structural representations across surveys, and a frozen-encoder inversion network is trained on synthetic models with sparse-well low-frequency priors. At deployment the network stays fixed and well data is used only for prior construction.

entry.title: MOON-RL: Multi-Objective Optimization via Objective Space Navigation with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Andrii Artomov, Soheyl Massoudi, J\"urg Schiffmann

entry.summary: Formulates constrained multi-objective engineering design as preference-directed navigation in objective space using a lightweight PPO policy that acts as an instance-specific adaptive search process. This reduces the many expensive evaluations required by population-based optimizers and gives online control over the trade-off direction.

entry.title: MechBench: A Domain-Specific LLM Benchmark for Parallel Mechanisms

author.name: Zhihao Xia, Tingting Wang, Hui Li, Yongheng Xing, Chunxu Tian

entry.summary: Presents MECHBENCH, a 2,541-question benchmark evaluating LLMs on parallel mechanism reasoning across professional knowledge, analysis, and design, built via a domain-grounded framework (MECHFORGE) with expert organization and executable analysis/design tasks. It fills a gap in systematic domain-specific LLM evaluation for mechanical engineering.

entry.title: Imputing Missing Near-Surface Air Temperature using Graph Attention Networks with Distance-Aware Edge Features

author.name: Emma C. Weber, Dominique Guillot, Daniyar Abykhanov, Julien Emile-Geay

entry.summary: Applies a graph attention network with distance-aware edge features to reconstruct historical near-surface air temperature fields from sparse records, representing grid cells as graph nodes to avoid polar distortions of flat lat-long processing. Trained on masked CMIP6 CESM2 simulations to address large early-record and high-latitude gaps.

entry.title: GLCR: Global-Local Collaborative Routing for Multi-Task Electromagnetic Signal Processing

author.name: Fang Lu, Yao Lu, Zhuangzhi Chen, Sicheng Zhang, Shanqing Yu, Yun Lin, Qi Xuan, Guan Gui

entry.summary: This paper proposes GLCR, a two-stage model-routing method that dispatches unknown electromagnetic signals to matched experts in a heterogeneous expert pool, balancing accuracy against the cost of electromagnetic foundation models. It also introduces HeteroSignal-7, a multi-task routing benchmark with 140,000 samples spanning six task types and seven experts under a unified evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Learning Temporal Dynamics with Derivative Representations for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Shujie Duan, Jia Hong Puah, Haocheng Wu, Yifei Mao, Hongting Zhou, Chenxuan Li, Zitao Fang, Yang Lu, Sim Kuan Goh

entry.summary: DeltaTSF is a dynamics-aware time series forecasting framework that jointly learns series values and their discrete temporal derivatives across input and forecast horizons, exploiting temporal structure via training strategy rather than architecture alone. It aims to improve on transformers' difficulty capturing system dynamics evolution.

entry.title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time

author.name: Davide Wiest

entry.summary: TeRL is a self-supervised learning rule that is local in both space and time, instantiating a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and running statistics, yielding per-neuron online losses with bounded state. The gradient reduces to Hebbian and anti-Hebbian updates, and the objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis.

entry.title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression

author.name: Carina Moreira Costa, Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Martin Schmidt

entry.summary: The paper derives an exact convex-analytic reformulation of data poisoning attacks on l2-regularized logistic regression, using convex conjugacy of the softplus to express the attacker's objective as concave with only bounded bilinear equalities as nonconvex constraints, plus finite bounds on all variables. This enables global optimization of the attack.

entry.title: Modeling Drug Overdose Mortality Levels Using Social Vulnerability Indicators in U.S. Counties: A Double Machine Learning Approach for Causal Analysis

author.name: Qunhui Guo, Jiongbai Liu, Md Noor E Alam

entry.summary: Using CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index data across 2016-2021, the paper applies double machine learning to estimate the adjusted exposure-response relationship between county social vulnerability and drug poisoning mortality. It moves beyond associational XGBoost/Random Forest comparisons toward causal characterization.

entry.title: Modelling the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related home insurance claims

author.name: Paul Wilsens, Katrien Antonio, Gerda Claeskens, Koos Gubbels

entry.summary: The paper jointly models daily occurrence and reporting delays of weather-related home insurance claims by combining portfolio data with high-resolution weather data, addressing partial reporting of recent claims and rarity of severe weather days. Actuarial authors from KU Leuven provide a continuous-process alternative to event-triggered models.

entry.title: What Does Each Part of Speech Need? Contexts, Subspaces and Dimensions in Static Word Embeddings

author.name: Jintang Xue, Chengwei Wei, Yun-Cheng Wang, C. -C. Jay Kuo

entry.summary: Using nine controlled corpora, the paper investigates which context words each part of speech needs in static word embeddings, whether POS tags require their own subspaces, and how dimension allocation should follow part of speech or frequency. Findings include that POS tags help verb similarity consistently while helping nouns less, and per-POS PCA bases preserve similarity better at fixed dimension.

entry.title: Temporal Context-Aware Spam Detection Using Transformer-Based NLP Models

author.name: Fariz Zeynalov, Razim Mammadli

entry.summary: This paper studies carrier-level outbound SMS spam detection, predicting at send time whether a carrier will flag a message, using a proprietary dataset of 43,741 messages with timestamps and delivery statuses. A DeBERTa-v3-base text classifier beats a TF-IDF baseline, and a deployed DistilBERT model augmented with inter-message temporal features improves performance further, showing that sender-level behavioral context matters beyond single-message classification.

entry.title: Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Sparse Convolution

author.name: Keshvi Tuteja, Yu-Hsiang Tsai, Gregor Olenik, Markus G\"otz, Achim Streit, Hartwig Anzt, Charlotte Debus

entry.summary: The paper analyzes convolution with sparse weights via roofline analysis, characterizing why sparsity is hard to exploit at runtime due to irregular memory access and workload imbalance. It provides both theoretical performance characterization and empirical guidance for deploying sparse convolutional models on edge devices.

entry.title: Better Boundary Prediction Does Not Guarantee Better Structural Representation

author.name: Michael Zhou, Markus Frohmann, Junghyun Min, En-Shiun Annie Lee

entry.summary: Tests whether punctuation restoration as a proxy for phrasal structure improves language models' representations of argument, semantic, and syntactic structure across decoder-only, encoder-only, and encoder-decoder architectures at under 1B parameters. The evidence suggests better boundary prediction does not guarantee better structural representation.

entry.title: Unibuc - NLP at "Voight-Kampff" Generative AI Detection PAN 2025

author.name: Teodor Marchitan, Claudiu Creanga, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: A system description paper for the CLEF 2025 Voight-Kampff generative AI detection shared task. The team finds that a majority-vote ensemble of classical ML models (LightGBM, XGBoost, logistic regression, SVM) over LLM embeddings matches fine-tuned LLM classifiers at about 99.4% F1, and explores layered feature combination for human-AI collaborative text classification.

entry.title: SyntheIce: A Synthetic Radargram Annotation Benchmark for Englacial Layer Reconstruction

author.name: Muhammad Behroze Hassan, Bayu Adhi Tama, Sanjay Purushotham, Vandana P. Janeja

entry.summary: Addresses englacial layer reconstruction in radio-echo-sounding radargrams with a slope-aware greedy fragment-linking algorithm using row-similarity gating and an EWMA slope predictor, plus content-based hash IDs for stable cross-radargram identity, releasing a synthetic annotation benchmark for continuity validation.

entry.title: OT-BLS: Optimal-Transport-based Backbone Layer Selection for Frozen DINOv3 in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation

author.name: Natsuo Okamoto, Kazuki Kobayashi, Yoshio Kato, Shuhei Tarashima

entry.summary: This paper introduces OT-BLS, a new layer-selection criterion for training-free cross-domain few-shot segmentation that uses optimal transport to evaluate whether predicted query foreground and background labels agree with corresponding support labels in frozen DINOv3 features. Because the optimal backbone layer varies across support-query episodes, this per-episode selection improves mask prediction without any parameter updates. The work matters as it makes better use of vision foundation models in unseen domains.

entry.title: Cat Royale Comprehensive Dataset: A Dataset for Pose Detection, Segmentation, Animal Action Recognition and Scene Understanding

author.name: Zane K. J. Hartley, Joseph Ho, Alan Chamberlain, Michael P. Pound, Steve Benford

entry.summary: The Cat Royale Comprehensive Dataset offers over 500 hours of feline video from a large art-research project, with annotations for pose detection, segmentation, action recognition, and scene understanding, including 20,000 annotated images. It supports animal behavior and welfare research alongside computer vision development. This is a substantial multi-task resource for an underrepresented domain (animal vision).

entry.title: Efficient Periocular Recognition through Model Scaling and Cross Spectral VIS NIR Verification

author.name: Fabian Stockhard, Juan E. Tapia, Christoph Busch

entry.summary: AdaEye systematically studies input and backbone scaling for periocular verification in visible and cross-spectral VIS/NIR settings using an AdaFace-style framework, comparing full-face, masked-face, and 80x40 periocular inputs across four protocols. Direct periocular processing cuts computation from 6.30 to 1.64 GMACs per image while improving accuracy, with a thorough cost-benefit analysis of width and embedding dimension.

entry.title: Validation-Guided Prompt Selection for Differential Morphing Attack Detection

author.name: Raghavendra Ramachandra, Hailin Li

entry.summary: Investigates whether labeled validation data can improve a frozen vision-language evaluator for face morphing attack detection via prompt selection instead of fine-tuning. Two versions use security-oriented loss ranking and recursive prompt revision, evaluated on subject-disjoint test pairs spanning several morphing generators.

entry.title: Interactive Perception of Granular Materials via Robotic Scooping and Force-Torque Sensing

author.name: Samuli Hynninen, Mohammad Amman, Meri M\"akel\"a, Anirvan Dutta, Ville Kyrki

entry.summary: The paper introduces Latent Filter++, an interactive perception framework that infers properties of granular materials (such as grain size) from force-torque data gathered while a robot scoops. It combines a bio-inspired frequency-temporal filter-bank representation with a causal latent dynamical model that updates as new interaction observations arrive. This enables robots to characterize difficult materials online without hand-crafted preprocessing or prior knowledge of physical properties.

entry.title: QVS-LIVO RiskMap: Health- and Information-Aware View Selection for Multi-Camera LIVO and Off-Road Risk Mapping

author.name: Zihan Pan, Jinghan Wang, Hang Li, Feng Cheng, Tianchen Liu, Gaoliang Peng

entry.summary: QVS-LIVO RiskMap decouples visual processing for state estimation from semantic mapping in multi-camera off-road settings, selecting at most one eligible camera view for direct photometric correction based on observation health and geometric complementarity evaluated against a shared lidar-inertial posterior. Channel health memory and switching hysteresis stabilize selection, and the system produces off-road risk maps. It targets robust perception in degraded environments where camera reliability varies strongly.

entry.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots on a Computing Field

author.name: Yonghwan Kim, Gil-Tak Kong, Un-Sook Choi

entry.summary: CABOT is a theoretical computational model for autonomous mobile robots in which the environment itself computes: the grid floor is a cellular automaton whose cell states evolve by a local rule and are visible to robots during the Look operation, shifting capability increases from the robots to the environment. The paper contrasts this with the classical Look-Compute-Move model where power is added to robots individually.

entry.title: Fr\'echet Oblique Forest for Non-Euclidean Regression

author.name: Jiaye Chen, Rui Qiu, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Frechet oblique forests for regression where predictors and responses live in metric spaces, using an Alexandrov inner-product score for directional splits and pairwise response distances to avoid repeated Frechet mean computations. It establishes consistency and polynomial risk bounds and demonstrates performance on matrices, distributions, and spherical data.

entry.title: FLEX-LBP: Learning Local Binary Patterns with Exact Binary Inference for Texture Classification

author.name: Mohamed Alimoussa, Amal El Kaid

entry.summary: FLEX-LBP makes the hand-tuned parameters of Local Binary Pattern descriptors learnable via backpropagation while keeping forward passes exactly binary and hard, using a straight-through estimator only in the backward pass. The deployed descriptor remains an interpretable 90-parameter hard LBP with unchanged inference cost.

entry.title: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency

author.name: Sailendra Kolluru, Maheshkumar Duvvarapu

entry.summary: This study investigates using small prompt-driven language models (Qwen2.5 from 1.5B to 14B) as routers that decide, per query, whether to activate optional reasoning, retrieval, web search, or tool use, evaluated with a fixed GPT-OSS-120B downstream model on 127 questions. It compares five prompting strategies and asks whether prompt optimization compensates for limited router capacity and whether classification gains translate into downstream efficiency. The work targets the cost-quality tradeoff of indiscriminate capability activation.

entry.title: A Modular Framework for ESG Prediction through Domain-Specific Language Modeling and Graph Learning

author.name: Sofia Baiocco, Gianluca Bonifazi, Christopher Buratti, Michele Marchetti, Camilla Mazzoli, Federica Parlapiano, Giulia Quaglieri, Davide Traini, Domenico Ursino, Luca Virgili

entry.summary: ESGPred is a modular framework predicting corporate ESG scores by combining domain-specific language modeling with graph-based learning over a network of company relationships. The paper motivates data-driven ESG prediction by inconsistencies in proprietary rating methodologies and demonstrates effective score prediction alongside additional downstream uses.

entry.title: Care, Human Enfeeblement, and the Existential Implications of AGI

author.name: B. Scot Rousse

entry.summary: A philosophical paper reinterpreting Stuart Russell's human-enfeeblement risk through recent work on care and caregiving (Christian, Gopnik, Spivak) and the ontological design tradition of Winograd and Flores. It argues enfeeblement is not mere cognitive off-loading but a disengagement from the world understood as erosion of cultivable capacities to care.

entry.title: Finite-Cadence Refresh Equilibria for Streaming Prior-Anchored Ridge: A Closed-Form Forgetting Window and Spectral Correction

author.name: Mrigank Shekhar Singh

entry.summary: A theoretical analysis of recursive ridge estimators on drifting data streams, deriving a closed-form spectral decomposition for the forgetting trade-off in prior-anchored ridge regression when the anchor is refreshed every k steps. It characterizes a finite-cadence equilibrium with an explicit lag and variance-reduction factor, and gives optimal refresh cadence and plug-in scheduling.

entry.title: Multiple-Choice Secretary Problem with Predictions

author.name: Jing Yuan, Qi Cai, Xin Gao, Shaojie Tang

entry.summary: Studies the multiple-choice secretary problem where value predictions are available before candidates arrive, improving on a known learning-augmented algorithm by removing a logarithmic factor through sharper analysis and a retuned threshold. The result yields a competitive ratio depending on selection capacity and maximum prediction error, with exact predictions approaching optimal selection.

entry.title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM

author.name: Maforikan Amoussou, Borja Aizpurua, Sukhbinder Singh, Rom\'an Or\'us, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: Introduces multi-head quantum neural networks that can replace transformer blocks inside pre-trained LLMs on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. The design partitions the hidden space into heads, angle-encodes each into small qubit registers, and couples heads with constrained classical mixers, claiming near-parity accuracy with far fewer parameters at 30B-model scale.

entry.title: WaveFlow-UIE: A Single-Pipeline Wavelet-Domain Flow Model for Efficient Underwater Image Restoration

author.name: Abdulaziz Alfaraj, Mohammed Al Naser, Hassan Al Nasser, Muzammil Behzad

entry.summary: Presents WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline model for underwater image restoration that applies a discrete wavelet transform, estimates physics-inspired degradation cues such as transmission and ambient light, and conditions a flow-matching velocity network in wavelet space. The design avoids costly multi-stage diffusion pipelines while addressing frequency-dependent degradation effects.

entry.title: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads

author.name: Fabrizia Giulia Garavaglia, Marco Giunti

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether groups of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions can be viewed as a biological construction of Transformer attention heads, under a mathematical instantiation that need not match the standard Transformer form. It maps correspondences between attention-head functional organization and neurophysiological mechanisms in human language processing.

entry.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN

author.name: Taiga Saito, Fabian Campos Montero, Bruno Zuada Coelho, Ana Martins Teixeira, Stephen Wu, Timo Schweckendiek, Yu Otake

entry.summary: The study applies TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on synthetic tabular data, to reconstruct 2D subsurface sections from sparse cone penetration test data without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. It evaluates against SchemaGAN and reference interpretations at two field sites in the Netherlands.

entry.title: Where in the Input Does a One-Pass Decision Encoder Look?

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Allan Kevin T

entry.summary: This paper analyzes Laya, a small one-pass multiple-choice question answering model limited to a 512-token window, measuring the accuracy cost when evidence falls outside the window. Using 177 controlled test items with evidence placed at chosen offsets across five tasks, three checkpoints, and four window sizes (93,275 scored requests), the authors find accuracy collapses to roughly 26-27 percent when evidence is beyond the window, near chance. The work offers a careful methodological study of positional limitations in fixed-window decision encoders.

entry.title: MusicRWKV: A Multimodal RWKV Framework for Music Representation Learning

author.name: Terry Tan

entry.summary: MusicRWKV applies the RWKV linear-attention architecture to music representation learning, jointly modeling waveform, spectrogram, and metadata in a unified self-supervised framework. It includes an invertible compression module for long musical sequences and FiLM-based conditioning, avoiding the quadratic attention cost of Transformers.

entry.title: Profile-Based Auditing of Domestic Violence Survey Selection Across South Asia

author.name: Mohammad Abu Obaida Mullick, Rezaur Rahman Ratul, Mymuna Nourin, Md. Motaharul Islam

entry.summary: Uses DHS data for nearly 800,000 women across five South Asian countries to identify six interpretable demographic profiles and assess whether these profiles predict selection into the domestic violence survey module. It evaluates 22 ML models under sampling-unit-aware cross-validation to audit potential selection bias in sensitive survey data.

entry.title: Serving-Aligned Entire-Space Conversion Modeling via Click-Through Rate Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Pavel Dolin, Xun Zou, Jiatian Wu, Deguang Kong

entry.summary: Identifies a training-serving mismatch in ESMM-style conversion modeling where the deployed pCVR tower is paired with a separately trained serving pCTR model that differs from the auxiliary tower. It distills logged serving pCTR scores into the auxiliary tower to align pCTCVR at serving time, improving ranking decisions.

entry.title: Protected Unbiased Sparsification: A Sharp Loewner Curve

author.name: Ziyang Wang, Menghao Li

entry.summary: Studies random sparsification of probability vectors subject to unbiasedness, exact preservation of protected linear statistics, and covariance guarantees, constructing schemes with a provably sharp covariance coefficient via a Loewner-order analysis. The result gives optimal variance bounds as a function of support size and effective rank of protected statistics.

entry.title: Observations Drift, Structures Remain: Structural Pretraining with Time Alignment for Electromagnetic Signals

author.name: Wenjin Gui, Junyu Shen, Haibo Xu, Yuchuang Sun, Luqing Luo, Wupeng Xie, Qian Huang, Fengxiang Wang, Yangang Sun, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Analyzes why reconstruction-based self-supervised pretraining on heterogeneous electromagnetic I/Q observations fails due to appearance and temporal mismatches from propagation and acquisition variation, and proposes structural pretraining with time alignment to learn reusable structure while discarding observation-specific artifacts.

entry.title: WELP : Weighted Ensemble in the LooP for committor learning

author.name: Jacky Chen, Rishal Aggarwal, David Ryan Koes

entry.summary: The paper couples committor function learning with weighted ensemble enhanced sampling in a WE-in-the-loop framework, alternating between refining the committor as a collective variable and using it to drive rare-transition sampling for molecular systems. This addresses the circular dependency of needing to sample the transitions the committor describes.

entry.title: Subject-Held-Out Evaluation of Deep Ground Reaction Force Estimators Across Two Laboratories: Leakage and Cross-Laboratory Transfer

author.name: Hernan David Santos, Yinong Chen, Yu Ding, Xudong Zhang, Jian Tao

entry.summary: This study evaluates three deep sequence models for estimating ground reaction forces under subject-held-out and cross-laboratory protocols, quantifying the cost of common leakage-prone trial-level splits and whether models transfer between labs. It uses two independent datasets, one pipeline, one tuning procedure, and multiple seeds for rigor.

entry.title: MS-rPPG: Multi-spectral State Space Model for Remote Photoplethysmography in Driver Monitoring Systems

author.name: Jiho Choi, Sang Jun Lee

entry.summary: MS-rPPG combines RGB and near-infrared face video via a cross-spectral state space model to estimate heart rate robustly under challenging driving conditions with variable illumination and head movement. It targets driver health monitoring where standard rPPG degrades.

entry.title: Clustering trajectories of modelled estimates: an uncertainty-aware framework, with an application to global cardiovascular disease burden, 1990 to 2023

author.name: Eben Afrifa-Yamoah

entry.summary: The paper proposes an uncertainty-aware trajectory clustering framework that separates level from shape, quantifies cluster membership via perturbation within uncertainty intervals, and selects clusters by stability, applied to cardiovascular disease DALY rates for 201 countries from GBD data. It reveals roles of development, region, and measurement quality.

entry.title: Katz Kernel Based Stratification of Breast Cancer Patients

author.name: Francesco Cellitti, Lorenzo Di Rocco, Livia Perfetto, Veronica Lombardo, Umberto Ferraro Petrillo

entry.summary: The paper applies graph kernels (Katz kernel) to mechanistic signaling network models of patients to stratify breast cancer cohorts by comparing pathway structures rather than mutations alone. This enables identification of clinically meaningful subgroups in precision oncology.

entry.title: On-Edge Acoustic Continual Anomaly Detection: A Cross-Platform Comparative Study

author.name: Rami Zewail, Yehia Ehab, Karim Ali, Ahmed Mahrous, Mohamed Awad, Bassem Mokhtar

entry.summary: This comparative study deploys continual acoustic anomaly detection for machine condition monitoring on two embedded platforms (ESP32-S3 and Arduino Nicla Vision) using a lightweight ShallowNet encoder with contrastive prototype learning and TensorFlow Lite Micro. It examines performance under microphone variation and operational drift, filling a gap left by offline-only research.

entry.title: Reliable Near-Field Source Enumeration and Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC

author.name: Jiaying Li, Haifeng Wen, Changsheng You, Yuanwei Liu, Hong Xing

entry.summary: This signal-processing paper develops conformal-risk-control-based source enumeration and MUSIC-informed positioning for near-field coherent multipath environments, calibrating penalty coefficients to bound miss-detection risk. The approach explicitly controls source-underestimation and positioning uncertainty for future location-aware wireless systems.

entry.title: Random Exploration is Random

author.name: Yingkang Luo, Hua-Dong Xiong, Hanbo Xie, Caroline Phelps, Madeline Harms, Ryan Smith, James Waltz, Robert Wilson

entry.summary: Using the Horizon Task with 1,392 participants and over 1.27 million trials, the authors test whether human random exploration reflects genuine stochasticity or deterministic structure that standard cognitive models miss. They find that more expressive computational models fail to beat simple random exploration in capturing choice variability, suggesting human exploratory variability is largely noise-like.

entry.title: Sheaf-Inspired Structured Scoring Extensions of LightGCN for Collaborative Filtering

author.name: Ksenia Belkovskaya, Timur Lidzhiev, Maria Stebliy, Alexander Tarakanov

entry.summary: The paper proposes a modular, sheaf-inspired scoring layer on top of a three-layer LightGCN backbone, replacing the standard inner-product scorer with diagonal, low-rank, or full matrix residual transformations of user and item embeddings. It compares these variants against parameter-matched MLP baselines on four standard recommendation benchmarks.

entry.title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models

author.name: Tiago de Souza Farias, Caio Moraes Porto, Matheus da Silva Fonseca, Nicolas Armando Cabrera Carpi, Anderson de Araujo Oliveira, Celso Jorge Villas-Boas

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether a frozen general-purpose LLM can generate parameters for variational quantum circuits from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions. LLM-generated parameters underperform Adam optimization on general Hamiltonians, but work comparatively better on structured parent Hamiltonians and molecular systems.

entry.title: IsharaBART: An efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation

author.name: Aonmoy Das, Ananna Dev Aishi, Md. Fazlul Kader

entry.summary: Introduces IsharaBART, a bidirectional BART-based generative framework for gloss-sentence translation in Bangla Sign Language, with a 1,000-pair professionally annotated dataset expanded to 4,831 pairs via augmentation. Targets low-resource, computationally light deployment.

entry.title: How Far Can Frozen Vision-Language Models Go on Event Data? A Training-Free Study on EventBench

author.name: Md Kamrujjaman Mobin, Md Salman Shamil, Md Adnan Arefeen

entry.summary: This challenge-entry study measures how far a frozen, RGB-pretrained Qwen3.5 9B vision-language model can go on event-camera tasks without any training, by rendering event bins as red/blue frames, selecting subsets, stitching grid images, and using category-specific prompts. It covers four of five EventBench categories including gesture recognition, causal reasoning, and event OCR. The result quantifies the zero-shot transfer gap between RGB and event-modal data for VLMs.

entry.title: Actuation and Control of Passive Tendon-Driven Soft Extensions Through Rigid Manipulator Motion

author.name: Ignacio Cuiral-Zueco, Gonzalo L\'opez-Nicol\'as, Youcef Mezouar

entry.summary: The paper proposes actuating a passive tendon-driven soft extension using only the motion of a rigid manipulator, avoiding dedicated actuation hardware, and develops a controller that regulates the soft tip while respecting end-effector constraints such as fitting through narrow apertures. This rigid-soft combination targets inspection tasks where industrial reach and precision must coexist with compliant contact. It is a clever systems contribution bridging soft robotics and industrial manipulation.

entry.title: SPARC: RoboCup Standard Platform for Autonomous Rescue Competition with Initial Datasets, Software, and Simulation Environments

author.name: Yuezhong Wang, Bichi Zhang, Zhongli Yin, Pingcong Li, Raimund Edlinger, S\"oren Schwertfeger

entry.summary: SPARC is a new RoboCup Rescue Robot League competition built around the Unitree A2-W as a standard platform, designed to let research groups without custom-hardware expertise work on autonomous rescue robotics. The paper describes the competition format, benchmark environments, released datasets, software, and simulation tooling. Standardized platforms have historically accelerated research communities, so this could do the same for disaster-response robotics.

entry.title: Robot-Induced Bias in Movement Smoothness Metrics for Rehabilitation: Quantification and Correction in Simulation

author.name: David Regev, Alex Scherbakov, Eran Beeri Bamani

entry.summary: The paper shows that robot mechanics can systematically bias kinematic recovery metrics such as log dimensionless jerk (LDLJ) used in rehabilitation, potentially invalidating cross-device comparisons. Using a closed-loop human-robot simulation calibrated to published healthy and stroke kinematics, the authors quantify bias (median 0.93 and 1.79 benchmark units for stroke and healthy profiles) and identify Coulomb friction and apparent mass as leading contributors via Sobol analysis. This is an important methodological warning for the rehabilitation robotics field.

entry.title: Prediction-Error-Tightened MPC for Socially Compliant Crowd Navigation

author.name: Alessandro Febbraro, Federico Rollo, Marcello Farina, Luca Bascetta, Navvab Kashiri

entry.summary: The work extends an MPC framework for crowd navigation by integrating pedestrian detection, Koopman-based motion prediction, and online prediction-error estimation directly inside the collision-avoidance mechanism, plus obstacle aggregation to reduce constraint counts in dense scenes. The goal is socially compliant navigation that respects pedestrian comfort while remaining computationally tractable. It is a competent control-theoretic contribution to a well-studied problem.

entry.title: Safe and Efficient Navigation Considering Texting Pedestrians via Attention-Aware Cost-map Tuning

author.name: Shunya Tadano, Yusuke Tamura, Ankit A. Ravankar, Yasuhisa Hirata

entry.summary: The paper presents an attention-aware robot navigation framework that classifies pedestrians as attentive or distracted in real time using 3D skeletal features and a Random Forest classifier, then dynamically widens cost-map safety margins around distracted individuals. A within-subjects user study with 12 participants and 252 trials shows significant gains in perceived smoothness and predictability. It targets the real safety problem of smartphone-distracted pedestrians who behave unpredictably.

entry.title: Ephemeral agents escape the Arrow Information Paradox

author.name: Keenan Pepper

entry.summary: The post argues that ephemeral AI agents, which can evaluate private information and then vanish without retaining or disclosing it, offer a novel resolution to the Arrow information paradox by making information appraisal possible without jumping the gun on the trade. This could enable new market mechanisms for selling secrets without NDAs or patents.

entry.title: There is no such thing as cosmophagous AI

author.name: Magmappie

entry.summary: A conceptual x-risk argument contesting the cosmophagous AI scenario (racing at near-light speed to grab cosmic resources before they recede over the cosmological horizon), which is sometimes invoked to argue an indifferent ASI would still kill humans. The author engages with Ryan Greenblatt's cost estimates for keeping humans alive and Tanner Cook's counterarguments to show the scenario is not physically coherent as stated.

entry.title: FDT and the sacrificial volunteer's dilemma

author.name: loops

entry.summary: The post analyzes a twin sacrificial volunteer's dilemma among 1000 identical deterministic agents, showing that not volunteering is dominant and all reasonable decision theories decline, then extends the analysis to agents with serial numbers to explore how functional decision theory handles asymmetries in the volunteering decision.

entry.title: Food Critic: An Agentic Visualization System for Auditable Restaurant-Safety Reasoning

author.name: Arleth Salinas, Ishrat Jahan Eliza, Valerio Pascucci

entry.summary: This paper presents Food Critic, an agentic visualization system for restaurant decision support that combines public health inspection records with crowd reviews. It compares three agent grounding conditions: a database-only ReAct agent, a retrieval-augmented agent with food-safety regulations, and an ontology-guided agent producing structured hypotheses. The focus on inspectable, auditable grounding addresses a real gap in agentic visualization.

entry.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings

author.name: Yiyu Qian, Pengfei Guo, Liyuan Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes ReShap, a policy-distillation framework extending Shapley-based interpretability of RL policies to high-dimensional state spaces and multi-action environments. It extracts compact features from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution, and fits surrogate policies to make deep RL behavior auditable.

entry.title: Can Model Answer Probabilities Represent Survey Populations? Conditional Prediction and Joint Validity in Jev Survey Simulation

author.name: Zengqing Wu, Chuan Xiao

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether the answer probabilities from Jev, a TypeSafe decision model, can faithfully simulate survey populations across 20 binary items from five archived survey waves. It compares population-only, conditional, and sequential prediction settings and examines joint validity of answer combinations rather than just marginal accuracy.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Generative Hallucination Detection and Correction for Aerial Image Captioning

author.name: Debolena Basak, Somsubhra De, Maunendra Sankar Desarkar

entry.summary: This paper targets hallucination in MLLM-generated captions for UAV aerial imagery, where extreme viewpoint variation and small objects amplify description errors. It proposes fine-grained detection and correction of generative hallucinations, supporting applications like surveillance, disaster response, and environmental monitoring.

entry.title: Edge-Gradient Augmentation under Reinforcement Learning for Temporal Graph

author.name: Yongqing Zhou, Jiawei Chen, Wenjun Wang, Xinyu Wang, Wei Yu, Qiyao Peng

entry.summary: EG-RL is a framework for temporal link prediction that explicitly encodes edge-change events (edge births and deaths) through dedicated node and link encoding modules, using a policy-driven reinforcement-learning mechanism to select and augment the most informative edge snapshots with critic-based feedback. It targets dynamic networks such as social networks and recommendation systems.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models

author.name: Tanzeel Abbas, Ahmad Kamran Malik, Nafees Qamar, Sana Liaqat

entry.summary: PECA introduces differentiable length control for smaller language models in clinical NLP, addressing excessive response verbosity that hinders point-of-care use. It avoids reliance on preference optimization, reward models, or proprietary teachers, keeping the approach accessible on commodity hardware.

entry.title: AI4Plasma II: Geometry-Aware Surrogate Modeling for Variable Electrode Gap GEC Plasmas

author.name: Hao Yang, Zhenyu Zou, Wenshuai Jie, Luowei Yin, Yufeng Wei, Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Zhichao Peng, Chun Chen, Kangxin Liu, Rubing Han, Haoran Guan, Yipei Chen, Peiting You, Yuwei Fan

entry.summary: Compares six geometry-aware surrogate modeling approaches (learned geometry mappings, extended-domain representations, continuous coordinates, geometry-native discretizations) for plasma simulations with variable electrode spacing, evaluating data-efficiency trade-offs for industrial plasma process design.

entry.title: Owned Edits to a Shared Decision Rule: Learning Private Exceptions as Typed, Gated, Withdrawable Weight Edits

author.name: John J. O'Hare

entry.summary: The paper describes a mechanism where organizations holding private evidence that a shared published decision rule is wrong learn owned, typed, gated, and withdrawable edits compiled into a ReLU network prior. Pre-registered analyses on synthetic data show the learner is non-inferior to pooled alternatives at small per-party data volumes without sharing data.

entry.title: Feature-Aware Edge Sampling for Approximate One-Step Laplacian Propagation

author.name: Jonathan Z. Sun, Zheng Wang, Kebin Xu

entry.summary: This work approximates one-step combinatorial Laplacian message passing in graph neural networks using a hybrid edge sampler combining feature-conditioned message scores and effective-resistance leverage scores, with derived optimal sampling probabilities and error bounds. Preliminary experiments on synthetic community graphs show modest accuracy gains as edge budget grows.

entry.title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes

author.name: Tobias Lettner, Tatyana Ivanovska, Anwar Al Assadi, Christian Bergler

entry.summary: This applied paper investigates deep learning methods for anomaly detection and error classification in industrial screwdriving processes, an area where traditional monitoring relies on window-based methods and envelope curves. Accurate detection of screwdriving errors matters for product quality, avoiding costly rework, and supporting sustainability through maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. The study evaluates how machine learning can leverage growing volumes of process data from manufacturing systems.

entry.title: Enhancing Preference Detection using Eye Movement Cascade and Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion

author.name: Yuanhong Wu, Mary Tsaryk, Sam Watson, Tahsin Ahmed, Christina Schweikert, D. Frank Hsu

entry.summary: This paper uses eye-tracking data of subjects comparing face image pairs to predict preference decisions from gaze behavior. It applies multiple ML classifiers combined through a Multi-layer Combinatorial Fusion framework that iteratively expands and prunes model fusions based on cognitive diversity.

entry.title: TAPES: Terminal Adjoint-Propagated Error Scheduling for Financial Diffusion Samplers

author.name: Yilie Huang

entry.summary: TAPES addresses numerical time-grid error in financial diffusion samplers used with few function evaluations, estimating signed local defects via Richardson comparisons and transporting them through the remaining flow and a terminal-report adjoint.
