It addresses a gap in existing benchmarks that give agents preprocessed inputs rather than raw multi-sensor archives.

entry.title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation

author.name: Reece Keller, Declan Kutscher, Xaq Pitkow, Aran Nayebi

entry.summary: The paper systematically integrates 24 intrinsic objectives — spanning curiosity, entropy, and competence — to study how intrinsically motivated experience collection shapes world-model representation learning and downstream control in the absence of extrinsic rewards. It addresses which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable world models that support generalization and adaptation.

entry.title: Darmok: Championship Cryptic Crossword Solving via Constraint Tightening and Resilient Orchestration

author.name: Siddhartha Chatterjee (The University of Texas at Austin)

entry.summary: Darmok is the first automated system to reach superhuman performance on British cryptic crosswords, solving all seven puzzles error-free at the 55th Times Crossword Championship and outpacing every human competitor, finishing the final 3m13s ahead of the human champion. It handles disguised definitions, compositional wordplay, and sparse grids via constraint tightening and resilient multi-agent orchestration.

entry.title: Wrong the Same Way: Cross-Prompt Sharing Both Suppresses and Amplifies Reward Hacking in RLVR

author.name: Michael Li, Rohan Pandey, Ray Chen

entry.summary: In a controlled environment where the full response distribution is computable, the paper shows that at its KL-regularized optimum RLVR acts as a filter over the accepted set, exactly inheriting reward-hack rates from the base model, with drift explained by covariances tied to cross-prompt leak universality and verifier false-positive rate. This reconciles the inherited-versus-amplified accounts of reward hacking.

entry.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Nathan Delisle, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: This work shows that massive activations in LLMs cause up to 99.9 percent of activation variance to lie along the first principal component, undermining standard sparse autoencoder evaluations based on variance explained and ablation damage. The authors demonstrate that PC1 features produce unstable importance rankings across SAE training runs and propose training SAEs on activations with the PC1 component bypassed as a correction.

entry.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Zihan Chen, Lei Nico Zheng, Di Zhu

entry.summary: Analyzing 1.27 million blind Chatbot Arena votes on version-fixed model pairs from May 2023 to August 2024, the authors show the share of both-are-bad votes rises about 1.7-1.9 percentage points per month, indicating human evaluators' standards are rising. This suggests perceived LLM regression partly reflects changing judges rather than degrading models.

entry.title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device

author.name: Evan Li, Krishna Deshpande, Wen Cheng, Shyamnath Gollakota

entry.summary: This paper introduces Mobile AI Factory, an agentic system that automatically produces fine-tuned and quantized small language models tailored to a specific task and mobile phone. An orchestrator LLM decides between hyperparameter tuning, real data mining, and synthetic data generation, while rule-based rollbacks discard harmful changes and searches span base models and quantizations using real on-device measurements. It matters because it automates expert-intensive SLM deployment, enabling private, offline AI on consumer hardware.

entry.title: Learn-To-Propagate: Distributionally Robust Motion Planning for Nonlinear Uncertain Systems

author.name: Eduardo Figueiredo, Adrien Banse, Qi Heng Ho, Raphael Jungers, Morteza Lahijanian, Luca Laurenti

entry.summary: L2P-DR-Forest is a distributionally robust sampling-based motion planner for nonlinear stochastic systems with unknown initial-state and noise distributions, using optimal transport to learn ambiguity sets from data while providing formal correctness guarantees. This relaxes the linearity and known-distribution assumptions of prior safe planning work.

entry.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey

author.name: Ehsan Mirafzali, Razvan Marinescu

entry.summary: This survey unifies flow and diffusion models through three geometric lenses (state space, probability-measure space, and path space), showing that core score identities reduce to integration by parts and connecting the theory to Malliavin calculus. It covers applications from images and video to proteins, molecules, physical fields, and increasingly language.

entry.title: Transformers Provably Learn Graph Search: Training Dynamics and the Exponential Power of Depth

author.name: Xutao Ma, Somayeh Sojoudi

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that one-layer transformers require Omega(N^2) size to implement the DFS child-selection primitive on dense graphs, while a two-layer transformer achieves full DFS with O(N log N) size, making the second layer necessary and sufficient for near-linear DFS reasoning. The analysis extends to deeper models, characterizing training dynamics and exponential benefits of depth.

entry.title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning

author.name: Bo Dai, Yilun Du

entry.summary: This tutorial by Bo Dai and Yilun Du uses energy-based models as a unifying lens over machine learning, organizing methods around three choices: the energy, the inference procedure, and the learning method. It covers sampling, variational inference, maximum likelihood, noise contrastive estimation, pseudolikelihood, score matching, and adversarial training within a single framework.

entry.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design

author.name: Zhangmai Li, Tianrui Ma, Zheng Weng, Mo Zou, Zidong Du, Yifan Hao, Yongwei Zhao, Wei Li, Jing Li, Qi Guo, Yunji Chen

entry.summary: ICLayout-Bench evaluates LLM agents using real EDA tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level netlists, scoring layouts via physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. It spans 165 tasks across 13 process design kits from 3nm to 180nm covering analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits, from a team associated with ICT/CAS chip research.

entry.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN

author.name: Denis Grachev, Damien LaRocque, Omar Moured

entry.summary: This paper shows that simple retrieval of nearby demonstrations with action-chunk reuse achieves 91.7% on LIBERO without any policy training, degrading least under LIBERO-Plus perturbations. Across nine public VLAs, fine-tuning largely improves the vision-language backbone as a retrieval key while outputs stay close to demonstrations, motivating a Local Action Consistency metric.

entry.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving

author.name: Haolin Jiang, Weihang Li, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jinwen Pan, Santosh Pandey, Hang Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a linear attention sink phenomenon: queries, keys, and values in linear attention concentrate in a stable low-dimensional subspace, making recurrent states effectively low-rank. SinkState exploits this by storing recurrent states in adaptive low-rank form via on-the-fly SVD, cutting memory traffic that otherwise dominates decoding cost at large batch sizes. This addresses a real inefficiency in serving hybrid attention models.

entry.title: Counterfactual Analysis of Extent Leakage from Annotation-Derived Prompts in Vision-Language Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Niran Nataraj, Ankita Das, C. Krishna Mohan, Kenji Kawashima

entry.summary: This paper reveals benchmark leakage in text-guided medical segmentation: on colonoscopy and chest X-ray benchmarks, caption words describing lesion size, count, and location were derived from the very masks used for scoring. Counterfactual experiments show keeping only the extent word recovers 84-98% of the caption's improvement over an empty caption, and a polyp called a rock segments just as well. The finding questions how much reported gains in text-guided segmentation reflect genuine visual grounding.

entry.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model

author.name: Amani Kiruga, Zhiyi Li, Ruojin Cai, Hansen Lillemark, Xiaoshan Wu, Ayush Tewari, Yilun Du

entry.summary: UGG is a unified generative framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric outputs such as depth and camera pose, formulating visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion in one model with modality- and time-dependent noise levels. This enables learning from heterogeneous datasets and unifying feedforward geometry prediction with generative synthesis.

entry.title: Framing-Induced Vulnerability in Large Language Models: Evidence from Chinese News Headlines

author.name: Mo Zhou, Yiwei Zhang

entry.summary: This study examines whether LLM judgments of news headlines track the underlying facts or the framing, combining an ecological audit of 63,926 Chinese headlines with controlled experiments on 30 real and 30 synthetic events across four Chinese models. Changing only the headline frame systematically shifted perceived misleadingness and severity, with emotionally intensified frames raising severity ratings by 0.65-0.88 points consistently across DeepSeek, MiMo, Dots, and LongCat. The findings matter because LLMs increasingly gatekeep news moderation, and framing susceptibility is a systemic vulnerability.

entry.title: Spatial-Spectral Coupling as Attention: Scaling Shape Correspondence to High-Resolution Surfaces

author.name: Bence Demeter, Kilian Ehrenreich, Amelie Kleber, Ioana Oprisiu, Philipp Spohn, Christian Wachinger, Fabian Bongratz, Lennart Bastian

entry.summary: The paper shows that the spatial-spectral coupling at the core of functional-map shape matching is mathematically equivalent to scaled dot-product attention, with descriptors as queries/keys and spectral bases as values. This insight allows modern efficient attention implementations to scale functional-map pipelines to high-resolution meshes, improving runtime and memory. A clean theoretical connection with immediate practical payoff.

entry.title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning

author.name: Xuheng Zhang, Yiming Zhang, Jialin Gao, Hao Chen, Jiaming Liu, Ji Li, Runzhong Huang, Yinxi Wang, Chenyang Gu, Zihan Yang, Yaowei Liu, Zhonghao Yan, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Peng Jia, Pheng-Ann Heng, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: LaST0.5 is a generalist world action model for manipulation that inserts an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation, arguing that global scene representations underemphasize local robot-object interactions. It aims to align representations optimized for world evolution with those needed for manipulation control.

entry.title: PARDIG: Global Precipitation Estimates Learned from Sparse Satellite Observations

author.name: Guy Shalev, Stephan Rasp, Boris Babenko, Andrew El-Kadi, Mohammed Alewi Hassen, Samier Merchant, Fred Zyda, Dominic Masters, Ferran Alet, Salva R\"uhling Cachay, Ilan Price, Akib Uddin, Nofar Peled Levi, Ben Gaiarin, Aaron Bell, Peter Battaglia, Alvaro Sanchez-Gonzalez

entry.summary: PARDIG is an AI framework using a spherical graph-mesh transformer to produce near-real-time global precipitation estimates, trained on dense multi-modal inputs (atmospheric state analyses and geostationary satellite imagery) to predict sparse, high-precision spaceborne radar measurements. The author list includes prominent researchers associated with Google DeepMind weather and precipitation work (e.g., Rasp, Battaglia, Sanchez-Gonzalez, Price). Global precipitation estimation is vital for disaster response and Earth system science, and this system trades off skill, latency, coverage, and resolution in a principled way.

entry.title: DexSeed: Expanding Human Hand-Object Interactions into Robot Demonstrations for Dexterous Policy Learning

author.name: Huaijin Pi, Zehong Shen, Yong Wang, Kechun Xu, Changpeng Wang, Dingkun Wei, Xueyang Wang, Wenjia Wang, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Taku Komura

entry.summary: DexSeed is a framework for generating diverse, physically executable robot demonstrations for dexterous VLA learning by expanding human hand-object interaction datasets, covering varied objects and manipulation locations while producing executable arm and finger actions and visual observations. It avoids the cost of teleoperated data collection.

entry.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases

author.name: Josip Vrdoljak, Akash Singh, Bas Steunebrink, Alex Yarotsky, John Lorenzo, Achille Nicoletti, Sam Pigott

entry.summary: ExpertCrowd-SWE is a benchmark of 100 expert-authored, multi-file software engineering tasks written by practicing engineers against pinned commits of 87 real open-source repositories across 11 languages, each with a sealed reference solution and a calibrated, weighted, mostly-executable grader. Median reference solutions change 471 lines, targeting realistic maintainer-level changes in unfamiliar large codebases.

entry.title: Agent Benchmarks Stop Ranking Before They Run Out of Tasks

author.name: Zihan Dong, Qishi Zhan, Minxuan Hu

entry.summary: This paper argues that saturation in agent benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified and MLE-bench stems largely from measurement design rather than task exhaustion, since most benchmarks reduce runs to a single pass/fail bit. Re-scoring released runs across eight benchmarks, the authors show top agents differ by less than test noise and that coarse binary scoring hides meaningful performance distinctions.

entry.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Federico Ravenda, Mirko Cesarini, Daniele Montagnani, Volodymyr Karpenko, Antonietta Mira, Andrea Raballo

entry.summary: Hx2Dx ARENA is an interactive benchmark of 1,000 NEJM-derived clinical cases evaluating whether LLMs can actively gather diagnostic evidence through history-taking and testing rather than merely inferring over pre-condensed vignettes. It reframes clinical LLM evaluation around the iterative inquiry process of real diagnosis.

entry.title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation

author.name: Daniel P. Jeong, Yewon Byun, John Giorgi, Peng Xu, Zachary C. Lipton, Michael Oberst

entry.summary: On real-world deployment data of an AI clinical documentation product, over 45% of clinician edits contain user-added information not supported by model inputs, so naive fine-tuning on edits risks teaching hallucination. The paper develops a method to filter and learn from only actionable feedback in clinician edit data.

entry.title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG

author.name: Dara Varam, Taraneh Aminosharieh Najafi, David Atienza

entry.summary: The paper extends weight-space programming, where language models read and edit a trained network's weights directly instead of relying on gradient descent, to biosignal models trained on EEG and ECG data. The authors show frontier models can debug planted faults without being told what they are, and can even write all network weights from scratch given only the architecture, task, and minimal specification.

entry.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Xinwei Yang, Rongqing Li, Luyu Chen, Kieran Wong, Yudong Guo, Xinrui Wang, Jiayin Zhu, Gu Simiu, Sulong Xu, Cong Fang

entry.summary: The paper tackles on-policy distillation for agent memory control, showing that distillation weakens when memory tools and compaction protocols lie outside both teacher and student pre-training. It introduces CAMG-II, a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments, and demonstrates that mapping memory control onto pre-trained file-operation primitives unlocks memory capability for long-horizon coding tasks.

entry.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models

author.name: Tomer Solberg

entry.summary: Sable is a cryptographic argument system that proves, bit for bit, that a quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a prompt, using a fully integer-defined inference function with no floating-point ambiguity. It combines sumcheck proofs, LogUp-GKR lookups, and Reed-Solomon/BaseFold commitments, with a streaming single-GPU prover.

entry.title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models

author.name: Anshul Kumar, Neha Prasad, Manoj Kumar, Barnab\'as P\'oczos, Deeksha Varshney

entry.summary: The paper argues that linear probe accuracy conflates four distinct claims about internal representations — decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use — and introduces a four-stage Bayesian pipeline to test them separately, applied to arithmetic structures in LLMs. This provides a more rigorous methodology for interpretability claims about geometric features.

entry.title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)

author.name: Ziqing Xu, Hancheng Min, Lachlan Ewen MacDonald, Salma Tarmoun, Enrique Mallada, Weijie Su, Rene Vidal

entry.summary: This theory paper explains two empirically observed properties of LoRA—robustness to catastrophic forgetting and the ability to merge independently trained adapters—via a unified margin-based analysis of multiclass linear classification under near-orthogonal task regressions. The authors analyze how low-rank updates preserve margins on previous tasks, yielding the MaLoRA method. Strong author list including Rene Vidal, Weijie Su, and Sham Kakade collaborators.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Sample Complexity of Deterministic Agnostic PAC Learning

author.name: Shai Ben-David, Steve Hanneke, Farnam Mansouri, Amirreza Shaeiri

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves a large gap in agnostic PAC learning under deterministic labels, a misspecification model between realizable and fully agnostic settings. It proves that classes of VC dimension d and finite diameter K are learnable with near-optimal sample complexity, sharpening prior bounds that left a wide gap.

entry.title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time

author.name: Daniel Barter, Jacob C. Bridgeman, Chris Dawson, Terry Farrelly, Shane Fleming, Mercedes Gimeno-Segovia, Paul Hartke, Timothy Hein, Sean Howell, Gregory Hyegang Jun, Siddhartha Kamalakara, Yehua Liu, Jose M. Monsalve Diaz, Eddie Richter, Sam Roberts

entry.summary: PRISM is a transformer-based machine-learning decoder for photonic fusion-based quantum computing that exploits known erasure locations under combined Pauli and erasure errors. Benchmarked across surface, color, and quantum LDPC fault-tolerant protocols at distances up to 24, it matches logical performance of strong baselines while addressing throughput, latency, and scalability requirements. This is a substantive step toward real-time decoding for fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.

entry.title: What drives the emergence of symbolic mechanisms in large language models?

author.name: Melody Zixuan Li, Taylor Webb

entry.summary: Trains transformers from scratch on abstract sequence tasks while varying architectural and data-distributional factors, then uses representational, attentional, and causal mediation analyses to identify what drives the emergence of symbolic mechanisms. It finds greater data diversity across multiple axes produces stronger symbolic signatures.

entry.title: OpticalRAG: Pixel-Space Compression for Token-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Senhao Liu, Yuheng Zhang, Chunyu Wei, Yueguo Chen, Xinran Zhang

entry.summary: OpticalRAG reframes RAG context-length bottlenecks as a problem of compression modality, rendering documents as page images and encoding them with a frozen vision encoder into roughly a hundred visual tokens with little semantic loss. This pixel-space compression opens a fidelity-cost tradeoff that one-dimensional textual compression cannot reach, since no information is irreversibly discarded at tokenization time. The approach is a notable direction for token-efficient retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference

author.name: Zhimin Hu, Chen Jiang, Hanbo Xie, N. Apurva Ratan Murty, Sashank Varma

entry.summary: This position paper argues that mechanistic interpretability (MI) research should focus not just on observing internal model structures but on the inferential logic connecting those observations to mechanistic explanations. Drawing parallels with neuroscience, the authors identify recurring inferential bottlenecks and propose five principles organized into a recurring framework for stronger causal and explanatory claims.

entry.title: The Target Is a Predicate: Predicate-State Grounding for Semantic-Level Video Reasoning Segmentation

author.name: Yuhuan Hong, Yiming Ren, Zhiqiang Lin, Feize Wu, Xingyun Liu, Yitong Xie, Lei Zhou, Lisheng Wu, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Predicate-State Video Reasoning Segmentation, where the segmentation target is a dynamic predicate over objects and time rather than a fixed identity, handling states like active versus vacant intervals and target switching. The authors build PS-Bench with 2,077 videos and 16,250 queries annotated with predicate states, temporal intervals, and masks, and propose a State-Bind-Emit pipeline. This addresses systematic over-emission of masks in existing video segmentation methods.

entry.title: RiSE-Drive: Risk-Sensitive Long-Horizon Candidate Evaluation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yu Zhao, Hongyi Duan, Ming Yin, Hongyuan Zhang, Fan Yang, Hongzhi Wang, Xiubo Liang

entry.summary: RiSE-Drive addresses trajectory-candidate selection in end-to-end autonomous driving by evaluating candidates via risk-sensitive latent future rollouts rather than deterministic point scores, aiming to capture tail risk, delayed failures, and ranking instability. This reframes the driving pipeline problem from generation to long-horizon evaluation under uncertainty.

entry.title: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats

author.name: Jan Wehner

entry.summary: Adapted from an IAPS report, this post proposes running honeypots—fake opportunities for malicious actions—continuously inside and around deployed AI agents rather than only during evaluations. The authors argue deployment-time honeypots can detect misbehavior, incriminate malicious agents, and deter attacks, and they lay out a concrete research agenda for implementation.

entry.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions

author.name: Adi Mashiach

entry.summary: Bonbon is a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on roughly 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences without task supervision. From a single representation space it exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at different resolutions: mechanism-of-action prediction, binding-site localization with orthosteric/allosteric discrimination, and covalent versus non-covalent bond classification, all generalizing to out-of-distribution complexes. This extends the emergent-capability paradigm to structural biology.

entry.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs

author.name: Subhrangshu Nandi, Hitesh Arora, Yunfei Bai, Udita Patel, Chirag Shah, Hannah Kwon, Wei Zhang, Weian Chen, Chloe Ruoqi Li, Alberto Sconfienza, Ayush Goyal, Yasmine Lee, Ming Xiong, Prathap Ramachandra

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of four LLM agent architectures (single function-calling agent, skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, triage swarm) across 13 enterprise SOPs, holding model, tasks, and tools fixed. It finds no universal best architecture — success on a given SOP ranges widely — and introduces a skill-definition quality rubric.

entry.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks

author.name: Daoan Zhang, Qinbo Bai, Dehai Min, Xingyu Mu, Ziyi Chen, Jianing Yin

entry.summary: Veritas is a harness that automatically generates verifiers for agent tasks, which are normally hand-written and do not scale, using three mechanisms: evidence headers stating what the verifier observes, a library of unstated domain rules, and authoring principles refined via self-improvement. It is evaluated on six benchmarks, including certifying official execution-based verifiers.

entry.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries

author.name: Zhenhong Zhou, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Qiankun Li, Kun Wang, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: The paper resolves debate over expert specialization in Mixture-of-Experts models by moving analysis to the neuron level with a new measure, Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP). It finds domain-specialized neuron sets with 58-74% within-domain overlap versus 15-24% across domains, and traces how this organization evolves during training.

entry.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation

author.name: Jin-Fei Qi, Yiduo Li, Jiang-Xin Shi, Kan Liu, Tao Lan, Hanlin Tang, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: ADIndex addresses the bottleneck that DeepSeek Sparse Attention's indexer scores the entire causal prefix per query, accounting for over 50% of prefill GPU time at long context. It combines layer-wise calibration for cross-query retrieval overlap, group-level distillation, and adaptive indexing to cut indexing latency in token-level sparse attention.

entry.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction

author.name: Mohamed Ghanem, Bernd Finkbeiner

entry.summary: This paper applies the path signature transform from rough path theory to encode execution traces for program synthesis from traces. The log-signature encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines across Karel, List, and RASP domains, with the largest gains in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Autonomous Optimization of Numerical Algorithms by an AI Agent: Application to Atomistic Simulation

author.name: Jeheon Woo

entry.summary: AIOA uses an LLM coding agent in a verifier-guarded loop to improve numerical algorithms in the ASE atomistic simulation library, optimizing both implementation speed and method convergence. Agents made six kernels 22-24x faster and reduced required force evaluations by roughly 3x on unseen problems.

entry.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution

author.name: Yikun Zhang, Minghao Guo, Guangxue Xu, Peter Yichen Chen, Wojciech Matusik, Wengong Jin, Jingjing Chai, Kaiyi Jiang

entry.summary: ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model for protein engineering, pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, that uses a mutation-biased attention architecture (MutationFormer) to jointly represent sequence, evolutionary, and structural information. It treats mutations as actions in a latent space whose functional consequences are predicted, enabling in silico closed-loop protein evolution across rugged fitness landscapes. The MIT-affiliated author list (Matusik, Chen) and DMS pretraining give it credibility in computational protein design.

entry.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?

author.name: Vikash Singh, Weicong Chen, Debargha Ganguly, Yanyan Zhang, Mohsen Hariri, Sreehari Sankar, Wang Yang, Chaoda Song, Alexander Nemecek, Osama Zafar, Yuting Shao, Kai Ye, Biyao Zhang, Xinpeng Li, Shouren Wang, Erman Ayday, Jing Ma, Sanmukh Rao Kuppannagari, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: The paper questions whether dense process rewards in GRPO-based RLVR justify their compute, noting that Monte-Carlo continuation sampling for step-level rewards consumed 91 percent of generated tokens in their setting. It introduces a matched-compute protocol that gives every training intervention the same token and GPU-hour budget and evaluates it in preregistered experiments.

entry.title: Specify Privacy Yourself: Assessing Inference-Time Personalized Privacy Preservation Ability of Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xingqi Wang, Xiaoyuan Yi, Xing Xie, Jia Jia

entry.summary: The paper introduces ITP3, the task of letting users dynamically specify personalized privacy boundaries through language, and SPY-Bench, a 32,700-sample benchmark evaluating whether large vision-language models can honor such specifications when images could reveal sensitive personal information. It finds current LVLMs handle universal privacy but struggle with personalized, context-dependent boundaries.

entry.title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks

author.name: Chenhui Hu, Pengfei Cao, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: The paper formally defines fundamental representational units (FRUs) in neural networks with fidelity and stability criteria, and proves that threshold-activated sparse autoencoders can identify FRUs under appropriate conditions. Large-scale experiments validate the theory and connect learned units to human conceptual structure.

entry.title: Byzantine-Robust Muon: Resilient Momentum Orthogonalization for Distributed Learning

author.name: Grigory Malinovsky, Yury Demidovich, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic robustness analysis of the Muon optimizer family, studying momentum-orthogonalization updates with robust aggregation under a unified first-order trust-region framework. It derives convergence guarantees for non-convex objectives without i.i.d. assumptions and introduces a non-Euclidean heterogeneity notion.

entry.title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent Depth for Causal Encoder-Decoders

author.name: Jiaqi Leng, Minshen Zhang, Zhaofeng Sun, Yu-Yang Qian, Peng Zhao, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper designs a looped causal encoder-decoder architecture that adds recurrent computation depth without any per-round growth of the KV cache, by placing recurrence in sparse encoder layers that produce the global KV states. Training under stochastic recurrence depth induces a fixed-point equilibrium, yielding language-modeling gains while preserving long-context scaling. This matters for inference efficiency, since KV cache size is a primary constraint on serving batch sizes.

entry.title: BioXArena-Pro: a research-grade benchmark for autonomous biomedical machine learning agents

author.name: Loka Li, Duzhen Zhang, Xingbo Du, Leonard Song, Kun Zhang, Le Song

entry.summary: BioXArena-Pro is a benchmark of 64 research-level biomedical modeling tasks rebuilt from published studies, with most tasks holding out entire biological units (species, cohorts) to prevent leakage. Across 22 agent configurations the best agent scores 55.1/100, and scaffold choice matters nearly as much as the model; on rebuilt tasks published methods trail agents by 8.2 points, suggesting agents benefit from adapting to new data. From strong authors (Kun Zhang, Le Song), this addresses saturation and leakage in existing agent benchmarks and measures whether coding agents can genuinely do biomedical research modeling.

entry.title: Deviation-Aware Pretraining for Cardiovascular Disease Detection from Electrocardiograms

author.name: Siyuan Yan, Haibo Zheng, Feng Lu, Wei Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces a self-supervised pretraining framework for 12-lead ECG analysis trained on nearly one million unlabeled recordings. It combines two modules: one that localizes waveform-level deviations from normal patterns and another that reconstructs cross-lead associations to capture abnormalities spanning multiple leads. The work targets better generalization across diseases, patient populations, and acquisition settings than supervised task-specific models.

entry.title: Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models

author.name: Ruize Zheng, Xuyang Liu, Siyu Ren, Xiaobing Tu, Yinggui Wang, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: In a controlled 1B-token mathematical corpus study, standard next-token prediction during continual pre-training helps Llama-3.2-3B but degrades Qwen3-1.7B-Base, showing training data has model-dependent effects under fixed recipes. The proposed OPMD reformulates mid-training as active, on-policy distillation rather than offline text imitation. This offers a data-efficiency and robustness improvement for adapting LLMs to specialized domains.

entry.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them

author.name: James Rice, Ji Hwan Park, Andres Kwasinski

entry.summary: This audit reproduces the CAGE Challenge 4 reference defenders (KEEP and H-MARL Expert) in a pinned container and shows the benchmark measures less than assumed: the simulator silently discards actions for busy agents while charging for discarded Restores, and the documented observation hides the busy flag. Disabling the undocumented check costs KEEP 99.58 points and H-MARL 145.98 per episode, meaning published results depend on undocumented wrapper behavior. The paper is a serious reproducibility critique of a learned cyber-defense benchmark.

entry.title: Catch It Where It Happens: Real Time Error Correction During LLM Reasoning

author.name: Rotem Elimelech, Michael Shalyt, Ido Kaminer

entry.summary: Proposes online deterministic verification of LLM reasoning steps: many steps (especially in math and code) can be checked by code in real time as they are written, with no verifier LLM or GPU cost. Failed checks point out the mistake so the model continues from the same spot instead of wasting tokens or restarting, improving efficiency and reliability.

entry.title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models

author.name: Zhiqun Zhao (Advanced Medical Research Institute and Key Laboratory for Experimental Teratology of the Ministry of Education, Cheeloo College of Medicine, Shandong University, Jinan, China), Xiaodong Yang (Department of Urology, Shandong Provincial Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medical University, Jinan, China), Bruce Gu (Shandong Computer Science Center, National entry.summary: The authors present Med Evidence Bench, a benchmark of 1,536 physician-constructed clinical reasoning items at three levels (guideline knowledge, standardized scenarios, real-world lab scenarios), where every medical claim is linked to a versioned source-text span. Testing ten LLMs, evidence trace scores were high for guideline knowledge (0.975-0.997) but dropped sharply for standardized (0.292-0.658) and real-world scenarios (0.182-0.447). This exposes a large gap between memorized medical knowledge and genuine clinical reasoning, with model rankings varying by level.

entry.title: When does text encoding matter for language modeling?

author.name: Eugene Jang, Catherine Arnett, Terra Blevins

entry.summary: This paper examines how byte-level tokenization choices, particularly UTF-8 and its variable-length structure, affect language model performance and create cross-lingual inequities. The authors systematically compare UTF-8 against alternative Unicode approaches, language-specific encodings, and custom encodings, and introduce Aether, a hybrid scheme using script-specific encodings with UTF-8 fallbacks to preserve full Unicode coverage. The work addresses an underexplored foundation-level question with direct fairness implications for non-Latin-script languages.

entry.title: Exploring Synchrony for Communication in Modular Neural Networks

author.name: Nikolas Willems, Qiyang Sun, Bj\"{o}rn W. Schuller

entry.summary: SyncNet is a modular neural architecture that separates module content from a dynamical phase state, using learned Kuramoto oscillator dynamics to coordinate module communication via synchrony, inspired by the perceptual binding problem. This addresses the problem that unrestricted inter-module communication can prevent the emergence of specialized, reusable modules needed for compositional generalization. It offers a novel mechanism for organizing modular computation.

entry.title: Lipschitz-Controlled Flow Matching for Robust Image Restoration

author.name: Sedjro Salomon Hotegni, Konstantin Sonntag, Paul-Christian B\"urkner, Sebastian Peitz

entry.summary: LipsFlower derives stability bounds for flow-matching-based image restoration, showing that learned dynamics can amplify small input perturbations, and introduces LipHDiT, a Lipschitz-aware hourglass diffusion transformer with spectral normalization and bounded modulation. The theory covers both noise-perturbed initialization and observation-conditioned posterior sampling. This brings formal robustness analysis to flow matching for inverse problems.

entry.title: From Prediction to Action: Learning Physical Context for Deformable Linear Object Manipulation

author.name: Chengxiao Dong, Alessio Caporali, Hongyu Lan, Gianluca Palli

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes predictive utility from decision utility in deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation, introducing a Geometry-Pointer-Flow policy that separates grasp selection from grasp-conditioned motion generation and achieves 32.8% lower shape error than a diffusion policy with 18.7x fewer parameters and ~193x faster inference. It then studies which physical context representations help action selection.

entry.title: We don’t understand whether GDM intentionally trains on CoT

author.name: Alek Westover

entry.summary: The author closely reads a passage from the Gemini 4 safety report suggesting Google DeepMind may apply auxiliary rewards based on chain-of-thought content during RL training, and examines the cited Kaufmann et al. (2026) paper on CoT training risks. The post argues the report's claims about obfuscation risk being low are ambiguous and partially in tension with the cited literature, flagging an important transparency gap around whether labs are optimizing directly on reasoning traces.

entry.title: We need more transparency about alignment overfitting

author.name: Nikola Jurkovic

entry.summary: Nikola Jurkovic argues the public lacks insight into whether AGI companies address misalignment at root causes or simply train away observed misbehaviors, which risks brittle alignment that fails out-of-distribution. The post surveys public evidence consistent with companies blurring the line between evaluation distributions and training data and calls for disclosure about such practices.

entry.title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation

author.name: Achuth Chandrasekhar, Amir Barati Farimani

entry.summary: This paper connects frontier LLM agents to a GPU evaluator via the Model Context Protocol for symbolic discovery of density functional theory exchange-correlation functionals, with training-only fitting, persistent memory, and self-consistent plus external physics validation. Notably, Opus-5.5 agents (an established release from September 2026) passed screening gates with roughly 40-fold fewer tokens than GPT-6-Astra-based agents and found a candidate with lower validation error.

entry.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows

author.name: Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya, Rohith Nama, Arushi Gupta, Carlos D. Castillo, Prathap Ramachandra, Xiaofan Jiang, Francesco Carbone

entry.summary: ReTrace converts an SOP plus a few logged LLM agent runs into a reusable workflow where deterministic code, not an LLM, selects each step, reducing latency and cost at scale. It extracts the conditions behind each step from agent-written explanations, merges them into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow with only the final stage depending on an LLM.

entry.title: Bursts That Outlast Themselves: Persistent Degradation in Prefix-Cached Agent Serving

author.name: Wen Huang, Jack Liu

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that prefix-cached LLM agent serving is metastable: a few minutes of arrival burst can push a vLLM server into a degraded regime with about 10% cache hit ratio, roughly half throughput, and a backlog persisting over an hour, while an identical no-burst server stays healthy. The phenomenon appears at loads a cache-warm server sustains, disappears without prefix caching, and replicates across setups including Qwen3-32B on SWE-bench traffic. This reveals a previously undocumented reliability hazard for production agent serving.

entry.title: Chem World: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Physics-Aware Framework for Trustworthy Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Tianyou Bai, Huan Wang, Mingchen Gao, Tongrui Yang, Fangyue Lin, Pinze Ren, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong

entry.summary: Chem World unifies 17 public datasets into a large-scale benchmark with over 800,000 molecular instances across 10 property tracks, covering single- and multi-component systems including drug solubility. Building on it, the authors propose PACM, a physics-aware compositional modeling framework for more trustworthy molecular property prediction.

entry.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL

author.name: Jiin Woo, Gauri Joshi, Yuejie Chi

entry.summary: The paper reframes reward heterogeneity in federated RL as an asset that catalyzes exploration rather than a barrier, proposing PF-UCBVI with optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. It also introduces PF-EFVI, a purely greedy exploration-free algorithm that exploits reward diversity for state-action coverage, backed by theory.

entry.title: An Analytical Model of Compute-limited Multistage Training Pipelines

author.name: Nishil Patel, Jin Hwa Lee, Basile Confavreux, Andrew Saxe

entry.summary: The paper builds an analytically tractable high-dimensional model of modern multistage training — unsupervised pretraining, noisy SFT, and sparse-reward RL — using random matrix theory to derive low-dimensional learning dynamics matching simulations. It shows finite pretraining data imposes a representation-dependent performance limit with Bayes error scaling as the inverse square root of the pretraining sample ratio.

entry.title: One Byte, One Token: Byteifying a 27B Hybrid-Attention LLM with Self-Generated Data

author.name: Liwei Zhang, ZhiMing Tong

entry.summary: This work converts Qwen3.8-27B, an already-trained subword model with hybrid Gated DeltaNet and full-attention layers, into a pure byte-level model by shrinking its vocabulary from 248,320 to 384 entries and continuing training on self-generated byte data with a two-stage curriculum. It addresses evidence that BPE fragments Chinese text poorly and hides spelling from the model. The result demonstrates a viable path from subword to byte-level models without full retraining.

entry.title: Stylization as Geodesic Navigation on Diffusion Manifolds

author.name: Yan Li, Zehao Li, Xinlong Sun, Fuchen Long, Xi Chen, Wenhan Luo, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Presents Stylus, a training-free facial style transfer framework that treats stylization as geodesic navigation on the curved latent manifold of a pretrained diffusion model rather than flat Euclidean interpolation. It lowers a ratio-weighted discrete geodesic energy under the pullback metric using a rank-one power-iteration Jacobian approximation, balancing strong stylization with identity preservation.

entry.title: MEOW: Medical Open-World Interactive Segmentation

author.name: Philip Matthias Winter, Maria Wimmer, Bernhard Sch\"{a}fl, David Major, Dimitrios Lenis, Astrid Berg, Theresa Neubauer, Ariharasudhan Muthusami, Johannes Novotny, Georg Zotti, Katja B\"{u}hler

entry.summary: MEOW is the first framework to turn non-interactive segmentation backbones into interactive open-world learners without updating model parameters, combining parameter-free transductive reasoning with memory consolidation. Focused on medical data, it continually improves predictions on unseen classes from user feedback over time. This extends interactive segmentation from open-set to open-world recognition.

entry.title: Camera equalisation of an 11.5x drop in environmental illuminance: four imitation-learning policies on an SO-101 arm

author.name: Simon Cowling

entry.summary: This work tests four imitation-learning policies (ACT, SmolVLA, Diffusion Policy, pi0.5) under an 11.5x illuminance drop and finds almost no performance change, showing that on low-cost rigs camera auto-exposure decouples image brightness from room lighting. It exposes a methodological flaw in real-robot benchmarks that record room illuminance as a lighting condition.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows

author.name: Bhaskar Gurram

entry.summary: Builds counterfactual medical images via inpainting-based lesion erasure and introduces an evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) metric to test whether medical VLMs report findings based on image content rather than question framing. Trains MedScope-4B (a Qwen3.5-4B-based agent with LoRA and image tools) with pre-registered selection and testing rules against nine frontier and six open VLMs.

entry.title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies

author.name: Madhu Sudhan Rao Beesetty

entry.summary: This study shows that reported fractions of LLM reasoning error categories can be artifacts of the measurement procedure itself, defining Compositional Collapse and measuring it across twelve models and eleven languages on a multilingual math benchmark. Over half of failures carry evidence for multiple categories, and reversing the order of classifier tests shifts reported plurality in eleven of twelve models.

entry.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans

author.name: Aalap D. Shah, Basil Saeed, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Tobias Gerstenberg, Hyowon Gweon, Ilker Yildirim

entry.summary: The paper introduces GenEA, an agent representation for reasoning over multi-step embodied plans that couples coarse biomechanics of an articulated body with object interactions by extending task-and-motion planning with simulation-based intuitive physics. Embedded in a generative model, GenEA yields joint probability distributions over plans, supporting inference about people's goals from their actions.

entry.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents

author.name: Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: The paper identifies memory-induced degradation in LLM agents, where agents fail tasks they would otherwise solve by following lessons distilled without their source evidence. It introduces WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system letting agents verify each lesson against the original trajectory it came from.

entry.title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English

author.name: Johin Johny, Ankur Ghosh, Shervin Sam

entry.summary: The companion paper to the token-tax study trains Havon v3/v4, byte-level BPE tokenizers with a combining-mark-aware pre-tokenizer and a SuperBPE-style multi-word stage. Havon v4 at GPT-4o's vocabulary size needs 6.1% fewer tokens, including on English, and far fewer on Indic languages.

entry.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols

author.name: Rumi Loghmani, Bozhang Song, Victor Alvarado, Aliyah Redding, Amir Barati Farimani

entry.summary: Curie's Jarvis enables a robot arm to execute chemistry experiments on a human-oriented bench: it reads steps from a photo of a printed protocol sheet, finds containers without fiducial markers, distinguishes identical containers by reading their labels from four camera views, and re-locates targets before each step. This inverts the usual lab-automation assumption of scripted procedures and fixed positions. It is a meaningful step toward robots operating in unmodified human laboratory environments.

entry.title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos

author.name: Lin Long, Tianren Ma, Zhong Chu, Di Wu, Maosong Cao, Qixiang Ye, Junbo Zhao, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose SPAR, an MoT architecture built on a pretrained VLM in which future visual state prediction from action-free human egocentric videos provides complementary learning signals alongside action prediction. Representations learned this way improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with gains scaling as video data grows.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks: Methods, Frameworks, and Perspectives

author.name: Lorenzo Cirillo, Irene Amerini, Andrea Cavallaro

entry.summary: A survey of mechanistic interpretability methods for deep neural networks across image, audio, and language domains, focusing on identifying components whose activations are causally responsible for model behaviors. It organizes advances around causal inference in networks, addressing phenomena like polysemantic neurons and interdependent internal representations.

entry.title: Interleaving anatomical inspection and diagnostic reasoning for explainable radiology report generation

author.name: Chentao Huang, Runlong Lin, Zhijun Wang, Yunxiang Li, Yuanyuan Sun, Jian Wang, Hongfei Lin, Ling Luo

entry.summary: ARIVE is an explainable radiology report generation framework that interleaves anatomical inspection with diagnostic reasoning before report composition, supported by 159,416 multimodal chain-of-thought trajectories built from MIMIC-CXR where visual evidence from inspected regions informs clinical interpretation. Models trained on these trajectories are further optimized for report quality.

entry.title: Causal Concept Explanations for Deep Neural Models

author.name: Josh Rountree, Pulkit Verma, Oswin So, Chuchu Fan, Julie A. Shah

entry.summary: CCW-Net is the first use of interventional mediation analysis as a training objective to align the causal effects of concept-based explanations with a model's output, addressing the problem that correlational concept explanations can be misleading. Mediation analysis is also applied as a per-concept evaluation tool.

entry.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction

author.name: Yuanrui Wang, Kaifang Li, Xuanyue Li, Ziyun Li, Yan Lu, Xingxuan Zhang, Peng Cui

entry.summary: This work introduces a large-scale benchmark evaluating whether a single generalist tabular model can handle generation, imputation, and prediction jointly, spanning 56 datasets, 46 methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned splits. It trains five backbones under all seven non-empty objective combinations to study how task capabilities interact.

entry.title: VIGOR: Benchmarking Visual Rationale Correctness in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yanlin Chen, Tang Li, Xi Peng

entry.summary: VIGOR is a benchmark evaluating whether multimodal LLM rationales are supported by correct visual evidence, representing rationales as concepts paired with pixel-level groundings across abstraction levels from low-level properties to high-level relations. An automatic annotation framework enables construction at scale by reusing dense supervision and proposal-based annotation.

entry.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn

author.name: Othmane Harraq, Tamer Aldwairi

entry.summary: This paper debunks the physiological premise behind rPPG-based deepfake detection: controlled experiments on Celeb-DF++ and FaceForensics++ show the discriminative signal is not a genuine cardiac signal. Simple chrominance traces reach 0.998 AUC on talking-face forgeries, exceeding a dedicated rPPG extractor, and the signal remains discriminative from background regions or full frames without faces, concentrated outside the heart-rate band. The apparent success of such detectors is instead explained by provenance-related artifacts.

entry.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance

author.name: Nathaniel S. O'Connell, Jaime L. Speiser

entry.summary: Derives an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of cross-validated estimates, expressing variance as a function of how random splits weight each observation in its training and evaluation roles, with constants depending on model, metric, and population. The result covers observation-averaged metrics such as mean squared error.

entry.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces

author.name: Jiahang Lin, Wanying Ren, Wanghan Xu, Huayu Sha, Yang Shu, Zhonghang Lu, Chengjun Pan, Yi Dong, Shichun Liu, Yuyang Hu, Shihan Dou, Honglin Guo, Huijie Lv, Pujun Zheng, Zhe Sun, Yuankai Ying, Yiding Wang, Jiahao Chen, Zhixiong Yang, Dingbo Yuan, Yicheng Zou, Zhecan Wang, Guoxiu He, Xiaoyu Xing, Qi Zhang, Tao Gui, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: ARE-bench evaluates research agents on advancing ongoing projects rather than standalone tasks, with 75 tasks grounded in real session context and in-progress workspaces containing unfinished files, outdated versions, and failed attempts. It tests whether agents respect prior decisions and existing workspace state, a gap in benchmarks emphasizing clean, curated setups. This is a timely contribution as agent benchmarks and real deployment needs diverge.

entry.title: FastWild-GS: Minutes-Scale In-the-Wild Gaussian Splatting via Compact Per-Image Appearance Adaptation

author.name: Donghun Ryu, Seokhyun Kim, Minhyeok Lee

entry.summary: FastWild-GS handles in-the-wild 3D Gaussian Splatting by modeling each photo with a 128-dimensional appearance token plus six per-image transform parameters, with a small MLP predicting Gaussian colors, reducing per-scene optimization from hours to minutes. Applying the same transform during densification scoring avoids appearance-driven densification bias. This is a notable efficiency advance for unconstrained photo collections.

entry.title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenjian Hao, Paulo C. Heredia, Shaoshuai Mou

entry.summary: K-MBRL learns control policies for nonlinear robotic systems with unknown dynamics by lifting them into a linear Koopman representation, combining analytical immediate cost with a critic-estimated future cost; the linear form makes model-dependent policy gradients a constant matrix product. This improves computational efficiency and stability of model-based RL.

entry.title: Misaligned Models Still Recognise When Their Responses Are Harmful. Can Training Make Them Care?

author.name: megasilverfist

entry.summary: This empirical post shows misaligned models can recognize harmful content when reviewing responses as an assistant's reply (62% vs 25% ethical flags for Llama) but almost never volunteer concerns unprompted, and that critique-then-regenerate prompting yields ~13x more safe responses than resampling. The findings suggest a cheap method for producing on-policy safety training data from misaligned models.

entry.title: "Hardwired Pause" should likely be your favorite (pause) plan.

author.name: David Scott Krueger

entry.summary: David Scott Krueger summarizes a 212-page, 26-author paper on the feasibility of a hardwired pause of frontier AI training, concluding a decade-plus pause could likely be implemented starting within a year without trusting China or tanking the economy. The post argues an immediate indefinite international moratorium via hardware-level mechanisms is technically easier than nuanced regulation.

entry.title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Sujato Dutta, Padala Indira Sneha, Kypu Mahitha, Shashank Vanga, Neeraj Choudhary

entry.summary: Third Eye asks whether a useful self-update remains useful after a model updates again, evaluating five 3-8B backbones including Qwen3 and Llama models across 64 fresh runs with disjoint selection and scoring sets. It finds that continuation of self-updates reduces utility in several models and that candidate-averaged immediate utility is already negative, with selection masking the negative first step.

entry.title: ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision

author.name: Haozhan Shen, Liangbo He, Jun Lan, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Tiancheng Zhao, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: ZoomGain is a data construction pipeline for fine-grained VLM supervision that exploits the gap between models' coarse global perception and their ability to recognize details once a region is zoomed. It derives questions about the full image from zoomed-in visual information, producing supervision with correct, unambiguous answers grounded in actual fine details rather than language priors.

entry.title: Plumbline: When the Loss Lies, Validating LLM Training Correctly

author.name: Ruochen Wen, Hongyang Wang, Siwei Li, Wenbo Chen, Xian Li, Jingguo Liu, Leo Fan, Yiming Yan, Qian Qu, Zheshen Wang, Benoit Dumoulin

entry.summary: Plumbline is a production correctness validation system for LLM training at Amazon that checks each stage of the training lifecycle, from data through served model, detecting both loud and silent faults that could waste long runs. Its diagnoses reuse these checks to trace failures to root causes across frameworks and libraries.

entry.title: Sim(3)-TurboReg: Robust and Efficient Scale-Aware Registration via Tri-Scale Consistency

author.name: Zijun Zhou, Shaocheng Yan, Zhenjun Zhao, Yutong Hu, Ke Yang, Yingdong Gu, Pengcheng Shi, Jiayuan Li

entry.summary: Sim(3)-TurboReg addresses monocular scale ambiguity in streaming 3D foundation model systems by reformulating compatibility graph construction with a strict Tri-Scale Consistency criterion that suppresses mismatching and coordinate-distortion outliers. The solver integrates into existing streaming pipelines for robust, efficient Sim(3) registration. Relevant to long-sequence 3D reconstruction where sliding-window chunking causes scale drift.

entry.title: Game-Enhanced Embodied Learning with Event and Foresight Pretraining

author.name: Lianlei Shan, Han Jin, Yaunchao Ma, Xinpeng Chen, Linhao Zhou, Xin Bin

entry.summary: The authors pretrain InternVLA-A1.5 on 394 recordings from 20 games (over 2 million training anchors), predicting keyboard/mouse events and history-conditioned visual futures via a frozen video model, then fine-tune on robot tasks. The work explores gameplay data as a cheap, scalable source of action-outcome supervision for robot policies.

entry.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Chih-Hao Hsu, Feng-Chun B. Chou, Pin-Hao A. Chen

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs internally represent psychological constructs by testing cross-persona prediction across 14 Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5 variants on seven psychological scales with real human data. Larger models amplify human cross-scale correlations, and contrastive direction analysis finds geometric structure internally corresponding to psychometric constructs.

entry.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research

author.name: Dong Bo, Fanjin Zhang, Ke Cheng, Xinxin Zhao, Xiaowei Su, Yang Wang, Jinghang Xu, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: BuySideFlow is a benchmark of 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language tasks testing whether LLM agents can correctly handle point-in-time validity in investment research, such as enforcing disclosure cutoffs and selecting correct historical record versions. The benchmark pairs executable references with expert audits and a taxonomy of temporal errors, evaluating nine agent configurations across equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics.

entry.title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xiaoyang Xing, Chun-Mei Feng, Anthony Cohn, Xiaoliang Gong, Asoke Nandi

entry.summary: This paper introduces APS-VLA, a method for pruning visual tokens in vision-language-action (VLA) models used for robotic manipulation, learning token selection from demonstrations while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens using visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception, reducing inference latency while preserving reliable action generation.

entry.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering

author.name: Genming Cui, Xiangyu Li, Zixu Hao, Xin Ding, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method where a full-precision teacher guides a low-bit quantized student agent to revise failed rollouts, with the teacher's guidance iteratively refined using feedback from student execution. This closed-loop approach addresses the problem that offline data misses the student's failure contexts while student rollouts contain few correct examples in those contexts.

entry.title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation

author.name: Eoin M. Kenny, Salim I. Amoukou, Tom Bewley

entry.summary: This work investigates whether multimodal large language models can serve as surrogate human participants for evaluating explainable AI techniques, replacing expensive and hard-to-reproduce human studies. It proposes a purpose-grounded evaluation framework with metrics applicable uniformly to both MLLMs and human users.

entry.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents

author.name: Runxuan Tang, Haoyu Gao, Yuyan Ding, Junyi Yao, Zihao Zheng, Zecheng Sheng, Liwei Hou

entry.summary: FGSE is a verifier-grounded framework that treats experience-derived lessons as structured hypotheses with explicit preconditions, behavior changes, expected effects, and verifiers. Candidate updates are tested in temporary state via target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes before being admitted into persistent agent memory.

entry.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game

author.name: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su, Yu Zhang, Daniel Khashabi, Kuan-Hao Huang

entry.summary: Re-Search adapts Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only a published paper's research problem, an LLM must rediscover its core idea via yes-or-no questions with oracle feedback. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, the benchmark shows that across six LLMs nearly all ideation progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, exposing limits in how models explore idea space.

entry.title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India

author.name: Johin Johny Arimbur, Ankur Ashit Ghosh, Shervin Sam

entry.summary: This study quantifies tokenizer disparity for all 25 languages of India in FLORES-200 plus Hinglish social media data across nine tokenizers. On GPT-4o's tokenizer, identical content requires 1.57x to 5.01x the English token count (up to 13.7x for Santali), translating directly into higher cost, latency, and reduced context.

entry.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement across Seven Open Reasoning Models

author.name: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Zhiyu Yang, Yi Gao, Bo Ma

entry.summary: This paper provides the first controlled, blind, multi-seed measurement of how deleting full reasoning-history traces affects performance in multi-turn tool calling, testing seven open-weight reasoning models across 794 tasks and three rendering conditions. It finds that identical deletions produce effects ranging from -4.4 to +51.3 points, showing that sensitivity to reasoning-trace stripping is a model-specific property. This matters for API routing and provider interoperability, where traces are bound to their issuer and stripped when requests cross providers.

entry.title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level R\'enyi Entropy from Particle Decoding for Adaptive LLM Reasoning

author.name: Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Milad Heidari Sorkhehdizaj, Shahab Rahimirad, Aliasghar Pourghani, Seyedarmin Azizi, Souvik Kundu, Abolfazl Hashemi, Joseph Campbell, Vijay Gupta

entry.summary: This arXiv paper shows that Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding under power sampling already computes the normalizing constant of the power distribution, allowing sequence-level Renyi entropy of an LLM's completion distribution to be extracted at zero marginal computational cost. The authors derive a Renyi chain rule yielding stepwise entropies of arbitrary order, prove connections between orders above one and the most likely token per step, and position the signal for selective prediction and adaptive compute without the many extra completions required by self-consistency.

entry.title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference

author.name: Linru Zhang, Xiangning Wang, Jun Jie Sim, Zhicong Huang, Jiahao Zhong, Huaxiong Wang, Pu Duan, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: This paper introduces MOAI, a homomorphic-encryption-based framework for non-interactive secure transformer inference over encrypted inputs when LLMs are deployed with cloud service providers. It achieves efficiency gains through a combined column and diagonal packing evaluation flow that avoids format conversions, plus rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm that reduce costly rotation operations.

entry.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting

author.name: Deyuan Liu, Jungang Li, Kaiwen Zheng, Kai Jiang, Jintao Chen, Yaole Wang, Ming Lin, Tao Lin, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu, Jintao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper extends the APEX few-step generation approach to streaming video via condition shifting, which estimates the velocity field of the generated distribution within the generator itself and eliminates the separate fake-score network required by distribution matching distillation. This reduces training memory and computation while retaining S2-Avatar's frozen reference teacher and perceptual regularization, evaluated on 180-second videos.

entry.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification

author.name: Martim Afonso, In\^es Lynce, Maurizio Morisio, Jo\~ao F. Ferreira

entry.summary: ProofCoder is an agentic proof-synthesis system for the Rocq proof assistant that treats theorem proving as a coding-agent task, reasoning continuously rather than inside a rigid tactic-generation loop. It uses proof-assistant feedback to guide premise retrieval, proof-state management, and backtracking autonomously.

entry.title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute

author.name: Sahar Admoni, Assaf Hallak, Yftah Ziser, Ofra Amir

entry.summary: The paper studies branch-and-commit, a test-time procedure for frozen RL agents in copyable digital environments where multiple continuations are sampled, evaluated, and the best branch is committed to. Across many environments, policies, and verifiers, it shows benefits depend on candidate return dispersion and characterizes where compute should be spent.

entry.title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost

author.name: Yitong Zhang, Ang Li, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: This paper evaluates recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods on continual task streams while explicitly charging the token cost of the self-improvement process alongside task execution costs. Across six methods and two language models, a simple bounded-note baseline matches or beats Meta-Harness, EvoSkill, and RRSI accuracy with 65.6-71.0% total-token savings, and the authors decompose the RSI Tax into verification, exploration, and writing components.

entry.title: Where to Approximate in Neurosymbolic Inference?

author.name: Samy Badreddine, Emile van Krieken, Luciano Serafini, Antonio Vergari

entry.summary: This paper unifies approximate weighted model counting (WMC) methods for probabilistic neurosymbolic inference under a three-step bottom-up approximate compilation pipeline and studies where approximation budget is best allocated. Inspired by tensor networks, it instantiates steps with tensor train decompositions and derives pipelines that multiply approximated factors exactly with SVD- or interpolation-based recompression. Across six tasks, the pipelines yield WMC estimates of improved accuracy at fixed cost.

entry.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model

author.name: Xukun Qin, Haochen Sun, Yuyang Tian, Ge Chen

entry.summary: HaiRuo pairs HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of global satellite-altimetry data, with a forecasting head that, from 30 days of sea-level maps, returns 15 days of physical fields, daily eddy masks, and trajectories of every live eddy in one forward pass. This replaces post-hoc tracking heuristics on ocean models with direct object-level eddy forecasting. Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy, so improved prediction matters for climate and oceanography.

entry.title: Discovering Equations for the Thermodynamics of South Asian Monsoon Precipitation

author.name: Savannah L. Ferretti, Jane W. Baldwin, Michael S. Pritchard, Tom Beucler

entry.summary: Using symbolic distillation—neural networks followed by symbolic regression—the authors discover interpretable closed-form equations for South Asian monsoon precipitation from 21 years of reanalysis data. Neural networks first compress vertical thermodynamic structure into grid-independent interpretable features, then symbolic regression derives equations combining these with surface state. The best equation explains substantially more variance than prior formulations.

entry.title: One-Sided Expert-Parallel All-to-All for Mixture-of-Experts Inference over NVLink

author.name: Bo Li, Chulian Zhang, Or Biri, Anthony Chang, Anton Korzh, Noam Duvdevani, XingFei Xi, Daniel Stokes, Zhenhuan Chen, Ludwig Schneider, Artem Y. Polyakov, Julien Demouth, Chandler Zhou

entry.summary: NVLinkOneSided is a one-sided expert-parallel all-to-all communication scheme for MoE inference within a single NVLink domain, where source ranks push tokens directly into rank-major buffers on target GPUs without metadata exchange. This targets the fixed per-operation latency costs that dominate at small inference batch sizes, letting grouped GEMMs read tokens in place.

entry.title: Exploiting Feature-invariant Scaling Laws for Efficient A/B Experimentation in Recommendation Systems

author.name: Zhiliang Chen, Sammy Nammari, Jiahao Su, Xiaoqiang Luo

entry.summary: This paper shows that modern recommendation models exhibit feature-invariant scaling: performance changes under feature modifications follow predictable scaling laws. Exploiting this, the authors introduce a statistical-inference method that predicts full-scale A/B experiment outcomes from cheap small-scale experiments with confidence guarantees. This can dramatically reduce the computational cost of iterating on industrial recommenders.

entry.title: MammothDP: Private Boosted Decision Trees Ready for Trusted Hardware and Leakage-free Hyperparameters

author.name: Moritz Kirschte, Thorsten Peinemann, Kari Kostiainen, Jan Wichelmann, Thomas Eisenbarth, Esfandiar Mohammadi

entry.summary: Introduces MammothDP, a system combining trusted execution environments with timing side-channel hardening and differential privacy to protect both the processing of sensitive tabular data (e.g., under the European Health Data Space) and the release of trained gradient-boosted decision tree models. It identifies and mitigates unexpected security gaps arising from the TEE-plus-DP combination, including leakage through hyperparameters.

entry.title: Measuring Definition Sensitivity in LLM Annotation of Social Science Concepts

author.name: Bogdan Mamaev, Qizhou Wang, Christopher Leckie, Matteo Vergani

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs actually apply the definitions supplied in annotation prompts for contested social-science concepts (hate speech, fake news, terrorism) or instead fall back on pretrained notions. By having models annotate the same texts under competing defensible definitions, it measures definition sensitivity and exposes reliability risks in LLM-based annotation.

entry.title: LLM Validation Makes Minimal-Pair Benchmarks Easier for Language Models

author.name: Guofang Tang

entry.summary: This paper tests whether LLMs can replace costly human validation of minimal-pair benchmarks, using BLiMP (English) and QFrBLiMP (Quebec French) with pre-registered experiments across forced-choice, rating, and panel validation modes. While forced-choice validators agree with held-out human majorities more than five-judge panels, they catch far fewer label errors than a single human judge, and errors are systematic: human-supported pairs appear easier for ten open LMs. The paper offers a cautionary result that LLM validation can silently bias benchmarks in models' favor.

entry.title: TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation

author.name: Yunkai Dang, Wanyu Zhang, Meiyi Zhu, Qi Fan, Tianyu Ding, Wenbin Li

entry.summary: TERM is an inference-time defense against LLM jailbreak attacks that uses prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to adaptively modulate residual activations without requiring predefined steering directions or learned safety regions. The input-adaptive design aims to block harmful generations while limiting over-refusal of benign prompts.

entry.title: Hint, Not Hole: Localization-Robust Video Overlay Removal

author.name: Dongyang Zhang, Wei Zhang, Renjie Zou, Zhiwei Huang

entry.summary: HintErase reframes video overlay removal (subtitles, logos, watermarks) by treating localization output as a soft hint channel rather than a strict hole-filling mask, letting the model see the full unmasked video. Training corrupts the hint to mimic real detector and segmenter failure modes, covering both missed regions and over-segmentation. This addresses a real gap between generative inpainting quality and unreliable localization in practice.

entry.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control

author.name: Santosh Mohan Rajkumar, Debdipta Goswami, Stephanie Stockar

entry.summary: This paper introduces FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs in linear model predictive control that uses CUDA graphs, constraint-dependent operator representations, and automatic device calibration to reduce latency. It demonstrates faster performance than competing GPU solvers on humanoid and quadrotor control simulations while preserving solution accuracy.

entry.title: Mitra-v2: Scaling synthetic pretraining for tabular foundation models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science introduces Mitra-v2, a second-generation tabular foundation model pretrained entirely on synthetic tables for classification and regression, scaling beyond the first Mitra model's limits on large, wide, and many-class tables. It aims to replace per-table pipelines of feature engineering, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter tuning with a single pretrained model.

entry.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings

author.name: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui, Ao Qu, Ou Zheng, Jiangbo Yu, Haris N. Koutsopoulos, Jinhua Zhao, Yuan Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks with human operators holding facts absent from the agent's request, using optimization solvers to determine which facts actually change the optimal plan. It evaluates whether LLM agents ask for clarification that matters for decisions, a capability underserved by fully-specified or LLM-simulated-user benchmarks.

entry.title: Disentangling Multimodal Rotary Positional Embedding in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhaoyi Liu, Haichuan Zhang, Xiaochuan Gong, Yancheng Zhu, Bowei Tian, Wanghao Ye, Yufan Zhang, Ang Li

entry.summary: This paper analyzes MRoPE positional embeddings in vision-language models, showing that assigning height and width coordinates to text tokens introduces spatial positional effects into text-vision attention, and systematically studies how different MRoPE variants' frequency allocations and coordinate layouts help or hinder text-vision interaction.

entry.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer

author.name: Wentao Lei, Li Liu

entry.summary: SELD detects silent evidence loss in context compression, where key evidence is dropped while the reader's answer stays unchanged, leaving answers unsupported for downstream reuse. It is training- and label-free, based on the observation that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among answers it does not emit shift even when its emitted answer does not.

entry.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood

author.name: Marie Amale Huynh, Laura Bravo-S\'anchez, Lauren Klein, Nick Haber, Philip Fisher, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: The paper introduces NEST, the first child-centric benchmark for nonverbal social reasoning in video, with manually annotated ~12-second clips spanning naturalistic settings, cultural contexts, and developmental stages. It exposes how poorly multimodal video models handle gaze-, gesture-, and contact-based social meaning in early childhood.

entry.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Chi Liu, Xin Chen, Yuchuan Weng, Srinivasan Manoharan

entry.summary: MCPO improves credit assignment in GRPO-style RLVR by allocating token-level advantages according to the policy's top-2 next-token probability margin as a hesitation signal, using fixed thresholds and preserving mean advantage. The margin is read from a forward pass the trainer already performs, requiring no extra model evaluations, with experiments on a 2B model trained with LoRA on DAPO-Math problems.

entry.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Amir Mann, Jonathan Fhima, Shaked Brody, Or Avitan, Asif Zamir, Shahar Tsiper, Niv Nayman

entry.summary: B3 accelerates block diffusion language models by refining two blocks in parallel within a shared forward pass, opening the next block adaptively once the model is ready. The method is training-free and hyperparameter-free, integrating with existing self-editing block-diffusion frameworks.

entry.title: Closing the BF16-FP16 Convergence Speed Gap in RL Post-Training with Stochastic Rounding
