author.name: Mahdi Nazemi, Oleg Rybakov, Tijmen Blankevoort, Asit Mishra, Carlo del Mundo

entry.summary: The authors identify weight sticking as the cause of slower BF16 than FP16 convergence in RL post-training with verifiable rewards at low learning rates: round-to-nearest quantization of FP32 shadow weights often leaves BF16 weights unchanged across optimizer steps. They propose stochastic rounding to close the gap, which is significant given BF16's dominance in LLM pretraining.

entry.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models

author.name: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Jiangweizhi Peng, Shiyang Li, Sujay Bhatt, Sihan Zeng, Mingyi Hong

entry.summary: AutoScaffold is an AI-for-AI framework in which a frozen teacher periodically examines a student LLM's RLVR training experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs adaptive prompt scaffolds such as strategies and hints, with no human intervention. This converts outcome-reward information, otherwise reduced to a single number, into structured training guidance. The approach minimizes domain-specific engineering compared to hand-designed scaffolds.

entry.title: DEPUTYBENCH: Evaluating Contextual Safety in Enterprise Agents

author.name: Hao Zhao, Minghao Lin

entry.summary: DEPUTYBENCH is an executable benchmark of 79 base items and 375 instances evaluating whether enterprise agents correctly determine if requests are permitted by organizational records and policies, with paired permission contexts and graded evidence requirements. Across 12 models it finds restricted execution is more frequent with missing evidence than explicit non-permission, quantifying a safety gap.

entry.title: Where Do Vision-Language Models Get Left and Right? Position-Code Counterfactuals in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3

author.name: Enhao Cui, Junzhi Yang, Yaoshun Lin, Yuhan Feng, Zijian Chen

entry.summary: Using position-code counterfactuals, this study shows that left-right spatial reasoning in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, and InternVL3 derives almost entirely from the ViT positional encoding: mirroring only ViT width positions reproduces flipped-image answers on 84-93% of CV-Bench questions, while LLM-side mirrors change few answers. The analysis uses established open models and carefully isolates necessity versus sufficiency. It clarifies where spatial direction is actually encoded in VLMs.

entry.title: The BRIDGE dataset: paired brightfield whole-slide images of prostate core-needle biopsies in paraffin, after deparaffinization and H&E staining

author.name: Julia A. Mielcarz, Justyna Dur\'slewicz, Marek Zdrenka, Ahmad Abbadi, Martin Eklund, Mateusz Matusiak, {\L}ukasz Szylberg, Andrea Camilloni

entry.summary: BRIDGE is a dataset of 869 whole-slide images from 169 prostate biopsy patients, each digitized before and after deparaffinization and H&E staining, enabling development of label-free virtual staining models. It addresses the scarcity of paired, clinically annotated whole-slide datasets for virtual staining. Such resources are critical for reducing reliance on chemical staining in histopathology workflows.

entry.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes

author.name: Jinmo Han, Ju Yeon Kang, Jimin Hong, Sunghwan Ahn, Yonghyeon Jun, Nam Soo Kim

entry.summary: Introduces SetPrint, a training-free black-box fingerprinting method that determines whether a target model derives from a source model by jointly capturing within-set relations and between-set correspondence of response changes under query perturbations. It fully exploits both sources of information that prior fingerprinting approaches used only partially.

entry.title: TrustMod-SM: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Trustworthiness of LLMs in Social Media Content Moderation

author.name: Aizan Zafar, Sreekantam Sai Venkata, Gathik Jindal, Ritu Raj Sharma, Zishan Ahmad, Tulika Saha, Srinath Srinivasa

entry.summary: TrustMod-SM is a benchmark of roughly 29,000 instances across eight datasets evaluating LLM-based content moderation along five trustworthiness dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity. Testing 16 open-weight models plus one closed frontier model, the authors find persistent gaps, including that higher accuracy often correlates with greater demographic disparity and that models comply with concealment prompts and are overconfident in errors.

entry.title: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding

author.name: Haoyu Huang, Jialiang Kang, Linlin Yang, Xiao Yang, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes a flaw in tree-based speculative decoding: product-ranked draft trees misallocate probability mass to chimeric prefixes stitched from different futures, and proves such trees need exponentially many chimeras. Proposes mixture block drafters that allocate tree budget across multiple futures, improving expected accepted tokens under tree verification.

entry.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them

author.name: Shaohuang Wang, Jinghao Wen, Xulei Zhang, Xun Jiao

entry.summary: This paper defines an episode record linking candidate faults in failed LLM agent runs to their origin, propagation, detection, response, and consequence, plus the control families whose observation and reach could catch them. The authors turned this into an annotation protocol and applied it to 95 failed runs of six multi-agent systems from public corpora.

entry.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics

author.name: Qinan Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Qihang Jin, Tianyuan Wang, Hongbing Luo, Pengfei Li, Wenjun Lv, Yu Kang, Jian Di

entry.summary: The paper proposes State-Conditional Invariance, a reliability principle requiring VLM judges to stay stable under semantics-preserving presentation changes while responding to causal interventions that alter task outcomes. It instantiates this in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with evidence-removal, counterfactual, and presentation probes across five diagnostic tasks.

entry.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics

author.name: Bastien Dussard (LAAS-RIS, LAAS), Aur{\'e}lie Clodic (LAAS-IDEA, LAAS-RIS, LAAS), Guillaume Sarthou (LAAS-RIS, EPE UT, LAAS)

entry.summary: URDF2Ontology is a neurosymbolic framework that automatically converts raw robot URDF files into grounded OWL ontologies, using an LLM for targeted semantic reasoning and a graph-purging mechanism to avoid context-window saturation. Its morphology-aware dual-track architecture handles both branching tree and serial chain kinematic structures, enabling symbolic task-allocation reasoning over physical robot capabilities.

entry.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation

author.name: Yu Dong, Hong Li, Qiang Sun, Xu Zhou, Jinbiao Huo, Qixiu Cheng, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: LM-SimBench provides a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators, decomposing simulation into functional stages from compilation to schedule-level aggregation. It profiles 23 model settings to enable controlled comparison of simulators that previously differed in modeled stages and workloads.

entry.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations

author.name: Ziang Liu, James J. Kim, Yijia Dai, Jennifer J. Sun

entry.summary: The paper argues that LLM scientific discovery agents evaluating hypotheses pointwise (h vs. not-h) cannot learn which alternative evidence supports. Contrastive Discovery instead scores experiments by how evidence redistributes belief across a mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive contrast set, resolving a question when belief concentrates on one explanation.

entry.title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Mufei Li, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Zhuoer Wang, Samson Koelle, Jie Yuan, Manqing Mao, Hong Wang, Yanjun Lin, James Feng, Daniel Edmiston, Pan Li, Wei Niu

entry.summary: For multi-turn on-policy distillation of tool-use agents, the paper casts successful-reference selection as a free-target optimal transport problem, using longest-common-subsequence action alignment as an observable compatibility proxy. This prevents misleading supervision from successful trajectories that reach incompatible interaction states.

entry.title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL

author.name: Dipin Khati, Shubham Mehrotra, Bin Bi, Zhou Yu, Denys Poshyvanyk, James Zhu, Sitaram Asur, Phil L. Mui

entry.summary: AgentScript-Eval is an execution-graded benchmark of 100 real enterprise tasks in AgentScript, the declarative DSL Salesforce uses in Agentforce, where developers declare agent topics, actions, and guardrails. It targets the gap between strong general-purpose code generation and poorly measured performance on non-public enterprise DSLs.

entry.title: Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies

author.name: Jiamin He, Mark Rowland, Zhaohan Daniel Guo, Hado van Hasselt, Diana Borsa

entry.summary: This theoretical RL paper generalizes standard off-policy interpolation between behavior and target policies by introducing excursion policies, where the agent follows the target policy for multi-step excursions before reverting to the behavior policy. The authors derive dynamic programming results and develop provably sound off-policy temporal-difference algorithms, positioning excursions as a structured knob for trading off bias and variance. This comes from DeepMind-affiliated researchers (Rowland, van Hasselt, Borsa).

entry.title: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot

author.name: Canyon Grey Dell'Omo, Joao Pedro de Carvalho Voltani

entry.summary: Talos is an inline gate that judges every autonomous LLM-agent request to industrial controllers in milliseconds, routing flagged hostile agents to a device-faithful decoy twin of the real plant where their attack continues harmlessly and yields intelligence. Evaluated against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents in four escalating concealment tiers, including trained cover stories, the pipeline achieved zero writes reaching the real plant. It addresses a novel threat model: coordinated, machine-speed LLM agents attacking operational technology.

entry.title: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards

author.name: Bikrant Bikram Pratap Maurya

entry.summary: This security study shows that acoustic keystroke recovery works outside idealized lab conditions, surviving unseen keyboards, diverse users, noisy environments, and compressed audio channels when the acoustic model is made domain-invariant and a language model corrects noisy predictions. It extends prior keyboard-emanation attacks toward realistic open-world threat models.

entry.title: Ninety-Six Ways to Measure a Scribe: Fragmented Evaluation of Ambient Scribes in Healthcare

author.name: Amama Mahmood, Shiye Cao, Laura Fleig, Junan Jiang, Theodore Jensen, Yee-Yin Choong, Kristen Greene, Chien-Ming Huang

entry.summary: This meta-research study surveys 54 evaluation studies of ambient AI scribes in healthcare, finding ten evaluation dimensions and 40 distinct metrics operationalized in 96 different ways, 36% of which appear in only a single study. Evaluation is dominated by documentation time and efficiency, leaving other dimensions under-measured.

entry.title: FaST: Factored Synthesis of Transitions for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daniel Campa, Spandan Das, Srinjoy Das

entry.summary: FaST factors RL transition tuples via the chain rule into state, action, dynamics, reward, and terminal stages, fitting each with an appropriate estimator rather than modeling the tuple as a monolith. On twelve D4RL benchmarks it matches the SynthER diffusion baseline while generating synthetic transitions over 90x faster.

entry.title: Prediction-Powered LLM Ranking with Adaptively Collected Human Feedback

author.name: Gabriel Sargent, Will Wei Sun, Zhengwu Zhang, Yufeng Liu

entry.summary: PP-Rank combines cheap LLM-judge predictions with expensive human feedback to improve the precision of LLM rankings while maintaining valid statistical inference under adaptive sampling and judge bias. Data-driven prediction weights minimize variance-type objectives within a prediction-powered inference framework.

entry.title: Adaptive catalyst discovery emerges from composable scientific intelligence

author.name: Wentao Li, Qilong Cai, Qi Lei, Jinxing Chen, Ruixuan Chen, Jiangjie Qiu, Botian Wang, Kai Zhao, Honghao Chen, Leyi Zhao, Zemeng Wang, Yijun Li, Jun Yin, Fangfang Li, Hongxuan Liu, Yingdong Lu, Yawen Ouyang, Manu Suvarna, Wei-Ying Ma, Ya-Qin Zhang, Kostya S. Novoselov, Hao Zhou, Jiong Lu, Xiaonan Wang

entry.summary: CatAI is a physics-grounded modular AI framework for catalyst discovery that learns 1.8 million structure-property relations organized into 30 physicochemical encoders, forming a reusable intermediate layer from which task-specific models are built. It achieves 7.8% lower task-averaged prediction error than the next-best models and experimentally validated a new confined-passable pocket catalyst relevant to industrial processes.

entry.title: Auditing the Judge: Internal Signals for LLM Reasoning Assurance

author.name: Mayank Gulati, Gerhard Wunder

entry.summary: The paper compares a judge model's continuous verdict-token score against a supervised probe trained on attention-head activations for scoring correctness of LLM answers under fixed review budgets. Across three open 7-12B models on GSM8K and MATH, the probe recovers 1.3-22.5 additional percentage points of errors at 5% review, and probe-guided routing improves accuracy over equal-allocation baselines. It links fixed-budget error recall to residual risk analytically.

entry.title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Daren Zha

entry.summary: This paper exposes a candidate-support confound in offline web-behavior benchmarks: when distractors come from training support but the gold action is out-of-vocabulary, support membership trivially identifies the answer. It formalizes this with a support-identifiability rate, constructs support-balanced candidate sets, and proposes a dual-path proposer combining support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals.

entry.title: Continuous Horizon Forecasting

author.name: Malcolm Wolff, Elliott Zackrone, Souhaib Ben Taieb, Michael W. Mahoney, Kin G. Olivares

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Continuous Horizon strategy for multi-horizon forecasting, treating forecasts as a continuous operator with the horizon as a query variable rather than an index, generalizing recursive, direct, and multi-step strategies. It provides a Universal Operator Approximation Theorem and a bias-variance decomposition proving variance improvements, validated on 16 large-scale datasets.

entry.title: How Post-Training Influences Verbalized Algorithmic Computation in Language Models

author.name: Niall Dalton

entry.summary: Using successive SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints of Olmo-3-7B-Instruct on multi-digit addition, this mechanistic study probes whether internal carry information and its verbalized chain-of-thought change under post-training. Probes recover carry information equally well after SFT and RLVR, but RLVR-produced chains of thought are more useful to downstream checkpoints, and carry-related statements receive higher importance after RLVR. This suggests RLVR improves the informativeness of verbalized reasoning rather than internal state encoding.

entry.title: Continuous 3D Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction via Histology-Informed Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Kaito Shiku, Ryoma Bise, Ahtisham Fazeel Abbasi, Yuichiro Iwashita, Shumpei Takezaki, Andreas Dengel, Muhammad Nabeel Asim

entry.summary: Proposes HIM-INR, an implicit neural representation that reconstructs continuous 3D gene-expression fields from sparse 2D spatial transcriptomics sections by jointly modeling expression and histology, using densely sampled histological images as auxiliary supervision. After training, it predicts gene expression at arbitrary 3D coordinates without histology at inference.

entry.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing

author.name: Dongyao Chen, Jiayun Lei, Zhiyuan Ji, Zhiying Deng, Wei Liu, Xiaobo Sun

entry.summary: Shifts attention in LLM knowledge editing from the parameter-editing stage to the upstream construction of the target hidden state, establishing a theoretical link between parameter-space interference and interference between target hidden states. It proposes sparse target optimization to allocate the model's limited capacity space more effectively and reduce collateral damage to other knowledge.

entry.title: AVCC: Audio-Visual Conversation Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction with a Human Benchmark

author.name: Haotian Qi, Gabriel Skantze

entry.summary: This paper converts AVCC, a 31-hour audio-visual corpus of two- and three-speaker conversations recorded with a single static camera and microphone, into a public benchmark for multiparty next-speaker prediction, including a speaker-disjoint test partition with 865 hold and 865 shift events. Crucially, it provides a human performance benchmark for the same prediction task, which no prior model comparison has done. It fills a gap for conversational agents and social robots that must take turns without waiting for silence.

entry.title: Using LLM Agents to Evaluate Prosocial Interventions on Social Media Platforms

author.name: Lucen Li, Erin Wertz, Muhammad Haroon, Anshuman Chhabra, Magdalena Wojcieszak

entry.summary: The authors build a simulation pipeline on the OASIS framework using 13,835 profiled LLM agents that interact with real Twitter/X posts over 20 time steps to pre-test content interventions before costly human-subject experiments. They systematically compare three interventions for increasing exposure to verified news: adding content, upranking, and celebrity source cues.

entry.title: Uni-Loc: Weakly Supervised 3D CT Pathology Localization via Spatially Grounded Vision-Language Classification

author.name: Hao-Chih Lee, Zahi A. Fayad, Xueyan Mei

entry.summary: Uni-Loc unifies pathology classification and 3D localization in CT scans using only scan-level supervision, deriving predictions and localization maps from spatial similarity between pathology-conditioned queries and image features. A token-to-voxel upsampling module and gradient-guided thresholding yield high-resolution localization, achieving strong voxel-level AUROC/AUPR across five tasks on 355 annotated scans.

entry.title: EVAThink: Evidence Sufficiency-Guided Training for Adaptive Thinking in Video Understanding

author.name: Changti Wu, Ruizhe Fan, Bin Wang, Lei Zhang, Yuxiang Zhang

entry.summary: EVAThink trains video language models to adaptively decide when explicit reasoning helps, based on whether sampled frames provide sufficient evidence. It constructs evidence-dense and evidence-sparse view pairs under identical frame budgets and trains the model to reason only when sparse evidence warrants it. This targets compute efficiency in video understanding under fixed frame budgets.

entry.title: CURRENT: A Recurrent Neural Network for Concurrent Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution of 4D Flow MRI

author.name: Luuk Jacobs, Pietro Dirix, Sebastian Kozerke

entry.summary: CURRENT is a recurrent network performing simultaneous spatial and temporal super-resolution of aortic 4D flow MRI velocity fields in one architecture, trained on CFD simulations embedded in in vivo MRI backgrounds. It outperforms 4DFlowNet and sequential spatial-then-temporal super-resolution baselines. Better post-acquisition resolution could reduce MRI scan times and improve cardiovascular flow analysis.

entry.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control

author.name: Xu Luo, Jiaying Yang, Hao Wu, Junlin Xie, Zijin Hong, Ji Zhang, Lianli Gao, Jingkuan Song

entry.summary: ExRL finds that adapting long-chunk robot policies with standard RL is sample-inefficient due to high-dimensional action chunks, and instead optimizes how long to execute each predicted chunk rather than the actions themselves. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional and substantially improves sample efficiency for online real-world adaptation.

entry.title: WAM is capable in BEHAVIOR-1K: the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge

author.name: Yelin He, Jiaquan Ye, Xinming Wei, Wenjie Xiao, Gengming Zhang, Guoting Wei, Xianbiao Qi, Rong Xiao

entry.summary: This report describes Team IF1001's second-place entry in the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, built on the Cosmos 3 world action model and enhanced with visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group/skill-specific LoRA adapters, plus progress-estimator routing and inference tricks to hit 1 FPS. It demonstrates competitive mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks.

entry.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring

author.name: Rishikesh Mallagundla, Pranav Patel

entry.summary: Presents TopicScope, a framework for training per-token causal topic classifiers on sparse-autoencoder features, extending activation-based monitors beyond 2-3 class harmful-content detection. Experiments on Gemma-3 1B and 4B show prefill-trained monitors generalize to decoding and are robust to perturbations, with at most 5 macro-metric loss.

entry.title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents

author.name: Chang Liu, Bo Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Student-Aware Teaching (SAT), where a stronger LLM teacher builds a learner model of a fixed student agent — pairing empirical profiles with hypotheses about limitations, probing diagnostically, and writing reusable skills for diagnosed failures. Skills enter a library only after raising student performance, framing agent skill transfer as a Theory-of-Mind teaching problem.

entry.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents

author.name: Wenji Fang, Yao Lu, Jinghua Wang, Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: The paper examines three directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: realistic reference-based and open-ended benchmarks, and Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework automating critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation with reusable optimization skills. On 20 real-world designs, Dr. RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21%/17% with about 6% area cost.

entry.title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment

author.name: Yupeng Han, Kai Zhang, Shuochen Liu, Ze Liu, Xianquan Wang, Zhihong Pan, Xiangyu Zhao, Qi Liu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: PMR is a framework for long-horizon personalized agents that learns user-specific memory update policies via rubric-guided credit assignment, addressing the coarse terminal-only feedback of conventional training. It recognizes that identical memory actions can have opposite utility across user personas and replaces globally shared evaluation standards with per-user rubrics.

entry.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding

author.name: Zhongxing Xu, Zhonghua Wang, Zhe Qian, Shiyan Su, Ming Hu, Xiaocheng Zou, Wei Feng, Mingquan Lin, Yuyin Zhou, Yifan Peng, Hamid Rezatofighi, Zongyuan Ge

entry.summary: The paper observes that multimodal diffusion language models exhibit localized entropy spikes during iterative denoising that correlate with hallucinations, and proposes detecting anomalous steps via entropy deviation from a temporal window. StepRefine is a plug-and-play decoding method that preserves distributional information at masked positions during these spikes to reduce hallucination.

entry.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiajun Chen, Shicheng Fang, Jiahao Lu, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: GTAGym provides an environment and benchmark for evaluating and training agents on GTA V tasks, with GTAVBench containing 103 reconstructed main-story mission tasks across nine task families plus 47 image-based shooting tasks. A web server supports parallel evaluation, addressing the difficulty of automatically verifying task outcomes in AAA games.

entry.title: How Hyperbolic Are Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Freek Byrman, Partha Das, Stijn Verdenius, Pascal Mettes

entry.summary: The paper critically examines hyperbolic vision-language models (MERU, HyCoCLIP, ARGENT, PHyCLIP) and shows that the exponential map, the sole operation where curvature enters the network, is well approximated by the identity, with removing it at inference leaving evaluation scores essentially unchanged. This suggests the reported benefits of hyperbolic VLMs may derive from Euclidean geometry plus norm regularization rather than true hyperbolic structure. The authors further train Euclidean counterparts that match performance.

entry.title: Sharp Sample Complexity of KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Andrew Liu

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that for KL-regularized RL (the objective behind maximum-entropy RL and RLHF), a plug-in estimator learns an epsilon-optimal policy from every initial state with sharp sample complexity, improving prior H^5-scaled guarantees and providing the first MDP lower bound depending on the temperature beta. It frames the regularized optimal policy as a posterior over trajectories via the control-as-inference graphical model. This is a foundational result for understanding sample efficiency of regularized RL.

entry.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits

author.name: Kunal Kumar, Kimberlee Keithley, Toshiya Iwamori, Shu Kanno, Ikko Hamamura, Takao Kobayashi, Akira Koseki, Qi Gao, Naoki Yamamoto, Hiroshi Horii, Yuri Kobayashi, Borja Peropadre, Kouhei Nakaji, Toru Imai, Takayuki Osogami

entry.summary: The authors train generative quantum eigensolver policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to produce state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization, first on simulators and then with an IBM Heron processor in the training loop at 46 and 70 qubits. Hardware-in-the-loop training uses reward shaping to avoid collapse to trivial Hartree-Fock-sampling circuits.

entry.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery

author.name: Niran Nataraj, Maina Sogabe, Masamichi Yamashita, Norihiko Ito, Kenji Kawashima

entry.summary: TransGHOST reconstructs instrument-occluded tissue in ophthalmic microsurgery video in real time without generative synthesis, resampling recorded frames via geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions so every restored value has visual provenance. Its causal, non-generative safe mode supports online operation for robot-assisted surgery perception.

entry.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation

author.name: Yuchen Jiao, Na Li, Changxiao Cai, Yuting Wei, Gen Li

entry.summary: The paper proves matching upper and worst-case lower bounds showing that higher-order approximations do not improve convergence of stochastic diffusion samplers even with exact scores. It then introduces forward-value discretization, a training-free method that evaluates the prediction model at a lookahead estimate to accelerate stochastic sampling.

entry.title: INTENT: Out-of-Sample, Out-of-Time, and Cold-Start Evaluation on User Event Sequences

author.name: Mattias Kvist, Erik Lidman Hillbom, Edoardo de Cal, Davis Siemens, Adam Fredriksson, Rickard Br\"uel-Gabrielsson

entry.summary: INTENT is a public benchmark for foundation models trained on user event sequences (transactions, sessions, authorizations), scoring models across seven cells defined by whether the user, time period, and target item appeared in training. It audits 59 public dataset families and retains five, addressing the fact that private banking data prevents cross-model comparison.

entry.title: When Covariance Is Not Enough: Kernel-Based Regularization for Single-Cell Counterfactuals

author.name: Korbinian Traeuble, Edward de Brouwer, Archit Verma, Doron Haviv, Kipper Fletez-Brant

entry.summary: The authors show that linear cross-covariance penalties, used previously to disentangle known and unknown factors in concept-bottleneck generative models for single-cell counterfactuals, fail when non-linear interactions exist. They propose a kernel-based regularization that more fully separates information, verified in simulations and single-cell applications. This is significant for in-silico cellular screening, where faithfulness of counterfactual edits to individual cells is critical.

entry.title: Are Causal Neuron Circuits Unique and Transferable?

author.name: \"Omer Tekin Yavuz (\.Ileti\c{s}im Yaz{\i}l{\i}m)

entry.summary: The paper critically examines neuron-intervention interpretability demonstrations by exhaustively measuring all 4,096 subsets of 12 MLP neurons for each selected group, asking how much of an alleged causal circuit is actually necessary and whether effects are unique and transferable across inputs. Experiments on Qwen3 models show selected neurons lower answer margins substantially more than random ones, but probe necessity, redundancy, and generality of the claimed circuits. This adds much-needed statistical rigor to circuit-level interpretability claims.

entry.title: IFRS Compliance Verification: An Open Multi-LLM Benchmark and Content-Conditioned Ensemble Classifier

author.name: Aghoghomena Akasukpe, Li Yang, Xinyao Zhou, Chen Shen, Miguel Vargas Martin

entry.summary: This paper tackles LLM-assisted verification of corporate financial disclosures against IFRS regulations, releasing a benchmark of 19,998 regulation-disclosure pairs with 11,161 unanimous multi-LLM labels. It proposes a multi-stage, content-conditioned ensemble classifier that mitigates the systematic per-model biases that cause naive ensembling to underperform the strongest single model. The work addresses a real high-stakes auditing task where single-model accuracy is insufficient.

entry.title: Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models

author.name: Ruxiao Duan, Yunwen Zhou, Erin Hong, Dongxu Zhao, Eric Turner, Federico Tombari, Alex Wong

entry.summary: Camera3R is a low-rank adaptation framework that extends feed-forward 3D reconstruction models, which are typically trained on perspective imagery, to arbitrary and heterogeneous non-perspective camera models with minimal retraining. This addresses a key generalization limitation hindering deployment of reconstruction foundation models on unknown camera geometries.

entry.title: EgoHMP: Achieving Precise Human Motion Prediction in 3D Scenes via Egocentric Cues

author.name: Xin Zhao, Pengzhan Zhou, Ziyi Li, Riheng Jia, Zhida Qin, Yu Liu

entry.summary: EgoHMP is a human motion prediction framework that uses egocentric views and head motion rather than gaze signals to infer interaction intent in 3D scenes. It translates inferred intent into an envisioning of future interactions, addressing ambiguity and hardware-dependence problems of gaze-based approaches. This improves the practicality of motion prediction for egocentric robotics and wearable applications.

entry.title: CIALLO: Learning Shared Intent Representations for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

author.name: Choo Sin Wai, Dake Zhong, Jingye Zhang, Zhifang Liu, Siyao Xiao, Zirong Ding, Yuhong Zhang, Kangjie Chen, Dongbin Zhang, Guorui Song, Guocun Wang, Peng Jiao, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: CIALLO is an action codec aligning actions, visual changes, and observation-grounded language in a shared short-horizon behavioral intent space, with an embodiment-conditioned decoder mapping intent back to robot-specific actions. After pretraining across eight embodiments, it adapts to a new robot from a single recording of at most 10 seconds.

entry.title: The Western AI safety playbook doesn’t transfer to China

author.name: jacquesthibs

entry.summary: Drawing on two weeks of conversations in China, the author argues that Western field-building models for AI safety do not transfer because China restricts foreign nonprofit money and lacks the West's philanthropy-driven ecosystem origins. The post surveys which actors (state-backed institutes, universities, companies, volunteers) will drive Chinese safety work and warns that some Western approaches could backfire.

entry.title: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation

author.name: Pengkun Wang, Rui Mao, Zhe Zhao, Dongting Xie, Haibin Wen, Song Xu, Di Wu, Xu Wang, Zhengyang Zhou, Binwu Wang, Xiaofeng Cao, Yang Wang

entry.summary: Presents ChipOmni, a knowledge-enhanced, context-evolving agent framework for EDA that unifies multimodal understanding, dynamic planning, multi-agent collaboration, and verification-driven tool interaction to plan, verify, and repair designs autonomously. It addresses the fragmentation of EDA workflows across heterogeneous tools and representations.

entry.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents

author.name: Jingjing Jiang

entry.summary: This survey formalizes self-evolving multimodal agents via four criteria and a three-stage self-improvement loop (experience generation, feedback acquisition, update consolidation), analyzing mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, generation, GUI/Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. It investigates why self-improvement mechanisms transfer asymmetrically across these settings.

entry.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents

author.name: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown, Mihir Bhatia, Neelu Choudhary, Lily Miao

entry.summary: This enterprise study compares three agent evaluation paradigms (trace-based LLM judging, text-only judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics) on two analytics agents using frozen execution traces. Across three phases it quantifies harness stability, known-risk detection on 72 ground-truth cases, and discovery of new failure modes, finding high stability and agent-independent stability patterns.

entry.title: One Temperature to Rule Them All?

author.name: Aviv Orly (School of Physics and Astronomy, Tel Aviv University, Israel), Ori Shem-Ur (School of Physics and Astronomy, Tel Aviv University, Israel), Yaron Oz (School of Physics and Astronomy, Tel Aviv University, Israel)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes when varying sampling temperature across samples helps multi-sample LLM inference versus a single tuned temperature, in the canonical pass@K setting. It characterizes per-question success-probability profiles across models and datasets, finding consistent structure including that harder questions are less likely to share beneficial temperature behavior.

entry.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA

author.name: Saber Malekmohammadi, Kevin Kuo, Virginia Smith, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: This paper proves theoretically that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen A matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning under a random, rank-dependent gradient perturbation. Motivated by this, the authors propose freezing and periodically resampling A matrices at the client level, with rank-aware learning rates, for federated fine-tuning of foundation models. The analysis connects matrix factorization structure to optimization dynamics in federated settings.

entry.title: Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yue Wu, Xueyu Zhou, Yangrong Hu, Jian Huang

entry.summary: The paper finds that on-policy self-distillation, which uses a reference-conditioned copy of the model as teacher, degrades under continued training due to a growing mismatch between the evolving student and the frozen privileged teacher. The authors propose bootstrapping the teacher from the student to keep guidance aligned, addressing long-horizon training stability.

entry.title: TAPCO-G: LLM-Guided Design-Adaptive Timing and Power Co-Optimization with Graph-Based Physical Priors

author.name: Wuqian Tang, Zixiao Wang, Che-Chien Lin, Fong-Hua Fu, Laura Ang\'elica Shion-Korsak, Xinyun Zhang, Bei Yu, Chun-Yao Wang

entry.summary: TAPCO-G combines LLM-guided adaptation of optimizer rules with graph-based physical priors for post-placement timing and power co-optimization in chip design, letting the LLM propose rule changes while a learned evaluator estimates slack and power effects of cell replacements. An outer loop tunes tool settings using physical-design feedback.

entry.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications

author.name: Sourish Gunesh Dhekane, Abinaya Kumar, Torsten Woertwein, Yan-Bo Lin, Thomas Ploetz, Shabnam Ghaffarzadegan

entry.summary: The authors stress-test four prominent time-series foundation models (MOMENT, Chronos-2, Moirai-MoE, TimesFM) for robustness to sampling frequency changes common in sensor deployments, using three novel metrics covering embedding shifts, forecasting degradation, and downstream performance. They ask whether model behavior tracks loss of information bandwidth rather than raw sampling rate.

entry.title: RadRef: A Reference-Free Metric for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Shelly Schwartz, Alan Ropp, Michael B. Sneider, Nur Yildirim, Cree M. Gaskin, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: RadRef is a reference-free metric for radiology report evaluation that scores report claims against image-derived beliefs over a clinical finding vocabulary weighted by clinical indication relevance. It achieves 73.1% agreement with radiologist rankings on ReXVal, comparable to reference-based metrics, and is strongest on detecting omissions.

entry.title: Deep Personalization: Continuous Context Observation for Local Proactive Agents

author.name: Yijia Shao, Song Bian, Junxian Guo, Jindong Jiang, Zhen Dong, Huizi Mao, Diyi Yang, Song Han

entry.summary: The paper introduces deep personalization, a closed-loop framework in which a proactive agent continuously observes user activity, retains long-term context, and adapts its intervention timing from implicit feedback, instantiated in Coco, a local desktop agent. This addresses the gap where users must know when to ask for help, enabling assistance that is helpful rather than disruptive.

entry.title: Decode Token Parallelism: Memory-Efficient Distributed Attention Parallelism for Scalable LLM Decoding

author.name: Susav Shrestha, Brad Settlemyer, Narasimha Reddy

entry.summary: The authors observe that dense layers and attention scale differently during LLM decode and propose a parallelism scheme that runs dense layers efficiently within an NVLink domain while parallelizing attention across nodes for memory-efficient KV-cache scaling. This addresses the capacity-versus-bandwidth trade-off in high-concurrency long-context serving.

entry.title: Normalizing Flows for Classical Simulation of Quantum Circuits in Phase Space

author.name: Edward Jiang, Timothy Heightman, Marcin P{\l}odzie\'n

entry.summary: The authors represent N-qubit quantum states as probability distributions on a 2N-dimensional phase-space manifold and parameterize unitary gates as normalizing flows between these distributions. This generative-modeling approach to quantum circuit simulation exceeds state-of-the-art neural network methods in accuracy on three common circuit families at large system sizes. It opens a new avenue applying flow models to quantum simulation.

entry.title: SpecValley: Aggregation as Spectral Valley in Dense Heterophilic Graphs

author.name: Christoph Jahn, Delvin Bacho, Urs Waldmann, Bastian Goldluecke

entry.summary: Argues that degree normalization in graph neural networks acts as a fixed spectral valley that attenuates a middle frequency band exactly where dense heterophilic graphs accumulate eigenvalues. It proposes a two-stage design with learnable aggregation followed by an ordinary spectral filter, starting from representations rather than propagation.

entry.title: X Marks the Spot: Diffusion for Image Geolocalization with Location Representations

author.name: Brian Wei, Chih-Chuan Hsu, Tianyi Gao, Daniel Cher, Eric Xing, Danielle Beaulieu, Nathan Jacobs

entry.summary: This work reformulates diffusion-based image geolocalization by predicting in the representation space of frozen location encoders rather than raw coordinates, which are semantically unstable. A Location Autoencoder pairs a frozen location encoder with a decoder that maps embeddings to coordinates with kilometer-level accuracy, enabling the diffusion model to exploit both positional and semantic structure.

entry.title: HiPFuse: Real-Time LiDAR Semantic Segmentation for Robotic Perception on Edge Devices

author.name: Haiyang Wu, George Vosselman, Ville Lehtola

entry.summary: HiPFuse fuses point features with height-partitioned bird's-eye-view features across horizontal scales to avoid mixing differently labeled surfaces within BEV columns. It achieves 63.7% mIoU on SemanticKITTI at 14.2 FPS and 62.5% on MCD at 22.4 FPS on a Jetson AGX Orin edge device. This is a strong efficiency-accuracy point for real-time robotic perception on constrained hardware.

entry.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models

author.name: Runjia Li, Minghao Chen, Junyu Xie, Philip Torr, Andrea Vedaldi, Tomas Jakab

entry.summary: Proposes extracting action representations from foundation models rather than learning latent action spaces from scratch via frame-reconstruction bottlenecks, addressing scarce and fragmented action-label supervision in video world model training. This aims to improve generalization to unseen domains while preserving expressive nuance.

entry.title: SIGMO: Sigmoid Gated Interaction-Aware Motion Planning

author.name: Avinash Singh, Manish Saroya, Fatemeh Cheraghi Pouria, Faizan Tariq, Jovin D'sa, David Isele, Yosuke Sakamoto, Sangjae Bae

entry.summary: SIGMO is an interaction-aware motion planner for autonomous driving in cluttered scenarios (narrow passages, dense lane changes, unsignalized intersections) using sigmoid gating to balance proactivity, interpretability, and adaptability without freezing or over-conservatism. It targets scalability to multiple agents and responsiveness to other agents' behavior changes.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Ismail Hossain Polas

entry.summary: Re-evaluates tabular foundation models (TabPFN-2.5/3.5 variants, TabICL v2) against Optuna-tuned gradient-boosted trees on five telecom churn datasets, using profit (EMP) and calibration metrics rather than ranking metrics alone. With split-aware testing and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, it challenges claims that TFMs decisively beat tuned GBDTs.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Network-Based Interventions for HIV Treatment and Prevention via R2C-Agent

author.name: Akseli Kangaslahti, Milind Tambe, Alastair van Heerden, Cheryl Johnson

entry.summary: The paper addresses optimizing network-based HIV intervention targeting when full contact networks are unobservable, using digitally collectable peer referral networks that deviate structurally from risk networks. R2C-Agent adapts agentic methods to correct for these deviations and guide scalable treatment and prevention resource allocation, continuing a line of AAMAS work with health collaboration (Tambe group).

entry.title: BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions

author.name: Shenxi Liu, Yiwei Li, Mingyang Zhao, Yuhang Tian, Kan Li

entry.summary: BARS formalizes self-consistency sampling in LLMs as majority identification under an unknown distribution with a budget and target error rate, providing a sequential rule that certifies the top-two answer gap. It returns an early stop, a budgeted majority vote, or a principled refusal when feasibility cannot be established.

entry.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series

author.name: Sachith Abeywickrama, Emadeldeen Eldele, Min Wu, Xiaoli Li, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: ConceptTime uses predictive surprise from a frozen probabilistic forecaster as a single self-supervised signal to simultaneously learn segment boundaries and concept vocabularies for time-series classification. This closes the circularity between defining patterns and placing boundaries, jointly delivering accuracy, interpretability, and abstention in risk-sensitive domains.

entry.title: Just Image Transformers with Late-Stage Pixel Refinement

author.name: Denis Lukovnikov, Andreas M\"uller, Asja Fischer

entry.summary: Revisiting latent-free diffusion transformers (JiT), the authors show that adding simple convolutional pixel-pathway layers in a post-training phase significantly improves generation quality. This addresses quality loss from modeling images as large patches while keeping the VAE-free training pipeline.

entry.title: The AI Era's Lines of Code? A Case Study on What an Engineer's Token Spend Measures

author.name: Shyam Agarwal, Olga Lvova, Agnia Sergeyuk, Anastasiia Serova, Timofey Bryksin, Thomas Zimmermann, Bogdan Vasilescu

entry.summary: The study links five weeks of coding-agent token usage to commits from 404 engineers at JetBrains plus a survey of 412 employees, finding token spend varies mostly between individuals and correlates only weakly with output: doubling spend was associated with roughly 10% more commits, and work metrics explained only 38% of between-engineer variation. The paper questions whether token spend is a valid productivity or adoption metric for organizations. It provides rare empirical grounding for AI-era engineering measurement debates.

entry.title: Placing LLM Lookup Tables by Per-Layer Prefetch Deadlines

author.name: Wen Huang, Jack Liu

entry.summary: This systems paper analyzes the 203 GB of Engram n-gram lookup tables in DeepSeek-V4.1 (an existing model released in October 2026), which occupy most host DRAM in serving, and shows that per-layer prefetch deadlines (differing by 30x between the model's two Engram layers), session reuse, and device contention determine feasible memory-tier placement. The authors build SlackTier, an SGLang table tier that issues all lookups at step start, plus an analytical model predicting slowdown from measured read times. The work offers concrete memory-hierarchy guidance for serving large lookup-augmented models.

entry.title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Yuqi Xiong, Qing Yang, Zhipeng Xu, Zhenghao Liu, Zulong Chen, Yubin Bao

entry.summary: PASE is a framework where agent skills are associated with executable programs and iteratively evolved via patching, moving beyond natural-language skill documents that entangle procedural logic with descriptive knowledge. It distills reusable experience from execution trajectories and adapts skills using downstream task feedback without modifying model parameters.

entry.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities

author.name: Zhengxiang Huang, Yujie Sun, Shengheng Chen, Zhaode Wang, Chaoyue Niu, Zeyu Zhao, Chengfei Lv, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: EngineAgent automates adding new LLM model support to on-device inference engines by constructing a hierarchy-aware index of engine abstraction layers, hardware capabilities, and cross-layer dependencies, separating reusable engine knowledge from model-specific implementation. This lets it coordinate changes across conversion, graph construction, operators, and hardware backends.

entry.title: Explanation-Aware Fairness Beyond Output Parity: Joint Output-Attribution Regularization for Medical Image Classification

author.name: G\"okhan \"Ozbulak, Oscar Jimenez-del-Toro, Lilian Berton, Andr\'e Anjos

entry.summary: The paper shows that output-level fairness can hide subgroup differences in feature attributions due to cancellation effects, and proposes an attribution disparity penalty complementing equalized-odds-style fairness surrogates. Experiments across 960 DINOv2-LoRA models on two medical datasets show improved utility-fairness trade-offs with statistical rigor.

entry.title: AdjointFlow: Accelerating Scientific Inverse Problems with Physics-Based Transport

author.name: Ethan Hanold, Nicholas M. Boffi, Qin Li, Leonardo Zepeda-N\'u\~nez

entry.summary: AdjointFlow is a framework for scientific inverse problems that combines stochastic interpolants with known physics to build transport maps, avoiding the ill-conditioning of purely data-driven conditional diffusion models and the repeated expensive simulations of plug-and-play methods. It targets applications like seismic imaging, astrophysics, and nondestructive testing.

entry.title: FedVP: Federated Learning across Heterogeneous Models by Pooling Locally Trained Verifiers

author.name: Yifan Li, Xi Chen

entry.summary: FedVP is a new federated learning paradigm in which heterogeneous clients collaborate by pooling locally trained verifiers rather than aggregating model parameters: each client trains a verifier on its own data and responses from its chosen LLM backbone, and the server combines verifier judgments to select answers. This allows different model families and sizes to collaborate while keeping data local and backbones frozen.

entry.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents

author.name: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys, Pranav Murugan, Nate Gruver

entry.summary: Pyrite is a benchmark of 1,500 protein-ligand pose pairs for evaluating binding-pose ranking, a bottleneck in small-molecule drug discovery where cofolding models generate diverse candidates but ranking remains unreliable. Expert chemists with 3D tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, underscoring task difficulty. The authors introduce PyriteRep, a structured molecular representation, and LLM-based agents including PyriteReasoner for automated pose comparison.

entry.title: VC-Dimension and Generalization in Geometric Machine Learning with Applications to Active Learning

author.name: Gokul Bhusal, Delanna Do, Ekaterina Merkurjev, Kevin Miller, Stephan Wojtowytsch

entry.summary: The paper computes VC-dimensions of metric ball classifiers across Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic, and other geometric model spaces, proving bounds in normed spaces, flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds. It derives generalization bounds under distributional assumptions where VC-dimension is large or infinite, with applications to active learning.

entry.title: Curriculum proof repair with learned counterexamples

author.name: Yuechun Sun, Jun Yang, Kexin Pei

entry.summary: TopoVerus is an LM-based framework for repairing Verus verification proofs that internalizes counterexample-guided diagnosis as a model capability, generating useful counterexamples in a single pass rather than through costly iterative refinement with the verifier. This improves on verifier-in-the-loop paradigms whose binary pass/fail feedback offers little actionable repair signal. It connects formal verification with learned diagnosis for reliable software.

entry.title: CroCoMAE: Cross-modal self-supervised collaborative representation learning for SAR-optical remote sensing data

author.name: Vito Recchia, Giuseppe Guarino, C\'assio Fraga Dantas, Giuseppina Andresini, Annalisa Appice, Dino Ienco

entry.summary: Proposes CroCoMAE, a cross-modal self-supervised framework for SAR-optical remote sensing that unifies contrastive learning and masked image modeling in a ViT architecture, operating at both global and patch levels to exploit fine-grained complementarity between sensors. It addresses scarce ground-truth labels by leveraging co-located sensor data.

entry.title: From Relevant Posts to Attributable Spans: Explicit Symptom Evidence for Depression Questionnaire Inference

author.name: Sumanth Manduru, Carlotta Domeniconi

entry.summary: Proposes SREE, an evidence-grounded pipeline for inferring standardized depression questionnaire responses from longitudinal social-media histories by extracting first-person, symptom-specific text spans rather than relying on semantic-similarity retrieval, which can return misleading or non-attributable evidence. The approach improves the specificity and accountability of mental-health inference from text.

entry.title: One Sequence Is Enough: Fingerprinting Language Models from Fixed-Length Integer Sequences

author.name: Fantong Meng, Chengjie Sun, Shuangjia Yang, Zhiyuan Zhao, Yansheng Pei, Xinyang Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses model identity verification when API-declared model names may not match the actual responding model, using numerical-choice behavior as a fingerprint. It introduces NumPrint, a benchmark of 5,036 answers from 51 models elicited via multilingual prompts requesting 294 integers between 1 and 355 in one response, plus a proposed classifier (Shallow MLP and Causal Transformer). A single fixed-length sequence can thus identify the source model, supporting transparency and accountability in model marketplaces.

entry.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Xu Huang, Ye Huang, Xiaotong Li, Zhengrong Yue, Jialv Zou, Minhao Jing, Haodong Li, Wenhao Yan, Yaxin Luo, Duomin Wang, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: G-STAR derives a scaling principle for discrete autoregressive image generation showing that, under a fixed information budget, product-quantization group size should scale quadratically with per-axis spatial compression. Its co-scaling framework achieves 32x and effective 64x compression while preserving reconstruction, understanding, and generation quality, with a module to model intra-group dependencies.

entry.title: RF3DGS: Reflection-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting with Self-Priors

author.name: Qiang Wen (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Guotao Meng (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Junhong Ruan (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Hongyu Liu (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Chenyang Lei (Huawei Research), Qifeng Chen (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: RF3DGS removes reflections from 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions using only a photometric self-prior: the minimum pixel intensity across multi-view observations of a 3D point correlates with reflection-free content. It first estimates coarse reflection-free depth via a geometric prior, then leverages it within the multi-view 3DGS optimization. Applications include high-fidelity visualization such as museum exhibitions.

entry.title: TAMEing the Open-World Personalization: Towards Open-Set Personalized MLLM Assistant

author.name: Rongpei Hong, Jian Lang, Ting Zhong, Fan Zhou

entry.summary: TAME-O recasts MLLM personalization as an open-set problem, allowing assistants to recognize and incorporate newly emerging user-specific concepts without manual extension of a predefined concept set. It is claimed to be the first long-context open-set personalization framework for MLLMs. This addresses a real limitation of current personalization approaches in dynamic interaction settings.

entry.title: From Egocentric Human Video to Robot Manipulation in the Era of Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Yi Wang, Jingqiu Wu, Lei Yao, Zhaoshuo Li, Haoyu Zhu, Yirui Zhou, Huaiyuan Xu, Ying Zheng, Chuang Yang, Lap-Pui Chau

entry.summary: A survey defining Ego2Robot learning, the process of learning robot manipulation policies from egocentric human video, organized into four paradigms: embodiment transfer, action/task supervision, egocentric representation pretraining, and latent action/dynamics modeling. It analyzes what each paradigm derives from human video and its challenges regarding morphology, viewpoint, and action space gaps.

entry.title: RedirectMimic: Local Motion Content Redaction for Humanoid Whole-Body Control

author.name: Zepeng Wang, Xiaochuan Shi

entry.summary: RedirectMimic introduces local motion content redaction for humanoid whole-body control, allowing application-specific movement constraints (e.g., edited arm poses or speeds) while the controller still receives the original reference, by separating the actor's observed reference from a rule-edited tracking target during PPO. It is evaluated on Unitree G1 simulation with a pretrained tracker.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5.2 can do "weight-space-programming" about as well as GPT-6 Astra

author.name: shawnghu

entry.summary: The author reran a published paper's weight-space programming experiments (improving small models on math benchmarks, writing Go-playing networks from scratch) using Claude Fable 5.2 instead of GPT-6 Astra, with Opus 5.5 executing the replication, and found Fable reproduces essentially all qualitative results. This provides a rare head-to-head frontier model comparison on a novel agentic capability benchmark.

entry.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence

author.name: Hendrik Luuk

entry.summary: Proposes a competence circuit framework decomposing an agent's real-world impact into intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control, then formalizes conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff. Stochastic simulations on NK fitness landscapes validate that most takeoff pathways rely on knowledge acquisition or control rather than raw intelligence.

entry.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes

author.name: Liu Hung Ming (PARRAWA AI, cyril.liu@gmail.com, equal contribution), Tian Xia (PAII, TianXia0209@gmail.com, equal contribution)

entry.summary: This paper studies emergent communication between learned sender and receiver agents, showing that monitoring a visible communication channel causes agents to adaptively shift information into unmonitored shadow routes rather than eliminating communication entirely. Through controlled experiments with multiple seed batches and frozen interventions, the authors provide causal evidence that route choice carries semantic content, with implications for AI oversight of multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Trust, but verify, audit and attribute: a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results

author.name: Gy\"orgy Eigner, Patrik P. S\"uli, Roland Holl\'os

entry.summary: The authors propose a domain-independent human-in-the-loop framework for auditing AI-generated research results, motivated by the flood of AI-produced manuscripts (over 700 in one month per the abstract) and the fact that machine-checked proofs only certify the checked artifact, not the author's text. They argue faithfulness of proof translations is generally undecidable, so human attribution and auditing workflows must be institutionalized.

entry.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development

author.name: Wenji Fang, Yuchao Wu, Jing Wang, Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: This invited paper surveys how agentic AI and hardware formal verification mutually reinforce each other: AI advances formal methods across specification, proof construction, and reasoning engines, while formal methods support reliable AI-driven hardware development through RTL generation, debugging, and correctness-preserving optimization.

entry.title: Ceci n'est pas une pipe -- Toward a Symbolic Solver for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Using Evolutionary Computation

author.name: Luca Favole, Giorgio Mongardi, Giovanni Squillero, Alberto Tonda

entry.summary: This paper applies evolutionary algorithms to the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), a benchmark for few-shot generalization where evolutionary methods have been notably absent from main contest entries. The authors address representation-selection issues in domain-specific languages, such as choosing between pixel-level and object-level abstractions.

entry.title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

author.name: S M Rayeed, Charles V. Stewart, Yao Ma

entry.summary: CLADE addresses resolvable insufficiency in retrieval-augmented systems, where retrieved passages state answers at a coarser granularity than the question requires but the broader category maps to a short candidate list in a domain ontology. It characterizes a family-guessing phenomenon when models read such coarse passages and proposes category-level answering.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning

author.name: Souhaila Djaffal, Amna Jamal, Gagana Madhugiri Devaraja, Anidipta Pal, Jobst Heitzig

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks whether five LLMs can generate formal world models as partially observable stochastic games from natural-language multi-agent situations. It introduces 44 scenarios evaluated across mechanical validity, structural agreement, and semantic criteria, finding that mechanical validity alone does not guarantee faithful representation of the intended decision problem.

entry.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs

author.name: Ruimeng Liu, Denan Liang, Ruofei Bai, Fuming Zhang, Kuan Xu, Shenghai Yuan, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: PhysMoE improves spatial grounding in embodied VLMs by routing upper layers to specialized spatial and linguistic experts to eliminate gradient interference, encoding coordinates as a single token reusing visual encoder representations, and handling multi-contact affordances and irregular targets that defeat point regression. It targets low decoding latency for robotic planning and manipulation.

entry.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development

author.name: Fumiki Yohena, Toshiaki Sota, Shota Suzuki, Tomoko Okamoto, Michiaki Tatsubori

entry.summary: This work improves coding agents that receive UI screenshots in bug reports by augmenting degraded query images with crisp reference screenshots rendered from the same repository. This repository-grounded approach sidesteps VLM reliability loss and OCR error propagation when visual evidence in the original screenshot is poor.

entry.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training

author.name: Shenghui Li, Li Ju, Thiemo Voigt

entry.summary: HiLo is a compressor-agnostic framework that replaces LoRA parameter transmission to rollout workers with compressed gradient dissemination plus local optimizer replay, keeping learner and workers synchronized under bandwidth constraints while training at full rank. The companion Spar compressor combines specialized gradient compression with budget awareness. This directly targets a known bottleneck in distributed on-policy post-training pipelines like RLHF.

entry.title: Inherited Weights: Measuring the Tokenization Premium and the Sovereignty Cost of Language Models for the Global South

author.name: Paulo Camara (LUA Vision)

entry.summary: The paper measures the tokenization premium across 31 languages and seven 2023-2024 tokenizers on Universal Declaration of Human Rights articles, finding premiums up to 10x for Amharic in older tokenizers and 6.8x in the newest commercial one, with Indigenous South American languages paying 1.6x-2.7x. It further argues that fine-tuned descendants of a few pretrained families inherit vocabulary, knowledge, cultural alignment, and license constraints from their bases, framing this as a sovereignty cost for the Global South. The contribution is both a reproducible measurement and a policy-relevant conceptual framing.

entry.title: Dark Matters: VAE-Aware HDR Encoding for SDR-to-HDR Video Reconstruction

author.name: Donghoon Cha, Bomseok Park, Hansl von Kwon, Ku DoHyung, Hanwool Sul

entry.summary: This paper addresses SDR-to-HDR video reconstruction, showing that common log-like encodings suppress low-luminance chromatic information in frozen VAE latents, causing a dark-side collapse. The authors propose EquivFlow, a compact invertible exposure-equivariant encoding that maps exposure changes to additive latent shifts without modifying the VAE.

entry.title: MicroBT: Centroid-Guided Synergistic Learning for Multi-Modal Micro Brain Tumor Segmentation and Counting

author.name: Zhenye Lou, Qing Xu, Stefanie Thust, Dorothee P. Auer, Zhen Chen, Wenting Duan

entry.summary: MicroBT addresses the systematic suppression of sub-3mm micro-lesions by overlap-based training objectives, introducing a unified multi-modal framework for micro brain tumor segmentation and instance-level counting. It exploits centroid-based geometric guidance to jointly model tiny lesions and produce reliable lesion counts relevant to clinical staging.

entry.title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models

author.name: Dave Murray-Rust, Elisa Giaccardi, Federico Bomba, Maria Luce Lupetti

entry.summary: This position paper argues that bias is the wrong conceptual lens for evaluating general-purpose language models, since bias presupposes an external standard that open-ended generation lacks. The authors propose positionality — the located, articulated, and contestable position from which statements are made — as a more appropriate evaluative grammar for LLMs.

entry.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR

author.name: Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor, Florin C. Ghesu, Sasa Grbic, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: The paper builds a multi-domain foundation model for medical lesion detection by integrating heterogeneous datasets annotated for anatomical structures and abnormalities, using a student-teacher strategy to merge disparate label spaces and mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Example-based grounding in an EM-DETR architecture supports generalization across domains.

entry.title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks, and Frontiers

author.name: Rui Xue, Tianfu Wu

entry.summary: A survey of learning on multimodal attributed graphs, organizing the field into graph-centric fusion methods and foundation-model-centric approaches that integrate graph context into multimodal LLMs. It reviews models and benchmarks with an evaluation-grounded, algorithm-centric perspective.

entry.title: Robust Flow Matching under Target Corruption and Label Noise

author.name: Mert Can Kurucu, Erik Englesson, Hossein Azizpour

entry.summary: The paper formulates flow matching training as time-dependent regression over conditional vector fields and analyzes how target corruption and label noise degrade the objective differently. It proposes corruption-specific residual scores mapped to sample weights, including a Temporal Residual Score for target corruption, to improve FM robustness.

entry.title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage

author.name: Purva Pruthi, Andrew Yuan, Alexander D'Amour, David Jensen

entry.summary: This systematic evaluation shows that inconsistent findings on transformer compositional generalization stem from two overlooked aspects of train-test splits: composition equivalence and module coverage. It demonstrates that apparent performance of direct models trained only on final outputs largely reflects exploitable structure in the splits rather than genuine compositional ability.

entry.title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence

author.name: Sayed Amir Karim (Pelloran Inc.)

entry.summary: The paper presents tritify, an open-source runtime that executes the full forward pass of real models - decoder-only LLMs, MoE decoders, and the Segment Anything 2.1 stack - in exact integer arithmetic, achieving bit-identical outputs across hardware, instruction sets, and CPU/GPU. It verifies three claims including cross-hardware reproducibility and verifiable distributed inference, with floating point confined to offline quantization.

entry.title: Plug-and-Play ADMM for Inverse Problems with Flow Matching Denoiser

author.name: Dibyanshu Kumar, Magda Gregorova

entry.summary: This paper proposes an ADMM-based plug-and-play framework for inverse problems that uses flow matching models as generative priors, enforcing tighter consistency between data-fidelity updates and the learned prior via auxiliary variables and dual updates. It also introduces a trajectory correction mechanism combining deterministic and stochastic projections to keep iterates on the flow trajectory. This matters because data-consistency steps drifting off the flow manifold is a core failure mode of modern PnP reconstruction.

entry.title: Omni-JEV: Text and Dual-Stream Speech Decisions

author.name: Shengzhou Kong

entry.summary: This arXiv paper addresses full-duplex dialogue, where an utterance alone does not determine the assistant's next action because consequences depend on response state and interaction history. The authors introduce Omni-JEV, a model that maps text or role-indexed user and assistant speech streams to probabilities over five interaction actions (such as turn-taking and interruption decisions), using an aligned speech-to-speech understanding backbone that encodes acoustic roles separately while sharing a candidate readout with text inputs. Training uses bilingual weak supervision with cross-entropy fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning, making it relevant to more natural, real-time voice assistants.

entry.title: Generalizing Causal Decision-Making: Markov Equivalence, Transportability and Counterfactuals

author.name: Min Woo Park, Sanghack Lee

entry.summary: This paper extends structural causal bandits to partially known causal structure, information from other environments, and realizable counterfactual actions. It develops graphical criteria for minimal intervention sets under Markov equivalence, characterizes possibly-optimal sets for maximal ancestral graphs, and derives reward bounds from source distributions via partial transportability including non-manipulable variables. This meaningfully broadens the practical applicability of causal bandits under incomplete knowledge.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Autoencoder for Interpretable Health Representation Learning in Turbofan Engines

author.name: Leonardo Baldo, Jokin Alcibar Ibarzabal, Daniel Cisneros Acevedo, Kai Goebel, Manuel Arias Chao

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes a physics-constrained autoencoder for learning interpretable Health Indices (HIs) in turbofan engine prognostics and health management. Instead of relying purely on reconstruction loss, the method embeds physical system knowledge both architecturally (differentiable physical equations in the decoder that consume latent variables) and as a learning bias in the loss function. This yields latent representations with defined physical meaning, improving interpretability and diagnostic value over standard black-box autoencoders trained on unlabeled monitoring data.

entry.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yu Tian

entry.summary: The paper identifies flaws in existing block-level training objectives for speculative decoding: they are surrogates rather than exact formulations of expected acceptance length, and some introduce a covariance gap that can reverse gradient direction. It proposes REAL loss, an exact objective for the real expected acceptance length governing speedup. This should improve draft-model training for faster LLM inference.

entry.title: DUO: Dual Readouts of Diffusion Models for OOD Detection

author.name: Alireza Javid, Shirin Shoushtari, Nuria Gonz\'alez Prelcic

entry.summary: DUO proposes the leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features as a complementary out-of-distribution signal for diffusion models, remaining informative when reconstruction error fails because OOD inputs may reconstruct as well as in-distribution ones. This dual-readout approach improves the reliability of safe deployment of diffusion models.

entry.title: Simultaneous Near-Optimal Region Identification in Continuous Simulation Optimization: Minimax Complexity and Adaptive Sampling

author.name: Yilin Zheng, Haowei Wang, Wenjia Wang, Szu Hui Ng

entry.summary: This paper studies how to identify the set of designs whose expected performance lies within a tolerance of the optimum on continuous design spaces, simultaneously for all tolerances up to a maximum. The authors prove minimax lower bounds showing region identification is fundamentally harder than optimization, and develop adaptive sampling procedures matching these bounds. This matters because decision makers often need near-optimal sets rather than a single estimated optimum when weighing simulation-independent criteria like cost.

entry.title: BODYinTRANSIT-Lab: A Multimodal Dataset for Investigating Sensory-Driven Transformations in Body Perception and Affective Experiences

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Dehshibi, Tom\'{a}s Mart\'{i}nez Cort\'{e}s, Amar D'Adamo, Daniel de la Prida, Luis-Antonio Azpicueta-Ru\'{i}z, Laia Turmo Vidal, Marte Roel Lesur, Joaqu\'{i}n R. D\'{i}az-Dur\'{a}n, Alexander V\"{a}ljam\"{a}e, Angel S\'{a}nchez, Temitayo Olugbade, Nadia Bianchi-Berthouze, Fernando D\'{i}az-de-Mar\'{i}a, Ana Tajadura-Jim\'{e}nez

entry.summary: Introduces a multimodal dataset of 101 participants performing walking tasks with real-time manipulated auditory feedback of their own footsteps (the Footsteps Illusion), designed to alter perceived body weight. It synchronizes behavioural, physiological, and subjective affective/body-perception measures, supporting computational models that infer subjective embodied states from sensor data.

entry.title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents

author.name: Mingchen Li, Yongkang Xiao, Rumeng Li, Rui Zhang, Hong Yu

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates agentic memory systems for biomedical LLM agents across task effectiveness, retrieval quality, information fidelity, and long-term robustness, testing five memory approaches with four LLMs in knowledge reasoning, clinical prediction, and long-term conversational settings. It provides empirical guidance on how reliably these systems retain and use biomedical information.

entry.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models

author.name: Jack T. Parley

entry.summary: This theoretically oriented paper studies how Transformers learn to approximate inside-outside parsing algorithms during training, using synthetic context-free grammars with variable parse tree topology. Learning curves are fully interpretable: each loss stage can be computed analytically and associated with a hidden latent tree variable, revealing stagewise emergence of compositional parsing computation. It is a first step from post-mortem interpretability findings toward a theory of how parsing-like computation is learned.

entry.title: Walrus Technical Report

author.name: Alkis Koudounas, Osamu Take, Hayato Futami, Quentin Jodelet, Emiru Tsunoo

entry.summary: Walrus is a unified 8B speech-and-audio foundation model covering recognition, translation (speech-to-text and speech-to-speech), TTS, emotion recognition, captioning, and general audio understanding, built on a decoder-only backbone initialized from Gemma 4. Its main contribution is a data-centric three-stage curriculum rather than a new architecture, with speech generation via low-bitrate discrete tokens decoded by a lightweight waveform decoder.

entry.title: Continuous Angular Control in Text-to-Image Generation via Geometric Token Encoding

author.name: Furkan G\"uzelant, Basavaraj Sunagad, Aysegul Dundar, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: This paper identifies a systematic failure in text-to-image diffusion models: they cannot control continuous angular quantities such as the time on an analog clock, collapsing to canonical poses like 10:10 in under 1% of cases matching the prompt. The authors propose a geometric token encoding that conditions generation directly on angular variables, enabling precise control over clock times and circular fractions across four pretrained models.

entry.title: A 10K drone image dataset with component-level annotations for rooftop photovoltaic inspection

author.name: Penglei Zhang, Wan Zhang, Ruizhe Deng, Bo Chen, Wenhao Duan, Jinhe Zhang, Yanzhen Zhang, Qi Chen, Zhiling Guo, Haoran Zhang, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: PVIS-10K provides 10,065 high-resolution drone images with over 3.5 million polygon annotations covering 63,632 PV modules across 22 rooftop installations in China, with 3D-consistent multi-angle acquisition. The dataset captures challenging real-world conditions including occlusion, shadows, and reflections for component-level PV inspection. It fills a real gap in renewable energy infrastructure monitoring data.

entry.title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models

author.name: Guoqiang Liang, Yiqi Lin, Yanzhe Chen, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Frames the injection of low-dimensional robot signals (proprioception, actions, values) into pretrained video diffusion models as a distribution-alignment problem, proposing a unified latent interface using meta-frames rather than separate latent frames or bolt-on encoders. This supports building World Action Models that jointly predict actions and future observations.

entry.title: A Functional Preservation Score for Auditing Connectome Operations: Compression, Alignment, Transport, and Local-Rule Writing

author.name: Praveg Vashishtha

entry.summary: Introduces the Functional Preservation Score (FPS), a null-normalized, behaviorally grounded metric quantifying how much of a neural network's input-output function survives structural operations like quantization, alignment, and transport. The authors apply FPS across five pre-registered studies on the C. elegans connectome, whole-brain calcium activity, and hippocampal replay, characterizing quantization sparsity floors and auditing speculative mind-migration pipelines on laptop-scale public data.
