entry.title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads

author.name: Xianghui Wang, Aoran Fu, Liyou Luo, Shanze Wang, Xiaoyu Shen, Dan Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: ReACT tackles the problem that carrying an object in one hand biases humanoid locomotion velocity tracking, causing position and heading drift that can lead to navigation failure. It uses reflection-consistent disturbance modulation and cross-load consistency to maintain accurate velocity command execution under asymmetric upper-body loads.

entry.title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions

author.name: Muheng Li, Peize Zhang, Xin Bing

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator for mixtures of logistic regressions with unspecified mixing distributions, deriving nonasymptotic estimation-error bounds under fixed and random designs that expose an explicit tradeoff between statistical error and sieve approximation error. It provides convergence rates under several tail conditions on the mixing distribution.

entry.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models

author.name: Shogo Sato, Tomoyasu Shimada, Kazuhiko Murasaki, Takashi Sano

entry.summary: Extends weight-space programming to PDE solving with Physics2Weight, which uses physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing to have LLMs directly generate network weights without gradient training. Iterative weight refinement improves both solution accuracy and physical consistency.

entry.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation

author.name: Mehmet Onur Keskin, Berk Buzcu, Nikhil Churamani, Reyhan Aydogan, Hatice Gunes, Catholijn Jonker

entry.summary: The paper introduces CLIFER, a continual-learning approach for facial expression recognition that personalizes valence-arousal perception in real time during human-agent negotiation, with differential feedback mapping affect changes to the agent's target utility. A within-subject study with 66 participants evaluated the affect-adaptive negotiation strategy against baselines.

entry.title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation

author.name: An Zhao, Yixiang Zhou, Zejian Li, Yi Guo, Pei Chen, Lingyun Sun

entry.summary: TRD combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision for distilling flow matching models into one-step generators, using a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. This policy simultaneously acts as generator, student marginal velocity estimator, and weight source, avoiding a separate score-tracking network required by pure distribution matching.

entry.title: Structured Kernel Surrogate Models for Multimodal Attribution

author.name: Ziniu Zhang, Zhenshuo Zhang, Jianglin Lu, Ruoxuan Xiong, Yun Fu, Hongyang R. Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces cross-sample modality attribution, measuring how a modality in one sample affects learning outcomes in other multimodal samples, and proposes structured kernel surrogate models to capture interactions across both samples and modalities. This extends influence-function-style analysis beyond single-sample settings.

entry.title: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules

author.name: Alexandros Hollender, Sonja Kraiczy

entry.summary: This alignment-theory paper models constitutional principles as voters that compare responses (e.g., preferring more helpful or less toxic outputs), represented as linear directions in embedding space following the Linear Representation Hypothesis. Building on a prior result that optimal linear reward models can violate Pareto optimality, the work studies when and how axiomatic properties can be enforced for loss-based rule aggregation in RLHF-style training. It brings formal social choice theory to bear on pluralistic alignment.

entry.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Huiyi Chen, Weitai Kang, Shicheng Fan, Xinshuo Wang, Zhixiang Shen, Yan Yan, Philip S. Yu, Baoxin Li

entry.summary: PhyRubric is a rubric-grounded framework for diagnosing physical commonsense violations in text-to-video models, constructing caption-specific semantic and physical rubric items before viewing videos and scoring from timestamped item-level verdicts. This replaces subjective single-score human ratings with diagnostic, principle-level evaluation.

entry.title: Satellite Pretraining Is Not One Thing: A Matched-Pair Study of Generic and Earth-Observation Foundation Models for Scene Classification

author.name: Sandarbh Agrawal, Rakshith Sathish, Ashwathi Nambiar

entry.summary: This matched-pair study compares five pairs of Earth-observation and generic encoders sharing objective and architecture, such as DINO versus SatDINO and MAE versus SatMAE, across 14 frozen encoders on five scene-classification datasets with paired significance tests. The key finding is that EO pretraining is not uniformly helpful; its advantage depends on the encoder and settings, correcting a common assumption.

entry.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge

author.name: Ilia Larchenko, Gleb Zarin, Atindra Nair, Keerti Manney, Vitaly Kleban, Mirko Kiefer, Anjana Yodaiken

entry.summary: The paper describes an independent team's 9th-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: a single VLA model, one checkpoint for 100 long-horizon household tasks in OmniGibson, built on a pi0.5-based 2025 winner. Most gains came from extended training, tuned hyperparameters, faster training steps, and reduced gradient noise, raising Q from 0.260 to 0.371 on shared tasks.

entry.title: High Probability Risk Control for Online Policy Learning

author.name: Yihong Guo, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Anqi Liu

entry.summary: The paper addresses risk control for online policy learning under feedback covariate shift, where data collection depends on evolving policies. It proposes a permutation-based weighted risk evaluator approximated via Sinkhorn iterations and selects policies with high-probability upper confidence bounds on risk.

entry.title: SLIC: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Small LMs for Multi-Turn Analog Circuit Optimization

author.name: Yan Xu, Zhengqi Gao, Ching-Yun Ko, Zhang-Wei Hong, Wenjie Lu, Tao Yu, Xin Zhang, Duane S. Boning, Ruonan Han

entry.summary: SLIC is a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that trains a 4B-parameter locally deployable language model for closed-loop analog circuit design optimization, using structured circuit representations, domain-gated multiobjective rewards, and Reward-Guided Rollout Steering that converts simulator feedback into learning signals. It targets the practical constraint that proprietary process design kits prevent hosted LLM workflows.

entry.title: Sanity Checks for Attention Surgery: Null Models and Matched Interventions for Representation-Motivated Design

author.name: Basavaraj R M, Aryan Bharat Kumar

entry.summary: The paper formulates three reusable sanity checks for representation-driven architectural modifications: whether a measured statistic exceeds its noise floor, whether it survives a geometric null, and whether training gains require the specific direction removed. Applied to self-attention removal across nine pretrained models (5,408 heads, 124M-6.9B parameters), an earlier-position causal null accounts for 48-63% of head-value cosine alignment.

entry.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime

author.name: Daniel Lenton

entry.summary: Continual-ARC is a lifelong learning benchmark built from the three ARC-AGI editions, presenting tasks as a continuous stream where the same tasks recur after dormant gaps with fresh instances. Learners may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act within the harness, allowing fair comparison of memory-based and weight-based continual learning systems. It addresses limitations of existing single-domain, single-use continual learning benchmarks.

entry.title: EvoSurv: Evolution-Aware Multimodal Survival Modeling Reveals Complementary Prognostic Signals

author.name: Wei Wang, Po-Yu Liang, Jun Bai

entry.summary: The paper introduces eTime, a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation of tumor genomic alterations covering clonal mutation burden, mutational spectra, and copy-number changes, and EvoSurv, a multimodal survival model integrating these with clinical and RNA data. Across six TCGA cohorts with 2,782 patients it achieves the highest mean concordance index, showing evolutionary signals complement standard modalities.

entry.title: Gradient Inversion through Linear and Affine Subspace Constraints

author.name: Konstantinos Bouros, Athanasios P. Liavas

entry.summary: This work strengthens gradient inversion attacks in federated learning by showing that aggregate gradients from a fully connected layer with correct scaling are an affine, not merely linear, combination of its inputs. The authors exploit this refined structural observation to improve reconstruction of client data from shared gradients. It highlights concrete privacy risks for federated learning deployments.

entry.title: DepthGS: Depth-Guided Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Regularization for High-Quality Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Xiao Ren, Yu Liu, Ning An, Jian Cheng, Xin Qiao, You-Fu Li, He Kong

entry.summary: DepthGS derives theoretical relations between depth discrepancies and reconstruction error under single- and multi-view settings, establishing upper bounds that inform adaptive depth-guided regularization for 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction. The principled analysis addresses the previously underexplored link between depth information and geometric optimization error.

entry.title: DailyWildfireCAN: A Dataset and Benchmark for Next-Day Wildfire Spread Prediction in Canada

author.name: Mahacine Ettahri, Hager Radi Abdelwahed, Toluwaleke Olutayo, Daniel Aloise, Ga\'etan Marceau Caron

entry.summary: DailyWildfireCAN is a multi-modal dataset and benchmark for next-day wildfire spread prediction in Canada, filling the gap left by US-focused wildfire datasets. It supports deep learning on heterogeneous environmental data capturing weather, fuel, and terrain interactions. This matters for fire management in a country with vast boreal forests and intensifying fire seasons.

entry.title: Few-Shot Residual Adaptation of Pretrained Latent World Models

author.name: Jakub Suliga, Pankhuri Vanjani, Nisarga Nilavadi, Wolfram Burgard, Rudolf Lioutikov

entry.summary: The paper shows that pretrained latent world models fail under physical parameter shifts like changed center of mass or friction, and introduces a few-shot residual adaptation method learning self-supervised corrections from latent prediction errors while keeping the pretrained weights frozen. It restores near-zero success rates in both simulation and on a real robot without identifying changed parameters.

entry.title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV

author.name: David D\"orner, Giancarlo Troni, Ignacio Torroba, Ivan Stenius

entry.summary: The paper develops a six-DoF nonlinear model predictive contouring controller for a holonomic underwater vehicle, augmenting the nominal dynamics with GP-learned residual models embedded via a zero-order robust optimization scheme. It addresses the difficulty of obtaining accurate dynamics models underwater for close-range structural inspection.

entry.title: One Curve, Different Weights: AUC, the Brier Score, Decision-Weighted AUC, and the Policy Youden Index

author.name: Yegor Baranovski

entry.summary: This paper shows that AUC, the Brier score, and a newly introduced decision-weighted AUC are all weighted averages of a single curve, the Youden index across cutoffs, differing only in their cutoff-weighting schemes that reflect all scores, true probabilities, or a decision maker's action probability. This unifying view clarifies when and why these metrics rank models differently.

entry.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding

author.name: Shanwen Wang, Sirui Wang, Xin Sun, Jungong Han

entry.summary: Proposes the first unified foundation model for landslides, connecting visual perception tasks with language-based contextual interpretation via a semi-supervised trust framework and parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a vision-language model. It targets low-label regimes and adds scene-understanding capability beyond isolated detection models.

entry.title: Earth Embeddings in Environmental Remote Sensing

author.name: Yuchi Ma, Jiaqi Yang, Mengyu Liang, Ivan Higuera-Mendieta, Caleb Robinson, Anthony Ortiz, Min Chen, David B. Lobell, Inbal Becker-Reshef, Juan M. Lavista Ferres

entry.summary: This survey/review examines Earth embeddings, general-purpose representations learned from multi-source satellite observations that support diverse downstream remote sensing tasks without task-specific feature engineering. It addresses how embeddings can mitigate uneven observation coverage, data gaps, and the heavy computational demands of multi-modal Earth observation processing.

entry.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data

author.name: Wei Gu, Weiwei Qi, Jiajun Tang, Tianhang Zheng, Bo Chen, Zhibo Zhang, Jinfei Liu, Kui Ren

entry.summary: TreeAgent is a memory agent for LLM processing of long hierarchical inputs like API responses and HTML, replacing flat fixed-length segmentation with structure-preserving methods that keep records intact and retain hierarchical context. It targets three failure modes of conventional memory agents: broken record fields, lost structural position, and discarded sibling-record details.

entry.title: Multimodal Abstention That Preserves Acquired Correct Answers

author.name: Jinyuan Zhang

entry.summary: ReFrain formulates abstention repair as maximizing correct abstention on unanswerable questions under a budget of newly lost correct answers, combining a first-token-logit linear probe, threshold calibration on held-out image clusters, and a deterministic veto mechanism. It achieves zero loss on the calibration set at the zero-budget target while preserving adapted-task capabilities.

entry.title: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces

author.name: Anastasis Kratsios, Yannick Limmer, Hans Buehler, Blanka Horvath, Raeid Saqur

entry.summary: AFNO is a neural operator framework that certifiably guarantees static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces, mapping RKHS inputs to convex combinations of arbitrage-free parameterizations. It is universal and addresses the practical problem that standard neural operators can produce negative PnL in downstream trading tasks.

entry.title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head

author.name: Llu\'is Arola-Fern\'andez, Aissam Khadraoui, Alex Arenas

entry.summary: The paper derives attention as the closed-form solution to a Kuramoto synchronization problem, where past tokens are oscillators whose frequencies encode age and the present token is a receiver aligned by content and position. Above a critical coupling the receiver locks and weights normalize; below it stays silent.

entry.title: MRFoundry: Knowledge-guided agent loops for end-to-end MRI research

author.name: Ke Wang, Atakan Topcu, Hossein Momeni, Molin Zhang

entry.summary: MRFoundry is an open-source package that connects AI coding agents to MRI domain knowledge, acquisition physics, specialized tools, and validation checks through knowledge-guided agent loops with project-local memory and reviewed shared guidance. The authors demonstrate supervised examples including sequence auditing and acquired-data reconstruction, and release MRI Agent Bench to compare agents on MRI tasks. This contributes both infrastructure and a benchmark for domain-specific scientific agents.

entry.title: You Don't Need Feature Learning to Do In-Context Learning

author.name: Joseph Turnbull, Jamie Simon

entry.summary: Studying the linear-regression in-context learning task with rotation-invariant kernel machines, the paper derives a spectral picture showing that as sample size grows, kernel machines learn successively higher-degree components of the memorizing solution, with the generalizing solution being a low-degree truncation. The model thus first generalizes and then degrades into memorization, all without any feature learning. This offers a clean kernel-eigenbasis account of memorization versus generalization in ICL.

entry.title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence

author.name: Stephen Peng, Vineet Jagadeesan Nair

entry.summary: The authors audit learned AC optimal power flow surrogates using thirteen metamorphic relations across 17 model configurations, finding every configuration violates at least six relations. For one released checkpoint they trace failures to an indexing bug and unstable preprocessing choices, demonstrating that surrogate accuracy can silently depend on grid serialization and encoding.

entry.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies

author.name: Jonas Limniatis, Bennet Schaarmann, Georg Reuber, Robert Stahlbock

entry.summary: TIGA formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process executed by tool-grounded LLM agents, ensuring constructed hierarchies are complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent rather than prone to hallucinated entities and inconsistent principles. Runtime-adaptive policies govern the agent's decisions during construction.

entry.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing

author.name: Naveen Babu Narayanan Nair, Sajay Kurup

entry.summary: VATC proposes a network QoS class for LLM-agent web traffic: a reserved DSCP marking declaring agent status, a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting the declaration, and a rate-limited priority queue. It is evaluated against DiffServ and fq_codel in simulators and on a real Linux kernel, including adversarial conditions.

entry.title: MicroLens: Read, Trace, and Rewire the Residual Stream with Two Lenses

author.name: Nika Zahedi, Fangyi Zhu, Anna Wu

entry.summary: MicroLens is an interactive interpretability viewer that decodes residual-stream cells with both logit and Jacobian lenses, traces them back to source tokens, and edits activations with live model reruns, demonstrated on Gemma-3-4B-it across hundreds of prompts. The two lenses reveal different directional information about what a vector reads as versus what the model uses.

entry.title: Settling the Burn-in Gap: Sharp Risk Bounds for Tail-Averaged SGD in Linear Regression

author.name: Qingyue Zhao, Xuheng Li, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: The authors establish matching instance-dependent upper and lower bounds on the excess risk of tail-averaged, constant-stepsize online SGD for high-dimensional linear regression, closing a previously known gap in the effective variance term related to initialization error in the head eigenspace. This resolves a theoretical inconsistency between earlier upper and lower bounds.

entry.title: SepsisFlow: an event-stream foundation model for continuous risk warning and trajectory modelling in ICU sepsis

author.name: Yawen Zhang, Wanzhe Xu, Zhenhua Zhang, Jinyu Wu, Yizhou Zhuang, Yitao Yang, Kenta Nakai

entry.summary: SepsisFlow is an end-to-end clinical foundation-model system for ICU sepsis that combines a Mamba model pretrained on 2.57 million EHRs with gradient-boosted trees for 6/12/24-hour risk prediction, fused encoders for onset context, and an attention bidirectional recurrent network for 72-hour post-onset trajectory modeling on a single hourly clock. It moves beyond binary alarm prediction to support the full clinical workflow.

entry.title: Universal Approximation Theorem for Metaplectic Neural Operators

author.name: Ahmed Abdeljawad, Malek Yacine Rezoug

entry.summary: The paper proves universal approximation for metaplectic neural operators on bounded Lipschitz domains, covering nonlocal branches built from whole-space metaplectic multipliers associated with free symplectic matrices. Under mild activation assumptions, a single hidden operator layer with one nonlocal branch achieves compact-uniform approximation between C^s/C^r and Sobolev spaces for arbitrary nonnegative integers s, r. This extends operator-learning theory to a mathematically rich class of nonlocal operators.

entry.title: Temporal Behavior Trees for Reinforcement Learning: Specifications as Rewards, Curricula, and Diagnostics

author.name: Vladimir Krsmanovic, Bernd Finkbeiner

entry.summary: TBTCL introduces Temporal Behavior Trees as a unified interface for specification-guided reinforcement learning: a single TBT defines the task, induces dense robustness-based rewards, defines a curriculum, and supports policy diagnostics. This removes fragmentation between task definition, reward shaping, curriculum design, and diagnostics that exists in prior formal-methods-for-RL pipelines. The unification preserves subtask structure such as ordering constraints and quantitative measures.

entry.title: Right for the Wrong Reasons? Evaluating Plausibility and Behavioral Change in Explanation-Guided Learning

author.name: David Dembinsky, Adriano Lucieri, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: This study uses a controlled synthetic shortcut dataset to test whether improved agreement between model explanations and human rationales in explanation-guided learning (EGL) actually changes the model's decision strategy. Across localized, background-based, and global shortcut types, effects are strongly objective-specific, revealing that explanation plausibility does not reliably imply behavioral change. This is an important caution for the increasingly popular practice of training models to match human rationales.

entry.title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making

author.name: Junhao Shen, Qing Zong, Yue Guo, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Hong Cheng

entry.summary: MMDM is a new benchmark of 5,448 questions across 16 task categories for evaluating System-1 decision models that make structured probabilistic decisions in a single forward pass. It combines newly constructed tasks with source-grounded reworkings to avoid contamination from prior benchmark exposure, and stresses long contexts, large option spaces, and complex logical dependencies. The benchmark targets generalization gaps left by existing evaluations.

entry.title: MediPFN: Amortized In-Context Nuisance Learning and Inference for Causal Mediation Analysis

author.name: Shi Bo, Jiaming Hu

entry.summary: MediPFN adapts pretrained tabular foundation models to causal mediation analysis by amortizing nuisance function prediction through in-context learning and combining estimates via a cross-fitted influence-function estimator with learned quantiles for confidence intervals. This accelerates estimation of direct and indirect treatment effects.

entry.title: Differentially Private Statistical Inference for Rankings from Pairwise Comparisons

author.name: Xintao Xia, Jia Gu

entry.summary: The paper develops differentially private score and rank inference under the Bradley-Terry model with edge differential privacy, motivated by protecting individual preference records in LLM evaluations from human comparisons. It provides finite-sample error bounds, asymptotically valid confidence intervals, and methods improving finite-sample performance.

entry.title: C$^2$-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference

author.name: Guorui Lu, Qinyu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes C2-Routing, a model-agnostic input reduction method for visual question answering that adaptively routes each query between cropping (better for small targets and local detail) and whole-image compression (better for global context), working across VLMs including black-box settings. It exploits the observation that the two strategies are complementary rather than interchangeable.

entry.title: Compute the Interactions, Not the Attributes: What a Fact Layer Must Supply in the Chinese Sexagenary System

author.name: Huixue Han, Jiaying Liu

entry.summary: Using the Chinese sexagenary system underlying BaZi chart analysis, this paper empirically measures what a deterministic fact layer paired with an LLM should supply, evaluating 682 items across twelve fact categories in eleven open-weight models. Errors concentrate where attributes must be combined: no model exceeds 4% accuracy on sexagenary days or 1% on transit-natal collisions, and providing static attributes or complete relation lists leaves most models near zero on direct answering. The conclusion is that fact layers must supply computed interactions rather than raw attributes.

entry.title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls

author.name: Alessio Brini

entry.summary: This paper addresses look-ahead bias in financial text encoders by training yearly vintages of encoders, each reading only text dated on or before its cutoff, from 412,248 earnings calls under four pretraining recipes, then fine-tuning each vintage on question-answer pairs from the calls. The 33.8M-parameter call-only vintages retrieve answers on held-out calls better than a general retriever trained on all text. This enables legitimate backtesting of finance retrieval and RAG systems.

entry.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking

author.name: Arjun Rao, Nishant Gopinath

entry.summary: FERN is a table-retrieval pipeline for text-to-SQL that fuses three frozen retrievers into a 100-candidate pool, then re-ranks using LightGBM rankers over 120 engineered features fitted only on BIRD training questions. Without any generative LLM, it matches or exceeds the published recall of RASL (which uses Claude 3.5 models) on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs, lifting Spider complete@5 from 83.9% to 95.6%.

entry.title: RetinexGS: Retinex-Inspired Gaussian Splatting for Low-Light RAW Reconstruction

author.name: Yulang Fei, Huaiyuan Weng, Chul Min Yeum

entry.summary: RetinexGS is a RAW-domain 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for low-light novel-view synthesis that factorizes each Gaussian's color into a view-independent base color and a shared position- and view-dependent modulation field, regularized separately in a Retinex-inspired manner. The approach leverages linear sensor measurements and noise metadata from RAW images to stabilize reconstruction of underexposed scenes.

entry.title: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Fracture Characterization in Acoustic Image Logs

author.name: Guangyu Wang, Xiaodong Ma, Xinming Wu

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune DINOv3, a vision foundation model pretrained on satellite imagery, on only 80 annotated acoustic image log samples to characterize natural and drilling-induced fractures, matching human interpretation on held-out boreholes. The adapted foundation model outperforms U-Net, YOLOv8, and Swin Transformer models trained from scratch. This demonstrates the value of foundation model adaptation in low-label scientific imaging domains.

entry.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks

author.name: Zequan Zeng, Kai Wang, Delvin Ce Zhang, Huaping Liu, Zhipeng Yuan, Junqin Yang, YunLong Zhang

entry.summary: Robo-MLT couples an explicit workflow monitor with learned action generation for medical lab automation: a vision-language planner orders atomic skills from a protocol, a multiframe monitor detects skill completion or infeasibility, and a skill-conditioned VLA policy executes manipulation. The design targets protocol-order fidelity and recovery from human intervention.

entry.title: First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds

author.name: Eunseong Bae, Wolfgang Polonik

entry.summary: Under uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold, the authors derive first-order asymptotic expansions for eigenvalues and eigenvectors of Gaussian-kernel normalized graph Laplacians with concentration inequalities for remainders, establishing weak convergence without a multiplicity-one eigenvalue assumption. This extends spectral convergence results to manifolds with nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.

entry.title: A Circularity at the Heart of Safety Assurance

author.name: Austin Long

entry.summary: Through an extended parable about verifying a claimed superintelligent-but-safe model on a hard drive, Austin Long argues that safety assurance faces a fundamental circularity: observations of a model are separated from the safety fact one cares about by vast empirical and logical uncertainty. The piece probes what evidence could ever license trust in a frontier model's safety.

entry.title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Vikram Ramavarapu, Himanshu Udupi, Ashish Gautam

entry.summary: The paper introduces Community Recurrent SNNs (CoRe SNNs), recurrent spiking networks partitioned into communities with fixed roles, where spiking activity forms walks between communities and learning is local and three-factor. It addresses how functional modules arise in recurrent SNNs for RL and what benefits modularity provides.

entry.title: Beyond the Log-Linear Frontier: Pre-Asymptotic Analysis of Finite-Budget Neural Scaling Laws

author.name: Tianyu Zhao, Zhixiang Ren

entry.summary: The paper analyzes departures from classical log-linear power-law scaling at finite compute budgets, using Mellin-Barnes analysis of covariance resolvents to derive a three-term expansion capturing spectral and regularization effects that produce finite-scale curvature and logarithmic transitions. It also proposes a well-conditioned estimator (Aitken differencing) for fitting scaling laws from narrow pilot grids.

entry.title: TRUER: Test-Time Reward Correction Using an Error-Aware Rectifier for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mingxiang Shen, Jinhao Li, Jiaming Xu, Yibo Han, Guohao Dai, Yijia Zhang, Ningyi Xu

entry.summary: TRUER addresses false-positive reward errors in test-time reinforcement learning, where majority voting reinforces incorrect solutions, by training a reward rectifier on a limited labeled source set that distinguishes correctness from consensus, with training emphasis on incorrect majorities and correct minorities. This targets the practical regime where ground-truth rewards are unavailable at scale.

entry.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology

author.name: Yeyuan Liu

entry.summary: This critical analysis examines connectome-constrained neural models, showing that claims that real wiring outperforms shuffled wiring can confound circuit structure with tuning of unmeasured physiological parameters. The author separates three estimands depending on whether physiology is tuned on the real wiring, on each wiring independently, or constrained by independent data, connecting the biases to known ML pitfalls like under-tuned baselines and winner's curse. The work quantifies how these biases affect structure-function conclusions.

entry.title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control

author.name: Haitian Li, Tianfu Li, Xuxi Zhao, Zizheng Liu, Yangcheng Yu, Yiwen Hou, Zeyu Xiao, Mutian Xu, Ziqian Yang, Haonan Chen, Lin Shao

entry.summary: Proposes adaptively allocating world-model refinement computation across denoising timesteps and spatial regions of the imagined future, governed by a unified spatiotemporal refinement demand field. This reduces the substantial inference overhead of iterative video denoising in World-Action Models compared to fixed refinement budgets.

entry.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable

author.name: Yihang Che, Zhongwei Yu, Yang Li, Xingyu Lu, Hongxia Yu, Jun Wang

entry.summary: A position-style paper arguing that current self-driving laboratories embed a paradox: foundation-model integration increases linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding, blocking development of embodied experimental intuition. The authors propose embedding learnability into experimental design to close the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation.

entry.title: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text

author.name: George Koomullil (Ascendr, PBC)

entry.summary: This paper studies AI-assisted monetary measurement over administrative text when human annotators disagree, using a testbed of 121,070 grant-purpose texts from US tax filings ($126.4B total) with a designed sample of 651 texts read by three people. It states exact conditions for fixed-predictor and cross-fitted difference estimators under Poisson sampling and validates by simulation.

entry.title: Living constitutions: Participatory alignment for sovereign foundation models

author.name: Stine Lyngs{\o} Beltoft, Jonas Vistrup, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: This position-style paper addresses how constitutions for Constitutional AI should be created, asking who contributes, who decides included norms, and how democratic the process must be. The authors argue that deliberate, evolving, participatory constitution-building is essential to prevent sovereign foundation models from defaulting to frontier-provider norms, and propose five desirable principles modeled on citizen science.

entry.title: Megrez: A Knowledge-Guided Agent for Formal Mathematics over MK Set Theory

author.name: Tiancheng Xu, Wensheng Yu

entry.summary: Megrez is a knowledge-guided agent for formalizing textbook mathematics in Rocq libraries built on Morse-Kelley set theory, addressing concept-library alignment, long-horizon search synchronization, and reliable proof integration. It coordinates a general coding agent via a source-rebuildable knowledge graph merging formal declarations, compiler references, and curated metadata.

entry.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming

author.name: Jongchan Park, Hyukjun Yang, Narim Jeong, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: The paper improves Lifted Bellman Linear Programming for offline RL by solving the constrained program via the method of multipliers instead of fixed hinge penalties, learning coefficients as dual multipliers with a single penalty parameter. In convex cases the fixed points are KKT pairs, and the critic can serve a Gaussian policy.

entry.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yubo Cui, Xianchao Guan, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzing visual representation drift in adversarial fine-tuning, the paper identifies complementary limitations of feature-matching and prediction-distribution-matching guidance for preserving zero-shot capability. It proposes textual response-aware guidance that better preserves pre-trained image-text relationships while improving adversarial robustness.

entry.title: When Proofs Are Abundant, What Is a Paper For?

author.name: Charles-Albert Lehalle

entry.summary: This position paper argues that as AI systems produce formally verified proofs at near-zero cost, a research paper's value lies not in the verified statement but in its intension, scientific chain of thought, and community-criticized narrative. It formalizes these ideas using logic and type theory, arguing machine-generated formal scripts convey neither narrative nor reasoning.

entry.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings

author.name: Oshando Johnson, Ranjith Krishnamurthy, Rohith Kumar Shanmuganathan, Goran Piskachev, Eric Bodden

entry.summary: This paper redesigns SAFE, an open-source IntelliJ plugin, so that LLMs explain static analysis security findings while detection remains with the rule-based analyser, preserving auditability. Requirements were derived from a 20-participant user study and a 19-practitioner workshop, with explanations tiered by confidence.

entry.title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention

author.name: Izzeddin Teeti, Vaibhav Kango, Nidhi Sridhar, Mohamed Moustafa

entry.summary: A unified multimodal, multitask framework that jointly performs road-closure classification (none, partial, complete) and associates closures with specific road segments. It fuses graph-structured map data, satellite imagery with projected street-level detections, and street-view images via cross-modal graph attention, applied at large scale (Meta-affiliated authors).

entry.title: PegasusAI Studio: Legible Cyberinfrastructure and Accountable AI Agents for Scientific Workflows

author.name: Komal Thareja, Mats Rynge, Berent Aldikacti, Angelina Ju, Ian Lumsden, Anirban Mandal, Rajiv Mayani, Kin Wai Ng, Hamza Safri, Michael Stealey, Sai Swaminathan, Michela Taufer, Karan Vahi, Michael Zink, Ewa Deelman

entry.summary: PegasusAI Studio builds an AI-assisted science gateway on the Pegasus and HTCondor stack that makes shared cyberinfrastructure legible to coding agents via a facility-curated knowledge base, workflow introspection, and grounded diagnosis, while attributing every agent action to a user and bounding it by that user's privileges. It tackles the operational and accountability problems of letting agents run scientific workflows on shared facilities. This addresses a gap between code generation and safe, attributable execution.

entry.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design

author.name: Maria Franz, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: The paper shows that generative drug-design pipelines typically select molecules on predicted potency and toxicity while ignoring pharmacokinetics, so computationally promising molecules may require impractical doses. Using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to re-evaluate 60 shortlisted molecules from three PARP1-targeted generative pipelines, the authors find seven fail to achieve sufficient target exposure and 28% of the remainder raise concerns. It argues for exposure-aware selection as a standard filter in generative drug discovery.

entry.title: A Concept-Based Interpretable Framework for Clinical Text-based Prediction via Token-Concept Attention without Concept Supervision

author.name: Jifan Gao, Junjie Hu, John Caskey, Madeline Oguss, Simona Cristea, Anoop Mayampurath, Matthew Churpek, Majid Afshar, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: This study proposes a framework for concept-based interpretation of language models on clinical prediction tasks without requiring annotated concept labels. It uses a tailored cross-attention bottleneck where clinical text and medical concept descriptions are embedded by a pretrained language model, enabling human-understandable concept attribution at zero annotation cost.

entry.title: CASCADE: Constraint-Aware SCAffolded DEcomposition for Logical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jinchan Kim, Jinhee Im, Hyunsouk Cho

entry.summary: CASCADE targets logical anomaly detection with large vision-language models, identifying a constraint-specific perception gap in text-only checklist decomposition where one raw image must support different forms of visual evidence. It introduces constraint-aware scaffolded decomposition so each check can extract appropriate visual evidence, addressing instance conflation and scale drift failure modes.

entry.title: Looking One Step Ahead: An Anticipation-guided Agent for Object State Readout in Videos

author.name: Yuanhe Tian, Yan Song

entry.summary: LASER is an anticipation-guided agent for object state readout in videos that uses predicted next-step changes to decide which visual attributes to inspect in the current frame. It converts anticipated changes into targeted visual questions to overcome under-specified descriptions from multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling

author.name: Izack Cohen, Dominik Kress, Lara Nehrke, Erwin Pesch, Shimrit Shtern

entry.summary: This OR/AI bridge paper systematically compares Branch-and-Bound and A* on the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem, establishing relationships between MILP, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. By studying basic implementations, it isolates fundamental differences in how the two search paradigms explore the space.

entry.title: Permutation-Based Pre-trained Model Merging via Reciprocal Orthogonality

author.name: Akira Ito, Daiki Chijiwa, Atsutoshi Kumagai

entry.summary: Building on prior work showing linear mode connectivity (LMC) between independently trained networks under softmax temperature calibration, this paper searches for permutations that encourage layerwise exponentially weighted connectivity without the extreme width previously required. It addresses the practical question of whether such widening (e.g., 16x for VGG-11) is necessary for merging.

entry.title: Audited Gradients, Anchored Policies: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Flow Control

author.name: Ruige Kong, Stefania Fresca

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in differentiable-surrogate policy optimization: surrogates can follow flow trajectories while misestimating the action gradient that optimization actually uses. It audits surrogate action gradients against finite-difference estimates from a high-fidelity solver on held-out states and anchors policies accordingly, reducing the need for expensive solver evaluations.

entry.title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models

author.name: Ian Christopher Tanoh, Scott W. Linderman

entry.summary: The authors introduce a quasi-Newton parallelization method for nonlinear state space models based on Broyden's approach, using diagonal-plus-low-rank Jacobian approximations to capture cross-dimensional coupling that diagonal approximations miss. This reformulates sequential evaluation as a root-finding problem solvable on modern parallel hardware with better cost-convergence tradeoffs.

entry.title: CP-MLPs: A Tensor-Rank Theory of Tied and Untied MLP Blocks

author.name: Md Rifat Arefin, Farzaneh Heidari, Irina Rish, Guillaume Rabusseau

entry.summary: The paper introduces a tensor framework (CP-MLPs) in which each multiplicative unit in transformer feed-forward blocks plays three roles - detecting an input feature, reading a value, and writing to output - and shows that untied gated blocks like ReGLU and SwiGLU are strictly more width-efficient than tied blocks like ReLU-squared for indefinite quadratic interactions, via exact tensor-rank separations. This gives the first degree-wise expressivity account of gating and parameter-tying design choices.

entry.title: Beyond Interaction Scores: Selecting Feature Interactions via Independent Replication

author.name: Jincheng Gao, Shuo Sun

entry.summary: LENS is a model-agnostic framework for selecting feature interactions by training two identically-configured models on disjoint data and keeping only interacting feature pairs whose patterns replicate across the two models. It removes main effects from joint-effect surfaces, ranks pairs by interaction strength, and tests replication. This bridges ranking-based and testing-based approaches and guards against selecting interactions that merely fit noise.

entry.title: Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic: Adaptive Switching Costs for Robust Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Khaled Ammoura, Aya Kayal, Naseem Daher

entry.summary: OC^2 replaces fixed or duration-based deliberation costs in hierarchical RL with a state-dependent opportunity cost defined as the positive value gap between the active option and its best alternative, encouraging persistence when the current option is clearly preferable and fast switching when a better one emerges. The framework directly learns this cost to prevent option collapse to primitive actions. It offers a cleaner, more principled mechanism for the option-critic family.

entry.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits

author.name: Hadi Salloum, Ammar Ali

entry.summary: Building on recent weight-space programming work where a frontier agent repaired a small Qwen model without gradients, this paper recasts LLM weight repair as sparse discrete optimization over BF16 weights using Ising-style edits such as sign flips and exponent shifts. The method defines an objective from forward statistics that weakens pathological loop directions while preserving useful layer outputs. It operates within a state-tree representation where lossless BF16 storage is a special case.

entry.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models

author.name: Vagn Krister Nes Glomsrud, Mathias Bynke, Lars Henry Berge Olsen, Dennis Christensen

entry.summary: The authors apply TabPFN, a tabular foundation model, to predict impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature, and crystal density of energetic materials. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN beats the best published models on all three properties and outperforms tuned XGBoost, random forests, and Gaussian processes—including when applied to Chemprop's own learned embeddings. This demonstrates tabular foundation models as strong out-of-the-box tools in materials chemistry.

entry.title: Alchemically Transferable Parameters for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers

author.name: Jonas Motyl, Jakob S. Kottmann

entry.summary: The authors show that machine-learned circuit parameters for variational quantum eigensolvers can transfer from hydrogenic training systems to organic molecules without retraining, using an alchemical geometric projection of surrogate hydrogen atoms onto target molecular bonds. This removes the costly classical optimization loop, avoiding barren plateaus and expensive gradient evaluations.

entry.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation

author.name: Haejoon Lee, Thomas Marshall Vielmetti, Xinyi Wang, Dimitra Panagou

entry.summary: Discrete MBD is a training-free sampling-based optimization method that extends model-based diffusion to discrete spaces by approximating categorical distributions, enabling near real-time solutions of NP-hard multi-robot task allocation problems. It bridges the gap between continuous MBD and offline-trained discrete diffusion solvers.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Battery-Assisted Grid-Import Smoothing in AI Data Centers

author.name: Xinda Zheng, Canchen Jiang, Frits de Nijs, Edward Lam, Markus Wagner

entry.summary: The authors formulate risk-aware battery energy storage scheduling to smooth grid imports for AI data centers, coordinating reserve commitments and demand-responsive dispatch with conditional value-at-risk objectives. Their BS-DFL approach uses a constraint-aware neural optimization layer trained without optimal-solution labels, then frozen to guide demand-predictor learning, enabling solver-free rolling-horizon scheduling. Validated in a 10,000-minute simulation, it targets the timely problem of AI data-center grid integration.

entry.title: On Federated Averaging with Partial Participation under a General Variance Condition

author.name: Ziming Wang, Kun Huang, Karl Henrik Johansson, Shi Pu

entry.summary: Analyzes convergence of Federated Averaging with uniform client subsampling under the general ABC variance condition, establishing finite-time stationarity bounds for smooth nonconvex objectives expressed via a heterogeneity measure and client sampling factor. Extends FedAvg theory to more realistic variance and participation regimes.

entry.title: Beyond Fluent Responses: Finding User Dissatisfaction in Human-AI Interactions

author.name: Yuka Saito, Ikumi Numaya, Jun Suzuki, Reina Akama

entry.summary: This study shifts LLM response evaluation from response-centered criteria toward user-centered signals, investigating whether user dissatisfaction can be detected from conversational text. It argues that real satisfaction depends on subjective preferences and perceived usefulness that do not align with conventional quality metrics. Detecting dissatisfaction signals from dialogue is important for genuinely useful conversational systems.

entry.title: Sckwoky at SHROOM-Visions: Character-Level Hallucination-Span Detection in Image-Conditioned VLMs via Dual-Prompted LoRA Decoders

author.name: Mikhail Kulakov (Novosibirsk State University), Ruslan Solikhov (Novosibirsk State University), Ivan Bondarenko (Novosibirsk State University)

entry.summary: A shared-task system (SHROOM-visions 2026) that detects character-level hallucination spans in vision-language model outputs across four languages, built on a frozen Gemma-4-12B-it backbone (an established model released in April 2026) with a small trainable LoRA adapter of about 10.7M parameters. Its key trick is repeating the candidate answer inside one prompt and reading hidden states from the second occurrence, which gives every character position near-bidirectional context in a single non-autoregressive pass. This matters because precise, cheap hallucination localization in multimodal outputs is a growing practical safety need.

entry.title: StaRSE: Compact Russian Sentence Embeddings with a Sign-Coded Static Encoder

author.name: Boris Malashenko, Ivan Jarsky, Egor Soldatov, Vladislav Luzhnov, Sviatoslav Stumpf, Vladislav Shmatkov, Viacheslav Shalamov, Andrey Stankevich, Valeria Efimova

entry.summary: StaRSE is a compact Russian static sentence encoder that eliminates Transformer inference at deployment: token directions are stored as sign bits and sentences encoded by mean pooling over norm-scaled sign directions, initialized from ruBERT and post-trained with contrastive learning directly on the sign-projected token table. On RuMTEB it reaches a task mean of 51.16, 7.98 points above the strongest static baseline. It enables CPU-friendly, frequently refreshable embeddings for Russian retrieval.

entry.title: The Left Ripple of Byte-Pair Encoding: Certified Lookbehind for Every Dictionary

author.name: Nicklas Nidh\"ogg

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves an open question about byte-pair encoding: how far a string prepended to the left can change a downstream tokenization. It characterizes the 'origin radius' for every dictionary via polynomial-time radius certificates, identifies exactly when the ripple is infinite via periodic tilings, and gives efficient algorithms for the finite case.

entry.title: GroundCascade: Selective Second Opinions for GUI Grounding

author.name: Adrian Phoulady, Hady Ahmady Phoulady

entry.summary: GroundCascade is a training-free cascade controller for GUI grounding that compares a grounder's full-screen and zoomed predictions and only escalates to a complementary model when they disagree. It achieves 85.33% on ScreenSpot-Pro and 88.43% on visible-target benchmarks with UI-TARS-family models, improving accuracy while limiting expensive second opinions.

entry.title: UniWeaver: Harnessing Unified Multimodal Models for Interleaved Text-Image Generation

author.name: Hongxu Chen, Zixuan Zhong, Donghao Zhou, Haodong Li, Xiaomin Yu, Tianhao Li, Shiyao Yu, Zhongwei Wan, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: UniWeaver is a model-agnostic harness that adds structured multimodal planning, generation, and visual feedback to unified multimodal models for coherent interleaved text-image outputs. The authors contribute UniWeaver-10K, a dataset of 10,000 tasks across 20 task families with execution trajectories, plus UniWeaver-Bench for systematic evaluation of interleaved generation.

entry.title: DroneSegEdit: Adapting Pretrained Generative Editors for UAV Segmentation with Language-Grounded Verification

author.name: Dehua Chen, Long Xin, Jiangtao Wei

entry.summary: DroneSegEdit adapts pretrained generative editors for language-guided UAV segmentation, identifying a Grounding-Rendering Gap where plausible masks attach to the wrong instance among small repeated objects. It combines RGB proposal rendering with language-grounded, proposal-constrained verification, adapting the open-weight LongCat-Image-Edit model with LoRA and fixed color-to-label decoding. This is a creative repurposing of generative editors for a discriminative task.

entry.title: Persistent Metric-Semantic Maritime Scene Memory from Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Kim Alexander Christensen, Dina Zimmermann, Martin Steinert, Eleni Kelasidi

entry.summary: This work evaluates how open-vocabulary 3D scene graph methods, developed mainly for indoor and terrestrial settings, transfer to maritime environments for robot spatial reasoning. It finds reasonable zero-shot agreement on geometry-supported objects but significant physical-entity fragmentation and unmet maritime spatial organization assumptions, then adapts the underlying mapping approach. Important reality-check for deploying 3DSGs on underwater or maritime robots.

entry.title: UniFlow-RS: Unified Generative Prediction for Heterogeneous Remote-Sensing Tasks

author.name: Jianlong He, Liang Liao, Jing Xiao, Chaofeng Chen, Gui-Song Xia

entry.summary: Proposes a single latent flow-matching predictor shared across heterogeneous remote-sensing tasks, casting diverse task outputs into structured visual targets in a common latent space. This unifies prediction across sensing modalities and tasks where separate decoders and objectives were previously fragmented.

entry.title: From Depth to Safe Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Monocular Perception for Mobile Robot Navigation

author.name: Saeid Firouzi Daghigh, Saeed Ayat

entry.summary: Shows that off-the-shelf monocular depth foundation models like Depth Anything V2 are unsafe for robot navigation, causing collisions in 63% of simulated episodes by over-estimating distances to nearby obstacles. A lightweight 0.58M-parameter plug-in head predicts log-depth corrections with per-pixel uncertainty, yielding conservative one-sided depth bounds that substantially improve navigation safety.

entry.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement

author.name: Delin Zhao, Zhengrong Yue, Junlin He, Yali Wang

entry.summary: RoboACE jointly evolves a curriculum harness and an execution harness around frozen foundation models, where the curriculum proposes capability-informative challenges and the execution harness produces reusable skill revisions. Alternating updates with fixed challengers aim to continually surface and repair weaknesses in robot skill libraries.

entry.title: Route-Time Conflict Maps for Cooperative End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Haohua Que, Mingkai Liu, Tianle Zhu, Zhipeng Bao, Yiping Li, Handong Yao

entry.summary: When2Go is a cooperative end-to-end driving system operating at SAE J3216 Class B, where vehicles broadcast detections with forecast motion plus their intended trajectories, and each receiver renders fused intents into a route-time conflict map to learn when to go. This intent-sharing addresses deadlocks and collisions that arise when status-sharing Class A vehicles each plan independently.

entry.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing

author.name: Shiva Ganesh Murali, Valentin Bhend, Deepak Ingole, Gabriele Fadini, Alisa Rupenyan

entry.summary: This paper presents an offline optimization-based path planner for robotic additive manufacturing that jointly handles joint-path regularity, self-collision, and process-specific costs, with an iterative weight-tuning scheme that derives weights from KPI targets. It is validated on carbon-fiber winding and 3D printing executed on a UR10e arm.

entry.title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects

author.name: Abdul-Nasah Soale

entry.summary: This paper generalizes sufficient dimension reduction to regression with both a Euclidean predictor and a random predictor object in a general metric space, embedding the object in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and using regularized kernel-response envelope models with partial adaptive estimation. It constructs a joint reduction that differs from the ordinary central subspace.

entry.title: Q3.5 Timelines Update: Looks Like the Intelligence Explosion Will Happen in 2027 After All

author.name: Thomas Larsen

entry.summary: A forecasting group updates their timelines based on METR's estimate that Anthropic is now making AI progress roughly twice as fast as historically, attributing much of the acceleration to AI itself. They now predict Superhuman AI Researcher will likely arrive in 2027, with a 35-65% chance of top-expert domination shortly after, treating this as an urgent revision of prior expectations.

entry.title: ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model

author.name: Javier Mar\'in

entry.summary: Observes that standard energy-based models define only relative compatibility, lacking a learned reference level to decide when no provided option is acceptable, and proposes ZeroPoint as a lightweight fix. The model learns an input-dependent reference energy enabling reject/none-of-the-above decisions while preserving standard EBM training and inference.

entry.title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI

author.name: Shu Jiang, Graham A. Colditz

entry.summary: The authors propose an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI longitudinally: individual agents form a cohort, the underlying model acts as genetic makeup, accumulated work is the time scale, and naturally occurring behaviors are exposures influencing downstream outcomes. This aims to shift evaluation from static task benchmarks to longitudinal behavior and risk study.

entry.title: Joint Quantization and Dynamic Partitioning for Context-Aware Edge Vision Transformers

author.name: Zhu Jiaqi, Jain Prakriti, Katare Dewant, Kumar Saurabh

entry.summary: This work proposes an edge orchestration framework for connected and automated vehicles that jointly selects vision transformer partition points, per-layer quantization bitwidths, and execution placement across heterogeneous vehicular nodes via a MILP formulation. It adapts to time-varying V2V bandwidth, processing load, and multi-stream traffic where static split-inference fails.

entry.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models

author.name: Dong Han, Jin Zhang, Kunyue Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Cognitive Learning-by-Thinking Framework mapping four mechanisms (reflective reasoning, synthetic memory formation, internal simulation, conceptual self-organization) onto LLM computational processes, covering chain-of-thought, self-consistency, self-reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts, Self-Instruct, and self-taught reasoning. It systematically accounts for LLM capabilities resembling human insight acquisition without new external input.

entry.title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption

author.name: Qiming Huang, Peixi Liu, Jianbo Jiao

entry.summary: TIB addresses the failure of information-bottleneck-based multimodal attribution when image-text pairs are not semantically aligned, providing theoretical analysis of how misalignment breaks global sufficiency-compression objectives. It introduces a sample-wise tempered information bottleneck that relaxes the alignment assumption for vision-language attribution.

entry.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration

author.name: Erik Derner, Ji\v{r}\'i Kubal\'ik, Robert Babu\v{s}ka

entry.summary: ASPIRE is a framework in which an LLM agent selects and executes nonlinear system-identification methods, building closed-form static or dynamic models from data plus optional physical constraints. Each model comes with parameters, estimation records, term interpretations, and test-set errors, with formal physical requirements verified independently.

entry.title: AURA: Auditory Spatial Intelligence via a Unified Representation from a General-Audio Encoder through Complete Alignment

author.name: Boyan Han, Xiaoyan Wang, Zhe Sun, Ziqi Wang, Yujun Cai, Hongli Cao, Yiwei Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Liang An

entry.summary: AURA studies whether a general-audio codec trained without spatial supervision can support both sound identification and localization, showing via layer-wise analysis that the frozen codec retains spatial cues in inter-aural differences but they are not readily accessible to models. The paper then builds a unified representation with complete alignment to make this spatial information usable for spatial question answering in multi-source scenes.

entry.title: Making Strides in Symbolic Imitation Learning: Offline Demonstrations, Online Tuning

author.name: Bryce MacInnis, Malcolm I. Heywood

entry.summary: The paper introduces Symbolic Imitation Learning, distilling an oracle policy from offline data into an interpretable decision list with linear motion primitives, then tuning constants and primitives with online augmented random search. Across 20 continuous-control benchmarks it approaches the oracle and exceeds it on 11 tasks while producing parsimonious, interpretable policies.

entry.title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs

author.name: Bernhard Voggenberger, Christian Ganh\"or, Levente Z\'olyomi, Sebastian B\"ock, Sepp Hochreiter

entry.summary: This paper observes that recurrent time series foundation models compute predictions from both the context window and an initial recurrent state, but the initial state is conventionally unused. Using the xLSTM-based forecaster TiRex as a case study, the authors freeze the backbone and train a small head that writes a context vector into the initial state, isolating its effect on accuracy. The initial state is thereby proposed as a general conditioning interface.

entry.title: Block-Sparse Gauss-Newton Optimization of Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Sparse Automatic Differentiation Approach

author.name: Denis Korolev, Adrian Hill, Jeeeun Lee

entry.summary: This work exploits the overlapping domain decomposition structure of FBPINNs to induce block sparsity in Gauss-Newton matrices, using sparse automatic differentiation with graph coloring to reduce differentiation cost and memory. The compressed Jacobians enable efficient second-order optimization for physics-informed neural networks.

entry.title: Optimal Last-Iterate Bounds for Nonexpansive Stochastic Approximation

author.name: Ramanan Tamizholi, Siddharth Chandak, Rahul Singh

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes last-iterate mean-square residual bounds for stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann iterations with nonexpansive fixed-point mappings and polynomially decaying stepsizes. Under three noise-moment conditions it obtains rates optimal up to logarithmic factors, including O(1/k^(1-eps)) matching the noiseless KM iteration when noise scales linearly with the residual. Such results underpin convergence analysis of optimization and root-finding algorithms used across ML.

entry.title: On the information rate of phones, syllables and words

author.name: Herman Kamper

entry.summary: This paper asks which linguistic units minimize the bitrate needed to encode speech content, comparing phones, syllables, words, multi-word combinations, and intermediate tokenizations on 960 hours of transcribed English audiobooks under n-gram and transformer language models. Words achieve the lowest bitrates, with slightly longer units sometimes best, connecting tokenization choices to information theory and theories of human language processing. The results inform both speech system design and cognitive science debates on information rate.

entry.title: Pair-Merge Tokenisation Is Hard to Approximate on Binary Strings and Strongly NP-Hard on Unary Datasets

author.name: Kundan Baliga, Aiden Xie, Aditya Byju

entry.summary: This theory paper proves strong hardness results for BPE-style tokenization: choosing k merges to minimize token count cannot be approximated within a factor of c*n/log n unless P=NP, even for a single binary string, and the problem is strongly NP-hard on unary datasets. The proof technique converts vertex-cover gaps into grammar-size gaps amplified across relabelled copies.

entry.title: Prompt2Echo (P2Echo): Text-Prompted Multi-View Echocardiography Segmentation with One Model

author.name: Moein Heidari, Alvin Kimbowa, Mahdi Tabatabaei, Afshin Bozorgpour, Sina Ghorbani Kolahi, River Jiang, Wenjin Chen, David J. Foran, Jasmine Grewal, Dorit Merhof, Ilker Hacihaliloglu

entry.summary: P2Echo is a unified text-prompted segmentation model for diverse cardiac structures across multiple standard echocardiographic views, conditioned via a Dynamic Image-Text Alignment module with differentiable routing and token differential operators. Unlike implicit latent-prior foundation model adaptations, it explicitly couples view-aware prompts to decoder behavior in a single model.

entry.title: FlashMotion: Ultra-Fast Long-Term 3D Motion Generation

author.name: Kaixing Yang, Xulong Tang, Ronghui Li, Xiangyue Zhang, Ziqiao Peng, Mingshuang Luo, Chenxi Zhao, Haoyu Wu, Ju Fan, Hongyan Liu, Puwei Wang, Zijiao Zeng, Jun He

entry.summary: FlashMotion co-designs a generative strategy and architecture to achieve ultra-fast, long-horizon 3D human motion generation suitable for real-time interactive applications like games and XR, addressing both multi-step sampling cost and heavy per-step computation for long sequences. The framework maintains quality under tight inference budgets.

entry.title: GARD: Gradient-Guided Adversarial Representation Defense against Backdoors in Multimodal Contrastive Learning Models

author.name: Yuhong Wang, Yujun Cai, Lei Feng, Songze Li

entry.summary: Proposes a post-hoc defense against backdoor attacks in multimodal contrastive models like CLIP, exploiting the observation that global perturbations expose distributed backdoors while local patch perturbations expose localized ones. Gradient-guided representation-space perturbations avoid the limitations of clean fine-tuning and trigger-inversion methods.

entry.title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning

author.name: Renhao Zhang, Mingzhe Li, Bruno Castro da Silva

entry.summary: Latent Barrier Steering decouples behavior selection from path certification for flow-matching generative planners: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margins, then applies a path-space control barrier function QP on the decoded path. This two-level intervention handles cases where a new constraint blocks an entire behavior mode rather than perturbing it locally.

entry.title: A human-in-the-loop Control Paradigm for Construction Robotics: From VR-Guided Teleoperation to Semi-Autonomous Dual-Arm Operation

author.name: Jinhua Chen, Xiaoji Xu, Zhongyuan Liao, Huang Zhenmin, Zhang Ye, Changying Xiang

entry.summary: This paper presents a human-in-the-loop paradigm for contact-rich dual-arm construction tasks that structures transitions among VR teleoperation, semi-autonomous shared control, and rule-based autonomy using skill primitives and explicit role-allocation and command-priority rules. It targets hazardous, unstructured construction environments.

entry.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding

author.name: Liming Zhu, Qinghua Lu, Ming Ding

entry.summary: Proposes understanding-first AI engineering, treating purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle organized into four rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance, and epistemic value. It provides a reference architecture and architectural patterns connecting production, verification, use, and learning.

entry.title: Decisions by Discrimination: Differential Evidence for Medical Reasoning

author.name: Yunpeng Xiao, Yuzhang Xie, Junhao Huang, Carl Yang, Xiao Hu, Kai Shu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a retrieval-grounded framework for medical multiple-choice QA that identifies compact differential evidence separating plausible answer options, rather than supplying broadly relevant knowledge or generic reasoning paths. This mirrors how clinicians distinguish overlapping conditions through decisive discriminating factors.

entry.title: SeqFold: Timestamp-Addressable Compressed States for User Action Sequence Backbones

author.name: Mianwei Zhou, Duo Zhang, Henry Tsai, Yuqi Zheng, Jian Li, Juexin Lin, Sujay Khandagale, Vijay Rajaram, Dong Jiao, Tao Cheng

entry.summary: SeqFold is a compressed-state interface that exports multi-layer user states from a frozen long-history sequential-recommendation backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream training and serving. It combines learned multi-channel fusion, channel-specific temporal decay, and Lookup-Free Quantization, allowing downstream systems to use only the state aligned to each target timestamp.

entry.title: Beyond the Document: Compiled Context and Governed Agents for Any Work Product

author.name: James Rhodes, George Kang

entry.summary: The authors propose a Portable Agent Format (PAF) package that delivers a work product together with its compiled context, evidence, provenance, and interaction rules, rather than just the final document. They evaluate four new packages across finance and engineering scenarios to test whether packaged context remains useful beyond the producing process.

entry.title: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jaeyong Song, Daniel Wang, Pratyush Patel, Jonny Kong, Preyas Shah, Shobhit Kanaujia

entry.summary: ForeSpark addresses inefficiency in parallel-drafter speculative decoding where every request drafts a full block even under high serving load, with drafting consuming up to 40% of step time, much of it discarded. The system jointly schedules draft and verification budgets, breaking the coupling between draft and verification lengths across the batch, to maximize goodput (accepted tokens per second). This is an applied serving optimization from an industrial team.

entry.title: Synapse-Control: Making Agent Experience Actionable with Lightweight Runtime Control

author.name: Zhiyuan Huang, Shengan Zheng, Chenghu Yang, Song Zhang, Lingyun Li, Chen Yu, Weiquan Huang, Linpeng Huang

entry.summary: Synapse-Control is an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects and times advice delivery for tool-using LLM agents, replacing costly model-generated failure diagnoses with a fine-tuned 1.7B classifier over rule-shortlisted candidates. It adds micro-contracts for interface checks and a Prompt Value Table recording early interventions.

entry.title: Obscured Wildfire Flame Detection by Spatio-temporal Analysis of Smoke Patterns Using Frame-wise Transformers

author.name: Uma Meleti, Abolfazl Razi, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: The paper proposes detecting both visible and smoke-obscured wildfire flames by jointly analyzing spatial and temporal patterns in RGB video with a frame-wise transformer that applies attention between consecutive frames while preserving within-frame spatial information. This departs from approaches that independently analyze frames or blend spatial-temporal information indiscriminately.

entry.title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework

author.name: Serhii Zabolotnii (Cherkasy State Business College, State Scientific Research Institute of Armament, Military Equipment Testing, Certification, Uzhhorod University), Alina Tarasova (PJSC "Finport Technologies Inc.")

entry.summary: The authors build an AI pipeline that screens draft legislation for corruption risks by pinpointing provisions an expert would criticize and naming the regulatory defect, combining deterministic parsing, model-guided qualification, and human oversight. They evaluate it on an open benchmark of 132 Ukrainian draft laws with 474 expert findings from the anti-corruption agency NAZK.

entry.title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies

author.name: Mahindra Rautela

entry.summary: The paper shows that for flow-matching robot policies, a fixed Euler step count chosen from offline accuracy sweeps can be too coarse for locally contracting directions, since accuracy and local stability impose different step requirements. It analyzes this on exact systems, augmented trained flow models, and a frozen pi-0.5-family policy.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models in Financial Predictions

author.name: Ed deHaan, Allen H. Huang

entry.summary: This technical note introduces tabular foundation models (TFMs) to accounting research, evaluating them on predicting firms' next-year earnings changes. Google's TabFM outperforms a fine-tuned open-weight LLM and tree-based baselines while being faster and less computationally intensive, and its synthetic pretraining avoids look-ahead bias from memorizing real firm outcomes.

entry.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics

author.name: Peng Chen, Yihang Wang, Zhongwen Rao, Yang Shu, Yuying Qiu, Yuxuan Chen, Lujia Pan, Bin Yang, Chenjuan Guo

entry.summary: TimeSeek is a generalized time series foundation model addressing two gaps: reliance on stacked Transformer layers without adaptive modeling of multi-domain patterns, and task-specific pretraining that fails to exploit task commonality and specificity. The model adaptively handles multiple analytics tasks such as forecasting and anomaly detection within one architecture. It aims to improve generalization across time series domains.

entry.title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Wei Zhang, Zhu Teng, Zhixiang Chi, Junnan Zou, Yi Liu, Jianping Fan

entry.summary: PR-OVD addresses base-category bias in CLIP-style embeddings used for open-vocabulary object detection by partitioning and refining the embedding space to explicitly reserve capacity for novel classes. The framework is detector-agnostic and aims to prevent semantic collapse and miscalibrated confidence on unseen categories.

entry.title: Post-OCR Correction of Mixed-Script Uzbek Text: Byte-Level ByT5 with an Empirical Homoglyph Noise Matrix

author.name: Mannon Ochilov, Oybek Narzullayev, Bahodir Zaripov

entry.summary: This paper addresses OCR errors in Uzbek documents that mix Cyrillic and Latin scripts, where visually identical characters (homoglyphs) across alphabets cause error densities roughly five times higher than in single-script text. The authors combine a byte-level ByT5 correction model with a noise generator whose sampling weights are derived from an empirically measured homoglyph confusion matrix, and the full pipeline runs on local hardware to satisfy data-sovereignty constraints of geological and ICT infrastructure reports. It matters because it demonstrates practical post-OCR correction for a low-resource, script-transition language setting that mainstream OCR research rarely covers.

entry.title: Outliers and the Hard-Margin Linear SVM in High-Dimension, Low-Sample-Size Settings

author.name: Yugo Nakayama

entry.summary: This analysis characterizes how outliers affect the hard-margin linear SVM when dimension grows with fixed sample size, deriving a closed-form limiting dual problem where all outliers act through one effective distance. It yields explicit thresholds for loss of inlier support, margin shrinkage, intercept displacement, and asymptotic misclassification, and shows at most one class can collapse under two-sided contamination. These are precise robustness guarantees for a classical method in modern high-dimensional regimes.

entry.title: Exploring Post-Hoc Disentanglement of Audio Foundation Models for Music Similarity

author.name: Lucas de Souza Brand\~ao, Gabriel da Costa Merlin, Diego Furtado Silva

entry.summary: Systematically studies post-hoc disentanglement of frozen audio foundation model embeddings (CLAP, MuQ, MERT) using Conditional Similarity Networks with learned masks to gate attribute-specific subspaces for music similarity. It evaluates different masking and pooling regimes across two datasets instead of training backbones from scratch.

entry.title: Alania-2: Turkish text-to-speech with instant and fine-tuned voice cloning

author.name: Sezgin Saygili, Emre Kaplaner, Oncel Ozgul, Fikri San Koktas

entry.summary: Alania-2 is a 488M-parameter Turkish TTS system with the VoxCPM architecture (a diffusion head over a language-model backbone), trained from scratch on 18,195 hours of Turkish speech, 90% of it filtered synthetic audio from a larger teacher. It offers built-in voices, voice design from text, and two voice-cloning modes, with a Turkish text normalizer proving essential for numbers and dates. It is a substantial full-stack TTS contribution for a single language.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Iterative Reasoning for the Diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases

author.name: Haoqing Li, Jun Shi, Tou Li, Xianmeng Chen, Rui Wang, Yating Peng, Qiwei Jia, Li Gao, Qianyi Chen, Hong An, Ruoyun Ouyang, Xiaowen Hu

entry.summary: DCLDs-EIR is a multimodal LLM framework for diagnosing diffuse cystic lung diseases that couples iterative hypothesis refinement with evidence acquisition and verification, using multiview renderings of predicted lung and cyst segmentations to initialize differential diagnosis. The design targets incomplete volumetric perception and weak evidence grounding in medical MLLMs under limited annotated data.

entry.title: AgenticConflictLens: From Long Traffic Videos to Verifiable Conflict Evidence

author.name: Boshra Khalili, Sonia Moshfeghi, Jinwoo Jang, Andrew W Smyth

entry.summary: AgenticConflictLens is a query-conditioned agentic framework for extracting auditable evidence of traffic conflicts, near misses, and unsafe interactions from hours of fixed-camera footage, replacing uniform processing with adaptive, verifiable analysis. It targets participant-level conflict verification that prior detection-trajectory and vision-language pipelines lack.

entry.title: Marrying Capacity and Precision for Efficient 2D Gaussian Image Representation

author.name: Lin Dong, Qi Ming, Liuqian Wang, Wentao Chao, Yufei Gao, Chengming Liu, Lei Shi
