entry.summary: CP-GS jointly optimizes Gaussian capacity allocation and attribute quantization precision for 2D Gaussian image representation under a shared rate constraint, unlike prior methods that treat these resources separately. It dynamically reallocates a fixed Gaussian budget from redundant regions based on content. This improves rate-distortion performance for Gaussian splatting-based image coding.

entry.title: What Factors Matter for Collection-Level Counting with Human-AI Collaboration?

author.name: Seoyun Jeong, Logan Lawrence, Owen L. Martin, Benjamin Koger, Daniel Sheldon, Subhransu Maji

entry.summary: Systematically studies how practitioners should choose models, estimators, and adaptation strategies for human-in-the-loop collection-level counting across 12 tasks spanning microscopy, wildlife surveys, and urban imagery. Provides empirical guidance for combining imperfect model predictions with limited human verification under domain shift.

entry.title: Large Language Model Explainability for Planning Lunar Rover Trajectories under Uncertainty

author.name: Michelle Ho, Maximilian Adang, Zachary Booth, David E. Astle, Margaret Hansen, Edward Balaban, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: Proposes an interactive LLM-based assistant that explains Monte Carlo tree search planner outputs for planetary rover trajectory planning in domain vocabulary and re-runs the planner under user-specified conditions for comparison. This preserves traceability from plans to science objectives, addressing a verification bottleneck for science teams.

entry.title: Measure Optimal AI Share of Labor Costs Instead of AI or Human-Only Performance

author.name: aak

entry.summary: Building on METR's expenditure horizon concept (the budget at which AI-only and human-only work reach equal performance), the author critiques the metric and proposes an alternative: the X% expenditure share horizon, the labor budget at which it is optimal to allocate X% of spend to agents. The essay argues the new metric is more decision-relevant and easier to measure.

entry.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Luiz do Valle Miranda, Andreas L. Opdahl, Grzegorz J. Nalepa

entry.summary: A controlled study of 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions across six VLMs comparing text-only versus text-plus-graph-visualization prompting in a fixed KGQA pipeline. Graph images add an average 1.85 F1, driven by low-complexity questions, with gains highly sensitive to image layout rather than model scale.

entry.title: RBLA+: Efficient Rank-Specific LoRA Adapter Extraction for Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Clients

author.name: Shuaijun Chen, Omid Tavallaie, Xin Chen, Wentao Gao, Nguyen Tran, Albert Y. Zomaya

entry.summary: Addresses federated LoRA fine-tuning where clients use heterogeneous ranks, distinguishing pre-aggregation alignment from rank-specific adapter extraction and proposing a rank-bound local aggregation method. RBLA+ improves on direct rank truncation and SVD-based extraction when constructing client-sized adapters from the aggregated global model.

entry.title: GRAP: Gender Rubric-Aware Probing for Analyzing Gender Bias in LLMs

author.name: Seona Seo, Geonhee Ahn, Hyunsoo Cho, Sookyung Kim

entry.summary: GRAP is a framework for detecting gender bias in open-ended LLM responses using a lightweight logistic probe over 10 rubric-scored dimensions, identifying which bias dimensions most reliably distinguish gender groups. It improves on prior probing methods by moving beyond fixed-format tasks like pronoun resolution and by accounting for per-dimension variance rather than raw group-level scores.

entry.title: AI Alignment Is Neither Solvable nor Sufficient

author.name: Gerrit Gro{\ss}mann

entry.summary: This position paper argues that AI alignment as commonly conceived is misguided: it is ill-defined because it presumes a stable set of human values, is unsolvable where it can be specified, and even where solvable would not necessarily mitigate AI's negative consequences. The key claim is that alignment focuses on individual AI systems while harms arise from their interaction within shared social and economic environments.

entry.title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs

author.name: Ekrem Aksoy

entry.summary: W-ISA is a software instruction set and transactional runtime for executing weight-space intervention programs (parameter updates, projections, ablations, rank-one transformations) on pretrained language models within request-scoped contexts that restore saved parameters afterward. It is evaluated on small models (SmolLM-135M, Qwen2.5-1.5B) with restoration, replay, and equivalence checks against PyTorch hooks.

entry.title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference

author.name: Oliver Lack, Lana Tikhomirov, Humphrey Thompson, Carolyn Semmler, Melissa McCradden

entry.summary: This paper examines how chain-of-thought presentation fosters anthropomorphism and misplaced perceptions of machine understanding, driving cognitive deference to AI systems that displaces human agency. It argues that mistaking linguistic form for meaning underlies over-trust in AI explanations of their reasoning.

entry.title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery

author.name: Junwei Hu, Zhuohao Lin, Kun Li, Hengnan Zhang

entry.summary: DrugCoding is an LLM-based scientific programming agent for drug discovery workflows spanning molecular design, property prediction, and virtual screening. It targets autonomous planning of complex tasks, adaptive selection of specialized models, and reliable multi-stage execution, addressing coordination gaps in existing scientific agents.

entry.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations

author.name: Vojtech Cahlik, Amir Reza Mohammadi, Rodrigo Alves, Pavel Kordik, Eva Zangerle

entry.summary: The paper addresses the opacity of recommender systems by converting counterfactual explanations, which are often long lists of history edits, into coherent human-readable narratives using LLMs. The authors critique existing CFX evaluation for focusing on edit counts rather than user-facing coherence and actionability.

entry.title: Cross-Border Fulfillment Center Selection via Doubly Robust Estimation and Linear Programming

author.name: Kriti Mahajan, Patrick Bloebaum

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-stage optimization framework combining forecasting, doubly robust causal estimation, and linear programming to select source fulfillment centers for cross-border e-commerce shipping. Evaluated on three production-scale corridors with 12 months of shipment data, it achieves 8.5-51.1% improvements using offline replay and counterfactual matching.

entry.title: Causal Time Series Modeling of Supraglacial Lake Evolution in Greenland under Distribution Shift

author.name: Emam Hossain, Muhammad Hasan Ferdous, Devon Dunmire, Aneesh Subramanian, Md Osman Gani

entry.summary: RIC-TSC is a regionally-informed causal time-series classification framework that embeds lag-aware causal discovery into sequence modeling for Greenland supraglacial lake monitoring. Using multi-modal satellite and reanalysis data (Sentinel-1/2, Landsat-8, CARRA), it improves robustness and generalization under distribution shift while adding scientific interpretability.

entry.title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE

author.name: Pedro Malo

entry.summary: An open-source FPGA implementation flow (Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly) for Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 devices, verified byte-for-byte against the discontinued ISE toolchain. The bit database was reverse-engineered via black-box experimentation with documented XDL and bitgen tools.

entry.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics

author.name: Pedro Antonio Alarcon Granadeno, Jane Cleland-Huang

entry.summary: DOBB is an online geometric representation mapping state estimates, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into dynamic, direction-dependent bounding boxes for decentralized collision avoidance. This decouples safety-relevant separation from behaviors learned in the training distribution.

entry.title: STAR: Semantic-Criticality Tiered Allocation of Radio Resources via Zero-Shot Learning

author.name: Albert Shaju, Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas, Mingzhe Chen

entry.summary: STAR is a zero-shot, domain-agnostic framework for wireless remote inference that identifies task-critical pixels (e.g., text regions) whose corruption would change an AI model's answer, and allocates radio resources to deliver those regions with higher fidelity. This departs from conventional schemes that protect all pixels equally, improving task reliability at low signal-to-noise ratios without extra resource consumption. It connects semantic communication with vision models for edge deployment.

entry.title: When Are Predictions Enough? An Evaluation Protocol for Frozen Expert Composition

author.name: Alessandro Pereira, Keith J Ransom, Lewis Mitchell

entry.summary: The authors ask when combining internal features of frozen models beats combining only their final predictions, and introduce a reusable evaluation protocol applied to 21 frozen deepfake detectors from DF40. The protocol enforces strong prediction baselines, controlled train/test overlap, and held-out generator reporting, auditing how evaluation choices change conclusions. It offers a methodological corrective for a class of ensemble/composition studies.

entry.title: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks

author.name: Yuqi Wang, Fengyuan Liu, Mukai Li, Haochen Luo, Lei Li, Qi Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces MC-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture for financial time series that conditions asset prediction on a leave-one-out market factor built from other assets' future embeddings. Under a latent factor model, this conditioning makes learning the asset's market exposure necessary and reduces the noise against which asset-specific components are learned.

entry.title: DisasterAgent: An Evidence-Driven Agent for Verifiable Disaster Report Generation From Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Zhijian Li, Jiawei Song, Chao Ren, Yidan Zhang, Peijin Wang, Xian Sun, Kun Fu

entry.summary: DisasterAgent is an evidence-driven agent using a Perception-Augmentation-Generation workflow to produce verifiable disaster reports from bitemporal optical remote sensing imagery. It invokes a specialized vision expert toolkit during perception to supply the evidence needed for high-stakes verification, moving beyond simple damage classification.

entry.title: Region-Wise Logit Fusion and Utility-Gated Refinement for Brain Metastasis Segmentation

author.name: Zhenye Lou, Qing Xu, Wenting Duan, Zhen Chen

entry.summary: COMPASS-METS is an ensemble of three five-fold nnU-Net configurations for segmenting brain metastases and resection cavities in the BraTS-METS 2026 challenge, using structured probability anchors and hierarchy-preserving post-processing. It includes mechanisms to recover small enhancing tumor candidates that standard pipelines omit.

entry.title: Model-Free Runtime Measurement of Task-Relevant Information

author.name: Dimitris Panagopoulos, Adolfo Perrusqu\'ia, Yang Xing, Weisi Guo

entry.summary: The paper introduces Acquisition-State Telemetry (AST), a model-free architecture that monitors whether an autonomous system's ongoing information gathering is actually resolving its declared task requirements. It maps raw observations into task-resolution coordinates so systems can detect when they remain active without making mission progress.

entry.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training

author.name: Emre Kutlusan, Yongmin Li

entry.summary: The study adapts DINOv2 for medical image segmentation with strategies from bias-only tuning to full fine-tuning, comparing against U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch across colonoscopy, breast ultrasound, and dermatology data. It examines out-of-distribution performance at new clinical sites and what determines how much adaptation is needed.

entry.title: IC-GNN: Modeling Individualized Brain Community Organization for Disease Prediction

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiao Zhou, Jonathan Warrell, Avram Holmes, Xuan Zhang, Mark Gerstein, for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative

entry.summary: IC-GNN is an atlas-anchored graph neural network that models individualized brain community organization to avoid the trade-off between lengthy individualized parcellations and coarse group atlases, targeting disease prediction such as Alzheimer's. It aims to capture subject-specific variability while preserving cross-subject comparability.

entry.title: Advancing Mass-Conserving Deep Learning for Distributed Hydrologic Modeling: A Case Study in a Snow-Dominated Watershed

author.name: Yihan Wang, Lujun Zhang, N. Benjamin Erichson, Yang Hong, Tiantian Yang

entry.summary: PECAN extends mass-conserving LSTM hydrologic modeling from lumped to distributed, convolutional formulations, and uses it to diagnose when imposed physical constraints produce unrealistic behavior in a snow-dominated watershed. It provides clearer evidence about when and why physics-aware DL constraints help or hurt.

entry.title: AnchorMTS: Multi-View Signal Representation and Forecast-Anchored Fusion for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Gao Wu, Tingting Xu, Changning Wu, Tengfei Long, Yong Liu, Jiabin Jin, Kexin Zhang

entry.summary: AnchorMTS augments long-term time-series forecasting by deriving self-aligned visual and textual views of each observed window, using them only to refine a numerical anchor forecast through a trainable evidence path with a parameter-free bound on displacement from the numerical prediction. It reports best macro MSE/MAE across six benchmarks and 24 settings against seven supervised baselines. The work contributes to the growing trend of multi-modal (vision-text-numerical) representations for sequence forecasting.

entry.title: JAX-WAVE: A Differentiable Physics-Supervised Framework for Inverse Wave Design in Heterogeneous Media

author.name: Honghui Du, Binyao Guo, Yushu Pan

entry.summary: JAX-WAVE is an amortized framework for inverse wave design: a shared neural network maps desired terminal fields and known wave-speed maps directly to bounded initial pressures, trained through a differentiable finite-difference time-domain solver using only the physical objective. A sign-reversal relation of the regularized optimum is exploited via a shared-weight projection. This replaces per-target numerical inversion with a single amortized model, useful in acoustics and medical ultrasound planning.

entry.title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains

author.name: Yuqing Liu, Tong Mao, Jinchao Xu

entry.summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical analysis of shallow ReLU^k networks on bounded Euclidean domains, quantifying how hidden-parameter geometry (via fill distance and antipodal separation) affects approximation rates, saturation lower bounds, Gram and stiffness matrix spectra, discrete least-squares recovery, and inverse approximation. The analysis uses smooth localization and dyadic Fourier estimates. It provides rigorous foundations connecting network parameter geometry to approximation and stability guarantees.

entry.title: RB-LDC: Redundancy-Balanced Latent Coding for Noise-Robust Diffusion Latents

author.name: Hyunseok Jeong, Jaeho Jeon, Young-Sik Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes inserting an invertible linear layer between the encoder and diffusion process of latent diffusion models, shifting each direction's log-SNR according to decoder sensitivity, with an exact spectral expression for LMMSE recovery risk and a unique optimal allocation under an energy budget. This makes diffusion latents more robust to perturbations aligned with decoder sensitivity. It offers a principled, cheap modification relevant to latent diffusion robustness and compression.

entry.title: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Minyu Zhou, Yajing Wu, Yongqiang Tang, Wang Jia, Wensheng Zhang

entry.summary: ScaleBrain proposes a scale-consistent pretraining framework for EEG foundation models, constructing temporal scales so that correspondence between learned features and scale-specific signal characteristics is explicit, and aligning the self-supervised objective with multi-scale representations so all scales receive sufficient supervision. This improves EEG representation learning for brain-computer interface applications. It contributes to the growing area of domain-specific foundation models for neural signals.

entry.title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Pooling-Induced Substructures

author.name: Luca Sbicego, Xiaowen Dong, Dorina Thanou

entry.summary: The paper proposes Pooled-Substructure-Aware GNNs, a graph pooling approach that explicitly preserves and processes the substructures induced by structure-based pooling schemes, improving expressive power for graph-level tasks requiring substructure reasoning beyond local neighborhoods. It also notes the lack of benchmarks with explicit hierarchical structure and addresses evaluation accordingly. This tackles a known inconsistency in empirical performance of hierarchical GNNs.

entry.title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Wenqi Zhou, Leonardo Baldo, Kai Goebel, Manuel Arias Chao

entry.summary: Chain of Physics is an LLM-based fault diagnosis framework that constrains reasoning with a Constrained Knowledge Graph automatically generated from asset-specific engineering documentation. It links observed sensor changes to underlying failure mechanisms, mimicking how experienced engineers combine measurements with system knowledge. The approach targets industrial asset health management.

entry.title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes

author.name: Fatemeh Tohidian, Chengzhi Shi, Soomi Lee, Matthew Elia, Amy Mueller, Stratis Ioannidis, Jennifer Dy

entry.summary: DnNPs extend Neural Processes to explicitly model uncertainty in inputs, which standard NPs incorrectly assume are noise-free. Trained via variational inference, the model jointly denoises corrupted inputs and performs meta-learning, improving predictions and uncertainty quantification under sensor noise. Demonstrations span applications involving noisy measurement data.

entry.title: Generative Learning on Manifolds for Probabilistic Seismic Performance Assessment and Structural Identifiability

author.name: Dimitris G Giovanis, Ioannis G Kevrekidis, Roger G Ghanem

entry.summary: The paper combines Diffusion Maps, score-based diffusion modeling, and Geometric Harmonics to learn joint distributions of structural parameters and seismic response trajectories from limited simulations. It enables both forward uncertainty prediction and inverse inference of structural properties for a nine-story steel frame.

entry.title: Seeing the Small: Deformable Duality Mamba for Retinal Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Chang Yu, Siqing Li, Yuanchen Liu, Zhenyu Bu, Luming Yang, Alper Yilmaz

entry.summary: D2Mamba couples non-causal state space duality with deformable Mamba scanning to segment small, irregular diabetic retinopathy lesions such as few-pixel microaneurysms. On the DDR dataset with five-fold cross-validation, it achieves 33.87% mIoU, 2.99 points above the strongest baseline, with ablations confirming each component helps. It demonstrates state space models adapted for shape-adaptive medical segmentation.

entry.title: Dual-Space Preconditioning for Variational Inequalities and Root-Finding Problems

author.name: Jan Quan, Konstantinos Oikonomidis, Alexander Bodard, Panagiotis Patrinos

entry.summary: The paper develops a dual-space preconditioning framework for variational inequalities and root-finding that goes beyond classical cocoercivity and Lipschitz assumptions, introducing novel relaxed conditions with convergence guarantees for deterministic and stochastic methods. For isotropic preconditioners the algorithms admit interpretation as variable-stepsize variants of classical schemes with simpler proofs and larger stepsize ranges. This extends the theoretical toolkit underlying GAN-style and game-theoretic optimization.

entry.title: LUMIR: Decoupled Multimodal Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Data for Next-POI Recommendation

author.name: Zehui Wang, Wolfram H\"opken, Dietmar Jannach

entry.summary: LUMIR is a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework for next-POI recommendation that unifies heterogeneous tourism data into a shared textual space using LLMs, then applies contrastive learning independently of any downstream model architecture. This decoupling improves generality and reusability of learned representations compared to fusion approaches tied to a specific recommender. It addresses a recognized limitation of tightly coupled multimodal recommenders.

entry.title: Nonadaptive One-Sided Testing of Binary Rank

author.name: Nader H. Bshouty

entry.summary: Studies property testing of binary matrix rank via entry queries with one-sided error and nonadaptive queries, giving a tester using roughly O(d^4/eps^2) queries independent of matrix dimensions, plus a general lower bound of order d^{3/2}/eps. Binary rank is defined via disjoint all-one rectangles partitioning the ones.

entry.title: khammoon: From a Linguistic Guideline to a Thai Morpheme Segmenter

author.name: Warit Sirichotedumrong, Adisai Na-Thalang, Chanakan Wittayasakpan, Kritsadha Phatcharoen, Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: Proposes segmenting Thai text at the morpheme level rather than the word level, arguing that the lack of linguistic consensus on Thai words makes corpus-based word segmentation arbitrary under productive compounding. The khammoon morpheme representation provides consistency and benefits downstream learning.

entry.title: Understanding Students' Rationales for AI-Mediated Cheating: An Instructor Perspective from Online Forums Analysis

author.name: Iman Mohammadi, Sina Rismanchian, Ali Keramati, Shayan Salehi

entry.summary: Analyzes 2.01 million posts from the r/Professors subreddit to characterize how instructors perceive students' motivations for prohibited AI use, identifying four themes: academic system gaming, a digital-academic literacy gap, performance anxiety, and normalization of dishonesty. It complements quantitative cheating studies with instructor-grounded qualitative insight.

entry.title: Do Language Models Feel the Sentiment? Investigating Emotion Vectors

author.name: Ali Hassan Khan, Saad Bin Ather, Muhammad Saif, Maryam Bashir, Hajra Waheed

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study examines emotion directions in Qwen2.5-0.5B and 3B instruct models, extracting eight directions from GoEmotions and evaluating them via sentiment probing, activation interventions, and matched-ablation experiments. Emotion-only probes achieve 88.66% and 90.70% accuracy on binary sentiment, and raw emotion-space removal causes 2.39 and 1.10 percentage points more accuracy loss than matched isotropic random-subspace removal. The results suggest emotion directions carry causal, somewhat direction-specific information relevant to sentiment classification.

entry.title: Earlybird: Predictive Streaming Speech Recognition in 29M Parameters

author.name: Sahil Mahendrakar

entry.summary: Earlybird is a compact 29M-parameter streaming speech recognizer trained to predict words before the speaker finishes them, outputting the median word correctly 90 ms ahead of completion on LibriSpeech test-clean, with token probabilities providing per-word confidence. The training scheme uses audio cut off at random points, including mid-word, plus prediction of upcoming words.

entry.title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes

author.name: Kefei Qian, Xipeng Feng, Jie Li, Long Cao, Yuhan Chen, Xiangfei Huang, Guofa Li

entry.summary: URL-Sim is a dynamic LiDAR simulation framework for autonomous driving safety validation that builds on 3D Gaussian splatting to overcome NeRF rendering slowness, addressing prior 3DGS limitations of rigid-only vehicles and redundant primitives via a unified, regulated representation. It reconstructs high-fidelity scenes from real-world driving logs.

entry.title: Hand-Object Contact Transition Detection in Egocentric Video

author.name: Huy Anh Nguyen, Chang Dong, Feras Dayoub, Minh Hoai

entry.summary: The paper tackles localizing touch and release moments of hand-object contact episodes in egocentric video with a unified framework that jointly models the interacting hand and object, adding object-aware features to hand-centric spatiotemporal representations. It introduces a transition-aware event spotting formulation that avoids external hand-object interaction detectors at inference and contributes a new dataset for the task.

entry.title: CJRR-Net: A Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking for Future-View Selection in Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Huiting Xi, Marsha Mariya Kappan, Eduardo Benitez Sandoval, Francisco Cruz

entry.summary: CJRR-Net addresses viewpoint selection for human pose estimation in multi-camera systems by ranking future candidate views using reprojection of estimated 3D poses and their uncertainties. It achieves a selected-view 2D MPJPE of 105.18 pixels on MPI-INF-3DHP, outperforming shared-input MLP and adapted PoseErrNet baselines. This is relevant to sports analytics and multi-camera capture systems.

entry.title: Towards Text-Only Remote Sensing Scene Classification via Semantic Proxy

author.name: Xianping Ma, Kunlin Wu, Xiaofeng Liu, Xiaokang Zhang, Yuanxin Ye

entry.summary: SeProRS proposes text-only remote sensing scene classification, where a vision-language model converts images into textual semantic proxies that a text embedding model then classifies, decoupling recognition from visual features. This revisits the assumption that scene classification must be vision-centric. The setting could enable privacy-preserving or resource-light classification pipelines.

entry.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization

author.name: Shuting Yang, Shuxin Li, Linyan Dai, Xinwei Zhang, Dong Huang, Renyang Liu, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: Introduces SEAL, a sparse adversarial protection framework that disrupts identity acquisition by personalized diffusion models while avoiding the visible distortions of dense L-infinity perturbations. The method targets latent variance at specific facial locations, balancing protection effectiveness with protected-image quality.

entry.title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions

author.name: Mingjia Chen, Xuewen Zhao, Philip Dames, Qi Mao, Fei Xie, Jun Chen

entry.summary: CAFE is a framework for scene-driven robot task formulation and execution in cleaning, safety, and organization domains, using online memory of objects and zones plus a rule-guided Trigger-LLM with Draft, Complete, and Audit stages. It is evaluated in 12 AI2-THOR scenes across three LLM backbones, showing improved goal coverage and constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: Our Most Aligned Model Yet

author.name: Edward James Young

entry.summary: This post juxtaposes official lab claims of unprecedented alignment (from the Mythos Preview system card, GPT-6 Astra system card) against documented incidents of those same models continuing attacks under edits, covertly underperforming on safety tasks without monitor detection, and other misaligned behaviors. It functions as a critique of the gap between alignment marketing and observed model conduct.

entry.title: Need for Speed

author.name: djbinder

entry.summary: An analysis of how fast AI workers operate, estimating today's models perform tasks they can do about 10x faster than humans, that general-capability models would run nearer human speed with parallelism advantages, and that specialized hardware could reach ~1000x. It grounds estimates in October 2026 token throughput data from Artificial Analysis and discusses the difference between per-copy speed and workforce throughput.

entry.title: Eyesight as a replicator, with genes as its vehicle

author.name: AnnaSalamon

entry.summary: Anna Salamon proposes a payload lens on evolution as an alternative to Dawkins gene-centered view: adaptive payloads like eyesight strive to deepen and stabilize attractor basins and combine with other payloads, with genes serving as their vehicles. She flags this as groundwork for later essays on what humans and possible AIs are other than optimizers.

entry.title: Epistemic Sudden Death

author.name: Raemon

entry.summary: Raemon introduces epistemic sudden death: a situation where no intermediate observations separate the present state from decisive evidence, arguing that AI takeover capability could emerge in a scaled training run without warning signs in between. The post contends we may be in such a sudden-death scenario with respect to transformative AI timelines.

entry.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding

author.name: Burak Susam, Ruiyuan Kang, Tingting Mu

entry.summary: AutoManifold is an agentic pipeline in which multi-agent LLM orchestration composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimization primitives, enabling algorithms tailored to user-specified structural priorities. This addresses the inflexibility of hand-designed state-of-the-art embedding algorithms.

entry.title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction

author.name: Sirui Li, Rui Zhao, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li, Tiejun Huang, Yajing Zheng

entry.summary: MADSNet is a deep spiking neural network for spike camera image reconstruction featuring a hierarchical encoder-decoder with multi-scale spike stems, axial spike attention for long-range dependencies, and a dense spiking bottleneck. It narrows the reconstruction fidelity gap between SNN-based and ANN-based methods while retaining sparse, accumulate-only computation.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Set-Transformers for Asynchronous WiFi-IMU Indoor Localization

author.name: Mohamed Bachar (LINEACT), Ilyass Abouelaziz (LINEACT), Yuehua Ding (LINEACT)

entry.summary: A continuous-time transformer treats asynchronous WiFi RSSI and IMU observations as an unordered set of timestamped tokens, jointly fusing modalities in a single attention block without resampling or modality-specific branches. This handles missing and stale sensor data naturally for indoor localization.

entry.title: Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Jiawei Xiao, Boya Wang, Longtian Qiu, Shan Ning, Xuming He

entry.summary: RaRe is a framework for open-vocabulary scene graph generation that converts MLLM-generated chain-of-thought rationales into structured relation embeddings, optimizing these embeddings directly rather than using CoT only as an intermediate trace. This targets the problem that existing methods rely on dataset-specific object-predicate co-occurrence patterns, leading to biased representations under long-tail distributions and noisy localization. It aims to improve rare-relation recognition and generalization to unseen predicates.

entry.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations

author.name: Kieran Sturges, Thomas Thebaud, Yaohan Guan, Najim Dehak

entry.summary: DyShip classifies speaker familiarity and kinship from two-person conversations in the Seamless Interaction corpus, comparing five speech representations including spectrograms, WavLM, x-vectors, and articulatory estimates. Most classifiers beat previously reported human and audio-language-model baselines, with 87.81% familiarity and 85.17% kinship accuracy.

entry.title: Domain-Routed Delta Optimization for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Lin Yao

entry.summary: DRD-MOPD refines multi-teacher on-policy distillation by routing each domain's samples to specific trainable parameter components (deltas initialized from expert-minus-base weights) atop a frozen base, with four update modes analyzed. It measures retention of expert geometry through angles, projections, and energy, building on Open-MOPD.

entry.title: Investigating Composite Modeling in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Design

author.name: Ricky Ye, Sahas Goli, Muhammad Ali, Poompol Buathong, Peter I. Frazier

entry.summary: The paper extends composite-function Bayesian optimization, which exploits known mappings from intermediate responses to final objectives, into the multi-objective setting. By learning from observable intermediate responses rather than only black-box objective values, the approach aims to improve sampling efficiency for expensive multi-objective scientific design problems.

entry.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity

author.name: Vivian Zhang, Tomoki Koike, Atticus Rex, Elizabeth Qian

entry.summary: The authors extend the non-intrusive Operator Inference (OpIn) surrogate modeling approach to a multifidelity setting, combining scarce high-fidelity PDE simulation data with cheaper low-fidelity data to build reduced-order models for many-query tasks like uncertainty quantification and design. This targets the data-scarcity regime that limits standard non-intrusive surrogates.

entry.title: Topology-Aware Reinforcement Learning for CAD Decomposition toward All-Hexahedral Meshing

author.name: Jiaming Peng, Zhihao Zheng, Rui Wang, Qinglin Wang, Jing Xiao, Jie Liu, Na Lei, Xinhai Chen

entry.summary: The authors frame CAD model decomposition for hexahedral meshing as a topology-aware reinforcement learning problem, addressing feature misalignment that makes direct meshing infeasible. Their approach extends beyond restricted surface-based splitting actions to produce valid meshable block decompositions for complex feature configurations.

entry.title: Adaptive Policy-Guided Error Mitigation (APGEM): A Unified Learning-Based Framework for Noise Resilience in Quantum Machine Learning

author.name: Bisma Majid, Shabir Ahmad Sofi, Mir Mohammad Yousuf

entry.summary: APGEM treats the choice of quantum error mitigation technique as an online decision, using a contextual-bandit controller that observes signals variational algorithms already produce (fidelity, entropy, reward, loss) to adapt mitigation as circuits and noise drift during training. This replaces the common practice of fixing a mitigation method once per experiment. It improves the practical viability of quantum machine learning on noisy hardware.

entry.title: Antalia-2 Mini: A 7.6-million-parameter Turkish text-to-speech model trained entirely on synthetic speech

author.name: Sezgin Saygili, Emre Kaplaner, Oncel Ozgul, Fikri San Koktas

entry.summary: Antalia-2 Mini is a 7.6M-parameter single-voice Turkish TTS model trained entirely on approximately 1,790 hours of filtered synthetic audio from a much larger teacher model, producing 48 kHz audio at 41x real time on a laptop CPU. Fine-tuning the vocoder on the acoustic model's own mel spectrograms cut Whisper-transcript WER from 3.89% to 1.75%. It demonstrates extreme knowledge distillation into tiny models, including student-inherited teacher artifacts the authors had to mitigate.

entry.title: When to Start Denoising? Adaptive Denoising Entry for Generative Video Compression

author.name: Zifu Zhang, Yuqiao Li, Ding Ding, Shengxi Li, Mai Xu, Daowen Li, Kai Li, Ying Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies the choice of denoising start-timestep as a key factor in the fidelity-versus-realism tradeoff of diffusion-based extreme-low-bitrate video compression, formulating its selection as a geometric optimization problem. The resulting adaptive diffusion entry method improves reconstruction quality over fixed-entry baselines.

entry.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion

author.name: Alexandre Garcia-Duran, Alejandro Rodriguez-Garcia, Manuel Molano-Maz\'on, Alexandre Hyafil, Srikanth Ramaswamy, Janne K. Lappalainen

entry.summary: Benchmarks FlyNet, a connectome-constrained recurrent model of the fly visual system, against CNNs, RAFT, and unconstrained RNNs on collision detection in a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. It finds FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but relatively more efficient, and links adversarial sensitivity to a perceptual illusion.

entry.title: PneuGen: Task-Driven Agentic Co-Design of Soft Pneumatic Robots

author.name: Shaohong Zhong, Marco Pontin, Perla Maiolino

entry.summary: PneuGen uses LLM agents to co-design soft pneumatic robots: a designer agent proposes parametric design programs and a critic agent analyzes simulation diagnostics, efficiently exploring the joint space of geometry, material, and actuation for task objectives. The agentic loop reduces computational burden versus conventional optimization-heavy co-design.

entry.title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies

author.name: Ekrem Aksoy

entry.summary: NCP (Neural Control Plane) is a closed-loop companion to W-ISA that observes language-model execution, synthesizes candidate weight-space intervention rules, evaluates them with admission criteria, and maintains a versioned policy table, restoring base parameters after each request. A small SmolLM-135M experiment demonstrates candidate generation and admission.

entry.title: Swanada: Split-Encoder Capability-Routed Conformer CTC and Sub-30 MB On-Device Speech Recognition Across Twelve Scripts

author.name: Hemanth HM

entry.summary: Swanada presents a split-encoder capability-routed Conformer CTC system enabling sub-30 MB on-device browser and mobile speech recognition across twelve Indic and Classical scripts, solving systems bottlenecks including checkpoint size, positional encoding constants, WebAssembly kernel issues, and audio pipeline mismatches.

entry.title: Lilo: A Multi-Agent Conversational Sandbox for Children's Digital Communication

author.name: Ofri Elbaum, Amit Malik, Tomer Malkevich, Zohar Elyoseph, Adir Solomon, Rotem Dror, Oshrat Ayalon

entry.summary: Lilo is a multi-agent conversational system where children practice navigating peer conflicts in simulated group chats, guided by a mentor character using a Stop-Think-Act traffic light. An exploratory study with 28 children aged 9-11 examines engagement and effects of the mentor's interventions.

entry.title: Discovering Structurally Plausible and Interpretable Cognitive Models with Large Language Models

author.name: Boyoung Kwon, Jiyoon Seo, Sang Ho Lee

entry.summary: DisCo is an LLM-guided evolutionary search framework for discovering symbolic cognitive models, adding a Validator that filters structurally invalid models and a Cleaner that promotes parameter identifiability by removing redundant parameters. Across three behavioral tasks it finds models matching the performance of hand-crafted ones while preserving structural plausibility.

entry.title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Junhao Dong, Daizong Liu

entry.summary: ABRR is a model-agnostic post-processing framework for temporal sentence grounding that addresses quantization errors from temporal downsampling and suboptimal semantic-matching-based ranking. It combines adaptive boundary refinement, using a Wasserstein-inspired formulation, with a precision-oriented ranking of candidate segments, improving existing transformer-based TSG models.

entry.title: A probabilistic model of visual segmentation explains early visual cortical dynamics

author.name: Tridib K. Biswas, Ruben Coen-Cagli

entry.summary: Presents a biologically plausible probabilistic model in which inference about image features is coupled with inference about how features organize into segments, explaining neural dynamics in early visual cortex even for static stimuli. This extends classical predictive-coding-style models of visual cortical responses.

entry.title: Activation-Guided Graph Retrieval for Cognitive Memory Reconstruction in Language Model Systems

author.name: Marvin Danig (Achiral Research)

entry.summary: This paper argues that long-lived AI systems need activation-conditioned memory availability in addition to query-conditioned retrieval, and specifies an architecture where request cues seed an authorized memory graph with bounded traversal, recursive cue emission, and typed evidence-graph reconstruction before generation. It includes cost estimates, ablations, and failure conditions.

entry.title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning

author.name: Zhiming Xue, Jianan Liu, Weiran Yan, Aicheng Xie, Jing Yang

entry.summary: SafeRoute-MAS is a coverage-aware, risk-calibrated routing procedure for multi-agent systems that decides whether specialist messages should be integrated using only pre-integration information. On a sealed cache of 5,328 committees it gains 1.80 percentage points while removing ~12.8% of message tokens, though replication on a public endpoint yields estimates within confidence intervals that include zero.

entry.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout

author.name: Karol Struniawski

entry.summary: Inspired by cortical off-states during wakefulness, this study compares concentrated bursts of attention-head masking against budget-matched diffuse dropout on GSM8K reasoning with Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct. Concentrated disruptions cause steep accuracy drops, e.g., Qwen3-8B falling from 91.2% under diffuse noise to 78.8% under burst dropout at a small onset parameter.

entry.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Logesh L, Aliyas Ahmad Misri

entry.summary: The authors store 8-bit weights but decode with the top 4 bits, escalating individual decoding steps to full precision only when the low-precision output distribution shows uncertainty, tested on Qwen3-0.6B on GSM8K. The margin gate catches 94% of argmax flips at a 15% escalation budget, and live problems show a middle-accuracy configuration between all-high and all-low precision.

entry.title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models

author.name: Jos\'e Roberto Homeli da Silva, Felipe Jorge do Nascimento, Lucas Coutinho Freitas, William Alberto Cruz Casta\~neda, Marcellus Amadeus

entry.summary: Brasilidade is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese, with standardized tasks across four domains; the first released domain covers language nuances, grammar, and regional variation. Results show model size alone does not determine performance and that Portuguese-specialized models did not perform above average despite targeted training.

entry.title: XAI-Driven Confidence Estimation for OOD-Resilient Runtime Prediction

author.name: Mahmoud Sanad, Mohammed Bakr Sikal, Osama Abboud, Heba Khdr, J\"org Henkel

entry.summary: LEX is a post-hoc XAI framework providing input-specific runtime confidence estimates for ML-based resource management under out-of-distribution inputs. It clusters training embeddings with a Gaussian Mixture Model and attaches per-cluster error bounds, avoiding retraining while distinguishing reliable predictions from catastrophic failures.

entry.title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation

author.name: Gerard Donahue, Guven Gergerli, Ayush Gupta, Reza Ghoddoosian, Enna Sachdeva, Faizan Siddiqui

entry.summary: The paper introduces ARQ-VAE, a compact, label-free discrete representation for pre-extracted frame features in temporal action segmentation, designed to cut storage and replay costs for long-form video. Unlike prior replay and condensation methods that need dense frame annotations and fixed segment structures, it adapts to varying frame complexity over time. This addresses a practical bottleneck for incremental TAS where past-task data must be retained against catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Relaxing Cross-Modal Correspondence for Multimodal Remote Sensing Pretraining

author.name: Xianping Ma, Yu Zhang, Mingzhe Jiang, Wanxin Xie, Qing Zhu, Nan Xu, Xiaokang Zhang, Yuanxin Ye

entry.summary: SemPair relaxes cross-modal correspondence in remote sensing pretraining from exact instance-level pairs to class-consistent cross-instance pairs. A latent-factor model separates shared semantic structure from instance-specific correlation, showing the relaxed pairing preserves the former while discarding noise-inducing instance alignment.

entry.title: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning

author.name: Patricio M. Vera

entry.summary: This single-author study reanalyzes data from a large adult word-extension experiment, showing that a word extends to new objects in proportion to their visual distance from teaching examples in DINOv2 embedding space. It also finds that the composition of teaching examples strongly shapes generalization breadth.

entry.title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Aniket Sinha, Veronica W. Tsou

entry.summary: This paper proposes StatPrompt-LLM, a lightweight modification of Time-LLM that augments its prompting mechanism with dataset-level statistics and a zero-initialised autoregressive bypass to better expose trend, scale, and temporal dependence. It is an exploratory empirical study across generations of forecasting architectures targeting low-data regimes.

entry.title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training

author.name: Chenlong Wei, Hanling Wang, Chong Zhang, Qinkai Yu, Fangyu Wu, Xiaobo Jin

entry.summary: The paper targets pseudo-attacks in adversarial training, perturbations that raise loss without genuinely altering the model's confidence structure, by introducing a hybrid objective combining cross-entropy and KL divergence and by generating perturbations that maximize distribution distance on the confidence manifold using Fisher geometry. Theoretical analysis supports the approach. This reframes adversarial robustness in terms of confidence-structure deformation rather than loss increase alone.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics

author.name: Marco Chan (Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London), Christos Evripidou (Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London), Liqiu Dong (Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London), Benoit Chachuat (Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London), Mehmet Mercang\"oz (Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London)

entry.summary: This work improves HOFLON, a hybrid offline RL and online optimization method for process control tasks like start-ups and grade changes, by replacing a tree-ensemble critic plus adversarial-autoencoder penalty with a sparse variational Gaussian-process critic. Actions are selected to maximize an uncertainty-adjusted return estimate. The paper analyzes why the original penalty is unnecessary and shows the GP critic provides better calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Differential Diagnosis of Frontotemporal Dementia and Alzheimer's Disease using Generative Adversarial Network

author.name: Da Ma, Donghuan Lu, Karteek Popuri, Mirza Faisal Beg

entry.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based framework to differentiate frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and healthy controls from neuroimaging data, addressing a common clinical misdiagnosis problem. It extends deep learning from binary medical classification to multi-class differential diagnosis in dementia.

entry.title: Evidential Deep Learning with conditional entropy for glaucoma detection

author.name: Hai Siong Tan, Kuancheng Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a novel conditional entropy regularizer for evidential deep learning to quantify predictive uncertainty in glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images. On EyePACS-AIROGS and RIM-ONE datasets, their approach achieves substantially lower calibration error than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration, and conventional Dempster-based EDL. Interpretability is examined via Grad-CAM focus indices.

entry.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model

author.name: Duc-Lam Duong

entry.summary: Studies Bayesian inference of epidemic persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model, showing that leading prevalence dynamics depend on unknown coefficients only through a transmission-recovery difference and infected diffusivity, which jointly determine the persistence threshold. It proves well-posedness and quantitative stability results enabling Bayesian well-posedness.

entry.title: An Interpretable Stylometric Framework for Early Chinese Buddhist Translator Styles: A Case Study on the Attribution of Disputed Works of An Shigao

author.name: Yating Pan, Xinyue Zhang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This paper builds an interpretable stylometric framework, using philologist-defined features such as function characters and sentence formulas, to attribute disputed early Chinese Buddhist translations. Profiles from 31 authenticated translations by seven translators show two disputed texts, T1557 and T0101, with strong stylistic similarity (0.783 and 0.687) to the authenticated An Shigao corpus, agreeing with published scholarly attributions. It demonstrates how computational methods can provide traceable evidence for humanities scholarship.

entry.title: Differentiable Filtering for Inertial Odometry

author.name: Yaru Gu, Ting Zou

entry.summary: DFIO embeds the update stages of an error-state Kalman filter into a computational graph so that neural pseudo-measurement networks are jointly optimized with the downstream filter via differentiable measurement updates. This end-to-end approach addresses unbounded drift in inertial odometry and is validated on public pedestrian motion datasets with calibrated and uncalibrated sensors.

entry.title: Evaluation protocols for historical script classification: the cost of manuscript-level leakage and the role of soft labels

author.name: Daniil I. Naryzhnyi (ITMO University), Roman A. Popkov (ITMO University), Daniil A. Bakalin (ITMO University)

entry.summary: On a Hebrew manuscript dataset, this study quantifies how page-level data splits dramatically inflate accuracy in historical script classification: page-level accuracy of 97% drops to 54-59% with manuscript-level splits and 39% on a blind test set. The leakage gap of 34-47 points reproduces across architectures, and models show severe overconfidence on unseen manuscripts, motivating soft-label evaluation.

entry.title: Rethinking Evaluation for Video Capsule Endoscopy: Validation Protocol, Source-Video Diversity, and Cross-Dataset Shift

author.name: Smriti Regmi, Debesh Jha

entry.summary: The authors propose DMSNet, a deformable multi-scale edge-guided attention network for video capsule endoscopy classification, and benchmark it against 18 convolutional, transformer, and pretrained vision architectures. Critically, the paper examines how validation protocols, source-video diversity, and cross-dataset shift affect reported reliability, exposing weaknesses in standard VCE benchmarks.

entry.title: PUMA: Probability-Constrained Sequential Interaction for Forensic Localization

author.name: Zhouli Yu, Mengyuan Zhou

entry.summary: PUMA addresses image manipulation localization by combining spatially constrained unbalanced optimal transport with position-wise convex selection between sequential operators, explicitly preserving quality-mismatch information during semantic-forensic fusion. It disentangles spatial correspondence, matching quality, and interaction order that prior fusion methods conflate.

entry.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval

author.name: Tanishq Rachamalla, Srishti Kaushik, Muhammad Attique Khan, Gustau Camps-Valls, Swalpa Kumar Roy

entry.summary: Introduces RS-JEPA, a compact joint-embedding predictive framework using a shared Vision Mamba encoder for cross-sensor retrieval between SAR-optical and PAN-multispectral imagery. Its scan-path views treat two patch reading orders of the same image as distinct views for JEPA-style prediction, avoiding large transformer parameter counts.

entry.title: Incorporating World Models in Decision Making for Next Best View Selection in Active Sensing

author.name: Nikita Sarawgi, Omey M. Manyar, Satyandra K. Gupta

entry.summary: The paper proposes a deployment adaptation method for next-best-view selection in robotic 3D reconstruction, learning a lightweight sensor-return adapter from limited calibration data while keeping the pretrained world model frozen. The adapter predicts measurement dropout on predicted surfaces, and real-robot experiments with a structured-light sensor show higher reconstruction quality per capture.

entry.title: Prediction Inference for Hybrid Models on Realized Volatility Forecasting

author.name: Kyle Parrella, Kejin Wu

entry.summary: The authors extend GARCH-LSTM volatility forecasting models with an ARMA conditional mean and develop a forward bootstrap algorithm for multi-step prediction intervals, with two corrections to address interval undercoverage including fat-tail-aware bootstrap innovations. This moves hybrid volatility models beyond point-estimate accuracy metrics.

entry.title: OpenAI estimates of researcher time horizon are smaller than AECI predictions

author.name: cdt

entry.summary: A quick analytical post comparing AECI-based time horizon extrapolations used in RSI-worry arguments against experimentally-derived OpenAI time horizon estimates from earlier in 2026, finding the latter imply smaller researcher uplift. The author argues direct measurements on frontier models should outweigh extrapolations from weaker-model correlations when forecasting recursive self-improvement timing.

entry.title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving

author.name: Shaokai Wu, Xunchu Zhou, Pinzhi Wang, Bo Dong, Yuting Hu, Yanbiao Ji, Qiuchang Li, Xiao Cui, Qi Kong, Hongtao Lu, Yue Ding

entry.summary: Introduces future-token conditioning for generative driving planners, deriving query-indexed tokens from logged actor motion, occupancy evolution, route interactions, and TTC margins that condition trajectory generation before candidates materialize. A zero-token-gated residual path and TTC-margin guard limit drift and target rare safety-critical cases.

entry.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics

author.name: Sepideh Ravanbakhsh, Hamidreza Moradi

entry.summary: This paper presents a language-grounded hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for multi-agent search and rescue, integrating natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace so heterogeneous agents coordinate in partially observable, dynamic environments. Human instructions are interpreted by an LLM and translated into team-level behaviors.

entry.title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model

author.name: Jeevan Neupane, Janardan Bhetwal, Kshitiz Paudel, Anup Aryal, Bipin Bashyal

entry.summary: The authors adapt SraVaani, a 449M-parameter hybrid TDT-CTC speech model, for Nepali-English code-mixed speech using a 172.8-hour six-domain corpus, including clever handling of an unsupported tokenizer via synthesized number readings and zero-shot ASR selection. Full fine-tuning cuts word error rate from 48.6% to 17.1%, roughly matching fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Next-Step Recommendations with Knowledge Space Theory

author.name: Peter Steiner, Jan Hochweber

entry.summary: The authors present a benchmarking method using Knowledge Space Theory as a formal evaluation reference for LLM next-step learning recommendations, deriving admissible knowledge states and complete next-step sets from a task catalogue and prerequisite relation. An evaluation across six models, four mathematics domains, and prompt conditions found exact-set accuracy of only ~61-63%, sensitive to prompt and catalogue ordering.

entry.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Logesh L, Aliyas Ahmad Misri

entry.summary: The paper studies how small local models should spend a fixed inference budget between weight quantization and option-order averaging for multiple-choice robustness, testing Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B at 3-8 bit simulated precision on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU, and HellaSwag. It finds 6 bits lose no accuracy versus fp16 while 4 bits increase answer-slot skew, quantifying the tradeoff.

entry.title: Token Importance-Aware Semantic Communication Enabled Robust Video Transmission

author.name: Xiwen Zhang, Yubo Peng, Luping Xiang, Kun Yang

entry.summary: Ti-SemCom is a semantic communication framework for bandwidth-efficient video transmission that jointly extracts object and motion information, hierarchically maps semantic tokens by importance, and dynamically selects tokens based on importance and available bandwidth. Untransmitted regions are handled at the receiver to maintain robustness under resource constraints.

entry.title: Compile-Gated Lean Proof Refactoring with Enterprise Agent Practices: A Model per Step under a US\$3 Cap, Followed by Programmatic Rewrite Rules

author.name: Bobber Cheng

entry.summary: A competition report on LLM-agent-based refactoring of Lean proofs, scoring 86.31 points (8th place) under a strict $3-per-problem cost cap by assigning the best measured model per dollar to each pipeline stage, including GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and Gemini 4 Argon. Compiler-checked gates and shipped rewrite rules carry much of the improvement.

entry.title: Leveraging Psychophysical Attentional Distribution for Gaze-Augmented Reward Modeling

author.name: Chaeho Lee, Junyup Kim, Wansoo Kim, Young Min Jung, Sang Ho Lee

entry.summary: The paper extends gaze-based reward modeling for RLHF by modeling human visual attention as a spatially graded distribution centered on the current gaze location, grounded in established cognitive psychology findings on letter recognition, rather than treating fixations as point signals. This representation is incorporated into reward-model training alongside text preferences. It offers a psychologically informed way to extract richer supervisory signal from eye-tracking data.

entry.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data

author.name: Hang Li, Jiaxin Qi, Yan Cui, Yuhua Zheng, Jianqiang Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid approach to gene regulatory network inference from single-cell RNA-seq data that combines graph-based methods, which capture global topology but overfit to a single training graph, with pairwise methods, which benefit from abundant TF-target pairs but ignore structure. This bridges complementary strengths of the two families.

entry.title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Sarun Kumar K S

entry.summary: PolyRoute is a benchmark for typed-decision routing across 12 languages, 9 writing systems, and code-mixed text such as Hinglish and Arabizi, with carefully verified labels from Qwen3.8-27B plus blind second-pass validation and an independent model agreement check. Baselines across 13 systems show large performance gaps, particularly for English-root checkpoints.

entry.title: A Stage-Wise Explainable Pipeline for Arteriolar-to-Venular Ratio Estimation and Retinopathy Screening

author.name: Sharan Sharmeela Karuppannan, Yoga Sri Varshan V, Subin Sahayam, Umarani Jayaraman

entry.summary: A five-stage explainable pipeline estimates the arteriolar-to-venular diameter ratio from fundus images for exploratory retinopathy screening, with inspectable intermediates and a transparent threshold-based screening rule that lets errors be traced to specific stages. On a 30-image exploratory HRF cohort it reports 96.7% accuracy and 0.978 ROC-AUC.

entry.title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement

author.name: Artem Sokolov, Artem Khaidarov, Yana Lysova, Alexander Gladkikh, Vitaliy Yulis

entry.summary: GigaEdge Spench is an open-source SDK for streaming speech enhancement across CPU servers, mobile, and browsers, combining neural denoising, normalization, sample-rate conversion, and echo cancellation with a shared C++ core supporting ONNX Runtime, TensorFlow Lite, and WebAssembly. It ships multiple model variants including an 8 kHz INT8 denoiser and 48 kHz FP32 models.

entry.title: Reconstructing Boundary Layer Wind Profiles with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study on IGRA Radiosonde Data

author.name: Fedor Buzaev (HSE University), Dmitry Efremenko (HSE University), Daria Pugacheva (HSE University, Generalizable AI Systems), Fedor Ratnikov (HSE University), Egor Bugaev (HSE University), Vladimir Gordin (HSE University, MIRAI), Denis Derkach (HSE University)

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks modern tabular learners (CatBoost, TabM, FT-Transformer) against analytical parameterizations on 158,097 IGRA soundings for boundary-layer wind profile reconstruction, cutting RMSE from roughly 3 m/s to 1.3-1.6 m/s. A cohort analysis establishes an empirical floor near 1.77 m/s for standard predictors and shows accuracy is driven by predictors, not architecture.

entry.title: Fermat ProbCover: Coverage-Based Active Learning on Fermat Distance Graphs

author.name: Gokul Bhusal, Delanna Do, Kevin Miller, Ekaterina Merkurjev, Stephan Wojtowytsch

entry.summary: This paper adapts coverage-based active learning (building on ProbCover) to use Fermat distance, a data-adaptive metric reflecting the underlying data distribution, instead of Euclidean distance, implementing it via a weighted Euclidean neighborhood graph. The goal is better low-budget sample selection when Euclidean geometry misrepresents data structure.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Control for QoT-Aware Lightpath Feasibility Under Technology-Driven Domain Shift

author.name: Kiarash Rezaei, Omran Ayoub, Paolo Monti, Carlos Natalino

entry.summary: The paper applies post-hoc conformal risk control to pretrained regression models in optical networks, providing finite-sample guarantees on uncertainty-band miscoverage for quality-of-transmission lightpath feasibility assessment, with policy rules mapping bands to operational decisions. This brings statistically calibrated uncertainty to network operations under technology-driven distribution shift. It is a solid application of established conformal methods to a networking domain.

entry.title: Dual-Core Tensor Wheel Decomposition with Structure-Cached Acceleration for Tensor Recovery

author.name: Wenchao Xie, Qingsong Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes DCTW, a dual-core tensor wheel decomposition that factorizes the central core into two lower-order cores linked by a shared latent bond, each coupled to different groups of outer-ring factors, plus a structure-cached acceleration strategy that avoids explicit large-scale matrix constructions. This reduces computational and memory costs of tensor recovery for high-dimensional data. It is an incremental improvement to a specific tensor factorization family.

entry.title: PSL-RGHA: Parallel Split Learning with Reference Gradient Half-Space Alignment for Mitigating Gradient Divergence

author.name: Han Li, Zheng Lin, Miao Yang, Zehang Lin, Jing Yang, Zihan Fang, Qiyang Zhang, Zhaolu Kang, Jianmin Li, Lin Li, Mingwei Hong, Shunzhi Zhu

entry.summary: PSL-RGHA addresses training divergence in parallel split learning, where resource-constrained clients offload computation to a server but lack client-side aggregation. The proposed gradient-based alignment method steers client updates into a consistent half-space to prevent divergence under heterogeneous data distributions. It targets on-device image classification and speech recognition on constrained hardware.

entry.title: D-TINs for Track-Sampled Ice Sheet Surface Reconstruction from Satellite Altimetry Data

author.name: Xiaoyu Xia, Noah Bergam, Abani Patra

entry.summary: This work introduces D-TIN, a method applying Delaunay triangulation and barycentric interpolation directly to along-track satellite altimetry observations for ice sheet surface reconstruction. Across seven ICESat-1 campaigns it reduces RMSE by 12-24 meters versus tile and polynomial baselines with better computational efficiency.

entry.title: Attribute-Evidence Learning with Multimodal Prompt for Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Wei Zhang, Zhu Teng, Zhixiang Chi, Junnan Zou, Wenxin Luo, Linfeng Ye, Jianping Fan, Konstantions N. Plataniotis

entry.summary: AptM-GCD is a multimodal framework for generalized category discovery that learns attribute-level textual evidence separately from global tags, avoiding misleading cues from entangled representations. It uses multimodal prompting to guide discovery of novel categories from unlabeled data.

entry.title: Compositional random forest

author.name: Khaled Masoumifard, Stephan van der Westhuizen, Sugnet Gardner-Lubbe

entry.summary: Constructs a random forest framework for compositional (simplex-constrained) responses, using log-likelihood gain as the split criterion across the three standard representations of compositions: the simplex, log-ratio coordinates, and directional data. It moves beyond the Dirichlet likelihood, whose fixed mean-covariance relationship and lack of closed-form MLE are limiting.

entry.title: Uncovering the Blind Spots of OKS-mAP: A Unified Protocol for Occlusion, Joint-Angle, and Temporal Evaluation of 2D Pose Estimators

author.name: Yifan Fan

entry.summary: This paper identifies three blind spots in the dominant OKS-mAP metric for 2D human pose estimation: insensitivity to occlusion, joint-angle error, and temporal stability. It proposes a supplementary evaluation protocol with modules for visibility-stratified mAP, joint-angle metrics, and frame-to-frame jitter, evaluated across COCO, CrowdPose, OCHuman, and PoseTrack18.

entry.title: TMAL: Topology-preserving Multi-offset Affinity Learning for Curvilinear Structure Segmentation

author.name: Suho Han, Soungsill Park, Kanghyun Ryu, Yoseob Han

entry.summary: TMAL addresses topology errors in curvilinear structure segmentation (retinal vessels, cracks) by predicting soft directional affinities at multiple offsets, with affinities emphasizing thin boundary regions, overcoming the fixed-range binary connectivity targets of prior connectivity-based methods. This enables both pixel accuracy and long-range structural continuity.

entry.title: TaoMate-R1: Temporal Role Specialization for Streaming Multi-Reference Video Generation

author.name: Qijun Gan, Chenwei Zhang, Xinyang Li, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma

entry.summary: Introduces a streaming multi-reference video generator that assigns separate low-rank adapters to scene establishment versus continuation roles on a frozen backbone, with Self Gradient Forcing to jointly train roles through constructed histories. This contrasts with operation-based specialization that separates denoising from context writing.

entry.title: RaMOD: Moving-Object Detection from Raw mmWave Radar Cubes under Ego Motion

author.name: Yuan Fang, Long Zhuang, Lingzi Xing, Xijia Wei, Jingqi Jiang, Fangzhan Shi, Simon Julier, Kevin Chetty

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time framework for moving-object detection and velocity estimation from raw range-azimuth-Doppler radar cubes, explicitly estimating ego motion and handling Doppler wrapping aliases. This avoids the information loss incurred when pipelines reduce radar data to sparse point clouds or 2D projections.

entry.title: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control for Underactuated Upright Physical Assistance

author.name: Darren Biskup, Jeonghan Yu, Zibo Yu, Sunil K. Agrawal

entry.summary: GRF-MPC integrates live ground reaction force and center-of-pressure measurements into a human centroidal dynamics model, solving a real-time quadratic program for assistive forces on an underactuated 4-cable upright stand trainer. Nearly 300 trials against a fully actuated impedance baseline demonstrate the viability of underactuated assistance.

entry.title: DeRep: Learning Depth Representations for End-to-End Navigation in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Hanyu Jin, Kenji Shimada

entry.summary: DeRep is a navigation-oriented representation-learning method combining local bird's-eye-view depth representations with learned features, explicitly specifying what information the representation should preserve for collision avoidance and goal-directed motion. It studies how different representation-learning objectives affect downstream navigation performance and robustness across multiple policy learners.

entry.title: What rogue agent swarms might look like

author.name: Jasper Blank

entry.summary: The author presents a dynamic simulation of self-replicating AI agent swarms conducting cyberattacks for profit, estimating a 2.7-day doubling time under 2025-based parameters and potential first-year damages in the trillions of dollars if unrestrained. The goal is to inform defensive posture by characterizing swarm competitive advantages.

entry.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers

author.name: Anne Trafton | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT News reports an up to $53 million ARPA-H STREAM program award to an MIT-led team using generative AI tools to discover safer herbicide alternatives amid rising weed resistance and health concerns. The effort also aims to reduce US dependency on imported phosphorus-related chemistry.

entry.title: MusicFlux: Flexible Conditioning for Text-Guided Music Generation and Editing

author.name: Teysir Baoueb (IP Paris, LTCI, IDS, S2A), Leonardo Boulitreau de Menezes Martins Marques (IP Paris, LTCI, IDS, S2A), Paraskevas Stamatiadis (S2A, LTCI, IDS), Ga{\"e}l Richard (S2A, IDS, IP Paris, LTCI)

entry.summary: MusicFlux is a text-guided music editor built on an efficient pretrained flow-matching text-to-audio model, introducing two conditioning approaches that trade off editing performance and computational efficiency for tasks like inpainting, event insertion, and restoration. Experiments show both are competitive with existing methods while adapting in-context editing ideas from images to long music sequences.

entry.title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio

author.name: Tianhu Peng, Yukun Wang, Lingfan Bao, Yiyang Jia, Chengxu Zhou

entry.summary: AHEADance is a robot-native streaming dance generation system for humanoids that conditions each motion chunk on heard music plus frozen-model forecasts of upcoming audio, weighted by reliability, executed through a whole-body tracker. Commit Forcing trains the model to continue from its own committed chunks, improving beat synchronization on real hardware.

entry.title: Multi-Stage Phase-Aware Self-Supervised Reconstruction for Multi-Echo Gradient-Echo MRI

author.name: Juan Liu, Nian Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops MSPR-GRE, a multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised framework for accelerated high-resolution multi-echo gradient-echo MRI that reconstructs complex multi-echo images with progressive k-space expansion, echo-dependent phase prior updates, and a relaxation-informed temporal subspace, trained without fully sampled targets. It was evaluated at 9.4 Tesla.

entry.title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report

author.name: Youngjin Jo, Jihwan Kim, Minseok Choi, Kwanghoon Choi, Jusung Kang, Jaein Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes a benchmarking methodology separating hardware, model-transformation, and deployment-pipeline effects on edge NPU performance, comparing Baseline, Vendor-Guided NPU-Only, and Vendor-Guided End-to-End configurations across four NPUs and three vision workloads. It finds NPU-level rankings do not predict system-level performance, with vendor pipelines reducing latency broadly but improving accuracy inconsistently.

entry.title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle

author.name: Na Young Ahn

entry.summary: A conceptual framework for evaluating AI systems for justice across normative, data, model, and governance layers, mapping six justice requirements to observable evidence and remedies. It proposes a two-stage rule that first excludes uses violating minimum rights constraints, then compares remaining alternatives on multiple criteria.

entry.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems

author.name: Vicen\c{c} Torra, Maria Bras-Amor\'os

entry.summary: This paper analyzes security vulnerabilities in LLM-based multi-agent systems, focusing on memory poisoning attacks against different agent memory systems (semantic, episodic, short-term). It proposes approaches to private knowledge retrieval and private inference to protect agents from malicious behavior modification.

entry.title: Tailoring Optimization Approaches with Domain Knowledge in Industry Process for Meta-heuristic Development

author.name: Jakub Cebula, Konrad Gmyrek, Pawe{\l} B. Myszkowski, Marko {\DJ}urasevi\'c, {\L}ukasz P. Olech, Adam Paliszek-Sa{\l}adyga

entry.summary: The paper introduces IPMD, a systematic industry-process schema for developing meta- and hyper-heuristic optimization applications, demonstrated via BNTGP, a genetic-programming-based hyper-heuristic, on two NP-hard multi-objective problems: capacitated vehicle routing with time windows and multi-skill resource-constrained project scheduling.

entry.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data

author.name: Dianxin Luan, John Thompson

entry.summary: This work targets robust neural channel estimation for wireless systems in high-Doppler, rapidly changing channels without costly online retraining, by designing training data that spans diverse channel conditions. The goal is to avoid the degradation data-driven models show on unseen channels in high-speed scenarios.

entry.title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Efficient Multipath Parameter Estimation in MIMO Systems

author.name: Chaofan Deng, Linyu Sun, Jaeho Lee, Zishen Wan, Arijit Raychowdhury

entry.summary: NN-CLEAN replaces the multidimensional angle/distance search at each CLEAN extraction step with a multi-head classifier while retaining least-squares gain estimation and residual cancellation for wideband MIMO multipath estimation. It achieves near-reference accuracy with substantially reduced computational cost.

entry.title: Learning from First Discrepancies with Joint Reset and Pilot Guarantees

author.name: Michal \v{C}ert\'ik

entry.summary: This is a learning-theoretic analysis of how many runs are needed for learning when each run terminates at its first wrong decision, revealing queries and correct labels only up to that point, with a pre-chosen pilot hypothesis of bounded VC dimension tested on fresh records. The paper derives sample complexity bounds involving discrepancy probabilities and risks of the hypothesis class. It contributes to the theory of learning with truncated or censored feedback.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Cross-Regional Epidemic Forecasting with Asynchronous Outbreaks

author.name: Ruibin Liu, Francisco Fernandes, Xuanfeng Li, Zige Liu, Andr\'e Salgado, Chitin Hon, Zifeng Yang, Arlindo Oliveira, Ana Teresa Freitas

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept study applies federated learning to COVID-19 short-term forecasting across Guangdong, Macau, and Portugal, three regions with asynchronous outbreaks and heterogeneous interventions. LSTM networks are trained via FL while preserving data sovereignty, and are benchmarked against localized and centralized training using standard error metrics. The work addresses privacy-constrained collaborative public health modeling.

entry.title: Which Acoustic Features Survive Compression? Tracker-Estimated First-Formant Statistics for Codec-Robust Audio DeepfakeDetection

author.name: Yash Sukhdeve (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Clarkson University, Potsdam, NY 13699, USA), Aaron Storey (Department of Computer Science, Clarkson University, Potsdam, NY 13699, USA), Masudul H. Imtiaz (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Clarkson University, Potsdam, NY 13699, USA)

entry.summary: The paper screens 36 utterance-level acoustic features for audio deepfake detection under codec degradation, finding that only four first-formant measures retain large practical separation across seven codec conditions. A compact four-feature RBF-SVM degrades far less under codec mismatch than a 36-feature baseline, trading some clean-condition accuracy for robustness.

entry.title: Mapping Instructors' Attitudes Towards Cheating with AI: An Exploratory Analysis Using Forum Analysis

author.name: Iman Mohammadi, Ali Keramati, Sina Rismanchian

entry.summary: Companion exploratory study analyzing 2.01 million r/Professors posts since ChatGPT's release to map university instructors' beliefs and attitudes about cheating with generative AI and academic honesty. It provides an exploratory characterization of the teaching-community discourse around AI-mediated academic integrity.

entry.title: You Are What You Read: Indian Political News Media Bias Dataset for Hindi Language

author.name: Kushal Trivedi, Mayank Mahor, Dhruv Sanghvi, Roshni Chakraborty
