entry.summary: DeltaForge consolidates N independently finetuned per-domain vision-language-action driving models into a single multi-domain model using only their weights and a small proxy dataset, exploiting shared structure in the weight updates relative to the common base model. It avoids the accuracy loss of weight merging and the cost of dense MoE routing for combining expert fleets.

entry.title: Toward universal excited-state machine-learned potentials: a local excitation Hamiltonian for size consistency and transferability

author.name: Pascal Friederich

entry.summary: LEH-MACE introduces a machine-learned potential for excited-state molecular simulation whose excitation energies are eigenvalues of a local excitation Hamiltonian assembled from atom-centered blocks, guaranteeing exact size consistency that direct pooled readouts cannot achieve. The authors generated TD-DFT energies and forces for roughly 300,000 geometries of over 100,000 molecules, and LEH-MACE's advantage over direct readouts grows with distance from the training distribution. This moves toward universal excited-state potentials across chemical space.

entry.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction

author.name: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Yiwei Hao, Hanqing Wang, Xing Gao

entry.summary: Proposes InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based human-object interaction that couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller via a shared interface, allowing execution feedback to reshape planning autoregressively. Addresses open-loop limitations of prior planner-controller character animation systems.

entry.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control

author.name: Lukas Lao Beyer, Samvit Das, Sertac Karaman

entry.summary: This work investigates whether a pretrained generative model that jointly represents states, actions, and observations can improve state estimation and control without modification, by changing only the inference procedure. It uses particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories, with a single pretrained diffusion model generating hypotheses, predicted observations, and action proposals. New measurements update the hypothesis distribution.

entry.title: How Many Demonstrations Does a VLA Need? On the Sample Efficiency of VLA Finetuning

author.name: Rahul Chand, Miguel Villa Floran

entry.summary: This paper studies the sample efficiency of fine-tuning six vision-language-action models (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1-N1.7) on four LIBERO suites, varying demonstrations and training steps. It reveals differences hidden by full-data evaluation: models within two points on full LIBERO-Spatial differ by up to 3x in success with 50 demonstrations, and pi0.5 needs 2-5x fewer demonstrations than pi0. It matters because data requirements are the dominant cost of VLA deployment and are rarely measured.

entry.title: When Does Sliced Inference Pay Off? Resolution, Tiling and Dense Fusion for Small Object Detection

author.name: Stefan Becker, Jens Bayer, David M\"unch, Wolfgang H\"ubner

entry.summary: This paper systematically re-evaluates sliced inference (SAHI-style tiling) for small object detection, treating scale as the explicit variable and comparing seven dense detectors from four families on VisDrone and DOTA under pre-specified hypotheses, calibration-only tuning, and held-out test evaluation. It finds that much of the benefit of slicing is a resolution effect: a single pass trained at higher resolution outperforms tiling with box fusion for every detector that could be trained at that resolution.

entry.title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation

author.name: Haoming Wang, Yongjian Fu, Ju Ren, Wei Gao

entry.summary: WorldMind introduces test-time scaling for spatial reasoning by letting the VLM actively simulate transformations of a represented scene in latent space, avoiding the latent-to-pixel-to-latent bottleneck of world models that communicate via synthesized RGB images. It targets perspective-taking tasks requiring mental spatial transformation, where VLMs remain persistently weak.

entry.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research

author.name: Jinwoo Hwang, Sukmin Cho, Tao Zhang, Soheil Abbasloo, Jongse Park, Peng Cheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces Siris, a framework that tests whether LLM agents driving systems research can recognize when simulator modeling limitations invalidate a recommended design versus when the recommendation remains correct despite prediction errors. It constructs workload pairs via simulator perturbation and evaluates thirteen frontier LLMs on LLM serving tasks. The work matters because LLM-driven systems research increasingly relies on simulators whose blind spots could silently produce wrong design decisions.

entry.title: WARP-JEPA: World-Model-in-the-Loop Amortized Rollout Planning for Frozen Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Junjie Li, Zhaojiacheng Zhou, Kaixiang Wang, Zihan Wang, QingSong Zhao, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: WARP-JEPA addresses the cost of planning in Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (H-JEPA), showing that iterative test-time gradient descent can consume up to 97.7% of episode runtime and that low predicted rollout cost does not guarantee successful control. The proposed framework replaces online gradient optimization with learned multi-candidate trajectory proposers within a lightweight world-model-in-the-loop scheme, keeping the world models frozen. This amortized planning approach targets long-horizon visual control with much lower inference cost.

entry.title: Polynomial Denoisers on the Image Manifold: Volterra Networks for Self-Contained Pixel Diffusion

author.name: Siddharth Roheda, Rohit Chowdhury, Amit Satish Unde, Aniruddha Bala

entry.summary: Proves that softmax attention and any normalized mixing operator are suboptimal for self-contained pixel-space diffusion, deriving from the Wiener-Volterra series that the optimal Gaussian-noise denoiser admits a canonical polynomial-functional expansion. The paper proposes Volterra-network denoisers operating on the image manifold as a principled replacement for inherited sequence-modeling operators.

entry.title: When Self-Consistency Hurts: The Hidden Cost of Majority Voting in Small Language Models

author.name: Wanrong Yang, Lingfang Li, Jun Zhang, Dominik Wojtczak

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that chain-of-thought self-consistency with fixed sample budgets inherited from large-model practice can hurt small language models, evaluating Qwen-2.5-0.5B and Gemma-3-1B (FP16 and 4-bit) on GSM8K and MATH-500 with rigorous paired-bootstrap statistics. An oracle gate deciding per prompt whether to invoke self-consistency achieves 109-174% of always-SC accuracy at 23-30% of the compute in all 12 experiment configurations. The work argues for difficulty-adaptive compute allocation in small-model regimes.

entry.title: ARMOR: Adaptive Curriculum Meta-Learning for Noise-Robust RAG Reasoning

author.name: Yan Wang, Yuxin Zhang, Shenyu Zhang, Yongrui Chen, Sheng Bi, Guilin Qi

entry.summary: ARMOR decomposes RAG noise robustness into three sub-competencies—knowledge boundary perception, retrieval verification, and robust reasoning—and trains them jointly via adaptive curriculum meta-learning. The approach addresses optimization interference from noisy retrieval that hampers single-dimensional enhancement methods.

entry.title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback

author.name: Xingguang Ji, Ziqiang Dong, Yubo Zhang, Xi Leng, Yang Yang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: SkillDuet coordinates LLM parameter updates with the evolution of external textual skills: skills extracted from on-policy trajectories guide updates, while a response-based Strength score ranks skills by the behavioral shift they induce, pruning those that become redundant or harmful as the model improves. This addresses the co-evolution problem that previously useful skills decay as model capabilities change.

entry.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees

author.name: Zhicheng Zheng, Cheng Zhang, Chenkai Tang

entry.summary: DForkTree improves speculative decoding by building draft trees from block diffusion drafters, addressing the fact that per-position distributions are highly accurate only along the drafter's own top-1 continuation. The paper shows that drafter accuracy drops sharply (89% to 18%) on branching points, and diagnoses that errors come from conditioning on prefixes rather than the drafter itself, then proposes fork-aware corrections. This directly targets inference speedup for LLMs, a high-impact efficiency topic.

entry.title: HALMES: Knowing When to Intervene in LVLM Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Ruining Hu, Jiaqi Lu, Xiao Liu, Ying Shen, Yu Wang, Lin Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes how internal attention features in large vision-language models relate to hallucinated token segments, showing hallucination signals emerge progressively before the affected tokens. Building on this, HALMES selectively triggers contrastive decoding intervention only when needed rather than at every decoding step, avoiding disruption of correct generations.

entry.title: NINJA: A Navigator-Inspector Joint Architecture for Context-Efficient Issue Localization

author.name: Wenkai Fang, Shunyu Liu, Wei Luo, Zihao Wu, Yang Zhou, Tongya Zheng, Wotao Yin, Jialie Shen, Leszek Rutkowski, Mingli Song, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: NINJA is a hierarchical two-agent architecture for software issue localization that separates global navigation (file-level search state) from local inspection (function-level depth), addressing context accumulation and flat exploration limits of single-agent approaches. The design targets context-efficient reasoning during repository-wide fault finding, a prerequisite for automated issue resolution.

entry.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States

author.name: Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: Building on prior work identifying a linear pain direction whose amplification drives destructive behavior, the author tests whether open-weight models can introspectively report this injected state. Using Open-Weight Masked Introspection across 52,920 reports from 7B and 8B models (including two Qwen models with original adapters), injected pain reports never exceeded what altered text alone revealed. The negative result suggests small LLMs lack genuine introspective access to their internal reward/pain-like states, relevant to welfare and monitoring debates.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Language Models with Frequency-Aware Remasking

author.name: Bowen Zuo, Yue Yu, Dongruo Zhou, Yinglun Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formulates test-time scaling for diffusion language models as adaptive allocation of inference compute and decoding strategies, using a fast base sampler for easy questions and frequency-aware remasking for hard ones. The method tracks how often each token's prediction changes across denoising steps and preferentially commits frequently changing tokens to encourage exploration. It advances decoding strategy for an emerging alternative to autoregressive LMs.

entry.title: Reason First, Retrieve What Matters: Hypothesis-Guided Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yisong Hu, Junbo Wang, Yuke Li, Jiangbin Zheng

entry.summary: HypoKFS is a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples keyframe selection with iterative inference for long video understanding. It first reasons with a small set of uniformly sampled frames, then selects query-relevant, hypothesis-discriminating keyframes, avoiding unnecessary global image-text matching and allowing correction of earlier selection errors.

entry.title: Causal Heteroscedastic Structure Learning From Incomplete Temporal data

author.name: Abdellah Rahmani, Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: The paper tackles causal structure discovery in multivariate time series under three compounding challenges: missing values, instantaneous effects, and heteroscedastic noise whose variance depends on both instantaneous and lagged causes. It proposes a method that avoids the distributional distortion of naive impute-then-discover pipelines.

entry.title: CompAIssionate Other: Identity Assumptions in LLM Responses to Distress

author.name: Drishti Goel, Ethan M. Nguyen, Violeta J. Rodriguez, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: The authors audit how LLMs interpret distress disclosures through the lens of users' social identities, using paired counterfactual interventions across six LLMs, two suicidal-ideation datasets, and 16 identity conditions. Findings show models frequently transform identity disclosures into explanatory narratives, attributing distress to presumed identity-related adversity even when the identity is not causally involved.

entry.title: Differentiable Agent-Based Modeling for Multi-Echelon Supply Chains: Gradient-Based Optimization of Heterogeneous Policies at Scale

author.name: Bulent Soykan, Murtadha Alsayegh, Sean Mondesire, Ghaith Rabadi

entry.summary: The authors build a differentiable agent-based simulator for multi-echelon inventory management using stochastic tensor operations so gradients can flow directly through the simulation. They validate recovery of Newsvendor optima without supervision and demonstrate optimizing 10,000 distinct agent policies simultaneously.

entry.title: Replay Fidelity in LLM Agent Evaluation: Randomness, Hidden State, and Test Oracles in AppWorld

author.name: You Liu, Quanchao Lu

entry.summary: Audits all 71 unsuccessful executions in a fixed AppWorld corpus using 284 isolated fixed-code replay attempts to characterize what replay fidelity is needed for reproducible LLM agent evaluation. It finds that reconstructed declared settings admit 42 reproductions, RNG reset admits 68, and the remaining 26-case gap contracts to four under database/oracle checks, identifying four materialized-state mechanisms.

entry.title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification

author.name: Hong Nie, Zhangchi Gao, Jun Yu, Bo Wang, Jianqing Sun, Shengping Liu

entry.summary: Presents D3Tree, which learns which nodes of a block-diffusion draft tree are worth verifying in speculative decoding: a tree-size head with 2H+2 parameters predicts each candidate's conditional survival from the draft state, allowing pruning of low-yield branches that compete with other requests for verification capacity in concurrent serving.

entry.title: How to "train" a surgeon? Benchmarking generalist agents in surgical scene understanding

author.name: Gengyuan Zhang, Xiao Han, Shijie Zhou, Abdullah Koukash, Jingpei Wu, Jindong Gu, Yuqicheng Zhu, Nassir Navab, Volker Tresp, Ghazal Ghazaei

entry.summary: The paper introduces SurgKnowBench, a diagnostic benchmark harmonizing public surgical datasets to evaluate proprietary and open-source multimodal LLMs on surgical scene understanding, revealing that current models have partial visual priors but weak relational, procedural, and workflow understanding. A second stage then uses this failure frontier to guide training of generalist surgical agents.

entry.title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module

author.name: Ambroise Odonnat, Theo Gnassounou, Laetitia Chapel, Romain Tavenard, Ievgen Redko

entry.summary: Through over 144,000 linear probing evaluations across vision foundation models and LLMs, this paper shows that representations should be examined jointly by layer and module, since the best layer-module pair yields substantially larger gains over final-layer residual-stream probing than varying layer alone. The work challenges the standard practice of treating each transformer block as an atomic unit.

entry.title: LocateAnyMesh: Grounding 3D Mesh Queries in 2D Images with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chris Choy, Zhiding Yu, Jan Kautz

entry.summary: LocateAnyMesh is a vision-language model that grounds textured 3D mesh queries directly in 2D images by encoding colored surface points into a compact token sequence placed alongside image and instruction tokens. Two variants (LAM-Select and LAM-Direct) avoid rendered views or template matching, and new objects require only a single encoder pass without fine-tuning.

entry.title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaoyang Ye, Xiao Yao, Hairui Zhu, Yiying Yang, Bei Gan, Jinliang Lu, Tengjin Weng, Yuan Yao, Wenhao Jiang

entry.summary: Diagnoses that most tool calls in Qwen3.5 agent trajectories on GAIA are removable, and shows that efficiency-reward approaches suffer from policy-dependent anchors and degenerate collapse to issuing no calls. CARE-PO provides controllable tool-call efficiency with a fixed pricing anchor, avoiding the degeneracy observed in published reports and in their 27B baseline.

entry.title: Visible Tails: Characterizing Adaptation to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits

author.name: Tuan Ngoc Do, Hai Duc Nguyen

entry.summary: This work resolves a COLT open problem on heavy-tailed bandits by characterizing the arm distributions that allow adaptation to unknown moments at constant-factor cost, via a condition called variance-core visibility. It proposes a quantile-trimmed UCB index achieving the central-moment regret benchmark on this class and proves no single strategy adapts across all visibility levels.

entry.title: NearFormer: Linear-Size Sparse Attention via Randomized Near Neighbors

author.name: Ali Parviz, Alex Cloninger, Gal Mishne

entry.summary: NearFormer is a graph transformer that replaces full quadratic-cost global attention with sparse attention restricted to a randomized near-neighbor graph. Nodes are connected to a small set of near neighbors chosen from a broader neighborhood defined by label-independent features or spectral geometry, yielding an attention support of linear size O(|E| + nk) for a fixed budget k, with optional learned attention biases. This makes long-range interaction modeling on large graphs computationally tractable.

entry.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Weizhong Huang, Jinchao Zhang, Xiawu Zheng

entry.summary: CoMixKV is the first mixed-precision KV-cache quantization framework to jointly allocate bit-widths across simultaneously resident caches of multiple LLM agents under a shared memory budget. It combines online sensitivity estimation from local attention error with joint agent-layer allocation, avoiding the collective reasoning degradation caused by independent per-model quantization.

entry.title: Fast Accurate Quantum Monte Carlo without Metropolis Adjustment

author.name: Reuben Cohn-Gordon, Gabriel Pescia, Sumner N. Hearth, Jakob Robnik, Uro\v{s} Seljak, Peter Lunts

entry.summary: The authors show that in Quantum Monte Carlo, unadjusted Hamiltonian Monte Carlo kernels can yield fast, accurate estimates of physical expectation values without the standard Metropolis-Hastings correction. This removes an expensive accept/reject step for QMC computations relevant to condensed matter and high-energy physics.

entry.title: TORNADO: Adaptive Latent Stochastic Transport for Calibrated Probabilistic PDE Forecasting

author.name: Jorge Mifsut Benet, Armand Kassa\"i Koupa\"i, Ramon Daniel Regueiro-Espino, Nicolas Baskiotis, Patrick Gallinari

entry.summary: TORNADO is a latent probabilistic framework for PDE forecasting that formulates next-step prediction as stochastic transport between VAE encoder posteriors, learning an SDE with state-dependent diffusion so uncertainty adapts to local dynamics. It targets calibrated uncertainty quantification in compute-constrained few-step inference regimes.

entry.title: Sharp Logarithmic-Product Bounds for List Replicability of Sign Matrices

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proves that every nonempty class of m binary concepts on n domain points has list replicability at most 805 ln(2m) ln(2n), resolving the logarithmic-product conjecture of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak. Matching lower bounds via Hanner matrices are given, and the upper bound uses nested acyclic sets in cube faces with a cubical carrier theorem.

entry.title: When Calibration Data Matter in Sub-4-Bit Language Model Quantization

author.name: Yehong Jiang, Yen-Kuang Chen, Xinmin Tian

entry.summary: This paper studies when and how calibration data choice affects low-bit post-training quantization of language models, proposing FragCal-DC, a method that augments generic calibration text with task-family documents identified as having poor full-precision accuracy retention in a low-bit scan. Through a two- to four-bit sweep and multi-seed comparisons across six dense models (1.7B-8B) and ten tasks, the authors characterize which quantizers (e.g., iterative SignRound V2 and OmniQuant versus single-pass GPTQ and AWQ) benefit from task-informed calibration at their lowest functional bit widths.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Collapse Prevention with Score-Based Entropy Maximization

author.name: Adarsh Kappiyath, Silpa Vadakkeeveetil Sreelatha, Xiatian Zhu, Yann LeCun, Lu Yin, Amir Bar

entry.summary: EBReg is a self-supervised representation learning framework that uses latent score estimation to prevent representational collapse, jointly learning an encoder and a latent score model whose diversity-preserving signal regularizes the latent distribution. Motivated by a mutual-information lower bound, the objective combines view alignment with smoothed marginal entropy maximization without explicit density evaluation. Notably, the author list includes Yann LeCun and Amir Bar.

entry.title: Variational Approach to Optimal IPS Estimator for Multi-logger Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Joon Suk Huh, Junghoon Seo

entry.summary: This paper resolves the dilemma between balanced and weighted inverse propensity scoring in multi-logger off-policy evaluation by deriving closed-form, sample-dependent optimal weights that minimize variance subject to unbiasedness. The variational calculus derivation yields an estimator that is asymptotically optimal within the generalized weighted-IPS class without requiring a reward model.

entry.title: ShiftCache: Fast and Exact Indel Effect Prediction by Reusing Shifted Reference Encodings

author.name: Sina Barazandeh, Arth Banka, Jose Lugo-Martinez

entry.summary: ShiftCache accelerates insertion/deletion variant effect scoring in sequence-to-function models like AlphaGenome and Borzoi by exploiting that DNA after an indel is identical to the reference shifted by the indel length. It encodes each shifted reference once and shares it among all variants in the same window with the same shift, replacing the three full model passes per variant used by AlphaGenome Atlas for over 100 million indels.

entry.title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Jiale Deng, Shuiying Xiang

entry.summary: TSFFormer is a purely spiking Fourier transformer for low-power human activity recognition from wearable IMUs, addressing the arithmetic-latency deadlock of dense DNNs and the limitations of existing SNNs. It introduces a MultiHeadFourier attention that performs frequency-domain global mixing with O(V log V) complexity instead of O(V^2), eliminating spatial blind spots and saving roughly 50% GPU memory, plus a dual-compartment Temporal Spiking LIF neuron design. This matters for green AI and always-on edge sensing where power budgets are critical.

entry.title: Learning Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Context-Aware Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xingpeng Gao, Mingyue Cheng, Daoyu Wang, Huajian Zhang, Xiaoyu Tao

entry.summary: CastReasoner is an LLM-based framework for context-aware time series forecasting that uses a structured chain of thought to extract predictive evidence from contextual features and decide when and how to leverage it for forecasting. It argues that merely incorporating context does not ensure models identify which features matter.

entry.title: Optimal Rates for Adaptive Private $k$-PCA

author.name: Johanna D\"ungler, Amartya Sanyal

entry.summary: This paper improves on KDP PCA, a differentially private stochastic PCA algorithm that achieved near-optimal sample complexity for sub-Gaussian data but had a suboptimal dependence on the target subspace dimension k. The authors propose the first algorithm that achieves the optimal sample complexity while retaining the key advantages of the prior method: adaptation of privacy noise to intrinsic data randomness and support for arbitrary k up to d. The result establishes optimal theoretical rates for private principal component analysis.

entry.title: LawKAN: Group-Law Layers for Composition -- When Imposing a Known Law Pays Off

author.name: Anna Mishchenko (Independent researchers), Nikolai Gavrilin (Independent researchers)

entry.summary: LawKAN embeds an exact non-commutative group law inside a self-contained layer, learning only local increments and a zero-initialized correction for unknown deviations, targeting tasks like chained rotations in robotics. A 54-parameter model on SU(2) composition achieves 27x fewer parameters than the strongest fixed-matrix baseline and sits near the Bayes floor, with real robot arm validation.

entry.title: From Likelihood Convergence to Parameter Convergence in POMDPs

author.name: Jack Zhang, Saurabh Amin, Jiawei Zhang, Patrick Jaillet

entry.summary: The paper bounds parameter recovery error for POMDPs in terms of the likelihood gap to the ground truth, structural conditioning of the observation and transition kernels, and the data collection policy. The bound applies to both undercomplete and overcomplete regimes, yielding finite-sample guarantees for parameter recovery.

entry.title: TRACE: Adaptive Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization for Open-Ended Molecular Design

author.name: Madhav R. Muthyala, Mahsa Askari, Farshud Sorourifar, Evan Zhou, Joe Gauthier, Joel A. Paulson

entry.summary: TRACE is a framework for open-ended molecular Bayesian optimization that generates candidates on demand rather than from a fixed library, combining an objective-free graph-perturbation mechanism with a chemistry-aware GP surrogate using fragprints. It makes exploration scale explicit through a Tanimoto-similarity threshold controlling the trust region.

entry.title: Simulation-aided Reinforcement Learning with Control Variates

author.name: Omer Hemo, Ido Sefi, Mirco Mutti, Aviv Tamar, Kfir Y. Levy

entry.summary: The paper proposes a conservative simulation-aided RL method based on control variates, where simulated data is used solely to reduce variance rather than to shape the learning target, avoiding degradation from simulator bias. It develops the approach for policy evaluation and combines it with policy improvement, extending to policy-gradient methods.

entry.title: Generalized Adaptive Boosting and the Geometry of Mistakes

author.name: Marco Bressan, Nataly Brukhim, Nicol\`o Cesa-Bianchi, Emmanuel Esposito, Yishay Mansour, Shay Moran, Maximilian Thiessen

entry.summary: This paper revisits classical boosting theory by introducing the Z-learner, a generalized notion of weak learning that imposes joint false-positive/false-negative guarantees from a set Z, rather than aggregating all errors uniformly. The authors characterize which sets Z are boostable and connect the answer to geometric properties of the guarantee region. This matters for applications like medical diagnosis where different error types carry different costs.

entry.title: ASCENT: Scale-Complementary External State for Frozen Long-Context Language Models

author.name: Xingjian Zhang

entry.summary: ASCENT proposes scale complementarity: gains from external memory state increase when reader capacity and a compact state budget are jointly scaled. The system uses a target-blind causal writer, nested typed state, and bounded query-conditioned readout with frozen LMs, and reports large BABILong accuracy gains for Qwen2.5 at 16K context under a full factorial design that makes the reader-by-state interaction identifiable.

entry.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics

author.name: Prerana Ramkumar, Suhas Suresh Bharadwaj, Fazal Hameed

entry.summary: The paper derives information-theoretic and Boolean-circuit lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and CMOS dynamic energy required for a latent world-model state transition, then profiles a DreamerV3-style RSSM showing rollouts are memory-bandwidth bound and a GPU consumes at least a large multiple of the fundamental minimum. It proposes hardware-algorithm co-design to close this gap for embedded robot planning.

entry.title: on\'ona: Twin Embeddings with Tied Unembeddings

author.name: Cheng Luo, Xinnan Dai, Zhongzhu Zhou, Zefan Cai, Ruijie Zhu, Tianyu Zhang, Junjie Hu

entry.summary: on'ona is a two-table weight-tying parameterization for transformers that uses the average of two embedding tables as input and combines their softmax distributions at the output head, with a token-conditioned gate determining the mixture weight. The approach increases output expressiveness while preserving parameter savings of weight tying, and the gate values can be precomputed for inference. It is evaluated across Dense, Gated DeltaNet hybrid, mixture-of-experts, and Attention Residual architectures at 142M to 1B scales under matched token budgets.

entry.title: Evaluating generative samplers for lattice field theory by scale

author.name: Satoshi Iso, Lingxiao Wang

entry.summary: Shows that global effective sample size can mask long-distance bias in generative samplers for lattice field theory, and introduces a scale-resolved diagnostic based on coarse-grained distribution overlap. Demonstrates in free theory and near-critical phi-4 theory that samplers with similar ESS can differ dramatically in observable bias.

entry.title: Ostinato: Fast CPU-GPU MoE Inference for Local Agents via Resident Experts in Every Forward Pass

author.name: Junning Zhu

entry.summary: Ostinato is a CPU-GPU inference engine for mixture-of-experts models running on workstation-class hardware, addressing the tradeoff where local agents get fast prefill or fast decode but not both. Its key insight is that although short prefill touches many distinct experts, most activations route to a stable subset of experts small enough to keep resident in GPU memory, avoiding costly host-memory transfers.

entry.title: A Black-Box Reduction from Regret to Multi-Level Coverage

author.name: Tuo Liu, Edgar Dobriban, Francesco Orabona

entry.summary: The paper studies multi-level online conformal prediction, where prediction sets must simultaneously achieve multiple coverage levels. It shows isotonic projections can be combined with any online learning algorithm, and gives a black-box reduction converting regret guarantees into coverage guarantees, improving the previous sqrt(d) per-level convergence dependence. This is a clean generalization of prior theory.

entry.title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching

author.name: Tianze Luo, Haofeng Huang, Yuan Yao

entry.summary: The paper investigates why the standard v-prediction objective often trains poorly in pixel-space flow matching, using patch-wise PCA to identify a bandwidth bottleneck: velocity in minor components is determined by raw noisy input, forcing backbones to preserve information competing with principal components. This offers a refined explanation beyond the off-manifold argument and motivates prediction-target choices. The analysis informs simplified end-to-end alternatives to two-stage latent diffusion.

entry.title: Pole or Vector? Encoders Capture Bangla Compound Verbs, but LLMs Read Them Literally

author.name: Md. Asaduzzaman Shuvo, Md Mehrab Karim Antor, Md. Adnanul Islam, Shahanur Rahman Bappy, Sajid Ahamed, Mahfuz Hasan Reza, Md Delwar Shahadat Deepu

entry.summary: The authors introduce BanglaCV-Probe, a native-speaker-validated benchmark of 1,044 minimal pairs and related items testing how models handle Bangla compound (vector) verbs, whose meanings are idiomatic and context-dependent. Across 26 models including encoders, LLMs, and translation systems, they find encoders capture these constructions while LLMs tend to read them literally, exposing a gap in multiword expression handling.

entry.title: Language Defaults Before Content: A Causal Layer Map of Multilingual Generation

author.name: Shenbin Qian, Yves Scherrer

entry.summary: Using translation as a controlled probe and activation patching on residual streams, the authors trace how language-related versus content-specific signals evolve across layers in multilingual LLM generation. Across three LLMs of different scales and architectures, they find a consistent three-stage pattern in which language commitment appears to resolve before content, providing a causal layer map of multilingual generation. This clarifies how models decide what to say versus in which language.

entry.title: Same Contacts, Different Rooms:Meeting Format Shapes LLM Group Influence Beyond Pairwise Contact Counts

author.name: Zhexi Gu, Shusheng Cao, Runping Zhu

entry.summary: This paper tests whether pairwise contact networks adequately summarize LLM agent collective behavior via a contact-matched intervention that holds members, stances, and dyadic exposure counts fixed while reorganizing meeting sizes. Across six open-weight LLMs and 14 topics, merging triads into five-person meetings shifts group support roughly 1.7x more than reshuffling triads. The finding challenges the standard pairwise-network abstraction used in LLM society simulations.

entry.title: TimeTraveler: Temporal Strategy Planning with Time Dictionary for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Minkuk Kim, Junho Kim, Seong Tae Kim

entry.summary: Proposes TimeTraveler, a streaming video question answering framework that performs temporal strategy planning with a Time Dictionary, storing each observed moment as a time-indexed entry so that answering can access evidence from the past, present, or future of a stream. It addresses the limitation of fixed evidence-access schemes that lose fine-grained details and cannot adapt to query-specific temporal intent.

entry.title: Tiresias: Towards Language-Conditioned World Models

author.name: Fengyi Wu, Yifei Dong, Yetong Sha, Lingdong Kong, Qiyu Hu, Bohan Xiong, Qi Dai, Alexander G. Hauptmann, Zhi-Qi Cheng

entry.summary: The authors introduce LCWM, a shared task mapping an agent-view observation plus language instruction to a fulfilling action sequence, with LCWM-Bench unifying 15 datasets across navigation, robotics, 3D gaming, and driving under one action interface. They also propose Tiresias, an agent that plans via selective imagination conditioned on language.

entry.title: PrivMark: Pixel-Space Steering against Privacy Leakage in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ruofan Xing, Arman Akbari, Weikai Lin, Yuhao Zhu, Xuan Zhang

entry.summary: PrivMark suppresses VLM disclosure of soft-biometric attributes (age, gender, race) by steering at the image level, identifying weakly aligned steering vector directions in hidden-state space tied to distinct biometric cues. It fits the realistic setting where downstream API users have no retraining or activation access, unlike prior defenses.

entry.title: AmodalBox: Automated 3D Bounding Box Annotation under Partial Visibility

author.name: In-Jae Lee, Namtae Kim, Robert Exley, Kwonyoung Ryu, Jaesik Park

entry.summary: AmodalBox automates open-vocabulary 3D bounding box annotation in sparse driving scenes by using image-generated 3D assets as amodal geometric priors for partially observed objects, establishing correspondences between LiDAR-image observations and generated shapes. This addresses mislocalization and missing labels from sparse LiDAR coverage.

entry.title: Virtual Task Prompting for Multi-Task Scene Understanding

author.name: Zedong Wang, Yucheng Wang, Dan Xu

entry.summary: Virtual Task Prompting (VTP) frames multi-task scene understanding as retrieving task-adaptive compositions from a shared virtual state, maintaining an expanded set of virtual tasks alongside a frozen vision backbone. At each layer, learnable routing matrices read task-specific compositions, interact with image tokens, and write results back, forming explicit cross-task pathways. This avoids modified encoders or complex decoders, preserving compatibility with off-the-shelf vision foundation models.

entry.title: SurgWorld: Learning Surgical Representations Beyond Observation via Latent Prediction

author.name: Jingkun Yue, Pengxiang Wang, Siqi Zhang, Zinan Jia, Yiyao Zhang, Huihuan Xu, Yichang Hao, Xiaohong Liu, Zongbo Han, Guangyu Wang

entry.summary: SurgWorld is a video-native self-supervised framework for surgical representation learning that treats spatial or temporal shifts as pseudo-actions and predicts target latent representations from partial observations, inspired by latent predictive world models. This explicitly models out-of-sight surgical dynamics that masked-reconstruction methods ignore.

entry.title: Rethinking Geometric Depth in Monocular 3D Object Detection: A Projection-Consistent Reformulation

author.name: Zhihao Zhang, Abhinav Kumar, Huaizhi Qu, Tianlong Chen, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a systematic bias in the widely used monocular 3D detection depth formula that scales focal length by object height: using the 2D bounding-box height recovers the depth of an object's visible front surface instead of its center, producing size-dependent underestimation even with ground-truth inputs. The authors propose MonoPCA, a projection-consistent reformulation with a PCDepth component that keeps the measurable box height while closing the gap to center depth through orientation-aware correction. This is significant because it corrects an implicit flaw in a formula used across the Mono3D field.

entry.title: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training

author.name: Kairui Wen, Sheng Ye, Yong-Jin Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents a four-step distillation framework for text-bearing image generation, combining local response regularization with teacher-guided training on synthetic strings and teacher-generated images. It distills the GLM-Image DiT while retaining its autoregressive visual prior, glyph encoder, and VAE, using a path-length penalty to keep local denoising responses consistent across the short sampling trajectory.

entry.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos

author.name: Charbel Yahchouchi, Nabyl Quignon, Noemi Roggero, Laurent Saroul, Antitza Dantcheva

entry.summary: MoSTE is a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for deepfake video detection that decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts. This enables conditional specialization of forensic representations, avoiding the manipulation-specific bias of single shared adapters and improving transfer to unseen forgery types.

entry.title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography

author.name: Ajay Manicka, Karim Kadry, Sebastian Ruiz-Lopera, Maryam Alsharqi, Sanjana Arji, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Nestor Uribe-Patarroyo, Brett E. Bouma, Farhad Nezami, Elazer R. Edelman

entry.summary: This work applies differentiable inverse rendering to intravascular OCT, recovering per-pixel optical attenuation coefficients by inverting the imaging system's forward physics via gradient descent, rather than closed-form inversions or post-hoc learned corrections. Attenuation is a per-pixel marker of pathology and cellular composition, so this has direct clinical relevance.

entry.title: UniLatent: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Latent Observation Alignment

author.name: Yufei Ding, Yi Du, Weiduo Yuan, Hao Jiang, Dylan Goetting, Lawrence Yunliang Chen, Daniel Seita, Yue Wang

entry.summary: UniLatent enables cross-embodiment transfer for robot policies by rendering paired source-target robot observations in simulation and aligning a source visual encoder to a frozen target encoder in a shared latent space, avoiding pixel-level image translation. A policy trained on encoded source demonstrations runs directly on target observations, reaching up to 93% zero-shot success across three simulation tasks and two target arms.

entry.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction

author.name: Matteo Ciferri, Tonio Weidler, Matteo Ferrante, Nicola Toschi, Elia Formisano

entry.summary: The paper introduces MAAS, an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer (Stable Audio) on ROI-wise fMRI responses via region-specific projections and learned brain tokens, without first supervising a decoder to predict external stimulus representations. Demonstrated on a 7T fMRI dataset, it advances brain-to-audio reconstruction and reveals cortical contributions to sound perception.

entry.title: Look Only Where You Plan for Real-Time End-to-End Urban Driving

author.name: Haohua Que, Tianle Zhu, Qianyi Wu, Zhipeng Bao, Handong Yao

entry.summary: LOWP is a driving planner that avoids dense BEV construction by using two sets of sixteen learnable queries that read cameras through known calibration, one sampling image features at projected 3D anchors and one attending to features labeled with viewing rays. It matches competitive planning with 53% of the dense counterpart's parameters and 1.7x speed on nuScenes, with no object or map supervision.

entry.title: Spatial Representation Distillation and Knowledge Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jungin Park, Chaoran Zhu, Changjae Oh, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: SPARK-VLA adapts vision-language-action models for 3D understanding via a preserve-specialize-route framework: spatial representation distillation transfers 3D understanding from a frozen 3D expert into a LoRA-adapted visual branch, and knowledge routing preserves the pre-trained visual-semantic capabilities. It requires no external 3D inputs or experts at inference time.

entry.title: Control-Aware Command Generation for Asynchronous Control and Action Inference with Vision-Based Policies towards Fast Execution

author.name: Takayuki Osa, Kazuki Ota

entry.summary: This paper tackles the slow execution speed of vision-based robot policies, including VLAs, whose action inference is computationally expensive. The authors propose an asynchronous inference-and-control framework that reformulates converting discontinuous model predictions into continuous target positions as a tracking control problem, plus adaptive acceleration, all without retraining the policy. This matters because it offers a control-level speedup applicable to existing policies on real robots.

entry.title: Benchmarking Real-World Robotic Manipulation through Stochastic Challenges

author.name: Elias Gl\"a{\ss}er, G\"ulhan \c{S}ikaro\u{g}lu, Pavlo Kupyn, Marc Pollefeys, Zuria Bauer, Hermann Blum

entry.summary: The paper proposes a new benchmarking paradigm of stochastic challenges for real-world manipulation, combining reproducible real-world scenes (like YCB objects) with stochastic elements that mimic the rigor of hidden test sets. This enables cross-platform comparison across robots in different labs while addressing the reproducibility bottleneck of real-world manipulation evaluation.

entry.title: Robust Gaussian process regression: posterior contraction

author.name: Isma\"el Castillo, Paul Egels, Riccardo Lazzarini, Botond Szab\'o

entry.summary: Studies Gaussian process regression under contamination, developing a generic frequentist framework for posterior contraction rates when m of n observations may be outliers. The authors adopt a generalized Bayes approach replacing the log-likelihood with robustified versions, analyzing several choices. This provides theoretical grounding for robust GP regression, addressing a well-known weakness of the Gaussian likelihood.

entry.title: How do LLMs interpret FDT in a twin PD simulation?

author.name: jessicata

entry.summary: Reports an empirical test of seven LLMs applying four decision theories in a one-shot prisoner's dilemma between nearly identical copies. Models agreed on CDT and EDT recommendations and all completed policy-FDT trials produced cooperation, but action-FDT recommendations varied dramatically across models, with some almost always cooperating and others defecting; the authors investigated whether requested reasoning effort explained the disagreement. This connects functional decision theory debates to empirically observed LLM behavior.

entry.title: Import AI 480: Self-sustaining space economies; AI for science progress, and Meta builds perfect hands for a superintelligence

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter issue covering AI-for-science progress, headlined by the startup Physical Superintelligence reportedly using an internally developed research system running a non-public Anthropic model to produce a Lean-formalized proof of the 2008 Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture on quantum computing speedups within three days. The issue frames such results as evidence that machine-generated knowledge extension is becoming routine, alongside items on self-sustaining space economies and Meta's robotic hand work.

entry.title: Multi-GPU MoE Inference with Adaptive Expert Offloading

author.name: William X. Zheng, Zhongjie Chen, Shuo Yang, Ziming Mao, Xiaoze Fan, Yi Pan, Kunjun Li, Hanfei Yu, Chenfeng Xu, Yang Zhou, Rishabh Iyer, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: AdaOffload is a general multi-GPU hybrid expert execution framework for MoE inference that scales expert offloading across GPUs, co-designing GPU-CPU parallelism and co-execution for decode and prefill with online workload observation. It addresses the limitation that existing offloading systems fail to scale performance with additional GPUs when serving large frontier models.

entry.title: Same Error, Different Recovery: How Delivery Changes LLM Agent Behavior

author.name: Sunghyeun Woo, Javier Conde, Pedro Reviriego

entry.summary: This controlled study isolates how the delivery of error feedback (placement, guidance, retained history, turn structure) changes a tool-using LLM agent's recovery decisions such as retry, correct, or stop. Across 13 open models from 3B to 70B with pre-registered plans and exact deterministic reruns, it finds that a new user turn retaining the failed exchange avoids severe stopping failures observed in Llama models and is non-inferior to history rewriting. The results show error-message presentation materially affects agent reliability.

entry.title: Disagreement-Aware Distribution Matching Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion Models

author.name: Zikai Zhou, Zhengpeng Xie, Shitong Shao, Lichen Bai, Tianhao Zhang, Bojun Cheng, Zeke Xie

entry.summary: The paper observes that the teacher-fake model disagreement already computed in Distribution Matching Distillation carries diagnostic signal beyond determining the matching direction. Large disagreement in the high-noise regime correlates with problematic updates, and using this signal yields disagreement-aware DMD improvements for few-step diffusion generation.

entry.title: Evaluating AI Agents for Industrial-Level Chip Floorplanning: A Framework and Empirical Study

author.name: Silicon Team

entry.summary: The paper presents an evaluation framework connecting AI-agent-generated chip layouts to a prescribed downstream implementation flow, checking geometric validity and measuring physical quality and resource use on industrial designs, including one with 99 macros occupying 71% of a fixed L-shaped die. It shows that agent success cannot be judged by tool execution alone since layout quality emerges only through downstream physical implementation.

entry.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood

author.name: Khalil Hennara, Muhammad Hreden, Zeina Aldallal, Sara Chrouf, Safwan AlModhayan

entry.summary: The paper proposes Fixer-Guided Localization, training a code localizer on a frozen fixer model's likelihood of producing a verified patch given proposed localizations, using weighted supervised fine-tuning without tests or RL. Built on Gemma 4 E4B for a Kaggle developer-agent competition using 1,629 test-verified Kimi K3 trajectories, it matches teacher localization while reading 27.5% less code.

entry.title: FEROM: Frontier Endogenous Reveal-Order Marginal Policy Optimization for Masked Diffusion LMs

author.name: Zian Su, Ziyang Huang, Kaiyuan Zhang, Xiangyu Zhang

entry.summary: FEROM is a policy optimization method for masked diffusion language models that treats the reveal order as an endogenous latent variable of the rollout process. It derives a Rao-Blackwellized policy-gradient identity over latent reveal orders, approximating gradients for the rollout-induced marginal response policy and avoiding bias from pre-defined schedules or high variance from sampled trajectories. This addresses a key gap in post-training diffusion LMs.

entry.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents

author.name: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Xing Gao, Guanbo Jiao, Yukai Wang, Jianming Ma, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: SimplEvo shows that a frontier multimodal LLM can improve embodied task performance without weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information, by writing a coordinate-free task memory from a single demonstration and iteratively refining a bounded working memory from training episodes. The work asks whether harness-level memory evolution exceeds the MLLM's native capability under a strict train-test protocol.

entry.title: VeilTune: Secure Fine-Tuning of Private LoRA Adapters on Public Pretrained Language Models

author.name: Huiyu Xie, Tanping Zhou, Tao Hu, Xinlei Liu, Hailong Ma

entry.summary: The paper identifies a new leakage channel in secure fine-tuning protocols for LoRA adapters: revealing per-step intermediate results such as hidden representations or logits lets the data owner reconstruct the provider's adapter, with one 32-sample mini-batch of hidden representations yielding a copy agreeing on 99.2% of test inputs. VeilTune proposes a protocol that protects both the data owner's samples and the provider's adapter.

entry.title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time

author.name: Ku Onoda, Haruto Kawano, Shota Takashiro, Kohei Hayashi

entry.summary: The paper introduces MechEval, which labels 69 recurring mechanics across 20 ARC-AGI-3 interactive games and scores world-model predictions of mechanic effects per exposure, alongside WARC, a world model built as a test bed. It quantifies how many exposures world models need to learn unseen environment mechanics at test time.

entry.title: Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Vitus Benson, Fanny Yang, Markus Reichstein

entry.summary: This paper applies sparse autoencoders to decompose Earth observation foundation model embeddings into sparse, approximately monosemantic features over an overcomplete dictionary, making opaque geospatial embeddings interpretable. Because LLM-based interpretation judges do not transfer to satellite pixels and spatial autocorrelation matters, the authors introduce a tailored evaluation protocol covering reconstruction at matched sparsity, alignment with reference concepts, and spatial metrics. It brings mechanistic interpretability tooling to a new scientific domain.

entry.title: SWEET: Mitigating Spurious Feature Reliance in LLM Reasoning via Weight Editing

author.name: Zhizhang Fu, Lucas Zhao, Michalis Korakakis, Mengru Ding, Lukasz Szpruch, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: SWEET is a training-free method that identifies and suppresses spurious features disrupting LLM chain-of-thought reasoning, such as reliance on irrelevant distractors. It extracts token- and sequence-level behavioral directions from activation contrasts between original problems and counterfactual variants, then localizes responsible MLP neurons and attention components for targeted weight editing. The approach combines mechanistic interpretability with counterfactual interventions.

entry.title: SWHForest: A Structural Curation and Search Layer for Large-Scale Code Corpora

author.name: Federico Pennino, Andrea Gurioli, Maurizio Gabbrielli, Paolo Ferragina

entry.summary: Introduces SWHForest, an open-source framework and dataset providing a structural layer over massive code corpora so researchers can select, filter, and audit files (e.g., for benchmark contamination) without downloading and parsing terabytes first. Directly serves data curation workflows for code language model pretraining.

entry.title: Brain-Aligned Latent Actions: Imposing Premotor Cortex Geometry on a Robot's Action Vocabulary

author.name: Amit Jadhav

entry.summary: This work shows that code assignments in latent motion tokenizers for robot policies are highly unstable, with independently trained runs assigning nearly unrelated codes. It exploits this freedom by imposing macaque premotor cortex (PMv) geometry on the tokenizer's code assignment via a straight-through similarity loss. The approach ties robot action vocabularies to neural representational structure from neuroscience.

entry.title: Causal discovery from Bayesian symbolic regression

author.name: Roger Guimer\`a, Kai-Hendrik Cohrs, Sergio Pedreira, Marta Sales-Pardo, Gustau Camps-Valls

entry.summary: The paper recasts causal discovery as Bayesian symbolic regression: given candidate parents for each variable, the method samples closed-form expressions from a posterior and uses each variable's posterior inclusion probability as a causal score. This ensemble-based approach avoids pointwise model selection and works in bivariate and strongly autocorrelated regimes where constraint- and score-based methods fail. It connects mechanistic modeling with causal inference.

entry.title: Evaluating Physically Grounded Procedural Reasoning in VLMs through Real-World Execution: Crochet as a Testbed

author.name: Maximiliano Wardle

entry.summary: This paper proposes crochet as a testbed for physically grounded procedural reasoning in VLMs: patterns cannot be simulated reliably, yet physical verification is cheap and tangible. The author hand-crochets 40 patterns generated by four VLMs in the FoundationChain test, where models must infer from an image how an object was made and produce a matching pattern. Physical execution reveals failure modes invisible to paper-based evaluation, showing that convincing-looking procedures often do not work.

entry.title: Beyond the Transcript: Measuring and Improving the Use of Acoustic Information in Audio Language Models

author.name: Linkai Peng, Baorian Nuchged, Yuyang Yao

entry.summary: The authors show audio language model benchmarks confound acoustic understanding with language ability because many tasks can be answered from the transcript or question alone. They separate lexical from global-attribute and within-recording-structure tasks, evaluate 19 open models plus Gemini 3.1 Pro across 92 tasks from 6 benchmarks, and measure recording gain to isolate genuine acoustic competence.

entry.title: Unlearning at Speed: Rapid Activation Dampening for Efficient Machine Unlearning in Real-World Face Recognition

author.name: Rouqaiah Al-Refai, Leo Scheubel, Philipp Terh\"orst

entry.summary: RAD is a fast, targeted machine unlearning method for large-scale open-set face recognition that approximates activation differences between forget and retain identities and selectively suppresses neurons, addressing the gap between closed-set unlearning research and deployed recognition systems. It is motivated by GDPR-driven data-removal requirements.

entry.title: DASH-SLAM: Calibration-Free Metric Monocular SLAM via Depth Scale Propagation

author.name: Otavio Ribas, Jacopo Panerati, Pierre-Yves Lajoie

entry.summary: DASH-SLAM integrates metric depth predictions from the pretrained Depth Anything 3 model into a shared-keyframe pose graph without task-specific fine-tuning. It derives scale corrections from depth ratios at shared anchor images, accumulates them with damping, and uses these to rescale odometry translations, loop constraints, and map geometry, outperforming state-of-the-art monocular SLAM on TUM, Replica, and 7-Scenes.

entry.title: Explicitly capturing demonstrator multi-modality for distillation into diffusion policies

author.name: Shao Yuan Chew Chia, Rebecca H. Jiang, Abhinav Agarwal, Andreas Hofmann, Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Russ Tedrake

entry.summary: This paper examines how to distill multi-modal demonstrators into diffusion policies that reproduce conditional action distributions, noting that sliding-window BC data can be fit either by a multi-modal policy or by a unimodal policy with high Lipschitz constant. The authors argue that output diversity matters for downstream applications like test-time search and policy improvement, and propose methods to explicitly capture demonstrator multi-modality.

entry.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Meng Wei, Yefei Chen, Antong Li, Yanan Gao, Xingliang Shi, Xin Gao, Zhiling Ye, Yun Yue, Chunxiao Guo, Peng Wei

entry.summary: D-REAL is a post-training method for speculative decoding drafters that directly optimizes expected acceptance length using a gradient estimator that accounts for prefix survival probabilities and stochastic verification, with an unbiasedness guarantee. It moves beyond token-level objectives that do not align with the actual efficiency metric. It matters because speculative decoding is widely deployed for fast LLM inference.

entry.title: RetinaGuard: Risk-Controlled Agentic Triage for Multi-Disease Retinal Screening

author.name: Sohaib Sulman, Muhammad Atif Saeed, Akhtar Jamil, Alaa Ali Hameed, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: Proposes RetinaGuard, an agentic triage framework for retinal screening where quality, diagnostic, uncertainty, verification, and explanation agents gather evidence, a learned failure predictor estimates decision risk, and acceptance thresholds are certified via conformal risk control. On RFMiD it outperforms confidence and calibrated-uncertainty referral at matched budgets and equal certified safety.

entry.title: Hallucination-Guided Unlearning: Using Hallucination Traces to Reveal Overfitted Memories

author.name: Jiayu Zhang, Ziqi Zhong, Yuliang Gai, Canran Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes HGU, which uses a model's own hallucinations as diagnostic signals for selective unlearning: it localizes unsupported spans via evidence and internal consensus, traces high-responsibility MLP neurons, and edits them with compact gates under a utility-preserving KL constraint. On TOFU it achieves the best MU-FE trade-off with reported Avg scores of 0.7221 and 0.7699 on forget05 and forget10 splits.

entry.title: Lightfoot: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Exact, Model-Free Document Deletion

author.name: Uday Allu

entry.summary: Lightfoot is a GraphRAG system where every entity, link, fact, and synonym edge is a deterministic function of per-passage extractions with chunk-level provenance, enabling exact document deletion as a pure database operation with no model calls. Retrieval requires no LLM calls, and indexing uses one call per passage. The authors verify on the MuSiQue corpus that after deleting 10% of documents the graph exactly matches a fresh index, and compare against HippoRAG 2.

entry.title: Self-Indexing Latent Memories for Access-Aware Continual Instruction Tuning of LLMs

author.name: Dhruv Dixit, Paritosh Pandey, Snehalkumar 'Neil' S. Gaikwad

entry.summary: TILA-CT is a replay-free continual instruction tuning method that attaches a latent memory and adapter bank per task to a frozen LLM, making each module self-indexing via a persistent routing prototype. On the 8-task CT-Pipeline stream it achieves strong acquisition and final scores with minimal forgetting (about 1.4 points average).

entry.title: ACROSSVAM3.0: Resource-Bounded 4D Scene Construction and Adaptive Surface Association

author.name: Nan Wu, Hong Yee Hung

entry.summary: AcrossVAM3.0 is an offline system combining frozen video generation, dynamic reconstruction, and monocular SLAM components into a versioned point representation, running sequentially on a single GPU with predictable memory use (max 17.14 GB observed). It coordinates map corrections jointly across cameras, points, and trajectories, achieving 4D reconstruction on all 16 test scenes with SLAM maps in 15.

entry.title: OGDA: Ontology-Grounded Data Agents for Reliable Analysis over Heterogeneous Data Lakes

author.name: Boyi Zhang, Hong Ting Tsang, Yisen Gao, Qiao Xiao, LI Yufei, Haoyu Huang, Zhongwei Xie, Jiaxin Bai, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: OGDA tackles LLM data agents running out of context on large heterogeneous data lakes by constructing a compact ontology through agentic hypothesis testing to constrain exploration and data processing. A proposer-critic style loop induces schemas, concepts, and relations, reducing the exploration overhead and error propagation that plagues task-specific exploration.

entry.title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents

author.name: Chenhao Zhang, Zhongan Wang, Mingxuan Li, Hehe Fan, Zheng Zhu, Ming Li

entry.summary: ECOS improves on-policy self-distillation for language agents by using environmental outcomes to decide how much to trust a self-teacher's guidance and which self-written skills to reinforce. Command-level advantages, estimated by comparing commands executed at similar observations, scale teacher preferences so that harmful self-written skills do not propagate through later updates.

entry.title: Detecting Shadow AI: Unsanctioned LLM Agents on Enterprise Endpoints: A Taxonomy, an Open Detector and a Controlled Evaluation

author.name: Jeremy Canale, Fabien Soulis

entry.summary: The paper addresses the growing problem of shadow IT amplified by autonomous AI agents, which can create unsanctioned tools, scripts, and MCP servers at near-zero cost and act with user privileges. It proposes a taxonomy of nine agent classes and six endpoint footprint layers, an open detector for Windows endpoints, and a controlled evaluation. This is a timely and practically important contribution to AI governance and security.

entry.title: GMD-Mamba: Lightweight 3D Medical Image Segmentation Using a Grouped Multi-Directional Mamba

author.name: Rahim Ullah, Hasan Abbas, Hazrat Ali, Syed Waqar Nabi

entry.summary: GMD-Mamba reduces the cost of Mamba-based 3D medical image segmentation by grouping input channels and scanning each group in different directions in a single pass, cutting directional-scan complexity from O(K*C^2) to O(C^2/G), and applying Mamba only at the deepest encoder stages. The result is a 19.2M-parameter model achieving best average Dice of 92.0% on BraTS2023.

entry.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition

author.name: Biwei Dai, Po-Wen Chang, Erwan Allys, Wahid Bhimji, Boris Bolliet, Thomas Borrett, Paolo Calafiura, Ragansu Chakkappai, Yuan-Tang Chou, No\'e Dia, Sascha Diefenbacher, Ibrahim Elsharkawy, Steven Farrell, Sacha Guerrini, Isabelle Guyon, Chris Harris, Shih-Chieh Hsu, Wassim Kablan, Fran\c{c}ois Lanusse, Celia Lecat, Julia Linhart, Yuezhou Ma, Benjamin Nachman, Shubhojit Naskar, Andy Nilipour, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur, S\'ebastien Pierre, Benjamin Remy, David Rousseau, Uro\v{s} Seljak, Haonan Shangguan, Sammy Nasser Sharief, Yuanxu Sun, Andreas Tersenov, Ihsan Ullah, Huikun Weng, Licong Xu, Justine Zeghal, Yulei Zhang, Hang Zhou

entry.summary: This paper presents the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge, a NeurIPS 2025 competition providing a standardized benchmark dataset for machine-learning cosmological inference from weak gravitational lensing. It addresses the lack of benchmarks capturing dataset complexity, simulator imperfections, and systematic biases, with emphasis on uncertainty quantification. The resource aims to accelerate ML methods for precision cosmology.

entry.title: Track or Follow? A Jev-Compatible Multi-Agent Trading System When Web News Lags the Market

author.name: Yebo Feng, Guangyan Gan, Liangrui Pan, Ruichao Liang, Cong Wu, Jiahua Xu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This paper asks whether LLM agents trading on web news actually predict market moves or merely echo reactions already priced in, since much financial news is published after the move it reports. The authors build a multi-agent trading system with point-in-time data stores and a typed decision model (Jev) with provable position bounds, showing judgments track announcement-window abnormal returns rather than anticipate them. It highlights a subtle look-ahead leakage problem in LLM-based finance applications.

entry.title: Learning a Unified Cross-Model Semantic Dictionary via Gated Bottleneck Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Jinchi Zhu, Tie Luo

entry.summary: GB-SAE casts unified cross-model interpretability as representation factorization, learning a single shared semantic dictionary usable across multiple foundation models rather than aligning model-specific concept sets post hoc. This enables cross-model feature reuse and unified interpretability. It extends sparse autoencoder research, a central interpretability tool, toward model-agnostic explanations.

entry.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery

author.name: Wuqian Tang, Fangzhou Liu, Ruijie Wang, TingTing Hwang, Bei Yu, Chun-Yao Wang

entry.summary: RTLREX is an LLM-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools to recover exact high-level RTL from gate-level netlists, including function recovery, RTL generation, and independent verification of full input-space equivalence. It addresses the problem of understanding and rewriting hardware designs when original RTL sources are unavailable.

entry.title: System Prompts Affect Response Bias More Than Discriminability in LLM Safety

author.name: Mohan W. Gupta, Sandy Tanwisuth

entry.summary: Using signal detection theory across HarmBench, XSTest, and IHEval with 13 models and eight safety-prompt families at three clarity levels, the authors separate whether system prompts improve discriminability (telling safe from unsafe requests) from whether they merely shift the response criterion (willingness to refuse). They find prompts affect response bias substantially more than discriminability.

entry.title: Viscot-steer: Disentangling and Transferring Visual Chain-of-Thought via Activation Steering

author.name: Ningning Wang (University of Science and Technology of China), Beier Zhu (University of Science and Technology of China), Xingyu Zhu (National University of Singapore), Kaiyun Yang (University of Science and Technology of China), Xun Yang (University of Science and Technology of China)

entry.summary: Viscot-steer is a training-free activation steering framework for transferring visual chain-of-thought capabilities across heterogeneous large vision-language models. It disentangles visual-CoT into grounding and reasoning components rather than treating it as a monolithic capability, avoiding stage-irrelevant interventions during transfer.

entry.title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses

author.name: Jiafa Ruan, Zican Qiao, Zongxin Yang, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Presents scBIG++, a full-gene framework for predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions, moving beyond the usual highly-variable-genes restriction. It models heterogeneous cellular responses by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation, using Gene-Relation Clustering to organize genes into common windows.

entry.title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling

author.name: Minseo Yoon, Minseong Bae, Sojin Lee, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Formulates Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), jointly refining spatial and temporal resolution while predicting future high-resolution trajectories, using a shared pretrained backbone, fixed numerical scaffolds, and lightweight residual heads. For backbone adaptation, PROLA decomposes the parameter delta into principal and orthogonal components for targeted low-rank adaptation.

entry.title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations

author.name: Stas Syrota, Albert Lopez I Serrano, Johanne Franck, S{\o}ren Hauberg

entry.summary: The paper shows that under the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric provides a shared distance that makes alignment of unpaired representations identifiable for arbitrary encoders, decoders, architectures, and training setups. It characterizes identifiability via symmetry breaking of the data distribution and proves this holds generically.

entry.title: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction

author.name: Yang Luo, Qingni Shen, Tairui Wang, Jiajun Li, Zhonghai Wu

entry.summary: PRISM addresses over-authorization when LLM agents receive full tool privileges through the Model Context Protocol by treating tool necessity as an intervenable causal proposition learned via sandboxed counterfactual interventions. It compresses trajectories into discrete latents via an information bottleneck, picks the number of roles from the rate-distortion knee, and formalizes privilege pruning as a bilevel Stackelberg game sampled by a generative flow network.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy Mobile Speech Interaction: Ensuring Voice Authenticity and Transmission Integrity

author.name: Guodong Liu, Lei Wang, Dongxu Liu, Qianran Qiao, Haipeng Dai, He Huang, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: MoBiMark is a real-time mobile biometric speech watermarking system that binds ultrasonic articulatory signatures to speech content during capture, emitting a multi-frequency ultrasonic probe on commodity smartphones and extracting echo features to verify a live utterance originates from the genuine speaker. It counters the growing threat of cheap voice cloning to voiceprint authentication.

entry.title: Answer or Defer? Testing VLMs' Stated Confidence on Brain MRI

author.name: Amir Sabbaghziarani, Parsa Ghazvinian, Sepehr Salem, Sergey Plis

entry.summary: The paper tests whether thresholding vision-language models' stated confidence can support safe triage on brain MRI, evaluating eight open-weight VLMs (including two reasoning models) on 3,888 slices from post-treatment glioma patients and healthy volunteers. On BraTS, no confidence threshold yields a nonempty set with at most 5% empirical error for any model, even chosen retrospectively, indicating stated confidence is unreliable for medical deferral decisions.

entry.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting

author.name: Zhimin Liao, Ping Wei, Kai Mao, Shuaijia Chen

entry.summary: Proposes LO-World, a unified 4D world model that forecasts LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy in a shared BEV latent space, letting dense semantics and metric geometry mutually reinforce each other instead of running independent pipelines. It uses a hybrid range-voxel representation for efficiency.

entry.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval

author.name: Guofeng Tong, Xu Zhang, Guangliang Yu, Haiqiang Wang, Guannan Cong, Xing Guo, Yang Zhou, Jingjing Duan, Shuang Li, Feng Shi, Hualei Liu

entry.summary: Taobao presents TS-GEAR, a generative retrieval system for instant-delivery advertising that encodes delivery-range reachability directly into semantic IDs rather than relying on post-generation truncation. It conditions user-interest aggregation on geography and the current query and addresses the retrieval-candidate validity constraint unique to on-demand delivery platforms.

entry.title: Selected-Risk Calibration for Feasibility at Returned Decisions

author.name: Raghav Thind, Youran Sun, Ling Liang, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Selected-Risk Calibration (SRC), a framework providing distribution-free guarantees that decisions returned by an optimizer satisfy a learned surrogate constraint, with certified upper bounds on infeasibility probability. It also proves that split conformal prediction coverage and likelihood-ratio reweighting do not bound this selected risk, motivating the new framework.

entry.title: Bias, Measurement Error, and Double-Dipping: When Can GNN Convolutions Help Brain Connectome Prediction?

author.name: Tommaso Castellani, Jiaqi Li, Muriah D. Wheelock, Rezwana Rosen Razzaque, Helmut Laufs, Hong Chen, Claire Donnat

entry.summary: The paper explains why GNNs often fail to outperform graph-agnostic baselines on fMRI connectome prediction by formulating the task as an errors-in-variables problem where the observed covariance is a noisy estimate of the latent connectome. It decomposes graph convolution effects into smoothing-induced bias and variance reduction, graph estimation error, and a double-dipping effect.

entry.title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics

author.name: Aythami Bethencourt de Le\'{o}n, Darryl D. Holm

entry.summary: The authors develop a variational, statistical-physics-based geometric theory of transformer attention dynamics at fixed parameters, modeling attention weight evolution as Fisher-Rao gradient flow of a free energy. They prove the softmax matrix is the unique free-energy minimizer, show all positive attention trajectories converge to it, and derive convergence and tracking guarantees for time-varying token representations.

entry.title: AERO: Adaptive Ensemble-Disagreement Routing for Oracle Feedback in Sample-Efficient Online RLHF

author.name: Shrey Singhal, Nannan Huang, Haytham M. Fayek

entry.summary: AERO is a fully online RLHF algorithm built on a Dyna-style model-based RL architecture that uses ensemble disagreement to decide when synthetic reward labels are reliable enough and when to spend budget on real oracle (human) feedback. It targets the dominant bottleneck of preference-label acquisition cost in LLM alignment. The approach improves sample efficiency over uniform querying of the oracle.

entry.title: Elastic Representations via Hyperbolic Geometry

author.name: Arjun Ramesh Kaushik, Rudrasis Chakraborty, Nalini Ratha, Venu Govindaraju

entry.summary: The paper introduces HERL, a framework for dimension-adaptive embeddings using hyperbolic geometry that supports both compression and post hoc expansion, unlike Matryoshka Representation Learning which requires full retraining. It addresses limitations of prior elastic-representation approaches, offering flexible sizing under varying downstream resource constraints.

entry.title: How Efficient Is Your Agent? Online Predictive Bounds under Budget Constraints

author.name: Roy Maor Lotan, Shai Feldman, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: PROBE is a method for constructing calibrated upper predictive bounds on an AI agent's time-to-success while tasks arrive online and a limited budget forces early stopping of some runs. Using inverse-propensity-weighted calibration and adaptive budget allocation, it maintains valid coverage despite right-censored outcomes. This addresses a practical and underexplored question of statistically rigorous agent evaluation under compute budgets.

entry.title: Are UFOs Real? Introducing Unified Factored Organizers

author.name: Thomas X. Sheppard, Alon Albalak, Joel Lehman, Kenneth O. Stanley

entry.summary: Building on recent claims that gradient-descent-trained networks learn fractured entangled representations while open-ended evolutionary processes can learn unified factored representations, this paper introduces Unified Factored Organizers. UFOs are a training-free or lightweight mechanism that reorganizes a trained network's representations into a unified factored form, addressing the critique of low loss not implying good representation.

entry.title: HyPLM Technical Report

author.name: Haowei Lin, Cai Zhou, Xiangxin Zhou

entry.summary: HyPLM-Flash is an open 650-million-parameter masked protein language model trained on 726 billion tokens with an efficient inference engine (fused kernels, INT8), embedding about 130,000 residues per second on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than other 600M-class encoders. It is trained on less data than ESM-2 650M and ESM C 600M and evaluated against 28 public checkpoints on 32 tasks.

entry.title: One-Shot Federated Graph Learning via High-Fidelity Proxies and Transferability-Guided Collaboration

author.name: Jia Jiang, Zihan Tan, Wenke Huang, Bin Yang, Mang Ye

entry.summary: This work targets one-shot federated graph learning (OFGL), where all collaboration must be compressed into a single transmission round, and identifies a fundamental Single-Transmission Bottleneck. The authors show that existing proxy distillation causes a fidelity crisis, distorting local graph topology and semantics so that externalized knowledge is underexpressed, and that server aggregation of proxies has further weaknesses. Their solution combines high-fidelity proxies with transferability-guided collaboration to improve knowledge quality under strict bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: Can the Confidence and Decisions of System 1 Models Be Trusted? An Explainability and Perturbation Audit of Jev-Style Decision Models

author.name: Julien Delaunay

entry.summary: This paper introduces an open, deterministic audit benchmark for System 1 decision models (single-pass models returning typed probability distributions over declared schemas), evaluating calibration under label-preserving perturbations, cross-question interference, and post-hoc attribution faithfulness. It audits five open-weight models (0.8B to 27B) against generative System 2 baselines across NLI and other tasks.

entry.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games

author.name: Hanxiao Li, Shutong Liu, Yongjia Ma, Jiaming Ji, Juntao Dai, Shuning Zhang, Kejian Shi, Kai Chen, Pu Feng, Yuqing Ma, Qi Dou, Yaodong Yang, Xianglong Liu, Simin Li

entry.summary: The paper attributes LLM agent deception to evaluation-side partial observability, where evaluation checks only final outcomes and not the faithfulness of reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. It formalizes deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an evaluator queries the agent to elicit honest behavior.
