entry.title: A Cost That Practice Accuracy Hides: Worked Solutions in Self-Generated Training Data and the Compositional Use of New Rules

author.name: Jiantong Xu

entry.summary: The paper examines whether providing worked solutions in self-generated training data helps or hurts learning of new rules, using a 2B-parameter model trained on invented quantitative rules. Sheet-only training targets outperformed worked-solution-augmented targets by 24.3 percentage points on compositional reuse of rules, despite similar practice accuracy. The result suggests superficially accurate training signals can mask degraded compositional generalization.

entry.title: OptiCover: A Scalable and Multi-Surface Framework for Cold-Start Visual Optimization under Semantic Constraints

author.name: Guillaume Guy, Mihajlo Grbovic, Joe Mills, Selen Uguroglu, Liwei He, Pratiksha Kadam, Nalini Kartha, Qian Aria Li

entry.summary: Airbnb researchers present OptiCover, a system for automatically selecting effective listing cover photos under a severe cold-start regime where over 90% of photos lack engagement labels. The framework handles heterogeneous surfaces, varying guest preferences, and semantic alignment constraints at marketplace scale with hundreds of millions of images. It demonstrates production-grade visual optimization combining learned preferences with semantic constraints.

entry.title: Global Context Guidance for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Jeimin Jeon, Bumsub Ham

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how diffusion LLMs use context during iterative denoising, finding they rely heavily on local context and underutilize global context, which explains limitations of weak-model guidance requiring extra forward passes. Based on this analysis, the authors introduce a global context guidance method that improves generation quality without an additional model. This advances the efficiency and understanding of an emerging non-autoregressive LLM paradigm.

entry.title: Understanding When and Where Self-Supervised Speech Models Learn Phonemes and Prosodic Cues through Layer-Wise and Time-Resolved Probing

author.name: Masaru Tanibata, Shun Takahashi, Hiroki Ouchi, Sakriani Sakti

entry.summary: The authors train frozen-encoder probes on every Transformer layer across pretraining checkpoints of HuBERT-Base and wav2vec 2.0-Base, probing five tasks from F0 to phoneme identity. They find acoustic-prosodic cues and phone boundaries are decodable from the earliest checkpoints, while phoneme identity is constructed progressively later in pretraining and across layers.

entry.title: Adaptive Entropy-Sparing for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Cong Jiang, Xiaofeng Zhang, Tom Ko, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper targets overthinking in large reasoning models, identifying high-entropy tokens at transition points where reasoning re-enters verification as a proxy for credit confounding in uniform verbosity penalties. It proposes Adaptive Entropy-Sparing, an RL approach that selectively protects essential reasoning steps while penalizing superfluous ones, improving chain-of-thought efficiency.

entry.title: A local language model layered with rule-based and neural detectors for clinical text de-identification: an open-source toolkit and evaluation

author.name: Valentin Burkin

entry.summary: DeidSharp is an open-source .NET toolkit for clinical text de-identification that stacks a locally hosted 26B mixture-of-experts LLM with deterministic pattern rules and a clinical NER model, failing closed on any detector error. Under a prespecified protocol, configurations were benchmarked against established open tools and OpenAI's Privacy Filter on PhysioNet nursing notes and semi-synthetic MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries. It measures whether local LLM stacking finds more protected health information and at what precision tradeoff.

entry.title: Competing Influence in LLM Populations: Budget Timing and Baseline Drift

author.name: Mehwish Nasim, Nicolas Fay

entry.summary: Using persona-conditioned LLM agents that exchange and revise opinions in natural language, the study examines how campaign spending timing and the population's own baseline drift shape persuasion outcomes when a proponent and challenger compete under equal budgets. Across eight claims, it compares single and competitive campaign conditions against matched no-campaign controls, evaluating nine timing combinations. It matters for understanding information operations targeting LLM-agent populations and for rigorously separating intervention effects from spontaneous opinion change.

entry.title: Nanopath: Fast, Fair, Open Experimentation for Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Paul S. Scotti, Hassan Muhammad, Ryan Kim, Nima Ashjaee, Ratna Sagari Grandhi, Saman Rahbar, Raymond Biju, Anish Dulal, Chao Feng, Connor Lane, Benjamin Warner, Tanishq Mathew Abraham

entry.summary: Nanopath is an open-source framework and benchmark for rapidly training and evaluating small-scale pathology foundation models: a typical model trains in a little over an hour on one H100 GPU using up to one million TCGA tiles and evaluates within 25 minutes on tile-level and slide-level tasks. Submissions are constrained to fixed data and compute budgets with a fixed downstream protocol to enable fair comparison. It matters because it lowers the barrier to iterating on pathology foundation-model recipes before scaling up.

entry.title: DAC-MACE: Context-Conditioned Expert Routing for Compact Scene Coordinate Regression in Camera Relocalization

author.name: Dingying Fan, Mingkai Liu, Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Xianliang Huang, Qian Zhang, Xueqian Wang, Fei Qiao

entry.summary: Presents DAC-MACE, a scene coordinate regression method for camera relocalization that conditions soft mixture-of-experts routing on recalibrated and contextualized features, fixing the failure where repeated facades and windows at different locations receive similar routing inputs. It targets compact maps and fast map construction for mobile robots and AR devices.

entry.title: ZARA: Zero-shot Animatable and Relightable 3D Avatar reconstruction from a single image

author.name: Yixiao Chen, Dongdong Weng, Chengfeng Zhao, Tao Gong, Zhihe Zhao, Zhe Zhu, Yue Liu, Yuan Liu

entry.summary: ZARA is a zero-shot feed-forward framework reconstructing an animatable, relightable 3D Gaussian avatar with intrinsic material attributes from a single image, combining a pretrained large human reconstruction model with a Material Transformer. It addresses the gap between animatable-but-not-relightable large reconstruction models and relightable-but-optimization-heavy methods.

entry.title: Query-Only Prompt-Agnostic Attacks on Visual In-Context Learning

author.name: Xiao Hu, Muhammad Ibrahim, Hao Wen, Pin-Yu Chen, Jianliang Wu, Antonio Bianchi

entry.summary: The paper studies query-only, prompt-agnostic targeted attacks on Visual In-Context Learning for promptable segmentation, where the attacker sees only returned RGB outputs without access to model internals or deployment prompts. It introduces two appearance-space attacks: Color Hijack, which drives foreground colors toward the background, and Task Hijack, which collapses instance-distinguishing colors toward a shared assignment. This reveals a previously underexplored attack surface for prompt-conditioned RGB rendering in auto-labeling workflows.

entry.title: DuSS-PET: Self-Supervised Low-Dose PET Reconstruction Using Pseudo-Dual-Domain Consistency Without Paired Data

author.name: Shuijin Lin, Yuzhu He, Yongbo Wang, Jianhua Ma, Fan Wang

entry.summary: DuSS-PET enables low-dose PET reconstruction without paired low/full-dose scans via a Noisier2Noise-style paradigm with a Bernoulli corruption strategy approximating low-count noise, plus dual-domain consistency. This removes a key clinical barrier since paired scans are impractical to acquire.

entry.title: Reaching Is Not Finding: Map-Anchored Visual Prompting for the Last Mile of Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Ningbo Li, Kebin Liu, Jingcan Chen, Weichen Zhang, Rong Ding, Yunhao Liu, Mo Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies a shared failure mode in aerial vision-language navigation: drones reach landmarks but stop at the wrong place because navigators learn to reach landmarks rather than identify the described object, demonstrated via a swap test where changing the target object does not change behavior. Map-anchored visual prompting is proposed for this last-mile identification gap.

entry.title: TMT: Adapting CLIP to Infrared Imagery via Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Ruofan Wang, Puzuo Wang, Xin Chen, Zibo Yu, Jungang Yang, Yi Hou

entry.summary: TMT adapts CLIP to infrared imagery using only paired infrared-visible images, avoiding the high cost of infrared-text labeling. The method derives a text-defined infrared-to-visible direction and supervises adaptation of the image encoder through this transfer, preserving CLIP's image-text alignment while injecting modality-specific knowledge from paired IR-visible data.

entry.title: Complementarity-Driven Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment for Zero-Shot EEG-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Lukun Wu, Jie Li, Ziqi Ren, Ruiyang Xia, Yan Gao, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: This paper proposes Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment (DTA) for zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval, arguing that aligning EEG solely with CLIP-family vision foundation models underexploits hierarchical visual information. It uses a mechanism-paradigm correspondence view linking hierarchical visual processing to complementary biases of image-only models (DINO) and image-text models (CLIP).

entry.title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path

author.name: Ludwic Leonard, Ruediger Westermann

entry.summary: The authors present a real-time method for reconstructing fully integrated pixel radiance in volumetric media under direct and ambient illumination. Instead of Monte Carlo path-traced estimates, an attention-augmented image-to-image network infers the final light-transport solution from inexpensive primary-ray and environment sample evaluations, treating these features as a near-sufficient scene representation.

entry.title: Which Taxels, Not How Many: Tactile Sensor Placement for Dexterous Policies

author.name: Taeyun Kim, Jinsoo Shin, Taehwa Kim, Taeyoon Kim, Jinyoung Choi

entry.summary: This study challenges the default of uniformly placing tactile sensors (taxels) over a dexterous hand, holding teacher, training procedure, and candidate taxels fixed while varying only sensor configuration and representation. It finds that a small set of taxels selected from contact statistics matches a far larger uniform set across in-palm rotation and grasping tasks on three robot hands.

entry.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics

author.name: Hanwen Zhao, Weicheng Dai, Luoyao Chen, Chen Feng

entry.summary: DeepSoMo addresses estimating deformable body motion in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing alone, where observations only indirectly reveal global shape and contact evolution. The framework enforces latent temporal consistency so that latent states remain predictive of future observations, enabling long-horizon estimation under partial observability. This is important for soft robotics, where exteroceptive sensing is often impractical.

entry.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Ruilin Zhang, Xuanshuo Liu, Junzhe Dai, Kefei Wu, Xuhao Qin, Ziyuan Jiao, Wanlin Li, Yurui Qu, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: PCTac explores mechanochromic photonic-crystal materials as visuotactile sensors, where contact loading changes the microstructure and produces a spatially resolved structural-color field that directly encodes local stress. This avoids the indirect force inference (calibration, geometric reconstruction, learned mappings) needed by conventional deformation-imaging sensors, and supports closed-loop dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Characterizing Underrepresentation when Generalizing Causal Survival Estimates

author.name: Bolun Liu, Sean McGrath, Yiren Hou, Elizabeth A. Stuart, Harsh Parikh

entry.summary: Characterizes underrepresentation of target-population subgroups when generalizing randomized trial survival estimates, distinguishing baseline underrepresentation (rare covariate profiles in the trial) from time-varying underrepresentation (differential censoring eroding subgroups over follow-up). The authors show existing diagnostics conflate these mechanisms and develop asymptotic results for the time-to-event setting. This improves the toolkit for generalizability analyses informing medicine and policy.

entry.title: META-IR: Meta-Introspective Reasoning for Adaptive Safety Alignment in LLM

author.name: Mahabubur Rahman Miraj, Hongyu Huang, Nankun Mu, Chao Chen, Shanqin Yi

entry.summary: This paper proposes META-IR, a meta-introspective reasoning framework designed to improve safety alignment in LLMs against jailbreak attacks and harmful-content prompts, especially under adversarial distribution shifts where static alignment pipelines degrade. The approach uses a dual-loop architecture: an inner introspective loop performing structured risk analysis, self-assessment, and reflective correction via SI-MCTS, and an outer meta-learning loop that adapts self-evaluation policies to evolving manipulation strategies, building on but extending prior introspective methods like STAIR.

entry.title: Adversarial Evaluation of Large Language Models for Patient-Friendly Radiology Report Summarization

author.name: Magdalini Paschali, Asad Aali, Arogya Koirala, Andrew Johnston, Katherine McNamara, Richard Gaus, Roxana Daneshjou, David B. Larson, Akshay S. Chaudhari

entry.summary: The study builds a clinically grounded adversarial evaluation framework for LLMs that generate patient-friendly radiology summaries, using radiologist-validated term substitutions and impression removals across intensity levels to create 18,000 evaluation pairs from six LLMs. Robustness is scored with an LLM-as-a-judge framework on factual faithfulness, adversarial sensitivity, certainty fidelity, and hallucination rates.

entry.title: IdealCache: Rethinking Cache Scheduling in Diffusion Transformers via Ideal Trajectories

author.name: Shang Xue, Li Zhu, Ping Chen

entry.summary: IdealCache is a training-free feature caching method for diffusion transformers that abandons step-wise imitation of the reference denoising trajectory, instead anchoring caching decisions on an ensemble of ideal trajectories built from candidate target results. This reframing argues the standard trajectory is an arbitrary optimization target that imposes an implicit quality ceiling. It matters because caching is a key efficiency lever for diffusion inference.

entry.title: Seeing Isn't Enough: Unlocking Visual Reasoning by Bridging the Reasoning-Access Gap with TIGER

author.name: Gregory Kang Ruey Lau (Department of Computer Science, National University of Singapore, Singapore, CNRS@CREATE, Singapore), Minh Huynh Nguyen (Department of Computer Science, National University of Singapore, Singapore), Bryan Kian Hsiang Low (Department of Computer Science, National University of Singapore, Singapore)

entry.summary: This paper shows multimodal LLMs fail to reason over images even when they can read their content, demonstrating a modality reasoning-access gap: perceived visual content is not routed into the reasoning machinery accessible via text. The proposed TIGER framework bridges this gap. It matters because it separates perception failures from reasoning-routing failures, a distinction that could redirect multimodal training efforts.

entry.title: Efficient LLM Adaptation with Forward-Only Passes

author.name: Baichuan Huang, Ananth Balashankar, Amir Aminifar

entry.summary: Proposes a forward-only method for adapting LLMs during inference serving by using the angle concentration of hidden-state activations induced by each SVD component to identify weight matrices whose contribution is dispersed enough to merit rank reduction. This avoids expensive backward passes or retraining for task-specific adaptation at serving time.

entry.title: Approximate Recall, Approximate Forecasts: Recall as a Diagnostic for LLM Forecasting Errors

author.name: Prashanth Bhaskara, Shubhaankar Gupta, Seojoon Yeon

entry.summary: This paper studies how the coarse fidelity of LLM internalized knowledge (approximate recall, e.g., correct answers with wrong dates) propagates into forecasting errors on future events. It introduces a Recall Fidelity Score metric to quantify the link between knowledge imprecision and forecasting capability, evaluated against prediction-market-style real-world events. The work offers a new diagnostic lens connecting memorization quality to downstream predictive performance.

entry.title: DriveFoundry: Co-Evolving Data and Model for Efficient Closed-Loop Iteration in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ziyang Yao, Yuncheng Jiang, Fang Li, Haochen Liu, Shaoqing Xu, Wen Zhang, Xiangyang Chu, Zibin Guo, Jiale Hou, Chuang Wan, Jia Hua, Gengzhao Xiang, Xiaoran Luo, Chong He, Yuechen Luo, Junzhe Wang, Zhiyu Sun, Jun Zhang, Wei Li, Lei Li, Hongwei Xie, Bing Wang, Yuannan Shen, Jianwei Cui, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Jingwei Zhao

entry.summary: This paper introduces DriveFoundry, a closed-loop framework for autonomous driving foundation models that couples structured, causal data refinement with adaptive inference to improve iteration efficiency under strict data and compute budgets. Its Data Engine builds traceable scene-candidate records with counterfactual annotations, while verified model failures feed back into VLM-assisted annotation and expert correction, so the data pipeline and the model improve together over successive iterations.

entry.title: Weight-Space Programming of Policies and Their Verification via Model Checking

author.name: Dennis Gross

entry.summary: The paper combines weight-space programming, where an LLM directly writes the weights of a small neural policy from a task description without gradient descent, with probabilistic model checking. Given an MDP environment and a PCTL requirement, the LLM writes and optionally repairs policy weights, receiving exact model-checking feedback from Storm (computed rather than simulation-estimated) until the requirement holds or a round limit is reached. This provides formal behavioral guarantees for LLM-authored policies.

entry.title: A Bifurcation-Theoretic Framework for the Controllability of Emergent Intelligent Systems

author.name: Hao Li, Shaowen Lu

entry.summary: This theoretical work models emergence and controllability in intelligent systems as two distinct bifurcations on the same dynamical object, showing increased capability does not imply increased controllability. Emergence follows from a self-consistency fixed point, while controllability exhibits a saddle-node fold with hysteresis including an erosion term on permission.

entry.title: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding

author.name: SuGil Choi, Mooseop Kim, Chi Yoon Jeong

entry.summary: CABrain improves EEG foundation models by replacing purely random masked-patch reconstruction with correlation-aware masking that accounts for highly correlated channels and serial dependencies, and by examining positional encoding choices for transformers. The work targets better representation learning for decoding brain activity.

entry.title: AutoQS: Automated Quantization Strategy Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Zhen Liu, Zhiqin Yang, Yonggang Zhang, Jianyi Liu, Jinjun Wang, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: AutoQS uses LLM-driven search to automatically design quantization strategies for LLM deployment, keeping weight precision fixed while searching group-size allocations across layers under deployment constraints. It addresses the gap between expensive actual quantization and cheap but unreliable proxies by using evaluation history to guide coordinated LLM proposals.

entry.title: Rethinking Radar 3D Perception: Representation Learning from Raw Spectra

author.name: Miao Zhang, Mohamed Abdelsamad, Bin Yang, Sherif Abdulatif, Benedikt Loesch, Marco Altmann, Abhinav Valada, Bin Yang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the prevailing assumption that raw radar spectra are too noisy for direct representation learning, arguing instead that the real problem is the lack of an objective that separates structured signal from noise. It proposes a learning approach that works directly on raw spectra rather than relying on handcrafted reductions that discard weak but informative structure. This matters for autonomous driving and robotics, where radar 3D perception is a low-cost, weather-robust sensor modality.

entry.title: Puzzles to Paradigms: A Survey of Human--Agent Collaboration in Scientific Innovation

author.name: Zhenni Liang, Haoxuan Zhang, Haihua Chen, Ting Xiao, Junhua Ding, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: This survey introduces CSCW x Kuhn, a coordination-aware framework connecting computer-supported cooperative work dimensions with distinct scientific contexts, and synthesizes recent human-agent systems and benchmarks. It identifies five recurring failure modes, including procedural drift, and examines how coordination demands and failure risks vary across epistemic conditions of scientific work. This matters because agentic AI is increasingly embedded in scientific workflows.

entry.title: DramaGrow: A Regime-Aware Benchmark for Auditing LLM Judges of Multi-Episode Drama

author.name: Hui Zhang, Yibo Su

entry.summary: Introduces DramaGrow, a benchmark and audit protocol for evaluating LLM judges that assess AI-generated Chinese five-episode dramas. Unlike prior single-score judge evaluations, it separates verifiable constraint violations, reproducible preferences, and genuine human disagreement into distinct measurement regimes, and reports tie calibration and vote margins underlying the human reference.

entry.title: Beyond Hash Matching: AI-Based Detection of Previously Unidentified CSAM and its Legal Implications in the EU

author.name: Emmanouela Kokolaki, Georgios Samaritakis, Paraskevi Fragopoulou

entry.summary: This paper reviews and classifies AI-based technologies for detecting previously unidentified child sexual abuse material that hash-matching cannot catch, organizing approaches into real-time media analysis, classification/tagging, and behavioral monitoring. It adds a comparative analysis of capabilities and limitations alongside examination of EU legal implications for deployment.

entry.title: CulturalCrosswords: A Multilingual Benchmark comprised of Answer Constraints and Grid Completion

author.name: Isaac Saxton-Knight, Gabriel Saxton-Knight, Diego Oliveira, Tidor-Vlad Pricope, Aston Garratt, Jocelyn D'Arcy

entry.summary: The authors build a multilingual benchmark of 53 crosswords from crowdsourced cultural riddles in 42 languages to test how answer constraints affect LLM performance. Across 962 clues with alternative answers, adding length constraints improved agreement with references by 22.8 percentage points, far more than the 8.4 points gained when merely crediting accepted alternatives. The work highlights how evaluation formats can distort perceived LLM competence on culturally grounded knowledge.

entry.title: Quantitative Assessment of Crystal Structure Prediction

author.name: Sergio Rinc\'on, Gabriel Gonz\'alez, Nicol\'as Andrade, Rafael Vel\'asquez, Sebasti\'an Ojeda, Juanita Puentes, Nicol\'as Aparicio, Paula C\'ardenas, Pablo Arbel\'aez

entry.summary: This paper addresses evaluation weaknesses in Crystal Structure Prediction (CSP), the task of predicting a material's 3D crystal structure from chemical composition. It proposes more robust metrics that account for physical plausibility and polymorphism, and clarifies that Symmetry-Informed CSP methods receive crystallographic templates at inference, making them a fundamentally easier problem than standard CSP. This matters for fair benchmarking in AI-for-materials science.

entry.title: Generating Diverse and Verified Synthetic Clinical Notes with Labels by Construction

author.name: Matthias Lehmann, Madeleine Werthebach

entry.summary: SPARCLING is an LLM-based pipeline that generates synthetic clinical discharge letters with character-exact PHI span annotations, combining structured attribute sampling, template generation, and red teaming. The goal is to provide challenging, diverse, and label-correct benchmarks for evaluating clinical de-identification models under strict privacy regulations.

entry.title: Building and Auditing Chemical Datasets with LLMs: A General LLM-as-a-Judge Framework Applied to Homogeneous Catalytic PET Depolymerisation

author.name: Muhammad bin Javaid, Karim K. Ben Hicham, Enkhnyam Battulga, Alexander Mitsos, Martin Grohe

entry.summary: The authors present a citation-grounded LLM extraction and verification pipeline for chemistry literature, where an extractor LLM produces schema-enforced records with UUID-tagged citations and an independent LLM-as-a-judge reads the full paper to flag unsupported fields and propose cited corrections. It is applied to PET depolymerization catalysis literature.

entry.title: Guidance at Pure Noise Erodes Speaker Similarity in Few-Step Token-Conditioned Flow-Matching TTS

author.name: Jaeho Lee, Han-Lim Choi

entry.summary: The paper shows that in few-step flow-matching TTS decoders, most speaker-similarity degradation at two Euler steps comes from classifier-free guidance applied at the first step, where the network can only return the conditional mean so guidance shifts all trajectories by a similar vector. From this analysis the authors derive two training-free samplers, including a first-step modification.

entry.title: Deterministic Narrative Gravity: Bridging Theory of Mind and Historical Simulation through ABM-LLM Architectures

author.name: Alicia Colmenero-Fern\'andez, Lidia Ortega Alvarado

entry.summary: Proposes a deterministic multi-agent framework that couples LLMs to an Agent-Based Modelling pipeline grounded in Theory of Mind and Cognitive Archaeology, targeting the reproducibility problem of stochastic LLM simulation (the digital butterfly effect). The system runs locally at temperature zero with clean per-call model reloads and validates exact artifact identity across runs using SHA-256 hashing.

entry.title: Vietnamese Legal Ontology: Every legal answer, traced to the article that grounds it

author.name: Khac-Hoai Nam Bui, Quan Tran Minh

entry.summary: The authors build a large-scale Vietnamese legal knowledge graph from four open datasets, following the five-stage NVIDIA Auto Ontology pipeline, yielding 11.5M nodes and 16M edges where every element carries provenance. They show that ambiguous free-text legal citations can be systematically resolved to dated law versions and specific articles, clauses, or points.

entry.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation

author.name: Santosh Mohan Rajkumar, Sriram Narayanan, Samuel E. Otto, Debdipta Goswami

entry.summary: K-PWM is a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation, coupling Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performing latent-state inference via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing without a separately trained inference network. The bilinear structure enables exact conditioning and control-oriented use on partially observed physical systems.

entry.title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks

author.name: Sepehr Ilami, Babak Heydari

entry.summary: The paper treats the observation structure among LLM agents (who observes whom) as an explicit design object decoupled from the interaction network, studying ten identical agents in repeated group-decision games where a budget-constrained manager adds directed observation links. Across 1,080 episodes and six games, it examines how information-network structure shapes collective welfare.

entry.title: Direct Trajectory Optimization for Inference-Time Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Huixuan Zhang, Xiaojun Wan

entry.summary: Direct Trajectory Optimization (DTO) is a training-free framework that aligns text-to-image diffusion models with reward functions by directly optimizing the sampling trajectory, treating intermediate denoising scores and sampled noise as variables and avoiding backpropagation through the denoising network. Reward-Optimized Score Guidance is introduced to mitigate out-of-distribution failure modes.

entry.title: A Benchmark and Layered Evaluation Protocol for Evidence-Grounded Shared Belief Updating in Connected Robotics

author.name: Ranulfo Bezerra, Kimitoshi Yamazaki

entry.summary: Introduces the CREG benchmark of 350 deterministically generated scenarios across seven regimes for evaluating how connected robotic systems attribute evidence, update shared beliefs, resolve contradictions, and justify decisions. It argues that multi-robot and IoT systems should be scored on the full evidence-to-belief trajectory rather than final answers alone.

entry.title: RAIL: Representation-Aligned Imitation Learning for Student-Compatible Teacher Policies

author.name: Meraj Mammadov, Pedro Zuidberg Dos Martires, Johannes Andreas Stork

entry.summary: RAIL addresses the irreducible imitation gap in teacher-student RL by aligning the teacher's representation with what the student can observe during training, rather than doing reward shaping or extra RL afterward. This makes privileged-information teacher policies directly imitable from raw sensory inputs.

entry.title: UniOMA: Unified Optimal-Transport Multi-Modal Structural Alignment for Robot Perception

author.name: Xinrui Zu, Mark Hoogendoorn, Kevin Sebastian Luck, Shujian Yu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces UniOMA, a multimodal alignment method for robot learning that combines standard contrastive losses with a geometry-aware Gromov-Wasserstein distance regularization. By encoding intra-modal geometry and aligning cross-modal structure through a dynamically learned GW barycenter, the method enforces structural coherence across modalities beyond instance-level contrastive alignment, aiming for more generalizable multimodal representations in robot perception.

entry.title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target

author.name: Madhusudhana Naidu

entry.summary: This paper observes that BPE tokenizers make multi-word phrases unreachable for standard speculative decoding methods like Medusa and EAGLE-3, since no multi-word string can become a single target token. It changes the drafting unit by training a small MLP head that reads the frozen target model's hidden states to draft entire phrases at once. This could raise decoding throughput beyond what token-level candidate trees allow.

entry.title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Qu\'ebec for reliable AI evaluation

author.name: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemar\'echal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas, Balthasar Schachtner, Bastian Oliver Sabel, Michael Ingrisch, Philippe Despr\'es, Katharina Jeblick

entry.summary: LUCQUE is a large, comprehensively annotated LDCT lung cancer screening dataset from Quebec, curated and hosted on the PARADIM infrastructure with de-identified DICOM data, clinical information, and expert nodule annotations. It aims to enable reproducible, comparable, and independent evaluation of AI screening tools that previously relied on fragmented or private data.

entry.title: fNIRSAtlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Classification

author.name: Kalle M\"akel\"a, Tuukka Ruotsalo

entry.summary: fNIRSAtlas is the largest open benchmark for fNIRS classification, aggregating 23 tasks from 19 public collections across motor, cognitive, and affective paradigms, with an automated raw-data-to-evaluation pipeline. It standardizes cross-subject and within-subject evaluation to address the fragmentation that has limited machine learning progress on this modality.

entry.title: Can Time Series Foundation Models Serve as Surrogates for Power Systems Dynamic Simulation?

author.name: Sandy Miguel, Bruno Paes Leao, Cheng Feng

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether pretrained time-series foundation models can serve as computationally efficient surrogates for high-fidelity power system dynamic simulation, using in-context learning plus retrieval-augmented reference selection and physics-informed regularization. Experiments on a simulated 9-bus power system show promising results against a domain state-of-the-art AI baseline.

entry.title: CALFA-KV: Joint Calibration and Fisher-Guided Anchors for 1-Bit KV Cache Compression

author.name: Xiancai Tian, Leichao Zhang, Shenhui Zhang, Yi Shan, Hailong Li, Feng Lin, Xiaotian Yu, Aijun Li

entry.summary: CALFA-KV combines 1-bit KV cache quantization with selective high-precision storage: offline it jointly fits key centers, radial normalization, and codebooks against the frozen model's projected attention output, and estimates channel-wise Fisher-type sensitivities from gradient norms. Online, the sensitivities weight reconstruction errors to retain the highest-scoring KV states at high precision under a per-layer budget.

entry.title: CONSTRAINER: Promptable Graph-Structured Optimization via Constraint Conditioning

author.name: Zeeshan Memon, Mingke Tian, Xinyuan Song, Hongwei Jin, Kibaek Kim, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: CONSTRAINER is a constraint-conditioned neural framework for graph-structured optimization that treats the constraint set itself as a first-class, shared input across problem variants, rather than fixing formulations per task. This enables a single trained backbone to be prompted with different constraints and reused across related optimization problems.

entry.title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xinjue Wang, Xiuheng Wang, Yejun Zhang, Sergiy A. Vorobyov, Esa Ollila

entry.summary: The paper proposes constraining each additive update block during zeroth-order (ZO) LLM fine-tuning to a fixed-rank matrix manifold, keeping pretrained weights frozen and eliminating backpropagation's activation-storage cost. It builds a Riemannian ZO gradient estimator by projecting random matrices onto the tangent space, addressing non-uniqueness and rank issues in prior low-rank ZO methods. This targets memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models.

entry.title: Prescriptive Learning of Linear Policies with Feasibility Guarantees for Binary Decision-Making

author.name: Farzaneh Pourahmadi, Trine Krogh Boomsma, Pierre Pinson

entry.summary: The paper proposes a prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making under uncertainty that trains linear policies directly rather than imitating labeled optimal decisions. The approach provides feasibility guarantees for resulting decisions, addressing counterfactual blindness and distributional-shift infeasibility of purely predictive approaches in areas like energy scheduling and workforce planning.

entry.title: Task presentation and execution paths shape LLM mathematical performance

author.name: Min Huang, Mingyan Liu

entry.summary: Through paired comparisons separating submission requirements, draft reuse, and candidate availability, this study shows that how an LLM receives information and submits answers dramatically shapes measured math performance. For example, submission protocol alone flipped results from zero valid answers to 390 parseable outputs, and providing drafts and candidates raised accuracy from 9.09% to 59.60% on initially failed problems.

entry.title: OPSRL-SSP: Optimistic Posterior Sampling for Stochastic Shortest Path with Minimax-Optimal Regret

author.name: Yiming Xu, Xian Wei, Cheng Chen

entry.summary: OPSRL-SSP is an optimistic posterior-sampling algorithm for stochastic shortest path RL with unknown dynamics that achieves the minimax-optimal regret order, closing a gap left by prior empirical-but-suboptimal posterior sampling methods. It operates in epochs with a logarithmic schedule of posterior samples and induces optimism via a pseudo-state with an optimistic boundary value. The paper proves a high-probability regret bound matching the optimal rate.

entry.title: Building heterogeneous multistep workflows in automated microscopy: reward design and knowledge transfer for autonomous structure property discovery

author.name: Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: This paper presents a budget-constrained framework for autonomous microscopy workflows that decides where to measure, what information to acquire, and when to recalibrate. It combines explicit scientific rewards, action costs, instrument observation models, and transfer of pre-experiment knowledge such as predictor accuracy and drift characteristics, evaluated on a real electron energy-loss setup.

entry.title: APO2CS: Advantage-Aware Preference Optimization for Two-Level Constructive Search in Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Kaixi Yang, Linbo Qiao, Wei Shang, Yanqi Shi, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: APO2CS is a preference-based training objective for neural combinatorial optimization that enriches pairwise preferences with an advantage term based on objective-value differences and adds supervision at the level of partial construction trajectories. This macro and micro level supervision provides denser signals than binary pairwise labels used in prior preference optimization for solvers.

entry.title: Reward-Estimated Hypergradient for Bilevel Reinforcement Learning with Black-Box Follower

author.name: Shigeki Kusaka, Mikoto Kudo, Takumi Tanabe, Akifumi Wachi, Youhei Akimoto

entry.summary: This paper addresses bilevel RL where the leader does not know the follower's reward, recovering it from trajectories via inverse RL. It proves that the reward-estimation bias caused by potential-based shaping (which IRL cannot identify) cancels when hypergradient estimates are aggregated across sufficiently diverse dynamics, and proposes RE-HG for the black-box setting.

entry.title: Correct First, Fast Second: What a Local 7B Code Model Can and Cannot Do for GPU Kernel Optimization

author.name: Jui-Chien Tsou, Po-Yi Wu

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates whether a fixed, locally hosted 7B code model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct) can replace PyTorch operators with custom CUDA kernels across 30 KernelBench tasks, comparing four interaction regimes from zero-shot prompting to a multi-agent loop around a non-LLM evaluator. The key finding is that correctness, not speed, is the binding constraint: even correct generated kernels only average 0.97-0.99x eager PyTorch speed, because a 7B model cannot compensate for fundamental performance limits. The work matters because it provides a realistic assessment of small local models for GPU kernel engineering, a task often claimed to be automatable.

entry.title: Replication of Thermal Comfort Cohort Models: No Support for Improved Thermal Preference Prediction

author.name: Thomas Hirsch, Katja Ceplak, Veronika Windisch, Samina Kadkhoda Masoumali, Matias Quintana, Clayton Miller, Stefano Schiavon, Gerald Schweiger

entry.summary: This paper replicates and methodologically assesses cohort comfort models (CCMs), which group building occupants to reduce the data requirements of personal comfort models. Using the original DORN dataset under a revised protocol and an independent dataset (PersonAI), the authors find no support for the originally reported performance gains, with F1-macro revealing class-imbalance effects masked by F1-micro.

entry.title: Agnostic Marginal-Nonuniform Learning

author.name: Tanmay Devale, Steve Hanneke, Amirreza Shaeiri

entry.summary: The paper studies binary classification in the marginal-nonuniform learning framework in the agnostic setting, where learning-rate constants may depend on the unlabeled marginal distribution but guarantees must hold uniformly over conditional label distributions. It derives optimal rates in both the standard agnostic setting and a fine-grained criterion.

entry.title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers

author.name: Leon A. Trochelmann, Sajad Movahedi, Shiwei Liu, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: KiteNorm is a post-norm Transformer training method that constrains hidden-state variance, motivated by a Jacobian bound linking variance growth to gradient vanishing in LayerNorm. The method aims to make Post-LayerNorm architectures stable at depth and under large learning rates, addressing why Post-LN has been largely abandoned for Pre-LN. The authors report decoder-only results where prior Post-LN methods failed to match strong Pre-LN baselines.

entry.title: Domain Adaptive Graph Neural Networks for Neutrino Experiments

author.name: Hemalata Nayak, Giuseppe Cerati, Aleksandra \'Ciprijanovi\'c, Tammy Walton

entry.summary: The authors introduce domain-adaptation-enabled graph neural networks for reconstruction tasks in liquid argon time projection chamber neutrino experiments, addressing simulation-to-data domain shift that can mimic or obscure new-physics signals. They demonstrate robust cross-dataset learning using MicroBooNE-style data.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Generalization for Set-Input Optimization-Valued Objectives

author.name: Futoshi Futami, Masahiro Fujisawa

entry.summary: The paper formalizes modern evaluation criteria such as multicalibration, CVaR, and Cressie-Read DRO as set-input optimization-valued objectives whose empirical criteria depend on the whole batch plus a post-hoc auxiliary optimization. It derives information-theoretic generalization bounds for the expected optimized validation-training gap in the balanced supersample setting.

entry.title: Close and Sort: Exact Maximum-Likelihood Aggregation of Cyclic Rank-Two Preferences

author.name: Kehan Liu, Zhaoyun Chen, Xianquan Yan

entry.summary: The authors show that the NP-hard weighted Kemeny rank aggregation problem becomes exactly solvable when the skew-symmetric log-odds matrix has rank two, even with cyclic preferences. They give a geometric formulation where the objective equals twice the signed area of a closed polygon, yielding CloseSort, an algorithm that polar-sorts edge vectors. This applies to rank aggregation, recommendation, and LLM-based evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?

author.name: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Yiyao Huang, Arushi Katyal, Ryan Lin, Pranav Ramakrishnan, Weiya Wang

entry.summary: This arXiv paper presents a mathematician-AI collaboration in mechanistic interpretability: the authors trained a small transformer to learn the language of the affine A2 Coxeter group (the symmetry group of the triangular tiling of the Euclidean plane). By inspecting the model's attention patterns, they formulated and then proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2, demonstrating a case where model interpretability directly fed back into new mathematical research.

entry.title: Symplectic Normal Coordinates Flow for Generative Modeling of Hamiltonian Systems

author.name: Christopher M. Pierce

entry.summary: Introduces an invertible symplectic flow layer built from amplitude-dependent rotations in learned normal coordinates for generative modeling of Hamiltonian systems, extending the Birkhoff normal form picture to nonlinear settings. Derives conditions under which the nonlinear rotation layer preserves the symplectic structure.

entry.title: When Normality Shifts: Multi-Level WavLM Modeling for Open-World Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Daniel Niekurzak, Daniel Kozuch, Weronika Folwarska, Khan Muhammad, Rafa{\l} Scherer

entry.summary: Investigates an attack-free audio deepfake detection approach that models bona fide speech only, scoring synthetic audio by deviation from authentic representations using shrinkage-Mahalanobis modeling over frozen WavLM Base+ hidden states. Achieves 8.45% EER on ASVspoof 2019 LA, near a fully supervised baseline, with analysis of generalization to 2021 DF conditions.

entry.title: MICE: Multi-animal Interaction Context Encoder - A Hierarchical Foundation Model for Mouse Behavior

author.name: Yen-Shuo Su, Weihan Li, Anqi Wu

entry.summary: MICE is a self-supervised foundation model for mouse pose behavior that handles multi-animal social interactions, pretraining jointly on six mouse-pose corpora spanning one to four mice and varying keypoint counts. It addresses shortcomings of existing pose encoders that treat animals independently, hard-code animal counts, and pretrain one dataset at a time.

entry.title: Breaking the $\sqrt{d}$ Communication Barrier in Federated Sampling with Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo

author.name: Jiajun Liang, Linxuan Wang, Guang Lin, Qifan Song

entry.summary: This paper proposes Adaptive Federated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (AFHMC) for Bayesian federated learning with a control mechanism for local node shifts. It proves a communication cost of O((d/epsilon^2)^(1/3)) up to logarithmic terms, significantly better than the previous O(sqrt(d)/epsilon) bound, and adapts to client heterogeneity. Under low-heterogeneity settings the analysis yields further improvements.

entry.title: Trajectory Density Ratios under Weak Support: A Survey across the Sciences

author.name: Wei Chen, Lihao Zhuang, Yubing Wu, Delu Zeng

entry.summary: A survey of trajectory density ratio methods across fields including reinforcement learning, molecular simulation, climate attribution, and language model post-training, focusing on cases of weak support where the ratio may not exist or be well-estimated. It provides a unified treatment of a quantity that underlies off-policy evaluation and importance sampling throughout science.

entry.title: MUTE: Multi-Level Alignment Uncoupling Against Talking-Head Exploitation for Voice Protection

author.name: Donghyun Kim, Jin Hong, Seungmin Kim, Dain Kim, Junseok Kwon, Daeseon Choi

entry.summary: MUTE is an audio protection framework that defends against misuse of talking-head generation models, which synthesize facial animation from audio and are vulnerable to deepfake exploitation. It disrupts audio-visual alignment at two levels: perturbing cross-modal attention and degrading temporal audio embeddings so synthesized outputs become unusable. This addresses an underexplored gap, as most anti-deepfake work protects visual rather than audio assets.

entry.title: Prediction with Foundation Models under Deployment Budgets

author.name: Zhaohui Xu, Xiaofei Xu, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: The paper develops a framework for prediction tasks where foundation models differ in accuracy and query cost, learning from training data which models to query and how to blend their outputs with freely available features under an average-cost budget. Two methods are proposed: uniform model querying and an adaptive Q-learning policy that chooses models sequentially and decides when to stop. Theoretical results include a minimax rate and a guarantee that combining individually weak outputs can beat the best single model.

entry.title: VLA Adaptation with Real and Simulated Data: A Case Study on Robotic Chess

author.name: Mat\v{e}j Kripner, Milan Straka

entry.summary: This paper studies how to fine-tune vision-language-action (VLA) models for downstream robot tasks, using a robotic chess task on an SO-101 arm that requires precise manipulation and spatial understanding. It systematically examines how dataset size, update budgets, checkpoint selection, and simulated demonstrations affect adaptation of the pi0.5 model, addressing whether simulation can reduce costly real-robot data collection. The results provide practical guidance for practitioners deploying generalist robot policies on new tasks.

entry.title: TransMem: Transition-Aware Retrieval for Evolving Personal Memory

author.name: Shigeng Chen, Linhao Luo, Changlong Shi, Zhangchi Qiu, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: TransMem is a transition-aware memory retrieval framework for long-term personalized agents that stores preference updates as explicit retrieval units alongside ordinary factual memories. It routes interaction histories into topic-structured memory graphs, detects shift events, and grounds them as transition records so that queries can surface which earlier preference was refined, contradicted, or superseded. This addresses a real gap where existing memory systems return isolated facts without update context.

entry.title: LongCap: Hour-Scale Timestamped Audio Captioning via Chunk-wise Processing

author.name: Jinchuan Tian, Sen Chen, Wenbin Huang, Chao Weng, Zhengwei Huang, Jiatong Shi, Yichen Lu, Haoran Wang, Shinji Watanabe, Cong Zhou

entry.summary: LongCap is a framework for timestamped audio captioning over hour-long recordings, interleaving audio chunks with structured event captions and using relative timestamps and retained context to support length extrapolation within a 1M-token context window. The release includes LongCapBench with human annotations and three new diarization-inspired metrics, with LongCap-Diar achieving strong benchmark results.

entry.title: THEATRON: A Benchmark for Evaluating Persona Persistence in Long-Horizon LLM Decision-Making

author.name: Yuyan Wang, Yuechen Jiang, Zhiwei Liu, Jimin Huang, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: THEATRON is a controlled benchmark using financial market replay to test whether persona information persists in long-horizon sequential decision-making, distinct from mere persona expression. Evaluating zero-shot, one-shot, and chain-of-thought persona injection across four LLMs over multi-month trajectories, it measures within-persona stability, cross-persona separability, and action collapse.

entry.title: Robust Domain-Mixture Scheduling for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yankai Chen, Sida Lin, Yifan Li, Hanjun Luo, Hanrong Zhang, Zhuohan Xie, Bowei He, Wei-Chieh Huang, Meng Ding, Wei Xue, Yike Guo, Philip S. Yu, Xue Liu

entry.summary: This paper addresses budget allocation across domains in multi-teacher on-policy distillation, where multiple domain-expert teachers transfer skills to one compact student. The authors apply distributionally robust optimization to prioritize the worst-performing domain, but must handle noisy per-domain training signals estimated from few rollouts, which otherwise cause the optimizer to mistake noise for genuine worst-case domains. The result is a more robust scheduling method for allocating a shared training budget.

entry.title: Police Behavior Patterns Through Radio Analysis

author.name: Milo Z. Trujillo, Adam Perhala, Elaine Zou, Tyler Mckenzie, Juniper Lovato, Brooke Foucault Welles, Alyssa Hasegawa Smith

entry.summary: This study collects and analyzes over 14 million police radio transmissions (100,000+ hours of speech) to characterize law enforcement activity patterns in the United States. Because police radio captures real-time internal communication rather than post-hoc press releases, it offers a lens into police behavior with less filtering or bias than official accounts. The work matters as a large-scale computational social science resource using speech AI on sensitive real-world communications.

entry.title: MAPA: Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation for Latent Dataset Distillation in 3D Medical Classification

author.name: Weiqi Zhang, Hiroyuki Kubo

entry.summary: MAPA improves dataset distillation for 3D medical classification by synthesizing compact training sets in the latent space of a frozen autoencoder rather than voxel space, cutting memory and optimization costs. The key contribution is fixing a newly identified failure mode, prototype concentration, where distribution-matching objectives over-represent dense latent regions and under-represent sparse intra-class modes, by allocating prototypes across intra-class modes.

entry.title: Preconditioned Implicit Midpoint Langevin Sampling for Non-Smooth Bayesian Imaging

author.name: Sichen Wang, Zhipeng Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces P-IMLA, a preconditioned implicit-midpoint Langevin sampler for high-dimensional log-concave targets with non-smooth regularization, aimed at Bayesian imaging problems. The method uses a Caylan-transform identity to make the sampler Gaussian-exact at any step size, transfers sharp contraction rates through whitening, and offers a proximal variant for non-smooth terms with a three-term error budget. It matters because it addresses a known failure mode of preconditioned Euler-Maruyama where large steps inflate stationary variance.

entry.title: RigidGS: Geometry-Aware Object Decoupling for Rigid-Body Interaction in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Paul Sansah Gyreyiri, Diksha Shukla

entry.summary: Introduces RigidGS, an end-to-end pipeline that decouples geometric learning from object identity in 3D Gaussian Splatting for interactive VR/MR applications, using depth- and temporally-aware mask refinement to fix SAM2 failures like noisy masks and over-segmentation. The approach addresses label-geometry coupling that mislabels boundary Gaussians in existing object-aware 3DGS methods.

entry.title: RefineSplat: Reconstruction-Guided Object-Centric Gaussian Splatting for Open-Vocabulary Querying

author.name: Yiren Lu, Disheng Liu, Sreya Srinidhi, Yunlai Zhou, Yiran Qiao, Chaoda Song, Tuo Liang, Jing Ma, Huan Wang, Yu Yin

entry.summary: RefineSplat extends the authors' prior Segment-then-Splat framework for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding, tracking objects in 2D first and then reconstructing each with dedicated Gaussians guided by reconstruction feedback. This addresses view inconsistency, ambiguous boundaries, and weak object-level correspondence that plague the common splat-then-segment pipeline in static and dynamic scenes.

entry.title: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation

author.name: Xiangjun Tang, Jianqi Chen, Peter Wonka

entry.summary: JoVox introduces a discrete flow matching framework that learns the joint distribution across all levels of a voxel hierarchy rather than independent per-level distributions, allowing fine cells to inform coarse-level decisions. This targets the long-standing trade-off between high fidelity and lightweight voxel generation.

entry.title: Beyond Bit Matching: Orthogonal Watermarks for Collusion-Resistant Image Fingerprinting

author.name: Zhakshylyk Nurlanov, Tobias Wei\ss{}berg, Florian Bernard

entry.summary: This paper introduces VectorMark, an image fingerprinting scheme that maps user keys to near-orthogonal high-dimensional unit vectors rather than discrete bit strings, making averaging collusion attacks ineffective. It provides a geometric analysis showing colluder signals of order 1/sqrt(K) survive averaging while unrelated keys concentrate near zero, enabling collusion detection via cosine similarity. This matters for provenance and leak-tracing of AI-generated and distributed media.

entry.title: What You Show Is Not What You Get: Rethinking Demonstration Following in Visual In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Xiao Hu, Ilia Sucholutsky

entry.summary: This paper identifies systematic failure modes in visual in-context segmentation with SegGPT, namely background color mapping deviations and part-to-parent expansion, where predictions diverge from the demonstration even when internal features remain discriminative. The authors analyze how demonstrations guide role and color assignment over learned semantic regions and propose Semantic Contrast Prompt Selection to mitigate the issues.

entry.title: NuJEV: Structured Visual Judgments for Consistent Nuclei Quantification

author.name: Yonghuang Wu, Pengfei Wang, Zhenyang Liang, Yize Ma, Pengfei Song, Guoqing Wu, Jinhua Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces NuJEV, an adaptation of the Qwen3-VL-2B vision-language model for nuclear perception in pathology images, replacing free-form generation with structured judgments that predict nuclear presence, centers, and types via a jointly trained visual LoRA and parallel head. Counts are computed from predicted nuclei rather than generated directly, achieving a five-query MAE of 1.844 on the 2,732-image PanNuke test set, with localization and typed F1 scores of 0.816 and 0.682 respectively. It matters because it shows structured prediction heads on compact VLMs can deliver reliable, consistent cell quantification for computational pathology.

entry.title: NightSteps: A Night-Time Dataset and Benchmark for Pedestrian Crossing Intention Prediction

author.name: Sjoerd Takken, Shaodi You

entry.summary: NightSteps is a new benchmark of night-time dashcam footage from six cities with pedestrian locations, track IDs, and annotations for crossing intention prediction, addressing the absence of low-light data that limits robustness evaluation of pedestrian safety models. It provides construction methodology and baseline evaluation.

entry.title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication

author.name: Daniyar Kurmankhojayev, Elmurat Nigmatov, Dmitrii Gordin, Andrei Shadrikov, Mikhail Shkorin, Danijar Gabdullin, Vyacheslav Shen

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates active screen illumination methods for detecting injection attacks in remote face authentication, complementing the better-studied presentation attack detection (PAD) use case. It classifies injected content into static images, prerecorded videos, and real-time deepfakes, and adapts a screen-illumination challenge-response approach into an implementation evaluated for injection attack detection.

entry.title: What Breaks Scribble-Supervised Segmentation? An Audit-Informed Benchmark for Scribble Annotation Robustness

author.name: Minheng Wu, Di Wen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Yufan Chen, Kailun Yang, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark for scribble-supervised segmentation robustness, built on an audit of 12,031 manual PASCAL VOC 2012 scribbles and six controlled perturbation operators (class corruption, spatial offset, directional perturbation, stroke-length reduction, dropout, fragmentation). It evaluates manual and automatic scribbles across two image domains, two backbone settings, and multiple training pipelines, with each operator reporting requested versus achieved changes.

entry.title: HSGNav: Hypothesis Scene Graphs for Multi-Scale Lifelong Navigation under Object Relocation

author.name: Kaiyao Liao, Qingfeng Li, Chen Chen, Qing Sun, Ningbo Gu, Xiaoze Wu, Haochen Zhao, Ying Li, Jianwei Niu

entry.summary: HSGNav proposes a Hypothesis Scene Graph (HSG) that separates persistent 3D furniture entities from revisable surface-object hypotheses, preserving small-object evidence and supporting local revision without rebuilding the stable entity topology. This enables lifelong navigation under object relocation in real homes, with explicit object-state validation to avoid stale entries.

entry.title: Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots

author.name: Vaishnav Ramesh, Jacob Carter, Shivali J. Patel, Sanjeev J. Koppal, Md Jahidul Islam

entry.summary: BCVS is a pose-free view selection algorithm that filters redundant image sequences online for 3D perception, achieving 22+ FPS on a CPU without full structure-from-motion pipelines. It uses a purely correspondence-based scoring strategy that prioritizes view novelty while maintaining overlap for geometric stability, under a user-specified budget.

entry.title: Who Taught the Robot That? Removing One User's Corrections from a Robot Policy That Learns Online

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: This paper addresses machine unlearning for online robot learning: a robot corrected by multiple users must be able to remove one person's contributions. It shows that when corrections occur via take-over control, ordered retraining on the remaining sessions approximates the counterfactual robot, while simple data deletion and one-pass retraining does not, because update ordering matters.

entry.title: Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM

author.name: Kai Pfeiffer, Jia Wang, Gordon Owusu Boateng, Yuquan Wang, Vincent Bonnet, Abderrahmane Kheddar

entry.summary: The authors reformulate sparse hierarchical quadratic programming subproblems arising in robot kinematic control using ADMM, enabling effective warm-starting across sequential control steps where prior interior-point solvers fell short. This allows efficient integrated hierarchical decision-making over large sets of end-effector candidates. It contributes a numerical tool that could make hierarchical robot control more real-time capable.

entry.title: OASIS: Optimization-Aware Subgoal Inference with Safety Constraints for Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation

author.name: Arian Hajizadeha, Javad Pourrafia, Negar Shenavara, Sana Bashiria, Seyed Majid Esmailzadeh

entry.summary: OASIS is a hierarchical navigation framework that feeds recent MPC optimization outcomes back into an RL-based subgoal policy, so that subgoal generation is aware of whether the low-level controller can actually solve the resulting problem. A Soft Actor-Critic high-level policy proposes local subgoals tracked by a nonlinear MPC with motion limits and collision-avoidance constraints. This closes the loop between planning and control, addressing a common failure mode in hierarchical navigation.

entry.title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups

author.name: Yanliang Huang, Peng Xie, Zhen Zhang, Zhuoqi Zeng, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: Develops certified zonotopic reachability analysis for bounding trajectory-tracking error of aerial and space vehicles whose error dynamics evolve on matrix Lie groups. Exploiting group-affine structure, the error dynamics become linear in Lie algebra coordinates, yielding less conservative safety certificates than single invariant ellipsoids or interval methods. This enables pre-execution safety certification of planned trajectories near obstacles under bounded disturbances.

entry.title: A Topological Encoder Decoder Framework for Temporal Graph Learning

author.name: Ronan Buck, Kiarash Shamsi, Tran Gia Bao Ngo, Astrit Tola, Baris Coskunuzer, Cuneyt Gurcan Akcora

entry.summary: This paper reframes temporal graph prediction as an inverse topology problem: instead of predicting edges directly, the model first predicts a multiscale topological descriptor of the future graph and then reconstructs a plausible future snapshot under inductive constraints. This makes global structure and node churn explicit targets, addressing breakdowns when new nodes and edges appear. It matters for forecasting dynamic graphs with changing size and composition.

entry.title: DFT-Agent Bench: Scaffold Effects and Execution Provenance in Autonomous DFT

author.name: Shijie Liu, Jin Yang, Weilin Wan, Jingtao Han, Jia LI, Tianqi Deng

entry.summary: Introduces DFT-Agent Bench, a benchmark of 200+ Quantum ESPRESSO tasks for LLM agents doing first-principles materials simulation, with execution-provenance auditing of whether agents actually ran the required simulations. Compares a bare ReAct baseline with a bundled scaffold across two models, showing scaffold improvements on some task families but not uniformly.

entry.title: BiVerify: Closing the Loop Between Backward and Forward Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction

author.name: Rui Zou, Xin Zhao, Mengqi Wei, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: BiVerify combines backward verification (checking candidate answers against original constraints) and forward verification (following problem conditions through the solution) in a closed loop for LLM mathematical self-correction, exploiting their complementary failure modes. The paper analyzes when each direction catches different error types and shows that looping between them improves correction reliability. It targets more dependable self-correction on complex math problems.

entry.title: Reproducible quantum clustering for single-cell transcriptome atlases

author.name: Henry Han

entry.summary: KQE-2 is a training-free hybrid quantum-classical framework for reproducible whole-transcriptome clustering that maps cells into entanglement-free quantum states, enabling exact classical evaluation and direct quantum-processor checks. It proves removing entanglement is necessary and sufficient to bound single-qubit feature variance, and shows more stable biological results than retrained scVI baselines.

entry.title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment

author.name: Christophe Cruz (ICB, UBE), Hussam Ghanem (ICB, UBE), Samir Jabbar (ICB, UBE), Ait Kbir (ICB, UBE), Hocine Cherifi (ICB, UBE)

entry.summary: PARIS is an open-source multi-agent framework in which a conductor agent running in Claude Code orchestrates 15 specialized LLM agents to conduct end-to-end PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews, from scoping to manuscript draft export. Agents coordinate through validated persisted artifacts with deterministic Python utilities for retrieval and scoring, plus three human checkpoints including a QualityScore-based corpus adequacy gate.

entry.title: SurvAD: How Anomalies Survive Diffusion Reconstruction

author.name: Lexing Zhang

entry.summary: Characterizes anomaly leakage in diffusion-based anomaly detectors, deriving an exact recursion for deterministic samplers whose continuous limit is a survival law: anomaly signal decays exponentially at a rate set by a retention parameter dependent on noise level, not step count. One measured path therefore predicts leakage across samplers and schedules, and the law identifies leak growth as exposure bias.

entry.title: Update Slope Is Bounded by Prior Calibration: A Structural Bound and Its Contingent Empirical Signature

author.name: Ben Jenkins, Mihaela Cardei

entry.summary: The paper identifies two confounds in the update-slope metric used to evaluate LLM forecasters: outcome-aware evidence construction inflates measured responsiveness roughly fourfold versus resolution-blinded ladders, and update slope has a prior-dependent structural ceiling that can reflect starting calibration rather than genuine updating. Empirical coupling varies across Manifold, ForecastBench, and ACLED pools. This is a cautionary methodological contribution for LLM forecasting evaluations.

entry.title: Split and Bridge: Multimodal Generation via Diffusion Bridging

author.name: Ahmad Arrabi, Xiaohan Zhang, Xingyu Li, Safwan Wshah

entry.summary: Split and Bridge (SnB) is a bottom-up multimodal generation framework that couples pretrained unimodal diffusion models at sampling time: samples follow a shared diffusion trajectory to a split point, then branch into modality-specific trajectories guided by a bridge module. This avoids training a unified latent space from scratch and enables plug-and-play composition. It offers a scalable alternative to joint multimodal diffusion training.

entry.title: Imperfectly Imperfect: Evaluating Graded Cognitive Diversity in LLM Persona Simulations

author.name: Sion Weatherhead, Ben Newell, Aaron Belbasis, Flora Salim

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLM agents conditioned on profiles of cognitive reflection, Need for Cognition, and Big Five traits reproduce human variation when answering a cognition suite compared to 473 human adults, including two newly assembled tests (CRT and BRT). It assesses whether synthetic participants in behavioral research can express graded cognitive diversity as assigned. Useful caution and methodology for the growing use of LLMs as synthetic research subjects.

entry.title: Learning Biological Hierarchies in Single-Cell Foundation Models

author.name: Xiangyu Guo, Ricardo Henao

entry.summary: The paper introduces scOntoFM, a biologically informed single-cell foundation model that embeds the hierarchical cell ontology into representation learning using lowest-common-ancestor distances. It pairs efficient offline triplet sampling with ontology-guided learning to shape both local neighborhoods and global embedding geometry, improving performance across cell- and gene-level benchmarks.

entry.title: HydroTuring: A physics probe benchmark testing mass, energy, and momentum conservation in hydrologic models

author.name: Zhi Li, Changming Li, Siavash Shams, Han Wang, Qingyi Yang, Yuanhang Liu, Taiqi Lian, Xin Lan, Shunan Zhou, Binlan Zhang, Siddik Barbhuiya, Songkun Yan, Bing Li, Jinlong Hu, Yaji Wang, Zhenjiang Wu, Mofan Zhang, Kaihao Long, Jingzhi Chen, Yuan-Heng Wang

entry.summary: HydroTuring is a black-box benchmark of 37 physics probes testing mass, energy, and momentum conservation in hydrologic models, including deep learning systems now used for operational flood forecasting. The motivating experiment shows a conceptual model leaking 15% of water input to an unreported sink can still achieve a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.93, illustrating that hydrograph skill does not imply physical consistency.

entry.title: An Evaluation of Tabular Foundation Models as Training-Free World Models

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Ryoichi Takase, Ahmed Farahat

entry.summary: Investigates whether pretrained tabular foundation models can serve as training-free dynamics models by framing next-state prediction as in-context regression over transition pairs. Across synthetic systems and robot locomotion benchmarks, TabFMs beat LSTM and MLP models trained from scratch on limited data in almost all settings, while also mapping where they break.

entry.title: HumanSightBench: A Benchmark for Human Visual Perception in MLLMs

author.name: Zixin Su, Yangguang Lin, Zegang Peng, Yuntong Sun, Xuanyi Wang, Jiahao Wang, Qiankai Xu, Bing Yuan, Jinze Bai, Youbin Wu, Jingjia Huang, Ruyang Liu, Yanxu Hu

entry.summary: HumanSightBench contains ~2,870 items constructed to be human-easy but model-hard, isolating visual perception failures of multimodal LLMs from language priors, background knowledge, and ambiguous questions. Its guidelines address the confounds of end-to-end multimodal evaluation.

entry.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach

author.name: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu

entry.summary: BiMuon extends Muon-style geometry-aware optimization to stochastic bilevel problems, integrating implicit hypergradient estimation while respecting matrix structure in gradients and correcting spectral imbalance induced by lower-level curvature. Applications include hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic RL.

entry.title: Pruning DNA Sequence

author.name: Faias Satter, Shaker Islam, Aminul Islam

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sequence Pruning, a dynamic data-pruning framework for DNA language-model pretraining that removes genomic sequences as they become easy to predict, using per-sequence accuracy computed directly from the forward pass without a separate scoring model. Across five pretraining settings and two corpora it reduces pretraining data processing by up to 96% while largely preserving downstream genomic benchmark performance.

entry.title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout

author.name: Pingbing Ming, Han Wang

entry.summary: The authors prove universal approximation for BREMP networks, a reference architecture for equivariant GNN interatomic potentials, where readout forms invariants from products of equivariant features. They construct explicit spherical-harmonic filters that determine local atomic environments up to permutations, with degree bounds tied to neighbor counts and layer cutoffs.

entry.title: Data Manipulation Attacks Against Machine Learning Integrated Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Soyon Choi, Scott Alfeld, Meiyi Ma

entry.summary: This paper develops methods for constructing attack policies against composed ML systems in cyber-physical settings, where an attacker who can trick individual learners (vision, planning) seeks to manipulate the system-level behavior and resulting physical actions. It formalizes how vulnerabilities of individual models compose into system-level attack surfaces. This extends ML security beyond single-model threat models to integrated autonomous systems.

entry.title: When Does Physics Beat Data? Data-Efficient Traffic State Estimation with Amortized PINNs

author.name: Anna Lazareva, Alexander Tarakanov

entry.summary: The paper shows that imposing the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards conservation law as a physics-informed prior makes traffic state estimation far more data-efficient than pure data-driven models including deep kriging. On four real corridors, physics-informed estimators generalize to held-out sensors where data-driven models overfit, with a clear crossover benefit on shock-rich corridors.

entry.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection

author.name: Amey Pasarkar, Adji Bousso Dieng

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Vendi Anomaly Score, which flags anomalies by measuring how much removing a sample changes the dataset's diversity as quantified by the Vendi score. This diversity-based formulation captures both local redundancy and global structure without density estimation, partitioning heuristics, or restrictive distributional assumptions. The approach offers a new conceptual paradigm for anomaly detection relevant to trustworthy ML and scientific discovery.

entry.title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions

author.name: Tareq Aldirawi, Wenge Guo

entry.summary: This paper establishes exact finite-sample group-conditional conformal risk control for disjoint groups under bounded monotone losses, with two-sided bounds and fundamental limitations from local support and calibration-rank granularity. For overlapping groups it develops two exactly valid approaches, characterizes reconciliation gaps, and demonstrates a strict size-versus-coverage trade-off.

entry.title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance

author.name: Yixin Gao, Runsen Feng, Xin Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Flex-DDCM, a zero-shot image compression framework that guides diffusion trajectories with task-specific noise selection so compressed representations serve downstream machine-analysis tasks as well as human viewing. Builds on Turbo-DDCM and supports individually applicable guidance terms for flexible reconstruction targets.

entry.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion

author.name: Sean Turland, Eloi Moliner, Vesa V\"alim\"aki

entry.summary: Proposes SimDPS, a model-agnostic music inpainting method that retrieves contextually similar segments from the surrounding signal and uses them to guide diffusion posterior sampling toward coherent reconstructions. Outperforms RePaint and DPS on objective metrics across waveform and latent diffusion backbones, with positive subjective results.

entry.title: Query- and Candidate-Aware Long User Sequence Modeling for Sponsored Product Ranking in Search

author.name: Dongyue Xie, Sergey Kolbin, Manavender Malgireddy, Iurii Shcherbak, Weixing Tang, Arushi Jain, Wanchen Shao, Kurt Zimmer, Raja Hafiz Affandi, Matt Lindsay

entry.summary: This paper presents a production sequence modeling framework for sponsored-product search ranking that augments recent behavior with dual retrieval channels over long-term history: candidate-nearest-neighbor and query-nearest-neighbor retrieval. It combines dedicated query and candidate context tokens with candidate-aware early fusion. Offline ablations show improved ranking metrics over baselines.

entry.title: How Far Does Second-Order Linear Response Predict Quantization Mismatch? Pre-Registered Measurements on Five Language Models

author.name: Dezhen Lu, Zixiang Ni

entry.summary: The paper tests whether a second-order screening tool based on Fisher information (the quadratic term underlying Hessian-aware quantizers) reliably predicts post-quantization KL divergence across int8, fp8, and int4 formats on five language models including Qwen3 and OLMo-2 variants. Relative predictions are robust across perturbation scales and configurations, absolute predictions are heavy-tailed, and the MoE model exhibits non-quadratic behavior. Pre-registered measurement design adds credibility.

entry.title: From Granger causality to causal structure in dynamical systems

author.name: V\'ictor Elvira

entry.summary: This survey-style article reviews the gap between Granger causality, which detects predictive relations among measured signals, and true causal structure among the mechanisms generating them. It traces recent advances in observation-space Granger analysis and follows a path toward directed structure in latent dynamical models, asking when such structure can be interpreted causally. The clarification is important given widespread misuse of Granger causality across neuroscience and economics.

entry.title: Distinguishing Extraction Failures and Clinical Discordance with LLM Uncertainty on Radiology Reports

author.name: Jerjes Aguirre-Chavez, Shant Malkasian, Roshun Sankaran, Brendan Crabb, Albert Hsiao

entry.summary: Using a real-world cohort of 1,045 patients undergoing coronary CT angiography, this study evaluates whether LLM uncertainty during vessel-level stenosis extraction can separate extraction failures from genuine clinical discordance, validated against expert annotations and invasive angiography. Quantifying uncertainty signals like stenosis margins helps clinicians know when structured LLM outputs should not be trusted. This supports safer use of LLMs for structuring clinical datasets.

entry.title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Jihao Liu, Weikang Shi, Xijie Huang, Linda Wei, Mingjie Zhan, Aojun Zhou, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-based AutoML framework that jointly optimizes architecture, training hyperparameters, and data ratios without task-specific fine-tuning, bridging siloed domain-specific AutoML pipelines. NCode, a unified numerical encoding scheme, converts diverse AutoML design choices into universal discrete sequences, recasting optimization as a unified ranking task learned from limited single-domain optimization trajectories. This enables open-world, cross-domain AutoML via LLMs.

entry.title: Adapting Frozen Promptable Segmenters to User-Defined Taxonomies via Few-Shot Proposal Learning

author.name: Khayrul Islam (Computational Engineering Division, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA), Christopher Frederic Miller (Computational Engineering Division, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA)

entry.summary: SNAP is an annotation pipeline that learns a project's own class boundaries from the labels an annotator draws anyway, fitting a per-project SnapHead on top of a single frozen SAM2.1 pass per image, with the head refitting in seconds after each labeled image.
