entry.summary: The authors introduce two visual focusing losses for self-supervised vision transformers (DINO-style) that align the model's attention with specific image regions, steering multi-head attention selectively during training. This induces emergent spatial specialization of attention heads, yielding diverse and spatially focused perceptual capabilities without labels.

entry.title: PTC-IoU: CPU-Friendly Detection Quality Estimation for Edge Video Analytics

author.name: Wei Geng, Hyerin Kim, Chang Lu, Zhenghao Lu, Joerg Ott

entry.summary: PTC-IoU is a CPU-friendly detection quality estimator for edge video analytics that predicts which frames have potential detection failures needing escalation to a stronger cloud model. It moves the workload off the GPU by compacting detection box histories to support deterministic temporal consistency predictions, avoiding additional neural network load on the GPU running detection.

entry.title: Engagement Estimation in Human-Robot and Human-Human Interactions across Domain, Age and Culture: MultiMediate'26 Challenge

author.name: Marius Funk, Daksitha Withanage Don, Michal Balazia, Victor Oei, Shogo Okada, Fran\c{c}ois Br\'emond, Andreas Bulling, Elisabeth Andr\'e, Philipp M\"uller

entry.summary: This paper describes the MultiMediate'26 challenge on engagement estimation, expanding from momentary continuous engagement in adult conversation to child-child and child-robot play sessions (PInSoRo dataset) with categorical task and social engagement annotations. It diversifies engagement types, age ranges, and interaction types.

entry.title: Maximizing Detection Probability in UAV Search Missions using Random-Key Optimizers

author.name: Antonio Dantas, Elcio Shiguemori, Antonio Chaves

entry.summary: The paper presents a data-driven routing architecture for UAV search-and-rescue missions that combines a closed-loop probability update with Random-Key Optimizers, modeling the problem as a dynamic probabilistic variant of the Open Vehicle Routing Problem. The solver adaptively switches between probability maximization and resource minimization, and notably finds that a systematically biased prior map performs about half as well as flying with no prior at all.

entry.title: Model-Based Imitation Learning For Monocular Vision-Based Navigation

author.name: Basant Sharma, Prajyot Jadhav, Saqi Hussain Kalan, Arun Kumar Singh

entry.summary: This paper proposes a middle ground between model-based planners and end-to-end imitation learning for monocular navigation: model-based imitation learning that embeds explicit collision-avoidance guidance into the model while retaining the flexibility of learned behavior. The goal is to reduce collision rates in novel scenarios without the computational cost and manual tuning of model-based planners.

entry.title: Enhancing Balance and Posture in Material Handling Tasks with a Wearable Robotic Tail

author.name: Eisa Anwar, Sajeeva Abeywardena, Stuart C. Miller, Ildar Farkhatdinov

entry.summary: This human-robot interaction study develops a wearable robotic tail as a dynamic counterbalance for heavy lifting, tested with ten participants in a shelf loading task across active, passive, and no-tail conditions. The active tail reduced centre-of-pressure displacement, trunk motion, and erector spinae and gastrocnemius muscle activity. It offers a novel assistive-wearable approach to reducing musculoskeletal strain in manual labor.

entry.title: Compact and Wide-Force-Range Magnetorheological Hand Exoskeleton for Kinesthetic Feedback in Teleoperation

author.name: Xianlong Mai, Rui Yu, Rui Chen, Daniele Leonardis, Wenbo Li, Domenico Chiaradia, Antonio Frisoli, Shuaishuai Sun

entry.summary: This paper presents a wearable hand exoskeleton using magnetorheological brakes for kinesthetic feedback in teleoperation, achieving a braking torque range of 0.01 to 0.918 Nm at only 39.8 g total mass. It addresses the trade-off between wide force-feedback range and compact wearable design, enabling high-stiffness object rendering.

entry.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors

author.name: Sandesh Thapa, He Bai

entry.summary: The paper develops an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller for quadrotors whose center of mass does not coincide with its geometric center, estimating mass, CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives. The controller corrects trajectory tracking for the estimated parameters.

entry.title: Whose Side? A game where you audit models for secret loyalties

author.name: Cookie penguin

entry.summary: Introduces Whose Side, a playable web game where users chat with a model and try to determine which party it secretly favors, motivated by concerns that open-weight models could be sleeper agents and that LLMs are increasingly trusted to audit other LLMs. The post frames detection of hidden misalignment as analogous to cybersecurity offense-defense dynamics, arguing mechanistic interpretability is not yet able to surface novel misalignment. It is an engaging crowdsourced experiment in detecting hidden loyalties.

entry.title: Spike-to-Field Mechanisms of Turbulence-Like Dynamics in Spatial Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Zequan Liu

entry.summary: This single-authored computational neuroscience study builds a spatial leaky integrate-and-fire spiking network and maps spikes into continuous activity-density and Hilbert phase fields. A delayed, distance-dependent passive-dendrite regime reproducibly generates turbulence-like field structure including phase defects, scaling relations, and power-law avalanche tails. Control experiments isolate which spike-level mechanisms are necessary for these macroscopic observables.

entry.title: Peer Memory Changes Who LLM Agents Consult Without a Detected Gain in Answer Accuracy

author.name: Jeffrey Chu, Anjali Joseph, Rivan Mandot, Feker Demere, Vincent Li

entry.summary: The authors study PeerMem, which saves and reuses multi-agent consultation state (MACE LinUCB estimates) when the same agents recur across tasks, comparing cold, warm, and shuffled initializations over six agents on HotpotQA with reference feedback. Warm memory lowers pooled hindsight regret and shifts consultation toward evidence holders, yet final answer accuracy (token F1) differences remain statistically uncertain. The paper therefore documents that peer memory reshapes agent social behavior without demonstrable accuracy benefit in this setup.

entry.title: LangDepth: Vision-Language Scene Priors for Semantic Binning and Cross-Domain Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Reyhaneh Ahani Manghotay, Jie Liang

entry.summary: LangDepth couples strong visual features with a scene-conditioned metric depth output space: a frozen CLIP encoder and learnable concept keys produce a compact scene descriptor that shapes semantic depth binning before dense prediction. The aim is to make monocular metric depth robust to the very different global scale structure of indoor versus outdoor driving scenes.

entry.title: The Infrastructure Divide: Analyzing Community Stance on Data Center Development via Reddit

author.name: Yoko Koyama, Gongfan Chen, Mansi Saxena

entry.summary: This study applies an LLM-powered opinion-mining framework with Chain-of-Stance prompting to 798 Reddit posts and over 102,000 comments spanning a decade to characterize community stance on data center development. Motivated by roughly 64 billion dollars in blocked or delayed US projects, it systematically mines public discourse where prior engagement methods like surveys fell short.

entry.title: Decentralised Drone Swarm Formation under Silent Failures with ACO Pheromone Claims and PSO Tuning

author.name: Md. Abu Horaira

entry.summary: This paper presents a decentralized drone swarm formation controller combining ACO-based pheromone claims gossiped between neighbors for task allocation and failure detection, PSO-based flight control, and a Voronoi separation filter, with proofs that destroyed-drone claims vanish in bounded time and conflicts resolve consistently. It targets harsh conditions: silent failures, lossy short-range radio, and noisy actuation. It matters for robust multi-robot coordination without central planners.

entry.title: A Gamified Framework for Conflict-Driven Design: Discovering Strategies for Collaborative Resilience with Multi-Agent Learning

author.name: Jin Gao

entry.summary: Models conflict-driven urban resilience design as a non-zero-sum board game in which MARL-trained stakeholder agents allocate scarce resources, reaching about 84% of a simulated-annealing benchmark's total return on a 4x4 board and showing self-play resilience preferences on larger boards, including a 12x12 simulation initialized from historical maps of Tatsumi, Tokyo.

entry.title: An Interpretable Fuzzy Tree for Turbofan Remaining Useful Life with an Auditable Per-Component Diagnostic Layer

author.name: Hugo Henry, Bharadwaj Dogga, Scott Philips, Kelly Cohen

entry.summary: The paper presents an interpretable genetic fuzzy tree for turbofan remaining useful life prediction on N-CMAPSS that exposes an auditable per-component diagnostic layer following the engine hierarchy from sensors to component health, bounded damage, spool damage, and RUL. Staged training fits health leaves to physical targets and freezes them so the prognostic objective cannot reshape diagnostic layers, keeping each level answerable to a distinct maintenance question. It trades some opacity-driven accuracy for rule-level auditability in safety-relevant prognostics.

entry.title: Where Did the Evidence Go? Diagnosing Proof-Set Loss in Long-Term Conversational Memory

author.name: Bogdan Roshchupkin, Maria Khodorchenko

entry.summary: The paper introduces EviCover, a retrieval approach for long-term conversational QA that converts questions into evidence requirements, checks coverage using retrieved source identifiers, and jointly selects supporting turns. It tracks annotated support sets through retrieval, reranking, and answer generation on LoCoMo and REALTALK conversations, diagnosing where complementary evidence is lost. Evaluation focuses on REALTALK's 108 multi-hop questions.

entry.title: VeV: Video-Enhanced Vibration Data Augmentation For Structural Difference

author.name: Joonhee Lee, Jiale Zhang, Sungmin Lee, Ruiqing Wang, Jeffrey Shulkin, Yiwen Dong, Pei Zhang, JeongGil Ko

entry.summary: VeV is a physics-consistent spatial augmentation framework that synthesizes vibration responses at unmeasured coordinates from sparse reference observations, coupling video-based sensing with physical structure-borne wave modeling. It targets smart-farm and structural-monitoring scenarios where vibration models break under relocation or structural change, avoiding costly recalibration. The approach reduces sim-to-real gaps versus numerical digital twins.

entry.title: LoCo: Selective Local Competition for Discriminative Open-Vocabulary Multi-Label Recognition

author.name: Zhuoming Li, Bo Han, Xiaoyu Wang, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: LoCo revisits local prediction in open-vocabulary multi-label recognition, showing it becomes a strong discriminative branch when spatial consistency of local features and compatibility-aware local competition are handled properly. The insight stems from local semantic sparsity: each image region relates to only a subset of queried concepts. The method instantiates these properties to improve recognition beyond global image-text matching.

entry.title: Compact Quantum Channel Attention for Static ASL Recognition: A Controlled Study with Parameter-Matched Baselines

author.name: Ronak Bhalgami, Deep Kothadiya, Nikita Bhatt

entry.summary: QCA-DenseNet uses an eight-qubit variational circuit as a channel-attention gate on DenseNet121 features for static American Sign Language recognition, comparing against parameter-matched classical baselines with signer-held-out splits. The quantum gate has 7.5x fewer parameters than a squeeze-and-excitation block and achieves 94.50% accuracy on unseen signers, slightly above the SE baseline. A controlled study of whether the quantum component genuinely helps.

entry.title: Evaluating Jev on Arabic: Comparing Decision Models and LLMs Across Arabic Tasks and Dialects

author.name: Hossam Elsafty, Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Rajkumar Ramamurthy, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: This evaluation compares 67 systems, including 47 decision models and 20 LLMs, across 43 Arabic tasks and 9 task families under a shared zero-shot protocol, examining performance differences between Modern Standard Arabic and dialects. Jev 1.14.0 scores 69.24 on the aggregate mean metric versus 68.77 for Jev 1.13.0, while Gemma-4-31B leads at 71.81; rankings are stable under various control-removal checks.

entry.title: Fine-resolution land-use segmentation and synthetic image-label augmentation in the Kathmandu Valley

author.name: Pranil Parajuli, Sugam Dahal, Kiran Chandra Dahal

entry.summary: The authors release a hand-annotated six-class land-use corpus covering 202 km2 of Kathmandu Valley across 408 fine-resolution RGB scenes, with challenges including high spectral similarity, near 100:1 class imbalance, and thin linear features. Evaluating five architectures, they show standard random splitting conceals massive spatial leakage: a strict sequence-block split drops performance by up to 0.095 mIoU.

entry.title: Advancements in Cloud-Native Systems: A Systematic Mapping Study of Reliability and Scalability across Cloud-Native, Edge-Native and AI-Enabled Systems

author.name: Shrinivass Arunachalam Balasubramanian

entry.summary: A PRISMA 2020 systematic mapping study covering cloud-native, edge-native, and AI-enabled systems reliability and scalability, screening 4,611 records and including 1,794 primary studies from 2017-2026 plus 95 secondary studies. It provides an evidence-graded synthesis across searches on cloud-native systems, edge AI, agentic AI operations, and physical AI.

entry.title: Feeling Easier, Working Harder: Cognitive Load in AI-Assisted Code Comprehension

author.name: Maryangela White, Maximilian Rose, Matthew Buckman, Amy McDonnell, Francisco Ortega, Bianca Trinkenreich

entry.summary: A 3x2 within-subjects study with 20 novice CS students measuring real-time cognitive workload, comprehension performance, and strategy when reviewing Java code with or without generative AI assistance, using physiological cognitive-load capture. It examines whether AI eases reading while adding extraneous load from the dual-task interaction.

entry.title: Do Machine Learning Models Predict?

author.name: Michele Pizzochero, Emanuele Ratti

entry.summary: This philosophy of science paper argues that the accommodation/prediction distinction survives the transition from theories to ML models but becomes fuzzy, hinging on the relation between a model's training patterns and its output-context patterns. It concludes most successful ML outputs carry strong accommodation character and traces consequences for confirmation and novelty.

entry.title: To SIMD or Not to SIMD: Comparing RVV vs. CGRA SoCs for Non-Linear Functions in AI

author.name: Sameer Deshmukh, Naoya Mizuki, Takumi Honda

entry.summary: The authors build two systems-on-chip, one using an RVV vector processor and one using an elastic (latency-insensitive) CGRA, both coupled to a matrix multiplication unit, to systematically compare hardware options for non-linear functions in LLMs. This fills a gap since prior reconfigurable-unit proposals were never rigorously benchmarked against traditional vector units backed by MMUs. The results are relevant to chip vendors designing edge and high-performance AI accelerators.

entry.title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned

author.name: Satabarto Sarkar, Prithwineel Paul

entry.summary: The paper proposes an exact information-theoretic yardstick for valuing symbolic knowledge added to graph neural networks: the largest log-loss reduction a rule can provide equals conditional mutual information given what the model family computes. It turns rule design into rule discovery by scoring candidate rules on out-of-fold residuals against calibrated permutation nulls, recovering hidden terms such as ring counts on ZINC. This provides a principled alternative to the usual expressivity-gap justifications for injecting symbolic features.

entry.title: $\Sigma$-LeWM: Learning World Models via S-Information for Robot Control

author.name: Xinrui Zu, Michael Przystupa, Zhao Yang, Shujian Yu, Kevin Sebastian Luck

entry.summary: This paper extends decoder-free world models such as JEPA-style and LeWM architectures by adding two extra latent losses, a backward dynamics predictor and an inverse dynamics action predictor, to impose more structure on the latent embedding for robot control. The goal is to show that this additional structure improves manipulation and locomotion performance over latent forward prediction with only an entropy stabilizer. It contributes to the ongoing debate on grounding in decoder-free representation learning.

entry.title: DeepChronos: Temporal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Multi-Step Attack Detection

author.name: Sofia Burkow, Andrea Agiollo, Enkeleda Bardhi, Fernando Kuipers, Kaitai Liang, Georgios Smaragdakis

entry.summary: DeepChronos is a neuro-symbolic system for detecting multi-step cyberattacks that unfold through temporally and causally related phases, addressing the gap between detect-first-correlate-later pipelines and learning-based detectors that cannot guarantee predictions follow real attack progression. It integrates explicit temporal-logical attack relationships with neural learning so that attack-step dependencies are enforced rather than inferred statistically. This targets a real weakness of current intrusion detection systems.

entry.title: The Fast Tree Transform

author.name: Paul Burchard

entry.summary: The paper defines a locally-aggregated transform for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes the Hadamard frequency transform and Haar wavelet transform on the circle. Its frequency part approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian, making it useful as a preconditioner for geometric optimization, and the full transform provides a sparse representation of signals with edges and textures.

entry.title: ConwayNet: Interpretability, Activation Coherence, and Noise Resilience via a Game-of-Life-Inspired Lateral Inhibition in Artificial Neural Networks

author.name: Yair Cohen, Scott M. Gilmore

entry.summary: ConwayNet introduces a differentiable, architecture-agnostic lateral inhibition mechanism for neural networks based on continuous Game-of-Life rules, blending excitatory and inhibitory responses into activation maps in a state-conditioned way. The rule parameters are fixed rather than learned, imposing structural regulation intended to improve noise resilience and mechanistic interpretability. It bridges cellular automata dynamics with deep network design.

entry.title: Stochastic Port-Hamiltonian Gaussian Processes for Learning from Noisy Dynamics on Lie Groups

author.name: Thribhuvan Rapolu, Luke McLennan, Chandrajit Bajaj

entry.summary: LieSPHGP is a Gaussian-process framework for learning rigid-body dynamics that encodes port-Hamiltonian structure and operates on Lie groups and Lie algebras, providing coordinate-consistent optimization without singular parameterizations like gimbal lock. The approach targets sparse, noisy observations of dissipative stochastic dynamics while preserving physical structure and long-horizon stability.

entry.title: Orthogonal Updates for the Win: Towards Accelerated Adaptive Minimax Optimization

author.name: Zhiwei Zhai, Xinyu Wang, Wenjing Yan, Lei Ding, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang

entry.summary: This paper develops AdaSGDA, an orthogonalized update framework for minimax optimization that reduces update anisotropy to stabilize tightly coupled primal-dual dynamics, combined with an adaptive stepsize rule driven by accumulated gradient norms. Orthogonalization changes the optimization geometry, so the method carefully coordinates primal-dual stepsizes. It targets the notorious stepsize sensitivity of single-loop minimax methods.

entry.title: Regret without Optimal-Arm Feedback under Reward-Dependent Delays

author.name: Zhong Han

entry.summary: This paper studies stochastic bandits with reward-dependent, possibly infinite, delays where feedback reports omit the originating round. The proposed Balanced Historical Optimism (BHO) algorithm achieves delay-dependent regret without requiring optimal-arm reports, with lower bounds showing an inverse-square slack cost in the logarithmic regime and linear minimax regret at the boundary. A growing-arm-count construction establishes an Omega(G log K) worst-case lower bound for all learners.

entry.title: Inversion-Free High-Dimensional Counterfactual Inference

author.name: Saketh Vishnubhatla, Pingchuan Ma, Shu Wan, Alimohammad Beigi, Andre Harrison, Adrienne Raglin, Huan Liu

entry.summary: The paper tackles counterfactual inference for high-dimensional nodes such as images, where conventional pipelines invert a factual image to a latent state, modify attributes via a causal graph, and re-render. The authors propose an inversion-free approach that avoids the costly and error-prone latent recovery step. This simplifies and potentially improves counterfactual generation in image domains.

entry.title: Preference-Augmented Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Sensitive Navigation

author.name: Zhaofan Zhang, Yue Chang, Rufeng Chen, Hechang Chen, Sihong Xie, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: The paper augments Implicit Quantile Networks with preference conditioning so that a single policy supports a family of risk preferences rather than a fixed or hand-tuned Conditional Value-at-Risk level. This resolves the mismatch between training-time preference exposure and deployment-time risk requirements for safe navigation under uncertainty. The work targets reliable autonomous navigation with flexible, user-adjustable risk attitudes.

entry.title: On Generalization in Bilevel Least Squares with Overparameterized Neural Networks

author.name: Fares El Khoury, Edouard Pauwels, Samuel Vaiter, Michael Arbel

entry.summary: The paper studies generalization properties of inexact gradient methods for bilevel optimization where both objectives are least-squares regression and hypergradients are obtained by implicit differentiation in function space. The authors derive stationarity bounds in terms of uniform generalization errors of the two regression functions needed for hypergradient estimation, in the overparameterized neural network regime. This addresses a gap in the theoretical understanding of bilevel methods such as hyperparameter optimization and meta-learning.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Sinusoidal Representation Networks for Damage Identification in Ultrasonic Guided Wave Structural Health Monitoring

author.name: Lukas Jilke, Caspar Wasle, Norbert Hosters, Florian Raddatz, Marek Behr, Gerko Wende

entry.summary: This work applies physics-informed SIRENs (implicit neural representations with sinusoidal activations) to ultrasonic guided wave inspection for structural health monitoring, embedding governing PDEs into training. This combats the spectral bias of MLPs in high-frequency regimes while improving interpretability and reducing labeled-data requirements. It demonstrates the value of physics-informed representations for wave-field modeling.

entry.title: AOP-Smart-Finder: A High-Throughput Human-AI Hybrid Framework for AOP Discovery and Evidence Mapping from Large-Scale Literature

author.name: Qinjiang Niu, Lu Yan

entry.summary: AOP-Smart-Finder is a human-AI hybrid framework combining LLMs, RAG, and Python automation for discovering biological events, mining relationships, and constructing Adverse Outcome Pathways from large-scale toxicology literature. It supports both single-compound and predefined-endpoint analysis modes for evidence mapping.

entry.title: Saidzoda-CA-EmbeddingGemma-300M: One Small Embedder for Tajik, Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz

author.name: Tohir Saidzoda, Nekruz Maxudov, Bedil Karimov, Abubakr Abdullozoda, Amin Jalilov, Jonibek Kishvarov, Rahmonali Sharipov, Mariyamkhon Shodyeva

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune EmbeddingGemma-300M into a single embedder for four Central Asian languages, training one more epoch on 279,904 synthetic question-passage pairs plus Tajik and English/Russian replay. Recall@1 rises by 14.4 to 26.0 points on Belebele for each language, with the unified model staying within about 2.8 points of per-language specialists.

entry.title: Generative AI and Oral Proficiency: How ChatGPT Is Transforming English Language Speaking Practice

author.name: Mohammad Mousazadeh

entry.summary: This quasi-experimental study with 380 Iranian English learners compared eight weeks of ChatGPT-mediated speaking practice against human pair work, assessing oral proficiency with CEFR-aligned measures. The design is unusually rigorous for this literature, with balanced gender groups and substantial sample size, providing empirical evidence on whether conversational GenAI can substitute or complement human practice. Findings inform the ongoing debate about AI in language education.

entry.title: RadAI: Gaze-Intention Fusion Pipeline for Attention-Guided Educational Videos in Chest X-Ray Interpretation

author.name: Kavish Mehta, Yuvan Siddharth Katamaneni, Akash Awasthi

entry.summary: RadAI is an end-to-end framework that transforms predicted radiologist gaze into attention-guided educational videos for chest X-ray interpretation training, removing the need for per-case eye-tracking sessions required by eye movement modeling examples. The approach targets visual-search failures in trainees who can identify abnormalities once told where to look. It matters for scalable medical training technology that encodes implicit expert search strategies.

entry.title: From Video to Digital Twin: An Exploratory Study of World Models and Gaussian Splatting on In-the-Wild Video

author.name: Somesh Mohapatra

entry.summary: This exploratory study examines how generative world models and 3D Gaussian Splatting behave on uncurated in-the-wild footage, using a public news walkthrough of a food bank warehouse as the sole input to build a digital twin. A commercial world model recovered camera poses and metric depth from 20 frames, fused into roughly 747,000 Gaussian splats for about 20 US cents, while locally optimized splat models were photorealistic near the filmed path but degraded away from it. It matters as a rare honest, uncaptured-condition stress test of these heavily hyped technologies.

entry.title: Disentangling Channel Semantics in Vision Transformers via Token Decorrelation and Composition-Aware Modulation

author.name: Daeun Kim, Hyesong Choi, Hyejin Park, Dongbo Min

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in multi-channel Vision Transformers where memory/context tokens collapse onto a few dominant channels under high inter-channel redundancy. It proposes MuCa-ViT, which uses token decorrelation and composition-aware modulation to preserve channel-specific semantics alongside shared spatial structure.

entry.title: Agent2BIM: A Systematic Evaluation of Reality-Capture Configurations and Prior Models for As-Built Modeling

author.name: Boyu Wang, Borja Garc\'ia de Soto

entry.summary: Agent2BIM is an agent-based Scan-to-BIM framework that systematically evaluates seven reality-capture configurations (360 panoramas, smartphone video, LiDAR, terrestrial laser scanning, and prior IFC models) against TLS-verified references. Results show high component recall (84-100 percent) but only 9 percent of components reconstructed to full geometric accuracy, revealing a key gap.

entry.title: ADC-RANet: Improving Resolution Adaptive Neural Networks with Attention, Distillation and Calibration

author.name: Jeferson Severino de Araujo, Lilian Hollard, Eric Granger, Marco Pedersoli

entry.summary: ADC-RANet improves the Resolution Adaptive Network (RANet) for dynamic, difficulty-conditioned image classification by combining bottom-up channel attention, top-down cascaded knowledge distillation, and overconfidence correction using a mixture-based calibration loss. The three components work together to improve performance across all computational budgets. This advances anytime/dynamic inference, where cost adapts per input sample.

entry.title: When to Trust Adaptation: Contextual Fusion for Transferable Vision-Language Prompting

author.name: Zhenyuan Chen, Wenshuo Tao, Zhuo Huang, Shuo Chen, Mingming Cheng, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Contextual Adaptive Fusion (CAF) retains four prediction branches pairing frozen and prompted visual and textual representations of a vision-language model, and arbitrates disagreements using predictive confidence combined with how frequently branches favor a class across the unlabeled target collection. Fusion coefficients are learned once on source data, aiming to know when prompt adaptation helps versus harms on a given target image.

entry.title: TIRAD: Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection

author.name: Seongsu Lee, Seunghyun Oh, Seungjae Moon, Youngmin Ro

entry.summary: TIRAD extends residual-based anomaly detection from purely visual discrepancies to the semantic level by defining a Text Residual Feature as the discrepancy between textual descriptions of normal and abnormal states, using it to guide image residual learning. This aims to improve generalization to anomaly types unseen during training.

entry.title: Semantic-Enhanced Sparse Temporal Modeling for Dynamic Engagement Estimation in Multimodal Interactions

author.name: Yangchen Yu, Taoliang Wang, Jia Li, Nor Mazlina Ghazali, Mohd Nazim Mohtar, Bingkun Bao, Richang Hong

entry.summary: SEST addresses dynamic engagement estimation by exploiting conversational semantics through a sparse temporal modeling framework that avoids dense frame-level modeling, which is computationally redundant and sensitive to annotation noise. It aligns dialogue context with continuous audio-visual signals for engagement prediction.

entry.title: Feel My Focus: Gaze-Triggered Digital Twin Creation for Remote Collaboration

author.name: Shih-Yu Ma, Suibi Che-Chuan Weng, Ming-Yuan Pai, Tom Yeh, Ellen Yi-Luen Do

entry.summary: Feel My Focus is a mixed-reality demonstration where sustained gaze on a physical object triggers single-image capture, attention-guided segmentation, and one-shot 3D reconstruction, creating lightweight digital twins for remote collaboration. It integrates gaze-tracking glasses, modular segmentation/reconstruction services, and an MR client with streaming.

entry.title: ExoStack: A Modular and Reconfigurable Software Framework for Wearable Robotics Using ROS 2

author.name: Debadrata Sarkar, Upamanyu Ray, Soumen Sen, Aman Arora

entry.summary: ExoStack is a modular ROS 2 software framework for wearable robots linking body-worn sensing, gait interpretation, assistance generation, and actuation across embedded hubs and a host computer. It includes an ESP32-based sensing/actuation library, multi-hub synchronization, gait-event detection, and human-in-the-loop optimization, with a desktop application for configuration and profiling.

entry.title: Modeling and Estimation of a Towed Marine System

author.name: Josef Matou\v{s}, Simon Hoff, Damiano Varagnolo, Marius S. Rundhovde, Kristin Y. Pettersen, Martin Saska

entry.summary: This paper models and estimates state for a towed marine system of two ASVs, umbilical cables, towfish, and a trailing loop cable, using a lumped-mass approach with Lyapunov-based stability analysis. Two state estimation methods (a reduced-order observer and a perfect-measurement extended Kalman filter) use only onboard ASV sensors, with numerical simulations and experiments.

entry.title: Advocating for a Shared AI Safety Compute Cluster

author.name: Daniele Pace

entry.summary: The author proposes a shared compute cluster for the AI safety community, observing that academic and fellowship groups waste significant resources redundantly setting up environments, downloading weights, and renting GPUs ad hoc without infrastructure expertise. The post sketches practical problems and candidate solutions for pooled, professionally managed compute rather than presenting a finished design.

entry.title: BAIR at CoRL 2026

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A BAIR blog roundup listing the lab's participation at CoRL 2026 in Austin, including 33 main-conference papers, 4 late-breaking posters, and 10 orals and spotlights, plus an early-career keynote from Professor Negar Mehr. It serves as a schedule and index of Berkeley-affiliated robotics learning research rather than presenting individual results.

entry.title: SpinSCI: Mask-Conditioned Spatial-Temporal Spin Transformer for Video Snapshot Compressive Imaging

author.name: Seungki Hong, Zhishuai Zhang, Taekwang Jang

entry.summary: SpinSCI is a mask-conditioned spatial-temporal transformer for video snapshot compressive imaging whose Mask-Conditioned Ising Refinement Block combines attention logits with sensing information as signed spin couplings, gated by finite mean-field updates. It improves PSNR over HiSViT-9 while cutting parameters by 16.9%, FLOPs by 21%, latency by 17-50%, and memory by 62-69%.

entry.title: What Is the Value of AI-Involved Art? Evidence From a Juried In-Person Exhibition

author.name: Wisdom Obinna, Hexuan Wang, Cecile Duncan, Kristelia Garcia, Nina Grgi\'c-Hla\v{c}a, Toni-Lee Sangastiano, Elissa M. Redmiles

entry.summary: Using data from an in-person juried AI art exhibition with 209 artists, lawyers, and computer scientists as creators or evaluators, this study finds nearly half of evaluators would buy AI-involved art, with pricing tied to perceived creativity, visual appeal, and effort. Creators priced by effort alone, and both groups favored prompting users and AI developers over training-data artists in rights and rewards.

entry.title: DiSARM: Diverse and Surprising Association Rule Mining with Large Language Models

author.name: Lijia Liu, Hisashi Kashima

entry.summary: DiSARM is a hybrid framework combining classical association rule mining with LLM world knowledge to assess subjective interestingness during exploratory data analysis, mitigating LLM scalability and statistical reliability concerns by using mining algorithms for candidate generation. It matters for making LLMs useful in data exploration pipelines without abandoning statistical rigor.

entry.title: ATHENA: Hypergraph-Based Learning for Toddler Autism Classification from Eye-Tracking

author.name: Quang-Anh N. D., Duc Pham Minh, Thao Pham Phuong, Minh-Anh Nguyen, Thuy Linh Nguyen Thi, Hung Ha Manh

entry.summary: Proposes ATHENA, an adaptive hypergraph model with a feature-level augmentation technique (FMMix) for classifying autism spectrum disorder in toddlers from gaze-coordinate data. It reports near-perfect metrics on two datasets, including AUCs of 99.80% and 99.86% and accuracies above 98%.

entry.title: Complementarity without ground truth?

author.name: Andrea Ferrario, Alessandro Facchini, Federico Cabitza

entry.summary: The authors examine the concept of human-AI complementarity, which is normally assessed against ground truth labels, and extend it to settings like medical treatment recommendations where no ground truth exists and adequacy is relative to practical goals. They argue for reframing complementarity evaluation along multiple evaluative dimensions. This is a conceptual/philosophical contribution to human-AI interaction methodology.

entry.title: Optimizing Multi-Tier Intermediation in Programmatic Advertising: A DAG-Based Mechanism for Supply Path Optimization

author.name: Amelia B\u{a}dic\u{a}, Costin B\u{a}dic\u{a}

entry.summary: This paper models programmatic advertising supply chains as directed acyclic graphs, using OpenRTB SupplyChain data to trace multi-hop intermediary routes that cause the so-called ad-tech tax. It introduces multi-attribute utility functions and a mixed-integer linear programming formulation handling OR-node substitutable routing and percentage-based fees, aiming to optimize the network equilibrium rather than heuristically trimming paths.

entry.title: Topic-Aware Multi-Task Mental Health Classification with Active Learning-Based Stepwise Relabeling for Social Media Conversations

author.name: Revathy Iswarya Sekaran, Vansh Bhardwaj, Aveek Sahana, Utkarshani Jaimini

entry.summary: Extends a Core Fusion Network for mental health classification on Reddit-style conversations by adding topic prediction as a task alongside condition, emotion, and sentiment classification, and uses active learning-based stepwise relabeling to improve noisy pre-trained model labels. The work targets earlier detection of mental health conditions from social media discourse.

entry.title: Beyond Frame-Level Accuracy: Analyzing Video-Level Stability in Transformer-Based Deepfake Forensics

author.name: Syed Azmul Hasan, Mowmita Pervin Hera, Afroza Lona Mim, M M Jihad Hossain, Hazrat Ali, Mohammad Farhad Bulbul

entry.summary: This is a controlled, reproducible comparison of ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, and ViT-B/16 within a unified face-centric deepfake detection framework using identical preprocessing, augmentation, optimization, and splits on Celeb-DF-like data. It emphasizes video-level stability rather than frame-level accuracy to address inconsistent evaluation pipelines in prior work. The study clarifies which architectures genuinely generalize in deepfake forensics.

entry.title: Frequency-Structure Complementary Modeling for Hyperspectral Image Fusion

author.name: Song Qiya, Tian Siyu, Li Shutao, Dian Renwei, Sun Long, Liu Jinyang

entry.summary: FSCM-Net proposes combining frequency-aware dependency learning (via Fourier-interacted attention) with structure-adaptive local refinement for hyperspectral image fusion. It addresses limitations of conventional spatial-spectral attention and fixed local convolution operators. A solid specialized computer vision contribution for remote sensing applications.

entry.title: Adapting Large Language Models via Multi-Task Learning for Mental Health Problem, Emotion, and Sentiment Detection

author.name: Amir Rafiq Bhat, Rahim Dehkharghani, Zeki Erdem

entry.summary: The study applies sequential multi-task learning with LoRA and 4-bit quantization on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct for mental health, emotion, and sentiment detection over 4,243 social media posts. It shows task ordering materially affects knowledge transfer, with a mental-health-first sequence best for that task and an emotion-first sequence best elsewhere; a joint MTL baseline suffers from task interference and format collapse.

entry.title: Where Should Models Run? A Collaborative Inference Framework for Embodied Intelligence in 6G

author.name: Wanlu Sun, Zhenhui Yuan, Xiang Ji, Yi Han, Qing Li, Gan Zheng

entry.summary: This survey/framework paper examines collaborative inference for embodied agents, partitioning LLM and vision-language-action models across devices, edge servers, and cloud to work within robotic compute and energy limits. It frames the problem of choosing the optimal partitioning point in 6G network settings.

entry.title: Auto-GlaKG: Automated Biomarker Reasoning for Explainable Glaucoma Detection

author.name: Cheng Huang, Zeyu Han, Yian Hu, Yaopeng Ding, Jingxi Qiu, Yadi Liu

entry.summary: Combines a ResNet50 biomarker predictor (cup-to-disc ratio and six morphological signs) with a knowledge-graph reasoner that aggregates signed clinical-prior rule contributions into a glaucoma score. Evaluated on 689 fundus images with stratified group-aware five-fold cross-validation, providing transparent image-to-diagnosis connections.

entry.title: Qubit-to-Motion: Traceable Action Provenance in Hybrid QRL for Robotic Bin-Packing Sequencing

author.name: Hassen Nigatu, Howard Li

entry.summary: This work presents Qubit-to-Motion, a hybrid quantum reinforcement learning framework for robotic bin-packing where four Pauli-Z circuit readouts are the only learned inputs, with a support mask enforcing admissible actions. Each decision is cryptographically logged (SHA-256 fingerprints) and linked to deterministic waypoints and MuJoCo simulation for full action provenance.

entry.title: BharatSynthQA: A Context-Grounded Question Answering Dataset on Indian Temples and Religious Heritage

author.name: Riya Naik (BITS Pilani, K K Birla Goa Campus, India), Shivam Sharma (Indian Institute of Technology Madras, India), Swati Agarwal (PandaByte Innovations Pvt Ltd, India)

entry.summary: Presents BharatSynthQA, a passage-grounded QA dataset on Indian temples and connected religious sites, built by crawling Wikipedia seeded from authentic heritage sources and generating Boolean, factoid, and explanatory QA pairs. It targets a cultural domain where current AI assistants are rarely trained or evaluated.

entry.title: Graph-Based RL for Sequential Rendezvous Planning with Multiple Patrolling USVs

author.name: Seung Woo Han, Hyeon Bin Yeo, Seung Heon Oh

entry.summary: The paper combines grid-based ocean-current-aware path planning, surrogate travel-time prediction, and graph-based reinforcement learning to sequence rendezvous missions for a command USV servicing multiple patrolling vehicles. It optimizes mission completion time and priority-weighted tardiness with empirically validated path feasibility.

entry.title: Evidence or Marginal? What Moment-Vector Propagation Computes in Polynomial Density Neurons

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Spyra

entry.summary: The paper clarifies two competing propagation formulas in polynomial density neurons, proving that p_CD implements Bayesian updating with the belief as virtual evidence while p_EU implements Jeffrey's-rule marginal installation. With a missing input, p_CD returns the model's conditional whereas p_EU generally does not, with proofs and illustrations.

entry.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection

author.name: Ahmed Y. Radwan, Shaina Raza

entry.summary: MARS is a two-path video detector for deepfake and fully generated video forgery detection that combines multiscale spatial and temporal difference operators on frozen features with adapted appearance representations. The design aims to capture forgery traces that vary across manipulation methods and scene content while avoiding false responses to natural texture and motion. It targets the persistent generalization problem in media forensics.

entry.title: ClusLoad: Cluster-Guided Model Sharing for Scalable Distribution Transformer Load Forecasting

author.name: Fangzhou Lin, Guoshun He, Yi Wang, S. Supraja

entry.summary: ClusLoad is a trend-clustered forecasting framework that shares models across distribution transformers with similar temporal behavior, addressing the trade-off between hard-to-scale per-device models and heterogeneous-blind global models. It uses T-Rep temporal embeddings to cluster devices and share forecasting models within clusters. This targets practical smart-grid deployment at scale.

entry.title: Daily Emergency Call Volume Forecasting using Univariate and Multivariate TimeGPT

author.name: Feriel Fass, Djemel Ziou

entry.summary: The study evaluates TimeGPT, a pretrained time-series foundation model, for forecasting daily emergency call volumes on roughly 2,100 daily observations under one-step and seven-day multi-step horizons. Multivariate variants incorporate meteorological, demographic, and socioeconomic variables with careful chronological splits to avoid leakage.

entry.title: LBSNet: Lightweight Brain State Modeling via Learnable Spectral Prototypes for EEG-Based Fatigue Detection

author.name: Kun Jia, Zhenyu Cao, Hanlin Yu, Zeyuan Li, Yixuan Liu, Zhongye Xia, Sen Song, Zhiyuan Ma

entry.summary: LBSNet is a lightweight EEG network for fatigue detection that links spectral band structure to temporal aggregation using learnable spectral prototypes matched to normalized descriptors of relative spectral activity. It combines band-specific temporal convolution, shared spatial projections, and cross-band recalibration.

entry.title: A Computational Model of Inclusive Pedagogy: From Understanding to Application

author.name: Francesco Balzan, Pedro P. Santos, Maurizio Gabbrielli, Mahault Albarracin, Manuel Lopes

entry.summary: The paper presents a computational model of teacher-student co-adaptation that integrates insights from human education into a testable framework, evaluated across teaching strategies in a synthetic classroom environment. It aims to bridge educational science and machine learning, arguing the lack of such models impedes both fields. The work positions inclusive pedagogy as a formal, simulatable process.

entry.title: Guided Co-Attention with Adaptive Gating for Multimodal Medical Data Fusion

author.name: Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Priyanka Siddappa, Md Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma, Md Ripon Ahammed

entry.summary: The paper introduces a multimodal fusion framework combining token-wise guidance, bidirectional cross-attention between image and text representations, and a sample-specific adaptive gating mechanism that learns how complementary cross-modal views should be combined. It is targeted at multimodal medical data fusion.

entry.title: Deep backward multistep high-order regression methods for high dimensional nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations

author.name: Qiang Han, Shaolin Ji, Zihao Xv

entry.summary: This paper proposes MHDBR, a deep learning method for solving high-dimensional semilinear parabolic PDEs via backward stochastic differential equation representations, combining multistep time discretization with regression targets based on conditional expectations. The authors prove error bounds separating time discretization, Monte Carlo sampling, and neural network approximation errors. GroupSort neural networks are used in cases where the generator is independent of the gradient variable.

entry.title: Bayesian transfer for offline Q-learning with multi-task Gaussian processes

author.name: Wenxing Guo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a target-aware Bayesian transfer framework for offline Q-learning using multi-task Gaussian processes that jointly model task-specific Q-functions. Source tasks are weighted via target predictive evidence and MMD, while posterior uncertainty and behavior-supported action sets guide conservative Bellman updates and policy extraction. The authors distinguish Bellman innovations from bootstrap errors to establish stability and predictive source-selection guarantees under task mismatch.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multi-Channel Tip-Over Prediction via Isolated Temporal Models for Planetary Rover Safety

author.name: Siddhant Shete, Raul Dominguez, Frank Kirchner

entry.summary: The paper presents a hierarchical framework for predicting planetary rover tip-over using isolated temporal models: a multi-horizon TCN learns gradual instability from inertial measurements while a GRU-based forward dynamics model flags unexpected deviations via prediction residuals. Combining slow-evolving and abrupt-disturbance signals improves safety in environments with no real-time human intervention. It targets a high-stakes robotics application.

entry.title: Modeling individual and item differences in atypicality inferences with ACT-R

author.name: Guifu Liu, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: The paper models how humans draw pragmatic atypicality inferences from mentions of predictable events using a resource-rational ACT-R framework, with individual exploration tendencies and item-level typicality parameters. These parameters are estimated independently from Raven's Matrices scores and typicality ratings, successfully predicting variation in inference rates.

entry.title: A generalized transition framework for identifying reduction domains in non-binary constituency parsing

author.name: Jungyeul Park, Zihao Huang, Eunkyul Leah Jo

entry.summary: The paper extends a delimiter-guided bottom-up approach to non-binary constituency parsing into a unified calculus covering top-down, in-order, and bottom-up parsing strategies. It provides a stack-invariant proof of soundness and completeness, derives exact oracle action-sequence lengths, and proves a projection-and-lifting theorem showing equivalence between delimiter-guided systems and canonical counterparts. This gives parsing research a cleaner theoretical foundation for non-binary reductions.

entry.title: Beyond Row Alignment: Virtual-Camera-Aware Online Stereo Rectification

author.name: Yizhao Peng, Rui Gong, Zaiwang Gu, Xudong Jiang, Jun Cheng

entry.summary: The paper shows that row alignment alone is insufficient for online stereo rectification in real deployments where calibration drifts, and proposes a virtual-camera-aware formulation that corrects image pairs during operation. This improves robustness of depth estimation under mechanical drift, vibration, and installation changes.

entry.title: Physically Guided TeX Generation for Low-Light Visual Tasks

author.name: Daoheng Li, Jianjun Qian, Mengkai Yan, Jian Yang

entry.summary: TeX-Gen is a physically guided framework generating TeX (thermal/extrinsic) representations from paired visible and infrared images in low-light conditions, aiming at physically interpretable fusion without hyperspectral hardware or pixel-level physical annotations. It disentangles coupled thermal factors that prior appearance-based fusion ignores.

entry.title: NanoNet: Ultra-Lightweight Network for MRI Brain Tumor Classification toward Edge AI

author.name: Tran Nguyen-Le, Huu-Thuan Huynh, Minh-Triet Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: NanoNet is an ultra-lightweight CNN for MRI brain tumor classification with only five inverted residual blocks and 8,132 parameters, inspired by MobileNetV2 but substantially reduced in depth and capacity. The authors further apply dependency-aware structured pruning, knowledge distillation, and INT8 quantization-aware training for additional compression. The goal is accessible medical image analysis on highly constrained edge-AI platforms.

entry.title: AscendMOEA: An Ascend NPU-Accelerated Platform for Tensorized Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms

author.name: Qianlong Dang, Zhiyang Zhang, Baosheng Li, Tianqing Zhu, Junhu Ruan

entry.summary: AscendMOEA is a platform that executes multi-objective evolutionary algorithms on Huawei Ascend NPUs and CPUs by representing decision vectors, objectives, constraints, and auxiliary states as tensors. It addresses the limited parallelism of loop-based implementations and provides reusable interfaces for algorithms, problems, and operators.

entry.title: Trajectory Inversion for a Rudderless Dual Vectored-Thrust Flying Wing

author.name: Weicheng Di, Qiqi Liu, Jinwu Xiang, Daochun Li, Zhan Tu

entry.summary: The paper addresses trajectory generation for a rudderless dual vectored-thrust flying wing, where vectored thrust couples translation and pitch control in the absence of aerodynamic control surfaces. It proposes a trajectory inversion method that jointly optimizes path geometry and timing, balancing curvature-induced acceleration against aerodynamic support to reduce thrust-vectoring demand.

entry.title: Design of a hybrid tendon-linkage finger with coupled and adaptive motion

author.name: Hyojae Kang, Giup Seo, Jae-Young Lee, Yeong Jae Park, Jongwoo Park, Hyunmin Do, So-Hee Park, Dongil Park, Jeongdo Ahn

entry.summary: The paper presents a robotic finger with four mechanical degrees of freedom driven by three actuators, combining bevel-gear abduction, bidirectional tendon-driven MCP/PIP flexion, and a four-bar linkage coupling the DIP joint with a torsional spring and mechanical stopper. Kinematic analysis accompanies the design. It contributes to underactuated dexterous hand hardware that balances capability and transmission simplicity.

entry.title: Industry case studies of adapting TTS for smooth interactions

author.name: Paige Tutt\"osi, El\'eonore Ferrier-Barbut, Anais Scipioni, Olivia Yung, Ha Eun Shim, Ajla Basic, Yue Wang, H. Henny Yeung

entry.summary: The paper reviews adaptive TTS research and notes that production-level implementations are scarce, then reports two case studies applying adapted TTS in real-world HRI settings: an older adult care home and an airport with high noise levels. It addresses the gap where neural TTS designed for average users underperforms for people with specialized listening needs or non-standard speech.

entry.title: Three Phases of Capabilities and Alignment

author.name: beren

entry.summary: Presents a phased framework arguing that as AI progresses through technological phases with different drivers of progress, the alignment challenge migrates in parallel, mirroring each phase's fundamental capabilities challenge. The author argues capabilities and alignment are intrinsically intertwined and that alignment problems become increasingly abstract as model autonomy and generality grow. It is a conceptual synthesis about the evolution of alignment research needs.

entry.title: CRAFT-AI: Capability and Requirement Alignment for Flexible Manufacturing through Agentic AI

author.name: Kiavash Fathi, Hans Wernher van de Venn

entry.summary: CRAFT-AI is an agentic system that translates changing production requirements into manufacturing configurations by combining natural-language requirement interpretation with Asset Administration Shell-based capability descriptions and reusable engineering knowledge. A tool-using agent matches requirements to capabilities and reference implementations, demonstrated on a Factory I/O prototype with twelve scenes.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Exploration of Moire Patterns

author.name: Panagiotis Krokidas, Christos Lazaridis, Vassilis Sioros, Efi-Maria Papia, Vassilios Constantoudis, George Giannakopoulos

entry.summary: This paper presents FruBO, a Bayesian optimization framework for accelerating discovery in computationally demanding materials design, applied to multilayer Moire patterns from six rotated hexagonal lattices. The benchmark contains 600,000 configurations with a highly skewed objective of maximizing pore-size uniformity.

entry.title: A Systematic Comparison of In-Context Learning Strategies for Peptide Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes

author.name: Jiantao Zhao, Andrei Voinea, Mathijs F. J. Mabesoone

entry.summary: The paper provides a systematic benchmark comparing foundation-model in-context learning strategies against classical baselines for peptide property prediction in low-data regimes, addressing a gap in like-for-like evaluations. It evaluates multiple LLM-based and transformer-based approaches on consistent peptide datasets. The results inform when foundation-model ICL genuinely helps for molecular property tasks.

entry.title: Path-Level Structural and Semantic Alignment for Hierarchical Multi-Label Text Classification

author.name: Xindi Wang, Aifen Xiong, Baiyang Wang, Xuri Ge, Robert Mercer, Frank Rudzicz, Yifan Peng, Zhumin Chen, Hongjun Wang

entry.summary: For hierarchical multi-label text classification, the authors use complete root-to-node label paths as a shared unit for both structural and semantic supervision, introducing PathSimNCE, a hierarchy-aware contrastive objective aligning document representations with label paths. The framework adds auxiliary training objectives while keeping a standard multi-label classifier at inference time. This unifies supervision that existing methods formulate separately.

entry.title: Aggregation-Induced Calibration Failure in Sum-Based Label Expansion for Multi-Label Facial Expression Recognition: A Diagnostic Study

author.name: Weihang Yuan

entry.summary: This diagnostic study evaluates Condition-Aware Label Expansion (CALE) for multi-label facial expression recognition across seven backbones and public benchmarks, finding that the aggregation rule rather than the representation determines success. With a fixed 0.5 threshold, aggregate scores vary up to 28x across backbones at low data, while threshold-free mAP stays stable within 1.28x, isolating aggregation-induced calibration failure.

entry.title: A Geometry-Guided Feature-Space Framework for Interpretable Unsupervised 4D-STEM Analysis of Complex Multiphase Materials

author.name: Arda Genc, Daniel A. Bolden, Albert Nguyen, Daniel S. Gianola, Ravit Silverstein

entry.summary: The paper presents an ML framework combining physics-informed geometric descriptors with weighted high-dimensional embeddings for unsupervised analysis of 4D-STEM diffraction data from heterogeneous multiphase materials. Constructing a regularized descriptor space before embedding and clustering improves cluster stability, suppresses noise-driven fragmentation, and reduces sensitivity to embedding hyperparameters.

entry.title: How a Model's Architecture and Performance Influences Explainability: A Study of Grad-CAM and CRAFT in CNN-Based Image Classification

author.name: Kilian G\"oller, Haadia Amjad, Steffen Seitz, Carsten Knoll, Ronald Tetzlaff

entry.summary: Systematically investigates how model performance and architectural complexity influence the quality of XAI explanations, building a pipeline with 10 subsets to evaluate Grad-CAM and CRAFT explanation methods on CNN classifiers. It aims to establish when explanation methods are reliable across scenarios in high-risk applications.

entry.title: FG-DSA: Frequency-Guided Depthwise Separable Attention for Efficient Dense Prediction

author.name: Yiyao Yang

entry.summary: FG-DSA injects frequency-domain priors into spatial attention via a 2D FFT high-pass filtering module, enabling lightweight networks to preserve high-frequency detail for dense prediction and generation under resource constraints. It targets boundary degradation caused by repeated downsampling.

entry.title: Scale-Consistent Monocular Fisheye Visual Odometry via Spherical Bundle Adjustment-Guided Unsupervised Depth Learning

author.name: Wanhui Luo, Hongbo Zhao, Yi Zhou, Qijun Chen, Yiming Nie, Rui Fan

entry.summary: S2D-FVO is a monocular fisheye visual odometry framework that couples spherical bundle adjustment with unsupervised depth learning to fight scale drift over long trajectories. It accounts for the non-uniform relationship between pixel reprojection residuals and angular deviations between viewing rays, addressing distortion-specific challenges of fisheye depth estimation.

entry.title: Evaluating classification and explainability in multimodal petrographic image analysis

author.name: Thomas James Wood, Oktay Karaku\c{s}, Can Ey\"upo\u{g}lu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the released LITHOS dual-stream vision transformer for petrographic thin-section classification using 105,802 expert-annotated grains across 25 categories, examining whether errors follow mineralogical taxonomy and how each optical view (PPL and XPL) contributes to predictions. It finds most misclassifications are taxonomically adjacent, suggesting errors reflect genuine mineral similarity. The work matters for trustworthy AI deployment in geoscience.

entry.title: Receiver-Resolution APS-PDP Maps for Wireless Channels: Benchmarking and Coarse-to-Fine Modeling

author.name: Peilin Zheng, Haozhe Jia, Xiucheng Wang, Wenshuo Chen, Nan Cheng

entry.summary: UrbanADPSMap is a benchmark that converts ray-traced wireless channel supervision into fixed-grid Angle Power Spectrum and Power Delay Profile targets by explicitly modeling bandwidth- and aperture-limited receiver kernels, removing ambiguity in learning targets and evaluation conventions. It also proposes coarse-to-fine modeling. It matters for standardizing AI-for-wireless research where inconsistent reconstruction conventions undermine comparisons.

entry.title: Automated Knowledge Acquisition Pipeline for Disassembly Instructions: A Comparison of NLP and Generative AI Frameworks

author.name: Tim Schnieders, Tareq Maximilian Gabriel Ahrari, Oliver Petrovic, Christian Brecher

entry.summary: This paper compares a rule-based NLP framework against a generative AI framework using LLMs for extracting disassembly instructions from unstructured manuals into structured, machine-readable formats, supporting circularity and Re-X principles for SMEs. It provides a data foundation for automating disassembly. The work is applied and domain-specific, contributing to industrial automation.

entry.title: How Many Examples, and Which Ones? A Study of In-Context Learning for Natural Language Inference

author.name: Georgos Dikaios, Isidoros Perikos, Ioannis Hatzilygeroudis

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks decoder-only LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and Phi 4) on natural language inference across MNLI, QNLI, and SciTail with zero-shot and few-shot prompting, examining how many examples and which ones matter. Prior work has focused on encoder or encoder-decoder models, so this fills a gap in decoder-only LLM in-context learning for NLI. Note that Phi 4 has been available since January 2025, so this is analysis of existing models rather than new releases.

entry.title: Federated Lightweight Transformer for Network-Layer Cyberattack Detection in O-RAN

author.name: Hong Nhung Nguyen, Abdulahi Badrudeen, Yekaterina Kim, Truong Thu Huong, Sunwoo Kim

entry.summary: Presents a federated lightweight Transformer for privacy-preserving network-layer intrusion detection in Open RAN, where each site trains locally on ordered network-flow records and shares only model parameters. Realistic heterogeneity is modeled via Dirichlet partitioning of client datasets across RAN sites.

entry.title: CXR-CMFA: A Cross-Modal Feature Aggregation Network for Chest X-Ray Pathology Classification

author.name: Talukder Hasnat Zadid, Jahin Sultana, Felipe Bochini Brisola, Kishore Roy, Mysha Rahman, Syeda Asrafa Islam, Md. Abdullah-Al-Jubair

entry.summary: CXR-CMFA is a lightweight cross-modal network for binary chest X-ray pathology classification that fuses a dual-stream visual encoder (EfficientNet-B0 for global anatomy, DenseNet-121 for local pathology) with TF-IDF features from radiology reports. It aims to capture complementary diagnostic context while remaining cheaper than large vision-language models. The work targets practical deployment under overlapping anatomy and image-quality variation.

entry.title: Structurally Separated DAG Learning with Multi-Scale Normalized Closure

author.name: Shuai Feng, Hao Yan

entry.summary: The paper extends continuous DAG learning by adding matrix-valued closure logits that explicitly represent multi-hop structural relations per ordered pair, built via repeated squaring in log space with per-scale path-length normalization. Supervised alongside data fit, sparsity, and a DAGMA-style barrier, SMNC counteracts product-style attenuation along long cycles in structure discovery.

entry.title: Does Pose Encoding Matter? Analyzing Geometric Representations for Discrete Motion Vocabulary Learning

author.name: Amir Kimiyaie, Nahal Mafi, Hamed Tabkhi

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how four different pose encodings (joint heatmaps, root-relative positions, 6D rotations, and others) affect the quality of vector-quantized discrete motion vocabularies, including a geometric characterization of heatmaps as morphological dilations of joint sets. The question is which latent geometry admits efficient discretization for motion pipelines.

entry.title: Jointly Optimizing Memory, Computing and Offloading for Energy-Efficient DNN Inference

author.name: Yunchu Han, Zhaojun Nan, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: The authors formulate energy minimization for DNN inference under deadline constraints as a mixed-integer nonlinear program that jointly optimizes memory allocation, computing resources (DVFS), and computation offloading, treating memory as a critical bottleneck. They address the coupling between offloading and resource optimization.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for License Plate Identification and Character-Recognition

author.name: Saurabh Kumar, Dewant Katare, Prakriti Jain

entry.summary: Presents a unified license plate detection and character recognition framework for low-power edge hardware using a shared CSP-Darknet/PANet encoder with anchor-free localization and RoIAlign-based sequence recognition, avoiding image-space cropping. Trained on an AI-assisted dataset of ~37,000 manually verified images covering all 50 US states and deployed as an INT8 TensorRT engine.

entry.title: The comparison of density estimation for transfer learning in Banach, Hilbert, Euclidean spaces

author.name: Maryam Alsadat Kazemian, Azam Bastanfard

entry.summary: This paper summarizes prior work on non-Hilbertian domain adaptation, proposing Banach Manifold Transfer Learning (BMTL), which embeds features on a geodesic manifold and uses total variation alignment via L1 density regularization. It critiques the standard reliance on Euclidean/RKHS geometry and symmetric L2 divergences in domain adaptation.

entry.title: Detecting Common Golfing Faults Using AI and Video-Derived Biomechanical Features

author.name: Oliver Martin, Jeff Clark, Nawid Keshtmand

entry.summary: The paper presents a marker-free pipeline that detects named golf swing faults from ordinary video by tracking body pose and clubhead in a body-centered frame and classifying coach-relevant biomechanical quantities with shallow boosted trees. It detects over-the-top and early-extension faults with cross-validated ROC-AUCs of 0.975 and 0.911 on several hundred public-source swings.

entry.title: Calibrated Alarm Thresholds for Compact Fire and Smoke Detectors

author.name: Vikas Sandireddy

entry.summary: This work reframes camera-based fire and smoke detection evaluation at the image-alarm level rather than box-level mAP, comparing three rules for aggregating detections into one alarm score and using split conformal prediction to set thresholds on held-out data with expected missed-fire guarantees. Two compact YOLOv8n-style detectors are evaluated on the D-Fire test set.

entry.title: Patching Up Circuit Learning via Parameter Sharing

author.name: Charles Bricout, Gennaro Gala, Viacheslav Borovitskiy, Antonio Vergari

entry.summary: This work revisits parameter-sharing and patch-based training practices for probabilistic circuits, generative models that guarantee tractable inference. The authors identify a surprising learnability issue where independence-assuming models can outperform non-independent ones in likelihood, and propose RePA, a recursive parameter-sharing construction that fosters weight sharing across patches to scale circuits to high-dimensional data. This advances the scalability of tractable probabilistic generative models.

entry.title: Adapting Small Language Models to Romanized Nepali: Tokenizer Fertility, Reference Likelihood, and Generation Metrics

author.name: Pujan Pant, Sagar Newpane, Hari Sitaula, Manish Sakhakarmy

entry.summary: This study adapts three 2-3B base models (Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B, Gemma-2-2B) to Romanized Nepali using an identical QLoRA recipe on deterministically transliterated instruction data, evaluated with reference-overlap metrics, byte-normalized likelihood, and output audits. Fine-tuning substantially improves chrF++ from roughly 10-14 to 29-31 and lowers bits per byte. It provides a careful, controlled recipe for low-resource, non-standard-script adaptation of small open models.

entry.title: reComposer: Editable Planning for Controllable Image Generation

author.name: Susie S. Y. Li, Angie Boggust, Fred Hohman, Donghao Ren, Dominik Moritz, Yannick Assogba

entry.summary: reComposer is a process-oriented image-generation interface that decomposes evolving user intent into editable creative decisions such as subject, composition, and palette, supporting conversational and direct manipulation of the plan. It aims to move beyond monolithic prompting by letting users explore underspecified goals and alternatives during creation. The work matters as an exploration of human-AI co-creation beyond prompt-revision loops.

entry.title: Clinical Evidence-Guided Residual Learning for Medication Recommendation with Dynamic DDI Regularization

author.name: Zesheng Li, Chengchang Pan, Honggang Qi

entry.summary: EviDrug is a framework for medication recommendation that combines a clinical-memory backbone (visit-aware encoder, training-case memory, interaction blocks) with gated residual corrections grounded in clinical evidence. It adaptively regularizes drug-drug interaction (DDI) constraints to balance safety and predictive quality.

entry.title: One-Shot Hierarchical Federated Clustering for Distributed Non-IID Biomedical Data Analysis

author.name: Shenghong Cai, Yiqun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a one-shot hierarchical federated clustering framework for multi-institutional biomedical data, where clients perform local distribution exploration and communicate one-way prototype-level summaries to a server for aggregation. The design avoids the recursive communication overhead and privacy leakage risks of standard hierarchical clustering on non-IID siloed data. It targets privacy-preserving disease-profile discovery across hospitals.

entry.title: Means vs. Foundation Models for Emergency Call Forecasting

author.name: Feriel Fass, Djemel Ziou, Marie-Flavie Auclair-Fortier

entry.summary: The paper compares generalized means, specifically Hölder and Lehmer means, against fine-tuned TimeGPT for daily emergency call forecasting across horizons of one to seven days. The simple mean families match or slightly beat the foundation model on short horizons, with MAE reductions around 1.24 percent, validated with Diebold-Mariano tests.

entry.title: How to start a conversation proactively?

author.name: Mohit Nathani, Aaditya Gupta, Eshwar Dhande, Chayan Sarkar

entry.summary: The paper addresses proactive conversation initiation by social robots and LLM agents, noting that current models are turn-reactive and produce generic openers even with contextual information. The authors propose a principled definition of conversational context and a framework for deciding how and when to initiate interaction. This targets a real gap for embodied agents where poorly timed initiations harm engagement.

entry.title: Optimized Car Damage Detection Using CNN and Object Detection Model

author.name: Sania Ejaz, Jaison Shajan Thomas, Zaheeruddin Ahmed, Sushma Hans

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage pipeline for vehicle damage assessment: a CNN first classifies images as damaged or undamaged, then an object detection model localizes and categorizes defects into scratch, dent, glass shatter, and smash. It targets practical applications such as insurance claims, accident reporting, and garage documentation, using unified models with transfer learning.

entry.title: Trainability-Simulability Tradeoff in Parameterized IQP-based Reinforcement Learning Policies

author.name: Andr\'e Sequeira

entry.summary: This paper analyzes parameterized IQP quantum circuits as RL policies, where classical decoders aggregate 2^n measurement outcomes into smaller action spaces. The aggregation mitigates initialization concentration but makes the policy classically simulable, and the authors characterize this trainability-simulability tradeoff via the decoder's Fourier-Pauli expansion, expressing policy variance exactly through groups of Pauli components. The analysis connects quantum circuit hardness conjectures to practical RL policy design.

entry.title: Recursive Pricing and Incumbent Subtree Column Generation for Solving Optimal Classification Trees

author.name: Tengmu Hu, Chen Chen, Theodore T. Allen

entry.summary: The paper develops ISCG-OCT, a column generation algorithm for provably optimal classification trees that exploits their recursive structure. It introduces a mixed set-packing/partitioning formulation and an incumbent-centered pricing scheme, showing that fixing branching decisions decomposes the remaining pricing problem into independent subproblems.

entry.title: SadaqahStories: A Verified English-Arabic Corpus of Charity Stories for Children, with an Audit of Errors in AI-Drafted Religious Narratives

author.name: Wajdi Zaghouani, Spencer Striker

entry.summary: The authors release SadaqahStories, a parallel English-Arabic corpus of 41 illustrated children's stories about Islamic charitable giving, drafted with LLM assistance, audited against hadith, Quranic, and historical sources, and finalized with scholar sign-off. Each story ships in three versions (AI draft, audited text, child-oriented final) with a correction log, enabling study of how AI drafts of religious and historical content fail. The audit reportedly found substantive errors in the AI drafts.

entry.title: ReGKG-2025: A GKG-Compatible Reconstruction of the GDELT Global Knowledge Graph for the Missing Period of 14 June to 2 July 2025

author.name: Nikita A. Klimin (HSE University, Moscow, Russia)

entry.summary: This paper reconstructs the missing segment of the GDELT Global Knowledge Graph caused by a June 2025 pipeline outage, producing 281,620 article records covering all 1,665 missing 15-minute batches. Records were recovered from Common Crawl and the Wayback Machine, translated, manually reviewed, and converted to the GKG 2.1 layout with full provenance. It matters primarily as a community resource restoring continuity for researchers dependent on GDELT data.

entry.title: Efficient 3D plant segmentation through multiscale graph learning and optimized geometric processing

author.name: Jesus Ivan Ruiz-Martinez, Andres Mendez-Vazquez, Eduardo Rodriguez-Tello

entry.summary: The paper develops a multiscale edge-based graph attention model with roughly 78 thousand parameters for plant point cloud segmentation, combining local shape descriptors, two neighborhood scales, and residual stem-leaf correction. It is validated on maize data and deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5 for precision agriculture, with comparisons against hierarchical, graph, and transformer baselines including PointNeXt. It targets accurate organ segmentation on compact computing platforms.

entry.title: End-to-End Joint Training of Super-Resolution and Compression Artifact Removal for Industrial Machine Vision

author.name: Dang BuiDinh, Sang NguyenQuang, Anh NguyenPhuong, Wen-Hsiao Peng, Xiem HoangVan

entry.summary: This paper proposes jointly training super-resolution and compression artifact removal in a single end-to-end framework for industrial machine vision, optimizing both human-perception and machine-perception (task-driven) objectives. It explores fixed-weight versus uncertainty-based dynamic weighting to balance the two goals, motivated by bandwidth-constrained edge-device defect detection.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Adaptation After Deployment: A Position on World Models for Remote Robot Teams

author.name: Jamie Santos, Kagan Tumer

entry.summary: This position paper argues that world models merit investigation for post-deployment adaptation of remote robot teams, where shifting deployment conditions can reorder the Pareto set of multi-objective policies. It outlines how world models could predict policy outcomes under updated conditions to reduce risk to hardware during evaluation.

entry.title: Compute Regeneration through Re-Productization: Reorganizing Retired Edge AI Silicon into a Delivered Multilingual Service Robot

author.name: Hongyu Luo, Sun Tie, John Wang

entry.summary: GEdgeBot is a case study in re-productization: rebuilding a multilingual service robot around a retired 32 GB Jetson AGX Xavier, with five on-device AI services, a seven-language speech chain, and a deterministic control boundary between AI orchestration and an STM32 motor controller. The paper frames retired-but-functional edge compute as a systems design resource and documents audits of the control state machine and readiness barriers. It contributes a sustainability-oriented engineering methodology rather than new AI methods.

entry.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow

author.name: Tielin Ma, Junlin Zhang, Jingcheng Fu, Chongwen Jiang, Chuan Ye

entry.summary: Using large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition, the paper studies aerodynamic forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow at Re ~ 1.0e4, comparing smooth cylinders and four stranded cables at four inclinations. It finds that cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth govern differences, and that surface pressure contributes 94.9-98.3% of mean normal force.

entry.title: My views on AI development and why I’m joining Anthropic

author.name: alexbleakley

entry.summary: The author publicly states their core views on AI risk and development on the eve of joining Anthropic's alignment team, deliberately recording their pre-employment positions to guard against future incentive-driven view distortion. They advocate an agenda focused on restraining AI development until safe AI can be achieved.

entry.title: Exploring the world's languages with Language Explorer

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post introducing Language Explorer, a tool or effort for exploring and analyzing the world's languages in the natural language processing domain. The supplied content is minimal, offering only the category tag and no substantive technical detail.

entry.title: Interactive Person Retrieval with On-the-Fly Visual Feedback

author.name: Lyucheng Qian, John Yuehan Zhang, Pingyu Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces VFI-PR, a new interactive person retrieval paradigm in which retrieved candidates generate visual feedback that informs the next question in a question-answer refinement loop, unlike prior methods that learn static offline question orderings. The answerer sees only witness-side memory and cannot report candidate-specific visual differences, making the feedback loop the core technical challenge.

entry.title: Perils and opportunities of AI for public climate services

author.name: Francesca Larosa, Sandro Calmanti, Matteo De Felice, Marcello Petitta

entry.summary: A perspective on how generative and machine-learning systems are transforming climate services production, access, and interpretation, highlighting opportunities in automation and tailoring alongside concerns about privately controlled algorithms, data infrastructure, governance, transparency, equity, and economic sustainability.

entry.title: SWXAI: A Unified Multimodal Explainability Library for Space Weather Forecasting and Heliophysics

author.name: Benedict Antonio Mervyn, Anli Ji, Manolis K. Georgoulis, Berkay Aydin

entry.summary: SWXAI is an open-source library unifying explainable AI workflows for image, time-series, and tabular models in space weather forecasting and heliophysics, with a common extensible interface, validation, adaptation, and persistent explanation storage. It addresses fragmented XAI tooling across heterogeneous scientific data types.

entry.title: When Sensors Fail: Coverage Auditing with Incomplete Sensor Records

author.name: Chung-I Huang, Wen-Yi Chang
