The authors prove the coverage guarantee carries over to adaptive intervals and derive all quantities in closed form without model retraining for fixed-basis cases.

entry.title: When does an agent learn its dynamics? An extension to Touchette-Lloyd

author.name: Sumayya M

entry.summary: Sumayya M extends the Touchette-Lloyd theorem (if a policy reduces environmental entropy beyond the best blind policy, its actions must share mutual information with the state) to the case of agents that must learn hidden environment dynamics, such as an unknown coin bias or transition parameter. ARIA-funded and developed with feedback from Alex Altair and Alfred Harwood, this formalizes when agents come to model rules rather than just states.

entry.title: Rethinking Agent Trajectory Compression: A Workflow-Aware Perspective

author.name: Qijia Zhuang, Rui Liu, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: WAAC is a workflow-aware framework for compressing long-horizon agent trajectories, which structurally models successful historical trajectories to extract reusable compression experience and applies online backward dependency analysis to preserve cross-step information that fixed truncation or text-importance rules would discard. This targets growing context overhead from multi-step tool interactions.

entry.title: Forecasting cumulative intraoperative hypotension burden: patient-disjoint evaluation of quantile boosting and alert policies

author.name: Yunfan Zhao

entry.summary: This study forecasts conditional quantiles of the next 15-minute mean arterial pressure deficit below 65 mmHg using public VitalDB data, going beyond binary hypotension alarms to capture depth and duration (burden). With patient-disjoint splits across roughly 100,000 labeled windows, it compares climatology, calibrated persistence, and quantile boosting variants, and explicitly separates forecasting performance from episode-warning utility in alert policies. The design addresses whether better forecast scores translate to better clinical alerts.

entry.title: Patching the Blind Spots: Reversible LLM Rule Overlay for Frozen Fraud Detectors

author.name: Bo Qu, Zhurong Wang, Frank Zahradnik, Ming Ouyang

entry.summary: The authors propose patching a deployed gradient-boosted fraud detector without modifying it: LLMs propose rules anchored on SHAP-identified underweighted features, which are screened, calibrated, and applied as a reversible additive log-lift overlay at the production cut-off. Pooling three LLM backbones trades peak gain for a bounded worst case on real-world selection-biased data.

entry.title: FusionCLIP: Multimodal Contrastive Pretraining for Fusion Plasma Diagnostics

author.name: Qiang Chen, Xiao Wang, Qingquan Yang, Hao Si, Zikang Yan, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: FusionCLIP is a multimodal contrastive pretraining framework aligning visible-light videos of tokamak discharges with asynchronous multivariate diagnostic signals. It handles challenges such as sparse plasma regions in video frames and differing sampling rates via spatiotemporal stability selection and a temporal query encoder. This extends CLIP-style representation learning to scientific fusion diagnostics, a relatively unexplored modality pairing.

entry.title: Active Learning of Robust Models

author.name: Mizu Nishikawa-Toomey, Andreas Kirsch, Laurent Charlin, Dhanya Sridhar

entry.summary: This paper unifies two previously separate research threads: active learning for label efficiency and robustness to distribution shift between training and deployment. The authors develop methods that intelligently select points to label so as to learn models robust under shift, motivated by domains like medical diagnosis where labeling is costly and shift is common. Combining these problems is a natural but underexplored direction with practical relevance.

entry.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents

author.name: Tural Mehtiyev, Biruk Tadesse, Lawrence Arkoh, Wesley Assun\c{c}\~ao

entry.summary: This study examines how stale repository instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) mislead LLM coding agents, framing the issue as documentation debt whose interest is paid in every agent session. It investigates what causes agents to act on stale instructions, the behavioral costs, and how agents recover, noting that task-success-only evaluations miss these hidden costs. It is a valuable software-engineering contribution as coding agents become standard development tools.

entry.title: SSF-Net: A Spatial-Spectral Fusion Network for Accurate PDE Operator Learning

author.name: Siqi Zhao, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: SSF-Net is a dual-branch architecture for PDE operator learning combining a multi-directional Mamba spatial branch for local dynamics with a spectral branch for global coupling effects. It aims to capture both local propagation and global interactions with low model complexity, improving on standard neural PDE solvers.

entry.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks

author.name: Eloi Martinet, Leon Bungert

entry.summary: Proves that the set of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with at most N neurons is weakly closed in W^{1,p}, guaranteeing existence of minimizers for coercive energies (covering Deep Ritz, Sobolev training, Lipschitz learning), while showing two-hidden-layer bounded-width ReLU networks are not closed. These topological results clarify when neural optimization problems are well-posed.

entry.title: Cutpurse: Decomposing Explanation-Guided Model Extraction on Tabular Data

author.name: Seyma Selcan Magara, Hanru Zhang, Fatme El Zahraa Hamad, Nico Pfeifer, Mete Akg\"un

entry.summary: Decomposes explanation-guided model extraction into an attribution channel (feature rankings) and a coordinate channel (candidate perturbation values), finding across six datasets and five target families that attribution rankings provide no systematic extraction advantage while useful bin edges are largely reproducible from adversary data. Challenges the assumption that explanation APIs inherently raise extraction risk.

entry.title: Turkish Multimodal Video Fact-Checking: A New Dataset and a Comparison of Zero-Shot Agentic and Fine-Tuned Systems

author.name: Azra A\c{c}{\i}l

entry.summary: Introduces TeViD, reportedly the first multimodal video fact-checking dataset for Turkish, built from IFCN-certified Teyit.org articles plus translated Snopes data and synthetic examples. Compares agentic zero-shot and fine-tuned verification pipelines sharing the same open-source base model.

entry.title: Bootstrap Your Own AV-Proxies: Adaptive Contrastive and Prototype Learning for Audio-Visual Segmentation

author.name: Junbo Zhang, Hang Su, Zhaofan Li, Hang Dong, Chao Sun

entry.summary: BYOAVP tackles audio-visual segmentation's semantic incompleteness and cross-modal gap with a self-supervised audio enhancement component and adaptive contrastive/prototype learning, avoiding complex data-dependent priors that hurt cross-domain generalization. The prototype-based framework suppresses fusion noise while simplifying audio-visual correlation modeling.

entry.title: ExQuery: Explicit Structured Query Priors for Temporal 3D Object Detection

author.name: Honglin Sun, Yifei Zhang, Junyang Zhang, Kenji Hashimoto

entry.summary: ExQuery restructures sparse query-based 3D detectors so each query is organized into a shared semantic context slice plus explicit physical-state slices for center, dimensions, orientation, and velocity. Predicted physical states are transformed by ego motion to reconstruct temporal queries, fused with stored latent features via gating. This improves temporal 3D object detection for autonomous driving.

entry.title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking

author.name: Shengjun Deng, Yinghan Zhang, Chengrui Wei, Liu Liang, Songyuan Liu, Pengkun Zheng, Yajun Zheng, Ying Zhang, Yuan Tian, Xi Li, Teng Wang

entry.summary: DobotTrack is a vision-language-action framework for language-guided embodied person tracking that combines auxiliary grounding supervision (segmentation, bounding boxes, visual-spatial classification, future prediction) with a target-conditioned historical visual compression module. It systematically ablates five auxiliary tasks to improve target identification and following from egocentric views.

entry.title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution

author.name: Haley Duba-Sullivan, Emma J. Reid, Charles A. Bouman, Gregery T. Buzzard

entry.summary: AdaptivePnP jointly estimates the step size and noise level parameters of plug-and-play image reconstruction at every iteration from the data-fitting residual, with a theoretical analysis showing the residual is zero-mean Gaussian with covariance parameterized by those parameters. This eliminates grid-search tuning and separate noise estimation for deconvolution problems.

entry.title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education

author.name: Subhankar Maity, Faiza Belbachir, Omar Boucelma, Guilherme Medeiros Machado

entry.summary: The paper extends the Min-K% probability membership inference approach with synthetic non-member code generation to trace code provenance, distinguishing student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced Python code. This addresses a growing problem in programming education, where LLM-generated submissions undermine the reliability of code as evidence of learning. Evaluations cover older open models like GPT-2 and DistilGPT-2 as well as commercial models including GPT-5 and Gemini.

entry.title: Typed-Centrality Grounding for Agentic GraphRAG: A Symbolic Approach for Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Rosario Napoli, Antonio Celesti, Massimo Villari, Maria Fazio

entry.summary: This work adds a symbolic layer to agentic GraphRAG via typed centrality measures on knowledge graphs, enabling deterministic reasoning alongside textual similarity rather than treating KGs as homogeneous graphs. The approach aims to ground agent reasoning in structured, deterministic knowledge.

entry.title: From Geometry to Function: A Multi-Task LiDAR Benchmark Dataset for Semantic and Functional Parsing of Urban Facades

author.name: Abdiaziz Muse, Tooba Javed, Tao Pu, Jiju Poovvancheri, Dong Chen

entry.summary: HFX3D is a large urban facade LiDAR benchmark with roughly 492 million points from 26 buildings in Halifax, captured across seasons, day/night, and weather conditions, annotated at semantic, instance, and functional-attribute tiers. It is claimed to be the first facade dataset pairing geometry and semantics with functional labels, supporting digital twin and heritage applications.

entry.title: SPSC: Zero-Shot Cross-Subject EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Semantic Preservation and Subspace Calibration

author.name: Yutang Lu, Shuai Jiang, Fei Su, Zhicheng Zhao

entry.summary: SPSC is a framework for zero-shot cross-subject EEG-to-image reconstruction that addresses low signal-to-noise EEG signals and cross-subject semantic shifts without target labels or target image embeddings. It combines Object Mask Contrastive Regularization during backend training with a subspace calibration step to align source EEG embeddings with unseen subjects' image-embedding manifolds. This advances brain decoding toward practical generalization across people.

entry.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters

author.name: Constantinos Karouzos, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: LambdaMix is a parameter-efficient post-training method that learns a preference-conditioned family of policies: one low-rank adapter per objective over a frozen base model, with a preference vector selecting the adapter mixture and weighting separately normalized rewards. A single training run then supports changing objective trade-offs at inference time without further optimization. This addresses the practical need to serve diverse user preferences from one model efficiently.

entry.title: Beyond the Grid: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for Interpretable Signal Decomposition

author.name: Nick Janssen, Melanie Schaller, Bodo Rosenhahn

entry.summary: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit (CDP) learns parameters of closed-form functions directly on a continuous manifold for interpretable signal decomposition, overcoming spectral leakage and grid mismatch in classical matching pursuit. Unlike prior continuous methods restricted to a single analytic family, CDP searches a heterogeneous library spanning periodic, trend, transient, and discontinuous structures via greedy optimization. This revives classical sparse coding with modern differentiable machinery.

entry.title: ELPAC: Endpoint-Anchored Latent Progression with Stage-Varying Multimodal Coordination

author.name: Shengxian Ding, Yifei Zhang, Xinyuan Tian, Yuanshuang Guo, Yize Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces ELPAC, a Bayesian framework jointly inferring latent disease stage, progression subtype, and stage-varying multimodal coordination in aging cohorts with partially observed imaging, plasma, and cognitive data. It targets the underexplored joint problem of endpoint-anchored staging with progression-resolved residual coordination across modalities.

entry.title: Grid-Oriented Probabilistic Load Forecasting for AI Data Centers

author.name: Qingyi Yao, Ding Lin, Tianqiao Zhao, Meng Yue, Jianhui Wang

entry.summary: Presents an open benchmark for probabilistic load forecasting of AI data centers using measured GPU power from a 448-GPU cluster, evaluated across prediction, online calibration, scenario generation, and reserve sizing. Shows that regime-conditioned online calibration substantially improves coverage under workload shifts and that temporal dependence is essential for realistic ramps.

entry.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction

author.name: Aadya Agrawal, Ho Kei Cheng, Alexander Schwing

entry.summary: FlowMoP is a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse, stochastic 3D motion futures for multiple people, modeling global trajectories and root-relative poses. It uses B-spline reparameterization for smoothness and a dual-stream transformer to condition each agent on neighbor motion for interaction-aware prediction.

entry.title: DINO-Nucleus: Multi-Level Self-Supervised Features for Nucleus Instance Segmentation

author.name: Mohammad Sarhangzadeh, Elyar Esmaeilzadeh, Doruk Oner

entry.summary: DINO-Nucleus is a parameter-efficient framework using multi-level self-supervised DINOv2 features for nucleus instance segmentation and counting, jointly predicting regions, instance flows, and nucleus centers with a consistency objective. It reduces reliance on complex models and sensitive post-processing for separating touching nuclei in microscopy.

entry.title: TriNetra: Thermal-Reliability-Guided RGB-Thermal Fusion and Tracking for Surveillance

author.name: Sadique Khatib, Aditya Ahirrao, Vedant Sonawane, Disha Kapse, Y. D. Bhise

entry.summary: TriNetra is a reliability-aware RGB-thermal surveillance framework that computes a label-free frame-level Thermal Reliability Coefficient from five image cues, uses it to gate the thermal branch of a dual-branch YOLOv8m detector, and passes the score to a ByteTrack-based tracker with rule-based behavior analysis. It addresses the failure of fixed-weight fusion when one modality degrades. On M3FD it reaches 87.6% precision.

entry.title: Beyond Segmentation: Enriching ImageCAS with Coronary Ostia Landmarks, Rooted Centerline Graphs, and Open-Weight Localization Models

author.name: Matteo Leccardi, Andrea Moglia, Marco Morandini, Michele Brembilla, Alessandro Nicosia, Andrea Penserini, Christian Brandini, Ender Konukoglu, Marco Marcon, Luca Mainardi, Pietro Cerveri

entry.summary: The authors enrich the ImageCAS coronary artery segmentation dataset with ostium annotations for 1000 patients and centerline graphs rooted at these landmarks, creating the largest public dataset for coronary ostium localization. They also release open-weight localization models, benefiting automated CCTA analysis from surgical planning to intraoperative tracking.

entry.title: When to Trust the BIM: Identifiability-Aware LiDAR-Inertial--BIM Fusion under As-Built Deviations

author.name: Yujie Zhang, Yuxuan Guo, Xinbao Sun, Chunlei Zhao, Langqi Miao, Xiaohui Jia, Jinyue Liu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes when scan-to-BIM disagreement in LiDAR-inertial localization can be attributed to pose error versus as-built deviations versus shifted geometry, deriving a geometric identifiability criterion over three fault classes. The proposed method abstains from attribution when the fault is not identifiable, improving localization robustness against imperfect building models.

entry.title: The Matthews Correlation Coefficient: Fifty years

author.name: Jesus S. Aguilar-Ruiz

entry.summary: This survey provides a comprehensive retrospective of the Matthews Correlation Coefficient fifty years after its introduction, clarifying misconceptions, formalizing its equivalences to Pearson correlation and Chi-squared statistics, and analyzing behavior under class imbalance. It also develops derivative-based and contour-plot frameworks that generalize to any confusion-matrix metric, exposing structural properties that scalar summaries conceal.

entry.title: SIMBAD: Spatio-Temporal Traffic Forecasting Robust to Aperiodicity

author.name: Daniel Y. Lee, Seungwon Shin, Seunghoon Han, Sungsu Lim, Susik Yoon

entry.summary: SIMBAD improves spatio-temporal graph neural networks for traffic prediction under aperiodic, event-driven irregularities through adaptive regulation of periodic signals and dynamic spatial modeling that adjusts node influence based on contextual similarity. Built on simple similarity metrics, it outperforms existing STGNN methods on real-world benchmarks, especially during irregular patterns. The work targets urban planning applications where periodicity assumptions break down.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games

author.name: Eduardo C. Garrido-Merch\'an

entry.summary: This paper explores weight-space programming, where every weight of a feed-forward network is set by hand from an explicit specification with no training, asking how far an LLM can carry this zero-shot across games of increasing difficulty. A four-rung ladder (Nim, tic-tac-toe, two Connect Four sizes, chess endgame) plus independent structurally unrelated networks per rung separates difficulty effects from game-specific effects. Ten networks are built and independently verified.

entry.title: Agentic AI for Healthcare Claim Denial Analysis: A Policy-Grounded Framework for Privacy Preservation

author.name: Sofia Campos, Carlos Martins, Pedro Pires, Jo\~ao Gama, Bruno Veloso, Pedro Santos

entry.summary: A modular agentic framework for healthcare claim denial analysis integrating denial risk prediction, risk factor identification, code relationship analysis, counterfactual analysis, a policy-grounded hybrid RAG pipeline, and a HIPAA compliance agent. Evaluation is on synthetic healthcare claim data.

entry.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency

author.name: Ruizhi Yuan, Zeqiu Yu, Wei Gao, Wei Chen, Xiwei Tang, Lu Tang

entry.summary: FlowAlign is a flow-guided alignment objective for mapping a source modality into a fixed target-modality space used directly downstream, preserving both global target distribution structure and instance-level correspondence via path consistency. It addresses gaps left by contrastive, distribution-matching, and pointwise regression losses individually.

entry.title: Towards Label-Efficient Geospatial Foundation Model Adaptation via Positive-Unlabeled Learning for Building Damage Mapping

author.name: Hengwei Zhao, Qirui Wang, Zhuo Zheng, Xiaoyan Lu, Rusty Feagin, Wenzhe Jiao

entry.summary: The paper tackles label-efficient adaptation of geospatial foundation models for building damage mapping after disasters using positive-unlabeled learning with weak supervision. It addresses the gap that parameter-efficient fine-tuning does not automatically reduce annotation requirements in time-critical disaster response.

entry.title: Random Symbolic Boosting: A Geometric Approach to Symbolic Regression

author.name: Jos\'e R. Ortegaa, Jos\'e Manuel Mu\~noz Contreras, Leonardo Trujillo

entry.summary: Random Symbolic Boosting constructs additive symbolic models by boosting over populations of randomly generated syntax trees, eliminating costly generational evolution in symbolic regression. It exploits semantic vectors of syntax trees and guarantees monotonic training error reduction for OLS in both regression and classification, with an adaptive geometric early-stopping scheme.

entry.title: GlobalPuzzle: Globally Informed Genetic Search for Eroded Jigsaw Puzzle Reassembly

author.name: Lunyan Wang, Chuanzhi Xu, Ziyuan Tao, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: Proposes GlobalPuzzle, a genetic-search method for reassembling jigsaw puzzles with irregularly eroded pieces, motivated by applications to damaged cultural artifacts. It combines global visual information with human-like iterative operations (adding pieces, replacing placements, moving connected groups), where prior methods achieve only 0.3% perfect assembly on 5x5 GAP-benchmark puzzles.

entry.title: Mitigating Covariate Shift in Behavioral Cloning via Robust Stationary Distribution Correction

author.name: Seokin Seo, Byung-Jun Lee, Jongmin Lee, HyeongJoo Hwang, Hongseok Yang, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: This paper tackles covariate shift in offline imitation learning, where behavioral cloning fails when expert data is collected from arbitrary rather than stationary state distributions. The authors propose a robust stationary distribution correction method to address these more pronounced distribution mismatches. It extends the practical applicability of simple behavioral cloning to realistic, non-stationary demonstration datasets.

entry.title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs

author.name: Peiyu Zhang, Heng Ping, Shinibali Bhattacharyya, Anwesan Pal, Nikos Kanakaris, Kevin Cheang, Shixuan Li, Wei Yang, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: QGPM is a training-free method that mitigates the lost-in-the-middle problem in long-context LLMs by reshaping rotary position embeddings using query relevance derived from the model's own attention heads. Unlike prior RoPE-level methods that apply the same remapping to every query, QGPM builds query-specific relevance maps across layers. This offers a deployment-friendly fix at the positional encoding level for a well-documented failure mode.

entry.title: Empirical Assessment of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in TLS

author.name: Md Ariful Haque, Sander Vinberg, Ben Edwards, Jo\~ao Cruz

entry.summary: This companion study measures PQC deployment across seven protocols (HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, RDP) using 10,000 target IPs per protocol, finding low adoption outside HTTPS (9.1% origin-level support) and LDAPS (7.39%), with other protocols below 1%. It highlights that the PQC migration is concentrated in a few high-profile services. The work provides a baseline for tracking quantum-readiness over time.

entry.title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents

author.name: Yuchen Li, Lisa Liu, Runqi Zou, Shuxuan Kuang, Qingquan Zhang, Julian Togelius

entry.summary: Using the LURK Werewolf framework, this paper runs controlled checkpoint-replay experiments (30 games, 4,335 replays) testing whether linguistic complexity and politeness of agent utterances change how other LLM agents judge trust and vote, finding no significant effects. The methodology cleanly separates speech-act content from its natural-language realization. The null results are informative for understanding what actually drives multi-agent trust dynamics.

entry.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Xun Tu, Minghao Zou, Karthik Desingh

entry.summary: Grasp-TAGS addresses loco-manipulation by selecting initial grasps based on their downstream task consequences, using critic distillation to transfer long-horizon task-awareness into grasp selection rather than assuming a fixed or predefined grasp. This improves large-object rearrangement for mobile manipulators in service robotics and warehouse settings. It highlights that geometrically stable grasps can still lead to very different task outcomes.

entry.title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning

author.name: Yifeng Lu, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a residual-interface constraint in graph transformers — fixed unit-coefficient accumulation of intermediate computations across depth — and hypothesizes this causes a depth-wise aggregation mismatch when the utility of contributions varies by node. It formalizes the problem and proposes adaptive depth aggregation to reweight per-node contributions in long-range graph reasoning. The analysis offers a useful architectural insight into how graph transformers combine multi-depth information.

entry.title: Does Country Matter? Evaluating Geographic Sensitivity of Large Language Models in Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening

author.name: Sirajam Munira, Muhammad Ashad Kabir

entry.summary: This study tests whether embedding geographic context in prompts changes LLM-based chronic kidney disease screening outcomes, using a 284-participant community dataset from Bangladesh and varying the country attribute across 25 global contexts while holding clinical inputs constant. Evaluating Qwen3 8B and Mistral 7B, it quantifies geographic sensitivity as a deployment reliability risk for clinical zero-shot LLM use.

entry.title: Foundation-Model Residuals as Signals of Urban Bus Irregularity

author.name: Csaba I. Sidl\'o, Jamil J. Ghazal, Domonkos R\'ozsay, Rita R\'onai, Andr\'as J. Moln\'ar

entry.summary: Rather than treating transfer errors of pretrained trajectory foundation models (UniTraj, TrajFM) as mere performance limitations, this work asks whether residuals on a new city reveal systematic local conditions. Using NetMob26 bus data for Niteroi, it tests whether spatial and travel-time residuals concentrate and which urban-context variables explain them.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation from Neural Networks to Differentiable Logic Networks

author.name: Hee Yun Suh, Niraj K. Jha

entry.summary: The authors introduce knowledge distillation from a trained MLP teacher into a differentiable logic network (DLN) student, closing some of the accuracy gap on datasets where DLNs lag conventional networks while retaining interpretability and orders-of-magnitude cheaper inference. The distillation objective is integrated into a two-phase training loop without architectural changes. This is a practical step toward interpretable, edge-deployable classifiers.

entry.title: TUGB: A Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding Framework

author.name: Luzhan Yuan, Chao Mi, Xiahao Shi, Yi Mao, Shengsheng Niu, Xin Zhu, Jie He, Zhangang Lin, Ching Law

entry.summary: TUGB combines Decision Transformer-style generative sequence modeling with reinforcement learning for auto-bidding in online advertising, using a two-stage pipeline where a pre-trained generative bidding model is fine-tuned via an ensemble-based uncertainty-aware environment model. Epistemic uncertainty estimates penalize high-risk actions, addressing limited offline exploration and sensitivity to traffic shifts. The author list suggests industry involvement in a commercially relevant problem.

entry.title: DiffusionRef-IMU: Guide-Anchored Residual Diffusion for Cross-Location Inertial Measurement Unit Translation

author.name: M. M. Golam Hafiz, Safia Akter Simi, Md. Rakibul Islam, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage framework translating wearable IMU signals across body locations: a deterministic network estimates the target signal, then a guide-anchored residual diffusion model refines only the remaining discrepancy. Evaluation uses subject-disjoint folds, matched baselines, ablations, and zero-shot tests on two independent datasets.

entry.title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming

author.name: Yingxue Zhao, Haoran Li, Haosu Zhou, Tobias Pfaff, Nan Li

entry.summary: Develops BiLoGo, a bipartite local-global learned simulator for sheet-metal forming that connects local node-element message passing (bidirectional GraphSAGE) with a Transformer-based neural operator for long-range exchange, explicitly targeting the tendency of transformer neural operators to oversmooth localized responses like thinning near sharp radii. Uses FE-guided design to accelerate forming simulation.

entry.title: From PAC bounds on the generalization error to PAC bounds on the parameter estimation error

author.name: Mihaly Petreczky, John Leth, Emma Lukacs, Balint Daroczy

entry.summary: Bridges two strands of statistical learning theory by deriving algorithm-agnostic finite-sample PAC bounds on parameter estimation error in system identification, extending classical generalization bounds. Unlike prior estimation bounds that are tied to specific least-squares formulations, these apply to any algorithm minimizing a cost function.

entry.title: Drift-admissibility via Optimal Transport

author.name: Abigail Langbridge, Enrico Biffis, Jakub Mare\v{c}ek, Robert Shorten

entry.summary: Introduces structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics for testing whether empirical time-series dynamics are compatible with a prescribed predictable-drift class, encoding admissibility as moment constraints on local couplings with a KL projection gap statistic. Includes a scalable Bregman-Dykstra algorithm retaining Sinkhorn-type efficiency.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo

author.name: Jie Hu, Lingyun Chen, Do Young Eun

entry.summary: Generalizes Score-Repellent Monte Carlo to GA-SRMC by tilting the target with a matrix-weighted score alignment, allowing different repellence strengths along steep and flat directions of anisotropic landscapes. A stochastic-approximation CLT identifies the trace-normalized inverse Fisher information as the optimal geometry.

entry.title: Half-precision inference of AI weather prediction models: negligible loss of skill at a fraction of the cost

author.name: Stefan Siegert

entry.summary: Evaluates five public AI weather models (Aurora, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet, SFNO, FastNet) in fp16 versus fp32 on a single 16 GB GPU, finding negligible skill loss (RMSE changes at most 1.4%, typically 0.5% or less) when keeping the physical state and normalization in fp32 while running networks in half precision. Also shows whole-model conversion fails due to overflow and precision loss.

entry.title: Contextual Search and Bilateral Trade with a Trace-Square-Root Potential

author.name: Romain Cosson, Federico Fusco, Anupam Gupta, Stefano Leonardi, Renato Paes Leme, Matteo Russo

entry.summary: This work presents a unified potential-based method for contextual search and bilateral trade with one-bit feedback, achieving order-tight loss and regret bounds expressed via the trace of the prior covariance matrix. The framework operates in a Bayesian model where predictions are based on posterior distributions over unknown targets or valuations.

entry.title: RL-ATTACK: A Generalized Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Language Models via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Taikun Chen, Yue Zhang, Wei Qian, Hui Fang

entry.summary: RL-ATTACK is a trainable black-box adversarial attack framework that uses reinforcement learning to learn tailored adversarial transformations from the target model's feedback, rather than guessing transformations with external knowledge. It reports lower post-attack accuracy, better query efficiency, and improved semantic preservation on natural language tasks.

entry.title: PhoPunct: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Transformer Architectures for Vietnamese Punctuation Restoration

author.name: Khoa D. Nguyen, Thai Bao Huynh, Binh T. Nguyen

entry.summary: The authors introduce a large-scale Vietnamese punctuation restoration benchmark with 22.1 million labeled tokens across News and Novels corpora, evaluating 17 architectures built from four pretrained Transformer backbones with optional Bi-LSTM and CRF layers. Under a fixed training budget without architecture-specific tuning, they find that adding Bi-LSTM and CRF layers does not reliably improve macro F1, with the finding holding in most comparisons. The benchmark PhoPunct, including a PhoBERT-large-Bi-LSTM-CRF model, enables controlled conclusions about how architectural choices scale with data volume.

entry.title: An Effective Spoken Language Understanding Approach Leveraging Query-Adaptive Intent Detection

author.name: Bing-Long Kuo, Yu-Hsuan Fang, Tien-Hong Lo, Hsueh-Wei Liao, Berlin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes APEX, a two-stage in-context-learning retrieval framework for spoken language understanding that first selects candidate intents via intent-level prototypes, then retrieves contextual exemplars within that intent space. Improves exact match accuracy on SLURP over direct query-based demonstration retrieval.

entry.title: MESAM: Enhancing SAM2 for Few-Shot Segmentation through Semantic-Visual Memory Generation and Refinement

author.name: Tianyu Zou, Shengwu Xiong, Rui Wu, Ruilin Yao, Yi Rong

entry.summary: MESAM extends SAM2 to few-shot segmentation by addressing appearance differences between support and query images, finding that semantic memory is more robust than visual memory for matching. It introduces a Semantic-Visual Memory Generation module that separately builds query semantic memory, foreground visual memory, and related components for better matching.

entry.title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Joao D. S. Marques, David Calhas, Arlindo L. Oliveira

entry.summary: Inspired by recurrent feedback in human visual cortex, this work appends lightweight recurrent refinement blocks (CRFs, modern Hopfield networks, convolutional GRUs) to segmentation backbones and studies test-time iteration behavior including beyond the training horizon. Experiments on Kvasir-SEG and ARCADE show improved robustness in low-data, artifact-heavy clinical settings. It connects neuroscience-motivated recurrence to practical medical segmentation.

entry.title: CRTrack-Cap: A New Benchmark for Cross-View Dense Video Object Captioning

author.name: Xiangqun Zhang, Likai Wang, Zekun Qian, Rui Zhou, Ruize Han, Wei Feng

entry.summary: The paper formulates cross-view dense video object captioning (CVDVOC), which associates per-camera tracklets into scene-level global trajectories and generates one caption per trajectory from synchronized views. CRTrack-Cap is built from CRTrack by auditing text-identity links, retaining 425 global trajectories. This enables unified multi-camera description rather than redundant per-view captions.

entry.title: Deep-Learning Algorithm for Indeterminate Thyroid Nodules: Comparison and Combination with Molecular Testing

author.name: Jichen Yang, Jeffrey Ashton, Jikai Zhang, Maciej A. Mazurowski, Benjamin Wildman-Tobriner

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether a CNN on routine ultrasound can stratify thyroid nodules with indeterminate cytology, comparing and combining it with costly molecular testing like Afirma and ThyroSeq on a retrospective cohort of 466 records. It explores a cheaper AI alternative for deciding between surgery and surveillance.

entry.title: Segmenting Geometric Textures of 3D Meshes

author.name: Weidan Xiong, Kaijie Qu, Shihao Feng, Shunqi Fan, Rongyu Xiong, Hui Huang

entry.summary: The authors present a method for segmenting middle-level geometric textures on 3D meshes, a capability missing from semantic-part-focused 3D segmentation methods, and fine-tune SAM3 for this task. They release a new geometric texture segmentation benchmark and cluster segmented regions using DINO features for applications like heritage protection and 3D printing.

entry.title: FATHOM: World-Model-Guided Diffusion Action-Trajectory Selection for Sparse-Marker AUV Tracking

author.name: Xiaorui Wang, Zeyu Sha, Mingyang Yang, David Chen Wang, Feitian Zhang

entry.summary: FATHOM is a framework for cooperative autonomous underwater vehicle tracking under sparse active-light marker observations, combining marker data, inertial measurements, and dynamics into a predictive world model that guides diffusion-based action-trajectory selection. It targets partial-observation control degraded by occlusion, reflections, and detection noise.

entry.title: FASTFUNNELS: Agile Multi Robot Navigation in Narrow Spaces via Adaptive Dynamic Funnels

author.name: Vignesh Rajagopal, Rohan Chandra

entry.summary: FASTFUNNELS tackles high-speed multi-robot navigation through tight spaces using adaptive dynamic funnels within a formation control framework for Ackermann-steering vehicles, replacing rigid predefined formations and transitions. The goal is to balance collision safety with agility, avoiding the usual trade-off of slowing near bottlenecks.

entry.title: LACART: Lookahead-Augmented Collision Avoidance and Reference Tracking Strategies for Safety-Critical Robots

author.name: Pedro Lopes, Amit Shivam, Luis Tiago Paiva

entry.summary: LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions, relaxed control Lyapunov functions, and quadratic programming to handle obstacle avoidance and reference tracking in autonomous racing within a single optimization layer. Simulations against a prior method show similar track performance with modestly lower computation times.

entry.title: A Generalized Bayesian Approach to Clustering with Dimension Reduction

author.name: Shen Jia, Weipeng Huang, Geng Yang, Eoin Gallagher, Tin Lok James Ng

entry.summary: The paper extends generalized Bayes product partition models — which cluster via exponentiated losses rather than likelihoods — by jointly learning an autoencoder with the partition, so the clustering loss is evaluated in a learned low-dimensional representation. This allows quantifying allocation uncertainty without a full generative model while handling high-dimensional or manifold-structured data.

entry.title: AI safety course update

author.name: Boaz Barak

entry.summary: Boaz Barak (Harvard, ex-OpenAI) reports on his ongoing AI safety course, sharing scribe notes, lecture videos, and student experiments across topics including cyber capabilities, LLM training, recursive self-improvement, economic impacts, and reward hacking, with guest speakers such as Nicholas Carlini, Dwarkesh Patel, and Erik Brynjolfsson. The course webpage serves as a substantive public resource.

entry.title: PHISHREV+: An ASP-Based Post-Hoc Defeasible Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Detection

author.name: Mainak Sen, Kumar Sanka Ray, Amlan Chakrabarti

entry.summary: PHISHREV+ is a hybrid phishing detection framework treating ML classifier predictions as defeasible beliefs revised by an Answer Set Programming non-monotonic reasoning layer, allowing new contextual evidence without retraining. In the ML phase, four classifiers produce initial predictions; the NMR phase then overturns or confirms them using structured reasoning. This post-hoc defeasible approach addresses the brittleness of fixed decision boundaries in evolving phishing threats.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Learning Framework for Linking Microscopic Surface Degradation to Bolted Joint Functional Behavior

author.name: Nehal Afifi, Gerhard Kachel, Sven Matthiesen

entry.summary: This paper presents a physics-informed multimodal framework linking microscopic and camera-based corrosion observations to functional indicators of bolted joints, with synchronized inspection and functional-response data, similarity-based alignment of microscopy and camera images, and calibrated corrosion-severity fields. It targets remaining-function assessment in circular engineering.

entry.title: FIND: Frequency Invariance Disentanglement for Test-Time Adaptation in LiDAR 3D Detection

author.name: Dongxiao Li, Zixuan Hu, Ling-Yu Duan

entry.summary: Proposes FIND, a test-time adaptation framework for LiDAR 3D object detection that disentangles domain-invariant content from domain-specific interference in the frequency domain using B-Spline-based locally adaptive filters. This targets domain shifts from sensor configurations and environmental conditions that spatial-domain self-supervision confounds.

entry.title: Embedding Consistent Recurrent Neural Networks in Finite Element Simulations for Path-Dependent Damage Prediction

author.name: Muhammed Adil Yatk{\i}n, Mihkel K\~orgesaar, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: This work embeds a trained recurrent neural network damage criterion directly inside Abaqus/Explicit as a Fortran user material subroutine, proposing ConsRNN, an architecture whose predictions converge as the solver's strain path is refined, ensuring increment-count consistency. This enables reliable surrogate-driven fracture prediction within production FEM solvers. It addresses a real gap between learned surrogates and numerical-solver consistency requirements.

entry.title: Structure is in the zoom: probing neural symmetry through dimensionality scaling

author.name: Adil Amin

entry.summary: Shows that reported dimensionality slopes of neural populations and language model layers partly reflect measurement subsampling rather than system structure, decomposing participation-ratio scaling exponents into a sampling floor and a structural shift. Analysis of mouse V1 data demonstrates that only some measured slopes carry genuine structure.

entry.title: Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation

author.name: Dongxu Wu, Sara Court, Micha Elsner

entry.summary: The paper constructs a controlled Mandarin-to-English translation task where familiar words receive new prompt-supplied meanings to isolate how LLMs resolve conflicts between contextual knowledge and prior lexical knowledge. Across nine models, reliance on supplied meanings increases for rarer words and supportive contexts, and prompt framing can shift behavior.

entry.title: Language, Not Code Abstraction: Natural-language Training Shapes Brain-aligned Geometry

author.name: I\~nigo Parra

entry.summary: Training 25 GPT-2-small models on TinyStories, Python, C, x86-64 assembly, and machine code, the study finds only natural-language training yields brain alignment on benchmarks like Pereira-243, while code training leaves alignment near random-weight levels. The advantage is benchmark-specific, disappearing on some datasets, complicating claims that code abstraction substitutes for language training.

entry.title: Real-Time Short-Response Selection for Spoken Dialogue Systems

author.name: Hien Ohnaka, Kazuyo Onishi, Koichiro Yoshino

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time short-response selection task and model that masks language-generation and speech-synthesis delays during turn-taking in spoken dialogue systems. Uses contrastive learning to map dialogue context to pre-generated short responses selected when a turn-taking event is detected.

entry.title: Look Closer, Align Better: Explicit Visual Attributes for Robust EEG-to-Image Decoding

author.name: Ke Xiao, Banghua Yang, Wenbin Guo, Fenqi Rong

entry.summary: AttrEcho improves EEG-to-image retrieval by enriching pretrained visual representations with explicit, spatially aligned visual attributes that carry EEG-relevant information beyond encoder features. A Region-Aligned Visual Attribute Fusion module integrates local attribute cues to better distinguish semantically similar images.

entry.title: Embedding Predictive Adaptation and Refinement for Multi-Modal Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jaeho Cho, Jinsik Bang, Taehwan Kim

entry.summary: This work improves memory-bank-based multi-modal industrial anomaly detection using RGB images and 3D point clouds by adapting frozen pretrained encoders and refining pixel-level anomaly maps. It targets two limitations: insufficient discrimination from the domain gap and coarse anomaly localization from patch-level score interpolation. The result is more precise anomaly localization in industrial inspection.

entry.title: Direct Regression and Geometric Recovery for Event-based Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: Pruthvi Nandan Janga, Kashyap Hegde Kota, Bharatesh Chakravarthi

entry.summary: This comparative study evaluates two independently developed approaches to synthetic-to-real event-based 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation: a modular pipeline with learned keypoints, domain adaptation, and geometric recovery, versus direct regression with physics-motivated synthetic corruptions. It addresses the gap between synthetic training streams and the noise of physical event cameras. The work informs design choices for space-domain event-camera perception.

entry.title: Trying to Steer PI with (Prefix) Label Directions

author.name: Z Dai

entry.summary: Building on the prompt-injection-as-role-confusion line of work, this post tests whether prepending label blocks with empty contents to a neutral-text probe improves reading out and steering a toolness direction. Across GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Gemma4-12B and two PI datasets, the prefix method only outperforms the bare method in a limited set of conditions with no consistent advantage.

entry.title: PreForceVision: Physics-Guided Optical Estimation of Bolt Preload from Bolt-Head Deformation

author.name: Nehal Afifi, Klaus Rappenecker, Florian Peinhardt, Gerhard Kachel, Alfred Isele, Sven Matthiesen

entry.summary: PreForceVision estimates bolt preload non-contact from preload-induced deformation of the bolt-head front face using a physics-guided optical framework, replacing hardware-dependent methods like strain gauges and ultrasonic measurement. This improves scalability of preload assessment across large numbers of standard fasteners.

entry.title: Generative Reconstruction of Full-Field Sensor States for Safety-Critical Digital Twins

author.name: Umme Mahbuba Nabila, Linyu Lin, Majdi I. Radaideh

entry.summary: This study develops a sparse-sensor reconstruction framework for a high-temperature test facility (HTTF), comparing six methods including conditional diffusion models, VAEs, GANs, recurrent networks, and ridge regression under intra- and inter-experiment protocols for safety-critical digital-twin state awareness. It addresses sensor drift and failure in harsh nuclear-adjacent environments. The systematic generative-vs-deterministic comparison is valuable for digital-twin practitioners.

entry.title: Beyond Truncation? Entailment-Licensed Elision and the Limits of Semantic Preservation in LLM Decoding

author.name: Mahmoud Alyosify, Mirna Imbabi, Eman Elkhamisi

entry.summary: The authors test whether a training-free entropy-gated logits processor can shorten verbose LLM answers beyond what simple truncation achieves, using pre-registered BERTScore non-inferiority margins. They prove and empirically confirm the controller's output is always a prefix of the original answer, and a survey of 23 training-free mechanism families finds none beats truncation without oracle labels.

entry.title: Evaluating Anterior Cruciate Ligament Risk of Injury Using a Graph Convolutional Autoencoder

author.name: Athanasios Babouras, Paul A. Martineau, Thomas Fevens

entry.summary: The authors build an unsupervised model, runnable entirely on a smartphone, that uses a graph convolutional autoencoder over pose estimation data to assess ACL injury risk during standard athletic tests like the drop vertical jump and single leg hop. This offers an accessible alternative to expensive motion-capture labs and subjective expert assessment. It accurately identifies high-risk athletes in both tests.

entry.title: When F1 Is Not Enough: Auditing Codebooks for LLM-Assisted Annotation

author.name: Yuehong Cassandra Tai, Qunhua Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a pre-deployment codebook audit for LLM-assisted text annotation in social science, using class-specific metrics, confusion matrices, and structured document-level review to attribute whether low F1 stems from codebook defects, annotation system limits, or reference-label inconsistency. Applying the audit to two published multi-class codebooks reveals under-specified and conflicting coding rules.

entry.title: Rethinking Optimization Methods for Hierarchical Feature Selection

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: This paper provides a unified analysis of four optimization families (MM, VQF, ADMM, weighted group lasso) for Hierarchical-Task Numerical conjunctive feature Learning, used to select interpretable conjunctive features in rare-event forecasting. It identifies three key factors that jointly determine optimization performance in this structured sparsity setting. The work is largely methodological, aimed at making a difficult optimization problem tractable in practice.

entry.title: ROAM: Retrieval-Augmented Optimization for Feasible Multi-Day Itinerary Planning

author.name: Ye Zihao, Lin Xiaoheng

entry.summary: ROAM couples retrieval over a curated POI database with explicit spatiotemporal optimization to produce feasible multi-day travel itineraries from LLM requests, using maximal-clique analysis, K-means day partitioning, and a quality-biased simulated-annealing TSP solver. It addresses common LLM failure modes like ignoring geography and opening hours.

entry.title: LLM-Enhanced Self-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Step E-Commerce Payment Fraud Risk Detection

author.name: Bo Qu, Zhurong Wang, Daisuke Yagi, Zhen Xu, Yang Zhao, Yinan Shan, Frank Zahradnik

entry.summary: The paper frames e-commerce payment fraud detection as a multi-step MDP solved with reinforcement learning, using LLMs to iteratively refine reward functions that would otherwise require significant human expertise. The approach improves fraud detection accuracy and shows zero-shot capability on a production-scale problem, apparently from an industry team.

entry.title: FinEvolveKG: Controlled and Attributable Prompt Evolution for Financial Knowledge Graph Construction

author.name: Abhinav Arun, Jayita Bhattacharyya, Fabrizio Dimino, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

entry.summary: FinEvolveKG is a harness for financial knowledge graph construction that separates reusable general prompt blocks from persona-policy blocks, mechanically confining the GEPA reflective prompt optimizer to the designated block. This keeps prompt evolution controlled, attributable, and auditable without costly fine-tuning.

entry.title: CrowdDirector: Runtime Orchestration of Crowd Simulation through Natural-Language Directives

author.name: Xiaohan Sun, Vuk Radovanovic, Merce Alvarez, Carol O'Sullivan, Yiorgos Chrysanthou, Panayiotis Charalambous

entry.summary: CrowdDirector uses an LLM only when users add or change instructions, translating natural-language requests into validated structured directives that a scene validator checks against the Unity scene; a graph neural network then executes continuously during simulation ticks. This avoids per-tick LLM latency, cost, and unsupported-action risks.

entry.title: Learning from How Users Interpret: Personalizing Recommendation Explanation Order

author.name: Deo Munduku, Elsa Negre

entry.summary: A controlled 122-participant study testing whether regularities in users' prior textual interpretations of explanations (selection, salience, relational organization) can be used to personalize the ordering of explanation sentences in recommender systems. It shifts personalization from explanation content to explanation structure.

entry.title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs

author.name: Jonas Oppenlaender, Johanna M. Silvennoinen

entry.summary: Introduces AlienBench, which adapts the structured-imagination task from cognitive psychology (imagining an alien creature) to measure structural novelty of LLM outputs against a known Earth-animal baseline, giving novelty ratings a fixed reference point. This addresses the lack of a grounding default in standard creativity evaluations that rely on human or LLM judges.

entry.title: How Much Conversation History Does an AI Agent Need?

author.name: Danny Kim, Fernando Koch

entry.summary: This empirical study measures how reducing conversational history and passage budgets affects reader-token usage and benchmark scores across 1,100 BEAM questions, finding diminishing returns to additional context and that abstention scores can rise when context shrinks. It also compares retained user messages against token-matched recency for conversational-state retention. The results offer practical guidance on context budgeting for retrieval and agent systems.

entry.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description

author.name: Rochak Dhakal, Chen Zhao, Soup Cobb, Xin Qian, Xiaofeng Yang, Weihua Zhou

entry.summary: GRAC represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomy, then retrieves similar graph-caption pairs from training data to generate automated surgical scene descriptions. The approach leverages recurring surgical activities to reduce the manual burden of operative reporting. It targets a concrete clinical workflow with clear documentation and training benefits.

entry.title: Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation for Wind Energy Predictive Analysis

author.name: Purbak Sengupta, Aparna S. varde, Emil J{\o}rgensen Njor

entry.summary: The paper proposes MSKC, a resource-aware computing principle that selects the least-costly knowledge and computation route meeting decision-risk constraints, escalating only when cheaper options fail. It instantiates this for wind ramp-event prediction at the edge, addressing the unconditional knowledge injection common in knowledge-guided machine learning.

entry.title: WearableBridge: Task-Guided Latent Transport for Free-Living Activity Recognition

author.name: Jingjing Zou, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: WearableBridge addresses wrist-worn activity recognition by learning a task-guided transport map (a bridge) that moves wrist features into the region a fixed reference classifier associates with each activity, leveraging scarce high-quality calibration data such as thigh recordings. The reference encoder and classifier stay frozen, making the approach practical for real deployments. It tackles a real domain-shift problem in large-scale wearable sensing.

entry.title: Open-world Reconstruction-based Classifier with Concept Drift Adaptation

author.name: Joanna Komorniczak

entry.summary: Proposes a data-stream classifier that detects and learns distributions of novel unknown classes while adapting to concept drift, using autoencoder reconstruction errors modeled via kernel density estimation with incremental adaptation. Addresses the combined open-world problem of drift and emerging classes in streaming settings.

entry.title: Improving Contextual Retrieval for Long Documents using Semantic Chunking and Hybrid Retrieval Strategies

author.name: Sakshi Garg, William B. Andreopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid RAG framework combining knowledge graphs with dense vector retrieval, using transformer-based summarization and semantic chunking to retain context in long documents. The dynamic knowledge graph captures explicit entity relationships to support multi-hop reasoning across distributed sources.

entry.title: Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation

author.name: Aoran Chen, Yang Feng

entry.summary: Derives sharp, exact conversion curves relating mixture excess risk to target excess hinge-risk under reweighting for binary classification, determined by density-weighted local votes, and establishes minimax adaptation on a tilted-boundary class. Provides precise finite-sample theory for transfer classification via weighted SVMs.

entry.title: Contextuality and Contradictions: Exploring Real-World Identifications of AI-Generated Writing

author.name: Michelle Morgenstern, Julia Witte Zimmerman, Tabia Tanzin Prama, Kristine Harootunian, June Clark, Bryn Loftness, Calla Beauregard, Juniper Lovato

entry.summary: This interdisciplinary study combines qualitative coding and computational lexical analysis, grounded in linguistic anthropology, to examine how Wikipedia editors and students identify AI-generated text in everyday practice. It finds these identifications draw on diverse contextual evidence and frequently involve contradictions in how AI writing is characterized.

entry.title: On the Effectiveness and Limitations of Open-Weight LLMs for Low-Resource Offensive Language Detection in Danish

author.name: Elnur Adl Zarabi, Amit Kumar, Adi Singh, Sierra Nelson, Megan Stubbs-Richardson, Taoran Ji

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates four open-weight LLM families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen) across eleven prompting strategies for Danish offensive language detection, comparing against fine-tuned BERT baselines under balanced and imbalanced distributions. Shows LLMs can beat fine-tuned BERT even without task-specific fine-tuning, with further gains from light fine-tuning.

entry.title: BayesCrop: Real-Time Probabilistic Multi-Crop Video Reframing

author.name: Cheng-Han Lee, Rajesh Sureddi, Neil Birkbeck, Yilin Wang, Balu Adsumilli, Alan Bovik

entry.summary: BayesCrop performs real-time probabilistic video reframing by representing crop preferences as a two-component spatially isotropic Gaussian mixture over crop position and scale, capturing multiple plausible regions of interest with local uncertainty. An anchor-and-propagation scheme enables efficient video processing with dual-view prediction and sampling of alternatives.

entry.title: Overview of the ImageCLEFmedical 2026 GANs task: Exploring fingerprint detection, privacy leakage, and synthetic medical image generation

author.name: Alexandra-Georgiana Andrei, Mihai Gabriel Constantin, Mihai Dogariu, Dzmitry Karpenka, Yuri Prokopchuk, Ahmedkhan Radzhabov, Dan-Cristian Stanciu, Liviu-Daniel \c{S}tefan, Vassili Kovalev, Henning M\"uller, Bogdan Ionescu

entry.summary: This overview describes the fourth edition of the ImageCLEFmedical GANs task on privacy and security in synthetic medical image generation. It introduces three subtasks: detecting which real images trained a GAN, identifying the latent vector behind each synthetic image, and generating privacy-preserving synthetic medical images. The task probes reversibility and leakage in generative medical imaging.

entry.title: Measurement-Aware Multimodal LLM for No-Reference Low-Dose CT Quality Assessment

author.name: Kerem Basim, Tolga Demiroglu, Mehmet Ozan Unal, Metin Ertas, Isa Yildirim

entry.summary: This paper builds a measurement-aware multimodal LLM on Qwen3.8-27B that rates CT slice quality by combining the image with six textual percentile measurements of noise, sharpness, and artifacts. It matches the retrained challenge winner on the LDCT-IQA 2023 test set while adding explainability.

entry.title: It Takes Two to Tangram: Multi-Agent Object Centric Reinforcement Learning for Assembly

author.name: Paul Knau{\ss}t, Kay Pompetzki, Nico Bohlinger, Niklas Funk, Cristiana de Farias, Rolf Findeisen, Jan Peters

entry.summary: This paper presents an object-centric multi-agent RL framework for geometric assembly where each part is an agent, using a graph neural network to represent pieces, target poses, and spatial relations, with per-agent PPO and a centralized graph critic. It is studied on planar Tangram assembly requiring tight-clearance sliding and rotation coordination.

entry.title: Wellness Robots and the Path to Full Autonomy

author.name: Mohammad H. Mahoor, Matthew Hessler, Lombe Chileshe, Ola Alsaadi, Eshrat Emamian, Kerstin S. Haring, Richard M. Voyles

entry.summary: This position/case-study paper defines the autonomous wellness robot as a category of socially assistive system spanning seven ICAA wellness dimensions and proposes the Care Robot Autonomy Scale (CRAS), a six-level taxonomy modeled on SAE J3016. It presents the Ryan wellness robot as a case study with longitudinal NIH-funded evidence (N=18, 887 hours) showing statistically significant cognitive improvement in older adults.

entry.title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Shubham Singh, Anand Singh, Anjali Tiwari, Lara Bri\~n\'on-Arranz, Katsuki Fujisawa

entry.summary: The paper presents a safety-critical control framework using higher-order control barrier functions and QPs for multi-robot circumnavigation of a target on heterogeneous orbital radii, requiring only range measurements and neighbor communication. A shared control law serves all robots regardless of assigned radius while enforcing standoff, spacing, and collision-avoidance constraints.

entry.title: Machine Learning Beyond Statistical Consistency for Hybrid AI

author.name: Jinsook Kim, Jinho Kang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a formal definition of machine learning based on successful computation in a formal derivation system, extending Godel's Representability Theorem to computable reals and admitting data as empirical definitions. It proves a machine learns a true probability if and only if both a Truth Condition (statistical consistency) and an Assurance Condition (formal derivability) hold.

entry.title: Hands-On Tutorials for Inspect AI

author.name: Alex the L

entry.summary: A four-person project team from the Spring 2026 Technical AI Safety Evals Course presents four Jupyter/Colab notebooks teaching AI evaluation engineering with the UK AISI's Inspect AI framework, progressing from first evaluations through benchmarks, LLM judges, and a small agent, plus revisions to the official tutorial. The authors argue eval-building skills matter more for safety than for capabilities.

entry.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?

author.name: Ruichen Zheng, Yihe Wang, Fabrice Harel-Canada, Sara Khosravi, Zeynep Senahan Yildiz, Amit Sahai, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether reasoning-enhanced post-training improves psychological depth in short stories, comparing DeepSeek-R1 versus DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-5 versus GPT-4o through 60 blinded pairwise evaluations with seven human annotators plus an LLM judge. Results show no universal reasoning advantage, with GPT-5 only slightly preferred over GPT-4o depending on reasoning exposure.

entry.title: Toward LLM Self-Play Under Data Scarcity: Effectiveness, Generalizability, and Trustworthiness

author.name: Zhiyin Yu, Yuchen Mou, Bingzhe Wu, Zhonghai Wu, Shiyang Feng, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: This position paper argues that LLM self-play - autonomous data generation and improvement - should be evaluated on effectiveness, generalizability, and trustworthiness under data scarcity, and outlines three blue-sky research directions to address current frameworks' lack of data-centric perspective, weak cross-domain transfer, and growing security concerns.

entry.title: Large Language Model Consensus and Corpus-Adaptive Topic Modeling for Classifying and Mapping Patent Innovation

author.name: Sercan Ozcan, Enes Ozgozler, C. Okan Sakar

entry.summary: This design-oriented study presents an auditable patent analytics pipeline in which three LLMs separately classify patents by novelty and innovation type with two-vote consensus requirements, combined with topic discovery via clustering PatentSBERTa embeddings. Each pipeline decision about model roles and retained evidence is kept open to audit. The work demonstrates how to structure multi-LLM classification transparently for innovation research.

entry.title: CID: Measuring Cognitive Work Through Semantic State Change

author.name: Ron Fulbright

entry.summary: This paper defines semantic state as a vector in a model's semantic space and cognitive work as transformation between semantic states, introducing the Contextual Information Differential, a covariance-aware metric quantifying movement through semantic space. It extends classical information theory toward meaning-based analysis using LLM embeddings.

entry.title: Scoring, Not Learning: Decomposing Catalog-Consolidation Gains in Web-Scraped Retail Product Recognition

author.name: Kaden Leis, Xiang Ma

entry.summary: This paper analyzes a 165,769-image retail product recognition archive to show that accuracy gains from catalog consolidation come from changing what counts as correct rather than improving the recognizer itself. It disentangles packaging noise filtering, near-duplicate removal, and label canonicalization effects on a fixed group-aware split.

entry.title: Reliable Prerequisite-Aware Learning Path Recommendation under Uncertain Knowledge Structures: Long-Horizon Evaluation and Cross-Dataset Validation

author.name: M. M. Golam Hafiz, A. K. M. Shahriar Emtiaz, Safia Akter Simi, Md. Rakibul Islam, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: This work builds a reliability-oriented framework for learning-path recommendation that jointly models next-resource ranking, uncertain prerequisite structures, constraint semantics, graph robustness, and autoregressive path generation. It uses 3,187 MOOCCubeX courses for development with frozen confirmatory evaluation and independent cross-dataset validation, emphasizing long-horizon path quality over immediate ranking accuracy. The focus on evaluation rigor in educational recommender systems is its distinguishing feature.

entry.title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression

author.name: Gon\c{c}alo Gomes, Bruno Martins, Chrysoula Zerva

entry.summary: BEiTScore++ extends the BEiTScore reference-free image captioning metric with conformally calibrated confidence intervals, modeling predictive distributions over human judgments in a single forward pass. Evaluated across benchmarks with human ratings, it preserves BEiTScore's ranking correlation while producing uncertainty intervals that track prediction error better than Monte Carlo baselines. This adds principled uncertainty quantification to a deployment-relevant evaluation task.

entry.title: Scaling Graph Similarity Learning with Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Ahmet T\"uzen, Helge Langseth, Kjetil N{\o}rv{\aa}g

entry.summary: FiLSim is a scalable GNN-based framework for graph similarity learning, targeting NP-hard problems like Graph Edit Distance and Maximum Common Subgraph that prior GNN approaches only tackled on small datasets. The work addresses the underexplored scalability dimension of graph similarity for applications such as chemical compound analysis and program comparison. It extends the practical applicability of learned graph similarity to larger graphs.

entry.title: RoleWalk: training-free structural embeddings for directed graphs that transfer across graphs

author.name: Maixent Chenebaux

entry.summary: RoleWalk produces training-free structural role embeddings for directed graphs by following a short lazy random walk from each node and encoding transition-probability distributions (via characteristic functions at fixed frequencies) and return-distance distributions at each step. Unlike graph-specific methods, the embedding is graph-agnostic and transfers across graphs while reading edge direction. This offers a simple, transferable alternative to struc2vec-style and GraphWave-style methods.

entry.title: Consensus-Constrained Dual-Federated Optimization with Client-Side Dynamic Weighting for Distributed Android Device Threat Defense

author.name: Mohammad Mashreghi, Mohammad Hossein Badiei, Md. Jalil Piran

entry.summary: Proposes DW-FedADMM, a federated optimization framework for Android malware detection that combines primal-dual (ADMM) coordination with performance-dependent client-side dynamic weighting, using dual variables to regulate disagreement between local and global models under partial participation. Targets privacy-preserving, scalable threat defense across phones, hubs, and wearables.

entry.title: AutoPYara: Next-Gen YARA Rule Generator for Malware Family Clustering

author.name: Mabon Ninan, Nhat Nguyen, Soumyajyoti Dutta, Sidharth Anil, Marcus Botacin

entry.summary: Improves on the state-of-the-art AutoYara system for automatic YARA rule generation with similarity-hashing-based centroid selection and a subcluster-estimation heuristic using historical VirusTotal data. Released as an open-source Python package, it increases rule coverage by 14 percent on realistic datasets with noisy clustering.

entry.title: Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation

author.name: Enzhan Zheng, Xiaoliang Song

entry.summary: Analyzes how individual loss components contribute to Adam's parameter updates in PINNs, identifying three training regimes and developing a singular perturbation / slow-manifold analysis of the early smooth regime. Proposes a gradient modulation method informed by this analysis to address imbalanced optimization.

entry.title: Interpretable Context-Aware Multi-Label Retinal Classification with Dual-Hub Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network

author.name: Proshanto Chanda, Munib Mesinovic, Tingting Zhu, Abhirup Banerjee

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-hub heterogeneous GNN that fuses spatial fundus features with structured clinical covariates via cross-modal message passing, exposing multi-level decision pathways natively rather than through post-hoc saliency. Evaluated on the BRSET retinal dataset for multi-label pathology classification.

entry.title: TensorMutation: Learning Weight-Space Mutations of Deep Learning Models on Neural Graphs

author.name: Zaheed Ahmed, Philip Makedonski, Jens Grabowski

entry.summary: TensorMutation uses a mutation-conditioned graph neural network over a trained model's neural graph to predict what a fault-informed pre-training mutation would do to weights, avoiding costly retraining for mutation testing. The GNN is trained offline once and reused across unseen models, narrowing the cost-realism tradeoff in DL mutation testing.

entry.title: Richness Is Not Evenness: Ordered Renyi Crossings under Self-Training

author.name: Pranjal Srivastava

entry.summary: Fine-tuning GPT-2 on its own output for nine generations, the author tracks Renyi entropies of the vocabulary and finds ordered temperature-dependent crossings where entropy change shifts sign, separating lexical richness from evenness. The study offers a fine-grained measurement lens on model collapse, showing reduced type counts can coexist with lower dominance of frequent words.

entry.title: Benchmarking Speaker Embedders in the Sub-Second Regime for Real-Time Voice AI Agents

author.name: Abhishek Gautam

entry.summary: Benchmarks five open-source speaker embedders (TitaNet-Large/Small, ECAPA-TDNN, CAM++, SpeakerNet) under strict sub-second latency budgets for separating active users from background speech such as TV audio or other voices. Combines a controlled benchmark with a human-annotated production set to address false acceptances in downstream speaker verification and ASR.

entry.title: MSR-ABC: Complementary Feature Fusion for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell

entry.summary: MSR-ABC is a global-local framework for ccRCC classification from CT that integrates MedVAE reconstructions, MedSigLIP image-text embeddings, and radiomic descriptors via cross-representation attention, gated residual fusion, and area-aware pooling. Radiomic auxiliary supervision helps retain quantitative tumor attributes. It aims to better exploit complementary tumor phenotype information than simple feature concatenation.

entry.title: Dual-Region Slice Aggregation for CT-Based Renal Tumor Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell

entry.summary: This companion work presents a region-aware architecture for CT-based ccRCC classification that pools tumor and peritumoral context separately from frozen DINOv3 features, with a position-aware slice aggregator and radiomics fusion via learned gates. On KiTS23 plus 111 external cases it achieves internal and external AUCs of about 0.81 and 0.91. Including peritumoral region modeling improves over single-tumor readouts.

entry.title: Two-Layer Evolutionary Scheduling for Machine Learning Jobs in Multi-Cluster Environments

author.name: Jingyuan Xu, Changwu Huang, Lemeng Pan, Ke Tang, Xin Yao

entry.summary: EVO-GP formulates multi-cluster GPU scheduling of ML jobs as online multi-objective optimization minimizing weighted queuing times while maximizing GPU utilization, and solves it with a two-layer evolutionary method decoupling global job-to-cluster allocation from intra-cluster scheduling. It addresses load imbalance and queuing delays in large-scale ML workloads.

entry.title: Mechanical Interaction Sensing for Robotic Kiwifruit Handling with an Optoelectronic Soft Suction Cup

author.name: Romina Adhami, Ebrahim Shahabi, Alessio Mondini, Samuel M. Youssef, Cosimo Della Santina, Gualtiero Volpe, Barbara Mazzolai

entry.summary: The study develops an optoelectronic soft suction cup with a kiwifruit-specific bicomponent design that estimates interaction forces during contact with real fruit from optical signals. A shallow network achieves pooled R-squared of 0.968 on held-out fruits, and even a simple monotonic mapping from mean optical response reaches 0.925, showing robust force-ratio estimation.

entry.title: Compressed Per-Player Local Methods for Multiplayer Federated Learning: Exact Convergence via Increment Sharing

author.name: Bhavika Balani, TaeHo Yoon, Nicolas Loizou

entry.summary: Addresses convergence failures of compressed communication in multiplayer federated learning by reformulating PEARL-SGD so players share strategy increments rather than strategies themselves, achieving exact convergence to equilibrium under compression. This extends compression-communication tradeoffs to the game-theoretic federated setting.

entry.title: Mind the Divergence: Divergence-Guided Reliability-Aware Fusion and Adaptive LLM Prompting for Conversational Emotion Recognition

author.name: Jingwen Wang, Jiao Li, Yuhang Qian, Yuyin Wang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: For multimodal emotion recognition in conversations (MERC), the paper models inter-modal predictive disagreement among unimodal emotion distributions as a unified signal of semantic incongruity, concealed emotion, and noise, then uses it to guide reliability-aware fusion and adaptive LLM prompting. This lets the system adapt multimodal processing sample-by-sample rather than treating modality reliability as fixed.

entry.title: StockASkill: A Local-First AgentSkill for Intelligent Stock Selection

author.name: Xiangjing An, Zhibin Jiao, Aiting Chen

entry.summary: StockASkill is a local-first agent skill for quantitative equity selection in Chinese A-share markets, embedding a DuckDB OLAP engine over 42.44 million price records and 186,432 financial disclosures, tailored to small agile portfolios with discrete lot execution and drawdown constraints. It is positioned as a quant co-processor for autonomous AI agents.

entry.title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics

author.name: Yubo Song, Pascal A. Schirmer, Subham Sahoo

entry.summary: Proposes a neuromorphic framework for data-light condition monitoring in power electronics, encoding three-phase AC current measurements as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons compatible with spiking neural networks. The latency-coding approach leverages circuit theory to estimate device parameters efficiently and adaptively.

entry.title: Syn2DRE: Synergistic Dual Teacher-Student Framework for Document-level Relation Extraction

author.name: Khai Phan Tran, Xue Li

entry.summary: Syn2DRE is a semi-supervised framework for document-level relation extraction that combines self-supervised learning with cross-supervision in a lightweight teacher-student architecture to generate more reliable pseudo-labels. It also introduces a unified end-to-end training strategy that improves efficiency, and reportedly outperforms prior semi-supervised state of the art on multiple benchmarks. The work reduces reliance on costly large-scale annotation for DocRE.

entry.title: Emergent Low-Dimensional Topological Dynamics Dictate Generalization and Escape Mechanics in Billion-Parameter Neural Networks

author.name: Dongqing Cao

entry.summary: This single-author theoretical paper claims that optimization trajectories in billion-parameter models are confined to a low-dimensional execution submanifold (empirical effective dimension at most 12), and derives a topological generalization bound using a regularized Hessian metric and projected persistent homology, plus results on saddle-escape mechanics. If verified, this would be a notable contribution to understanding why over-parameterized networks generalize. The claims are ambitious relative to prior loss-landscape literature.

entry.title: Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning: A Multi-Objective Framework for Learning Local Distance Functions in Nearest Neighbor Classification

author.name: Isaac Touza

entry.summary: EAML learns instance-dependent positive-definite metrics for nearest neighbor classification via softmax interpolation between anchor points combined with a global low-rank correlation component. An elitist real-coded genetic algorithm optimizes a multi-objective scalar combining prediction error, robustness, smoothness, and regularization.

entry.title: TOFS: Feature Selection with Swap Supervision for Semantic Communication over Fading Channels

author.name: Zhiyi Zhu, Eiji Takimoto, Patrick Finnerty, Chikara Ohta

entry.summary: TOFS is a task-oriented feature selection framework for semantic communication that evaluates feature replacements using receiver classification loss after transmission, using loss differences under independent channel samples as pairwise ranking supervision for a selector network. It accounts for feature interactions and channel-induced distortion when prioritizing what to transmit over fading wireless links. This targets efficient inference under constrained communication resources.

entry.title: Electoral Intelligence: A Neural Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Model for Forecasting Swedish Municipal Elections

author.name: Haodong Qi, Stefano M. Iacus, Pieter Bevelander, Derek S. Hutcheson

entry.summary: Develops a bounded neural zero-inflated negative binomial model for forecasting party-level vote counts in Swedish municipal elections, combining count, zero-inflation, and dispersion components with learned embeddings for party-municipality structure. Trained on 2014-2022 elections and evaluated with held-out performance.

entry.title: pESTO: Iterative p-greedy kernel regression with risk-driven Early STOpping

author.name: L. Bruni Bruno, P. Massa, E. Perracchione, M. Trombini
