The paper is significant because it moves embodied retrieval from what objects exist to what actually works for a task.

entry.title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments

author.name: Mingxuan Li, Huanzhi Mao, Qiuyang Mang, Hanchen Li, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Alex Dimakis

entry.summary: EnvOpt proposes optimizing an LLM agent's stationary environment (shared workspaces like Slack or document collections) as a third optimization axis alongside model and harness tuning. Using real or synthetic tasks without graders or reference answers, it reduces Claude Haiku 4.5 cost by 72% on AutomationBench while improving success, treating environment modification as an automated end-to-end problem.

entry.title: TCSExam: Evaluating Frontier LLMs on the Full Range of TCS Research

author.name: Yifan Luo, Zhengying Liu, Yang Yuan, Zhilin Yang, Andrew Chi-Chih Yao

entry.summary: TCSExam is a benchmark spanning the full range of theoretical computer science research, evaluating theorem proving, solver engineering, and constructions plus direct attempts at open conjectures. TCSExam-Full has 100 expert-reviewed tasks with Lean-kernel or executable checker verification; TCSExam-Lite cuts attempts by 80% at the same per-attempt budget. The authors evaluate eight agents to measure progress toward LLMs contributing to TCS research.

entry.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection

author.name: Woosang Lim (SAINT Machines, KAIST), Yeseul Chang (Chung-Ang University), Jaewoo Lee (Chung-Ang University)

entry.summary: Proposes SPILLWAY, a defense for tool-using agents against prompt injection that separates target admission from sanitization by reading action destinations from tools' typed return fields (such as email sender or payment account) rather than trusting free text. This creates a deterministic, per-task-plan-free security floor that does not depend on a language model making the admission decision, avoiding both model-vulnerability and per-step cost problems of prior defenses.

entry.title: Leave It Better Than Found: Value-Guided Cooperation in Sequential Tasks

author.name: Mario Gomez Andreu, Michael Amir, Antonio Marino, Tianxu An, Marco Hutter, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: This paper tackles ad hoc sequential cooperation between heterogeneous robots that never trained together, avoiding the combinatorial explosion of co-training all robot combinations. It introduces a value-guided approach where a robot improves on a workspace state left by a previous robot. With authors affiliated with strong groups (Prorok, Hutter), the problem framing of embodiment-agnostic cooperation is timely and important.

entry.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale

author.name: Solim LeGris, Philipp Mondorf, Jinran Jin, Akshay K. Jagadish, Brenden M. Lake, Todd M. Gureckis

entry.summary: The authors introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS), an automated search for interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior, applied to hundreds of reasoning problems for both humans and machines. Analysis of the synthesized programs reveals that people and LLMs alike oversimplify, adopt partial explanations, and misinfer dependencies.

entry.title: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance

author.name: Dikshant Kukreja, Gautam Gupta, Avni Mittal, Avinash Anand, Kritarth Prasad, Zhengkui Wang, Timothy Liu, Rajiv Ratn Shah, Aik Beng Ng, Simon See, Erik Cambria

entry.summary: The paper gives a mechanistic account of why language models lose accuracy in the presence of non-evidential, irrelevant context: MLPs enrich irrelevant-token representations, parroting heads transport prefix content to the prediction position, and relational readers fail to fully exclude unrelated sources. The authors then locate where in the computation the intrusion happens. This is relevant to retrieval-augmented, tool-using, and long-context deployments where noisy context is ubiquitous.

entry.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation

author.name: Kangjie Zheng, Amirhossein Vahidi, Liying Jin, Joseph Clarke, Vijaya Baskar MS, Connor Rogerson, Mengji Zhang, Muzlifah Haniffa, Anshul Kundaje, Mo Lotfollahi

entry.summary: MUSS is a sequence-based multi-scale model for single-cell gene regulation that jointly represents DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression while preserving both DNA-level and cell-level resolution. It derives peak- and gene-level representations from DNA via a frozen pre-trained sequence encoder and integrates them with peak-peak self-attention and distance-biased peak-gene interactions. This addresses a real gap between sequence-only models and single-cell omics models that treat genes as opaque vocabulary tokens.

entry.title: A Night at the LLM Zoo: Data Conditioned Flow Matching for Generating Pretrained LLM Weights

author.name: Scott Biggs, Bedionita Soro, Saumya Gupta, Bruno Andreis, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Trains a curated population of 300 GPT-2-scale models (51M-355M parameters) with systematically varied data mixtures across web text, books, math, coding, and French, then applies flow matching to generate pretrained LLM weights conditioned on the training mixture. The paper analyzes the zoo's diversity and shows that generated weights correspond to meaningful, structurally coherent models, advancing weight space learning to LLMs.

entry.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model

author.name: Achille Raviez, Lan Wang, Brendan Delaney

entry.summary: This study introduces time-context, the calendar lookback window before prediction, and systematically evaluates decade-scale time-context (up to 30 years) for an EHR foundation model predicting incident colorectal cancer. The authors pretrain a 34.6M-parameter decoder-only transformer on 1.4B coded events from 3.6M North West London primary-care patients and evaluate on a frozen cohort of over 1,000 cases and matched controls. It provides the first empirical answer to how far back medical history must reach for long-latency disease prediction.

entry.title: KOSMOS: Self-scheduling Persistent Kernels for Communication-Compute Overlap

author.name: Alexander Magro, Aristotle Martin, Ye Wang, Wen Chen

entry.summary: KOSMOS is a library of self-scheduling persistent kernels whose workgroups dynamically switch between communication and computation roles based on queues ordered by consumer demand, eliminating fixed schedules, cost models, and tuned splits for tensor/sequence and expert parallelism. It fuses every TP+SP collective of a transformer layer with its GEMM and runs entire expert layers, targeting idle windows on the critical path of distributed transformer training and inference. This addresses a core systems bottleneck for large model scaling.

entry.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time

author.name: Teresa Delgado, Hugo Hazard, Martin Benfeghoul, Jun Wang, Zafeirios Fountas

entry.summary: LowRAM exploits the observation that attention-head values are largely predictable from their keys, fitting lightweight per-head predictors at test time and storing only residuals for hard-to-reconstruct tokens. This achieves roughly 4x near-lossless value-cache compression, with meta-learning initialization to cut prefill overhead. KV cache memory is a major bottleneck for long-context LLM serving, so this is directly relevant to inference efficiency.

entry.title: When Scores Conflict with Preferences: Pre-Alignment Diagnosis and Adaptive Correction of Constraint Drift in DPO

author.name: Ping Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: This paper identifies constraint drift as a systematic failure mode of DPO when pairwise preferences conflict with pointwise criteria such as safety or correctness scores: conflict pairs tend to increase constraint cost while matching pairs repair it. The authors derive a closed-form pre-alignment diagnostic computable from dataset statistics that predicts whether drift will occur, enabling adaptive correction. This gives practitioners a cheap way to audit preference datasets before alignment.

entry.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity

author.name: Jun Liu, Dajie Sun, Zhenglun Kong, Zhenjiang Fan, Peiyan Dong, Fan Yang, Wenbin Zhang, Geng Yuan, Xue Lin, Yanzhi Wang, Dong Huang

entry.summary: A pre-registered audit of test-time scaling for world-action models on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa finds that claimed gains are largely illusory: a learned value selector underperforms random selection, a hindsight oracle gains little, and most states have identical candidate outcomes. Token pruning cuts FLOPs substantially but delivers far smaller real end-to-end speedups, highlighting simulator and evaluation integrity issues.

entry.title: Familiar letters, not related languages, let unseen languages into a shared space of meaning

author.name: Yuliang Liu, Xinyu Wang, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: Introduces GlyphMind, a tokenizer-free vision transformer reading text as pixels, pretrained to align translations across 27 writing systems. Fine-tuned on untranslated Lao, it retrieves English translations seven times more often than baselines, and controlled experiments show script familiarity, not linguistic relatedness, enables entry into the shared meaning space.

entry.title: ArcRAG: Agentic Compositional Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Jyotin Goel, Abhinav Arun, Tejas Prakash Agarwal, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

entry.summary: ArcRAG addresses cross-construction portability in GraphRAG by inducing a query-local graph interface at inference time from the entities a question mentions, then planning, executing, and repairing multi-hop traversals against it without construction-specific schemas or retuning. This matters because existing retrieval strategies are typically tied to the quirks of the pipeline that built the graph, and this work tests whether retrieval survives graph construction changes.

entry.title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge

author.name: Drake Benjamin Brown, Khushbu Pahwa, Yubin Ge, Salvatore Romeo, Akhil Agnihotri, Yi Zhang, Xiaofei Ma, Daniele Bonadiman

entry.summary: This paper shows that tool-using agent judges remain vulnerable to confirmation bias: a single false pre-screening note attributed to an authority, with no evidential bearing on the verdict, overturns up to 40% of correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets even when judges collect decisive evidence themselves. The cue is treated as a controlled diagnostic of confirmation bias rather than a real-world attack.

entry.title: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models

author.name: Shengjie Wang, Mohsen Fayyaz, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This work shows that Mixture-of-Experts routers provide a training-free interface for controlling reasoning behaviors: sentence-level segments of reasoning traces are labeled with six behaviors (planning, execution, reflection, etc.), enabling targeted regulation of overthinking. Rather than imposing token budgets, the method shapes which behaviors consume test-time compute. It addresses the overthinking problem that wastes compute and can degrade accuracy.

entry.title: AffineGS: Unlocking Accurate Geometry in 3DGS via Spatially Varying Affine Rectification

author.name: Tze Ho Elden Tse, Jizong Peng, Richard Chen, Angela Yao

entry.summary: AffineGS improves geometric accuracy in 3D Gaussian Splatting by identifying a fundamental flaw in depth-guided 3DGS: monocular depth networks exhibit region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions that break global scale-and-shift alignment assumptions. The paper introduces a spatially varying affine rectification model that corrects monocular disparity into scene-consistent geometry. This addresses the well-known gap between 3DGS visual quality and geometric fidelity.

entry.title: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching

author.name: Zeping Zhang, Zhuoya Zhao, Samy Metari, Robert Lagani\`ere

entry.summary: Introduces FreeOcc, a lightweight 4D occupancy world model that factors out ego-motion via explicit SE(2) geometric decoupling within a conditional flow-matching framework, using the planner-provided future ego-motion rather than expensive cross-attention. This creates a purely dynamic feature space enabling attention-free temporal fusion and physics-constrained ODEs on residual agent kinematics.

entry.title: TactileLab: Sim-to-Real Dexterous Robot Manipulation with Efficient Shear-Sensitive Tactile Simulation

author.name: Yijiong Lin, Wenhao He, Toby Jack, Max Yang, Haoran Li, Nathan F. Lepora

entry.summary: TactileLab is a scalable multimodal tactile simulation framework built on IsaacLab, introducing simulated tactile flow, an optical-flow-based representation that estimates dense tangential contact motion from rigid-body simulation instead of expensive soft-body physics. This makes shear-sensitive tactile simulation tractable for large-scale RL and sim-to-real transfer. Given growing interest in tactile sensing for dexterous manipulation, this could become a widely used tool.

entry.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training

author.name: Fuhao Li, Wenxuan Song, Qizhou Huang, Ziyang Zhou, Jingbo Wang, Junwu E, Pengwei Wang, Yan Wang, Shunbo Zhou, Haoang Li

entry.summary: SLA is a spatial-language-action model that makes implicit 3D spatial alignment a transferable foundation-model capability by scaling it into continual pre-training rather than only task-specific adaptation. Initialized from the pretrained pi05 policy, it jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual representations and 3D spatial structure, maintaining this alignment through downstream post-training.

entry.title: Understanding the Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Nuo-Jing Liang, Xiao-Tong Yuan, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical account of chain-of-thought reasoning as compositional OOD generalization, showing CoT generalizes by repeatedly applying a shared single-step predictor to compose in-distribution transitions. It derives bounds relating OOD task risk to in-distribution sub-task risks, number of reasoning steps, training samples, and tokens per step.

entry.title: AI #193: Progress May Dramatically Accelerate

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi Mowshowitz's weekly AI news roundup highlights Anthropic's S-1 filing warning that the company may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI. The post also surveys the week's developments including a major crypto hack, debate over Scott Alexander's critique of SURA, and OpenAI's Model Spec update.

entry.title: WaSP: Wasserstein Data Synthesis Pipeline for Solver-Free Operator Learning

author.name: Ryan Liu, Chuwei Wang, Ricardo Baptista, Andrew Stuart, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: WaSP addresses the distribution mismatch in solver-free training of neural operators by synthesizing manufactured data whose distribution approximates the target in Wasserstein distance, avoiding the mutual-singularity failure of naive manufactured solutions and the optimization issues of physics-informed residuals. The author team includes Anima Anandkumar, Andrew Stuart, and Ricardo Baptista from Caltech.

entry.title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories

author.name: Mingxuan Li, Huanzhi Mao, Ruitao Zheng, Jarod Stanbury James, Yunze Li, Natanya Anderson, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Alex Dimakis

entry.summary: SlackBench evaluates agents on realistic knowledge work that requires locating channels and messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting repository state, reconciling conflicting evidence, and synthesizing across sources, grounded in real code repositories and workplace conversations. It addresses the gap left by benchmarks that rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks.

entry.title: Reconciling Privacy with Provenance for Language Model Watermarks

author.name: Elise L. Han, Tatsunori Hashimoto

entry.summary: The authors propose locally differentially private watermarks that limit the evidential contribution of any individual text while still enabling accurate estimation of aggregate LM usage, reframing watermarking from individual tracking to population-level statistics. This addresses user privacy objections that fuel paraphrasing-based evasion and undermine watermark adoption. The theoretical reconciliation of provenance and privacy is a meaningful contribution to the governance toolkit.

entry.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation

author.name: Christian Clason, Tapio Helin, Medet Nursultanov, Lauri Oksanen

entry.summary: The authors present AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory and its underlying functional analysis were autoformalized using AI proof agents. They organize the library so human reviewers only need to verify formal statements against natural-language intent, finding that risks concentrate in statements rather than machine-checked proofs.

entry.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery

author.name: Haichuan Tan, Bowen Gao, Tao Huang, Jiaxin Tan, Xin Hong, Baoguo Yao, Yifei Wang, Zhichao Deng, Hanji Du, Dapeng Jiang, Yiheng Li, Weiwei Ma, Xin Ma, Yuqi Shi, Zixiang Wang, Kelin Wu, Tianxiang Wu, Wenxuan Xie, Jie Zang, Huiyu Zhang, Mojia Zhang, Yuying Zhang, Ya-Qin Zhang, Wei-Ying Ma, Yanyan Lan

entry.summary: PharmAgents2 is an autonomous multi-agent system for end-to-end drug discovery that combines decision knowledge extracted from scientific literature (Paper2Skill) with self-scaling parallel exploration across targets and hypotheses. The authors also release PharmAgents-Bench v0.1 with 121 expert-assessed questions spanning nine decision scenarios and three end-to-end tasks. It represents a substantial step toward scientific agentic systems in a high-impact domain.

entry.title: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale

author.name: Gautam Gupta, Dikshant Kukreja, Unique Kumar, Avni Mittal, Deepanshu Dabas, Kshitij Sah, Erik Cambria, Rajiv Ratn Shah, Zhengkui Wang, Avinash Anand

entry.summary: This paper studies how quantization and pruning damage in-context retrieval carried by a small set of identifiable attention heads, exactly decomposing observed loss into direct damage and network compensation. It finds the balance between damage and compensation shifts with model scale, so compression can hurt more as models grow. The work goes beyond benchmark scores to explain why compression effects are nonlinear in model size.

entry.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks

author.name: E. Kelly Buchanan, Crystal Zhou, Scott W. Linderman, Christopher R\'e

entry.summary: The paper introduces the concept of benchmark maintenance debt - the growing gap between agentic benchmark scores and the capabilities they are meant to measure as models and infrastructure evolve. The authors propose a continuous-validation workflow combining community reports, agent traces, automated oracle checks, and human-gated repairs, demonstrated on Terminal-Bench.

entry.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists

author.name: Taiming Lu, Sachin Konan, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: Scientist World converts research papers into executable environments: an autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open research question and reproduces its method as a baseline, then evaluates an AI-Scientist against the human authors' achievements. The authors release 1,000 verified environments and report that frontier AI-Scientists surpass human researchers 74 percent of the time on this evaluation. It aims to give AI scientists a runnable world rather than a merely readable literature.

entry.title: Interactive Backdoor Attacks in LLM-Based Proactive Dialogue Systems

author.name: Zhiyang Xia, Yuming Shang, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: Describes an interactive backdoor attack framework against LLM-based proactive dialogue systems, where poisoned fine-tuning data implants a trigger-conditioned policy bias that steers multi-turn post-trigger interactions toward attacker objectives without deployment-time modification. Three complementary attacks are instantiated, showing a novel class of backdoor risk specific to sustained multi-turn dialogue.

entry.title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hong kyu Lee, Kai Shu, Li Xiong

entry.summary: This arXiv paper examines how large vision-language models can be harmed compositionally, where a benign image and a benign prompt combine into harmful content through cross-modal reasoning. The authors propose auditing alignment robustness via un-alignment: they show that minimal supervised fine-tuning can match an LLM-judge safety score achieved by a multi-stage reinforcement-learning pipeline, and that a model's ability to recognize compositional harm is decoupled from its willingness to refuse it. This suggests current safety benchmarks overstate robustness and that un-alignment probes offer a complementary audit signal.

entry.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence

author.name: Canmiao Fu, Chen Li, Guohui Zhang, Hao Lu, Hongyang Wei, Huadong Wu, Huaisong Zhang, Hubery Yin, Liyuan Cui, Qixin Yan, Tong Shao, Xiaoqiang Zhou, Xinhang Leng, Ying Zhang, Zhenhai Liu, Zhipeng Huang

entry.summary: Presents WeLM-Image, a unified image foundation model from WeChat that integrates multimodal understanding with text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. It uses a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone with MoE modules (31.7B stored, ~5.4B activated parameters) designed for single-GPU deployment in large-scale consumer apps. The work is notable for combining unified capabilities with real-world deployment efficiency.

entry.title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Verifier-Based RL Beyond Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Amit Sagtani, Saloni Garg

entry.summary: The paper builds a deterministic benchmark of 1,877 synthetic GPU and LLM training failure diagnosis tasks to directly measure the marginal contribution of RL from verifiable rewards beyond supervised fine-tuning. A striking pilot finding shows 1,200 gold demonstrations nearly solve the benchmark via SFT, while the RL stage's contribution can be measured exactly in a controlled comparison.

entry.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations

author.name: Xiaobo Chen, Genliang Zhu, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang

entry.summary: A preregistered study of 73 tasks across 60 documented API/runtime changes in CPython, Node.js, and SQLite showing that LLM-repaired code can pass typical-input release checks yet return wrong results, with an all-assertions gate releasing 0.410 of wrong repairs. Adding a single edge input derived from release notes cuts the release rate to 0.065, and even blind adversarial inputs from an LLM writer reach similar protection.

entry.title: Structured Machine Theory of Mind from Agent Trajectories

author.name: Nigel F. Doering, Rahath Malladi, Arshia Sangwan, M Tanjid Hasan Tonmoy, Jacob Doan, David Danks, Tauhidur Rahman

entry.summary: SMToM attributes explicit, independently supervised belief and desire representations to agents from observed trajectories within a Belief-Desire-Intention causal structure. Unlike purely predictive behavior models, it supports counterfactual intervention on mental states, answering how behavior would change if beliefs or preferences differed. This advances interpretable and causally grounded machine theory of mind.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Selection: The Importance of Coverage over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lalchand Pandia, Kanishka Misra, Allyson Ettinger

entry.summary: This paper finds that difficulty-based data selection scores, effective for small classifiers, often fail to beat random selection for LLM fine-tuning because random selection better covers the input distribution. The authors propose a simple clustering-based method that selects representative data and outperforms difficulty-based approaches across diverse single-domain tasks. The result challenges a common intuition in the data-selection literature.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Guan Zhe Hong, Sumeet Ramesh Motwani, Liang Chen, Yangchen Pan, Junchi Yu, Jialin Yu, Philip Torr, Yi Ren

entry.summary: This paper provides a mechanistic analysis of on-policy distillation's learning dynamics, treating it as a feedback loop with two stages: conversion of the distillation signal into parameter updates, and broadcast through which updates change predictions across prefixes and reshape the rollout distribution. The framework explains both limited student retention of teacher behavior and generalization behavior. As OPD becomes a major LM post-training paradigm, understanding these dynamics is increasingly important.

entry.title: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization

author.name: Anyuan Zhuo, Shaohua Zhang, Yuan Lin, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: The authors train a sparse autoencoder on the output of a Mixture-of-Experts layer and exploit the affine structure of the SAE encoder to decompose each latent's pre-activation exactly over experts, yielding per-expert feature attributions. This reveals fine-grained, human-interpretable specialization of experts, going beyond coarse domain-counting analyses of routing statistics. The method offers a new lens on what individual MoE experts contribute, relevant to modern sparse models.

entry.title: Capturing Membrane Dynamics and Spike Timing of Human Neurons at Scale using Neural Operators

author.name: Luca Ghafourpour, Cindy Zhao, Valentin Duruisseaux, Bahareh Tolooshams, Philip H. Wong, Costas A. Anastassiou, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: The authors extend the NOBLE neural-operator framework to learn a shared, cell-type-specific operator across heterogeneous neuron populations conditioned on interpretable electrophysiological features, enabling scalable biophysically realistic modeling of human neurons. This avoids training separate surrogate models per neuron while preserving cellular dynamics and within-type variability.

entry.title: PlayGen2: Learning Real-Time Playable Worlds with Explicit 3D State

author.name: Jihai Zhang, Yuhan Zhou, Junyou Li, Deheng Ye, Qi Dou, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: PlayGen2 is a real-time interactive world model that separates learned 3D state evolution from neural rendering, maintaining persistent world memory with a volumetric occupancy grid and identity-indexed 3D entity states instead of using generated frames as the sole recurrent representation. This design targets long-term spatial and temporal consistency and responsive control in playable world generation.

entry.title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents

author.name: Shuli Jiang, Khushbu Pahwa, Yuting Zhang, Yi Zhang, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: This paper formulates human decision capacity allocation: given limited human attention, at which decisions should an LLM agent consult a human? It introduces Consultation Value Distillation (CVD), which estimates consultation value offline via Monte Carlo executor rollouts, noting that value is executor-relative since the same human input benefits different downstream agents differently, and distills these values into the agent. This matters as agent capabilities scale while human oversight capacity does not.

entry.title: Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining

author.name: Daichi Hotta, Yohei Kobashi, Takeshi Kojima, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Tests whether looped Transformers (recurrently reusing layers without extra parameters or data) help multimodal pretraining under a strict 100M-word BabyLM budget with pre-registered comparisons and three seeds per condition. A 12-layer stack looped four times exceeds a standard 48-layer Transformer in the text-only comparison, clarifying both benefits and limits of recurrent depth.

entry.title: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations

author.name: Nil-Jana Akpinar, Eugenia Kim, Natalie Isak, Amanda Minnich, Victoria Westerhoff, Matthew Dressman

entry.summary: The paper proposes detecting observable AI response-level behaviors that are risk factors for psychological harm, then aggregating them for longitudinal monitoring, since direct harm measurement is impractical. It operationalizes eight behaviors, builds a synthetic multi-label corpus of 47,062 responses with 373,873 labels plus human validation, and compares embedding classifiers, LLM judges, and a classifier-judge cascade.

entry.title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models

author.name: Lele Yang, Muxi Diao, Zhonghao Yan, Jiankang Chen, Bin Wen, Tingting Gao, Wentao Zhang, Kongming Liang, Zhanyu Ma, Weiran Xu

entry.summary: LooM improves looped transformers by looping only decoder layers after the first, which read a global memory written once per token and publish KV entries only on first visit, so the cache does not grow with loop count. Layers loop independently, allowing any budget from 3 to 21 layer executions per token, and one model trained on random budgets can adapt compute at inference.

entry.title: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models

author.name: Douglas Guilbeault, Bhargav Srinivasa Desikan

entry.summary: This paper finds a systematic link between conceptual abstraction and gender across roughly 40,000 single-word and 67,000 multi-word expressions drawn from billions of internet words and millions of images: more abstract concepts are more strongly associated with men. The pattern replicates across languages, semantic domains, grammatical structure, and multiple measurement methods including human and AI classifiers. It matters because it documents a large-scale societal bias embedded in the data that trains language models.

entry.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?

author.name: Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu, Tianyi Men, Yupu Hao, Jiachun Li, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: Using a Pass@(K,T) metric over sampling breadth and interaction depth, the paper shows that multi-turn agentic RL gains depend heavily on turn budgets and shrink when budgets tighten, and that such RL improves error recovery and long-horizon resilience rather than single-step decision quality. The authors discuss process supervision signals and propose BudgetMix RL, which varies budgets during training, as a mitigation. It offers a sharper empirical picture of what agentic RL actually teaches.

entry.title: Where Do Reported Long-Video QA Gains Come From? A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection, and Expert Routing

author.name: Shih-Yao Lin

entry.summary: VideoRouteAudit is a controlled audit showing that on the full Video-MME long bucket, no tested frame selector significantly beats uniform sampling when backbone, budget, decoding, prompt and grader are held fixed, with all effects within confidence intervals of zero. It also demonstrates that contrasts reported at the commonly used n=200 subset scale are unstable. This is a valuable replication-and-rigor study for the long-video QA literature.

entry.title: ArtCrafter: Feed-Forward Generation of Articulated 3D Object with Analytic Joint Derivation

author.name: Minh Canh Tu, Quang-Binh Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen

entry.summary: ArtCrafter is a feed-forward DiT-based generative model that produces articulated 3D objects from paired images showing an object at rest and in an open state. It uses a slot-attention-inspired 1+2N slot layout to jointly generate part-level meshes consistent across articulation states, with analytic derivation of joints. This matters for robotics simulation, where articulated assets are a key bottleneck.

entry.title: TerraMesh-Masks: Open-Vocabulary Segmentation for Earth Observation

author.name: Benedikt Blumenstiel, Hugues Devimeux, Johannes Jakubik, Konrad Schindler

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale open-vocabulary segmentation dataset for Earth observation with 16 million binary masks aligned to nine million multimodal samples, annotated using OpenStreetMap and Overture-derived semantics, plus an expert-reviewed benchmark. It addresses the poor transfer of natural-image OVS models to satellite imagery due to differences in semantics, scale, and sensing modality.

entry.title: Spatial-UMI-Dream: Scaling World Action Models with Metric Geometry for UMI Manipulation

author.name: Weiduo Yuan, Ze Yuan, Sihan Liu, Jionghao Wang, Liang Heng, Zhenyu Zhao, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Spatial-UMI-Dream is a 5B-parameter spatial world action model pretrained on 605 hours of RGB-D Universal Manipulation Interface data, jointly predicting future RGB, fisheye-aligned metric depth, and actions through two-stage world-only and world-action training. Making metric geometry explicit via stereo-derived depth enables evaluation of UMI policies in learned world models rather than real rollouts.

entry.title: LMGN: A Unified Policy Learning Model for Last-Mile Grasp-Navigation

author.name: Xuenmin Hu, Qingxue Qian, Wei Luo, Benyi Ma, Bo Tang, Long Chen

entry.summary: This paper addresses the underexplored last-mile navigation problem for legged robots with manipulators, where base placement, approach direction, and grasp execution must be jointly decided. The authors propose LMGN, a unified policy learning model for quadruped loco-manipulation, introducing an Explicit Distance and Directional Reachability representation to guide the integrated behavior. This matters because it bridges the gap between navigation and manipulation research on mobile manipulators.

entry.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control

author.name: Satvik Sharma, Hengyuan Hu, Mihika Kamat, Dorsa Sadigh, Jeannette Bohg

entry.summary: RoboARCade is a benchmark for agentic robot control (ARC), where multi-modal foundation-model agents act directly as robot policies on long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments. Built on MuJoCo with modular task packs and interchangeable agent interfaces, the benchmark hardens existing open-source tasks and separates leading agents such as the GPT-6 Astra family.

entry.title: Flexible Intensities Matter: A Comprehensive Re-evaluation of Hawkes Processes and Neural Temporal Point Processes

author.name: Hendrik Mehrtens, Florian Buettner, Oliver Stegle

entry.summary: This systematic re-evaluation compares Poisson and Hawkes processes of increasing flexibility against neural temporal point processes on standard benchmarks and two large-scale medical datasets (UK Biobank and MIMIC-IV). The authors find earlier claims of neural superiority stem from unfair comparisons against overly restricted classical baselines.

entry.title: Regression with Many Generated Controls

author.name: Timothy Christensen, Daniel Vebman

entry.summary: This econometrics paper studies linear regression when covariates are endogenous, a latent variable that would control for endogeneity exists, and practitioners can cheaply generate many proxies for that latent control using different AI/ML imputation methods. The authors use a transparent model to characterize what estimand each practical approach targets (including all proxies, factor aggregation, instrumental variables, and nonlinear variants), determine when each recovers the true parameter of interest, and provide practical recommendations. This matters as ML/AI-generated imputations increasingly enter empirical research pipelines without principled statistical guidance.

entry.title: Adversarial Training Can Further Hide a Backdoor, but Does It Improve Trigger Identification?

author.name: Tom Angsten

entry.summary: This post reexamines the Sleeper Agents paper's claim that adversarial training teaches backdoored models to better identify when to act unsafely, showing that firing-rate saturation means weaker benign explanations are also consistent with the results. The authors propose using log-odds of the backdoor response as a more precise metric and replicate the picture on Redwood Research's open-weight Llama 3.1 8B sleeper agent with and without red-team prompt safety fine-tuning.

entry.title: Responsible GenAI Use During Active Armed Conflict: Evidence from Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms

author.name: Dalia Ali, Yearin Lee, Cheng Yu, Ro Encarnaci\'on, Alsanosi Adam, Dana\'e Metaxa, Ingmar Weber, Orestis Papakyriakopoulos

entry.summary: Through a survey of 89 respondents and 15 interviews, this study examines how Sudan's community-led Emergency Response Rooms use generative AI in humanitarian work under active conflict, where war makes human expertise dangerous or hard to reach. Participants found GenAI most useful precisely where outputs were hardest to verify, while cautioning that it could not independently replace local knowledge. It fills a real gap by centering community responders in responsible-AI research.

entry.title: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels

author.name: Kwanyoung Park, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: MAC-v2 tackles long-horizon model-based value expansion in pixel-based offline RL by training a reconstruction-free latent world model with action chunking, learning representations from prediction and control objectives rather than pixel reconstruction. This avoids encoding control-irrelevant visual details that compound errors during imagined rollouts. It addresses a known weakness of model-based RL in visual domains.

entry.title: What the Middleman Delivers: Answer Behavior, Tool Permissions, and Billed Usage in LLM API Relays

author.name: Xiaodong Wu, Zhimin Zhao, Qi Li, Chaklam Cheong, Xiangman Li, Jianbing Ni

entry.summary: This audit tests 20 third-party API relay services reselling access to established models GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5, finding behavioral differences from official responses in several low-price relays and probing billing accuracy and tool permissions beyond answer comparison. The study highlights risks that relays may substitute models or misreport usage.

entry.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception

author.name: Sacha Jungerman, Kaustubh Sadekar, Avery Gump, Sriram Narayanan, Shantanu Gupta, Bhuyashi Deka, Srinivasa Narasimhan, Atul Ingle, Mohit Gupta

entry.summary: VisionSIM is a physically grounded simulation platform modeling the raw measurement process of heterogeneous robot perception sensors including LiDAR, event cameras, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal imaging, exposing modality-specific failure modes like LiDAR pileup and iToF phase wrapping. By elevating sensor realism to a first-class concern, it enables training and evaluation under realistic degradation that idealized simulators hide.

entry.title: Neural Compression over Equivalence Classes: Exact Gauges and Functional Rate-Distortion

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino

entry.summary: This paper exploits the fact that neural networks have many function-preserving parameterizations, searching exact gauge transformations and controlled functional perturbations to find cheaper representations selected by an unchanged compressor. Across SmolLM2 and Qwen3 checkpoints, the method reduces Zstandard-compressed checkpoint size by up to 23.4 percent. This is a genuinely novel angle on model compression via representation symmetry.

entry.title: Provable Zeroth-Order Safe Exploration for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

author.name: Weiqin Chen, Xinmeng Huang, Dongsheng Ding, Santiago Paternain

entry.summary: The paper proposes ZO-LBPG, a reward-model-free log-barrier policy gradient method with zeroth-order estimates from human preferences, guaranteeing that every policy executed during Safe-RLHF training — including exploration policies — remains feasible. Conservative constraint margins and coupled rollouts handle noisy feedback. This strengthens the safety guarantee beyond convergence-to-feasibility of primal-dual approaches.

entry.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision

author.name: Michal Shavit, Yongji Wang, Tristan Buckmaster

entry.summary: The paper combines physics-informed neural networks used as a search mechanism with rigorous computer-assisted certification and formal verification to compute periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves, learning wave profiles, speed, and surface tension from governing equations without data. Networks reach near-machine-precision equation residuals even in strongly nonlinear regimes, recovering high-amplitude Stokes waves.

entry.title: The Harness Is the Model: Agent Scaffolding Changes a Fixed LLM's Compliance with Banking Conduct Rules, Unevenly Across Models

author.name: Mehmet Murat Huyut

entry.summary: Tests whether agent scaffolding changes regulatory compliance when the underlying LLM is held fixed, running four open-weight models under five harnesses on 156 pre-registered cases in a simulated retail bank covering EU consumer-credit, payments, AML, and related rules. Findings show harness choice alters compliance behavior and does so unevenly across models.

entry.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria

author.name: Zainab Afolabi, Nikita Kozodoi, Jack Butler, Babs Khalidson

entry.summary: NaijaFacts is a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria authored by native speakers in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa, grounded in official statistics. By asking parallel questions about the UK and US, it separates a language effect (knowing a fact but degrading in a low-resource language) from a knowledge effect (the fact absent in all languages) across eight frontier and Nigeria-adapted models.

entry.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs

author.name: Austin C. Kozlowski, Avital Mintz, Madison Lee

entry.summary: This study shows that prompting an LLM to adopt political personas systematically alters the representational geometry of latent space, comparing projections of over 9,000 words and 33 semantic axes under liberal and conservative personas against neutral baselines. The finding challenges the assumption underlying linear probes and sparse autoencoders that features maintain consistent representations across contexts.

entry.title: Does Context Compression Preserve Refusal Alignment?

author.name: Anthony Nguyen, Wenjun Lin

entry.summary: The paper shows that encoder-based context compression systematically weakens refusal behavior in instruction-tuned LLMs despite high reconstruction fidelity, persisting across model families and compression architectures. Mechanistic analysis attributes this to attenuation of activations along the decoder's learned refusal direction, and the authors propose Memory Steering, an inference-time intervention restoring refusal rates near baseline. It reveals an alignment blind spot in compression pipelines.

entry.title: MetricTrail: Revisiting the Power of Metric Depth and Local Optimization for Long-Sequence Streaming 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jingnan Gao, Jiahui Huang, Sven Elflein, Jianhao Zheng, Bingxin Ke, Xiaokang Yang, Yichao Yan, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Qunjie Zhou, Jiawei Ren, Shengyu Huang

entry.summary: MetricTrail is a streaming system for camera motion estimation and dense reconstruction from long monocular videos, improving DPVO-style sparse local estimation with single-image metric depth priors and DINOv3-augmented correspondence features, trained only on short clips. Strong author team including Leal-Taixe (TUM) and collaborators. Long-sequence streaming SLAM/reconstruction is an active, important problem.

entry.title: StitchEdit: Stitching Depth Priors into Image Editors via Per-Layer Gradient Probing

author.name: Qin Guo, Dan Xu

entry.summary: StitchEdit enables geometry-aware spatial edits in diffusion-based image editors by activating the backbone's latent depth priors. Using per-layer gradient probing, the authors show depth and editing objectives are compatible in early transformer layers but conflict in late layers, explaining why naive depth conditioning fails. The method stitches depth guidance only where compatible, preserving visual quality while enabling viewpoint, occlusion, and object manipulation edits.

entry.title: PhySA: Decoupling Aesthetic and Physical Rewards for Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Yunwan Fu, Sicheng He, Jiageng Mao, Yue Wang

entry.summary: This paper finds that VLM aesthetic preferences for humanoid gaits conflict with physical smoothness: across four production VLMs, clips with higher joint acceleration actually received higher aesthetic scores. PhySA keeps VLM aesthetic rewards and physical smoothness corrections on separate, independently removable reward channels. This counterintuitive finding about VLM reward signals is valuable for anyone using foundation models as reward sources.

entry.title: Towards the Query Complexity of Sampling under Strong Log-Concavity and Log-Sobolev Inequalities

author.name: Huanjian Zhou, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: This theory paper proves query-complexity lower bounds for sampling with first-order oracles: any randomized sampler for strongly log-concave targets with condition number 2 requires exp(Omega(log^(1/3) d)) queries even from a warm start, ruling out polylogarithmic dimension dependence and separating this class from Gaussian sampling. It further proves an Omega(kappa) lower bound for L-smooth targets satisfying log-Sobolev inequalities, showing log-Sobolev sampling is strictly harder.

entry.title: Pediatric ECG foundation model via adult-to-pediatric fine-tuning: downstream tasks and clinical evaluation

author.name: Yu Cao, Haiyan Xu, Xiaohan Li, Jian Yang, Yuqing Feng, Wei Wang, Haomin Li

entry.summary: Using 339,563 pediatric 12-lead ECGs from 238,189 children, the authors show that fine-tuning an adult ECG foundation model substantially outperforms both direct transfer and training from scratch (AUC 0.9695 vs 0.8256 and 0.9661), and reaches strong performance with only 1% of training data. External validation on 10,999 ECGs across 30 labels plus age regression and congenital heart disease classification supports generalization. This is a meaningful clinical AI result for an underserved population.

entry.title: Finite-Time Convergence and Regret Guarantees for Neural Reinforcement Learning in POMDPs

author.name: Jingjuan Huang, Zhiyao Zhang, Alvaro Velasquez, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Jia Liu

entry.summary: Provides finite-time convergence and regret guarantees for neural reinforcement learning in POMDPs under the filter stability assumption, using truncated-history superstate MDP surrogates. The analysis removes the restrictive i.i.d. sampling oracle required by prior work and goes beyond linear function approximation, addressing long-range history dependence with non-i.i.d. trajectory data.

entry.title: Localization Does Not Imply Steerability: A Mechanistic Study of Sign Errors in LLM Mathematics

author.name: Shradha Agarwal, Tariq J., Deepak Rajbhar

entry.summary: Investigates where sign errors arise inside LLMs during multi-step mathematics, showing across six open models (14B-675B) that wrong signs are committed late by MLP layers in the last quarter of the network, present even in the base Qwen model before instruction tuning. Mechanisms vary, including fixed minus-stamp layers that push a minus regardless of the correct answer. The title thesis is that locating a behavior mechanistically does not guarantee it can be reliably steered.

entry.title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking

author.name: Moonseok Choi, Jongwon Jeong, Minki Kang, Giung Nam, Juho Lee

entry.summary: SKIM introduces the first pruning and distillation framework designed for LLM agents under grammar-constrained structured generation, exploiting the insight that only decision-critical token positions matter for output validity. It partitions positions into context, decision, and format roles and applies role-guided masking across both pruning and distillation stages.

entry.title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks

author.name: Zhiyu Liu, Xinyu Yang

entry.summary: This carefully controlled study tests whether frontier LLMs can audit clinical prediction networks from raw weights alone, using tanh networks (105-38,401 weights) trained on simulated subarachnoid haemorrhage cohorts with planted relationships and a subgroup under-recording bias. GPT-6 Astra and four other GPT models were evaluated under pre-specified conditions separating weight reading from running code. The key finding — that computation, not raw weight access, drives auditing capability — has real implications for model auditing and the earlier claims that LLMs can read network weights.

entry.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression

author.name: Sheldon Liang, Ali Taghibakhshi, Saurav Muralidharan, Sharath Turuvekere Sreenivas, Ashwath Aithal, Pavlo Molchanov, Nima Tajbakhsh

entry.summary: AutoCompress incorporates hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and GPU memory directly into differentiable architecture search for LLM pruning, using serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end measurements. It jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous compressed architectures, moving beyond parameter-count proxies.

entry.title: TrustMix: Graceful Degradation for Pretrained Models under Distribution Shift

author.name: Juliusz Ziomek, Maike Osborne, Yee Whye Teh

entry.summary: TrustMix is a lightweight post-hoc method that blends a pretrained model's predictive distribution with a user-specified fallback distribution, collapsing toward the fallback as an out-of-distribution deviation statistic grows. This makes a network's implicit extrapolation assumptions explicit and controllable, providing graceful degradation rather than overconfident OOD predictions. The fallback can encode domain-specific priors.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration:Higher-Order Interactions in Policy Improvement

author.name: Kaixuan Liu, Guojun Xiong

entry.summary: The paper identifies a flaw in training LLM multi-agent orchestrators with per-decision advantages: it ignores interactions between orchestration decisions whose joint effect is not the sum of individual effects. The proposed IAPO framework explicitly models higher-order interactions in policy improvement for orchestrators that select agents and control information flow. This addresses a real gap as learned orchestration becomes central to LLM agent systems.

entry.title: Instrumental Variables in Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes

author.name: Lars Pennig, S{\o}ren Wengel Mogensen, Niki Kilbertus

entry.summary: This work extends instrumental variable methods for causal identification under unobserved confounding to continuous-time stochastic processes governed by SDEs, with a stochastic-process instrument and structural assumptions encoded at the infinitesimal drift level. The authors contrast these assumptions with those on discretized versions of the same process. This fills a real gap between static IV theory and continuously evolving causal systems.

entry.title: PBPO: Prefix-Block Policy Optimization for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Katherine Tieu, Dongqi Fu, Si Zhang, Hanqing Zeng, Tianxin Wei, Chenglin Wei, Yinglong Xia, Hong Li, Jingrui He

entry.summary: The paper develops PBPO, a block-level policy optimization method for diffusion language models that decode autoregressively across blocks while denoising multiple tokens per block. Because exact block likelihood is intractable, the authors construct a prefix-block state and a factorized one-step surrogate where the block surrogate ratio is a product of token ratios, enabling stable policy-gradient-style training for dLLMs. This extends the RLHF/policy optimization toolkit to the emerging diffusion LM paradigm.

entry.title: Reading a neuron's tuning from its correlations with other neurons

author.name: Francesco L\"assig

entry.summary: This paper shows a transformer trained on unlabeled correlation matrices of 512 sampled neurons can decode mouse visual cortex neurons' preferred orientation and receptive-field position without stimulus information, achieving substantially better-than-chance accuracy in-vivo and on digital twins. This demonstrates that pairwise population correlations contain stimulus-tuning information previously thought to require stimulus recordings.

entry.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription

author.name: Daniel Huang, Qi He, Shaoxiong Duan, Yingjie Li, Qiao Cheng, Yitao Duan

entry.summary: Presents R2T2, a streaming ASR model post-trained from Qwen3-ASR-1.7B that never revises its earlier output while maintaining accuracy and low latency, aimed at machine consumers that act on each token immediately. It introduces the Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) notion, proving monotonicity properties, and trains on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio.

entry.title: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation

author.name: Chenyang Le, Pei Zhang, Yuxiang Chen, Bing Han, Derek F. Wong, Baosong Yang, Yanmin Qian

entry.summary: CRESiST proposes an end-to-end interleaved read-write framework for simultaneous speech translation built on an omni-modal LLM, interleaving speech chunks and text tokens to achieve full KV cache reuse and segmentation-free infinite-stream inference. A reinforcement-style policy learns when to read and write without rigid offline alignment, reducing reliance on external voice activity detection.

entry.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability

author.name: Xiangdong Zhang, Xiaohan Qin, Sunan Zou, Tuo Dai, Bizhao Shi, Zhuo Xia, Yebin Yang, Yizhou Chen, Yuliang Liu, Yu Cheng, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: This paper systematically dissects Hyper-Connections, an architecture increasingly adopted in frontier language models, showing that learned read/write gating and unconstrained mixing each alone match full mHC performance, and that repeated access to the expanded residual state drives training overhead. These findings yield SimpleHC, a simplified variant with reduced overhead. It provides valuable architectural clarity for an area of growing industrial relevance.

entry.title: VINO: Revisiting 3D Representation Learning with Volume Transformers

author.name: Adrian Kruse, Kadir Yilmaz, Daan de Geus, Francis Engelmann, Bastian Leibe

entry.summary: VINO revisits core design choices in self-supervised 3D representation learning, replacing hierarchical PTv3 backbones with a ViT-like Volume Transformer and redesigning student-teacher objectives for cross-view matching and masked prediction. It aims to bring the success of 2D vision foundation models to 3D scenes. This matters because 3D representation learning has lagged behind its 2D counterpart.

entry.title: Compact Motion Embeddings for Feed-forward Unified Human Animation

author.name: Seonwook Park, Hyunsoo Cha, Amrita Mazumdar, Shengze Wang, Tianye Li, Hanbyul Joo, Koki Nagano, Shalini De Mello

entry.summary: FUHA is a real-time-capable feed-forward transformer that learns a compact motion embedding covering face, hand, and body articulation while excluding driver appearance, using a Q-Former over frozen visual features and a contrastive loss for motion-appearance disentanglement. It unifies full-body, upper-body, and face animation from a reference image. Strong author list (Meta/NYU-affiliated researchers including De Mello, Joo, Nagano).

entry.title: BiGrounder: Bidirectional Training Unlocks the Potential of GUI Grounding

author.name: Dengyao Shi, Tianyu Fu, Fei Hu, Anyang Su, Hanning Wang, Shuo Wang, Minghui Wu, Chenxu Zhao, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: BiGrounder improves GUI grounding (mapping natural language instructions to screen coordinates) via bidirectional training that generates varied descriptions for the same target coordinate, addressing the sparsity of descriptions in training data. This increases robustness to linguistic variation and helps models with limited exploratory capability during reinforcement learning. GUI grounding is a critical capability for autonomous computer-use agents.

entry.title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity

author.name: Rupam Mukherjee, Mehakdeep Singh, Shirin Dasgupta, Subhamoy Mandal

entry.summary: Proposes a patient-level oral cancer screening model that reads smartphone photographs with a segmentation-guided foundation model, fuses multiple photographs per patient with risk factors, and refers through a threshold with finite-sample sensitivity guarantees. It correctly reframes screening as a patient-level referral decision with a bounded miss rate rather than per-image classification.

entry.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding

author.name: Yu-Cheng Chou, Shihao Wang, Jin Huang, Chi-Pin Huang, Chiao-An Yang, Xianzhe Fan, Jing Wang, Zhiqi Li, Yuanguo Kuang, Ruijie Zheng, Johan Bjorck, Sifei Liu, Hang Su, Abhishek Badki, Lei Zhang, Alan Yuille, Linxi "Jim'' Fan, Jan Kautz, Zhiding Yu

entry.summary: VFlash accelerates visual planning in physical AI by jointly predicting structured visual primitives (points, boxes, trajectories) instead of generating coordinate tokens one at a time, using a lightweight drafter that emits an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to primitive type, dimensionality, and length, making richer spatial predictions much cheaper.

entry.title: Semantics-to-Contact: A Stagewise Framework for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Guanren Qiao, Ruixiang Ouyang, Sheng Xu, Yueci Deng, Yunxin Tai, Kui Jia, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: S2C decomposes contact-rich manipulation into semantic focusing, where a vision-language model localizes task-relevant regions across visually diverse scenes, and contact refinement via real-world human-in-the-loop residual reinforcement learning. This two-stage design reduces visual overfitting and exploration burden. It is a practical recipe for transferring RL manipulation policies to varied real-world visual conditions.

entry.title: Terrain-Indexed Motion Priors and Geometric Support for Extreme Humanoid Parkour

author.name: Chenghao Sun, Youhao Lyu, Zizheng Li, Shuting Zhang, Ziyang Dong, Wenhao Cui

entry.summary: The paper presents a three-stage progressive imitation framework for humanoid parkour: privileged imitation produces executable references, terrain-indexed adversarial motion priors guide skill acquisition, and geometric support guidance with reduced prior weight adapts hand-knee contacts. Demonstrations supply traversal behavior while contact patterns adapt to the robot's proportions and support surfaces. This pushes humanoid agility into extreme terrain regimes.

entry.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions

author.name: Arpit Bahety, Skand Peri, Sriniket Ambatipudi, Chen Xu, Haruki Nishimura, Masha Itkina, Roberto Mart\'in-Mart\'in

entry.summary: OopsieRecover teaches VLA models to recover from manipulation failures using semantics to capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, so only a handful of corrective demonstrations are needed. By intervening on semantic descriptions rather than associating corrective actions purely with raw observations, the learned corrections generalize beyond demonstrated scenarios, avoiding the high interaction cost of DAgger-style fine-tuning.

entry.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction

author.name: Zheyu Zhang, Yuanhao Huang, Fan Feng, Jie Liu

entry.summary: The authors audit the state-transition decoder used in STATE (a foundation model for perturbation response prediction) across multiple encoders and cell lines under CRISPRi, finding its first attention layer has a low-rank output. They show this low-rank bottleneck ties prediction reliability to distance from training responses, providing a way to assess per-prediction trustworthiness for experiment prioritization.

entry.title: An Information Bottleneck for Post-hoc Memorization Mitigation in LLMs

author.name: Dina EL Zein, Shashi Kumar, James Henderson

entry.summary: The authors propose a plug-and-play nonparametric variational information bottleneck inserted between a frozen LLM backbone and its language modeling head, compressing final hidden representations to filter out memorized copyrighted or private sequences without retraining the model. This addresses serious privacy and IP concerns around verbatim memorization. Evaluation covers memorization extraction benchmarks.

entry.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Guhan Chen, Bohan Li, Jun Rao, Hejin Wang, Songtao Tian, Yexin Xie, Xiaojun Meng, Peng Yuan, Jiansheng Wei, Xuebo Liu, Zixiong Yu

entry.summary: CoRD addresses a blind spot of on-policy distillation: states the teacher would reach but the student does not are rarely supervised. It keeps the on-policy loss while shifting the training-state distribution toward the teacher, drawing rollouts from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher via maximal coupling of speculative decoding, so interventions are rare and recede as the student improves. Experiments span six base students from the Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 families across sizes from 0.6B upward.

entry.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenruo Liu, Zihan Wang, Yijun Dong, Qi Lei

entry.summary: Tracking singular spectra and subspaces of LoRA updates across SFT and RL stages on mathematical reasoning tasks, the authors find RL concentrates the spectrum at all learning rates while SFT expands it, and RL rotates singular subspaces faster at small learning rates. A one-ingredient-at-a-time interpolation identifies group-mean baseline subtraction as the source of both contrasts, supported by a quadratic multi-index model analysis. This sharpens understanding of the SFT-to-RL pipeline used widely in LLM training.

entry.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting

author.name: Lingfei Qian, Yan Wang, Xueqing Peng, Yupeng Cao, Yuechen Jiang, Zhuohan Xie, Anke Xu, Wenbo Cao, Jiarui Chen, Zehan Li, Jimin Huang, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Yuehua Tang, Sophia Ananiadou, Jian-Yun Nie

entry.summary: FinDendro is a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. facts from 1999 to 2026 designed to verify whether vendor knowledge cutoffs, self-reports, or role-play date instructions can be trusted when backtesting LLMs on financial prediction. Each fact yields value, recall, and predict prompts, probing whether models actually know or merely claim not to know future outcomes.

entry.title: Guidance Is a Field, Not a Scalar: Interval-Integrated Classifier-Free Guidance for One-Step Video Generation

author.name: Zijie Meng, Xixin Cao

entry.summary: The paper argues optimal classifier-free guidance varies with noise level, spatial content, and frame position, and resolves the conflict with one-step MeanFlow generators by absorbing an arbitrary guidance field into the integral-based training target. This enables guidance-field scheduling for single-function-evaluation video generation where multi-step rescheduling is impossible. A conceptually sharp contribution to generative modeling theory.

entry.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes

author.name: Hao Yu, Zhenwei Wang, Yongzhen Hu, Yuning Gong, Junta Wu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Tengfei Wang, Chunchao Guo, Sida Peng

entry.summary: Identifies that feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods predict attributes in radial-distance-normalized spaces whose mismatch with actual Gaussian spacing across scene scales causes systematic supervision ambiguity. SplatAnything introduces Gaussian Spacing Normalization to canonicalize a robust scene-level spacing statistic, plus a benchmark to assess generalization across arbitrary scenes.

entry.title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization

author.name: B\'alint Gyevn\'ar, Simon DeDeo

entry.summary: Using a simulated collaboration methodology on nine major human Lean collaborations with 4.7M definitions, the authors measure where AI agents diverge from human preferences during proof construction. They find agents are far more drawn than humans to explicitly marked surface syntax over deeper semantics, and map systematic preference divergences across the proof-making process.

entry.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance

author.name: Yupeng Cao, Xueqing Peng, Lingfei Qian, Haohang Li, Yangyang Yu, Anke Xu, Wenbo Cao, Yan Wang, Yuechen Jiang, Yuyan Wang, Zhuohan Xie, Yankai Chen, Zehan Li, Jimin Huang, Xue Liu, Jian-Yun Nie, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: FINCOSMOS is an open-world evaluation paradigm for financial agents in which a simulated user holds a hidden strategy from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked, while the agent must fetch live web data under time-dependent correctness. This surfaces silent failure modes (unrequested strategies, unverified data, lookahead backtests) that closed-world benchmarks remove by construction.

entry.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents

author.name: Yizhen Jiang, Haowei Guo, Tianyi Bai, Zengjie Hu, Lu Ma, Zhengyang Zhao, Haoze Sun, Peng Pei, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: MCPHallu is a benchmark of 358 tasks across five capability domains, run on 36 production MCP servers in isolated containers, designed to diagnose hallucination-prone agent failures along reasoning, execution, and memory axes. Unlike prior MCP benchmarks that measure task completion, tasks embed structural triggers for specific failure modes. It addresses a timely gap as Model Context Protocol adoption grows.

entry.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics

author.name: Trinh T. Nguyen, Minh-Khoi Nguyen-Nhat, Duy-Tung Pham, Hoang-Son Do, Tan Minh Nguyen, Thieu N. Vo

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of token dynamics in deep Mamba (state-space) models, focusing on why the first token acts as an attractor. Because Mamba uses full matrix-valued interaction coefficients rather than positive scalar attention weights, the authors develop a new analytical framework based on a high-dimensional invariant box and exit-time arguments to recover sign-definiteness and characterize the model's limiting behavior.

entry.title: Learning Noise Optimization for Reward Alignment in Few-Step Generative Models

author.name: Hongeun Kim, Jeongsol Kim, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Introduces LeNO, which amortizes reward-guided initial noise optimization into a learned residual transport for few-step diffusion and flow-based generators, keeping the pretrained model frozen. Using Local GRPO with scalar rewards, it removes the costly per-sample test-time search required by prior gradient-free methods, with theoretical guarantees for Gaussian initial noise under norm-preserving projection.

entry.title: TriAttention: Unified Sparse Mixed-Precision Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan, Yan Huang, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: TriAttention combines sparsity and quantization for long-context attention by assigning query-key tiles to skipping, 4-bit, or 8-bit computation based on per-interaction precision tolerance. It encodes each head's computation regions with two diagonal-distance boundaries so policy storage stays independent of context length, with offline calibration selecting boundaries via projected-output error and execution cost. This targets efficiency of LLM inference at long context.

entry.title: Efficient Diffusion Policy Fine Tuning with Latent Noise Representation Bridging

author.name: Yuanchu Liang, Yue Yang, An-Chi He, Hanna Kurniawati

entry.summary: The authors propose the Latent Noise Linear MDP (LNL-MDP), a framework for reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of pre-trained diffusion and flow policies used in robotics. Their derived Bridge Equation aligns value estimates between the initial-noise space and the action space, resolving the noise-aliasing problem that plagues prior noise-space fine-tuning approaches while avoiding costly backpropagation through the denoising chain. This matters because it makes RL adaptation of diffusion policies more sample-efficient and, notably, comes with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs

author.name: Xiaobo Chen, Genliang Zhu, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang

entry.summary: Reports a preregistered study showing that requirement information degrades during multi-agent handoffs, and compares free-text, structured JSON, and cryptographically signed requirement-manifest protocols where each requirement is a verbatim quote plus checkable predicate, HMAC-SHA256 signed and deterministically verified. With Qwen3-8B across 1,440 trajectories and five threat models, signed manifests cut unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% with no loss of conformant commits versus structured handoffs. The results suggest cryptographic signing, not structure alone, defeats certain handoff attacks.

entry.title: Action-Conditioned VLM Monitoring for Autonomous Vehicle Semantic Anomalies

author.name: Daniel Adejumo, Omkar Ankalkope, Kunal Runwal, Aliasghar Arab

entry.summary: The paper proposes monitoring autonomous vehicle behavior by having a vision-language model predict the scene-required action from outcome-hidden video and comparing it against the realized ego-motion trajectory, rather than flagging visually unusual scenes. The authors contribute a taxonomy of 112 paired scenarios covering both normal and anomalous behaviors in semantically unusual scenes, plus a generated video corpus.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data

author.name: Nikita Koriagin, Nikita Balagansky, Daniil Gavrilov

entry.summary: This work derives a scaling law describing how many unique activations sparse autoencoders need: quality improves rapidly with buffer size then plateaus, after which replaying stored activations is nearly as effective as fresh data. Validated across dictionary sizes, layers of Llama-3.1 and Qwen3 models, and multiple SAE variants (BatchTopK, TopK, JumpReLU). It directly addresses activation storage, a real bottleneck in interpretability research, and could substantially reduce SAE training costs.

entry.title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure

author.name: Sumaya Nur Adan, Joanna Wiaterek, Nourhan Abdelrhim, Sydney Reis, Robert F. Trager, Benjamin Rosman, Marina Jirotka

entry.summary: This governance paper introduces PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence), a framework for analyzing who controls AI evaluation infrastructure and on what terms, drawing on STS, political economy, and evaluation standards. It applies the framework to twelve African AI evaluation projects from 2022-2025, highlighting how infrastructure arrangements determine who can evaluate AI independently.

entry.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tal Oved, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: The authors replace mean-field decoding's similarity proxy in diffusion language models with direct measurement of token coupling - how much committing one token changes confidence at another - using cheap probes inside the forward pass with no extra model or training. Across three models and four benchmarks the method needs far fewer steps and is faster in most settings at an average accuracy cost of 1.1 points.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yunru Zheng, Wun Ting Chan, Sampras Dsouza, Zhenyu Hong

entry.summary: The paper presents a scalable Bayesian Gaussian process classification framework operating on frozen pathology foundation-model embeddings (Phikon), combining RPCholesky low-rank factorization, HMC sampling with non-centered parameterization, and a pivots-as-inducing-points prediction scheme. The goal is calibrated uncertainty under hospital-to-hospital distribution shift in cancer diagnosis. This addresses a critical safety requirement for clinical deployment of foundation-model-based diagnostics.

entry.title: Calibrated Target Noise Recovers Curvature from the Gradients

author.name: Arash Jamshidi, Katsiaryna Haitsiukevich, Aristides Gionis, Kai Puolam\"aki

entry.summary: The paper shows that injecting zero-mean noise into targets, with variance calibrated to local output curvature, makes the covariance of resulting mini-batch gradients recover practical curvature information without per-sample gradients or second-order derivatives. This has applications in preconditioning, sampling, and early stopping where only aggregate gradients are available. It is a surprising and useful algorithmic trick.

entry.title: Reinforcing What the Student Has Learned: Teacher-Guided On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Bozhen Fang, Linhao Zhong, Xuehao Wang, Huanyi Zheng, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: This work identifies an amplitude disparity in on-policy distillation: style-related token positions show 3.5 times the teacher-student log-probability gap of mathematical content positions, causing updates to over-weight surface expression. The authors propose using the student's own pretrained base model as a reference, leveraging the student-base difference to supervise token preferences acquired during post-training independently of teacher distance. This reframes OPD weighting toward meaningful reasoning content.

entry.title: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees

author.name: Soroush H. Zargarbashi, Mohammad Sadegh Akhondzadeh, Aleksandar Bojchevski

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for cheap robustness certification of classifiers by delegating certification to a proxy function whose deviation from expensive certificates like randomized smoothing is statistically controlled via conformal risk control on a calibration set. It guarantees only a bounded marginal false-approval rate rather than pointwise certificates, drastically reducing the number of forward passes needed per input. This matters because certifiable robustness has largely been too costly for practical deployment.

entry.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout

author.name: Tushaar Gangavarapu, Gil Tabak, Clemens JS Schaefer

entry.summary: Muir improves gated delta-rule linear attention by exploiting an empirical asymmetry: state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes, since key energy concentrates on sparse channels while value writes scale all channels. This enables lower-rank erase gates and a matched-filter readout that corrects norm imbalance between slow- and fast-decaying state rows. It builds directly on Gated DeltaNet-2 for linear-time training and constant-memory inference.

entry.title: Efficient Kernelized Learning in Polyhedral Games Beyond Full-Information: From Colonel Blotto to Congestion Games

author.name: Andreas Kontogiannis, Vasilis Pollatos, Gabriele Farina, Panayotis Mertikopoulos, Ioannis Panageas

entry.summary: This work extends efficient computation of coarse correlated equilibria in polyhedral games with exponentially large action sets from the full-information setting to the harder partial-information setting, using kernelization to achieve polylogarithmic regret and per-iteration complexity. Examples include Colonel Blotto and congestion games.

entry.title: OPRD-Imp: a dataset of experimentally observed impurities and side products in multi-step pharmaceutical syntheses

author.name: Heejeong Kim, Seonbin Kim, Jihwan Kim, Tim Pinkhassik, Magdalena Lederbauer, Suong Tran, Connor W. Coley, Juyoung Yoon, Joonyoung F. Joung

entry.summary: This paper introduces OPRD-Imp, a curated dataset of 229 organic reactions from Organic Process Research & Development publications, annotated with 784 experimentally observed impurities and their mechanistic origins. It addresses a persistent data gap in benchmarking machine learning models for reaction impurity prediction in pharmaceutical process chemistry.

entry.title: 4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering

author.name: Adnan Armouti, Guanyue Qian, Rajalakshmi Nandakumar

entry.summary: This work introduces 4D Point Splatting (4DPS), a physics-based differentiable renderer that fits an explicit moving scene to real mmWave radar micro-Doppler captures, enabling radar data synthesis that closes the sim2real gap. It uses synchronized camera input to initialize the room and body scene representation. This matters because radar datasets for sensing tasks like gait and vital-sign recognition lag far behind vision and language corpora.

entry.title: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining

author.name: Jo\~ao Eduardo Batista, Emil Vatai, Mohamed Wahib

entry.summary: Accelerates the remaining full-attention layers in hybrid LLMs at long context using training-free combined sparse attention: a sliding window, pinned prefix, and fixed budget of relevant tokens, with per-layer parameters found by multi-objective search. It validates across six hybrid models from three families spanning 4B to 397B parameters.

entry.title: Reasoning over Non-Parametric Memory in Multilingual LLMs: A Cognitive-Based Analysis of Relational Knowledge

author.name: Zohreh Abbasi Liasi, Batoul Hammoud, Anas Madkoor, Ehsaneddin Asgari

entry.summary: Rel-Bloom is a controlled multilingual diagnostic of 450 multiple-choice questions from 30 Wikidata relations, instantiated at five Bloom-inspired cognitive levels and three veracity conditions, testing whether models reason over facts supplied directly in context.
