entry.summary: A short interpretability follow-up showing that in Gemma-4-31B, two small coordinate-aligned subspaces account for 80-95% of the J-lens readout, identifiable by a distinctive small post-norm diagonal weight pattern that protects the coordinates from edits across layers. The author also notes that semantically valuable information exists outside these spaces, complicating a clean isolated workspace story.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration

author.name: Sungil Son, Hoseong Jung, Dahyun Oh, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: EFXPLORER is a constrained exploration framework for cooperative MARL that maximizes intrinsic exploration objectives subject to preserving established task performance, solved via an epigraph reformulation with adaptive exploration budgets. This separates intrinsic rewards from task objectives, avoiding the signal distortion of naive reward combination.

entry.title: Towards Generalist Graph-Level Anomaly Detection

author.name: Junjun Pan, Yixin Liu, Yu Zheng, Fuyi Li, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: This work formalizes generalist graph-level anomaly detection: a single unified model that detects anomalous graphs across multiple domains with minimal target supervision, departing from dataset-specific training paradigms. The paper identifies the key challenges of cross-domain generalization for GLAD and presumably proposes a corresponding approach. It pushes anomaly detection toward the foundation-model-style generality seen in other areas.

entry.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone

author.name: Doojin Baek, Junyeob Baek, Mingyu Jo, Hosung Lee, Taegu Kang, Gyubin Lee, Sungjin Ahn

entry.summary: BabyTheorist is a benchmark for observational theory learning: acquiring reusable theories from pure before-after visual observation streams without program labels or support sets, then applying them to new situations. It generates continual observation streams from hidden compositional programs, enabling controlled training and evaluation. The benchmark targets whether machines can truly build world theories rather than solve few-shot rule puzzles.

entry.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma

author.name: Pengkai Wang, Wei-Wei Zhang, Yan Li, Min Tang, Zhitian Hou, Zeyu Liu, Guanghao Zhu, Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Wenjun Wang, Minheng Ni, Congkai Xie, Zhijie Sang, Jianmin Wu, Ying Sun, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: NPCBench is a new medical benchmark evaluating whether multimodal models can perform longitudinal care-pathway reasoning for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, mimicking the full arc of specialist training rather than isolated question answering. It includes 4,777 component and consultation items plus a 100-patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care decisions.

entry.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts

author.name: Yubo Wang, Rui Meng, Jaehyun Nam, Tomas Pfister, Jinsung Yoon

entry.summary: ReproBridge defines a standardized artifact design (refined codebase, environment setup, launchers, reproduction guide) and an agent workflow for constructing reproducible ML research artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers to evaluate whether coding agents can independently reproduce experiments. The work targets whether reproduction success depends on artifact quality versus agent improvisation.

entry.title: Oscillatory Phase Coding Emerges in Adaptive RNNs for Flexible Working Memory

author.name: Kehan Lu, Tianhao Chu, Aiersi Tuerhong, Yiwen Sun, Huan Luo, Fang Fang, Si Wu

entry.summary: Trains RNNs with neural adaptation on sequence working-memory tasks with variable delays and finds oscillatory phase coding emerges spontaneously: oscillation amplitude encodes item identity while phase encodes serial order. Ablations identify adaptation dynamics, variable delay, and flexible readout as the minimal ingredients, connecting recurrent network models to a known biological phenomenon.

entry.title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan, Yan Huang, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: Introduces TileQuant, a training-free mixed-precision post-training quantization framework that allocates precision at the level of hardware-aligned 2D weight tiles rather than whole columns, using offline input-activation-aware scoring from forward statistics. This addresses sensitivity variation within columns and avoids the decoding overhead of runtime outlier detection, reducing LLM deployment costs.

entry.title: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence?

author.name: David Nordfors

entry.summary: This paper validates a prior hypothesis that language models store domain-independent relational patterns, called archetypal contexts (e.g., tipping point, winner-takes-all), separately from topic and language. Using Qwen3.8-27B, the authors show disentangled neuron sets encode archetype, topic, and language respectively, and silencing each set selectively removes that component of model behavior. This offers evidence for compositional, human-recognizable abstractions inside LLM internals.

entry.title: Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error:Detection Limits and Falsification Budget

author.name: Ramnarayan Choudhary

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that adaptive experimental design can systematically avoid regions where a working model fails, making model misspecification invisible to adequacy tests. The authors bound the power of any valid adequacy test in terms of the experimenter's sampling distribution and propose a training-free rule that reserves part of the design budget specifically for falsification, plus a computable diagnostic for unresolved model error.

entry.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays

author.name: Orhun G\"orkem, Athanasios Vasilopoulos, Georgios Pagonis, Victoria Clerico, Hadjer Benmeziane, Irem Boybat, Hsinyu Tsai, Abu Sebastian, William Andrew Simon

entry.summary: CAMP tackles weight mapping on 3D analog in-memory computing arrays for LLM inference, where vertical stacking increases capacity but placement determines which matrix-vector multiplications can run concurrently. The paper develops context-aware mapping and placement strategies to improve utilization, latency, and throughput, addressing KV cache and weight-loading overheads.

entry.title: O$^2$PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix

author.name: Shuaishuai Zu, Jihao Zhao, Pengfei Li, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Yuhan Liu, Biao Qin, Baochuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper addresses two gaps in on-policy distillation of language models: which student-generated tokens the teacher should supervise, and how to compute the alignment divergence. It proposes an overlap-gated scheme that distills only on reliable prefixes and reconsidered top-k reverse KL support, improving on standard on-policy distillation setups. The work matters because distillation from stronger to weaker models is a core efficiency technique for deploying capable small models.

entry.title: Value or Attention: Investigating Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Graph Attention Networks

author.name: Ken Schreiber, Ren\'e P. Klausen, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek, Jonas Naujoks

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified LRP-based explanation method for Graph Attention Networks that explicitly separates content relevance flowing through the value path from routing relevance through the attention path. The authors present a single product rule with free weights that recovers prior approaches as special cases, addressing why existing explainers mishandle attention layers.

entry.title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging

author.name: Ismail Huseynov, Mohammad Orabe, Srikantan Nagarajan, Stefan Haufe

entry.summary: This paper introduces a simulation-based framework for assessing whether uncertainty estimates in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging methods are empirically well calibrated. It compares Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sparse Bayesian learning using sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX), deriving joint source- and noise-variance updates and showing S-FLEX avoids degenerate zero variances at voxel level. Reliable calibrated uncertainty matters for clinical neuroscience applications of brain source localization.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for Resource Allocation in Integrated Sensing and Communication

author.name: Junyu Liao, Lili Chen, Tian Han, Jamie Evans

entry.summary: This paper proposes GNN-ISAC, a graph neural network that solves nonconvex power allocation in vehicular integrated sensing and communication networks by modeling inter-provider interference and intra-provider power sharing as distinct edge types. The learned amortizer replaces costly per-layout iterative optimization, maximizing communication sum-rate under sensing SINR constraints. It matters because ISAC is a key enabler of next-generation wireless systems.

entry.title: Monotone Viability Learning for Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ziqian Wang, Zhen Zhang

entry.summary: MoViL learns viable (safe) sets from offline data via monotone finite-horizon Hamilton-Jacobi set recursion that preserves safety semantics and converges to the infinite-horizon viability kernel, with binary supervision avoiding discount-induced numerical attenuation. It establishes conditions for recovering behavior-supported viable subsets. This strengthens the foundations of offline safe RL.

entry.title: $O(1/n)$ Convergence Rate for RVI $Q$-Learning

author.name: Avik Kar, Siddharth Chandak, Rahul Singh, Shalabh Bhatnagar

entry.summary: This paper establishes finite-time convergence guarantees for synchronous relative value iteration Q-learning on finite weakly communicating MDPs. Using stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration analysis under martingale-difference noise, the authors derive last-iterate mean-squared residual bounds and show polynomial stepsizes yield an O(n^-1) convergence rate. This provides some of the tightest known finite-time guarantees for average-reward Q-learning.

entry.title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory

author.name: Nir Krakowski, Tamir Cohen, Ohad Zohar, Chen Zarfati

entry.summary: E-Gaborformer is a strictly causal streaming speech recognizer combining Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention in a 3:1 ratio, using convolutions built from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming state is constant at roughly 19 MB per call versus over 1 GB for causal-attention encoders after ten minutes, and it reaches target accuracy up to 18 percent sooner on LibriSpeech. This is relevant to real-time voice agents with long-duration calls.

entry.title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation?

author.name: William Raftery, Dario Farina

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates three surface electromyography (sEMG) foundation models across three gesture classification datasets, comparing intra-session and inter-subject data splits with three fine-tuning strategies to isolate the effect of pretraining. The key finding is that pretraining gains largely evaporate under cross-subject conditions, exposing that current sEMG foundation models overfit to individual recording sessions rather than learning truly generalizable representations. This matters for wearable robotics, prosthetics, and HCI applications where models must generalize to new users without per-user recalibration.

entry.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories

author.name: Timon S. Gutleb

entry.summary: The paper introduces dACE, an adaptation of the atomic cluster expansion to self-propelled agents, providing an exactly equivariant, systematically improvable expansion of an agent's acceleration that uniquely splits into one-, two-, three-body and higher interaction contributions. On simulated collectives with known rules, dACE recovers interaction laws body order by body order from little data, outperforming the neural baseline Social-Implicit in interpretability. This enables scientific discovery of many-body collective behavior.

entry.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems

author.name: Ilker Gurcan, Kadir Ustun, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

entry.summary: The authors formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery from differential-equation data as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data, identifying admissible generators and separating them from redundant and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary, with a rank-stabilization preflight test diagnosing degenerate systems. It enables model reduction and scientific ML without closed-form governing equations.

entry.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness

author.name: Yi Feng, Andrea Paudice

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes gradient descent dynamics in adversarial training with large constant step sizes, unlike most prior analyses that assume vanishing steps. It establishes results on implicit bias and loss convergence for adversarial linear logistic regression and characterizes loss sharpness evolution during neural network adversarial training.

entry.title: FastAFD: When Does Attention-FFN Disaggregation Pay on Rack-Scale NVLink?

author.name: Yichao Fu, Yuxuan Zhang, Minshen Zhang, Ruitian Wang, Junda Chen, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper builds FastAFD, an engine for attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) of MoE models on GB200 NVL72 rack-scale NVLink hardware, overlapping the MoE computation of one microbatch with the attention of another. It rigorously tests whether the previously reported decode-throughput benefits of AFD hold against strong wide expert-parallel vLLM baselines, finding only a modest advantage of up to 1.17x. The work matters because it gives system builders clear empirical guidance on when disaggregated serving architectures are actually worth the added complexity on modern rack-scale clusters.

entry.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Shi Jin, Tian-ai Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network method for high-dimensional, multiscale kinetic equations such as Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck in the high-field regime, using CP decomposition of tensor neural networks to cut cost and memory. The approach retains asymptotic limits across scales and extends to uncertainty quantification for plasma and semiconductor simulation.

entry.title: Statistical and Privacy Guarantees for Deep M-Regression via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Yeheng Ge, Jian Huang, Shuyuan Wu

entry.summary: The authors provide PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bounds for deep nonparametric regression trained with stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics, jointly accounting for approximation error, statistical complexity, and algorithmic noise along the SGLD trajectory. The analysis shows the estimator retains minimax-optimal regression rates while the injected Gaussian noise yields privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Series-wise Cross-validation for Global Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Vitor Cerqueira, Mariana Oliveira, Luis Roque

entry.summary: This paper formalizes series-wise cross-validation for global deep learning forecasting models, which can partition data across both time and series rather than only temporally. The authors benchmark K-fold, bootstrapping, and Monte Carlo CV variants on 11 datasets with 10 neural architectures, evaluating performance estimation, overoptimism, and model selection accuracy. This matters because CV methodology directly affects model evaluation and selection in forecasting practice.

entry.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines

author.name: Yuqin Dai, Zhanwei Zhang, Honghui Yang, Zhouheng Yao, Yueqi Zhang, Jingyu He, Chaoyang Shi, Fanding Wei, Boyuan Pan, Kai Xu, Yao Hu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces CARTBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM shopping assistants on complex, ambiguous, time-constrained requests, built from real commercial dialogues across 17 retail domains with 1,603 product records. It proposes case-specific rubrics distilled from successfully completed orders and a Principle-Guided CART Prompting strategy for structured recommendations.

entry.title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering

author.name: Zewen Zhan, Hui Lu, Xueyuan Chen, Huimeng Wang, Yikai Huang, Xixin Wu, Shiyin Kang, Bin Xia, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a dataset and benchmark for real-time streaming speech interaction, where models must answer questions using only the audio chunks received so far rather than complete utterances. It fills a gap since most speech LLMs operate offline, and real applications require continuous streaming responses.

entry.title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, Hemanth Kandula, Jeff Ma, William Hartmann, Matthew Snover

entry.summary: This paper introduces SAUCE, a reference-free evaluation pipeline for cross-lingual conversational speech summarization that measures summary accuracy and fact coverage via entailment between the conversation and the summary text. It captures information loss from transcription and translation errors and offers explainability, unlike black-box LLM judges or embedding-based metrics. This matters because evaluating open-ended conversational summaries remains a persistent weakness in LLM and speech application assessment.

entry.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory

author.name: Junhyung Ahn

entry.summary: AGORA is an item-response-theory aggregator for LLM-as-a-judge pools that places items on a latent quality scale and models each judge with a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, learning reliability from all data. It targets the small-validation-set regime where per-item means over-weight weak judges and Dawid-Skene error tables are underdetermined.

entry.title: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation

author.name: Guotao Liang, Haitao Zhou, Biao Liu, Huanxuan Liao, Lingfeng Qiao, Qian-Wen Zhang, Qian Yu, Di Yin, Xing Sun

entry.summary: SVGFaith is a meta-evaluation framework showing that raster-image metrics applied to rasterized SVG outputs poorly capture prompt faithfulness. It includes 1,842 controlled contrastive pairs across eight capability axes and 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs, with faithfulness determined by construction or human judgment. The finding that CLIP-like embedding metrics score near chance is a significant caution for how text-to-SVG systems are evaluated.

entry.title: T$^2$-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals

author.name: Zhihao Tang, Youjia Zhang, Mingbo Zhao, Wei Yang

entry.summary: T2-Splat is a mesh-based splatting method for novel view synthesis that decouples topology adaptation from appearance refinement: Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation initializes connectivity, Dynamic Topology Evolution adapts triangles via edge collapse and vertex split, and per-face Mip-texture residuals refine appearance. It improves PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360 with compact meshes across three standard datasets. It bridges neural rendering with conventional graphics pipelines.

entry.title: Wide View Synthesis from Overlapping Perspective Cameras in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Kaixuan Zhang, Zhipeng Xiong, Minxian Li, Mingwu Ren, Xiatian Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formulates wide view synthesis (WVS), generating a geometrically consistent wide view from multiple spatially separated automotive cameras, handling depth-dependent parallax and occlusions that defeat simple stitching. It adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to avoid per-scene optimization for driving scenes. This is practically relevant for surround perception in autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: OptIMerge: Optimization-Based Merging of Diffusion Models

author.name: Viraj Shah, Ashwini Pokle, Peyman Milanfar, Mauricio Delbracio, Hossein Talebi

entry.summary: OptIMerge studies merging image-to-image diffusion models fine-tuned for dense restoration tasks, where naive model souping causes destructive parameter interference. It proposes an optimization-based merging method for this underexplored setting. Google-affiliated authors (Milanfar, Delbracio, Talebi) lend credibility.

entry.title: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement

author.name: Songhe Wang, David Miller, Charles A. Kamhoua

entry.summary: Proposes DCAP, which reframes language-guided 3D object placement as a drop-to-equilibrium process instead of predicting a rigid 6-DoF pose. A semantic release state (drop location, scale, deformable components) is fed to a coupled rigid-deformable simulator so objects settle under gravity and friction, avoiding floating or interpenetrating placements. Evaluated on a benchmark of over 2,000 prompt-asset cases.

entry.title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks

author.name: Yuze Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a zero-rate conditioning signal built from robot joint states, the robot model, and camera calibration that lets both ends of a remote-policy video link predict ego-motion, dramatically improving learned video codec efficiency. The authors prove that history-only or global-pose conditioning cannot access this information under large motion, and show coding gains translate into task gains for bandwidth-limited robot teleoperation.

entry.title: Real-Time Event-Based LED Tracking and Pose Estimation with PWM-Encoded Markers

author.name: Junkai Niu, Sheng Zhong, Delei Kong, Xin Wang, Kaizhen Sun, Yusen Zhang, Mingzhen Gan, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: The authors present a real-time event-camera framework for LED tracking and 6-DoF relative pose estimation using PWM-encoded markers, where LEDs share a blinking frequency and encode identity via duty cycles. A dual-rate asynchronous tracking scheme reduces frequency-resource and computational demands. This enables robust high-speed pose estimation under motion blur and HDR conditions.

entry.title: H-BRICK: Hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene Closure for Directed Grid Graphs

author.name: Tolga \"Ozaslan, Elif A. \"Ozaslan

entry.summary: H-BRICK is a hierarchical index for answering exact cell-to-cell reachability queries on directed grid graphs, common in online path planning and swarm control where full transitive closure is too large to store. It tiles the graph, computes local Boolean Kleene closures projected onto boundary ports, and composes these summaries recursively, with algebraic proofs of exactness.

entry.title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation

author.name: Matthew S. Scott, Yaniv Plan, \"Ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz

entry.summary: The authors prove exact uniform signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for ReLU networks with a final sigmoid activation, removing the common expansivity assumption. They derive sample complexity in terms of network depth and the geometric mean of layer widths, showing recovery with roughly k(d log(K/k)) measurements.

entry.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers present UQ-DAAAM, a robot memory system that quantifies uncertainty in object descriptions by comparing multiple viewpoint-dependent captions, actively selecting additional views to reduce uncertainty, and saving corrected descriptions to memory. This addresses mislabeled object memory that could cause robots to fail tasks like retrieving a defibrillator in an emergency.

entry.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone

author.name: Shivesh Rane

entry.summary: This privacy study asks whether a classifier can recover the training-data domain of a LoRA fine-tune from the artifact alone, using Qwen3.5-0.8B (an existing model) fine-tuned on 18 datasets across five domains with white-box, gray-box, and black-box feature families. A leave-one-dataset-out protocol frozen before evaluation tests generalization to unseen datasets.

entry.title: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for Agentic AI in Chemical Engineering

author.name: Artur M. Schweidtmann

entry.summary: ChemE-as-Code is an open-source environment where LLM-based agents perform chemical engineering work — catalysis, process simulation, plant layout, HAZOP, life cycle assessment — with calculations executed outside the LLM, provenance tracked per value, and automated consistency checks. An illustrative ammonia case has an agent produce a preliminary basic-engineering package including simulation files, P&IDs, HAZOP, and datasheets. It emphasizes verifiable, auditable agentic engineering rather than free-form generation.

entry.title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?

author.name: Yuanchuan Guo, Jiashun Jin, Zheng Tracy Ke, Bingcheng Sui

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether AI involvement in mathematical proofs can be detected separately from AI-assisted writing, building five cohorts totaling 8,281 papers that span varying levels of AI involvement, including matched case-control pairs and manuscripts from OpenAI. The work constructs features capturing proof-level signals and addresses disclosure-incompleteness challenges.

entry.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization

author.name: Qile Jiang, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: SwarmEvolve speeds up LLM-guided evolutionary search by running hundreds of low-cost agents per round that reason in latent space without decoding text, sharing information via KV caches. Swarms attack problems from different angles, a novelty filter keeps distinct ideas by measuring hidden-state distances, and crossover combines promising candidates. This targets the latency and cost bottlenecks of function-evaluation-style evolutionary LLM search such as FunSearch-style systems.

entry.title: BrainPFN: Amortized Brain-Behaviour Prediction via Prior-Data Fitted Networks

author.name: Carlo Alberto Barbano (MIND), Demian Wassermann (MIND)

entry.summary: Introduces BrainPFN, a Prior-Data Fitted Network for predicting behavioral phenotypes from fMRI functional connectivity, replacing per-cohort kernel ridge regression with an amortized in-context model that transfers across datasets and works with few subjects. The paper notes that existing brain foundation models have not consistently beaten KRR on continuous behavioral scores, which this approach targets directly.

entry.title: ReferClaw: Disambiguating User Intent for Egocentric Assistance

author.name: Hangyu Qin, Junbin Xiao, Angela Yao

entry.summary: ReferClaw formulates egocentric streaming video QA as an interactive process in which the assistant asks cost-aware clarifying questions to resolve ambiguous referents before answering, using three cooperating agents for candidate identification, clarification, and grounded answer generation. This avoids committing to a single plausible but intention-misaligned interpretation.

entry.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information

author.name: Linqian Wu, Diaoxuan He

entry.summary: This theory paper asks when mechanism-level quantities - functionals of a system's causal transition law such as integrated information phi - are identifiable and certifiable from finite, noisy interventions, answering exactly for small stochastic networks with known ground truth. It demonstrates that behavior can be silent about mechanism: recurrent and feedforward networks with identical input-output laws can differ in integrated information.

entry.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers

author.name: Carlos Boned Riera, David Romero Sanchez, Oriol Ramos Terrades

entry.summary: SSoG replaces dense self-attention in Vision Transformers with a separable sum-of-Gaussians spatial operator, reducing per-layer cost from quadratic to subquadratic in token count. Unlike dot-product attention, the fixed-kernel operator is globally Lipschitz continuous, which guarantees unique solutions for its continuous-depth ODE variant via Picard-Lindelof. It shows competitive results on CIFAR-scale benchmarks and links attention efficiency with neural-ODE well-posedness.

entry.title: English Calibration Erodes Lithuanian in Expert-Pruned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Tomas Rasymas, Povilas Kvedaras

entry.summary: This study tests whether English calibration data transfers to Lithuanian when pruning MoE language models with REAP, finding strong asymmetry: at 25% expert pruning, English comprehension dropped 1.7 points while Lithuanian dropped 21.4 points, whereas Lithuanian calibration preserved Lithuanian without significantly hurting English. The result challenges assumptions that English calibration transfers across languages for MoE compression.

entry.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zuo Gou, Chenhao Lu

entry.summary: The paper treats the environment-trainer boundary in distributed robot RL as a wire protocol and systematically injects up to 23 fault types across Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Pusher, finding that learning-curve thresholds and seed comparisons catch at most 10-21% of silent faults. Of 728 boundary-fault runs passing both checks, 723 scored within three standard deviations in clean evaluation.

entry.title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models

author.name: Hongnian Huang, Hongliang Liu

entry.summary: Uses numerical choice (where every integer in 1-30 is valid) as a probe of how preference is computed across layers and tokens in language models. Combining perturbation probing, activation edits, and attention-head interventions in a Qwen3-4B case, it traces how an edit's influence propagates to later digit decisions.

entry.title: How Far Can You Steer? Behavior-Capability Frontiers in Contrastive Activation Addition

author.name: Deepanshu Raj

entry.summary: The paper studies activation steering via Contrastive Activation Addition through a behavior-capability frontier, selecting interventions that maximize behavioral change subject to explicit budgets (1-5%) on degradation of unrelated capabilities. Evaluated across four instruction-tuned models and seven behaviors, validation-selected effects generalize strongly. It reframes steering safety as a quantified tradeoff rather than a binary success or failure.

entry.title: TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Pengfei Gu, Huimin Li, Guangyu Meng, Hao Zheng, Haoteng Tang, Bin Fu, Danny Z. Chen

entry.summary: TRiST integrates persistent homology (H0 and H1) computed at each Swin Transformer stage into feature construction, refinement, and attention for medical image analysis, so topological patterns like connected components and loops inform multiscale representations. Topology-aware medical segmentation can better preserve lesion and organ-boundary structure. From an experienced medical imaging group (Chen lab).

entry.title: OcTreeMamba: Topology-Aware Mamba for 3D Medical Segmentation via Octree Sparsification

author.name: Kaixiang Mai, Jiaqi Yu, Yuzhu Ji, Yiqun Zhang, Zhijie Wang, Haijun Zhang, Yiu-ming Cheung

entry.summary: OcTreeMamba integrates octree structures into state-space models for 3D medical segmentation, using anatomy-adaptive sparsification to respect the intrinsic spatial hierarchy and sparsity of anatomical structures. It addresses the problem that heuristic selective-scan strategies in Mamba-based segmenters disrupt spatial hierarchy and add computational redundancy. The result is topology-aware long-range context propagation with linear-time complexity.

entry.title: ProtoGestalt: Interpretable Prototypes for Facial Phenotyping and Diagnosis of Rare Genetic Disorders

author.name: Ranga Baminiwatte, Alexander Hustinx, Fabio Hellmann, Aaron J Masino

entry.summary: Presents an interpretable prototype-based framework for facial phenotyping and rare genetic disorder screening that constrains learned features to select facial regions, so predictions are explained via localized additive evidence. It is evaluated for distinguishing syndromic from unaffected faces across multiple control datasets and prevalence settings.

entry.title: Message-passing graph persistence

author.name: Jorge Luiz Franco, Arthur Queiroz Moura, Moacir Ponti, Amauri Souza

entry.summary: The paper introduces Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), topological descriptors that weave message passing into graph filtrations, updating node embeddings at each filtration step and tying them to persistence events. The authors prove MGP is more expressive than the 1-Weisfeiler-Leman test that bounds standard GNNs, integrating persistent homology into representation learning.

entry.title: Better honeypots, fewer tries: training an optimizer to make PPO cheat

author.name: Aniket Ghosh

entry.summary: A course project that reframes the construction of reward-hacking honeypots as a black-box optimization problem, training an optimizer with evolution strategies on synthetic functions to find gridworld levels where PPO cheats. The learned optimizer found cheating-inducing levels 79% of the time versus 70% for CMA-ES, and found strong levels in a median of 6 PPO runs versus 46 for GP Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization

author.name: Priyanath Maji

entry.summary: This paper introduces a cross-agent protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into Dafny predicates and an Implementer model writes code checked against them, showing that even same-model independent re-extraction agrees only 59.3% of the time. Across four configurations on 96 clinical trial documents, agreement is highly sensitive to how capability is allocated between the two roles.

entry.title: CST-Bench: Benchmarking Counterfactual Spatial Transition Reasoning with Causal Transition On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Ying Li, Yongle Cheng, Jing Li, Xingquan Cai, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: CST-Bench is a 7,082-example benchmark for counterfactual spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs, covering 6 intervention types and 12 transformation operators with dense causal annotations (sources, affected relations, expected effects, invariants). The authors benchmark general MLLMs and compare post-training strategies including on-policy self-distillation against standard spatial reasoning data.

entry.title: How Finite Brains Generalize Without Bound: Spatial Memory as a Universal Computer

author.name: Yuhang He, Si Wu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper distinguishes learners that read coordinates (positions, counts, times, which take novel values as inputs grow) from learners that read coincidences (same/not-same relations, whose answers are size-invariant), arguing this determines whether finite experience yields unbounded generalization. It frames spatial memory as carrying input size while the rule stays finite, connecting to why children extrapolate arithmetic but LSTMs and Transformers trained on short sequences fail on longer ones. It offers a conceptual account of length generalization.

entry.title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation

author.name: Hang Zhang, Qihao Ye, Litong Liu, Yunbei Zhang, Yugyung Lee, Yue Zhou, Bowen Liu, Emily First, Cheng Han, Qiao Zhuang

entry.summary: LeanContext is a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof generation problems designed to measure the advantage of target-selected mathematical declarations over comparable alternatives and how training affects this. It separates Mathematical Context from Environment Context across four aligned input views for crossed training and inference evaluations with original Lean verification. It covers both diffusion- and autoregressive-based models.

entry.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines

author.name: Roko Parac, Christos Ziakas, Leo Ardon, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: RM-VLM removes the manually engineered labelling function bottleneck in reward machines by having an LLM generate the reward machine from a natural-language task description and a vision-language model act as the proposition-grounding oracle over observations. This extends reward machines to non-Markovian tasks in visual environments without per-environment engineering. It connects formal RL reward structure with foundation-model perception.

entry.title: Polynomial-Time Computation of Extensive-Form Proper Equilibria in Two-Player Zero-Sum Games

author.name: Sam Ganzfried

entry.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for computing an exact extensive-form proper equilibrium in two-player zero-sum extensive-form games with perfect recall and rational data. The approach uses geometric permutahedra of allowable action probabilities and a scaled doubly stochastic embedding in sequence-form polytopes, yielding a saddle point satisfying local properness inequalities.

entry.title: InfMasking: A Unified Variational Framework for Synergistic Multimodal Learning

author.name: Liangjian Wen, Qun Dai, Jiang Duan, Yong Dai, Jianzhuang Liu, Dongkai Wang, Jun Wang, Fuyuan Cao, Zenglin Xu, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: InfMasking promotes synergistic multimodal learning by randomly masking each modality's features before fusion so that all partial cross-modal combinations must remain consistent with a reference representation, preventing fusion modules from relying on a dominant modality. It provides a unified variational framework for encouraging genuinely synergistic information use.

entry.title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes

author.name: Seong-Eun Hong, JuYeong Hwang, Jinhyun Kim, Hanyoung Jang, HyeongYeop Kang

entry.summary: The paper argues that human-aware navigation needs action-conditioned foresight to catch failure modes invisible from the current state, such as drifting onto roads or cutting into pedestrian flows, but full world-model rollouts at every step are too costly. It proposes placing the world model strategically rather than at every decision step, resolving the foresight-versus-speed trade-off.

entry.title: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher

author.name: Madelon Bernardy, Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani, David M Knigge, Riccardo Valperga, Artem Moskalev

entry.summary: This work proposes shape-teacher alignment, a training-time mechanism that uses pretrained Point-MAE 3D shape features as alignment targets for image-based robot policy encoders, transferring geometric structure while keeping a purely image-based interface at deployment. The goal is 3D-aware manipulation policies without requiring 3D sensing at test time.

entry.title: Server-Side Sparse Assignment for Federated Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Xue Zheng, Aylin Yener

entry.summary: The paper addresses heterogeneous federated fine-tuning of LLMs with Mixture-of-Experts, proposing a server-side sparse assignment method with guarantees for recovering client-relevant experts from partial observations. Existing partial-expert approaches rely on heuristics or load-balancing without such recovery guarantees. This improves both efficiency and personalization in federated MoE training on edge devices.

entry.title: Reweighting is not Harmless: Understanding the Role of Dataset Characteristics

author.name: Amalia Ionescu, Jose G. Hernandez, Emily F. Wong, Anil K. Saini, Jason H. Moore, Tiffani J. Bright

entry.summary: Using 3,000 controlled simulations varying group size and baseline event prevalence, the authors show that reweighting for fairness can produce misleading improvements: reducing underestimation for one group while introducing it for another. Reweighting improved parity metrics while harming other error characteristics under low-prevalence conditions. This is a cautionary, empirically grounded result for fairness pre-processing practice.

entry.title: MambaTG: Candidate-Aware State Space Modeling for Future Link Prediction on Temporal Graphs

author.name: Nguyen Hong Quan, Sitao Luan, Yilun Zheng, Lihui Chen

entry.summary: MambaTG targets the harder unseen-edge case in temporal graph link prediction by identifying complementary sequential signals beyond historical recurrence and modeling them with candidate-aware state space models. Existing methods over-rely on recurring-interaction signals, degrading sharply on first-time interactions. The state space (Mamba-style) formulation offers linear-complexity temporal modeling.

entry.title: QRAE: Query-Relevant Attention Entropy for Context Compression in DeepSearch Agents

author.name: Yingjie Tan, Haiquan Qiu, Quanming Yao, Manyi Zhong, Xianzhi Yu, Yaqing Wang

entry.summary: QRAE is an online context compression method for DeepSearch LLM agents that uses sparse evidence-assessment heads to decide which retrieved chunks persist across reasoning steps. It scores candidate chunks via paired prefills—a query-free control suppresses shared attention responses while normalized entropy measures response breadth—and high-scoring chunks enter a persistent evidence whitelist. This reduces the token consumption and latency caused by accumulating retrieved context.

entry.title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels

author.name: Hyojun Yi, Geunyoung Kim, Hogeon Seo, Seunghyoung Ryu

entry.summary: PRISM shows that anomaly detection can be strong without any learned representations, combining fixed random nonlinear features with Mahalanobis scoring against normal references for both tabular detection and dense visual localization. On 47 ADBench tabular datasets PRISM-T achieves the highest mean AUROC among compared methods, and it performs well on MVTec AD. The result challenges the assumption that representation learning is necessary for anomaly detection.

entry.title: BUMP: Brief Unexpected Mid-Interpolation Peak

author.name: Melinda Fl\'ora Kiss, M\'arton Muntag, Adri\'an Csisz\'arik, D\'aniel Varga

entry.summary: The authors document and systematically analyze BUMP, a phenomenon where test accuracy briefly improves near the endpoints when linearly interpolating between permutation-aligned neural networks before dropping toward the midpoint. The effect is consistent across datasets, architectures, and training regimes, and survives perturbations like early checkpoints and extreme pruning, with ablations ruling out trivial regularization explanations. Documenting such mode-connectivity anomalies advances understanding of loss landscape structure.

entry.title: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others

author.name: Hong Jun Lee, Ziyan Wang, Jun Wang, Stefanos Leonardos, Yali Du

entry.summary: Building on opponent-shaping methods like LOLA and M-FOS, which require access to opponent parameters or learning rules, this work develops learned update rules capable of shaping other agents' learning without such access, drawing on meta-learned single-agent rules like DiscoRL. This targets a central problem in general-sum games where self-interested learning leads to poor outcomes for all. It bridges multi-agent opponent shaping with learned optimizer research.

entry.title: Context-Aware Automated NMR Structure Elucidation

author.name: Frank Hu, Jonathan M. Tubb, Grant M. Rotskoff, Matthew W. Kanan, Thomas E. Markland

entry.summary: The authors present a protocol for combining AI-based NMR spectroscopic structure elucidation with contextual chemical information, such as known reactants or desired products, using automated retrosynthetic analysis to generate large context-conditioned training sets. Incorporating this context improves structure prediction performance and real-world applicability in chemical discovery.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods for Unbounded Problems

author.name: Kevin Kurian Thomas Vaidyan, Ahmet Alacaoglu, Michael P. Friedlander

entry.summary: This paper establishes last-iterate convergence rates for proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions, motivated by black-box variational inference. Under relaxed variance assumptions it obtains near-optimal anytime rates and the optimal O(1/sqrt(T)) rate when the horizon is known.

entry.title: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models

author.name: Hanna M. Tolle, Carles Balsells-Rodas, Yixin Wang, Pedro A. M. Mediano, Amin Nejatbakhsh

entry.summary: This paper extends interventional state-space models beyond linear latent dynamics, proving affine identifiability under general injective emission functions with Gaussian transitions and identifiability up to permutation, scaling, and shift with interventions. The theory enables recovering low-dimensional neural circuit dynamics from high-dimensional observations.

entry.title: Same Origin, Different Verdicts: Text Production Conditions Confound Machine-Generated Text Detection in Russian

author.name: Stanislav Kirichenko

entry.summary: This study shows that text production conditions confound machine-generated text detection: origin is a property of the process, not an observable property of text, and conditions push text in the same direction as generative models do. Using a 1882-document Russian corpus spanning four generation channels across 45 tasks plus archival human text annotated for regimentation level, it measures the contribution of production conditions while holding origin fixed. This matters because detection verdicts carry real consequences for authors.

entry.title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse

author.name: Yuxing Peng, Zhiqing Tang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: Analyzes where a small KV-cache repair budget is best spent in non-prefix cache reuse, showing reuse loses 19-100% of context-dependent questions relative to full prefill and degrades most when surrounding chunks resemble the answer-bearing target. Repairing the target chunk via contextual compatibility recovers far more than repairing distractors.

entry.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents

author.name: Mattia Greiche, Reihaneh Rabbany, Maximilian Puelma Touzel

entry.summary: The paper tackles the validation problem in LLM-based social simulation, where agents change behavior under meaning-preserving prompt variations. It formalizes controlled context enrichment as prompt substitutions that hold semantics fixed, enabling controlled tests of whether richer grounding improves robustness, and introduces selective robustness as a measurement concept. The work directly targets a foundational methodological weakness of LLM social simulation.

entry.title: TraCE: Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding

author.name: Wooil Lee, Junpyo Hong, Jongseo Lee, Tuomas Oikarinen, Tsui-Wei Weng, Jinwoo Choi

entry.summary: TraCE is a concept-based explainability framework for video models that discovers source-flexible motion concepts by clustering optical-flow trajectories, capturing dynamic evidence from people, objects, and interactions alongside static object and scene concepts. It identifies motion-source under-specification as a flaw in existing video XAI, where region-centric explanations are ambiguous and pose-only vocabularies incomplete. It improves faithfulness of video model explanations.

entry.title: Vis2State: Visual Reasoning through Executable State Abstractions

author.name: Sheng Jin, Wentao Liu, Chen Qian

entry.summary: Vis2State is a training-free agentic framework that converts visual puzzles into explicit, revisable problem states linked to generated programs, allowing iterative refinement via inspection and execution feedback. It requires no predefined puzzle schemas. This connects visual perception with symbolic execution for reliable reasoning.

entry.title: Integrating Learned Priors through Prior-Space Reparameterization for Physically Based Inverse Rendering

author.name: Hun Hwangbo, Minjun Park, Yongsung Kim, Wooseok Song, Jungmin Ko, Junghyun Hwang, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: The paper proposes incorporating learned material priors into physically based inverse rendering via a reparameterization that shares material variables among surface points with similar predicted features on a permutohedral lattice, rather than adding auxiliary regularization losses. This leaves the optimization objective unchanged while restricting the search space. A neat methodological alternative to loss-based priors.

entry.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation

author.name: Kotaro Oishi, Kazuma Ikeda, Ryosei Hara, Ryo Yoshida, Mariko Isogawa, Kentaro Yoshioka

entry.summary: The paper tackles full-waveform LiDAR transformer bottlenecks—redundant low-intensity tokens and scarce labeled data—via intensity-guided token reduction and physics-aware augmentation exploiting FWL signal structure, targeting real-time performance for autonomous driving. FWL preserves rich reflection characteristics that improve robustness to adverse conditions. Addresses both efficiency and generalization.

entry.title: MV-Sign: Multi-View 3D Motion Integration and Enhanced Text-to-Motion Conditioning for Sign Language Production

author.name: Singyu Muk, Kaustubh Kundu, Kunyuan Xie, Weijie Wang, Kalin Stefanov

entry.summary: MV-Sign tackles noisy supervision and weak text conditioning in 3D sign language production by introducing How2Sign-MV3D, a high-fidelity multi-view 3D motion dataset built through a cross-view curation pipeline that resolves occlusion and preserves hand details. It also optimizes the text-conditioning pathway for motion generation. Better hand detail is crucial since sign language meaning depends heavily on fine hand articulation.

entry.title: Fault-Guided Cross-Layer Prediction for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a single-class anomaly detector that treats the depth of a frozen DINOv2 ViT as discrete block-to-block transitions, learning directed predictors over token hidden states. Analysis of adjacent-layer cosine similarity reveals fault lines separating stable depth segments, and cross-layer prediction exposes information that cannot be reliably transferred, flagging anomalies.

entry.title: Data-Driven Configuration of Protective Separation Zones in Collaborative Robot Cells from Operator Occupancy

author.name: Aulon Bajrami, Theo Jacobs, Werner Kraus

entry.summary: This paper proposes a camera-based method that sizes protective separation zones in collaborative robot cells from accumulated operator occupancy data across production shifts, trading off robot velocity against required safety distance per ISO/TS 15066. The resulting configuration is advisory and reviewed within the risk assessment. It offers a practical, standards-aligned way to reduce overly conservative safety zoning in factories.

entry.title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents

author.name: Shanghao Shi, Jian Xiao, Ching-Hsiang Chan, Sanjoy Baruah, Sastry Kompella, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, William Yeoh, Ning Zhang

entry.summary: SCALE is a real-time latent communication method for cyber-physical agents that exchange intermediate model representations instead of raw data, exploiting spatio-temporal continuity to reuse tokens across consecutive latent messages and avoid redundant transmission. It profiles semantic gain versus communication cost to schedule what to send under bandwidth constraints and heterogeneous task deadlines.

entry.title: Offline Learning of Reserve Prices from Censored Bids

author.name: Lavanya Marla, Yunzong Xu, Boxuan Zhou

entry.summary: The authors study learning a second-price auction reserve price from censored bid data, characterizing exactly when an optimal reserve is identified under a monotone hazard rate assumption even when the value distribution is not. When identification fails, they derive minimax-regret-optimal reserves over distributions consistent with the data.

entry.title: Align Before Aggregation: Basis-Consistent Federated LoRA under Heterogeneous Ranks

author.name: Pengpeng Qiao, Yang Cao, Lingling Zhang, Guo Cheng, Junwei Chen, Manjiang Yu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim, Masatoshi Yoshikawa

entry.summary: The paper identifies basis inconsistency in federated LoRA fine-tuning when clients have heterogeneous ranks: server-side refactorization in the compose-aggregate-factorize-dispatch loop yields unstable rank-r prefixes for lower-rank clients. The proposed aggregator aligns LoRA factors into a consistent basis before aggregation, stabilizing training across heterogeneous clients.

entry.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels

author.name: Jinho Park, Se Young Chun, Mingoo Seok

entry.summary: DictLLM is a post-training compression scheme that decomposes weight matrices within grouped layers into a shared dictionary plus layer-specific sparse coefficients, obtained directly from a pre-trained model without further training. The four-step optimization includes SVD of input-scaled weight matrices with rank amortization across groups. It targets mobile-class deployment where compute and memory are constrained.

entry.title: Continued Training of Continuous Language Flows with Token Identity Squared Supervision

author.name: Jiawei Jiang, Zhaoxiang Zang, Zhengtao Yu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a deficiency of continuous MSE supervision for diffusion and flow language models—different token distributions can yield identical weighted embedding vectors—and proposes Token Identity Brier Flow, which applies squared supervision directly to token identities when continuing training from pretrained representations.

entry.title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes

author.name: Ayal Klein

entry.summary: This paper argues that equal probe accuracy does not imply valid concept extraction, since probes can conflate target concepts with correlated nuisance attributes. Across four target-nuisance settings and two LLMs, the authors measure nuisance dependence at fixed target and responses to nuisance-only input edits, showing statistically equivalent extractors can differ substantially in validity.

entry.title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models

author.name: Xiaozhe Ji, Renfen Hu, Hai Hu

entry.summary: This paper introduces PinyinBench, a controlled benchmark of homophones, phonological features (initials, finals, tones), and polyphonic characters, applied to 17 text-only and multimodal LMs via behavioral evaluation, layer-wise probing, and activation steering. A frontier model (DeepSeek's V4 Flash, an existing model released in fall 2026) scores 90%+ on homophone judgment but drops to 72% when characters differ only in lexical tone. It reveals both substantial implicit phonological knowledge and specific tonal blind spots in LMs.

entry.title: TRACEMARK: Editor-Aware Watermarking for User Attribution in Text-Guided Image Editing

author.name: Xiaodong Wu, Xiangman Li, Jianbing Ni, Rongxing Lu

entry.summary: Tracemark embeds user-specific watermarks before image editing and recovers the user from edited images via a shared detector comparing edited features with learned reference vectors, trained jointly through a fixed editor. It addresses attribution once images are shared, surviving semantic editing that erases naive watermarks. Relevant to provenance and accountability in generative media ecosystems.

entry.title: PVDepth: Panoramic Video Depth Estimation via Geometry-Aware Spatiotemporal Adaptation

author.name: Chuanxin Song, Peixi Peng

entry.summary: PVDepth adapts perspective video depth models to panoramic (equirectangular) video, tackling ERP-specific geometric distortions and nonlinear temporal dynamics through geometry-aware spatiotemporal adaptation modules. The paper also releases PanoCARLA, a large-scale synthetic RGB-D panoramic video dataset with natural drone-like motion. Panoramic depth matters for VR and world-model applications.

entry.title: InstantHand: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Animatable Hand Avatar Reconstruction from a Single Image

author.name: Chanho Kim, Muhammad Salman Ali, Kyeonghwan Gwak, Muhammad Shaheryar, Incheol Park, Jeongwan On, Seungryul Baek

entry.summary: Presents a feed-forward framework that builds an animatable 3D Gaussian hand avatar from a single image using off-the-shelf MANO, camera, and mask estimates without test-time optimization. Two targeted techniques — a Soft Alpha Band regularizer for silhouette leakage and reliability-gated appearance transfer against color drift — address key failure modes of single-image supervision.

entry.title: KDASO: Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization for Liability Adjudication Tasks

author.name: Zi-Jian Cheng, Weiming Wu, Jie Meng, Zhen Peng, Shan Huang, Qun Li, Guobing Wu, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: KDASO addresses three limitations of skill-based LLM legal reasoning: stale skill libraries, semantic gaps between skill descriptions and execution, and context-budget overflow. It combines knowledge-driven and data-driven signals to continuously optimize skills for liability adjudication tasks such as legal charge determination.

entry.title: Goal-Branching LaCAM: Temporary Goals as Search Branches in Dense Multi-Agent Pathfinding

author.name: Stephen Chang, Daniel Harabor

entry.summary: The paper improves LaCAM for dense, corridor-heavy multi-agent pathfinding by introducing Goal-Branching, which gives blocking agents temporary goals tried as additional search branches instead of enumerating one-agent constraints. This helps escape deadlocks that PIBT's greedy successors rarely propose, using random and corridor-aware rules for candidate selection.

entry.title: FARR: Forecast-Aware Residual Refinement with Matched Endpoint Evidence for Long-Horizon Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yiyang Zhang, Yuli Zheng, Bin Li, Meimei Zhang, Qiang Sun

entry.summary: FARR observes that auxiliary conditioning in LLM-based time-series forecasting does not consistently help and can hurt when mismatched to temporal context. The method obtains a valid forecast and a null forecast under a predefined null condition, uses their difference as endpoint evidence, and trains a shared residual refiner with horizon-wise gating to correct remaining error. This is a targeted fix for an underexamined failure of conditioning in long-horizon forecasting.

entry.title: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting the Development of AI through Executable Properties

author.name: Rolf Drechsler, Christina Plump

entry.summary: Extending Formal Raising — a Turing-inspired developmental view of machine intelligence augmented with explicit behavioral properties — this paper adds security of the raising environment itself. Secure Formal Raising models policy integrity, authorization, and confidential data flow using four-valued evidence that preserves unknown and inconsistent assessments, proves six security invariants, and validates them with bounded exhaustive exploration of a plain-C reference implementation, which also surfaces a confused-deputy gap closed by a provenance requirement. It is a formal-methods take on securing AI development environments.

entry.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?

author.name: Yue Zhang, Jilei Sun, Liqiang Jing, Yijie Wei, Ruohan Yang

entry.summary: PCBRouteAgent is a multimodal LLM agent that automates printed circuit board routing by coordinating a Global Routing Planner over board images and structured electrical data with a Detailed Routing Executor driving KiCad's native engine. Unresolved failures are escalated, mirroring how human engineers separate strategy from local execution. It probes how close LLM agents are to expert-level EDA engineering work.

entry.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Yang Ouyang, Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: StepBack is a test-time decoding method that improves the efficiency of self-consistency reasoning by localizing the likely first error step in draft reasoning trajectories and resampling only the error step and its suffix, followed by majority voting. Across seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks it matches self-consistency accuracy at substantially lower sampling cost.

entry.title: KG-AST for Cheaper CI/CD: Budgeted Test Selection and AI Bug Review

author.name: Henry Yeung

entry.summary: Presents KG-AST, which scores commit risk from git history and code-graph features to prioritize expensive testing and AI-assisted review toward the riskiest commits in CI/CD pipelines. Evaluated on 155 open-source projects across 11 languages, a single cross-language model ensures heavy testing of the riskiest 20 percent of commits catches 49-64 percent of bug-introducing commits, beating baselines in every language.

entry.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Qingyun Liu, Yuankun Liu, Jiaye Feng, Jie Huang, Zonghong Dai, Haochen Li, Jingkun Wang, Weiping Li, Tong Mo

entry.summary: PSGAgent is an agentic framework that lets multimodal LLMs dynamically refine their visual perception for panoptic scene graph generation via a think-act-observe loop. It provides tools such as a Region Zoom-In Tool so models can explore small or peripheral objects and resolve ambiguous predicates that fixed-resolution viewing misses. This targets the static-observer perception bottleneck in MLLM-based scene understanding.

entry.title: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization

author.name: Kang Liu

entry.summary: This optimization theory paper establishes query-round complexity lower and upper bounds for finding approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions in a parallel query model, showing the standard subgradient rate is optimal in high dimensions even for randomized parallel algorithms. It also proves deterministic function-value-only algorithms achieve logarithmic round complexity on the real line with matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping

author.name: David Berghaus, Arber Zela, Behzad Shomali, Markus Frey, Mehdi Ali, Rafet Sifa, Volkan Cevher

entry.summary: Typed decision models make single-forward-pass predictions and cannot spend extra test-time compute the way generative models do; the RELOAD method retrofits a damped loop over a middle block with a lightweight adaptive controller, trained jointly with the decision model. Across six models from 0.4B to 4B parameters, training with loops yields gains where retrofitting loops into pretrained models previously showed none. This offers a path to adaptive test-time compute for classification-style models without extra parameters.

entry.title: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism

author.name: Joonyoung Lim, Younghwan Yoo

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how massively parallel safe RL with short rollout horizons creates a mismatch with CMDP safety constraints defined over full-episode returns, modeling staggered resets as a phase-mixture distribution. It derives a phase-aggregated cost estimator that reconstructs episode-level costs from short rollout batches, enabling safe RL at high throughput.

entry.title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Sateesh Kumar, Arnav Balaji, Arpit Bahety, Skand Peri, Georgios Pavlakos, Roberto Mart\'in-Mart\'in

entry.summary: MOMASPLAT addresses viewpoint sensitivity in imitation-learned mobile manipulation by augmenting demonstrations with novel views, extending prior static-scene novel-view synthesis to re-render the manipulated object during post-contact interaction. This targets the most critical parts of demonstrations that existing NVS augmentation leaves unaugmented.

entry.title: Stochastic Dynamics of Generative AI: From Autoregressive Models to Interacting LLM Networks and Neural SDEs

author.name: Vikram Krishnamurthy, Yiming Zhang, Luke Snow

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified stochastic dynamical-systems framework covering LLMs as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models, networks of interacting LLMs described by mean-field dynamics, and neural SDEs. It offers probabilistic interpretations of pretraining and token generation and models emergent phenomena like preferential attachment and glass-ceiling effects in LLM populations. It is a theory/survey contribution connecting generative AI to classical control and stochastic processes.

entry.title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters

author.name: Cath Pham, Kadesha Reynolds

entry.summary: This survey reviews nonlinear filtering and data assimilation methods for chaotic dynamical systems such as weather prediction and wildfire tracking, covering failure modes of Kalman-based and particle-based approaches. It then covers recent generative AI-enabled score-based filters that address these limitations. A useful bridge between classical data assimilation and modern diffusion/score generative methods.

entry.title: Scenario Augmentation for Rare Financial Events via Multimodal Latent Diffusion

author.name: Mahdi Arab Loodaricheh, Anita Raja, Indranil SenGupta

entry.summary: The authors address the scarcity of extreme market events by generating synthetic rare-event scenarios with a class-conditional diffusion model operating on jointly learned latent codes from three aligned modalities: structured variables, image transforms, and portfolio returns. CVaR labeling provides a risk-aware definition of rare windows. This could improve risk models that are typically starved of tail-event data.

entry.title: ConvPE: Convolutional Position Embedding Improves Transformers

author.name: Zehao Wang

entry.summary: ConvPE injects a windowed, content-dependent bias into attention scores via a lightweight causal convolution over a low-dimensional projection of hidden states, improving both performance and efficiency in language modeling, long-context extension, and vision. It is a plug-in compatible with RoPE, attention masks, and KV concatenation, and supports high-dimensional position embeddings. In reproductions it outperforms five 1D and eight 2D position-embedding baselines, with code released.

entry.title: Neural Collapse on Imbalanced Datasets and Open-Set Scenario

author.name: Qiufu Li, Huibing Xiao, Linlin Shen, Yongdong Huang

entry.summary: This paper theoretically reformulates neural collapse, the elegant geometric structure features and classifiers exhibit at loss minima, for imbalanced datasets and open-set settings. Using class-wise averaged losses rather than global averaged losses, the authors prove standard neural collapse emerges when class-wise losses attain minima, for both cross-entropy and binary cross-entropy, including an open-set extension where some classes are excluded. This resolves how class imbalance distorts or preserves NC geometry.

entry.title: Invariance before structure: two modes of emergent compression in representation learning

author.name: Hardik Rajpal, Dan Goodman

entry.summary: The authors propose EARL, a framework distinguishing two modes of emergence in learned representations: state-space compression, where a representation predicts its own future beyond what individual units can, and parameter-space compression, where networks with different micro-level parameters converge to the same representation. Both are formalized as Fisher sensitivities with ensemble-level information-theoretic measures. The framework explains striking representational invariance observed across biological and artificial neural networks.

entry.title: Optimal Competitive Ratios for Chasing Convex Functions with Quadratic Growth

author.name: Linzhe He, Sifan Yang, Wei Jiang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper closes gaps in the convex function chasing problem, where a learner incurs hitting and movement costs against an adversarial sequence of convex functions. It resolves the polynomial gap between upper and lower bounds for well-conditioned functions under Euclidean movement and characterizes the optimal competitive ratio for squared Euclidean movement under quadratic growth. The work is technically significant for online learning and smoothed analysis communities.

entry.title: PersonaAgent: Retrieval-Augmented Transaction Anomaly Scoring with Refreshable Multi-Entity Persona Memory

author.name: Zhengyu Fang, Liang Wang, Yingtong Dou, Yuzhong Chen, Shubham Jain, Junpeng Wang, Xiran Fan, Menghai Pan, Jiarui Sun, Yan Zheng, Yiwei Cai

entry.summary: PersonaAgent is an agentic anomaly detection framework for large-scale payment networks that represents recent entity behavior as refreshable personas stored in memory, updated by weekly batch jobs and retrieved by a lightweight adapter at inference time. This addresses the mismatch between fast-changing transaction patterns and slower model refresh schedules while sidestepping high-cardinality embedding table issues. It reflects a growing trend of agentic memory architectures in industrial fraud detection.

entry.title: Nowcasting of Tropical Cyclone Wind Fields and Intensity from Geostationary Imagery

author.name: Simon Donike, Pritthijit Nath, Cristina Radin, Arthur Avenas, Ruben Cartuyvels, Emiliano Diaz, William K. Jones, Anna Jungbluth

entry.summary: The authors train simple neural networks to predict 2D tropical cyclone surface wind fields and storm-scale intensity metrics from continuous geostationary satellite imagery, addressing the sparsity of SAR-derived wind observations. Ablations show joint prediction of fields and scalar metrics from a shared latent space improves retrieval of maximum wind radius, especially for rapid intensification events. This has operational value for hurricane monitoring.

entry.title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions

author.name: Angel Daruna, Michael Cogswell, Tixiao Shan, Yi Yao, Han-Pang Chiu, Ajay Divakaran

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hidden Markov model for online prediction of an adversary's next action, where the latent state captures behavioral regimes that can switch within an episode, and actions are structured as operations with state-dependent feasible arguments on a masked action tree. The same likelihood supports next-action prediction and belief updating, useful for cyber defense and adversarial planning scenarios.

entry.title: Coverage Hides Churn: Auditing and Preserving Conformal Decisions as VLM Label Registries Grow

author.name: Jai Kumar Sharma, Peeyush Tapadiya

entry.summary: The paper shows that adding new text-learned labels to vision-language classifiers silently changes conformal prediction decisions for old labels, because softmax-based conformal scores depend on an average over all labels. Across eleven settings, recalibration changes 53-90% of old decisions on new images while marginal coverage guarantees remain satisfied, motivating audit and preservation methods.

entry.title: Which Signals of Code Correctness Survive Distribution Shift? Hidden-State and Causal Predictors of Program and Verdict Correctness

author.name: Viola Campos, Thomas Klassert, Adrian Ulges

entry.summary: The authors compare six execution-free code correctness predictors from four families on Qwen3-Coder-30B and gpt-oss-20b under benchmark shift (LiveCodeBench to BigCodeBench) and language shift across Python, C++, and Java. The study evaluates which signals from output probabilities, sampled solutions, or hidden states reliably identify model judgments warranting verification.

entry.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching

author.name: Thanapong Intharah, Zhichao Gao, Yiliang Liu, Hao Dong

entry.summary: USB Gym is a standardized Gymnasium testbed for ultrasound guidance that simulates ultrasound from public patient CT and evaluates complete guidance pipelines rather than isolated components. It provides three replaceable slots (organ segmenter, controller, reward), into which 20 published methods were inserted and compared on the same held-out patient episodes. It matters because prior ultrasound-guidance methods were evaluated in separate simulators, making end-to-end comparison impossible.

entry.title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue

author.name: Ibrahim Khebour, Nikhil Krishnaswamy

entry.summary: This paper studies strategic clarification in dialogue: asking clarification questions in a reference game only when answers will meaningfully narrow candidate referents, countering LLMs' bias toward premature single-turn answering. The authors build a controlled test environment from SIMMC 2.1 that records how many questions each ambiguous reference requires, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods fare. It matters for building collaborative, multi-turn agents.

entry.title: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit?

author.name: Zehao Lin, Kai Chen, Xixuan Hao, Erenkai Zhu, Chunyu Li, Helan Hu

entry.summary: Studies why improved confidence estimates in LLM-built knowledge graphs often fail to translate into better human audit outcomes, formalizing auditing as budgeted covering and deriving conditions via repairability, selection headroom, and label validity. Experiments on Re-DocRED across five extraction configurations quantify when better error prediction is decision-relevant.

entry.title: Overview of the NTCIR-19 SciClaimEval Task: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers

author.name: Xanh Ho, Andr\'{e} Greiner-Petter, Florian Boudin, Yun-Ang Wu, Sunisth Kumar, Tian Cheng Xia, Hiba Akbi, Tim Schopf, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: Describes SciClaimEval, an NTCIR-19 shared task on verifying scientific claims against the tables and figures of the papers they come from, with 180 papers across ML, NLP, and medicine and contrastive supporting/refuting evidence versions. Fourteen teams submitted 177 runs, mostly based on prompted multimodal LLMs with multi-stage pipelines.

entry.title: Ruby-OPD: Enhancing Pronunciation Controllability and Accuracy for Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Rui Hu, Xiaolong Lin, Zhenpeng Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes Ruby-OPD, a two-stage framework for Japanese TTS that combines Ruby text representations preserving both lexical semantics and pronunciation readings with on-policy distillation in a flow-matching model. It bridges the gap between controllable cascaded systems and natural zero-shot TTS while reducing polyphone errors.

entry.title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries

author.name: Wenhui Chu

entry.summary: This single-author study examines whether long-running LLM agents' context-compaction handoff summaries contain unsupported permissions or restrictions, whether such sentences change successor agent behavior, and where they originate. Using synthetic tool-use tasks with a ground-truth permission ledger and replay-based counterfactual tests, it finds unsupported restrictions in 1.2-2.4% of summaries, with mixed statistical evidence on behavioral impact.

entry.title: Autonomous agents for electricity-system planning

author.name: Yoon Pyo Lee, Samrendra Roy, Jay Phil Yoo, Kazuma Kobayashi, Souvik Chakraborty, Syed Bahauddin Alam

entry.summary: The authors present an autonomous LLM-agent framework for electricity system planning that cycles through proposal, numerical evaluation, feedback interpretation, redesign, and final selection while executing real investment-and-dispatch optimizations. Evaluated across forty carbon-constrained trajectories, agents decide investment bounds, storage conditions, and feeder interventions under fixed acceptance criteria. It demonstrates a credible route to applying agentic AI in a high-stakes infrastructure domain.

entry.title: LegalEvolver: Agentic Legal Judgment Prediction via Rubric-Guided Self-Evolution

author.name: Xinyu Yang, Jiejun Tan, Chenlong Deng, Chenghao Zhang, Tongyu Wen, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: LegalEvolver is a query optimization framework for legal judgment prediction that improves retrieval agents, which typically issue naive queries from the user request and miss latent legal issues. It uses rubric-guided self-evolution to sample and select legally informative queries and search trajectories. It targets a domain where retrieval quality directly determines prediction quality.

entry.title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation

author.name: Yajie Bao, Jiaye Fu, Youtian Lin, Shuang Wu, Jiachen Qian, Feihu Zhang, Xun Cao, Yao Yao

entry.summary: MIKU provides a unified framework for standardized physically based rendering (PBR) material generation, with a normalization scheme harmonizing heterogeneous material parameterizations across 3D content domains. It addresses instability caused by differing material definitions and rendering conventions. Standardized PBR generation is valuable for graphics and 3D asset pipelines.

entry.title: Subspace Learning with Outlier Exposure for Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Hongxu Shen, Kun Fang, Jiahui Zheng, Jian Sun, Qinghua Tao

entry.summary: RecOE is an outlier-exposure-based OoD detection framework that learns feature subspaces from in-distribution and auxiliary outlier data, moving beyond logit-centric approaches to exploit richer feature-space information. Reliable OoD detection matters for safe deployment of neural networks. The theoretical framing around subspace learning adds depth.

entry.title: Which Objects Stay? Learning Hierarchical Persistence Beliefs for Lifelong Open-Vocabulary Object Maps

author.name: Thanh Nguyen Canh, Haolan Zhang, Nak Young Chong
